Archmages are powerful (and usually quite old) spellcasters dedicated to the study of the arcane arts. Benevolent ones counsel kings and queens, while evil ones rule as tyrants and pursue lichdom. Those who are neither good nor evil sequester themselves in remote towers to practice their magic without interruption.
An archmage typically has one or more apprentice mages, and an archmage's abode has numerous magical wards and guardians to discourage interlopers.
combat-strategy: Pre-buff with Mind Blank and Mage Armor, then open at 150 ft with four Arcane Burst attacks (108 average damage if all connect) against the highest-threat target. Level-7 Lightning Bolt or level-9 Cone of Cold on clustered groups — 12d10 cone cold is a party-wipe button; save it for a moment when enemies bunch in a corridor. Misty Step (3/Day) plus 30-ft kiting keeps melee out of reach, and Protective Magic (Counterspell or Shield, 3/Day) defuses the fight's turning point — read the party's casters and interrupt their burst or heal. Invisibility then reposition, Fly to break ground-based chases, and Teleport out when outmatched or to relocate the fight. He fights defensively at range, never within a fighter's reach, and escapes via Teleport the moment his reaction pool is spent.

name: Archpriest

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The archpriest makes three Radiant Burst attacks.

actions.name: Radiant Burst
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. Hit: 27 (4d10 + 5) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Holy Word (Recharge 4-6)
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 17, each enemy in a 20-foot Emanation originating from the archpriest. Failure: 21 (6d6) Radiant damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the end of the archpriest's next turn. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 21 (6d6) Radiant damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the end of the archpriest's next turn. Success: Half damage only.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The archpriest casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17):
At Will: Light, Thaumaturgy
1/Day Each: Flame Strike (level 6 version), Greater Restoration, Raise Dead, Zone of Truth

bonus_actions.name: Divine Aid (3/Day)
bonus_actions.description: The priest casts Bless, Dispel Magic, Healing Word, or Lesser Restoration, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

combat-strategy: Open by buffing the front line with Bless via Divine Aid, then hang back at 60 feet and plink away with Radiant Burst, which works in melee or at range so it never has to give up its action to stay safe. Hold Holy Word for the moment two or more martial threats cluster within 20 feet — stunning a heavy hitter while minions swing is the fight-defining play. Spend remaining Divine Aid uses on Healing Word to keep a bloodied ally standing and Dispel Magic on the party's strongest buffs or magical effects. Retreat behind cover or full defenders when surrounded, and if a key minion falls, Raise Dead can turn a pyrrhic enemy victory around in a single round.

name: Assassin

traits.name: Evasion
traits.description: If the assassin is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, the assassin instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the save and only half damage if it fails. It can't use this trait if it has the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The assassin makes three attacks, using Shortsword or Light Crossbow in any combination.

actions.name: Shortsword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Piercing damage plus 17 (5d6) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the assassin's next turn.

actions.name: Light Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +7, range 80/320 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Piercing damage plus 21 (6d6) Poison damage.

bonus_actions.name: Cunning Action
bonus_actions.description: The assassin takes the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.

description: Trained in the use of poison, assassins are remorseless killers who work for nobles, guild masters, sovereigns, and anyone else who can afford them.
combat-strategy: Open from concealment with Light Crossbow poison shots (6d6 poison) at an isolated backline caster or healer, using the Stealth +10 first-round ambush advantage. Kite to keep 80 feet of distance, using Cunning Action to Disengage and Hide between volleys, and never stand in the open against a concentrated party. If enemies close, switch to Shortsword — the Poisoned condition gives their attacks disadvantage, which shields the fragile 97 HP frame. Break off with Cunning Action and vanish when it drops below half hit points or when hiding spots run out.

name: Awakened Shrub

actions.name: Rake
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +1, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Slashing damage.

description: An awakened shrub is an ordinary shrub given sentience and mobility by the awaken spell or similar magic.
combat-strategy: This is a lookout, not a fighter: pose as an ordinary shrub until enemies pass, rake one for its 1 slashing damage, then let the ambush it springs do the real work. Use 20-foot speed and camouflage to stay at the edge of the fight and re-hide the moment anyone turns toward it. Flee to its owner once it takes so much as a scratch — losing a 10 HP shrub is information, not a defeat.

name: Awakened Tree

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

description: An awakened tree is an ordinary tree given sentience and mobility by the awaken spell or similar magic.
combat-strategy: Ambush from a stand of trees where its camouflage and 10-foot Slam reach punish anything that steps close. Hold chokepoints and doorways, using its Huge size to physically block corridors while its Slams outrange most melee weapons. Its 20-foot speed means it cannot chase, so pick where the fight happens and make the party come to it. Sink back into the treeline and disengage when concentrated damage or axes start chopping it down — wood burns and splinters, so keep fire and sharp axes at arm's length.

name: Axe Beak

actions.name: Beak
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Slashing damage.

description: An axe beak is a tall flightless bird with strong legs and a heavy, wedge-shaped beak. It has a nasty disposition and tends to attack any unfamiliar creature that wanders too close.
combat-strategy: Pack-hunt across open terrain, using 50-foot speed to run down stragglers separated from the party. Flock around a target so several beaks gang up on one engaged foe, pecking at flanks and backs. Individually fragile at 19 HP, they should wheel away and circle whenever hit hard, and scatter if the flock loses two or three members to an area effect.

name: Azer

actions.name: Warhammer
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) bludgeoning damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack, plus 3 (1d6) fire damage.

traits.name: Heated Body
traits.description: A creature that touches the azer or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 ft. of it takes 5 (1d10) fire damage.

traits.name: Heated Weapons
traits.description: When the azer hits with a metal melee weapon, it deals an extra 3 (1d6) fire damage (included in the attack).

traits.name: Illumination
traits.description: The azer sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 ft..

description:
Natives of the Elemental Plane of Fire, azers are master crafters, expert miners, and sworn foes of the efreet. In appearance and manner, an azer resembles a male dwarf, but this is a facade. Beneath its metallic­ looking skin, an azer is a being of fire, which outwardly manifests in its fiery hair and beard.

Made, Not Born. Azers don't reproduce. They are each crafted from bronze by another azer and imbued with a portion of the crafter's inner flame. Each azer is sculpted with unique features. This crafting process limits the growth of the azer population and is the primary reason that these creatures remain rare.

Volcanic Dwellers. Azers dwell in a kingdom on the border between the Elemental Plane of Earth and the Elemental Plane of Fire - a range of mountains and volcanoes whose spires rise as a series of fortresses. Beneath mountain peaks, under volcanic calderas, and amid rivers of magma, azers extract gleaming metals and glittering gems from the earth. Squads of azer patrol the passes and tunnels of their realm, fending off the salamander raiders whose efreet masters order strikes against the azer kingdom.

Enemies of the Efreet. Long ago, the efreet and the azers were allies. Azers helped create the City of Brass, forging that home of the efreet into one of the most wondrous places in creation. When the azers had finished their work, the efreet betrayed them, making a failed attempt to enslave the azers so as to protect the secrets of the city. Despite occasional raids and skirmishes, however, the two sides have so far refrained from all-out conflict. The azers believe that only the threat of them revealing the hidden ways into the City of Brass keeps the efreet in check.

Masters of Metal and Gems. Azers are masterful artisans, and create beautiful works from the gems and precious metals found in their volcanic habitat. They rate the value of such treasures above all other things, sometimes dispatching parties across the planes to seek out rare metals and gemstones.
When azers are called by magic to the Material Plane, it is typically to help forge an elaborate magic item or work of art, for it is said that their skill in such craft knows no equal.

Living Fire. An azer doesn't require food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Fight in press: drag the brawl into cramped corridors and forge-workshops where Heated Body burns every enemy that swings at it and Heated Weapons add fire to every hit. Two-hand the warhammer for the extra damage die and let weak melee foes win the exchange only to lose the attrition. Immune to fire and poison, so it can stand in its own forge fires and ignore poison spray. Cluster tightly in groups to become living barricades, but avoid sustained focus fire — AC 17 hides only 39 hit points.

name: Azer Pyromancer

traits.name: Fire Aura
traits.description: At the end of each of the azer's turns, each creature of the azer's choice in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the azer takes 11 (2d10) Fire damage unless the azer has the Incapacitated condition.

traits.name: Illumination
traits.description: The azer sheds Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The azer makes two Flame Burst attacks.

actions.name: Flame Burst
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Fire damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The azer casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15):
At Will: Elementalism, Mage Hand
1/Day: Fireball

reactions.name: Hellish Rebuke (2/Day)
reactions.description: The azer casts Hellish Rebuke in response to that spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

combat-strategy: Open with Fireball on a clustered party, then fall back behind cover and trade Flame Burst volleys at its 120-foot reach. Its 11-fire Fire Aura makes melee pursuit cost a turn tax every round, so when chargers close, back 30 feet away and let the aura bleed them. Save the two Hellish Rebukes for the first rounds to torch a martial attacker who commits to reaching it. Once Fireball and rebukes are spent, kite at maximum range behind minions and disengage if the party tries to surround it.

name: Azer Sentinel

traits.name: Fire Aura
traits.description: At the end of each of the azer's turns, each creature of the azer's choice in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the azer takes 5 (1d10) Fire damage unless the azer has the Incapacitated condition.

traits.name: Illumination
traits.description: The azer sheds Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet.

actions.name: Burning Hammer
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) Fire damage.

combat-strategy: Hold the post: stand in doorways, stair heads, and corridor bends where its Fire Aura taxes every attacker who comes within 5 feet. Swing Burning Hammer at whatever lingers in reach while the aura cooks grapplers and anyone shoving past. Its real job is the alarm, not the kill — trade a few rounds, raise the alarm, then fall back to the guard post before it goes down standing in the open.

name: Baboon

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The baboon has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the baboon's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +1, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 (1d4 − 1) Piercing damage.

combat-strategy: Swarm in packs and surround the lone or smallest target so Pack Tactics grants Advantage on every Bite. Use 30-foot climb speed to dart onto branches, crates, and rocks, chitter, dive-bite, then vanish upward when struck. Each baboon has 3 hit points, so any solid hit should send it scrambling to regroup — keep the pack tight enough that at least one ally is always within 5 feet of the target to keep Advantage online.

name: Badger

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage.

combat-strategy: Ambush from the burrow: erupt at passing ankles, land a Bite, then dive back underground where most attackers cannot follow. Use its 5-foot burrow speed to fight from cover, popping up elsewhere as a persistent nuisance that can't be pinned down. At 5 hit points, go to ground when struck hard, and prefer night fights where its darkvision flips the advantage.

name: Balor

traits.name: Death Throes
traits.description: The balor explodes when it dies. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 20, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the balor. Failure: 31 (9d6) Fire damage plus 31 (9d6) Force damage. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: If the balor dies outside the Abyss, it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Abyss.

traits.name: Fire Aura
traits.description: At the end of each of the balor's turns, each creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the balor takes 13 (3d8) Fire damage.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If the balor fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The balor has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The balor makes one Flame Whip attack and one Lightning Blade attack.

actions.name: Flame Whip
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +14, reach 30 ft. Hit: 18 (3d6 + 8) Force damage plus 17 (5d6) Fire damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, the balor pulls the target up to 25 feet straight toward itself, and the target has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Lightning Blade
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +14, reach 10 ft. Hit: 21 (3d8 + 8) Force damage plus 22 (4d10) Lightning damage, and the target can't take Reactions until the start of the balor's next turn.

bonus_actions.name: Teleport
bonus_actions.description: The balor teleports itself or a willing demon within 10 feet of itself up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space the balor can see.

description:
Figures of ancient and terrible evil, balors rule as generals over demonic armies, yearning to seize power while destroying any creatures that oppose them.
Wielding a flaming whip and a longsword that channels the power of the storm, a balor's battle prowess is fueled by hatred and rage. It channels this demonic fury in its death throes, falling within a blast of fire that can destroy even the hardiest foes.
combat-strategy: Open with Teleport to a flanking position, then use Flame Whip to yank a soft backliner 25 feet straight into Fire Aura range and knock them Prone for the follow-up Lightning Blade, which also strips their Reaction. Its 30-foot reach controls the midfight — dance at that edge, reel fighters into the fire, then Teleport out of concentrated counterattacks. Lean on Magic Resistance and spend Legendary Resistance only on fight-enders like Banishment, Power Word Kill, or petrification. Manage Death Throes as a weapon: if cornered, refuse to die near the dense cluster — instead drag the killing blow into the open or the Abyss, where the 30-foot, 62-damage explosion scatters the party rather than ending the fight.

name: Bandit

actions.name: Scimitar
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Light Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +3, range 80/320 ft. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) Piercing damage.

description:
Bandits rove in gangs and are sometimes led by thugs, veterans, or spellcasters. Not all bandits are evil. Oppression, drought, disease, or famine can often drive otherwise honest folk to a life of banditry.
Pirates are bandits of the high seas. They might be freebooters interested only in treasure and murder, or they might be privateers sanctioned by the crown to attack and plunder an enemy nation's vessels.
combat-strategy: Ambush from cover with crossbow volleys on the tail of the road, then demand tribute before the party can draw weapons. If charged, half close to melee with scimitars while the rest shoot from 80 feet, using carts and trees as firing cover. These break and run at roughly half casualties and surrender when their captain falls — morale, not hit points, is the stat to track.

name: Bandit Captain

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The bandit makes two attacks, using Scimitar and Pistol in any combination.

actions.name: Scimitar
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Pistol
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +5, range 30/90 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Piercing damage.

reactions.name: Parry
reactions.description: Trigger: The bandit is hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon. Response: The bandit adds 2 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

description:
Bandits rove in gangs and are sometimes led by thugs, veterans, or spellcasters. Not all bandits are evil. Oppression, drought, disease, or famine can often drive otherwise honest folk to a life of banditry.
Pirates are bandits of the high seas. They might be freebooters interested only in treasure and murder, or they might be privateers sanctioned by the crown to attack and plunder an enemy nation's vessels.
combat-strategy: Lead from the second rank, mixing Pistol shots at range with Scimitar cuts when engaged, since its Multiattack freely combines them. Save Parry's +2 AC for the party's hardest-hitting melee attacker, where it converts big hits into misses. Focus wounded or isolated targets, and use its +4 Athletics to shove foes off ledges, into fires, or away from doorways. Holds the line while any bandits stand, but flees when more than half the crew falls or it drops below a quarter of its hit points.

name: Bandit Crime Lord

traits.name: Evasion
traits.description: If the bandit is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, the bandit instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the save and only half damage if it fails. It can't use this trait if it has the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The bandit makes three attacks, using Scimitar or Pistol in any combination.

actions.name: Scimitar
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Slashing damage plus 14 (4d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Pistol
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +9, range 30/90 ft. Hit: 10 (1d10 + 5) Piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) Poison damage.

bonus_actions.name: Deadly Aim
bonus_actions.description: The bandit gives itself Advantage on the next attack roll it makes during the current turn. If that attack hits, the target takes an extra 28 (8d6) Poison damage.

combat-strategy: Vanish with Stealth +13 before the shooting starts and open with unseen Pistol volleys, taking ambush Advantage on the opening shots at the healer or caster. Commit Deadly Aim every round against the single biggest threat — Advantage plus 28 extra poison damage is its signature execution. Kite to stay within 90-foot Pistol range, spending an action to re-hide when spotted, and rely on Evasion to shrug off the party's area spells. Never let a grappler corner it; Dash and Disengage to reset distance, and slip out an escape route once its guard is dead or it has lost more than half its hit points.

name: Bandit Deceiver

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The bandit makes three Dagger attacks.

actions.name: Dagger
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) Piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Blinding Flash (Recharge 4-6)
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 14, each creature in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point the bandit can see within 120 feet. Failure: 13 (3d6 + 3) Radiant damage, and the target has the Blinded condition until the start of the bandit's next turn. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 13 (3d6 + 3) Radiant damage, and the target has the Blinded condition until the start of the bandit's next turn. Success: Half damage only.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The bandit casts one of the following spells, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14):
At Will: Disguise Self, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion
1/Day Each: Hold Person (level 4 version), Mage Armor (included in AC), Major Image

combat-strategy: Infiltrate in Disguise Self, then blow the fight open with level-4 Hold Person on the martial leader — a paralyzed target eats three auto-critical Dagger hits for roughly 60 damage in one turn. Use Blinding Flash as a repositioning grenade, detonating the 10-foot sphere at 120 feet into a cluster of pursuers to blind them while it escapes. Fill dead rounds with Major Image false exits and phantom reinforcements to split the party's attention, keeping STR 8 and its low saves out of contact. Once Hold Person is spent, it fights by blinding, bluffing, and kiting — flee when the deception collapses, but the dagger poison keeps paying even on the run.

name: Banshee

traits.name: Detect Life
traits.description: The banshee magically senses the direction of creatures up to 1 mile away that aren't Constructs or Undead.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.description: The banshee can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The banshee makes two Corrupting Touch attacks and uses Horrify.

actions.name: Corrupting Touch
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Horrify
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature the banshee can see within 60 feet that can see the banshee. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition until the start of the banshee's next turn. Success: The target is immune to this banshee's Horrify for 24 hours.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target has the Frightened condition until the start of the banshee's next turn. Success: The target is immune to this banshee's Horrify for 24 hours.

actions.name: Deathly Wail (1/Day)
actions.description: The banshee releases a mournful wail if it isn't in sunlight. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature within 30 feet that can hear the wail and isn't a Construct or an Undead. Failure: If the target has 25 Hit Points or fewer, it drops to 0 Hit Points. Otherwise, the target takes 10 (3d6) Psychic damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: If the target has 25 Hit Points or fewer, it drops to 0 Hit Points. Otherwise, the target takes 10 (3d6) Psychic damage. Success: The target takes no damage.

description:
When night falls, unlucky travelers hear the faint cries of the forlorn dead. This woeful spirit is a banshee, a spiteful creature formed from the spirit of a female elf.
Banshees appear as luminous, wispy forms that vaguely recall their mortal features. A banshee's face is wreathed in a wild tangle of hair, its body clad in wispy rags that flutter and stream around it.

Divine Wrath. Banshees are the undead remnants of elves who, blessed with great beauty, failed to use their gift to bring joy to the world. Instead, they used their beauty to corrupt and control others. Elves afflicted by the banshee's curse experience no gladness, feeling only distress in the presence of the living. As the curse takes its toll, their minds and bodies decay, until death completes their transformation into undead monsters.

Sorrow Bound. A banshee becomes forever bound to the place of its demise, unable to venture more than five miles from there. It is forced to relive every moment of its life with perfect recall, yet always refuses to accept responsibility for its doom.

Beauty Hoarders. The vanity that inspired the banshee's cursed creation persists in undeath. These creatures covet beautiful objects: fine jewelry, paintings, statues, and other objects of art. At the same time, a banshee abhors any mirrored surface, for it can't bear to see the horror of its own existence. A single glimpse of itself is enough to send a banshee into a rage.

Undead Nature. A banshee doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Hunt at night — Deathly Wail fails in sunlight, so she controls when and where the fight starts. Use Detect Life to home in on living prey from a mile off, drift through walls with Incorporeal Movement, and drop into the middle of a camp or corridor with Deathly Wail to instantly drop anyone at 25 hit points or fewer. Follow with Horrify on whichever survivor looks most dangerous, then Corrupting Touch the Frightened targets who can't press the attack. Hover 40-foot flight above melee and phase through obstacles when pincered; she withdraws once the Wail is spent and her 54 hit points are halved.

name: Barbed Devil

traits.name: Barbed Hide
traits.description: At the start of each of its turns, the devil deals 5 (1d10) Piercing damage to any creature it is grappling or any creature grappling it.

traits.name: Diabolical Restoration
traits.description: If the devil dies outside the Nine Hells, its body disappears in sulfurous smoke, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Nine Hells.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The devil has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The devil makes one Claws attack and one Tail attack, or it makes two Hurl Flame attacks.

actions.name: Claws
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13) from both claws.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 14 (2d10 + 3) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Hurl Flame
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +5, range 150 ft. Hit: 17 (5d6) Fire damage. If the target is a flammable object that isn't being worn or carried, it starts burning.

description:
Creatures of unbridled greed and desire, barbed devils act as guards to the more powerful denizens of the Nine Hells and their vaults. Resembling a tall humanoid covered in sharp barbs, spines, and hooks, a barbed devil has gleaming eyes that are ever watchful for objects and creatures it might claim for itself. These fiends welcome any chance to fight when victory promises reward.
Barbed devils are known for an alertness that makes them difficult to surprise, and they attend to their duties without boredom or distraction. They use their sharp claws as weapons or hurl balls of flame at foes that try to flee them.
combat-strategy: Rush the most dangerous mid-tier threat, Claws to Grapple (escape DC 13), and let Barbed Hide auto-shred it every turn it stays grabbed or tries to grapple back. Once pinned, work at 10-foot Tail reach, slashing a grappled target that cannot dodge away, while claws rip if it fails to escape. Use Hurl Flame at 150 feet on backline casters, or ignite cover, wagons, and supplies to deny the party ground. Magic Resistance makes their banishment and control saves unreliable against it — grapple, bleed, and outlast, retreating only when its quarry is dead or Hell-born reinforcements arrive.

name: Bard

actions.name: Shortsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: S (1d6 + 2} piercing damage.

actions.name: Shortbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack:+4 to hit, range 80/ 320 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2} piercing damage.

traits.name: Spellcasting
traits.description:
The bard is a 4th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell at- tacks). It has the following bard spells prepared:

Cantrips {at wil1): friends, mage hand, vicious mockery
1st level (4 slots): charm person, healing word, heroism, sleep, thunderwave
2nd level (3 slots): invisibility, shatter

traits.name: Song of Rest
traits.description: The bard can perform a song while taking a short rest. Any ally who hears the song regains an extra 1d6 hit points if it spends any Hit Dice to regain hit points at the end ofthat rest. The bard can confer this benefit on itself as well.

traits.name: Taunt
traits.description: The bard can use a bonus action on its turn to target one creature within 30 feet of it. If the target can hear the bard, the target must succeed on a DC 12 Charisma saving throw or have disadvantage on ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws until the start ofthe bard's next turn.

description: Bards are gifted poets, storytellers, and entertainers who travel far and wide, commonly found performing in taverns or in the company of jolly bands of adventurers, rough-and-tumble mercenaries, or wealthy patrons.
combat-strategy: Hang back and control the fight from the second rank: open with Sleep or Thunderwave on a clumped party, then keep allies up with Heroism and Healing Word. Spend the bonus action on Taunt each round against the party's fighter or leader — disadvantage on their attacks, checks, and saves is the single strongest thing this bard does. Fill the action with Vicious Mockery or Shortbow from range, and Invisibility covers its withdrawal when the front collapses. Given a parley it will charm instead of fight; run the moment the line breaks.

name: Barlgura

traits.name: Demonic Restoration
traits.description: If the barlgura dies outside the Abyss, its body dissolves into ichor, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Abyss.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The barlgura makes one Tormenting Bite attack and two Thrash attacks.

actions.name: Tormenting Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage plus 13 (2d12) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Thrash
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The barlgura casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13):
2/Day Each: Disguise Self, Invisibility (self only)
1/Day Each: Entangle, Phantasmal Killer (level 6 version)

bonus_actions.name: Leap
bonus_actions.description: The barlgura jumps up to 40 feet by spending 10 feet of movement.

description:
The barlgura represents the savagery and brutality of the Abyss. Barlguras gather in packs to take down tougher foes, keep gruesome trophies from their victories, and decorate their territory with such objects.
A barlgura looks like a hulking orangutan with a gruesome, drooping visage and tusks jutting from its jaw. Standing just under 8 feet tall, it has broad shoulders and weighs 650 pounds. It moves apishly along the ground, but it climbs with great speed and agility.
combat-strategy: Cast Invisibility, then Leap 40 feet as a bonus action and cover the rest with its 40-foot walk to land on a caster 80 feet out before anyone can react. Tormenting Bite plus two Thrash attacks knocks the target Prone, and Prone grants the barlgura Advantage on every attack for the rest of the round. Save Phantasmal Killer (level 6) for a Wisdom-weak spellcaster early, and Entangle to pin clusters while it picks them apart. If the hunt goes badly, boom up a tree or into underbrush and vanish with Stealth +5 and 30-foot blindsight — it never fights fair, and never fights to the death.

name: Basilisk

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage.

bonus_actions.name: Petrifying Gaze (Recharge 4-6)
bonus_actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. If the basilisk sees its reflection in the Cone, the basilisk must make this save. First Failure: The target has the Restrained condition and repeats the save at the end of its next turn if it is still Restrained, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second Failure: The target has the Petrified condition instead of the Restrained condition.

description:
Travelers sometimes find objects that look like pieces of remarkably lifelike stone carvings of wildlife. Missing parts appear to have been bitten off. Seasoned explorers regard such relics as warnings, knowing that the basilisk that created them is likely to be nearby.

Adaptable Predators. Basilisks thrive in arid, temperate, or tropical climates. They lair in caves or other sheltered sites. Most often, basilisks are encountered underground.
A basilisk born and raised in captivity can be domesticated and trained. Such a trained basilisk knows how to avoid meeting the eyes of those its master wishes to protect from its gaze, but it makes a daunting guardian beast. Because of this use, basilisk eggs are highly prized.

Gaze of Stone. Basilisks are ponderous for hunting creatures, but they needn't chase prey. Meeting a basilisk's supernatural gaze can be enough to affect a rapid transformation, transforming a victim into porous stone. Basilisks, with their strong jaws, are able to consume the stone. The stone returns to organic form in the basilisk's gullet.
Some alchemists are said to know how to process the basilisk's gullet and the fluids contained within. Properly handled, the gullet produces an oil that can return petrified creatures to flesh and life. Unfortunately for such a victim, any parts lost in stone form remain absent if the creature revives. Revivification using the oil is impossible if a vital part of the petrified creature, such as its head, is detached.
combat-strategy: Fight in tunnels and corridors where the 30-foot Cone of Petrifying Gaze cannot be ducked, turning to face pursuers and using the gaze on every Recharge 4-6 it comes up. Gaze first, Bite second: a first failed save leaves the target Restrained and auto-hittable, and a second failure petrifies for good, so pin the Restrained target against a wall and grind it while it rerolls. Shift its angle constantly so the cone sweeps between cover positions, forcing PCs to choose between losing line of sight and risking stone. Slow at 20 feet, it fights defensively — if the party advances with eyes averted or mirrors, fall back to a deeper, narrower den where the cone has nowhere to miss.

name: Bat

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage.

combat-strategy: Not a combatant so much as a hazard: burst from a cave mouth in a shrieking swarm, darting in pitch darkness on 60-foot blindsight to break concentration, spring traps, and bite for 1 damage apiece. Scatter at the first serious blow since each has 1 hit point, then regroup overhead and re-swarm. Their real value is marking prey for something bigger or herding panicked travelers into an ambush.

name: Bearded Devil

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The devil has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The devil makes one Beard attack and one Infernal Glaive attack.

actions.name: Beard
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the devil's next turn. Until this poison ends, the target can't regain Hit Points.

actions.name: Infernal Glaive
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Slashing damage. If the target is a creature and doesn't already have an infernal wound, it is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12. Failure: The target receives an infernal wound. While wounded, the target loses 5 (1d10) Hit Points at the start of each of its turns. The wound closes after 1 minute, after a spell restores Hit Points to the target, or after the target or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to stanch the wound, doing so by succeeding on a DC 12 Wisdom (Medicine) check.
actions.save_effect: The target receives an infernal wound. While wounded, the target loses 5 (1d10) Hit Points at the start of each of its turns. The wound closes after 1 minute, after a spell restores Hit Points to the target, or after the target or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to stanch the wound, doing so by succeeding on a DC 12 Wisdom (Medicine) check.

description:
Bearded devils serve archdevils as shock troops, fighting shoulder-to-shoulder and reveling in the glory of battle. They respond with violence to any slight, real or imagined, gorging themselves on violence as their infernal saw-toothed glaives carve a path through their foes.
A bearded devil is humanoid in form, with pointed ears, scaly skin, a long tail, and claws that clearly show its fiendish nature. These devils take their names from the snakelike growths that adorn their chins, which they use to lash and poison enemies, weakening them with their virulent venom.
combat-strategy: Lock onto the party's healer-reliant frontline: Beard hits leave the target Poisoned and unable to regain hit points, while Infernal Glaive stacks an infernal wound bleeding 1d10 each of their turns. That one-two stalls entire healing economies, so keep both effects stacked on the same victim instead of spreading them. Magic Resistance blunts control spells, so the party cannot safely shut it down with saves. At 58 hit points with a 10-foot reach glaive, it grinds willingly — stay in the clinch and let the wounds do the killing.

name: Behemoth
damage_resistances: Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing from Nonmagical Attacks

traits.name: Thick Hide
traits.description: Behemoth has Resistance to nonmagical Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

traits.name: Unstoppable Charge
traits.description: If Behemoth moves at least 30 ft. straight toward a target and hits it with a Gore on the same turn, the target takes an extra 14 (4d6) Bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a DC 25 Strength saving throw or be knocked Prone.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Behemoth makes two Gore attacks and one Stomp attack.

actions.name: Gore
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +18, reach 10 ft. Hit: 26 (3d10 + 10) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Stomp
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +18, reach 10 ft. Hit: 32 (4d10 + 10) Bludgeoning damage. The target has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Earthshaker (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 25, each creature within 60 ft. on the ground. Failure: 55 (10d10) Bludgeoning damage. Success: Half damage.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Gore
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Gore attack.

legendary_actions.name: Stomp
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Stomp attack.

legendary_actions.name: Trumpet (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Behemoth bellows. Each enemy within 60 ft. that can hear it must succeed on a DC 23 Wisdom saving throw or be unable to use Reactions until the end of its next turn.

description: The land-walker of the old scriptures — a river-horse of impossible bulk whose grazing reshapes valleys and whose tread makes the plain tremble.
combat-strategy: He charges the densest line; a Gore on the run topples, and Earthshaker turns formations into rubble.

name: Behir

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The behir makes one Bite attack and uses Constrict.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 10 ft. Hit: 19 (2d12 + 6) Piercing damage plus 11 (2d10) Lightning damage.

actions.name: Constrict
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 18, one Large or smaller creature the behir can see within 5 feet. Failure: 28 (5d8 + 6) Bludgeoning damage. The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 16), and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.
actions.save_effect: 28 (5d8 + 6) Bludgeoning damage. The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 16), and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.

actions.name: Lightning Breath (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 16, each creature in a 90-foot-long, 5-foot-wide Line. Failure: 66 (12d10) Lightning damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: 66 (12d10) Lightning damage. Success: Half damage.

bonus_actions.name: Swallow
bonus_actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 18, one Large or smaller creature Grappled by the behir (the behir can have only one creature swallowed at a time). Failure: The behir swallows the target, which is no longer Grappled. While swallowed, a creature has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the behir, and takes 21 (6d6) Acid damage at the start of each of the behir's turns. If the behir takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from the swallowed creature, the behir must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate the creature, which falls in a space within 10 feet of the behir and has the Prone condition. If the behir dies, a swallowed creature is no longer Restrained and can escape from the corpse by using 15 feet of movement, exiting Prone.

description:
The serpentine behir crawls along floors and clambers up walls to reach its prey. Its lightning breath can incinerate most creatures, even as more powerful foes are constricted in its coils and eaten alive. A behir's monstrous form resembles a combination of centipede and crocodile. Its scaled hide ranges from ultramarine to deep blue in color, fading to pale blue on its underside.

Cavern Predators.Behirs lair in places inaccessible to other creatures, favoring locations where would-be intruders must make a harrowing climb to reach them. Deep pits, high caves in cliff walls, and caverns reached only by narrow, twisting tunnels are prime sites for a behir ambush. A behir's dozen legs allow it to scramble through its lair site with ease. When not climbing, it moves even faster by folding its legs beside its body and slithering like a snake.
Behirs swallow their prey whole, after which they enter a period of dormancy while they digest. While dormant, a behir chooses a hiding place where intruders in its lair might overlook it.

Foes of the Dragons. In times long forgotten, giants and dragons engaged in seemingly endless war. Storm giants created the first behirs as weapons against the dragons, and behirs retain a natural hatred for dragonkind.
A behir never makes its lair in an area it knows to be inhabited by a dragon. If a dragon attempts to establish a lair within a few dozen miles of a behir's lair, the behir is compelled to kill the dragon or drive it off. Only if the dragon proves too powerful to fight does a behir back down, seeking out a new lair site a great distance away.
combat-strategy: Ambush from a cliff or cave mouth, opening with Lightning Breath down a corridor or ledge where the party is packed — 66 lightning on a failed DC 16 save is the fight opener. Then Constrict the softest target it can reach and immediately Swallow as a bonus action, removing them from healing and support while they take 6d6 acid each round. Do not swallow the party's biggest striker: 30 or more damage from inside forces a DC 14 Constitution save or regurgitation — eat the caster, keep the bruiser grappled outside. Shift the fight up a rock face using its 50-foot climb speed where only it can comfortably fight, and slither into its burrow at half strength.

name: Beholder

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)
traits.description: If the beholder fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The beholder uses Eye Rays three times.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Eye Rays
actions.description:
The beholder randomly shoots one of the following magical rays at a target it can see within 120 feet of itself (roll 1d10; reroll if the beholder has already used that ray during this turn):
Charm Ray. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 16. Failure: 13 (3d8) Psychic damage, and the target has the Charmed condition for 1 hour or until it takes damage. Success: Half damage only.
Paralyzing Ray. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 16. Failure: The target has the Paralyzed condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.
Fear Ray. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 16. Failure: 14 (4d6) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.
Slowing Ray. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 16. Failure: 18 (4d8) Necrotic damage. Until the end of the target's next turn, the target's Speed is halved; the target can't take Reactions; and it can take either an action or a Bonus Action on its turn, not both. Success: Half damage only.
Enervation Ray. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 16. Failure: 13 (3d8) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn. While Poisoned, the target can't regain Hit Points. Success: Half damage only.
Telekinetic Ray. Strength Saving Throw: DC 16 (the target succeeds automatically if it is Gargantuan). Failure: The beholder moves the target up to 30 feet in any direction. The target has the Restrained condition until the start of the beholder's next turn or until the beholder has the Incapacitated condition. The beholder can also exert fine control on objects with this ray, such as manipulating a tool or opening a door or container.
Sleep Ray. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 16 (the target succeeds automatically if it is a Construct or an Undead). Failure: The target has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute. The condition ends if the target takes damage or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to wake it.
Petrification Ray. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 16. First Failure: The target has the Restrained condition and repeats the save at the end of its next turn if it is still Restrained, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second Failure: The target has the Petrified condition instead of the Restrained condition.
Disintegration Ray. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 16. Failure: 36 (8d8) Force damage. If the target is a nonmagical object or a creation of magical force, a 10-foot Cube of it disintegrates into dust. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: If the target is a creature and this damage reduces it to 0 Hit Points, it disintegrates into dust.
Death Ray. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 16. Failure: 55 (10d10) Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: The target dies if the ray reduces it to 0 Hit Points.
actions.save_effect: Charm Ray: 13 (3d8) Psychic damage and Charmed condition. Paralyzing Ray: Paralyzed condition, repeats save at end of each turn. Fear Ray: 14 (4d6) Psychic damage and Frightened condition. Slowing Ray: 18 (4d8) Necrotic damage, Speed halved, no Reactions. Enervation Ray: 13 (3d8) Poison damage and Poisoned condition (can't regain HP). Telekinetic Ray: Target moved up to 30 feet, Restrained and Incapacitated. Sleep Ray: Unconscious for 1 minute. Petrification Ray: First failure - Restrained, second failure - Petrified. Disintegration Ray: 36 (8d8) Force damage, disintegrates at 0 HP. Death Ray: 55 (10d10) Necrotic damage, kills at 0 HP. Success on damage rays: Half damage.

rays.name: Charm Ray
rays.duration_note: for 1 hour or until it takes damage — damage-wake is GM-enforced (no charmed-wake consumer).
rays.save_effect: 13 (3d8) Psychic damage, and the target has the Charmed condition for 1 hour or until it takes damage. Success: Half damage only.

rays.name: Paralyzing Ray
rays.duration_note: Paralyzed — repeats the CON save at the end of each of its turns, ending on a success; auto-succeeds after 1 minute (10-round clock).
rays.save_effect: The target has the Paralyzed condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

rays.name: Fear Ray
rays.duration_note: until the end of its next turn (rounds:2 clock).
rays.save_effect: 14 (4d6) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.

rays.name: Slowing Ray
rays.duration_note: Speed halved, no Reactions, and either an Action or a Bonus Action (not both) until the end of its next turn (rounds:2 clock — MA-0087 slowed trio te).
rays.save_effect: 18 (4d8) Necrotic damage. Until the end of the target's next turn, the target's Speed is halved; the target can't take Reactions; and it can take either an Action or a Bonus Action on its turn, not both. Success: Half damage only.

rays.name: Enervation Ray
rays.duration_note: Poisoned until the end of its next turn; while Poisoned it can't regain Hit Points (no_healing te, rounds:2 clock).
rays.save_effect: 13 (3d8) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn. While Poisoned, the target can't regain Hit Points. Success: Half damage only.

rays.name: Telekinetic Ray
rays.duration_note: Restrained until the start of the beholder's next turn (rounds:2 clock); the 30-foot movement placement is GM-enforced (no grid-move consumer).
rays.save_effect: The beholder moves the target up to 30 feet in any direction. The target has the Restrained condition until the start of the beholder's next turn or until the beholder has the Incapacitated condition. Success: none — the ray deals no damage.

rays.name: Sleep Ray
rays.duration_note: Unconscious for 1 minute (rounds:10 clock); waking on damage or a 5-foot wake action is GM-enforced.
rays.save_effect: The target has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute. The condition ends if the target takes damage or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to wake it. Success: none — the ray deals no damage.

rays.name: Petrification Ray
rays.duration_note: First fail: Restrained, repeats the CON save at the end of its next turn; second fail: Petrified (two-stage eye_ray_petrifying ladder).
rays.save_effect: First failure: The target has the Restrained condition and repeats the save at the end of its next turn if it is still Restrained, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second failure: The target has the Petrified condition instead of the Restrained condition.

rays.name: Disintegration Ray
rays.duration_note: If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points it disintegrates into dust — 0-HP kill is GM-enforced (no instakill consumer).
rays.save_effect: 36 (8d8) Force damage. If the target is a nonmagical object or a creation of magical force, a 10-foot Cube of it disintegrates into dust. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: If the target is a creature and this damage reduces it to 0 Hit Points, it disintegrates into dust.

rays.name: Death Ray
rays.duration_note: The target dies if the ray reduces it to 0 Hit Points — 0-HP kill is GM-enforced (no instakill consumer).
rays.save_effect: 55 (10d10) Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: The target dies if the ray reduces it to 0 Hit Points.

bonus_actions.name: Antimagic Cone
bonus_actions.description: The beholder's central eye emits an antimagic wave in a 150-foot Cone. Until the start of the beholder's next turn, that area acts as an Antimagic Field spell, and that area works against the beholder's own Eye Rays.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair)
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, the beholder can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The beholder regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Chomp
legendary_actions.description: The beholder makes two Bite attacks.

legendary_actions.name: Glare
legendary_actions.advisory_message: uses Eye Rays — advisory record: GM picks one eye ray and adjudicates its save/damage (Eye Rays multi-ray d10 block unparseable, MA-0374 pending subsystem; no ray picker consumer). Canonical cost is 1 legendary use — the engine spends 1 per click.
legendary_actions.description: The beholder uses Eye Rays.

lair_actions.name: Slimy Ground
lair_actions.description: A 50-foot square area of ground within 120 feet of the beholder becomes slimy; that area is difficult terrain until initiative count 20 on the next round.

zone.advisory: Canonical shape is a 50-foot square — modeled as a 25-ft radius picker (square→radius approximation; GM positions the area). Difficult terrain (1 ft costs 2 ft) has no movement-cost consumer in this engine — GM-enforced. No saving throw. Lasts until initiative count 20 on the next round — GM-enforced (no initiative-20 lair seam).

lair_actions.name: Grasping Walls
lair_actions.description: Walls within 120 feet of the beholder sprout grasping appendages until initiative count 20 on the round after next. Each creature of the beholder's choice that starts its turn within 10 feet of such a wall must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be grappled. Escaping requires a successful DC 15 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.
lair_actions.save_effect: The target is grappled by the wall. The DC 15 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) escape check and the initiative count 20 round-after-next expiry are GM-enforced (no grapple state-machine or initiative-20 lair seam consumer).

lair_actions.name: Surfaced Eye
lair_actions.advisory_message: opens a surfaced eye and shoots ONE random eye ray — advisory record: GM rolls d10 (rerolling any ray already used this turn), picks the ray, and adjudicates its save/damage (Eye Rays d10 block unparseable, MA-0374 pending subsystem; no ray picker consumer). The surfaced eye then closes and disappears. No saving throw or grapple is enforced by this row.
lair_actions.description: An eye opens on a solid surface within 60 feet of the beholder. One random eye ray of the beholder shoots from that eye at a target of the beholder's choice that it can see. The eye then closes and disappears.

description:
One glance at a beholder is enough to assess its foul and otherworldly nature. Aggressive, hateful, and greedy, these aberrations dismiss all other creatures as lesser beings, toying with them or destroying them as they choose.
A beholder's spheroid body levitates at all times, and its great bulging eye sits above a wide, toothy maw, while the smaller eyestalks that crown its body twist and turn to keep its foes in sight. When a beholder sleeps, it closes its central eye but leaves its smaller eyes open and alert.

Xenophobic Isolationists. Enemies abound, or so every beholder believes. Beholders are convinced that other creatures resent them for their brilliance and magical power, even as they dismiss those lesser creatures as crude and disgusting. Beholders always suspect others of plotting against them, even when no other creatures are around.
The disdain a beholder has for other creatures extends to other beholders. Each beholder believes its form to be an ideal, and that any deviation from that form is a flaw in the racial purity of its kind. Beholders vary greatly in their physical forms, making conflict between them inevitable. Some beholders are protected by overlapping chitinous plates. Some have smooth hides. Some have eyestalks that writhe like tentacles, while others' stalks bear crustacean-like joints. Even slight differences of coloration in hide can turn two beholders into lifelong enemies.

Eye Tyrant. Some beholders manage to channel their xenophobic tendencies into a terrible despotism. Rather than live in isolation, the aptly named eye tyrants enslave those other creatures, founding and controlling vast empires. An eye tyrant sometimes carves out a domain within or under a major city, commanding networks of agents that operate on their master's behalf.

Alien Lairs. Because they refuse to share territory with others, most beholders withdraw to frigid hills, abandoned ruins, and deep caverns to scheme. A beholder's lair is carved out by its disintegration eye ray, emphasizing vertical passages connecting chambers stacked on top of each other. Such an environment allows a beholder to move freely, even as it prevents intruders from easily creeping about. When intruders do break in, the height of its open ceilings allows a beholder to float up and harry foes on the floor.
As alien as their creator, the rooms in a beholder's lair reflect the creature's arrogance. It festoons its chambers with trophies from the battles it has won, including petrified adventurers standing frozen in their horrified final moments, pieces of other beholders, and magic items wrested from powerful foes. A beholder judges its own worth by its acquisitions, and it never willingly parts with its treasures.

effects: Creatures within 1 mile of the beholder's lair some­ times feel as if they're being watched when they aren't.

When the beholder sleeps, minor warps in reality occur within 1 mile of its lair and then vanish 24 hours later. Marks on cave walls might change subtly, an eerie trinket might appear where none existed before, harmless slime might coat a statue, and so on. These effects apply only to natural surfaces and to nonmagical objects that aren't on anyone's person.
regional_effects.summary: A region containing a beholder's lair is warped by the creature's unnatural presence, which creates one or more of the following effects:

combat-strategy: Hover at 120 feet and rain three Eye Rays every turn, dreading the party into spreading out — Disintegration, Petrifying, and Paralyzing rays end fights outright, while Telekinetic Ray relocates whoever clusters. Manage the Antimagic Cone like an artillery grid: pin it on the party's primary caster to kill concentration, buffs, and magic items, but never let your own rays cross it — fire at targets outside the cone or drop the cone the round you need full ray output. In its lair, spend all four legendary uses on Glare to fire extra rays between PC turns and bank the four Legendary Resistances for Banishment and instakills. Bite only fools who fly into reach; use minions and vertical geometry to split the party, and retreat to the deepest lair chambers below half hit points or once its resistances are spent.

name: Beholder Zombie
languages: Understands Deep Speech and Undercommon but can't speak

traits.name: Undead Fortitude
traits.description: If damage reduces the zombie to 0 Hit Points, it makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 5 plus the damage taken) unless the damage is Radiant or from a Critical Hit. On a successful save, the zombie drops to 1 Hit Point instead.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The zombie uses Eye Rays twice.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 16 (4d6 + 2) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Eye Rays
actions.description:
The zombie randomly shoots one of the following magical rays at a target it can see within 120 feet of itself (roll 1d4; reroll if the zombie has already used that ray during this turn):
Paralyzing Ray. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 14. Failure: The target has the Paralyzed condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.
Fear Ray. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 14. Failure: 13 (3d8) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn.
Enervation Ray. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 14. Failure: 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn. While Poisoned, the target can't regain Hit Points. Success: Half damage only.
Disintegration Ray. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 14. Failure: 27 (5d10) Force damage. If the target is a nonmagical object or a creation of magical force, a 10-foot Cube of it disintegrates into dust. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: If the target is a creature and this damage reduces it to 0 Hit Points, it disintegrates into dust.
actions.save_effect: Paralyzing Ray: Paralyzed condition, repeats save at end of each turn. Fear Ray: 13 (3d8) Psychic damage and Frightened condition. Enervation Ray: 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage and Poisoned condition (can't regain HP). Disintegration Ray: 27 (5d10) Force damage, disintegrates at 0 HP. Success on damage rays: Half damage.

rays.name: Paralyzing Ray
rays.duration_note: Paralyzed — repeats the CON save at the end of each of its turns, ending on a success; auto-succeeds after 1 minute (10-round clock).
rays.save_effect: The target has the Paralyzed condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

rays.name: Fear Ray
rays.duration_note: until the end of its next turn (rounds:2 clock).
rays.save_effect: 13 (3d8) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.

rays.name: Enervation Ray
rays.duration_note: Poisoned until the end of its next turn; while Poisoned it can't regain Hit Points (no_healing te, rounds:2 clock).
rays.save_effect: 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn. While Poisoned, the target can't regain Hit Points. Success: Half damage only.

rays.name: Disintegration Ray
rays.duration_note: If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points it disintegrates into dust — 0-HP kill is GM-enforced (no instakill consumer).
rays.save_effect: 27 (5d10) Force damage. If the target is a nonmagical object or a creation of magical force, a 10-foot Cube of it disintegrates into dust. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: If the target is a creature and this damage reduces it to 0 Hit Points, it disintegrates into dust.

combat-strategy: Advance relentlessly, 20 feet of hover per turn, firing two random Eye Rays and hoping the 1-in-4 Disintegration Ray catches a low-Dexterity backliner or a magic door it needs. Paralyzing Ray is the set-up: once a target is frozen, drift into Bite range for an automatic critical worth 22+ piercing damage. Corner the party in tunnels where the rays and its body deny dodge and cover, and use it to smash sealed doors and stone barriers that stop the party. It never retreats and Undead Fortitude keeps it rising at 1 hit point — it must be put down with Radiant damage or critical hits, so plan for the extra round.

name: Berserker

traits.name: Bloodied Frenzy
traits.description: While Bloodied, the berserker has Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws.

actions.name: Greataxe
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d12 + 3) Slashing damage.

description: Hailing from uncivilized lands, unpredictable berserkers come together in war parties and seek conflict wherever they can find it
combat-strategy: Open by closing straight on the nearest target and swinging Greataxe every turn; at +5 with 67 HP and 13 AC it wins short, brutal trades, not drawn-out ones. Prioritize isolated or already-wounded foes, since Bloodied Frenzy flips the math in its favor once it has taken damage — a berserker at half HP is more dangerous than a fresh one, so don't let the party assume a hit enemy is finished. It has no ranged options or disengage tools, so pick fights in open ground or ambush from cover; if an enemy kites beyond 30 feet, chase the slowest target rather than the furthest. Retreat is beneath it — Bloodied Frenzy has no off-switch, and it should keep attacking until it drops.

name: Berserker Commander

traits.name: Bloodied Frenzy
traits.description: While Bloodied, the berserker has Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The berserker makes three attacks, using Greataxe or Javelin in any combination.

actions.name: Greataxe
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (1d12 + 4) Slashing damage, plus 10 (3d6) Thunder damage to the target or another creature within 5 feet of the target.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft. Hit: 18 (4d6 + 4) Piercing damage, and the target's Speed decreases by 5 feet until the start of the berserker's next turn.

bonus_actions.name: Frenzied Rush
bonus_actions.description: Each ally within 30 feet of the berserker can take a Reaction to move up to half the ally's Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. The berserker can also move up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

combat-strategy: Open at range with Javelin volleys (30/120 ft.) to soften and slow key targets by 5 feet each hit, then use Frenzied Rush as a bonus action to launch itself and every ally within 30 feet forward without provoking Opportunity Attacks — that charge-and-swing round is its signature opening. In melee, Multiattack with Greataxes, dumping the bonus Thunder damage onto a clustered enemy or spilling it onto an adjacent second target; Javelin the mobile ones to pin them in place. Its 40-ft. speed and Bloodied Frenzy make it a second-wave crusher: let the rank-and-file berserkers eat the first blows, then surge in advantage-seeking. Fight in narrow terrain where its line of attack can't be flanked, and if its escort is wiped and it faces the full party alone, use Frenzied Rush to withdraw and regroup rather than die in place.

name: Bestial Spirit (Air)

actions.name: Beast's Strike
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d8+2+WIS modifier Piercing damage.

traits.name: Flyby
traits.description: The spirit doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

description: A bestial spirit summoned by Summon Beast or Bestial Spirit. Air variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: Use 60-ft. flight and Flyby to dive in, land a Beast's Strike, and fly straight back out beyond melee reach without provoking Opportunity Attacks — never end its turn adjacent to a martial character. Hover at 10-20 feet altitude where only reach weapons, ranged attacks, or flight can touch it, and single out low-AC or low-HP casters that can't easily reply. As a conjured spirit with a spell-attack-based strike, spend it attacking whoever the summoner points at or harrying concentrating spellcasters to force concentration checks. At 20 HP it's expendable: if cornered by an area effect or a readied attack, keep kiting in a wide circle until it dies flying.

name: Bestial Spirit (Land)

actions.name: Beast's Strike
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d8+2+WIS modifier Bludgeoning/Piercing/Slashing damage.

actions.name: Beast's Strike — Charge
actions.description: The beast charges forward 20 ft. The target must succeed on a DC 20 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.
actions.save_effect: The target is knocked prone.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The spirit has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the spirit's allies is within 5 ft. of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

description: A bestial spirit summoned by Summon Beast or Bestial Spirit. Land variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: Fight in packs and lean on Pack Tactics: position two or more spirits on opposite sides of the same target so every Beast's Strike lands with Advantage. Use Beast's Strike — Charge from at least 20 feet away on a Medium-or-smaller target, since knocking them Prone with a DC 20 Strength save grants Advantage to the whole pack's follow-up attacks on the downed foe. Its 30-ft. climb lets it attack from cliffs, trees, and rooftops, so pick ambush terrain where enemies must climb to reach it. Target whoever is separated from the group; once a target is prone, swarm it and burst it down before it stands. These are disposable spirit-summons — commit fully, and if the pack is breaking, keep attacking the nearest target rather than fleeing.

name: Bestial Spirit (Water)

actions.name: Beast's Strike
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d6+2+WIS modifier Bludgeoning/Piercing damage.

actions.name: Beast's Strike — Grapple
actions.description: The beast lunges to grapple the target. The target must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw or become grappled.
actions.save_effect: The target becomes grappled.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The spirit has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the spirit's allies is within 5 ft. of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The spirit can breathe only underwater.

description: A bestial spirit summoned by Summon Beast or Bestial Spirit. Water variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: Fight underwater where it belongs: Pack Tactics with the pack, and use Beast's Strike — Grapple (DC 20 Wisdom) to seize a swimmer, dragging the grappled target into deeper water, stronger current, or the maw of a bigger aquatic monster while the pack piles on with Advantage. Grappled targets can't dodge away from the second spirit's strikes, so always attack flanking a grapple. Force encounters into lakes, rivers, or flooded ruins where surface dwellers are slowed and have disadvantage on melee without waterborne adaptations. If its grapple victim is breaking free and the party's firepower is turning the tide, release the grip and fade into the murk — darkvision plus water cover is its escape route.

name: Black Bear

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The bear makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Slashing damage.

combat-strategy: Open with the standard two-Rend Multiattack on whatever is closest; at +4 for 5 slashing each it wins against low-AC commoners but struggles against armored adventurers, so avoid fair fights it can't win. Attack from concealment in forest or brush where it can flank with cubs or other animals for numbers, and use its 30-ft. climb to drag the fight onto rocks and trees that armored pursuers can't easily follow. Target the smallest or least-armored party member, and if pack tactics from other bears apply, split the party's attention. A bloodied bear will still swing twice — but at 19 HP it should disengage into thick cover after taking real damage, since it has no ranged fallback once the fight goes badly.

name: Black Dragon Wyrmling

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The dragon can breathe air and water.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dragon makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Slashing damage plus 2 (1d4) Acid damage.

actions.name: Acid Breath (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 11, each creature in a 15-foot-long, 5-foot-wide Line. Failure: 22 (5d8) Acid damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 22 (5d8) Acid damage. Success: Half damage.

combat-strategy: Open with Acid Breath (DC 11 Dexterity, 5x15-ft. line) down a corridor or across a crowded cluster of humanoids — 22 acid damage at CR 2 is burst enough to scatter an unprepared party — then land two Rend attacks on the survivors from the water's edge. Use its amphibious swimming to fight from a swamp pool: wade in where only ranged attackers can reach it, then Rend-and-dive, submerging 30 ft. per turn since most land-bound melee can't follow. Save the breath weapon for recharge rolls; when it's spent, harry from the water's edge. It's vain but not stupid — at around 10 HP or when outmatched, fly or swim to its hoard and call for help or lure pursuers into murky water where its blindsight and stealth (+4) give it the advantage.

name: Black Pudding

traits.name: Amorphous
traits.description: The pudding can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

traits.name: Corrosive Form
traits.description: A creature that hits the pudding with a melee attack roll takes 4 (1d8) Acid damage. Nonmagical ammunition is destroyed immediately after hitting the pudding and dealing any damage. Any nonmagical weapon takes a cumulative −1 penalty to attack rolls immediately after dealing damage to the pudding and coming into contact with it. The weapon is destroyed if the penalty reaches −5. The penalty can be removed by casting the Mending spell on the weapon. In 1 minute, the pudding can eat through 2 feet of nonmagical wood or metal.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The pudding can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

actions.name: Dissolving Pseudopod
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 17 (4d6 + 3) Acid damage. Nonmagical armor worn by the target takes a −1 penalty to the AC it offers. The armor is destroyed if the penalty reduces its AC to 10. The penalty can be removed by casting the Mending spell on the armor.

reactions.name: Split
reactions.description: Trigger: While the pudding is Large or Medium and has 10+ Hit Points, it becomes Bloodied or is subjected to Lightning or Slashing damage. Response: The pudding splits into two new Black Puddings. Each new pudding is one size smaller than the original pudding and acts on its Initiative. The original pudding's Hit Points are divided evenly between the new puddings (round down).

description:
A black pudding resembles a heaving mound of sticky black sludge. In dim passageways, the pudding appears to be little more than a blot of shadow.
Flesh, wood, metal, and bone dissolve when the pudding ebbs over them. Stone remains behind, wiped clean.
combat-strategy: Slide it down a corridor or drop it from a ceiling (spider climb) directly onto the party's formation, since Dissolving Pseudopod's 10-ft. reach and Corrosive Form punish whoever swings back — nonmagical weapons degrade a point per hit and wear down to destruction, dragging the party's damage output down turn by turn. Never let a warrior hit it twice with a mundane blade if you can avoid being nearby; instead let ranged spellcasters waste slots, since it has no ranged options and 20-ft. speed means kiting is its only real threat. Deliberately eat slashing and lightning damage while at 10+ HP to Split into two smaller puddings — it doesn't split into nothing when reduced below 10, so splitting is free extra bodies and momentum, and corner it in a hallway so both halves get free attacks. Amorphous lets it squeeze through doors, portcullises, and cracks, so dungeon chases should always be loseable; funnel the party onto stone floors and steal dropped armor and packs. If it drops below roughly 15 HP without split value, retreat through the narrowest gap available and dissolve into the plumbing to return later.

name: Blink Dog
languages: Blink Dog; understands Elvish and Sylvan but can't speak them

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Piercing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Teleport (Recharge 4-6)
bonus_actions.description: The dog teleports up to 40 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.

description: A blink dog takes its name from its ability to blink in and out of existence, a talent it uses to aid its attacks and to avoid harm. Blink dogs harbor a long-standing hatred for displacer beasts and attack them on sight.
combat-strategy: Fight alongside allies in a friendly pack — Blink Dogs are guardians, so position it beside the ward or party it protects and bite (+5) whoever threatens them. Open at 40-ft. speed by closing distance fast, then use Teleport (recharge 4-6, 40 ft.) to pop behind an enemy for Advantage with Pack Tactics or to blink away from a closing big hit; treat the recharge as a surprise get-out-of-danger card the players won't see coming. Use Stealth (+5) to vanish between fights and re-engage from an unexpected angle, forcing a surprise round where its bite hits first. Keep it off the front line against heavy hitters: bite, teleport, repeat hit-and-run. If its charges fall and its ward is secure, teleport out and melt into the underbrush — it has no reason to die standing.

name: Blob of Annihilation

traits.name: Astral Implosion
traits.description: If the blob is reduced to 0 Hit Points, it implodes and ejects any creatures and objects engulfed by it into the Astral Sea. The blob itself vanishes, leaving behind a layer of slime on everything that was within 600 feet of it. In 1d20 years, the blob reconstitutes on a random world in the Material Plane.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (4/Day)
traits.description: If the blob fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The blob has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The blob makes two Pseudopod attacks and uses Engulf. It can replace one attack with a use of Restraining Glob.

actions.name: Pseudopod
