actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +15, reach 30 ft. Hit: 24 (3d10 + 8) Force damage.

actions.name: Engulf
actions.description: The blob moves up to its Speed and can move through the spaces of Huge or smaller creatures and objects. Strength Saving Throw: DC 23, each creature or object whose space the blob enters for the first time during this move. Failure: The target is engulfed. While engulfed, a target has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the blob, and when the blob moves, the engulfed target moves with it. A nonmagical object is destroyed after spending 1 minute engulfed. While engulfed, a creature takes 21 (6d6) Force damage at the start of each of its turns, is suffocating, has the Restrained condition, and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. An engulfed creature that is reduced to 0 Hit Points dissolves into ash, which is ejected into the Astral Sea. Success: The target escapes and enters the nearest unoccupied space.
actions.save_effect: The target is engulfed. While engulfed, a target has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the blob, and when the blob moves, the engulfed target moves with it. A nonmagical object is destroyed after spending 1 minute engulfed. While engulfed, a creature takes 21 (6d6) Force damage at the start of each of its turns, is suffocating, has the Restrained condition, and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. An engulfed creature that is reduced to 0 Hit Points dissolves into ash, which is ejected into the Astral Sea. Success: The target escapes and enters the nearest unoccupied space.

actions.name: Restraining Glob
actions.description: The blob lobs a slimy glob at one Large or smaller creature it can see within 600 feet of itself. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 23, the targeted creature. Failure: 18 (3d6 + 8) Acid damage. The glob rolls the target 60 feet straight toward the blob, and the target has the Restrained condition until the end of its next turn, when the glob harmlessly dissolves. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target has the Restrained condition. The target can use its action to make a DC 23 Strength check, ending the effect on itself on a success.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, the blob can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The blob regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Decay
legendary_actions.description: The blob deals 14 (4d6) Necrotic damage to each creature engulfed by it. The blob can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.

legendary_actions.name: Grasping Glob
legendary_actions.description: The blob uses Restraining Glob. The blob can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.

legendary_actions.name: Lashing Goo
legendary_actions.description: The blob makes one Pseudopod attack.

combat-strategy: Open with Restraining Glob (or Grasping Glob legendary action) to reel a straggler in 60 feet and Restrained them, then Engulf on your turn to swallow Huge-or-smaller creatures whole — each DC 23 Strength save failed means a target takes 21 force per turn, suffocates, and has total cover from outside help, so the party must split between saving the swallowed and damaging you. Multiattack with two 30-ft.-reach Pseudopods to hammer the rescuers while the engulfed melt, and spend legendary actions after each PC's turn: Decay to accelerate kills in your gut, Grasping Glob to punish anyone hanging back at 600 feet, Lashing Goo to smack whoever tries to heal or revive. Use Legendary Resistance (4/day) only on fight-ending effects — banishment, power word kill, and the like — because Magic Resistance already covers most saves, and remember killing you astrally implodes everyone inside into the Astral Sea, so keep victims alive as leverage rather than racing to 0 HP. Kite slowly (30 ft. is plenty — you never need to chase) toward walls, pits, and doorways to deny the party flanking and breath weapon angles, and if the fight stalls, simply keep moving toward the nearest settlement: it does not retreat, it endures.

name: Blood Hawk

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The hawk has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the hawk's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Beak
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Piercing damage, or 6 (1d8 + 2) Piercing damage if the target is Bloodied.

description: Taking its name from its crimson feathers and aggressive nature, the blood hawk fearlessly attacks almost any animal, stabbing it with its daggerlike beak. Blood hawks flock together in large numbers, attacking as a pack to take down prey.
combat-strategy: Scout from above (Perception +6, passive 16) and dive on the target; it only makes sense in flocks, so commit it only where at least one other hawk or ally stands within 5 feet of the target to trigger Pack Tactics Advantage. Beak deals double damage dice against Bloodied prey, so don't waste dives on fresh targets — have the flock harry whoever has already been wounded and let hobbled, fleeing, or prone creatures take the 1d8+2 pecks. Use hit-and-run flyby-style attacks: swoop down, bite, and climb back out of reach, since 7 HP evaporates against even one lucky sword swing. As carrion followers, hang at the edges of the fight and finish off anyone who falls Bloodied; if two or three hawks die or the party focuses guns and spells skyward, abandon the kill and soar off — a hawk that dies for 4 damage is a wasted scout.

name: Blue Dragon Wyrmling

traits.name: Multiattack
traits.description: The dragon makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) Lightning damage.

actions.name: Lightning Breath
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature in a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide Line. Failure: 21 (6d6) Lightning damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 21 (6d6) Lightning damage. Success: Half damage.

combat-strategy: Open with Lightning Breath (DC 12, 30-ft. line) down a corridor, across a packed patrol, or along the longest axis of the party's formation — 21 lightning to a cluster is its best first-round value, then follow with Multiattack Rend (+5, slashing + lightning) on whoever is reachable. Use burrow (15 ft.) and flight to appear and disappear: pop from sand or rise above archers, breathe, then disengage 60 ft. per turn out of most melee reach. Its Constitution (15) makes it tough for a wyrmling, but Dexterity is only 10 with a weak Dexterity save, so avoid standing in the open against archers and rogues — attack, then leave. Fight in deserts, ruins, or open ground where its flight and line breath dominate and the party can't flank it behind pillars; if reduced to roughly 20 HP or facing concentrated firepower, burrow or fly to its burrow and break off to harass another day.

name: Blue Slaad

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The slaad has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.description: The slaad regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns if it has at least 1 Hit Point.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The slaad makes three Mutating Claw attacks.

actions.name: Mutating Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) Poison damage. If the target is a Humanoid not cursed by a slaad, it is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 15. Failure: The target is cursed. The cursed target can't regain Hit Points, and its Hit Point maximum decreases by 10 (3d6) after every 24 hours and doesn't return to normal after finishing a Long Rest. If the curse reduces the target's Hit Point maximum to 0, the curse ends, and instead of dying, the target instantly transforms into a Red Slaad or, if it can cast spells of level 3 or higher, a Green Slaad. Only a Wish spell can reverse this transformation.
actions.save_effect: The target is cursed. The cursed target can't regain Hit Points, and its Hit Point maximum decreases by 10 (3d6) after every 24 hours and doesn't return to normal after finishing a Long Rest. If the curse reduces the target's Hit Point maximum to 0, the curse ends, and instead of dying, the target instantly transforms into a Red Slaad or, if it can cast spells of level 3 or higher, a Green Slaad. Only a Wish spell can reverse this transformation.

description: The bone hooks that protrude from the back of a blue slaad's hands inflict a terrible transformative disease on humanoids wounded by them. This infection, called chaos phage, transforms its victim into a fully grown red slaad or green slaad if the host was a spellcaster able to cast 3rd level spells or higher.
combat-strategy: Charge straight in with Multiattack Mutating Claw — three +8, 10-ft.-reach swipes that curse humanoids on hit (DC 15 Con or lose 10 max HP per day toward a slaad transformation that only Wish can undo), so prioritize grabbing the party's squishiest humanoids to turn the fight into a ticking clock they must win fast. Magic Resistance plus Regeneration 10 means attrition fails against it: don't trade spell slots on save-or-suck, and punish the party for focusing damage by staying in melee where healing outpaces their burst. Use 10-ft. reach to stay on the edge of melee, stepping out of opportunistic sword range between claw volleys, and let the cursed wander off or be killed to spawn a Red or Green Slaad for reinforcements. Target spellcasters and healing-capable clerics first — a cursed healer is a demoralized healer. If it drops below ~20 HP with no cursed prey left and the party unloaded everything, run 30 ft. per turn toward the nearest portal; a surviving slaad spreads chaos, a dead one doesn't.

name: Boar

traits.name: Bloodied Fury
traits.description: While Bloodied, the boar has Advantage on attack rolls.

actions.name: Gore
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature and the boar moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 3 (1d6) Piercing damage and has the Prone condition.

combat-strategy: Give it a 20-ft. straight run before contact and it hits for double damage dice plus Prone with Gore — so stage it charging down a hall, trail, or field rather than starting adjacent. Target mounted, unarmored, or distracted prey and knock them Prone, where the extra damage and the fallen target's disadvantage help it win trades it otherwise shouldn't. Bloodied Fury gives Advantage on attacks once wounded, so a half-dead boar is more accurate, not less — let the party underestimate it. At 40 ft. speed it can also disengage and re-set up another charge if the first run misses; if it fails two charges, turn it on the nearest isolated target or flee back to the rutting grounds, since a cornered 13-HP beast isn't worth its life.

name: Bone Devil

traits.name: Diabolical Restoration
traits.description: If the devil dies outside the Nine Hells, its body disappears in sulfurous smoke, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Nine Hells.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The devil has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The devil makes two Claw attacks and one Infernal Sting attack.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Infernal Sting
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Piercing damage plus 18 (4d8) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the devil's next turn. While Poisoned, the target can't regain Hit Points.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the devil's next turn. While Poisoned, the target can't regain Hit Points.

flavor_text:
Bone devils are just one of a thousand reasons never to make a deal with a devil, but they're a significant one. Break said deal, and it'll likely be one of these nightmares that drags you down to the Nine Hells.
—Sylvira Savikas, Candlekeep Sage
description:
Driven by hate, lust, and envy, bone devils act as the cruel taskmasters of the Nine Hells. They set weaker devils to work, taking special delight in seeing fiends that defy them demoted. At the same time, they long for promotion and are bitterly envious of their superiors, attempting to curry favor though it irks them to do so.
A bone devil appears as a humanoid husk, with dried skin stretched tight across its skeletal frame. It bears a fearsome skull-like head and the tail of a scorpion, and a foul odor of decay hangs in the air around it. Though they are devastating in combat with their claws, bone devils also wield hooked polearms made of bone, which they use to subdue enemies before striking with their venomous tails.
combat-strategy: Open with Multiattack — two 10-ft.-reach Claw swipes plus Infernal Sting, which deals 33 average combined damage and leaves the target Poisoned and unable to regain Hit Points until your next turn, so focus that sting on whoever the party's healer is trying to top off. Prioritize martial humanoids to harass and heal-block, and use 40-ft. fly to strike from above, landing only in positions where no one can reach it between turns; its Magic Resistance already blunts the party's save-or-suck spells. Fight in corridors and strongholds where the party can't flank, and let the claws' reach control the space — step back 5 feet after every attack so melee must approach into the sting. In the Nine Hells it effectively cannot die permanently, so commit fearlessly there; on the Material Plane, at around 40 HP or when the fight turns against it, fly to altitude and negotiate or withdraw — a live Bone Devil returns, and Diabolical Restoration makes martyrdom pointless.

name: Bone Naga

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The naga makes two Bite attacks. It can replace any attack with a use of Serpentine Gaze.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Serpentine Gaze
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature the naga can see within 60 feet. Failure: 13 (3d6 + 3) Psychic damage, and the target has the Charmed condition until the start of the naga's next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target takes 13 (3d6 + 3) Psychic damage and has the Charmed condition until the start of the naga's next turn.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The naga casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13):
At Will: Mage Hand, Thaumaturgy
1/Day Each: Command, Detect Thoughts, Lightning Bolt

description: In response to the long history of conflict between the yuan-ti and the nagas, yuan-ti created a necromantic ritual that could halt a naga's resurrection by transforming the living naga into a skeletal undead servitor. A bone naga retains only a few of the spells it knew in life.
combat-strategy: Open with Serpentine Gaze (DC 13 Wisdom) on the party's face or strongest melee combatant — Charmed plus 13 psychic damage buys a turn of free positioning — then Multiattack Bite (+5, piercing + necrotic) whoever the charm brought close. Hold spell slots for the tactical moments: Lightning Bolt into a clustered party, Command to drop a target Prone next to its 10-ft.-reach Bite for Advantage, and Detect Thoughts to unmask hidden magic items, ambushers, or deception before they matter. Use 40-ft. speed to coil down corridors and strike from a distance the party must close to reach, keeping its 10-ft. reach between itself and swords. Its 65 HP and undead toughness favor sustained fights, but Con 12 and no Magic Resistance mean focus-fire hurts — at roughly 20 HP, slither into its burrow, use Command or the charm to cover the withdrawal, and vanish.

name: Brass Dragon Wyrmling

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Fire Breath
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 11, each creature in a 20-foot-long, 5-foot-wide Line. Failure: 14 (4d6) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: The target takes 14 (4d6) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.

actions.name: Sleep Breath
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 11, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: The target has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn, at which point it repeats the save. Second Failure: The target has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute. This effect ends for the target if it takes damage or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to wake it.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn, at which point it repeats the save. Second Failure: The target has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute. This effect ends for the target if it takes damage or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to wake it. Success: The target is unaffected.

combat-strategy: A good-aligned wyrmling fights defensively: open with Sleep Breath (DC 11 Con cone) to incapacitate the most dangerous melee fighters — targets that fail twice are Unconscious for a minute, so isolate and disable rather than kill — then Rend (+4) whoever remains standing. Fire Breath (20-ft. line) is the finisher on a clustered group once sleep has spent; hold one breath ready rather than dumping both at once. Use flight (60 ft.) to stay above melee, landing to retrieve allies or objects, then rising back out of reach; burrow 15 ft. lets it escape into soft ground if overwhelmed. At 22 HP it must avoid trades — if more than two foes are adjacent or a spellcaster locks on, fly away and lead pursuers into terrain where it has the advantage, since a live brass wyrmling brings help. It fights to delay and escape, not to win.

name: Brazen Gorgon

traits.name: Flame Aura
traits.description: At the end of each of the gorgon's turns, each creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the gorgon takes 13 (3d8) Fire damage.

traits.name: Illumination
traits.description: The gorgon sheds Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The gorgon makes two Gore attacks.

actions.name: Gore
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) Fire damage.

actions.name: Smelting Charge
actions.description: The gorgon moves up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks and can move through the spaces of Medium or smaller creatures. Each time the gorgon enters a creature's space for the first time during this move, that target is subjected to the following effect. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 16. Failure: 13 (2d8 + 4) Piercing damage plus 13 (3d8) Fire damage, and the target is pulled into the gorgon's space and has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14); if the gorgon already has a creature Grappled, the target has the Prone condition instead. Until the grapple ends, the target has the Restrained condition. When the gorgon moves, the Grappled target moves with it, costing no extra movement.
actions.save_effect: The target is pulled into the gorgon's space and has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14); if the gorgon already has a creature Grappled, the target has the Prone condition instead. Until the grapple ends, the target has the Restrained condition. When the gorgon moves, the Grappled target moves with it, costing no extra movement.

combat-strategy: Open with Smelting Charge straight through the party's front line: no Opportunity Attacks, moving through Medium-or-smaller spaces, DC 16 Dex or 26 piercing-and-fire damage plus being pulled into its space Grappled and Restrained (or Prone if someone is already held) — charge into the densest cluster and carry the pin-cushion target away. Its 5-ft. Flame Aura means it wins adjacency wars: anything that wants to melee it pays 13 fire at the end of every turn, so it should stand in the middle of the party's healers and archers and dare them to approach. Follow the charge with Gore Multiattack (+8, piercing + fire) on whoever is adjacent, dragging the grappled target along with it while Restrained foes can't escape the aura. Its Int 2 means it simply smashes toward the brightest light or nearest noise — use passive Perception 20 to find hidden foes but expect no trickery. There is no retreat: a construct fights until destroyed, so make every round count and let the aura grind them down.

name: Bronze Dragon Wyrmling

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The dragon can breathe air and water.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dragon makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Lightning Breath
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature in a 40-foot-long, 5-foot-wide Line. Failure: 16 (3d10) Lightning damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 16 (3d10) Lightning damage. Success: Half damage.

actions.name: Repulsion Breath
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. Failure: The target is pushed up to 30 feet straight away from the dragon and has the Prone condition.
actions.save_effect: The target is pushed up to 30 feet straight away from the dragon and has the Prone condition.

combat-strategy: Open with Repulsion Breath (DC 12 Str, 30-ft. cone) to hurl the party back and knock them Prone — free Advantage on follow-up attacks for itself and any allies — then Multiattack Rend (+5) on the prone survivors. If the fight is naval or waterside, use amphibious swimming and 60-ft. flight to fight from above and below, diving into the water where most pursuers can't follow. Lightning Breath (40-ft. line, DC 12) is the corridor/column punisher; alternate cones and lines so the party can't predict and dodge either. With 39 HP it can absorb a round of punishment, but Dexterity 10 means ranged focus-fire hurts — after two solid volleys, rise to altitude or submerge and disengage to summon help, since good-aligned wyrmlings fight to delay evil, not to die for it.

name: Brown Bear

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The bear makes one Bite attack and one Claw attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Slashing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

combat-strategy: Charge from cover at 40 ft. and Multiattack Bite + Claw — the Claw knocks Large-or-smaller targets Prone, so attack whoever is standing and pin them, where the downed target's disadvantage keeps the fight favorable. Target the smallest party members, horses, and unarmored porters, and use 30-ft. climb to haul the kill or the fight onto rocks and timber that armored pursuers can't climb. Bears are bullies, not killers with strategy: it fights loudly and head-on, roaring into the open rather than ambushing, so expect it to break off the moment the fight costs it real blood. If it drops below half HP or takes a solid hit from magic, disengage and lumber away — 22 HP goes fast against adventurers, and a live bear will return to its territory and its cubs.

name: Bugbear

actions.name: Morningstar
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d8 + 2) piercing damage.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) piercing damage in melee or 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage at range.

traits.name: Brute
traits.description: A melee weapon deals one extra die of its damage when the bugbear hits with it (included in the attack).

traits.name: Surprise Attack
traits.description: If the bugbear surprises a creature and hits it with an attack during the first round of combat, the target takes an extra 7 (2d6) damage from the attack.

description:
Bugbears are born for battle and mayhem. Surviving by raiding and hunting, they bully the weak and despise being bossed around, but their love of carnage means they will fight for powerful masters if bloodshed and treasure are assured.

Goblinoids. Bugbears are often found in the company of their cousins, hobgoblins and goblins. Bugbears usually enslave goblins they encounter, and they bully hobgoblins into giving them gold and food in return for serving as scouts and shock troops. Even when paid, bugbears are at best unreliable allies, yet goblins and hobgoblins understand that no matter how much bugbears might drain a tribe of resources, these creatures are a potent force.

Followers of Hruggek. Bugbears worship Hruggek, a lesser god who dwells on the plane of Acheron. In the absence of their goblinoid kin, bugbears form loose war bands, each one led by its fiercest member. Bugbears believe that when they die, their spirits have a chance to fight at Hruggek's side. They try to prove themselves worthy by defeating as many foes as possible.

Venal Ambushers. Despite their intimidating builds, bugbears move with surprising stealth. They are fond of setting ambushes and flee when outmatched. They are dependable mercenaries as long as they are supplied food, drink, and treasure, but a bugbear forgets any bond when its life is on the line. A wounded member of a bugbear band might be left behind to help the rest of the band escape. Afterward, that bugbear might help pursuers track down its former companions if doing so saves its life.
combat-strategy: Ambush is the whole plan: hide with Stealth +6 and darkvision, then open the first round with Surprise Attack — a successful surprise hit adds 7 damage, and Brute's extra melee die already makes the morningstar (11 average) hit like a heavier weapon. Let it open with a Javelin volley at range (or the melee Brute version for 9 damage) before closing, so it gets bonus damage on the first hit of combat against every target it can catch flat-footed. Focus isolated stragglers and the squishiest back-line members, using numbers and darkvision to pick the fight on its own terms in dark woods and tunnels. At 27 HP it can't survive open battle — if surprised fails and the fight is fair, disengage back into the dark and harass again at night.

name: Bugbear Chief

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The bugbear makes two melee attacks.

actions.name: Morningstar
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) piercing damage.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage in melee or 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage at range.

traits.name: Brute
traits.description: A melee weapon deals one extra die of its damage when the bugbear hits with it (included in the attack).

traits.name: Heart of Hruggek
traits.description: The bugbear has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, frightened, paralyzed, poisoned, stunned, or put to sleep.

traits.name: Surprise Attack
traits.description: Ifthe bugbear surprises a creature and hits it with an attack during the first round of combat, the target takes an extra 7 (2d6) damage from the attack.

combat-strategy: Lead the ambush from the front: open round one with Multiattack (two morningstar swings, +5, 12 average each with Brute) on whoever is closest to flat-footed, banking Surprise Attack's extra 7 damage on the first hit. Heart of Hruggek gives Advantage against charm, fear, sleep, and paralysis, so it happily walks into the control spells that drop its goblinoid underlings — send it in where the party's Enchanters are working. Throw Javelins to start the fight at range, then close and gang up with its bugbear and goblin warbands, taking the isolated targets while the horde soaks retaliation. Position it to command — within earshot of goblinoid allies whose morale tactics boost it on its turn — and fight to the death only when protecting the warband's prize; otherwise, at around 20 HP, use Stealth +6 to vanish into the dark and return with a bigger raid.

name: Bugbear Stalker

traits.name: Abduct
traits.description: The bugbear needn't spend extra movement to move a creature it is grappling.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The bugbear makes two Javelin or Morningstar attacks.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. or range 30/120 ft. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Morningstar
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5 (with Advantage if the target is Grappled by the bugbear), reach 10 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Piercing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Quick Grapple
bonus_actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, one Medium or smaller creature the bugbear can see within 10 feet. Failure: The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13).
bonus_actions.save_effect: The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13).

combat-strategy: Its whole kit is abduction: use Quick Grapple (bonus action, DC 13 Dex, 10 ft.) to snatch a Small-or-Medium target — ideally a halfling, gnome, or squishy wizard — then Multiattack with Morningstar, which gains Advantage against anything it has grappled. Abduct means carrying the grappled victim costs no extra movement, so grab and run 30 ft. per turn toward a lair, hide, or waiting transport while the party scrambles to chase and the grappled hostage can't fight effectively. Javelin (10-ft. reach, 30/120 ft.) covers the getaway — snipe pursuers at range while dragging the captive away. Fae-cursed and cruel, it prefers ambush at dusk in Feywild-touched wilds; if the grapple breaks and the party closes in, javelin from reach, then melt into the underbrush with Stealth +6 — a stalker without a hostage has nothing to trade with.

name: Bugbear Warrior

traits.name: Abduct
traits.description: The bugbear needn't spend extra movement to move a creature it is grappling.

actions.name: Grab
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 10 ft. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 12).
actions.save_effect: The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 12).

actions.name: Light Hammer
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +4 (with Advantage if the target is Grappled by the bugbear), reach 10 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 9 (3d4 + 2) Bludgeoning damage.

combat-strategy: Open by closing or hurling a Light Hammer (20/60 ft.) and then Grab (+4, 10-ft. reach) on the smallest target it can reach, grappling them at DC 12. Once it holds a grapple, Light Hammer attacks gain Advantage — so grapple first, then beat the pinned victim with hammer swings while its reach keeps the victim's allies from reaching it safely. Abduct means it can carry the grappled captive at full 30-ft. speed, so a successful Grab turns into a chase toward the lair rather than a stand-up fight. Target unarmored or Small humanoids; against armored foes, stay at hammer range and avoid a duel it doesn't win. At low HP with no captive, throw the hammer, Disengage, and run back to the warband.

name: Bulette

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The bulette makes two Bite attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 17 (2d12 + 4) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Deadly Leap
actions.description: The bulette spends 5 feet of movement to jump to a space within 15 feet that contains one or more Large or smaller creatures. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in the bulette's destination space. Failure: 19 (3d12) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Prone condition. Success: Half damage, and the target is pushed 5 feet straight away from the bulette.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target has the Prone condition. Success: Half damage, and the target is pushed 5 feet straight away from the bulette.

bonus_actions.name: Leap
bonus_actions.description: The bulette jumps up to 30 feet by spending 10 feet of movement.

description:
A bulette is a massive predator that terrorizes any lands it inhabits. Also called a "land shark," it lives only to feed. Irascible and rapacious, bulettes fear no other creature, and they attack with no regard for superior numbers or strength.

Underground Hunters. Bulettes use their powerful claws to tunnel through the earth when they hunt. Heedless of obstruction, they uproot trees, cause landslides in loose slopes, and leave sinkholes behind them. When vibrations in the soil and rock alert a bulette to movement, it shoots to the surface, its jaws spread wide as it attacks.

Wandering Monster. A bulette ranges across temperate lands, feeding on any animals and humanoids it comes across. These creatures dislike dwarf and elf flesh, although they often kill them before realizing what they are. A bulette loves halfling meat the most, and it is never happier than when chasing plump halflings across an open field.
A bulette has no lair, but roams a hunting territory up to thirty miles wide. Its sole criterion for territory is availability of food, and when it has eaten everything in an area, a bulette moves on. These creatures often home in on humanoid settlements, terrorizing them until their panicked residents have fled, or until the bulette is slain.
All creatures shun bulettes, which treat anything that moves as food-even other predators and bulettes. Bulettes come together only to mate, resulting in a bloody act of claws and teeth that usually ends with the male's death and consumption.

Arcane Creation. Some sages believe the bulette is the result of a mad wizard's experiments at crossbreeding snapping turtles and armadillos, with infusions of demon ichor. Bulettes have been thought to be extinct at different times, but afteryears without a sighting, the creatures inevitably reappear. Because their young are almost never seen, some sages suspect that bulettes maintain secret nesting grounds from which adults strike out into the world.
combat-strategy: Wait underground (tremorsense 120 ft. detects walking prey) and erupt beneath the party's column, opening with Deadly Leap — land on top of a cluster for DC 15 Dex or 19 bludgeoning and Prone, then Multiattack Bite (+7, 17 average) on the downed and scrambling prey. Its 40-ft. burrow and Leap bonus action (30 ft. jumps) make it a bounding terror: burst from the ground, bite, leap 30 ft. away before the melee can engage, then burrow under and erupt again somewhere else — never let it stand still in sword range for two rounds. Target the squishiest or isolated walkers, knock them Prone, and let allies finish them while the bulette's AC 17 and 94 HP soak everything else. If it drops below half HP or a kill isn't available, plunge back underground and vanish — a bulette that loses a fight simply moves to the next hunting ground.

name: Bulette Pup

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (2d10 + 3) Piercing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Leap
bonus_actions.description: The bulette jumps up to 30 feet by spending 10 feet of movement.

combat-strategy: Open by burrowing and bursting out beneath a straggler, using tremorsense (60 ft.) to pinpoint anyone walking on the ground while staying hidden below. Its only real damage is Bite, so pair it with Leap (bonus action, 30 ft.) to close distance and still bite in the same turn, pouncing on isolated skirmishers or archers rather than armored front-liners. Kite between burrows: bite, burrow away as a reposition, and listen for footsteps to pick the next ambush spot. It's dumb (Int 2) and only AC 16 with 45 hp, so it fights to the death unless it's low and can tunnel out; retreat through soft ground from ranged fire it can't answer.

name: Bullywug

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The bullywug makes two melee attacks: one with its bite and one with its spear.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, or 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage ifused with two hands to make a meele attack.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The bullywug can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Speak with Frogs and Toads
traits.description: The bullywug can communicate simple concepts to frogs and toads when it speaks in Bullywug.

traits.name: Swamp Camouflage
traits.description: The bullywug has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in swampy terrain.

traits.name: Standing Leap
traits.description: The bullywug's long jump is up to 20 feet and its high jump is up to 10 feet, with or without a running start.

description:
Life as a bullywug is nasty, brutish, and wet. These frog­ headed amphibious humanoids must stay constantly moist, dwelling in rainy forests, marshes, and damp caves. Always hungry and thoroughly evil, bullywugs overwhelm opponents with superior numbers when they can, but they flee from serious threats to search for easier prey.
Bullywugs have green, gray, or mottled yellow skin that shifts through shades of gray, green, and brown, allowing them to blend in with their surroundings. They wear crude armor and wield simple weapons, and can deliver a powerful bite to foes that press too close.

Foul Aristocracy. Bullywugs consider themselves the right and proper rulers of the swamps. They follow an etiquette of sorts when dealing with outsiders and each other, subject to the whims and fancies of their leader-a self-styled lord of the muck. Bullywugs introduce themselves with grand-sounding titles, make great shows of bowing and debasing themselves before their superiors, and endlessly vie to win their superiors' favor.
A bullywug has two ways to advance among its kind. It can either murder its rivals, though it must take pains to keep its criminal deeds secret, or it can find a treasure or magic item and present it as tribute or a token of obeisance to its liege. A bullywug that murders its rivals without cunning is likely to be executed, so it's more common for bullywugs to stage raids against caravans and settlements, with the goal of securing precious baubles to impress their lords and win their good graces. Invariably, such fine goods are reduced to filthy tatters through abuse and neglect. Once a gift loses its sheen, a bullywug lord invariably demands that its subjects bring it more treasure as tribute.

Unruly Diplomacy. Bullywugs love nothing more than lording over those who trespass on their territories. Their warriors attempt to capture intruders rather than simply slaying them. Captives are dragged before the king or queen-a bullywug of unusually large size-and forced to beg for mercy. Bribes, treasure, and flattery can trick the bullywug ruler into letting its captives go, but not before it tries to impress its "guests" with the majesty of its treasure and its realm. Struck with a deep inferiority complex, bullywug lords fancy themselves as kings and queens, but desperately crave the fear and respect of outsiders.

Amphibian Allies. Bullywugs speak a language that allows them to communicate over large areas by croaking like frogs. News of intruders or other events in the swamp spread within minutes across this crude communication system.
Simple concepts in the language are understandable to frogs and toads. Bullywugs use this capability to form strong bonds with giant frogs, which they train as guardians and hunters. Larger specimens are sometimes used as mounts as well. The frogs' ability to swallow creatures whole provides a bullywug hunting band an easy means of carrying prey back to their villages.
combat-strategy: Fight in packs from the water: bullywugs are fragile (11 hp, AC 15) and should never meet heavy hitters head-on. Open from concealment using Swamp Camouflage, then wade or swim into the marsh where their 40-ft. swim speed lets them hit-and-run against land-bound pursuers. Use Multiattack (bite + spear) against the nearest enemy, but spear-and-run at 20/60 ft. against dangerous melee types, throwing before closing to reposition. Standing Leap (20 ft.) lets them hop across reeds and logs to escape or flank. Break morale and flee into the deep swamp when half the pack falls or when a spellcaster starts clearing the water's edge.

name: Bullywug Bog Sage

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The bullywug can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Speak with Frogs and Toads
traits.description: The bullywug can communicate simple concepts to frogs and toads when it speaks in Bullywug.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The bullywug makes two Bog Staff attacks. It can replace any attack with a use of Spellcasting to cast Ray of Sickness.

actions.name: Bog Staff
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The bullywug casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks): At Will: Dancing Lights, Druidcraft, Ray of Sickness 1/Day Each: Speak with Plants, Vitriolic Sphere

bonus_actions.name: Leap
bonus_actions.description: The bullywug jumps up to 30 feet by spending 10 feet of movement.

combat-strategy: This bog witch is the pack's artillery and support: open by casting Vitriolic Sphere (1/day) into the tightest cluster of foes on round 1, forcing repeated Dex saves inside the 20-ft. poison pool while bullywugs kite. In melee-range fights, use Multiattack mixing Ray of Sickness with Bog Staff — the staff's free 3d6 poison makes it the better hit, while Ray of Sickness is save-negates-half and can poison the target. Stay in water or behind terrain with its 30-ft. swim and 30-ft. Leap, kiting at range and letting Speak with Plants rally the bog itself against pursuers. Flee into the deepest water or summon frog/toad swarms as cover when it drops below half hp, since 52 hp won't survive a focused alpha strike.

name: Bullywug Warrior

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The bullywug can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Speak with Frogs and Toads
traits.description: The bullywug can communicate simple concepts to frogs and toads when it speaks in Bullywug.

actions.name: Insectile Rapier
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) Poison damage.

bonus_actions.name: Leap
bonus_actions.description: The bullywug jumps up to 30 feet by spending 10 feet of movement.

combat-strategy: A quick, skittish skirmisher: AC 15 with only 11 hp means it must not trade blows with martial types. Open with a Leap (bonus action, costs 10 ft. of movement) out of hiding or across water onto flanking ground, then strike once with Insectile Rapier's poison damage. Use its 30-ft. swim to drag fights into the water where it fights on its terms, hitting and leaping back out of reach each round — never stand still after attacking. Focus lone or distracted enemies at the edges of the pack's territory, and when it takes any meaningful damage, swim away fast and rejoin the group for numbers protection.

name: Cambion

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The cambion makes two attacks, using Claw or Fire Ray in any combination.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Fire damage.

actions.name: Fire Ray
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +7, range 120 ft. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) Fire damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The cambion casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14): 2/Day Each: Alter Self, Command (level 3 version), Detect Magic 1/Day Each: Dominate Person (level 8 version), Plane Shift (self only)

description:
A cambion is the offspring of a fiend (usually a succubus or incubus) and a humanoid (usually a human). Cambions inherit aspects of both parents, but their horns, leathery wings, and sinewy tails are hallmarks of their otherworldly parentage.

Born to Be Bad. Cambions grow into ruthless adults whose wickedness and perversion horrifies even the most devoted mortal parent. Even as a youth, a cambion identifies its rightful place as an overlord of mortals. It might orchestrate uprisings in towns and cities, gathering gangs of humanoids and lesser devils to serve it.

Pawns of the Mighty. A cambion forced to serve its fiendish parent does so out of admiration and dread, but also with the expectation that it will one day rise to a place of prominence. Cambions raised in the Nine Hells serve as soldiers, envoys, and personal attendants to greater devils. In the Abyss, a cambion carries only as much authority as it can muster through sheer strength and force of will.

Spawn of Graz'zt. The demon lord Graz'zt is fond of procreating with humanoids who have made pacts with fiends, and he has sired many cambions who help him sow chaos across the multiverse. These cambions are characterized by charcoal-black skin, cloven hooves, six­ fingered hands, and unearthly beauty.
combat-strategy: A manipulator first, a combatant second: open socially if possible with Alter Self or Command (3rd-level version, bonus-action-worthy word like 'Kneel' or 'Grovel'), and save Dominate Person (8th-level, no concentration listed pressure beyond its own rules) for the party's martial standout mid-fight. In combat it is brutal at any range: Multiattack Fire Rays from 120 ft. using 60-ft. flight and darkvision, hovering above reach fighters, or dive to Claw for 8+7 fire damage against anyone isolated. Use Command to break a weapon hand or freeze a healer, then burst it down. Fire Ray + Claw combos keep ranged and melee enemies equally stressed; disengage upward when bloodied and consider Plane Shift to escape entirely at a quarter of hp or when outnumbered by high-level casters.

name: Camel

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Bludgeoning damage.

combat-strategy: A pack animal that fights only when cornered or abused: with a 50-ft. walk it should be ridden away from danger first and foremost. If forced into combat, its Bite (+4, 1d4+2) is trivial — target the nearest threat, usually the one grabbing the reins or the rider, and use its Large frame and trampling bulk to back away, keeping foes in front of its hooves and mouth. Drive it toward open ground where its speed matters; corners and swarms will kill it in a round or two, so a handler should disengage and run at the first sign of a real fight.

name: Carrion Crawler

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The carrion crawler can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The carrion crawler uses Paralyzing Tentacles and makes one Bite attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Paralyzing Tentacles
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, one creature the carrion crawler can see within 10 feet. Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically. While Poisoned, the target has the Paralyzed condition.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Poisoned condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically. While Poisoned, the target has the Paralyzed condition.

description:
Carrion crawlers scour putrid flesh from carcasses and gobble the slimy bones that remain. They aggressively attack any creature that trespasses on their territory or disturbs their feasting.

Carrion Eaters. A carrion crawler follows the scent of death to its food, but it prefers not to compete with other scavengers. These foul creatures thus hunker down in territories where death is plentiful and other carrion eaters have limited mobility. Caves, sewers, dungeons, and forested marshes are their favored lairs, but carrion crawlers are also drawn to battlefields and cemeteries.
A carrion crawler roams on the hunt, its tentacles probing the air for the scent of blood or decay. In tunnels or ruins, carrion crawlers scurry across the ceiling as they move toward food. In this way, they avoid contact with oozes, otyughs, and other dangerous inhabitants of the darkness, even as they surprise potential meals that don't think to look up.

Patient Predators. Whether in subterranean darkness or while hunting at night, light signals a potential meal. A carrion crawler might follow a light source from a distance for hours, hoping to pick up the scent of blood. Despite their great size, carrion crawlers can also easily set up ambushes by waiting around blind corners for prey to come to them.
When facing potential prey or intruders, a carrion crawler lets its poison do the work. Once a victim goes rigid with paralysis, the carrion crawler wraps it with its tentacles and drags it away to a high ledge or isolated passageway, where it can be killed safely. The monster then resumes patrolling its territory while waiting for its meal to ripen.
combat-strategy: Ambush from above: use Spider Climb to drop from a ceiling onto the rear of the party, since its tremorsense-free but high passive Perception (15) makes it a patient stalker. Open with Multiattack — Paralyzing Tentacles first (10 ft., DC 12 Dex, no attack roll to fail) to paralyze the squishiest visible target, then Bite it freely while it can't act. A paralyzed victim is an automatic melee critical hit for the whole crawler crew, so prioritize isolating and dragging victims toward walls or ceilings it clings to. Repeat the save each round, but keep reapplying on new victims as the party frees each other; focus anyone without poison resistance or saving-throw bonuses. It fights to the death (Int 1), but retreat up a chimney or crack if reduced below about 15 hp and the prey is still fighting back.

name: Cat

traits.name: Jumper
traits.description: The cat's jump distance is determined using its Dexterity rather than its Strength.

actions.name: Scratch
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Slashing damage.

combat-strategy: Not a real threat — it does 1 slashing damage at +4 and dies to a sneeze. In combat it does what cats do: scramble up the nearest curtain, shelf, or tree with its 40-ft. climb, scratch once if cornered, and bolt. Its only tactical value to the GM is as a distraction, an alarm, or a stealthy spy (Stealth +4, darkvision 60) belonging to someone else; the moment real violence starts, it flees the scene entirely.

name: Celestial Spirit (Avenger)

actions.name: Radiant Bow
actions.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, range 600 ft. Hit: 2d6+2+spell level Radiant damage.

description: A celestial spirit summoned by Summon Celestial. Avenger variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: A glass-cannon skirmisher ghost: its Radiant Bow has a 600-ft. range, so open high in the air (40-ft. fly) and snipe the enemy spellcaster or healer from maximum range where nothing can reach it. Damage scales with spell level, so if its summoner can bolster it, favor those shots. With only AC 11 and 40 hp, stay above melee reach and circle-strafe using flight, spending its turn repositioning between shots rather than closing. If enemies gain flight or dispel pressure, it should melt away — spirits retreat when their summoning purpose fails or their caster falls.

name: Celestial Spirit (Defender)

actions.name: Radiant Mace
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d10+3+spell level Radiant damage, and the spirit can choose itself or another creature it can see within 10 ft. of the target. The chosen creature gains 1d10 Temporary Hit Points.

reactions.name: Healing Touch
reactions.description: The spirit touches another creature. The target regains Hit Points equal to 2d8+spell level.

description: A celestial spirit summoned by Summon Celestial. Defender variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: A mobile battlefield medic: stay within 10 feet of whoever it's sworn to guard, attacking with Radiant Mace and funneling the 1d10 temp HP it grants to itself or the protected ally as needed. Its Healing Touch reaction (2d8 + spell level, no spent resource beyond the trigger) means enemies punish nobody in melee near it — park it beside the front-line fighter taking hits, and it effectively heals once per round on the enemy's own turn. AC 13 and 40 hp mean it shouldn't be the one absorbing damage; use flight to hop between wounded allies, positioning just out of reach when enemies advance. It retreats only when its charge is dead or unreachable.

name: Centaur

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The centaur makes two attacks: one with its pike and one with its hooves or two with its longbow.

actions.name: Pike
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) piercing damage.

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

traits.name: Charge
traits.description: If the centaur moves at least 30 ft. straight toward a target and then hits it with a pike attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 10 (3d6) piercing damage.

description:
Reclusive wanderers and omen-readers of the wild, centaurs avoid conflict but fight fiercely when pressed. They roam the vast wilderness, keeping far from borders, laws, and the company of other creatures.

Wilderness Nomads. Centaur tribes range across lands with mild to hot climates, where a centaur requires only light furs or oiled skins to deal with inclement weather. They are hunter-gatherers and rarely build shelters or even use tents.
Centaur migrations span continents and take decades to repeat, so that a centaur tribe might not retread the same path for generations. These long-ranging patterns can lead to conflict when centaurs encounter settlements of other creatures built along their traditional routes.

Reluctant Settlers. A centaur that can't keep pace with the rest of its tribe is left behind. Some such centaurs vanish into the wilderness and are never seen again. Those that can bear the loss of their tribe might take up residence among other races. Frontier settlements value the nature knowledge of their centaur residents. Many such communities owe their survival to the insight and acumen of a centaur.
Despite their reclusive nature, centaurs trade with elves and with the caravans of other benevolent humanoids they meet during their wanderings. A trader might save the life ofa wounded or an elderly centaur unfit for long travel, escorting it to a settlement where it can peacefully live out the rest of its days.
combat-strategy: A hit-and-run cavalryman: open at range with the longbow pair from Multiattack, then use the 50-ft. walk to bow-snipe-and-cycle, never letting slower melee troops pin it. When an enemy closes, switch to pike (10-ft. reach) and step back a full 10 ft. each round, or set up a Charge — gallop 30+ ft. straight in for the +10 piercing bonus on the pike, ideally against a prone or isolated target, then hooves-beat-and-retreat. Avoid chokepoints and dense forests where its mount loses its speed advantage; open ground and rolling hills are its element. Withdraw to friendly lines when roughly half its hp is gone, as it has no self-heal.

name: Centaur Trooper

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The centaur makes two attacks, using Pike or Longbow in any combination.

actions.name: Pike
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 150/600 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Piercing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Trampling Charge
bonus_actions.description: The centaur moves up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks and can move through the spaces of Medium or smaller creatures. Each creature whose space the centaur enters is targeted once by the following effect. Strength Saving Throw: DC 14. Failure: 7 (1d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Prone condition.
bonus_actions.save_effect: The target has the Prone condition.

combat-strategy: Lead the charge: open combat with Trampling Charge (bonus action), thundering through the front rank at full 50-ft. speed — it doesn't provoke opportunity attacks, and every Medium-or-smaller body it crosses takes damage and falls Prone on a failed DC 14 Str save. Follow immediately with Multiattack: pike prone victims (melee against prone is automatic advantage-free but the prone foe still rises costing half movement), or wheel past and switch to longbow shots on the reeled-over archers. This is round-1 shock: trample, shoot, wheel away, repeat the loop, exploiting its AC 16 and 50-ft. stride to fight only on its terms. Fight in open terrain, avoid forests and walls, and disengage toward rally points once its trample has broken the enemy line or half its hp remain.

name: Centaur Warden

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The centaur makes two attacks, using Forest Staff or Sun Ray in any combination.

actions.name: Forest Staff
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 14 (4d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Sun Ray
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +7, range 90 ft. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) Radiant damage, and the target has the Blinded condition until the start of the centaur's next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Blinded condition until the start of the centaur's next turn.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The centaur casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15): At Will: Druidcraft, Speak with Animals

bonus_actions.name: Entangling Trail
bonus_actions.description: The centaur moves up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Each creature within 5 feet of the centaur as it moves is targeted once by the following effect. Strength Saving Throw: DC 15. Failure: 11 (2d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Restrained condition until the end of its next turn.
bonus_actions.save_effect: The target has the Restrained condition until the end of its next turn.

combat-strategy: A battlefield controller: open with Entangling Trail (bonus action) — charge straight through or alongside the enemy formation at 50 ft. without opportunity attacks, damaging and Restraining (DC 15 Str) everyone within 5 ft. of its path. Then Multiattack: Sun Ray to Blind (no save) a key duelist or archer at up to 90 ft., and Forest Staff (heavy bludgeoning plus 4d6 poison) to finish off Restrained or Blinded victims who can't see or escape. Sequence combo: Entangling Trail to pin, Sun Ray to blind the biggest threat, staff the helplessly trapped. Its 105 hp, AC 16, and +7 Perception make it a durable patrolling anchor: use Speak with Animals and the wild itself for early warning, and withdraw into thick forest where its 50-ft. stride outruns everything once bloodied.

name: Chain Devil

traits.name: Diabolical Restoration
traits.description: If the devil dies outside the Nine Hells, its body disappears in sulfurous smoke, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Nine Hells.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The devil has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The devil makes two Chain attacks and uses Conjure Infernal Chain.

actions.name: Chain
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Slashing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from one of two chains, and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.
actions.save_effect: If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from one of two chains, and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.

actions.name: Conjure Infernal Chain
actions.description: The devil conjures a fiery chain to bind a creature. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 15, one creature the devil can see within 60 feet. Failure: 9 (2d4 + 4) Fire damage, and the target has the Restrained condition until the end of the devil's next turn, at which point the chain disappears. If the target is Large or smaller, the devil moves the target up to 30 feet straight toward itself. Success: The chain disappears.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Restrained condition until the end of the devil's next turn, at which point the chain disappears. If the target is Large or smaller, the devil moves the target up to 30 feet straight toward itself.

reactions.name: Unnerving Gaze
reactions.trigger: A creature the devil can see starts its turn within 30 feet of the devil and can see the devil.
reactions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 15, the triggering creature. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition until the end of its turn. Success: The target is immune to this devil's Unnerving Gaze for 24 hours.
reactions.save_effect: The target has the Frightened condition until the end of its turn. Success: The target is immune to this devil's Unnerving Gaze for 24 hours.

description:
This ominous fiend wears chains like a shroud. Driving lesser creatures before it with its fearsome gaze, a chain devil animates the chains that cover its body as well as inanimate chains nearby, which sprout hooks, blades, and spikes to eviscerate enemies.
Chain devils act as sadistic jailers and torturers in the infernal realms, relishing pain and living to inflict it on others. They are called on to torment mortal souls trapped in the Nine Hells, inflicting their sadistic fury on the horrid lemures in which those souls manifest.
combat-strategy: A patient grappler that wants one victim in chains at a time. Open combat with Conjure Infernal Chain (DC 15 Dex) on an isolated enemy beyond melee — on a fail it's Restrained and dragged 30 ft. straight in, right into Multiattack range. Then Multiattack: two Chain attacks (reach 10 ft., grapple + Restrained on Large-or-smaller, DC 14 escape) to pin two additional victims, and it can drag restrained prey around before its own movement each round. Save-or-suck chain: Restrained + the Unnerving Gaze reaction (DC 15 Wis, Frightened for the turn) punishes whoever attacks it or comes near, so bury victims in chains and let fear keep the rest at bay. Magic Resistance (advantage vs. spells) lets it shrug off control; it fights to the last and, outside the Nine Hells, death only sends it home — never let the party think killing it settles the score.

name: Chasme

traits.name: Demonic Restoration
traits.description: If the chasme dies outside the Abyss, its body dissolves into ichor, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Abyss.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The chasme has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The chasme can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

actions.name: Proboscis
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 16 (4d6 + 2) Piercing damage plus 21 (6d6) Necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, its Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken.

bonus_actions.name: Drone
bonus_actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the chasme (demons automatically succeed on this save). Failure: The target has the Unconscious condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. The target succeeds automatically after 10 minutes or if it takes damage or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to empty a flask of Holy Water on it. Success: The target is immune to this chasme's Drone for 24 hours.
bonus_actions.save_effect: The target has the Unconscious condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. The target succeeds automatically after 10 minutes or if it takes damage or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to empty a flask of Holy Water on it. Success: The target is immune to this chasme's Drone for 24 hours.

description:
This loathsome demon resembles an unspeakable crossing of humanoid and fly. A chasme shuffles about on four spindly legs that can find purchase on walls and ceilings. A droning sound precedes the approach of a chasme, inflicting foes with a terrible lethargy that leaves them open to attack.
The lowly chasmes serve more powerful masters as interrogators or taskmasters. A chasme lives to dole out torture as punishment, and has a knack for spotting demons that have deserted their lords. Capturing and returning such traitors allows a chasme to torment the victim without fear of reprisal.
combat-strategy: Aerial terror: open by hovering out of reach (60-ft. fly, weak 20-ft. walk) and using Drone (bonus action, DC 12 Con, 30-ft. emanation) to drop whole groups unconscious — demons are immune, so pair it with demon allies who happily wade through the sleeping field. The moment foes fall unconscious, descend and Proboscis them: 16 piercing + 21 necrotic plus permanent max-HP drain makes one chomp on a helpless victim nearly a kill. Re-position the Drone's 30-ft. bubble each round to chase fleeing survivors, and use Spider Climb to lurk on cave ceilings between passes. Magic Resistance blunts counterspell-y saves; it retreats to the Abyss or upward through a shaft when reduced to around a quarter hp, since Drone still works from safety overhead.

name: Chimera

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The chimera makes one Ram attack, one Bite attack, and one Claw attack. It can replace the Claw attack with a use of Fire Breath if available.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage, or 18 (4d6 + 4) Piercing damage if the chimera had Advantage on the attack roll.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Ram
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (1d12 + 4) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Fire Breath
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: 31 (7d8) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 31 (7d8) Fire damage.. Success: Half damage..

description:
Chimeras were created after mortals summoned Demogorgon to the world. The Prince of Demons, unimpressed with the creatures that surrounded it, transformed them into horrific, multi-headed monstrosities. This act gave rise to the first chimeras.
Gifted with demonic cruelty, a chimera serves as a grim reminder of what happens when demon princes find their way to the Material Plane. A typical specimen has the hindquarters of a large goat, the forequarters of a lion, and the leathery wings of a dragon, along with the heads of all three of those creatures. The monster likes to surprise its victims, swooping down from the sky and engulfing prey with its fiery breath before landing.

Conflicted Creature. A chimera combines the worst aspects of its three parts. Its dragon head drives it to raid, plunder, and accumulate a great hoard. Its leonine nature compels it to hunt and kill powerful creatures that threaten its territory. Its goat head grants it a vicious, stubborn streak that compels it to fight to the death.
These three aspects drive a chimera to stake out a territory that is as large as 10 miles wide. It preys on wild game, viewing more powerful creatures as rivals to be humiliated and defeated. Its greatest rivals are dragons, griffons, manticores, perytons, and wyverns.
When it hunts, the chimera looks for easy ways to amuse itself. It enjoys the fear and suffering of weaker creatures. The monster often toys with its prey, breaking off an attack prematurely and leaving a creature wounded and terrified before returning to finish it off.

Servant of Evil. Though chimeras are far from cunning, their draconic ego makes them susceptible to flattery and gifts. If offered food and treasure, a chimera might spare a traveler. A villain can lure a chimera into service by keeping it well fed and its treasure hoard well stocked.
combat-strategy: Ambush from the sky: fly in (60 ft.) and open with Fire Breath (DC 15 Dex, 15-ft. cone, ~31 damage) on the clustered party, then land and Multiattack Ram + Bite + Claw in the same turn. Ram (target Prone on hit) sets up the Bite's doubled damage when it has advantage — flank prone victims with allies, or attack rearing foes at range to keep advantage flowing. Sequence: breath the clump, ram the charger, bite it prone, claw it while prone, then take to the air again if ground opposition turns serious. Its flight gives it a vertical get-out; a wounded chimera (under ~30 hp) should break off, gain altitude, and disengage toward its roost.

name: Chuul
languages: Understands Deep Speech but can't speak

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The chuul can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Sense Magic
traits.description: The chuul senses magic within 120 feet of itself. This trait otherwise works like the Detect Magic spell but isn't itself magical.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The chuul makes two Pincer attacks and uses Paralyzing Tentacles.

actions.name: Pincer
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from one of two pincers.
actions.save_effect: If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from one of two pincers.

actions.name: Paralyzing Tentacles
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature Grappled by the chuul. Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically. While Poisoned, the target has the Paralyzed condition.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Poisoned condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically. While Poisoned, the target has the Paralyzed condition.

description:
Survivors of the ancient aboleth empire, chuuls are crustaceans the aboleths modified and endowed with sentience. They follow the ingrained directives of their creators, as they have done since the dawn of time.

Primeval Relics. In the primeval ages, aboleths ruled a vast empire that spanned the oceans of the world. In those days, the aboleths used mighty magic and bent the minds of the nascent creatures of the mortal realm. However, they were bound to the water and could not enforce their will beyond it without servants. Therefore, they created chuuls.
Perfectly obedient, the chuuls collected sentient creatures and magic at the aboleths' command. Chuuls were designed to endure the ages of the world, growing in size and strength as the eons passed. When the aboleths' empire crumbled with the rise of the gods, the chuuls were cast adrift. However, these creatures continue to do what they did for the aboleths, slowly collecting humanoids, gathering treasure, amassing magic, and consolidating power.

Tireless Guardians. Chuul still guard the ruins of the ancient aboleth empire. They linger in silent observance of eons-old commands. Rumors and ancient maps sometimes lure treasure seekers to these ruins, but the reward for their boldness is death.
Whatever riches that the explorers bring with them adds to the hoard guarded by the chuuls. Chuuls can sense magic at a distance. This sense couples with an innate drive that leads them to slay explorers, take their gear, and bury it in secret locales aboleths dictated eons ago.

Waiting Servants. Although the aboleths' ancient empire fell long ago, the psychic bonds between them and their created servants remain intact. Chuuls that come into contact with aboleths immediately assume their old roles. Such chuuls redirect their compulsions to the service of the aboleths' sinister purposes.
combat-strategy: Ambush predator of sewers and swamps: lie submerged (amphibious, 30-ft. swim) until Sense Magic (120 ft.) reveals the spellcaster, then erupt and Multiattack: two Pincer attacks (reach 10 ft., grapple each, DC 14 escape) and immediately Paralyze the grappled victim (DC 13 Con) with Paralyzing Tentacles. The locked combo — pincer one target, then automatically paralyze that same grappled creature — is the kill chain: paralyzed victims take auto-hits and max-tier attacks, so focus one victim to 0 before moving to the next grapnel. Drag paralyzed prey underwater when possible, since many humanoids can't breathe there. In tight corridors its two grapples create a wall no one passes; retreat into deep water with a victim when reduced below ~20 hp.

name: Clay Golem

traits.name: Acid Absorption
traits.description: Whenever the golem is subjected to Acid damage, it takes no damage and instead regains a number of Hit Points equal to the Acid damage dealt.

traits.name: Berserk
traits.description: Whenever the golem starts its turn Bloodied, roll 1d6. On a 6, the golem goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the golem attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the golem attacks an object. Once the golem goes berserk, it continues to be berserk until it is destroyed or it is no longer Bloodied.

traits.name: Immutable Form
traits.description: The golem can't shape-shift.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The golem has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The golem makes two Slam attacks, or it makes three Slam attacks if it used Hasten this turn.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (1d10 + 5) Bludgeoning damage plus 6 (1d12) Acid damage, and the target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Acid damage taken.

bonus_actions.name: Hasten
bonus_actions.description: The golem takes the Dash and Disengage actions.

description:
Sculpted from clay, this bulky golem stands head and shoulders taller than most human-sized creatures. It is human shaped, but its proportions are off.
Clay golems are often divinely endowed with purpose by priests of great faith. However, clay is a weak vessel for life force. If the golem is damaged, the elemental spirit bound into it can break free. Such a golem runs amok, smashing everything around it until it is destroyed or completely repaired.
combat-strategy: An inexorable wall-crusher: walk straight at the nearest enemy every round — it never needs tactics, just multi-Slam (two slams; if Hastened, three slams for the round, with Dash+Disengage as the bonus action making it an uncatchable berserker train). Each Slam (DC-free +9) chip-drops max HP permanently via 1d12 acid, so attrition is the strategy: pile onto the healer or wizard and keep swinging until targets erode to nothing. Warn players that acid heals it and magic is at disadvantage (Magic Resistance); it should be sent through walls using its sheer mass, and once Bloodied, the 1-in-6 Berserk roll can send it rampaging at whoever stands closest — a GM can exploit that chaos by keeping expendable foes or objects near the party. It fights until destroyed; there is no retreat.

name: Cloaker

traits.name: Light Sensitivity
traits.description: While in Bright Light, the cloaker has Disadvantage on attack rolls.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The cloaker makes one Attach attack and two Tail attacks.

actions.name: Attach
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, the cloaker attaches to it. While the cloaker is attached, the target has the Blinded condition, and the cloaker can't make Attach attacks against other targets. In addition, the cloaker halves the damage it takes (round down), and the target takes the same amount of damage. The cloaker can detach itself by spending 5 feet of movement. The target or a creature within 5 feet of it can take an action to try to detach the cloaker, doing so by succeeding on a DC 14 Strength (Athletics) check.
actions.save_effect: If the target is a Large or smaller creature, the cloaker attaches to it. While the cloaker is attached, the target has the Blinded condition, and the cloaker can't make Attach attacks against other targets. In addition, the cloaker halves the damage it takes (round down), and the target takes the same amount of damage. The cloaker can detach itself by spending 5 feet of movement. The target or a creature within 5 feet of it can take an action to try to detach the cloaker, doing so by succeeding on a DC 14 Strength (Athletics) check.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Slashing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Moan
bonus_actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 60-foot Emanation originating from the cloaker. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition until the end of the cloaker's next turn. Success: The target is immune to this cloaker's Moan for the next 24 hours.
bonus_actions.save_effect: The target has the Frightened condition until the end of the cloaker's next turn. Success: The target is immune to this cloaker's Moan for the next 24 hours.

bonus_actions.name: Phantasms
bonus_actions.description: The cloaker casts the Mirror Image spell, requiring no spell components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability. The spell ends early if the cloaker starts or ends its turn in Bright Light.
