bonus_actions.recharge: after a Short or Long Rest

description:
Cloakers earned their names for the resemblance they bear to dark leathery cloaks. Lurking in remote dungeons and caves, these stealthy predators wait to slay lone or injured prey stumbling through the darkness.

Camouflaged Lurkers. Like a stingray, a cloaker's body is composed of cartilage and muscle. With its tail and fins unfurled, it flies through darkness and lurks among the shadows of caverns the same way a stingray glides through water and hides on the ocean floor. Parallel rows of round, black eyespots run along its back like buttons, and the ivory-colored claws on its cowl resemble bone clasps.
When a cloaker unfurls and moves to attack, it reveals its pale underside and makes its true nature evident. Red eyes glow above rows of sharp teeth, and a long pendulous tail whips behind it.

Opportunistic Predators. When hunting, cloakers glide through the shadows at a safe distance behind groups of other creatures traversing the Underdark. They follow parties of humanoids to prey on the wounded after a battle, or pursue herds of Underdark beasts, attacking the sick, the weak, or the straggling.
Cloakers strike quickly and consume their meals as swiftly as possible, enveloping and devouring their victims. While it feeds, a cloaker uses its swift, whiplike tail for defense, although it rarely takes a stand against dangerous foes or groups of creatures. As an added defense, cloakers can create illusory duplicates of themselves.

Haunting Moan. Cloakers' thoughts are alien to other life-forms, and they communicate with one another through subsonic moans inaudible to most creatures. At higher intensities, a cloaker's haunting moan becomes audible, evoking sensations of doom and dread in creatures that hear it.

Cloaker Conclaves. Cloakers prefer isolation, but they sometimes convene with other cloakers for defense or to exchange information about new dangers, suitable hunting grounds, or developments that might affect their habitats. When this convergence is complete, the cloakers separate again.
combat-strategy: The classic dark ambush: hang motionless (Stealth +5, 120-ft. darkvision, looks like old cloth) in unlit passages and let a torch-carrying explorer pass, then drop and Attach (auto-blinds the victim, halves the cloaker's incoming damage by dumping half onto its host — so the party literally cannot burn it down without killing the host). Open with Moan (bonus action, DC 13 Wis, 60-ft. emanation) to Frighten the rescuers before they reach the attached victim, then Multiattack Attach + two 10-ft. Tail attacks on anyone who closes. Keep Phantasms (Mirror Image) up as its opener the moment it's spotted in dim light, and remember Bright Light ends the images and gives disadvantage — it drags victims into darkness, retreats through chimneys to darker warrens when the party brings daylight weapons, and detaches (5 ft. movement) rather than die on a corpse.

name: Cloud Giant

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The giant makes two attacks, using Thunderous Mace or Thundercloud in any combination. It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting to cast Fog Cloud.

actions.name: Thunderous Mace
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +12, reach 10 ft. Hit: 21 (3d8 + 8) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Thunder damage.

actions.name: Thundercloud
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +12, range 240 ft. Hit: 18 (3d6 + 8) Thunder damage, and the target has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The giant casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15): At Will: Detect Magic, Fog Cloud, Light 1/Day Each: Control Weather, Gaseous Form, Telekinesis

bonus_actions.name: Misty Step
bonus_actions.description: The giant casts the Misty Step spell, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

description:
Cloud giants live extravagant lives high above the world, showing little concern for the plights of other races except as amusement. They are muscular with light skin and have hair of silver or blue.

High and Mighty. Cloud giants are spread to the winds, encompassing vast areas of the world. In times of need, scattered cloud giant families band together as a unified clan. However, they can seldom do so quickly.
Attuned to the magic of their airy domains, cloud giants are able to turn into mist and create clouds of billowing fog. They dwell in castles on high mountain peaks, or on the solid clouds that once held their fiefs. Still gracing the skies on occasion, these magic clouds are a lasting remnant of the giants' lost empires.
Better spellcasters than most other giants, some cloud giants can control weather, bring storms, and steer the wind almost as well as their cousins, the storm giants.

Affluent Princes. Although cloud giants are lower in the ordning than storm giants, the reclusive storm giants rarely engage with the rest of giantkind. As a result, many cloud giants see themselves as having the highest status and power among the giant races. They order lesser giants to seek out wealth and art on their behalf, employing fire giants as smiths and crafters, and using frost giants as reavers, raiders, and plunderers. Dimwitted hill giants serve them as brutes and combat fodder-sometimes fighting for the cloud giants' amusement. A cloud giant might order hill or frost giants to steal from nearby humanoid lands, which it considers to be a fair tax for its continued beneficence.
On their mountain summits and solid clouds, cloud giants keep extraordinary gardens. Grapes as big as apples grow there, along with apples the size of pumpkins, and pumpkins the size of wagons. From the errant seeds of these gardens, tales of cottage­ sized produce and magic beans are spread in the mortal realm.
As humanoid nobles keep an aerie for hunting hawks, so do cloud giants keep griffons, perytons, and wyverns as their own flying beasts of prey. Such creatures also patrol the cloud giants' gardens by night, along with trained predators such as owlbears and lions.

Children of the Trickster. The patron god and father of the cloud giants is Memnor the Trickster, the cleverest and slyest of the giant deities. Cloud giants align themselves according to the aspects and exploits of Memnor that they most admire, with evil cloud giants emulating his deceitfulness and self-interest and good cloud giants emulating his intellect and silver­ tongued speech. Family members usually align in the same direction.

Wealth and Power. A cloud giant earns its place in the ordning by the treasure it accumulates, the wealth it wears, and the gifts it bestows on other cloud giants. However, value is only one part of the assessment. The extravagances a cloud giant wears or places about its home must also be beautiful or wondrous. Sacks of gold or gems are worth less to a cloud giant than the jewelry that might be crafted from those materials, creating treasures that bring esteem to a cloud giant's household.
Rather than steal from one another or fight over treasures, cloud giants are inveterate gamblers with a hunger for high risks and high rewards. They frequently bet on the outcome of events nominally outside their control, such as the lives of lesser creatures. Ordning ranks and kings' ransoms can be won and lost in bets over the military triumphs of humanoid nations. Fixing wagers by interfering in the conflict causes the loss of the bet, but such deceit is considered to be cheating only if it is discovered. Otherwise, it is cleverness honoring Memnor.
combat-strategy: A floating skirmisher god: open by rising (hovering flight) out of all reach and hurling Thunderclouds (range 240 ft., and on a hit the target is Incapacitated until the end of its next turn) at the two most dangerous members of the party — that's two free rounds of removal before anyone touches it. Use Fog Cloud (at-will) to screen its approaches and your allies' line of sight, and Misty Step (bonus action) the instant a charger closes, teleporting 30 ft. away while still taking both mace or thundercloud attacks that turn. Thunderous Mace (+12, 28 avg bludgeoning/thunder) is for flyovers over trapped foes; Telekinesis (1/day) grabs a airborne or disarms a champion. Use Control Weather to deepen the cloud layer it lives in. Below a third of its 200 hp it should drift up into the cloud bank and disengage — from there it's untouchable.

name: Cockatrice

actions.name: Petrifying Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) Piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 11. First Failure: The target has the Restrained condition. The target repeats the save at the end of its next turn if it is still Restrained, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second Failure: The target has the Petrified condition, instead of the Restrained condition, for 24 hours.
actions.save_effect: First Failure: The target has the Restrained condition. The target repeats the save at the end of its next turn if it is still Restrained, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second Failure: The target has the Petrified condition, instead of the Restrained condition, for 24 hours.

description: The cockatrice looks like a hideous hybrid of lizard, bird, and bat, and it is infamous for its ability to turn flesh to stone. These omnivores have a diet that consists of berries, nuts, flowers, and small animals such as insects, mice, and frogs-things they can swallow whole. They would be no threat to anything else if not for their fierce and frenzied response to even a hint of danger. A cockatrice flies into the face of any threat, squawking and madly beating its wings as its head darts out to peck. The smallest scratch from a cockatrice's beak can spell doom as its victim slowly turns to stone from the injury.
combat-strategy: A nuisance ambush predator: flit low (40-ft. fly) and target the unarmored or constitution-light members of the party, since Petrifying Bite requires only a melee hit then a DC 11 Con save, with the second failure petrifying for 24 hours. The one-two combo is the whole fight: land, bite once to leave a target Restrained, take wing out of reach, then land next round on that same Restrained foe to finish petrification — with no Multiattack, every dive must carry a bite. Use its 20-ft. walk and short flight to harass in ruins and rock-strewn ground where archers can't lead their shots; if it fails to start a petrification chain within a few rounds, it should flee into a crevice before a spellcaster ends it.

name: Cockatrice Regent

traits.name: Flyby
traits.description: The cockatrice doesn't provoke an Opportunity Attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The cockatrice makes one Petrifying Bite attack and two Talons attacks.

actions.name: Petrifying Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 14. First Failure: The target has the Restrained condition and repeats the save at the end of its next turn if it is still Restrained, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second Failure: The target has the Petrified condition instead of the Restrained condition.
actions.save_effect: First Failure: The target has the Restrained condition and repeats the save at the end of its next turn if it is still Restrained, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second Failure: The target has the Petrified condition instead of the Restrained condition.

actions.name: Talons
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 18 (4d6 + 4) Slashing damage.

reactions.name: Magical Backlash
reactions.trigger: A creature within 120 feet of the cockatrice deals damage to it.
reactions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 14, the triggering creature. Failure: 13 (3d6 + 3) Force damage.

combat-strategy: A flying petrification boss: use Flyby to dive through the party without taking opportunity attacks, opening Multiattack (Petrifying Bite + two 18-damage Talons) on a constitution-weak target — DC 14 Con with the same two-stage bite (Restrained, then Petrified) means focus one victim across consecutive dives to turn them to stone. Magical Backlash (DC 14 Dex, ~13 force) punishes spellcasters who attack it, so bait the wizard into cantrips while you harry the ranged and mobile foes instead. Sequence: dive-bite the healer to Restrained, circle out, next dive finish petrification while the party scrambles; its 60-ft. flight and 136 hp let it control tempo entirely from the air. Retreat into rocky towers or a maze of pillars (bad terrain for aimed shots, great for Flyby cover) below a third of hp, dragging its stone garden's protection around it.

name: Colossus
languages: Understands Celestial and Common but can't speak

traits.name: Immutable Form
traits.description: The colossus can't shape-shift.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the colossus fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead. (4/Day)

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The colossus has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Siege Monster
traits.description: The colossus deals double damage to objects and structures.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The colossus makes three attacks, using Slam or Radiant Ray in any combination.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +18, reach 20 ft. Hit: 32 (4d10 + 10) Bludgeoning damage, and the colossus pushes the target up to 20 feet straight away from itself.
actions.save_effect: The colossus pushes the target up to 20 feet straight away from itself.

actions.name: Radiant Ray
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +18, range 300 ft. Hit: 22 (4d10) Radiant damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.
actions.save_effect: If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Divine Beam
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 26, each creature in a 300-foot-long, 10-foot-wide Line. Failure: 65 (10d12) Radiant damage. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by this beam disintegrates into dust, leaving behind any magic items it was wearing or carrying.
actions.save_effect: Failure or Success: A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by this beam disintegrates into dust, leaving behind any magic items it was wearing or carrying.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 2
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, the colossus can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Smite
legendary_actions.description: The colossus makes one Radiant Ray attack.

legendary_actions.name: Stomp
legendary_actions.description: The colossus moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, and it can make one Slam attack at any point during that move.

combat-strategy: The battlefield itself is its weapon: choose a route straight through the enemy stronghold — Siege Monster doubles all damage to structures, so it wins by collapsing the castle on the party rather than dueling them. In the open, Multiattack: Radiant Ray (range 300 ft., knocks Large-or-smaller Prone) to knock key flyers and casters flat, then Slam (+18, reach 20 ft., 32 damage + 20-ft. push) to crush what it steps to. Save Divine Beam (DC 26 Dex, ~65 radiant, disintegrates anyone it reduces to 0) for the tight 300-ft. corridor when the whole party bunches behind cover or on battlements — firing it through the structure to catch them all is the signature play. Two legendary actions per enemy turn keep it lethal off-turn: Smite a caster mid-spell with Radiant Ray, Stomp (half movement, no opportunity attacks, Slam en route) to chase down anything that flees. With 4 legendary resistances, don't burn your save-or-suck early; make them spend them on the beam setup. It advances relentlessly and never retreats — the only 'retreat' is redirecting toward the biggest structural target.

name: Commoner

actions.name: Club
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 2 (1d4) Bludgeoning damage.

description: Commoners include peasants, serfs, slaves, servants, pilgrims, merchants, artisans, and hermits.
combat-strategy: A terrified civilian, not a combatant: with 4 hp, AC 10, and a club doing 2 damage, commoners should spend every turn Dodging, running, or hiding behind cover, screaming for the guard. If forced to fight — a militia levy or a riot — keep them in a pack of ten or more so sheer numbers create opportunity attacks and flanking, clubbing only isolated, already-wounded stragglers. The moment one drops, the rest break and flee; GMs should mostly use them as hostages, human shields, moral dilemmas, and refugees to protect rather than as attackers.

name: Constrictor Snake

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Constrict
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 12, one Medium or smaller creature the snake can see within 5 feet. Failure: 7 (3d4) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 12).
actions.save_effect: The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 12).

combat-strategy: A hide-and-crush ambush hunter: lie coiled in reeds or rafters (Stealth +4, blindsight 10 ft. so it can strike invisible prey that stumbles within reach) and let the nearest Medium-or-smaller explorer step within 5 ft. Open with Constrict (DC 12 Str): on a fail the victim is Grappled (DC 12 escape) and takes 3d4 damage; then bite the grappled target each round for free close-range hits. Constrict doesn't require it to stay put — a grappled victim can be hauled at half speed — so once a victim is seized, slither away with it toward water or thick cover, prioritizing drowning or isolating the lone straggler. It dies to any serious blade in two hits, so if the grapple fails or the pack turns on it, slither into the water where its swim speed buys escape.

name: Construct Spirit (Clay)

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d8+4+spell level Bludgeoning damage.

reactions.name: Berserk Lashing
reactions.description: Trigger: The spirit takes damage from a creature. Response: The spirit makes a Slam attack against that creature if possible, or the spirit moves up to half its Speed toward that creature without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

description: A construct spirit summoned by Summon Construct. Clay variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: Charge straight at the biggest threat it can reach and Slam it, since Berserk Lashing lets it punish whoever hits it — either with an immediate Slam or a free 15-ft. closing move without provoking opportunity attacks. Position it so enemies who want to melee it can't easily disengage: any damage it takes turns into its next attack. It's AC 13 with only 40 HP, so focus fire on squishies like wizards and clerics rather than trading with a heavily armored fighter. Because attacking it triggers its reaction, clever enemies will open with ranged or area effects; if it's being kited, spend its turns closing distance via Berserk Lashing reactions rather than exposing it to pure ranged attrition.

name: Construct Spirit (Metal)

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d8+4+spell level Bludgeoning damage.

traits.name: Heated Body
traits.description: A creature that hits the spirit with a melee attack or that starts its turn in a grapple with the spirit takes 1d10 Fire damage.

description: A construct spirit summoned by Summon Construct. Metal variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: Fight in a grapple-and-hold brawler style: Slam, stay adjacent, and let Heated Body tax every enemy that swings back (1d10 fire per melee hit) or starts a turn grappled with it. Seek out martial warriors and rogues who must close to melee — they're the ones bleeding fire every round — while avoiding long duels against casters who can attack from range without triggering the trait. Clamp onto a bruiser who grapples it (they take the fire each turn start) and pin them while the fight goes on. With 40 HP and AC 13 it can't win a pure slugfest against concentrated fire, so use its reaction-free punishment aura to control chokepoints and hallways where enemies can't bypass it.

name: Construct Spirit (Stone)

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d8+4+spell level Bludgeoning damage.

traits.name: Stony Lethargy
traits.description: When a creature starts its turn within 10 ft. of the spirit, the spirit can target it with magical energy if the spirit can see it. WIS Saving Throw: DC = your spell save DC. Failure: Until the start of its next turn, the target can't make Opportunity Attacks, and its Speed is halved.

description: A construct spirit summoned by Summon Construct. Stone variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: Open by planting itself next to the party's fastest martial threat and feeding Stony Lethargy to whatever starts its turn within 10 ft. — halved speed and no opportunity attacks turns a rogue or monk into a lumbering target it can Slam freely. Station it in corridors and doorways so enemies must either start their turn in the aura (taking theWis save) or take a long detour. Focus Slams on whoever fails the save, since they can't react or reposition to escape. Kiting works against it (30 ft. speed, AC 13), so its best play is always staying glued to a target; if the party disengages and ignores it, guard objectives or the spellcaster instead of chasing.

name: Copper Dragon Wyrmling

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Acid Breath
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 11, each creature in a 20-foot-long, 5-foot-wide Line. Failure: 18 (4d8) Acid damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 18 (4d8) Acid damage. Success: Half damage.

actions.name: Slowing Breath
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 11, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: The target can't take Reactions; its Speed is halved; and it can take either an action or a Bonus Action on its turn, not both. This effect lasts until the end of its next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target can't take Reactions; its Speed is halved; and it can take either an action or a Bonus Action on its turn, not both. This effect lasts until the end of its next turn.

combat-strategy: Open with Slowing Breath (Con save DC 11 — most PCs fail this) on a clustered group or the most dangerous melee fighter: halved speed, no reactions, and action-or-bonus-action crippled is devastating against Martials. Use its 60-ft. fly and 30-ft. climb to hit from unexpected angles, dropping into a perch Rend attacks are still usable from while staying out of reach. Line up Acid Breath down corridors or across a narrow front where it catches two or three targets. It's only 22 HP, so never let it get surrounded: hit-and-fade using altitude, use its +3 Stealth and good senses to pick the ambush spot, and if reduced to single digits HP or cornered on the ground, flee upward — a clever, good-aligned wyrmling talks, tricks, or retreats rather than dying.

name: Couatl

traits.name: Shielded Mind
traits.description: The couatl's thoughts can't be read by any means, and other creatures can communicate with it telepathically only if it allows them.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (1d12 + 5) Piercing damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the end of the couatl's next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Poisoned condition until the end of the couatl's next turn.

actions.name: Constrict
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 15, one Medium or smaller creature the couatl can see within 5 feet. Failure: 8 (1d6 + 5) Bludgeoning damage. The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13), and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13), and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The couatl casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15): At Will: Detect Evil and Good, Detect Magic, Detect Thoughts, Shapechange (Beast or Humanoid form only, no Temporary Hit Points gained from the spell, and no Concentration or Temporary Hit Points required to maintain the spell) 1/Day Each: Create Food and Water, Dream, Greater Restoration, Scrying, Sleep

bonus_actions.name: Divine Aid
bonus_actions.description: The couatl casts Bless, Lesser Restoration, or Sanctuary, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

description:
Couatls are benevolent serpentine beings of great intellect and insight. Their brilliantly colored wings and gentle manner speak to their celestial origins.

Divine Caretakers. Couatls were created as guardians and caretakers by a benevolent god not worshiped since the dawn of time, and which is forgotten now by all but the couatls themselves. Most of the divine mandates given to these beings are long since fulfilled or failed. However, a number of couatls still watch over ancient power, await fulfillment of prophecy, or safeguard the heirs of creatures they once guided and protected. Regardless of a couatl's task, it prefers to remain hidden, revealing itself only as a last resort.

Truth Tellers. A couatl can't lie, but it can withhold information, answer questions vaguely, or allow others to jump to the wrong conclusions if doing so is necessary to protect something, to keep promises, or to hide the secret of its existence.

Ancient and Few. A couatl can live for ages without sustenance, even surviving without air, but these creatures can die of disease or the passage of time. A couatl can sense its end up to a century beforehand, but it has no insight into the manner of its demise.
If a couatl has already accomplished what it set out to do, it accepts its fate. However, if its imminent death endangers the completion of its goals, it actively seeks out another couatl with which to produce offspring.
The mating ritual of couatls is a beautiful and elaborate dance of magic and light, which results in a gem-like egg from which a new couatl hatches. The parent that sought out the mate raises the newborn couatl and instructs it as to its duties, so that it can complete whatever task the parent leaves unfinished.
combat-strategy: Open combat with a bonus-action Sanctuary on itself or a key ally, or Bless on the party it's defending, then use 90-ft. flight to stay out of melee reach while raining Bite attacks. Its real combo is Constrict (Str save DC 15) on a Medium or smaller target, then flying upward with the grappled, Restrained victim (escape DC 13) — they can't attack effectively and may fall. Use Sleep (one/day) on the toughest warrior or as an opening gambit against a low-HP group, and 1/Day Greater Restoration to shrug off a bad condition on itself or allies. With 120-ft. truesight, illusions, invisibility, and shapechangers can't hide from it; it also can't be mind-read or surprised by psychic tricks. AC 19 and 60 HP are solid but not immortal — disengage and heal via Sanctuary/Lesser Restoration when focused, and if heavily outnumbered it will try to de-escalate or fly away, since it's a lawful good guardian, not a killer.

name: Crab

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The crab can breathe air and water.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Bludgeoning damage.

combat-strategy: A crab is vermin, not a combatant: it pinches with Claw for 1 damage and otherwise scuttles. Run it as an ambush gimmick in swarms — dozens dropping from rocks or surfacing in shallow water to swarm a traveler, using Stealth (+2) and 30-ft. blindsight to close unnoticed before attacking. Target anything edible, shiny, or unattended rather than armored adventurers, and scatter into water or crevices (20-ft. swim, amphibious) when threatened since 3 HP means almost any hit kills it. In an encounter, use numbers: harrass spellcasters'Component-pouches, snatch dropped items, or block a narrow tidal path long enough to matter.

name: Crawling Claw

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 2 Necrotic damage.

flavor_text:
Is it possible for any creature, any living being, to be inherently evil? Such an assertion may itself facilitate the committing of evil acts. By defining a person as evil, we give them free rein to behave as they will, absolving them from the wickedness of their words and the evil of their hands.
—Ansolm Haas, The Isolation of Evil
description:
Crawling claws are the severed hands of murderers animated by dark magic so that they can go on killing. Wizards and warlocks of a dark bent use crawling claws as extra hands in their labors.

Magical Origins. Through dark necromantic rituals, the life force of a murderer is bound to its severed hand, haunting and animating it. If a dead murderer's spirit already manifests as another undead creature, if the murderer is raised from death, or if the spirit has long passed on to another plane, the ritual fails.
The ritual invoked to create a crawling claw works best with a hand recently severed from a murderer. To this end, ritualists and their servants frequent public executions to gain possession of suitable hands, or make bargains with assassins and torturers.

Creator's Control. A crawling claw can't be turned, nor can it be controlled by spells that control undead. These foul monsters are entirely bound to the will of their creator, which can concentrate on a claw in sight to mentally command its every action. If the crawling claw's creator doesn't command it, the claw follows its last command to the best of its ability.
Commands given to a crawling claw must be simple. A claw can't be tasked with finding and killing a particular person, because its limited senses and intelligence prevent it from tracking and picking out specific individuals. However, a command to kill all creatures in a particular locale works. A crawling claw can easily feel out the contours of keys and doorknobs, crawling from room to room on a blind killing spree.

Malign Intelligence. A crawling claw possesses little of the intellect and memories of the individual of which it was once a living part. The hate, jealousy, or greed that drove that person to murder lingers on, however, amplified by the claw's torturous fragmented state. Left to its own devices, a crawling claw imitates and recreates the same murderous acts it committed in life.

Living Claws. If a crawling claw is animated from the severed hand of a still-living murderer, the ritual binds the claw to the murderer's soul. The disembodied hand can then return to its former limb, its undead flesh knitting to the living arm from which it was severed. Made whole again, the murderer acts as though the hand had never been severed and the ritual had never taken place. When the crawling claw separates again, the living body falls into a coma. Destroying the crawling claw while it is away from the body kills the murderer. However, killing the murderer has no effect on the crawling claw.

Undead Nature. A crawling claw doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: A crawling claw is a terror prop, not a threat: use 20-ft. climb speed and blindsight to skitter down from ceilings, doorframes, and tombs unseen, then Slam the least-armored character for 2 necrotic damage before scrambling back out of reach. Ambush from above is its entire game — PCs rarely watch the ceiling, and its Tiny size plus 30-ft. blindsight make it hard to spot in dark ruins. It has 2 HP, so any serious attack ends it; after the first hit, flee into cracks, rubble, or up walls where melee attackers can't follow. Swarm them (dozens at once) if you want real danger, and have them go for torches, spell components, or a sleeping PC's throat for maximum creep factor.

name: Crocodile

traits.name: Hold Breath
traits.description: The crocodile can hold its breath for 1 hour.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 12). While Grappled, the target has the Restrained condition.
actions.save_effect: If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 12). While Grappled, the target has the Restrained condition.

combat-strategy: Ambush from submerged cover: crocodiles have Stealth +2, Hold Breath for an hour, and can float motionless just below the surface of swamp or river terrain. Wait for a target to wade within 5 ft., then Bite (attack +4) — on a hit against Medium or smaller, the victim is Grappled and Restrained (escape DC 12) and the croc drags them into deep water using its 30-ft. swim speed, where allies may need to swim to help. On land it's slow (20 ft.) and clumsy with only 13 HP, so pick fights exclusively at the water's edge; once it has a grappled victim, swim away from the party rather than standing and trading. If the victim escapes the grapple and the crocodile has taken meaningful damage, submerge and vanish — it holds its breath and waits for the next meal to come to it.

name: Cthulhu

traits.name: Insane Geometry
traits.description: The demigod's form defies mortal understanding. Creatures that start their turns within 30 ft. of it must succeed on a DC 24 Wisdom saving throw or take 11 (2d10) Psychic damage and have the Frightened condition until the start of their next turn.

traits.name: Star-Spawn Immortal
traits.description: When reduced to 0 Hit Points, Cthulhu's body dissolves and reforms elsewhere unless the killing blow was dealt by a blessed weapon or Radiant damage. A Disintegrate spell or a wish unmakes it truly.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: Cthulhu can breathe air and water and faces no penalty for fighting submerged.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Cthulhu makes three attacks: two with its claws and one with its tentacles. It can replace one Claw attack with a use of Psychic Shatter.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +18, reach 15 ft. Hit: 32 (4d10 + 10) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Tentacles
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +18, reach 20 ft. Hit: 28 (4d8 + 10) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it must succeed on a DC 26 Strength saving throw or be pulled 20 ft. toward Cthulhu and have the Grappled condition (escape DC 26). While Grappled this way, the target automatically takes 18 (4d8) Bludgeoning damage at the start of its next turn.

actions.name: Psychic Shatter
actions.description: Intelligence Saving Throw: DC 24, each creature within 60 ft. that can see Cthulhu. Failure: 33 (6d10) Psychic damage and the target has the Stunned condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage and no Stun. Cthulhu can't use this action again until its next turn.
actions.save_effect: Failure: Stunned until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage and no Stun.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Claw
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Claw attack.

legendary_actions.name: Tentacles
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Tentacles attack.

legendary_actions.name: Madness Whisper (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Cthulhu projects a maddening whisper at one creature within 120 ft. The target must succeed on a DC 24 Wisdom saving throw or take 14 (4d6) Psychic damage and be unable to take Reactions until the end of its next turn. No damage on a success.

description: The high priest of the Old Ones sleeps and dreams beneath a drowned city, and when the stars align its vast, many-tentacled form rises to warp the minds of civilizations. Its mere geometry hurts to look upon.
combat-strategy: It wades through the front line letting Insane Geometry grind the edges, reeling enemies in with Tentacles to feed, and saving Psychic Shatter for when half the party crowds together in its line of sight.

name: Cult Fanatic

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The fanatic makes two melee attacks.

actions.name: Dagger
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.

traits.name: Dark Devotion
traits.description: The fanatic has advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

traits.name: Spellcasting
traits.description:
The fanatic is a 4th-level spellcaster. Its spell casting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 11, +3 to hit with spell attacks). The fanatic has the following cleric spells prepared:

Cantrips (at will): light, sacred flame, thaumaturgy
1st level (4 slots): command, inflict wounds, shield of faith
2nd level (3 slots): hold person, spiritual weapon

description: Fanatics are often part of a cult's leadership, using their charisma and dogma to influence and prey on those of weak will. Most are interested in personal power above all else.
combat-strategy: Open with Inflict Wounds (spell attack +3) on an isolated squishy — 3d10 necrotic from a position of partial cover — or Command a martial foe to 'Kneel' or 'Grovel' to shut down their turn before they close. Hold Person on the party's frontliner (Wis save DC 11 is very hittable) converts them into an automatic-crit piñata for the fanatic and its cultist minions to stab while paralyzed. Use Shield of Faith on itself or the cult leader, Spiritual Weapon (bonus action) to add 3d8+3 damage without giving up its turn, and Sacred Flame against anyone reluctant to make Dex saves in cover. Stay behind cultist bodies at 20/60-ft. dagger range; Multiattack only when cornered since 4-point daggers are weak. Dark Devotion makes charm and fear useless against it, so don't expect to intimidate or turn it — it fights to the death, which means the smart play is softening the party with save-or-suck before the melee starts.

name: Cultist

actions.name: Ritual Sickle
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) Slashing damage plus 1 Necrotic damage.

description: Cultists swear allegiance to dark powers such as elemental princes, demon lords, or archdevils. Most conceal their loyalties to avoid being ostracized, imprisoned, or executed for their beliefs. Unlike evil acolytes, cultists often show signs of insanity in their beliefs and practices.
combat-strategy: A cultist is a body, not a battle plan: swing the Ritual Sickle (+3, 1d4+1 plus 1 necrotic) at whoever is closest and let numbers do the work. Use them in packs of four or more surrounding a single PC for the action economy, or as wave fodder to blunt the party's big area spells before the real threats arrive. They have 9 HP and AC 12 — expect half of them to drop to the first AoE. Give them simple terrain jobs: man a barricade, guard a door, chant at a ritual altar while the party has to cross the room to stop it, and use their Deception +2 to blend into a crowd until the ambush signal.

name: Cultist Fanatic

actions.name: Pact Blade
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The cultist casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks): At Will: Light, Thaumaturgy 2/Day: Command 1/Day: Hold Person

bonus_actions.name: Spiritual Weapon
bonus_actions.description: The cultist casts the Spiritual Weapon spell, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

combat-strategy: Open with Spiritual Weapon (bonus action) so it deals 3d8+2 force every turn while saving its action, then use Pact Blade (+4, 1d8+2 plus 2d6 necrotic — nearly 10 average damage per swing) on adjacent targets or Command from range. Hold Person (1/day, Wis DC 12) on the biggest martial fighter turns them into an auto-hit target for itself and nearby cultists while they thrash paralyzed. At 44 HP and AC 13 with +4 Dex, it can survive a round or two of focused fire but not a full volley, so stay behind cultists, use cover, and Thaumaturgy for creepy disembodied-voice misdirection before the fight. Command is its emergency button — 'Halt', 'Fall', or 'Grovel' buys a full round against a charging barbarian or rogue. Once out of spells and surrounded, it flees into hidden passages where its cult's traps can cover the retreat.

name: Cultist Hierophant

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The cultist makes three attacks, using Pact Blade or Radiant Ray in any combination.

actions.name: Pact Blade
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Slashing damage plus 18 (4d8) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Radiant Ray
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +9, range 120 ft. Hit: 31 (4d12 + 5) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The cultist casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17): At Will: Mage Armor (included in AC), Thaumaturgy 1/Day Each: Jallarsi's Storm of Radiance (level 7 version), Mass Suggestion

combat-strategy: This is a boss: open with Mass Suggestion (Wis DC 17) on the party — 'drop your weapons and kneel' can end the fight before it starts — or unleash Jallarsi's Storm of Radiance (level 7) on the opening round if the party clusters. In the fight, pick your range: Radiant Ray (+9, 120 ft., 31 avg radiant) lets it snipe squishies from beyond most melee reach, while Pact Blade (+9, 36 avg slashing/radiant with Multiattack x3) punishes anyone who closes. At AC 16 (Mage Armor + 18 Dex), 144 HP, and DC 17 saves, it dictates terms; use Persuasion +9 to demoralize, misdirect, or turn would-be allies mid-confrontation. Position it elevated or behind cultist bodyguards with clear firing lanes, and kite melee bruisers with 30-ft. movement plus Radiant Ray. When reduced below roughly a quarter HP or its cult is routed, it escapes via a hidden ritual chamber or Plane Shift-style fallback it has prepared — its value is as the surviving architect of the cult's next scheme.

name: Cyclops

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The cyclops makes two greatclub attacks.

actions.name: Greatclub
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (3d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Rock
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 28 (4d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

traits.name: PoorDepth Perception
traits.description: The cyclops has disadvantage on any attack roll against a target more than 30 feet away.

description:
Cyclopes are one-eyed giants that eke out a meager existence in wild lands. Isolationists by nature, they avoid contact with other races and try to drive away strangers in their territory.
Nonreligious. Legends claim that the cyclopes are the spawn of one of the gods of the giants, but these creatures pay little heed to any deities. They see little benefit in prayer and dislike ritual, which they perceive as complex and foreign. However, a cyclops that gains direct benefit from some site of divine power, or which is threatened by a supernatural force or creature, will pay homage as long as the benefit or threat remains.

Unsophisticated. Though they are reasonably intelligent, cyclopes live simple, reclusive Jives, keeping herds of animals for food. They prefer to dwell alone or in small family groups, lairing in caves, ruins, or rough structures of dry stone construction they build themselves. A cyclops keeps its herd animals with it at night, sealing the entrance to its home with boulders to let it serve double duty as a barn.
A cyclops lairs within a day's journey of other cyclopes, so that they can meet to trade goods or seek mates. They craft weapons and tools of wood and stone, but will use metal when they can find it. Although cyclopes understand the Giant tongue, they write nothing and speak little, using grunts and gestures for their interactions with each other.
Cyclopes don't use money for trade, but they value gold, shells, and other glittering and colorful objects as jewelry. A cyclops might wear a necklace strung with feathers and silver coins, but also with pewter goblets, cutlery, and other bits of ruined metal.

Unwise. Cyclopes aren't great thinkers or strategists. Slow to learn and bound to their traditional ways, they find innovation difficult. Although they are a terrifying threat in combat due to their size and strength, they can often be tricked by clever foes.
Cyclopes can be cowed and awed by obvious displays of magic. Rustics with little exposure to magic, they can be deceived into mistaking a warlock, cleric, or other caster for a powerful divine figure. However, their sense of pride causes them to react with vengeful, bloodthirsty violence once they learn that the individual they assumed was a "god" is a mere mortal.
combat-strategy: Charge immediately and get within 30 ft. — Poor Depth Perception gives it disadvantage beyond that range, so it must close to fight, and Rock (range 30/120) is only safe to throw inside its reliable 30-ft. band. Multiattack two Greatclubs (19 avg each) on whatever is nearest, preferring to trample clustered enemies since its 10-ft. reach threatens anyone standing in melee. Target spellcasters by rushing past the front line — 22 Str and 138 HP let it ignore spears and go straight for the soft targets. Drive prey into confined terrain like caves, ravines, or the shore where there's nowhere to kite and its reach dominates; in the open, clever parties will strafe at 60+ ft., so have it grab rocks and punish anyone who lingers just past 30 ft. (inside range, no disadvantage). It's dumb (Int 8, Wis 6), so bait it with noise, shiny objects, or a decoy away from the real objective, and it will grudge-fight to the death for honor or appetite.

name: Cyclops Oracle

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The cyclops makes three attacks, using Radiant Strike or Flash of Light in any combination.

actions.name: Radiant Strike
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 10 ft. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Flash of Light
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +10, range 120 ft. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) Radiant damage, and the target has Disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of the cyclops's next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target has Disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of the cyclops's next turn.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The cyclops casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16): 2/Day Each: Arcane Eye, Detect Magic, Locate Object 1/Day: Legend Lore

reactions.name: Portent
reactions.trigger: The cyclops or an ally it can see makes a D20 Test.
reactions.description: The cyclops rolls 1d20 and chooses whether to use that roll in place of the d20 rolled for the D20 Test.

combat-strategy: Fight smarter, not closer: use Flash of Light (+10, 120 ft., disadvantage on the target's attacks) to neutralize the party's heavy hitter from safe range, trading one or two of its three Multiattack slots for ranged blinding pressure while its 30-ft. truesight sees through every illusion and disguise. Radiant Strike (3d10+6 radiant, 10-ft. reach) is its melee finisher — let enemies come to it at chokepoints where the oracle's 207 HP and 40-ft. speed control the room. Save Portent reactions for the pivotal rolls: force a save fail on a key spell, drop the rogue's attack to garbage, or hand an ally a nat-20. Its divinations (Arcane Eye, Locate Object, Legend Lore) are scouting tools — use them to never be ambushed and to know which door the party will come through, then set the fight on its own ground. At 11th-level threat it won't die easily, but if outmatched it retreats into deep tunnels where its 40-ft. speed and knowledge of the terrain let it vanish to deliver its prophecies another day.

name: Cyclops Sentry

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The cyclops makes two attacks, using Stone Club or Rock in any combination.

actions.name: Stone Club
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 10 ft. Hit: 16 (3d6 + 6) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.
actions.save_effect: If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Rock
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +9, range 30/120 ft. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) Bludgeoning damage.

reactions.name: Limited Foresight
reactions.trigger: A creature the cyclops can see makes an attack roll against it.
reactions.description: The cyclops imposes Disadvantage on the roll, and the cyclops gains Advantage on attack rolls against the target until the end of the cyclops's next turn.

combat-strategy: Station it at a gate, bridge, or tunnel mouth where enemies must approach head-on: Multiattack combines Stone Club (knocks Huge-or-smaller foes Prone) and Rock (22 avg bludgeoning) for a mix of melee control and ranged pressure. Knock the frontliner Prone with Stone Club, then pile Rock attacks on the grounded target while they spend their turn standing up. Use Limited Foresight on the sneakiest attacker — disadvantage on their big hit attempt plus advantage on its next swing against them turns the rogue's burst into whiffs and a 19-damage club in return. 40-ft. speed lets it chase down kiting attempts in rough or enclosed terrain; choose lairs without long open sightlines, and if the fight goes badly fall back through the door it was guarding and collapse it behind you.

name: Dao

traits.name: Earth Glide
traits.description: The dao can burrow through nonmagical, unworked earth and stone. While doing so, the dao doesn't disturb the material it moves through.

traits.name: Elemental Restoration
traits.description: If the dao dies outside the Elemental Plane of Earth, its body dissolves into dirt, and it gains a new body in 1d4 days, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere on the Plane of Earth.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The dao has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Wishes
traits.description: The dao has a 30 percent chance of knowing the Wish spell. If the dao knows it, the dao can cast it only on behalf of a non-genie creature who communicates a wish in a way the dao can understand. If the dao casts the spell for the creature, the dao suffers none of the spell's stress. Once the dao has cast it three times, the dao can't do so again for 365 days.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dao makes three Earthen Maul attacks or two Earth Burst attacks.

actions.name: Earthen Maul
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 5 ft. Hit: 20 (4d6 + 6) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.
actions.save_effect: If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Earth Burst
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +10, range 120 ft. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) Bludgeoning damage. Hit or Miss: Earth explodes from the target's space, creating the following effect. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 16, each creature in a 10-foot Emanation originating from and including the target. Failure: 10 (3d6) Thunder damage.
actions.range_save: 10-foot Emanation originating from and including the target
actions.save_effect: Failure: 10 (3d6) Thunder damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The dao casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16): At Will: Detect Evil and Good, Detect Magic, Stone Shape 1/Day Each: Gaseous Form, Invisibility, Move Earth, Passwall, Plane Shift, Tongues, Wall of Stone

description:
Dao are greedy, malicious genies from the Elemental Plane of Earth. They adorn themselves with jewelry crafted from precious gems and rare metals, and when they fly, their lower bodies become columns of swirling sand. A dao isn't happy unless it is the envy of other dao.

All That Glitters. The dao dwell in complexes of twisting tunnels and glittering ore-veined caverns on the Elemental Plane of Earth. These mazeworks are continually expanding as the dao delve into and reshape the rock around them. Dao care nothing for the poverty or misfortune of others. A dao might grind powdered gems and gold dust over its food to heighten the experience of eating, devouring its wealth as mortals consume a precious spice.

Lords of the Earth. A dao never assists a mortal unless the genie has something to gain, preferably treasure. Among the genies, dao are on speaking and trading terms with the efreet, but they have nothing but scorn for djinn and marids. Other races native to the Elemental Plane of Earth avoid the dao, which are always seeking new slaves to mine the mazeworks of their floating earth islands.

Proud Slavers. The dao trade for the finest slaves that money can buy, forcing them to work in dangerous subterranean realms that rumble with earthquakes.
As much as they enjoy enslaving others, the dao hate being enslaved. Powerful wizards have been known to lure dao to the Material Plane and trap them in the confines of magic gemstones or iron flasks. Unfortunately for the dao, their greed makes it relatively easy for mages to cozen them into service.
combat-strategy: Fight on your terms in earth and stone: burrow (Earth Glide leaves no trace) to reposition unseen, erupt beside isolated targets, and knock them Prone with Earthen Maul (auto-prone on Large or smaller, 20 avg damage) while Multiattack finishes them. Earth Burst (120 ft.) is the ranged option — aim it so the 10-ft. thunder burst catches clusters or fails-saved squishies behind cover. Use Wall of Stone to partition the battlefield, splitting casters from the party or sealing tunnels; Passwall and Stone Shape turn its lair into a maze only it can navigate, and Move Earth reshapes the ground under the party mid-fight. Magic Resistance plus 200 HP and AC 18 make it durable, but it's smart (and Neutral): if outmatched, Invisibility then burrow away — or Plane Shift out entirely. Negotiate first: a dao cares about earth, gems, and freedom more than killing, so a deal that protects its treasure beats a fight, and if it dies on another plane it merely reforms on the Elemental Plane of Earth, so never threaten it with mortality — threaten its hoard.

name: Darkmantle

actions.name: Crush
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Bludgeoning damage, and the darkmantle attaches to the target. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature and the darkmantle had Advantage on the attack roll, it covers the target, which has the Blinded condition and is suffocating while the darkmantle is attached in this way. While attached to a target, the darkmantle can attack only the target but has Advantage on its attack rolls. Its Speed becomes 0, it can't benefit from any bonus to its Speed, and it moves with the target. A creature can take an action to try to detach the darkmantle from itself, doing so with a successful DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check. On its turn, the darkmantle can detach itself by using 5 feet of movement.

actions.name: Darkness Aura
actions.description: Magical Darkness fills a 15-foot Emanation originating from the darkmantle. This effect lasts while the darkmantle maintains Concentration on it, up to 10 minutes. Darkvision can't penetrate this area, and no light can illuminate it.

zone.advisory: No illumination model (§70): darkvision suppression and light immunity are not computed in-engine — GM-enforced.

description:
A darkmantle clings to cavern ceilings, remaining perfectly still as it waits for creatures to pass beneath it. From a distance, it can pass itself off as a stalactite or a lump of stone. Then it drops from the ceiling and unfurls, surrounding itself with magical darkness as it engulfs and crushes its prey.
Darkmantles are found throughout the Underdark, but they are equally common on the Shadowfell. Thriving in that dark realm, they fill an ecological niche similar to bats on the Material Plane. Intelligent creatures of the Shadowfell sometimes train darkmantles as guardians or companions.
combat-strategy: Drop from a cave ceiling: with 30-ft. fly, +3 Stealth, and blindsight, a darkmantle waits camouflaged above a tunnel and Crushes the first target that passes underneath. If it has advantage (it does, attacking unseen from above), it covers the target — Blinded and suffocating — then has advantage on every subsequent Crush while the victim's party panics. Maintain Darkness Aura to blind everything without blindsight, making the party's torches and light cantrips useless while the darkmantle sees perfectly, and it becomes immune to the light-based countermeasures that normally stop it. Anchor onto the strongest melee fighter so they can't see or effectively defend, forcing allies to spend actions on DC 13 Athletics detach attempts. It only has 22 HP and AC 11, so it wins ambushes, not fair fights: if the fight goes against it (AoE, bludgeoning from detach attempts), detach with 5 ft. of movement, fly back up, and wait in the dark for the next pass — or suffocate the hostage into submission and bargain.

name: Death Cultist

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The cultist makes three attacks, using Dread Scythe or Deathly Ray in any combination.

actions.name: Dread Scythe
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Slashing damage plus 11 (2d10) Necrotic damage, and the target can't regain Hit Points until the end of its next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target can't regain Hit Points until the end of its next turn.

actions.name: Deathly Ray
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +6, range 120 ft. Hit: 22 (4d10) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The cultist casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14): At Will: Speak with Dead, Thaumaturgy

bonus_actions.name: Spirit Wail
bonus_actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 14, each creature in a 20-foot Emanation originating from the cultist. Failure: 14 (4d6) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.
bonus_actions.save_effect: The target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn.

combat-strategy: Open with Spirit Wail (Wis DC 14, 20-ft. burst, 14 psychic plus Frightened) on the clustered party before anyone closes — frightened PCs fleeing its 10-ft.-reach Dread Scythe is the core image of this fight. Multiattack mixes Deathly Ray (120 ft., 22 necrotic) to snipe healers and spellcasters with Dread Scythe hits that block healing entirely (no HP regain until the end of their next turn), so it never lets the party stabilize the targets it marks. Prioritize whoever just cast a big healing spell — stacking anti-healing scythe hits and necrotic volleys on them grinds the party's resource economy to nothing. At AC 17 and 127 HP it can stand in melee, but use Frightened-induced forced movement and reach-10 ft. advantage to control spacing; Speak with Dead turns fallen PCs or cultists into intelligence. When cornered it fights with apocalyptic zeal — its cult's ritual matters more than its life — but a smart one casts nothing wasted: no slots to hoard means it trades everything for maximum bodies before the end.

name: Death Dog

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The death dog makes two Bite attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12. First Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition. While Poisoned, the target's Hit Point maximum doesn't return to normal when finishing a Long Rest, and it repeats the save every 24 hours that elapse, ending the effect on itself on a success. Subsequent Failures: The Poisoned target's Hit Point maximum decreases by 5 (1d10).
actions.save_effect: First Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition. While Poisoned, the target's Hit Point maximum doesn't return to normal when finishing a Long Rest, and it repeats the save every 24 hours that elapse, ending the effect on itself on a success. Subsequent Failures: The Poisoned target's Hit Point maximum decreases by 5 (1d10).

description: A death dog is an ugly two-headed hound that roams plains, deserts, and the Underdark. Hate burns in a death dog's heart, and a taste for humanoid flesh drives it to attack travelers and explorers. Death dog saliva carries a foul disease that causes a victim's flesh to slowly rot off the bone.
combat-strategy: Hunt in packs of three or more in dark, open terrain: use Stealth +4 and 120-ft. darkvision to close unseen, then Multiattack two Bites (+4) on a straggler to stack the lingering poison — first failed Con DC 12 saves gives Poisoned and locks their max HP from recovering on a Long Rest, and each later failure shaves another 5 (1d10) off permanently. The HP-max drain makes it a campaign-level menace: let one live to bite again, and the party keeps losing hit point capacity between rests unless they get restoration. 40-ft. speed lets it run down mounted couriers and circle around front-line fighters to reach the rear of a traveling party. It won't fight fairly — break off when a member dies and the rest flee into the dark, returning the next night to bite the watchful-but-weakened targets. Use it as a tracker and harasser that drives PCs to exhaustion: they can't rest safely, can't fully heal, and must decide whether to spend precious spell slots hunting a pack of 39-HP dogs through the dark.

name: Death Knight

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the death knight fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead. (3/Day)

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The death knight has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Marshal Undead
traits.description: Undead creatures of the death knight's choice (excluding itself) in a 60-foot Emanation originating from it have Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws. It can't use this trait if it has the Incapacitated condition.

traits.name: Undead Restoration
traits.description: If the death knight is destroyed before it atones for its evil, it gains a new body in 1d10 days, reviving with all its Hit Points. The new body appears in a location significant to the death knight.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The death knight makes three Dread Blade attacks.

actions.name: Dread Blade
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +11, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Slashing damage plus 13 (3d8) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Hellfire Orb
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 18, each creature in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point the death knight can see within 120 feet. Failure: 35 (10d6) Fire damage plus 35 (10d6) Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Half damage

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The death knight casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 18): At Will: Command, Phantom Steed 2/Day Each: Destructive Wave (Necrotic), Dispel Magic

reactions.name: Parry
reactions.trigger: The death knight is hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon.
reactions.description: The death knight adds 6 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 2
legendary_actions.description: The death knight takes 2 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only immediately after another creature's turn. The death knight regains expended legendary uses at the start of its turn.

legendary_actions.name: Dread Authority
legendary_actions.description: The death knight uses Spellcasting to cast Command. The death knight can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.
legendary_actions.advisory_message: uses Spellcasting to cast Command (Charisma save DC 18) at one creature it can see within range — advisory record: GM adjudicates the command word and the target's response (no command-word-to-condition consumer; MA-0058/MA-0270 advisory template). The can't-repeat clause is enforced by the legendary row cooldown latch.

legendary_actions.name: Fell Word
legendary_actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 18, one creature the death knight can see within 120 feet. Failure: 17 (5d6) Necrotic damage, and the target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the damage taken. Failure or Success: The death knight can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.
legendary_actions.save_effect: The target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the damage taken.

legendary_actions.name: Lunge
legendary_actions.description: The death knight moves up to half its Speed (movement advisory — GM moves the token; no movement-distance consumer), and it makes one Dread Blade attack.

description:
When a paladin that falls from grace dies without seeking atonement, dark powers can transform the once-mortal knight into a hateful undead creature. A death knight is a skeletal warrior clad in plate armor. Beneath its helmet, one can see the knight's skull with malevolent pinpoints of light burning in its eye sockets.

Eldritch Power. The death knight retains the ability to cast divine spells, but no death knight can use its magic to heal. It also attracts and commands lesser un­ dead, although death knights that serve powerful fiends might have fiendish followers instead. Death knights of­ ten use warhorse skeletons and nightmares as mounts.

Immortal Until Redeemed. A death knight can arise anew even after it has been destroyed. Only when it atones for a life of wickedness or finds redemption can it finally escape its undead purgatory and truly perish.

Undead Nature. A death knight doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Command the battlefield as an undead general: keep Marshal Undead's 60-ft. aura over your zombie/wight/skeleton minions so every undead ally attacks and saves with advantage, and spread them so the party must break through waves to reach you. Open with Hellfire Orb (DC 18 Dex, 20-ft. radius, 70 avg fire/necrotic) on the heaviest cluster or the concentrated healers, then Multiattack three Dread Blade swings (25 avg each) at whatever survives. Use legendary actions relentlessly: Fell Word (5d6 necrotic plus permanent max-HP reduction) on the healer or tank each round, Command to disrupt a caster mid-spell, and Lunge to close on a fleeing target. Parry (+6 AC) against the rogue's sneak attack or the fighter's big swing, and burn Legendary Resistance only on fight-ending saves — power word kill doesn't work (undead), but holy-flavored effects, banishment, and hold person are real threats worth spending it on. At AC 20, 199 HP, MR, and 3 LR it's engineered to outlast burst damage; if truly overwhelmed it retreats to defile a sanctified site or dives into a tomb — it'll reform in 1d10 days anyway, so its defeats are plot beats, not endings.

name: Death Knight Aspirant

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The aspirant has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Marshal Undead
traits.description: Undead creatures of the aspirant's choice (excluding itself) in a 60-foot Emanation originating from it have Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws. It can't use this trait if it has the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The aspirant makes three Dread Blade attacks.

actions.name: Dread Blade
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Hellfire Orb
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point the aspirant can see within 120 feet of itself. Failure: 21 (6d6) Fire damage plus 21 (6d6) Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Half damage

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The aspirant casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15): At Will: Phantom Steed 1/Day Each: Destructive Wave (Necrotic), Dispel Magic

reactions.name: Parry
reactions.trigger: The aspirant is hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon.
reactions.description: The aspirant adds 4 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

combat-strategy: Fight like a hungry predecessor: Multiattack three Dread Blade swings (24 avg each) at whoever steps into reach, and use Parry (+4 AC) to bait big-hit warriors into whiffing on a 20 AC monster. Save Hellfire Orb (DC 15 Dex, 42 avg fire/necrotic) for the first moment the party clusters — an early sphere on a healing-focused back line can end the fight in one turn. Marshal Undead is your force multiplier: stay within 60 ft. of your undead servants and let them swarm while you hold the middle, because attacking the aspirant through a wall of minions wastes the party's actions and feeds you opportunity attacks. Dispel Magic (1/day) on the party's buffs — heroism, aid, spiritual weapon, freedom of movement — denies them the tools others of its kind fear. Magic Resistance plus AC 20 and 178 HP make it durable, but lacking Legendary Resistance, concentrated damage and banishment can put it down for good, so disengage via minions when below about a third HP and reform the lines — an aspirant has a destiny, and dead champions don't finish the test.

name: Death Slaad

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The slaad has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.description: The slaad regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns if it has at least 1 Hit Point.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The slaad makes two Chaos Blade attacks.

actions.name: Chaos Blade
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 10 ft. Hit: 11 (1d12 + 5) Slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage. Until the start of the slaad's next turn, the target has a condition determined by rolling 1d4: on a 1, Charmed; on a 2, Frightened; on a 3, Poisoned; or on a 4, Incapacitated.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The slaad casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16): At Will: Detect Magic, Detect Thoughts, Invisibility (self only), Mage Hand, Major Image 1/Day Each: Blight (level 8 version), Cloudkill (level 6 version), Fly, Plane Shift, Tongues

bonus_actions.name: Shape-Shift
bonus_actions.description: The slaad shape-shifts into a Small or Medium Humanoid, or it returns to its true form. Other than its size, its game statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

flavor_text:
Fight a slaad and lose, the story's over. Fight a slaad and win, there's a thousand more standing in line just to prove they're tougher.
—Jebeel Sloom, guide to the Plane of Limbo
description: Death slaadi are suffused with energy from the Negative Energy Plane and exemplify evil's corruption of chaos, and they take sadistic pleasure in bringing harm to others. They propagate their race by dragooning mobs of red and blue slaadi and invading other planes. Humanoids who survive the incursion become incubators for new slaadi.
combat-strategy: Infiltrate first: shapeshift (bonus action) into a trusted humanoid and travel with the party or their enemies until the perfect moment, then revert and Multiattack two Chaos Blades (18 avg plus a random Charmed/Frightened/Poisoned/Incapacitated condition on every hit) at the most valuable target. That random condition is the weapon — a Chaos Blade hit on a caster who then rolls Incapacitated means the fight is already decided; reroute hits toward whoever can end it fastest. If discovered openly, Fly plus 40-ft. ground speed and Cloudkill (level 6) let it carpet a corridor in gas and let Regeneration (10 HP/turn) grind out anyone chasing it. Regeneration means ignoring chip damage entirely: never retreat from a war of attrition unless fire or acid specialists are present (its regen isn't specified as stopped here, but assume focused burst is the only real answer). At DC 16 saves with Magic Resistance, save-or-suck rarely lands, so it fights patiently, kills isolated targets, planes-shifts out when the party commits everything, and returns wearing someone else's face.

name: Death Tyrant

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the death tyrant fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead. (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The death tyrant uses Eye Rays three times.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 feet. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Eye Rays
actions.description: The death tyrant randomly shoots one of the following magical rays at a target it can see within 120 feet of itself (roll 1d10; reroll if the death tyrant has already used that ray during this turn): Charm Ray. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 17. Failure: 13 (3d8) Psychic damage, and the target has the Charmed condition for 1 hour or until it takes damage. Success: Half damage only. Paralyzing Ray. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 17. Failure: The target has the Paralyzed condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically. Fear Ray. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 17. Failure: 10 (3d6) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only. Slowing Ray. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 17. Failure: 18 (4d8) Necrotic damage. Until the end of the target's next turn, the target can't take Reactions; its Speed is halved; and it can take either an action or a Bonus Action on its turn, not both. Success: Half damage only. Enervation Ray. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 17. Failure: 16 (3d10) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn. While Poisoned, the target can't regain Hit Points. Success: Half damage only. Telekinetic Ray. Strength Saving Throw: DC 17 (the target succeeds automatically if it is Gargantuan). Failure: The death tyrant moves the target up to 30 feet in any direction. The target has the Restrained condition until the start of the death tyrant's next turn or until the death tyrant has the Incapacitated condition. The death tyrant can also exert fine control on objects with this ray, such as manipulating a tool or opening a door or container. Sleep Ray. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 17 (the target succeeds automatically if it is a Construct or an Undead). Failure: The target has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute. The condition ends if the target takes damage or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to wake it. Petrification Ray. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 17. First Failure: The target has the Restrained condition and repeats the save at the end of its next turn if it is still Restrained, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second Failure: The target has the Petrified condition instead of the Restrained condition. Disintegration Ray. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 17. Failure: 36 (8d8) Force damage. If the target is a nonmagical object or a creation of magical force, a 10-foot Cube of it disintegrates into dust. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: If the target is a creature and this damage reduces it to 0 Hit Points, it disintegrates into dust. Death Ray. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 17. Failure: 55 (10d10) Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: The target dies if the ray reduces it to 0 Hit Points.
actions.save_effect: Charm Ray: 13 (3d8) Psychic damage and Charmed condition for 1 hour. Paralyzing Ray: Paralyzed condition, repeats save at end of each turn. Fear Ray: 10 (3d6) Psychic damage and Frightened condition. Slowing Ray: 18 (4d8) Necrotic damage, Speed halved, no Reactions. Enervation Ray: 16 (3d10) Poison damage and Poisoned condition (can't regain HP). Telekinetic Ray: Target moved up to 30 feet, Restrained. Sleep Ray: Unconscious for 1 minute. Petrification Ray: First failure - Restrained, second failure - Petrified. Disintegration Ray: 36 (8d8) Force damage, disintegrates at 0 HP. Death Ray: 55 (10d10) Necrotic damage, kills at 0 HP. Success on damage rays: Half damage.

rays.name: Charm Ray
rays.duration_note: for 1 hour or until it takes damage — damage-wake is GM-enforced (no charmed-wake consumer).
rays.save_effect: 13 (3d8) Psychic damage, and the target has the Charmed condition for 1 hour or until it takes damage. Success: Half damage only.

rays.name: Paralyzing Ray
rays.duration_note: Paralyzed — repeats the CON save at the end of each of its turns, ending on a success; auto-succeeds after 1 minute (10-round clock).
rays.save_effect: The target has the Paralyzed condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

rays.name: Fear Ray
rays.duration_note: until the end of its next turn (rounds:2 clock).
rays.save_effect: 10 (3d6) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.

rays.name: Slowing Ray
rays.duration_note: Speed halved, no Reactions, and either an Action or a Bonus Action (not both) until the end of its next turn (rounds:2 clock — MA-0087 slowed trio te).
rays.save_effect: 18 (4d8) Necrotic damage. Until the end of the target’s next turn, the target’s Speed is halved; the target can’t take Reactions; and it can take either an action or a Bonus Action on its turn, not both. Success: Half damage only.

rays.name: Enervation Ray
