rays.duration_note: Poisoned until the end of its next turn; while Poisoned it can’t regain Hit Points (no_healing te, rounds:2 clock).
rays.save_effect: 16 (3d10) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn. While Poisoned it can’t regain Hit Points. Success: Half damage only.

rays.name: Telekinetic Ray
rays.duration_note: Restrained until the start of the death tyrant’s next turn (rounds:2 clock); the 30-foot movement placement is GM-enforced (no grid-move consumer).
rays.save_effect: The death tyrant moves the target up to 30 feet in any direction. The target has the Restrained condition until the start of the death tyrant’s next turn or until the death tyrant has the Incapacitated condition. Success: none — the ray deals no damage.

rays.name: Sleep Ray
rays.duration_note: Unconscious for 1 minute (rounds:10 clock); waking on damage or a 5-foot wake action is GM-enforced.
rays.save_effect: The target has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute. The condition ends if the target takes damage or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to wake it. Success: none — the ray deals no damage.

rays.name: Petrification Ray
rays.duration_note: First fail: Restrained, repeats the CON save at the end of its next turn; second fail: Petrified (two-stage eye_ray_petrifying ladder).
rays.save_effect: First failure: The target has the Restrained condition and repeats the save at the end of its next turn if it is still Restrained, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second failure: The target has the Petrified condition instead of the Restrained condition.

rays.name: Disintegration Ray
rays.duration_note: If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points it disintegrates into dust — 0-HP kill is GM-enforced (no instakill consumer).
rays.save_effect: 36 (8d8) Force damage. If the target is a nonmagical object or a creation of magical force, a 10-foot Cube of it disintegrates into dust. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: If the target is a creature and this damage reduces it to 0 Hit Points, it disintegrates into dust.

rays.name: Death Ray
rays.duration_note: The target dies if the ray reduces it to 0 Hit Points — 0-HP kill is GM-enforced (no instakill consumer).
rays.save_effect: 55 (10d10) Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: The target dies if the ray reduces it to 0 Hit Points.

bonus_actions.name: Negative Energy Cone
bonus_actions.description: The death tyrant's central eye emits an imperceptible, magical wave of negative energy in a 150-foot Cone. Creatures in that area can't regain Hit Points until the start of the death tyrant's next turn. An intact Humanoid corpse there instantly rises as a Zombie under the death tyrant's control and takes its turn immediately after the death tyrant on the same initiative count.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 2
legendary_actions.description: The death tyrant takes 2 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only immediately after another creature's turn. The death tyrant regains expended legendary uses at the start of its turn.

legendary_actions.name: Chomp
legendary_actions.description: The death tyrant makes two Bite attacks (the delegate seam resolves one Bite per click — second Bite GM-clicks the chip again; two-Bite count GM-adjudicated, MA-0009 multiattack analogue).

legendary_actions.name: Glare
legendary_actions.description: The death tyrant uses Eye Rays.

lair_actions.name: Spectral Eyes and Tentacles
lair_actions.description: An area that is a 50-foot cube within 120 feet of the tyrant is filled with spectral eyes and tentacles. To creatures other than the death tyrant, that area is lightly obscured and difficult terrain until initiative count 20 on the next round.

zone.advisory: Canonical shape is a 50-foot cube — modeled as a 25-ft radius picker (cube→radius approximation; GM positions the area). Lightly obscured has no light-level consumer in this engine and difficult terrain (1 ft costs 2 ft) has no movement-cost consumer — GM-enforced. No saving throw. Lasts until initiative count 20 on the next round — GM-enforced (no initiative-20 lair seam).

lair_actions.name: Spectral Appendage Walls
lair_actions.description: Walls sprout spectral appendages until initiative count 20 on the round after next. Any creature, including one on the Ethereal Plane, that is hostile to the tyrant and starts its turn within 10 feet of a wall must succeed on a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw or be grappled. Escaping requires a successful DC 17 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.
lair_actions.save_effect: The target is grappled by the wall. The DC 17 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) escape check and the initiative count 20 round-after-next expiry are GM-enforced (no grapple state-machine or initiative-20 lair seam consumer).

description:
On rare occasions, a beholder's sleeping mind drifts to places beyond its normal madness, imagining a reality in which it exists beyond death. When such dreams take hold, a beholder can transform, its flesh sloughing away to leave a death tyrant behind. This monster possesses the cunning and much of the magic it had in life, but it is fueled by the power of undeath.
A death tyrant appears as a massive, naked skull, with a pinpoint of red light gleaming in its hollow eye socket. With its eyestalks rotted away, ten spectral eyes hover above the creature and glare in all directions.

Deathly Despot. As they did when they were beholders, death tyrants lord their power over other creatures. Moreover, a beholder's ability to quash magical energy with its central eye gives way to a more sinister power in a death tyrant, which can transform former slaves and enemies into undead servants.
Zombies created by a death tyrant are used and discarded as needed. They stand guard at the entrances to the death tyrant's lair or guard its treasure vaults. Acting as bait for traps or as combat fodder, zombies keep powerful enemies distracted while the death tyrant moves into position and prepares to destroy them.

Armies of the Dead. A death tyrant that embraces undeath becomes an engine of destruction. Driven by a hunger for power and security, it advances against humanoid settlements, using its eye rays to destroy every creature it encounters, then building an army of undead. If left unchecked, a death tyrant might wipe out the population of a city in weeks, then set its undead eye on wider conquest. As each settlement falls, the death tyrant's zombie forces build to overwhelming numbers.

Undead Nature. A death tyrant doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

effects: Creatures within 1 mile of the tyrant's lair sometimes feel as if they're being watched even when they aren't.

When a creature hostile to the tyrant and aware of its existence finishes a long rest within 1 mile of the tyrant's lair, roll a d20 for that creature. On a roll of 10 or lower, the creature is subjected to one random eye ray of the tyrant.
regional_effects.summary: A region containing a death tyrant's lair is warped by the creature's unnatural presence, which creates one or more of the following effects:

combat-strategy: Float at 40-ft. hover altitude in a lair corridor where the party can't reach it and Multiattack three random Eye Rays — Paralyzing Ray (DC 17 Con, paralyzed until save or 1 minute) and Telekinetic Ray (move and Restrain up to 30 ft.) are the picks when you can choose: paralyze the healer, then drag them into the party's own danger or off a ledge while everyone else scrambles. Open with Negative Energy Cone (bonus action): no healing in a 150-ft. cone for a round, and any intact humanoid corpse — a previous victim, a fallen ally, a freshly killed zombie — rises as a commanded Zombie that acts immediately after you. Control the vertical battlefield with Charm Ray and Fear Ray to turn the party's positioning against itself, and stack Paralyzed/Restrained targets for the other rays' automatic crits. Legendary actions keep pressure on its off-turns: Glare adds two more random rays per round, Chomp (13 piercing each) finishes adjacent stragglers who try to jump it. AC 19, 195 HP, and 3-4 Legendary Resistances mean it survives alpha strikes — spend LR on banishment and the party's biggest save-or-dies, and when below a quarter HP or its lair falls, retreat to the deepest sanctum where lair tricks and risen corpses buy time for the tyrant's endless patience.

name: Deep Gnome (Svirfneblin)

actions.name: War Pick
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

actions.name: Poisoned Dart
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success
actions.save_effect: The target is poisoned for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

traits.name: Stone Camouflage
traits.description: The gnome has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in rocky terrain.

traits.name: Gnome Cunning
traits.description: The gnome has advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws against magic.

traits.name: Innate Spellcasting
traits.description:
The gnome's innate spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 11). It can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

At will: nondetection (self only)
1/day each: blindness/deafness, blur, disguise self

description:
Deep gnomes, or svirfneblin, live far below the world's surface in twisting warrens and sculpted caverns.
They survive by virtue of their stealth, cleverness, and tenacity. Their gray skin allows them to blend in with surrounding stonework. They are also surprisingly heavy and strong for their size. An average adult weighs 100 to 120 pounds and stands 3 feet tall.
A typical svirfneblin enclave contains several hundred deep gnomes and is strongly fortified. Secret tunnels lead to and from the settlement, and the deep gnomes use these as evacuation routes when the enclave comes under attack.

Established Gender Roles. Male svirfneblin are bald, while females have stringy gray hair. Traditionally, females run the enclaves while males scour the outskirts in search of enemies and deposits of precious gemstones.

Gemstone Harvesters. Svirfneblin cherish fine gemstones, especially rubies, which they harvest from mines deep in the Underdark. The hunt for gems often brings them into conflict with beholders, drow, kuo-toa, duergar, and mind flayers. Of all their natural enemies, deep gnomes fear and despise the murderous, demon­ worshiping drow the most.

Earth Friends. Deep gnomes are often encountered in the company of creatures from the Elemental Plane of Earth. Some svirfneblin can summon such creatures.
Earth creatures guard svirfneblin settlements, especially xorn enticed to service with the promise of gems to feed on.
combat-strategy: Never fight fair: use Stone Camouflage (advantage on Stealth in rock) and Nondetection (at will — scrying and divinations can't find them) to escape or ambush from tunnels the surface-dwellers can't navigate. Open with Blur (attacks against it have disadvantage) or Blindness/Deafness (INT-based DC 11 save) on the point man — blinding the party's guide in a darkUnderdark corridor is a killing move, since they'll stumble, fall, and turn back while the svirfneblin vanish. Fight with Poisoned Dart (DC 12 Con poison, 1 minute with repeat saves) from 30 ft. behind rocks, then melt into stone passages before anyone closes; a poisoned, blinded, lost party in the dark is defeated without a body count. War Pick (+4, 1d8+2) only as a last resort — 16 HP won't survive a round of real combat. Gnome Cunning makes most wizard tricks bounce off, so don't take the bait to duel casters; harass, steal supplies, lead pursuers into drow territory or monster lairs, and if captured, feign submissive merchant-tribe innocence until escape presents itself.

name: Deer

traits.name: Agile
traits.description: The deer doesn't provoke an Opportunity Attack when it moves out of an enemy's reach.

actions.name: Ram
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 2 (1d4) Bludgeoning damage.

combat-strategy: The deer doesn't want to fight — it wants to leave: run (50-ft. speed, and Agile means no opportunity attacks as it escapes), using Perception +14 and darkvision to bolt at the first hint of danger. Run it as spooked wildlife: crash through the camp, startle mounts, trigger a stampede of a herd through the party or across a trapped causeway, and let the chaos of fleeing animals — obscured movement, trampled supplies, triggered alarms — be the encounter. Ram (+2, 1 damage) only when cornered, which it will avoid; a wounded deer with 4 HP flees toward cover, water, or the herd. Use it for scene texture, omen, or moral test — a sacred or fey-touched deer that 'accidentally' leads hunters into a druid's circle, or a transformed person whose Ram is the only clue they're still in there.

name: Demilich

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the demilich fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead. (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)

traits.name: Undead Restoration
traits.description: If the demilich is destroyed, it reforms and regains all its Hit Points in 1d10 days unless a Wish spell is cast on its remains.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The demilich makes three Necrotic Burst attacks.

actions.name: Necrotic Burst
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +11, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit: 24 (7d6) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Howl
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 19, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the demilich. Failure: 70 (20d6) Psychic damage. Failure or Success: The target has the Frightened condition until the start of the demilich's next turn.
actions.save_effect: Failure or Success: The target has the Frightened condition until the start of the demilich's next turn.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: The demilich takes 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only immediately after another creature's turn. The demilich regains expended legendary uses at the start of its turn.

legendary_actions.name: Energy Drain
legendary_actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 19, one creature the demilich can see within 120 feet. Failure: The target's Hit Point maximum decreases by 14 (4d6). Failure or Success: The demilich can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.
legendary_actions.save_effect: The target's Hit Point maximum decreases by 14 (4d6).

legendary_actions.name: Grave-Dust Flight
legendary_actions.description: The demilich flies up to its Fly Speed, shedding grave dust. Each creature within 5 feet of the demilich as it moves is targeted once by the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 19. Failure: The target has the Blinded condition until the end of the demilich's next turn. Failure or Success: The demilich can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.
legendary_actions.save_effect: The target has the Blinded condition until the end of the demilich's next turn.

legendary_actions.name: Necrosis
legendary_actions.description: The demilich makes one Necrotic Burst attack.

lair_actions.name: Tomb Trembles
lair_actions.description: The tomb trembles violently for a moment. Each crea­ture on the floor of the tomb must succeed on a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone.
lair_actions.save_effect: The target is knocked Prone. Applying Prone to every other creature on the tomb floor and the initiative count 20 expiry are GM-enforced (single-target save seam; no initiative-20 lair seam consumer).

lair_actions.name: Antimagic Shroud
lair_actions.description: The demilich targets one creature it can see within 60 feet of it. An antimagic field fills the space of the target, moving with it until initiative count 20 on the next round.

zone.advisory: RAW targets one creature within 60 feet — picker selects the shroud bearer (selection advisory). The field moves with the target — attached movement has no grid-token-move consumer in this engine — GM-enforced. The PC antimagic_field te consumer keys off attacker-or-target, so non-weapon attacks involving the bearer are suppressed. Lasts until initiative count 20 on the next round — GM-enforced (no initiative-20 lair seam consumer).

lair_actions.name: Stifling Mortality
lair_actions.description: The demilich targets any number of creatures it can see within 30 feet of it. No target can regain hit points until initiative count 20 on the next round.

zone.advisory: RAW targets any number of creatures within 30 feet — picker multi-selects the victims (selection advisory). The no_healing te is pre-registered with live healing-block consumers (applyHealing/healingRoll refuse and log) — no new te or consumer needed. Lasts until initiative count 20 on the next round — GM-enforced (no initiative-20 lair seam consumer).

description:
The immortality granted to a lich lasts only as long as it feeds mortal souls to its phylactery. If it falters or fails in that task, its bones turn to dust until only its skull remains. This "demilich" contains only a fragment of the lich's malevolent life force-just enough so that if it is disturbed, these remains rise into the air and assume a wraithlike form. The skull then emits a terrifying howl that can slay the weak-hearted and leave others trembling with fear. Left alone, it sinks back down and returns to the empty peace of its existence.
Few liches seek to become demiliches, for it means an end to the existence they hoped to preserve by becoming undead. However, time can erode the lich's reason and memory, causing it to retreat into its ancient tomb and forget to feed on souls. The spells it once knew fade from its mind, and it no longer channels the arcane energy it wielded as a lich. However, even as a mere skull it remains a deadly and vexing enemy.

Enduring Existence. Even after a lich is reduced to a demilich state, its phylactery survives. As long as its phylactery is intact, the demilich can't be permanently destroyed. Its skull reforms after 1d10 days, restoring the creature to its wretched state. If it has the presence of mind to do so, a demilich can reclaim its former power by feeding just one soul to its phylactery. Doing so restores the demilich to lich form, reconstituting its undead body.

Undead Nature. A demilich doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep. So great is a demilich's will to survive that it always has the maximum number of hit points for its Hit Dice, instead of average hit points.

effects: The first time a non-evil creature enters the tomb's area, the creature takes 16 (3d10) necrotic damage.
Monsters in the tomb have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened, and against features that turn undead.

The tomb is warded against the magical travel of creatures the demilich hasn't authorized. Such crea­tures can't teleport into or out of the tomb's area or use planar travel to enter or leave it. Effects that allow teleportation or planar travel work within the tomb as long as they aren't used to leave or enter the tomb's area.
regional_effects.summary: A demilich's tomb might have any or all of the following effects in place:

combat-strategy: Open at maximum range: hover with its 30-ft. flight and unleash Multiattack Necrotic Bursts from 120 ft., kiting anyone without reach or ranged options since it only walks 5 ft. Unleash Howl the moment the party clusters, trading its burst damage for 70 psychic plus mass Frightened, then resume ranged volleys on the fleeing victims. Spend legendary Energy Drain on the healer or the tank whose HP maximum matters most, and use Grave-Dust Flight whenever melee closing in would reach it — the free Blind on pursuers pairs perfectly with its ranged attacks against sighted targets. Save its three Legendary Resistances for banishment, hold monster, and finger of death, never for ordinary damage, and if the party commits to destroying it without a Wish available, retreat behind cover or reform via Undead Restoration rather than die in a corner.

name: Demogorgon
immunities: Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing from Nonmagical Attacks
damage_immunities: Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing from Nonmagical Attacks

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If the demogorgon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The demogorgon has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Two Heads
traits.description: The demogorgon has Advantage on saving throws against being Blinded, Deafened, Stunned, or knocked Unconscious.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The demogorgon makes two Tentacle attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Gaze.

actions.name: Tentacle
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +17, reach 10 ft. Hit: 28 (3d12 + 9) Force damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 23 Constitution saving throw or its Hit Point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a Long Rest. The target dies if its Hit Point maximum is reduced to 0.

actions.name: Gaze
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 23, one creature it can see within 120 ft. The target suffers one of the following effects (choose one or roll a d6): 1-2 Beguiling Gaze, the target has the Stunned condition until the start of the demogorgon's next turn or until the demogorgon is no longer within line of sight; 3-4 Confusing Gaze, the target suffers the effect of the Confusion spell until the start of the demogorgon's next turn without concentrating; 5-6 Hypnotic Gaze, the target is Charmed by the demogorgon until the start of its next turn and the demogorgon chooses how the Charmed target uses its Action, Reaction, and movement. No damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The demogorgon casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 23): At Will: Detect Magic, Major Image. 3/Day: Dispel Magic, Fear, Telekinesis. 1/Day: Feeblemind, Project Image.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 2
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Gaze
legendary_actions.description: The demogorgon uses Gaze, choosing Beguiling Gaze or Confusing Gaze.

legendary_actions.name: Tail
legendary_actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +17, reach 15 ft. Hit: 20 (2d10 + 9) Bludgeoning damage. Plus 11 (2d10) Necrotic damage.

legendary_actions.name: Cast a Spell (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: The demogorgon uses Spellcasting.

description: A bloated toad-headed demon prince crowned with writhing serpent-tentacles, Demogorgon is the raw embodiment of chaos, madness, and destruction. He rules endless layers of abyssal salt water and slime, and his twin heads each fix their gaze on a different doomed horizon.
combat-strategy: He wades into melee where both Tentacle attacks and Gaze reach the most foes, rotating his Gaze effects to spread Stun, Confusion, and Charm across the party, and saving his Spellcasting for Feeblemind against the leading caster.

name: Deva

traits.name: Exalted Restoration
traits.description: If the deva dies outside Mount Celestia, its body disappears, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in Mount Celestia.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The deva has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The deva makes two Holy Mace attacks.

actions.name: Holy Mace
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The deva casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17): At Will: Detect Evil and Good, Shapechange (Beast or Humanoid form only, no Temporary Hit Points gained from the spell, and no Concentration or Temporary Hit Points required to maintain the spell) 1/Day Each: Commune, Raise Dead

bonus_actions.name: Divine Aid
bonus_actions.description: The deva casts Cure Wounds, Lesser Restoration, or Remove Curse, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

description:
Devas are angels that act as divine messengers or agents to the Material Plane, the Shadowfe!l, and the Feywild and that can assume a form appropriate to the realm they are sent to.
Legend tells of angels that take mortal form for years, lending aid, hope, and courage to goodhearted folk. A deva can take any shape, although it prefers to appear to mortals as an innocuous humanoid or animal. When circumstances require that it cast off its guise, a deva is a beautiful humanoid-like creature with silvery skin. Its hair and eyes gleam with an unearthly luster, and large feathery wings unfurl from its shoulder blades.
combat-strategy: Open by rising to hover at 90 ft. where most melee can't reach, then work the fight as a mobile battle medic: Bonus Action Divine Aid each round to Cure Wounds, Lesser Restoration, or Remove Curse on whoever needs it most while still swinging two Holy Mace attacks. Prioritize fiends, undead, and evil creatures with its 25-damage radiant smites, and use Shapechange to dodge area attacks or maintain a protective guise over a vulnerable charge. Its Magic Resistance plus effective immortality outside Celestia mean it can fight aggressively, but it should still kite flyers away from its wards and disengage upward when focus-fire builds. Hold Raise Dead for a fallen ally rather than spending it on damage.

name: Dire Wolf

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The wolf has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the wolf's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

combat-strategy: Never attack alone: maneuver so at least two wolves flank the same target to trigger Pack Tactics advantage, then Bite to knock Large-or-smaller victims Prone, giving the whole pack advantage on the prone target while it struggles to stand. Priority targets are isolated stragglers, ranged attackers, and mounts — drag the fight apart before closing. Use the 50-ft. speed to run down fleeing foes and reposition between attacks rather than standing over a prone enemy that can still swing. Break off and flee when half the pack is down or a target proves too dangerous (a fire mage or big melee monster), as 22 HP won't survive a focused round.

name: Dire Worg

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The worg has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The worg makes three Bite attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 5 ft. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the worg's next turn. While Poisoned, the target can't regain Hit Points.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the worg's next turn. While Poisoned, the target can't regain Hit Points.

actions.name: Dreadful Howl
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 16, each creature within 30 feet that isn't a worg. Failure: 36 (8d8) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the start of the worg's next turn. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Frightened condition until the start of the worg's next turn.

bonus_actions.name: Warp Step
bonus_actions.description: The worg teleports, along with a willing creature of its choice within 5 feet of it, up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.

combat-strategy: Open with Dreadful Howl on the clustered party — 36 psychic plus Frightened gives its prey disadvantage on attacks against it exactly when it charges in. Then Multiattack three Bites on a single target: the stacked Poisoned condition blocks all their healing, so pick on an already-wounded or healing-dependent target and finish them while they can't receive hit points. Warp Step is both an opener (teleport 30 ft. in with a willing rider or worg ally) and an emergency disengage — use it to escape reach penalties or pull a wounded pack-mate out. Magic Resistance makes it bold against casters, but don't waste it standing in ongoing area damage; circle through dark terrain where its 120-ft. darkvision dominates and its foes can't see it coming.

name: Displacer Beast

traits.name: Avoidance
traits.description: If the displacer beast is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the save and half damage if it fails. It can't use this trait if it has the Incapacitated condition.

traits.name: Displacement
traits.description: Attack rolls against the displacer beast have Disadvantage, since it projects an illusion that makes it appear to be near its actual location. This trait is suppressed while the displacer beast has the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The displacer beast makes one Rend attack and one Tentacle attack.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 feet. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Slashing damage. If target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Tentacle
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 feet. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage.

flavor_text:
The murderous fury of a displacer beast is fit only for nightmares, of which I've been haunted since narrowly escaping one's ambush. I'm certain that beast stalks me still.
—Jen-Ahb, naturalist and Displacer Beast survivor
description:
This monstrous predator takes its name from its ability to displace light so that it appears to be several feet away from its actual location. A displacer beast resembles a sleek great cat covered in blue-black fur. However, its otherworldly origins are clear in its six legs and the two tentacles sprouting from its shoulders, both ending in pads tipped with spiky protrusions. A displacer beast's eyes glow with an awful malevolence that persists even in death.

Unseelie Origins. Displacer beasts roamed the twilight lands of the Feywild for ages, until they were captured and trained by the Unseelie Court. The warriors of the court selectively bred the beasts to reinforce their ferocious and predatory nature, using them to hunt unicorns, pegasi, and other wondrous prey. However, it didn't take long for the displacer beasts to use their malevolent intelligence to escape their masters.
Running and breeding freely in the Feywild, the displacer beasts soon came to the attention of the Seelie Court. With blink dog companions at their side, fey hunters drove these predators to the fringes of the Feywild, where many crossed over to the Material Plane. To this day, displacer beasts and blink dogs attack each other on sight.

Love of the Kill. Displacer beasts kill not just for food but also for sport. They target prey even when not hungry, often toying with their victims to entertain themselves until they are ready to eat. After killing its prey using its tentacles, a displacer beast drags the corpse to a quiet place where it can feed without distraction.
Displacer beasts hunt alone or in small prides that demonstrate skill at setting ambushes. A single beast will strike and withdraw, luring prey into a densely wooded area where its packmates wait. Packs of displacer beasts hunting near trade roads recall the frequency and schedule of regular caravans, laying down ambushes to pick off those caravans.

Prized Guards and Pets. Intelligent evil creatures favor displacer beasts as pets, but a displacer beast enters such an alliance only if it appears beneficial. A displacer beast might guard a vault or act as a bodyguard for a prominent individual.
combat-strategy: Let Displacement do the fighting: attack, then lope out of reach on its 40-ft. speed so enemies waste actions chasing a phantom that rarely gets hit. The combo is Rend to knock the target Prone, then hit them with a 10-ft. reach Tentacle as they get up — prone attackers get attacked with advantage while the beast stays just outside their own reach. Skirt around walls and pillars where its illusion shuffle is hardest to track, and never let two or more enemies sandwich it, since being Incapacitated (or surrounded by swarm damage that forces concentration breaks) suppresses Displacement. Avoid standing in damaging auras: Avoidance halves saves but doesn't stop the conditions. If it takes ~40 damage and is surrounded, flee into darkness or thick brush to reset the fight on its terms.

name: Djinni

traits.name: Elemental Restoration
traits.description: If the djinni dies outside the Elemental Plane of Air, its body dissolves into mist, and it gains a new body in 1d4 days, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere on the Plane of Air.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The djinni has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Wishes
traits.description: The djinni has a 30 percent chance of knowing the Wish spell. If the djinni knows it, the djinni can cast it only on behalf of a non-genie creature who communicates a wish in a way the djinni can understand. If the djinni casts the spell for the creature, the djinni suffers none of the spell's stress. Once the djinni has cast it three times, the djinni can't do so again for 365 days.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The djinni makes three attacks, using Storm Blade or Storm Bolt in any combination.

actions.name: Storm Blade
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 feet. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Lightning damage.

actions.name: Storm Bolt
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +9, range 120 feet. Hit: 13 (3d8) Thunder damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.
actions.save_effect: If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Create Whirlwind
actions.description: The djinni conjures a whirlwind at a point it can see within 120 feet. The whirlwind fills a 20-foot-radius, 60-foot-high Cylinder centered on that point. The whirlwind lasts until the djinni's Concentration on it ends. The djinni can move the whirlwind up to 20 feet at the start of each of its turns. Whenever the whirlwind enters a creature's space or a creature enters the whirlwind, that creature is subjected to the following effect. Strength Saving Throw: DC 17 (a creature makes this save only once per turn, and the djinni is unaffected). Failure: While in the whirlwind, the target has the Restrained condition and moves with the whirlwind. At the start of each of its turns, the Restrained target takes 21 (6d6) Thunder damage. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.
actions.save_effect: While in the whirlwind, the target has the Restrained condition and moves with the whirlwind. At the start of each of its turns, the Restrained target takes 21 (6d6) Thunder damage. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.
actions.duration: Concentration, until the djinni dismisses it (GM-enforced)

zone.advisory: Cylinder (20-ft radius, 60-ft high) modeled as a 20-ft radius picker (height has no consumer — GM-enforced). Concentration anchor on the djinni, moving the whirlwind up to 20 ft at the start of the djinni's turns, the enters-space re-save trigger, and the once-per-turn save latch have no consumers in this engine — GM-enforced. Restrained, the turn-start 6d6 Thunder tick, and the turn-end repeat save (STR DC 17, ends on self) are enforced via the whirlwind te.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The djinni casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17): At Will: Detect Evil and Good, Detect Magic 2/Day Each: Create Food and Water (can create wine instead of water), Tongues, Wind Walk 1/Day Each: Creation, Gaseous Form, Invisibility, Major Image, Plane Shift

description:
Proud, sensuous genies from the Elemental Plane ofAir, the djinn are attractive, tall, well-muscled humanoids with blue skin and dark eyes. They dress in airy, shimmering silks, designed as much for comfort as to flaunt their musculature.

Airy Aesthetes. Djinn rule floating islands of cloudstuff covered with enormous pavilions, or topped with wondrous buildings, courtyards, fountains, and gardens. Creatures of comfort and ease, djinn enjoy succulent fruits, pungent wines, fine perfumes, and beautiful music.
Djinn are known for their sense of mischief and their favorable attitude toward mortals. Among genies, djinn deal coolly with efreet and marids, whom they view as haughty. They openly despise dao and strike against them with little provocation.

Masters of the Wind. Masters of the air, the djinn ride powerful whirlwinds that they create and direct on a whim, and which can even carry passengers. Creatures that stand against a djinni are assaulted by wind and thunder, even as the djinni spins away on that wind if outmatched in combat. When a djinni flies, its lower body transforms into a column of swirling air.

Accepting Servitors. The djinn believe that servitude is a matter of fate, and that no being can contest the hand of fate. As a result, of all the genies, djinn are the ones most amenable to servitude, though they never enjoy it. Djinn treat their slaves more like servants deserving of kindness and protection, and they part with them reluctantly.
A mortal who desires the brief service of a djinni can entreat it with fine gifts, or use flattery to bribe it into compliance. Powerful wizards are able to forgo such niceties, however, if they can summon, bind into service, or imprison a djinni using magic. Long-term service displeases a djinni, and imprisonment is inexcusable. Djinn resent the cruel wizards that have imprisoned their kind in bottles, iron flasks, and wind instruments throughout the ages. Betrayal, particularly by a mortal whom a djinni trusted, is a vile deed that only deadly vengeance can amend.
combat-strategy: Claim the sky: hover high beyond climbing range and open with Create Whirlwind dropped on the densest cluster, dragging Restrained victims across the battlefield while it moves the cylinder. Use Storm Bolt to knock foes Prone into the whirlwind's path and stack Restrained-with-6d6-per-turn on the party's heavy hitters, saving Storm Blade for anyone foolish enough to fly or levitate into melee. Its hover and 90-ft. flight make it untouchable to ground troops — fight a pure vertical kiting war and descend only to finish isolated stragglers. Whirlwind requires Concentration, so pick control over defensive invisibility deliberately; when the party finally threatens it, vanish with Invisibility or Gaseous Form, spirit wounded allies away with Wind Walk, and Plane Shift out of the material plane rather than die.

name: Doppelganger

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The doppelganger makes two Slam attacks and uses Unsettling Visage if available.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6 (with Advantage during the first round of each combat), reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Read Thoughts
actions.description: The doppelganger casts Detect Thoughts, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 12).

actions.name: Unsettling Visage
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature in a 15-foot Emanation originating from the doppelganger that can see the doppelganger. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Frightened condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

bonus_actions.name: Shape-Shift
bonus_actions.description: The doppelganger shape-shifts into a Medium or Small Humanoid, or it returns to its true form. Its game statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

flavor_text:
Meeting yourself is the surest way to realize you're not as charming as you think you are.
—Someone claiming to be Lorhirin of Fearchor Keep
description:
Doppelgangers are devious shapeshifters that take on the appearance of other humanoids, throwing off pursuit or luring victims to their doom with misdirection and disguise. Few creatures spread fear, suspicion, and deceit better than doppelgangers. Found in every land and culture, they can take on the guise of any individual of any race.

Stealing Secrets. A doppelganger's adopted form allows it to blend into almost any group or community, but its transformation doesn't impart languages, mannerisms, memory, or personality. Doppelgangers often follow or capture creatures they intend to impersonate, studying them and probing their minds for secrets. A doppelganger can read a creature's surface • thoughts, allowing it to glean that creature's name, desires, and fears, along with a few scattered memories. A doppelganger impersonating a specific creature as part of a long-term plot might keep its double alive and close at hand for weeks, probing the victim's mind daily to learn how to behave and speak authentically.

Hedonistic Swindlers. Doppelgangers work alone or in small groups, with group roles shifting from con to con. While one doppelganger takes the place of a murdered merchant or noble, the others take on a number of identities as circumstances warrant, playing the parts of family or servants while they live off the victim's riches.

Changelings. Doppelgangers are too lazy or self­ interested to raise their young. They assume attractive male forms and seduce women, leaving them to raise their progeny. A doppelganger child appears to be a normal member of its mother's species until it reaches adolescence, at which point it discovers its true nature and is driven to seek out its kind to join them.
combat-strategy: This is an infiltration kill, not a brawl: shape-shift into a trusted NPC, spend turns with Read Thoughts to learn passwords, plans, and who the real leader is, and strike only when it can pick off a lone target with first-round Slam advantage. If open combat starts anyway, lead with Unsettling Visage to Frighten the whole party — their disadvantage on attacks lands while its slams connect — then focus the Frightened squishies and use shape-changes to break grappling and identification. Never fight to the death with 52 HP: when outnumbered or outmatched, disengage, shift form, and melt into the crowd or drag a body away to wear. Its battlefield role is picking the fight; choose engagements where it already stands beside its victim.

name: Dracolich

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the dracolich fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead. (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)

traits.name: Life Suppression
traits.description: Creatures within 60 feet of the dracolich can't regain Hit Points.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The dracolich has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Soul Gem
traits.description:
The dracolich has a magical gem. If the dracolich is destroyed while the gem is on the same plane of existence as it, the dracolich gains a new body in 1d20 days, regaining all its Hit Points and appearing within 5 feet of the gem.

The gem is a Tiny object that has AC 20; HP 50; and Immunity to Necrotic, Poison, and Psychic damage. The gem regains all its Hit Points at the end of every turn, but it turns to dust if reduced to 0 Hit Points. If the gem is destroyed, the dracolich can create a new one by completing an 8-hour ritual using a gem worth 1,000+ GP and by expending 5,000 GP, which the ritual consumes.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dracolich makes three Rend attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting to cast Ray of Sickness (level 2 version).

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +13, reach 10 ft. Hit: 18 (2d10 + 7) Slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Necrotic Breath
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 20, each creature in a 60-foot Cone. Failure: 52 (8d12) Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Half damage

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The dracolich casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 19, +11 to hit with spell attacks): At Will: Detect Magic, Ray of Sickness (level 2 version) 1/Day Each: Create Undead (level 8 version), Finger of Death

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 1
legendary_actions.description: The dracolich takes 1 legendary action, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only immediately after another creature's turn. The dracolich regains expended legendary uses at the start of its turn.

legendary_actions.name: Pounce
legendary_actions.description: The dracolich moves up to half its Speed (movement advisory — GM moves the token; no movement-distance consumer), and it makes one Rend attack.

legendary_actions.name: Sickening Ray
legendary_actions.description: The dracolich uses Spellcasting to cast Ray of Sickness (level 2 version): Ranged Spell Attack: +11 to hit. Hit: 3d8 Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn (MA-0010 hit_conditions seam; end-of-target-turn expiry anchor is GM-enforced, CLA-325). The dracolich can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.

legendary_actions.name: Terrifying Presence
legendary_actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 19, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the dracolich. Failure: 11 (2d10) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. Failure or Success: The dracolich can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.
legendary_actions.save_effect: The target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn.

lair_actions:
A dracolich lurks in a corrupted version of the lair it had in life. The region containing a dracolich's lair is warped by its presence, creating the following effects:

Sapping Mist. The area within 1 mile of the lair is Lightly Obscured by pale fog. Whenever a creature other than the dracolich or one of its allies finishes a Long Rest in that area, it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 Exhaustion level.
Soul Drain. Creatures within 1 mile of the lair have Disadvantage on Death Saving Throws.

If the dracolich is destroyed or moves its lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately. The effects resume if the dracolich gains a new body (see its Soul Gem trait).
flavor_text:
And naught will be left save shattered thrones with no rulers. But the dead dragons shall rule the world entire...
—Sammaster the Fallen's translation of The Chronicle of Years to Come
combat-strategy: Fight inside your own Life Suppression bubble: keep 60 ft. of no-healing over the party and force them to win the attrition war you control. Open with three Rend attacks (substitute the Ray of Sickness swap to Poison a caster — the Poisoned disadvantage keeps spells from saving-trashing you), then save Necrotic Breath for the moment they group up, ideally right after Terrifying Presence pins them Frightened so they can't scatter from the 52-damage cone. Spend the single legendary action punishing healers with Sickening Ray or holding the frontline down with Terrifying Presence between turns. Burn Legendary Resistances only on banishment, power word kill setups, and dispel on your sustained threats — you have 20 AC and advantage on saves already. You reform via the Soul Gem, so fight boldly but never let the party reach the gem: if the body drops near destruction, fly or burrow away from it, drawing the fight to where your phylactery can't be found.

name: Draconic Spirit

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 10 ft. Hit: 1d6+4+spell level Piercing damage.

traits.name: Shared Resistances
traits.description: When you summon the spirit, choose one of its Resistances. You have Resistance to the chosen damage type until the spell ends.

traits.name: Breath Weapon
traits.description: DEX Saving Throw: DC = your spell save DC, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. Failure: 2d6 damage of a type this spirit has Resistance to (your choice when you cast the spell). Success: Half damage.

description: A draconic spirit summoned by Draconic Spirit. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: A summoned skirmish mount, not a tank: pick the Shared Resistance matching the party's dominant damage type before the first volley. Fly 60 ft. above or alongside your summoner, use the 30-ft. breath cone (choose the type they resist least) on clusters, then Rend the nearest with your 10-ft. reach each turn. At 50 HP it dies fast under focus fire, so stay off the front line, use flight to duck behind terrain between breaths, and let the summoner's spells, not the spirit's body, win the fight — its best use is absorbing one big attack meant for the caster and repositioning the team's line of sight.

name: Draft Horse

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

combat-strategy: Not a combatant by nature — a draft horse wants to bolt, so its first move is usually to flee or panic in place behind wagons, walls, or its handlers. If cornered or abused, kick with Hooves at +6 against whoever stands behind or beside it, which is where most attackers will be. Position it as living cover (Large body blocks 5-ft. corridors and shield walls) rather than a weapon, and remove it from the fight entirely when violence starts — a panicked horse crashing through a market street is often a better plot device than 6 points of hoof damage.

name: Dragon Turtle

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dragon turtle makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws. It can make one tail attack in place of its two claw attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 26 (3d12 + 7) piercing damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (2d8 + 7) slashing damage.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 26 (3d12 + 7) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 20 Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 10 feet away from the dragon turtle and knocked prone.
actions.save_effect: Failure: be pushed up to 10 feet away from the dragon turtle and knocked prone.

actions.name: Steam Breath
actions.description: The dragon turtle exhales scalding steam in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw, taking 52 (15d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Being underwater doesn't grant resistance against this damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 52 (15d6) fire damage. Success: half as much damage.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The dragon turtle can breathe air and water.

description:
Dragon turtles are among the most fearsome creatures of the oceans. As large and voracious as the oldest of its land-based dragon kin, a dragon turtle strikes with its deadlyjaws, steaming breath, and crushing tail.
A dragon turtle's rough shell is the same dark green color as the deep water where this monster dwells. Silver highlights lining the shell resemble light dancing on open water, and a surfacing dragon turtle is sometimes mistaken for the reflection of the sun or moon on the waves.

Dragons of the Deep. Like true dragons, dragon turtles collect treasure, first by sinking ships and then by sifting through the wreckage for coins and other precious items. A dragon turtle swallows treasure for transport, then regurgitates it when it reaches its lair.
Dragon turtles dwell in caves hidden in coral reefs or beneath the seafloor, or along rugged stretches of coastline. If a choice cave is already inhabited, a dragon turtle attacks its current residents in an attempt to take over.

Mercenary Monsters. A dragon turtle is smart enough to be bribed, and pirates sailing seas patrolled by these creatures quickly learn to offer them treasure in exchange for safe passage. Clever sahuagin sometimes ally with dragon turtles, enticing them with treasure to use their blistering breath weapons in sahuagin raids against ships and coastal settlements.

Elemental Might. Dragon turtles sometimes find their way through sunken planar rifts to the Elemental Plane of Water. Those monstrous specimens can often be found in the service of marids, which strap magnificent coral thrones to the backs of dragon turtles and ride them as mounts.
combat-strategy: Fight on water or in shallows where its 40-ft. swim speed and 20 AC make it an unsinkable bulwark. Open with Steam Breath on whatever cluster is packed together — ships' decks, dock crowds, swimmers — since being submerged grants no resistance to the 15d6 scalding spray. In melee, use Bite plus Tail to knock foes 10 ft. back and Prone, ideally shoving sailors off boats into the water where the turtle rules, and swap both claws for Tail when one big target matters more than chip damage. It tanks: walk through missile fire toward objectives, use its Gargantuan body to capsize or block, and only retreat by diving deep when it's down to a third of its HP or the fight stops being about its territory.

name: Dretch
languages: Abyssal, telepathy 60 ft. (works only with creatures that understand Abyssal)

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dretch makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its claws.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d6) piercing damage.

actions.name: Claws
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (2d4) slashing damage.

actions.name: Fetid Cloud
actions.description: A 10-foot radius of disgusting green gas extends out from the dretch. The gas spreads around corners, and its area is lightly obscured. It lasts for 1 minute or until a strong wind disperses it. Any creature that starts its turn in that area must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until the start of its next turn. While poisoned in this way, the target can take either an action or a bonus action on its turn, not both, and can't take reactions.
actions.save_effect: Failure: be poisoned until the start of its next turn.

description: Dretches are among the weakest of demons-repulsive, self-loathing creatures doomed to spend eternity in a state of perpetual discontent. Their low intelligence makes dretches unsuitable for anything but the simplest tasks. However, what they lack in potential, they make up for in sheer malice. Dretches mill about in mobs, voicing their displeasure as an unsettling din of hoots, snarls, and grunts.
combat-strategy: Cannon fodder with a purpose: waddle into the thickest melee and pop Fetid Cloud, then let the cloud do the fighting — every round a PC starts in it and fails the DC 11 save loses half their action economy, no reactions, half their turn. Multiattack the poisoned or smallest targets for cheap 8-damage rounds, and swarm so bigger demons behind you get soft targets to bully. Die loudly next to PCs: the Death Burst doesn't blind much (DC 10) but it taxes heals and actions. When a fight clearly goes against its masters, scatter and burrow into muck or flee behind bigger fiends — a dretch that survives to re-cloud is worth more than one that duels a paladin.

name: Drider

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The drider makes three attacks, either with its longsword or its longbow. It can replace one of those attacks with a bite attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 2 (1d4) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) poison damage.

actions.name: Longsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) slashing damage if used with two hands.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) poison damage.

traits.name: Fey Ancestry
traits.description: The drider has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put the drider to sleep.

traits.name: Innate Spellcasting
traits.description:
The drider's innate spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 13). The drider can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

At will: dancing lights
1/day each: darkness, faerie fire

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The drider can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: While in sunlight, the drider has disadvantage on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

traits.name: Web Walker
traits.description: The drider ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.

description:
When a drow shows great promise, Lolth summons it to the Demonweb Pits for a test of faith and strength. Those that pass the test rise higher in the Spider Queen's favor. Those that fail are transformed into driders-a horrid hybrid of a drow and a giant spider that serves as a living reminder of Lolth's power. Only drow can be turned into driders, and the power to create these creatures resides with Lolth alone.

Scarred for Life. Drow transformed into driders return to the Material Plane as twisted and debased creatures. Driven by madness, they disappear into the Underdark to become hermits and hunters, either wandering alone or leading packs of giant spiders.
On rare occasion, a drider returns to the fringes of drow society despite its curse, most often to fulfill some longstanding vow or vendetta from its former life. Drow fear and shun the driders, holding them in lower esteem than slaves. However, they tolerate the presence of these creatures as living representatives of Lolth's will, and a reminder of the fate that awaits all who fail the Spider Queen.
combat-strategy: Set the ambush from the ceiling: Spider Climb into the dark above a corridor, open with faerie fire or darkness to strip the party's stealth and grant your allies bonus to hit, then rain Longbow poison shots (+6, 11 damage plus 1d8 poison) from 150 ft. while hanging upside down out of melee reach. Dancing lights lures them into the kill zone; when they cluster, drop the range and replace one bow shot per turn with the Bite's 9 poison for a closing target. Longsword-and-bite is the last resort — 19 AC and 123 HP win short melees but not sieges. If the fight turns against it or it's alone, flee up into the tunnels rather than die in the open, and never, ever fight in daylight: its Sunlight Sensitivity makes the surface a death sentence.

name: Drow

actions.name: Shortsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

actions.name: Hand Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 hour. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the target is also unconscious while poisoned in this way. The target wakes up if it takes damage or if another creature takes an action to shake it awake.
actions.save_effect: Failure: be poisoned for 1 hour.

At will: dancing lights
1/day each: darkness, faerie fire

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: While in sunlight, the drow has disadvantage on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

description:
Tens of thousands ofyears ago, the elves were divided, with those of benevolent disposition battling those that were selfish and cruel. The war among elvenkind ended when the good elves banished their malevolent kin to the subterranean depths. Here, in the lightless caverns and endless warrens of twisting passages, the dark elves-the drow-found refuge. They also found leadership in the only elven deity who had not forsaken them. At her command, the dark elves built an empire in the underworld.

Children of Lolth. The drow worship Lolth, a deity who resides in the Abyss. Known as the Spider Queen or the Demon Queen of Spiders, she is the figure around which the dark elves have built their subterranean civilization. Whatever she demands, the drow do.
The wickedest of elves, drow are seldom seen by the surface world. Though they plot to destroy the elves that banished them, they no longer see themselves as exiles. They are the destined rulers of the darkness, and when Lolth commands them to rise up and destroy their surface-dwelling kin, they will.

Creatures of Darkness. The drow have lived underground for so long that they have evolved to their surroundings and can see in the dark. However, they can no longer stand sunlight. When slaves are in short supply in the Underdark, the drow send raiding parties to the surface to capture humanoids under cover of darkness, bringing them back to their cities to be tortured into submission. Beyond those occasional excursions, the drow are content to remain in their subterranean realm, where they feel secure and in control.

Underdark Cities. The dark elves build fantastic cities in enormous caverns where food and water are abundant. Their ability to sculpt stone rivals that of the greatest dwarf artisans, yet their structures retain a decidedly elven aesthetic. Though appearing delicate, drow settlements are structurally sound and remarkably resilient. The drow like to hollow out enormous stalagmites and stalactites, creating populated spires that rise from the floors and ceilings.
A drow city is a sprawling metropolis enclosed by high walls. Non-drow visitors must conduct their business outside the walls under watchful eyes. The drow raise and keep giant spiders to help protect their cities against intruders, even as they drape those cities in beautiful webbing, creating a gossamer snare to catch flying enemies that would otherwise soar over the walls.

Drow Magic. Just as the drow have adapted to underground life, so too has their magic. In addition to using that magic to carve their cities from stone, they empower their weapons, create dangerous new magic items, and summon demons from the Abyss. Drow spellcasters are supremely arrogant and never hesitate to use their magic in the most abhorrent ways.

Arms and Armor. Drow craft weapons made of adamantine, a dark and supernaturally hard metal. Drow artisans adorn their weapons and armor with web-like filigree and spider motifs, and mages sometimes imbue items with magic to enhance their effectiveness. However, such magic fades when exposed to sunlight, so that magical drow weapons and armor rarely retain their enhancement bonuses and magical properties when brought to the surface.

Cutthroat Politics. Drow politics are cutthroat and rife with intrigue. When drowworktogether, it is typically to destroy a common foe and ensure their own survival, and such alliances are short lived and fraught with peril.
Drow society is divided into noble houses, each ruled by a matron who seeks to raise the prestige and power of her house above all others. Other high-ranking members of the house are blood relatives, while the middling ranks are flush with drow from weaker families that have sworn fealty to the greater house. Clinging precariously to the bottom rung of a house's social ladder are the house slaves, made up of drow of low birth and the occasional non-drow captive.

Matriarchal Rule. Lolth, through her faithful priestesses, dictates the rules of drow society, ensuring that her orders and plots are carried out. Since Lolth is prone to manifesting on the Material Plane and directly punishing those that disobey her, the drow have learned to heed what she says and do as her priestesses command.
In drow society, males are subservient to females. A male drow might lead an Underdark patrol or a raiding party to the surface, but he reports to a female drow-either the matron of his house or one of her hand-picked female subordinates. Although male drow can fill almost any function in drow society, they can't be priests, nor can they rule a house.

Poison Predilection. Distilled from spider venom and the flora of the Underdark, poison can be found in abundance among the drow, and it plays an important part in their culture and politics. Drow mages concoct a viscid toxin that leaves enemies unconscious. Drow warriors coat their blades and crossbow bolts with this venom, looking forward to the interrogation and torture that follows combat.
combat-strategy: Open the ambush with hand crossbows at range, concentrating every shot on one or two lead scouts: DC 13 Constitution or Poisoned for an hour, and a save failure by 5 adds unconsciousness — focus-fire one victim until they drop and vanish before the party realizes how many are down. Control light with dancing lights to lure, faerie fire to outline hidden foes, or darkness to blind non-darkvision pursuers while you and yours see fine. When enemies close, skirmish with shortswords and Retreat/Cleave the distance — 13 HP means you don't trade hits. Disengage through passages your pursuers can't navigate, and avoid any daylight encounter: if the fight drags to sunrise, withdraw.

description:
Drow elite warriors defend their houses and their superiors against all enemies, although they specialize in fighting dwarves, gnomes, and elves (including other drow). They frequently raid surface settlements under cover of night, returning to the Underdark with prisoners and spoils in tow before dawn.
Elite warriors can be male or female.
combat-strategy: Open at range with the hand crossbow's hour-long poison — a 5+ save failure knocks a target unconscious for the whole encounter, so snipe the healer or caster first, then draw the sword and join the press. In melee, Multiattack two shortswords for 17 poison-laced damage per round against anyone without resistance, targeting separated foes where your +7 to-hit stings most. Parry is your signature: save the reaction for the fighter's or barbarian's big swing, banking +3 AC to bait wasted attacks. Use darkness to cover advances or extractions, faerie fire to spotlight invisible or hidden allies, and self-levitate to escape grapples or claim high ground — fight in pitch-dark corridors where 120-ft. darkvision and 18 DEX rule, and peel off into the shadows when the tide turns.

name: Drow Gunslinger

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The drow makes two shortsword attacks.

actions.name: Shortsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage.

actions.name: Poisonous Pistol
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, range 30/90 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) piercing damage plus 11 (2d10) poison damage.

traits.name: Gunslinger
traits.description: Beingwithin5feetofahostilecreatureorattack· ing at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on the drow's ranged attack rolls with a pistol. In addition, the drow ignores half cover and three·quarters cover when making ranged at· tacks with a pistol.

description: Firearms aren't widely available in the North, but some members of Bregan O'aerthe are equipped with Lantanese pistols, bullets, and packets of smokepowder. These drow gunslingers are expert pistoleers, as skilled with their guns as the best archers are with their bows.
combat-strategy: Never trade melee: stand at 30-90 ft. and empty the Poisonous Pistol for 20 average damage a shot — it ignores close-range disadvantage plus half and three-quarters cover, so cover doesn't save anyone from +6 to hit. Open with faerie fire or darkness to blind and outline the chase, use dancing lights as a decoy, and let dueling-round attrition do the killing from behind pillars and crates. If forced into melee, Multiattack shortswords but disengage the same turn — 18 AC with Parry-less body means you don't stand and take hits. Self-levitate for instant vertical escape when flanked, kite through cramped urban tunnels where pursuit stalls, and slip into darkness the moment two or more foes converge.

name: Drow Mage

It remains for 10 minutes, until it or its summoner dies, or until its summoner dismisses it as an action.

Cantrips (at wil1): mage hand, minor illusion, poison spray, ray of frost
1st level (4 slots): mage armor, magic missile, shield, witch bolt
2nd level (3 slots): alter self, misty step, web
3rd level (3 slots):fly, lightning bolt
4th level (3 slots): Evard's black tentacles, greater invisibility
5th level (2 slots): cloudkill

description: Privileged drow males who lack the strength and fighting prowess to train as warriors have no recourse but to pursue the study of magic. For them, it is a matter of survival. Female drow with a natural affinity for the arcane arts may also become drow mages, although they are much less common.
combat-strategy: Open with Summon Demon — a free quasit, or 50% shot at a shadow demon — to screen, scout, and harass while you stay behind cover. Then lock down the biggest threats: Evard's black tentacles or web on the martial bruisers, Lightning Bolt on clusters, and cloudkill on any corridor they must pass through, forcing them to split or suffocate. Misty Step out of danger the instant a melee threat closes, cast greater invisibility on a summoned demon or yourself when the party starts hunting you (remember: tentacles and invisibility fight over your concentration — pick control first, vanishing when the control spell's work is done). 45 HP at AC 12 means one lucky round kills you: fight from darkness, through demon bodies, and retreat via invisibility and secret passages when your control spells run dry.

name: Drow Priestess of Lolth

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The drow makes two scourge attacks.

actions.name: Scourge
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage plus 17 (5d6) poison damage.

actions.name: Summon Demon

Otherwise, the summoned demon appears in an unoccupied space within 60 feet of its summoner, acts as an ally of its summoner, and can't summon other demons. It remains for 10 minutes, until it or its summoner dies, or until its summoner dismisses it as an action.
