Cantrips (at wil1): guidance, poison spray, resistance, spare the dying, thaumaturgy
1st level (4 slots): animal friendship, cure wounds, detect poison and disease, ray of sickness
2nd level (3 slots): lesser restoration, protection from poison, web
3rd level (3 slots): conjure animals (2 giant spiders), dispel magic
4th level (3 slots): divination, freedom of movement
5th level (2 slots): insect plague, mass cure wounds

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: While in sunlight, the drew has disadvantage on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

description:
Female drow with blood ties to a noble house are molded and trained from birth to become priestesses of Lolth. The Spider Queen doesn't allow male drow to hold such positions.
Such priestesses execute the will of the Spider Queen, and as a result, they wield tremendous power and influence in drow society. The matron mothers who rule the drow houses are the most powerful of Lolth's priestesses, but they must constantly balance their devotion to the Spider Queen with their devotion to their families.
combat-strategy: Open by invoking Lolth: attempt the yochlol summon (or conjure two giant spiders as a sure thing) to screen the temple chamber, then herd the party with web and punish clusters with insect plague. Mass cure wounds when your forces take a volley, freedom of movement on your spider-riders or front-line guard so pinning tricks bounce off, and ray of sickness on advancing casters to poison their aim. The scourge hits for 17 poison per swing at +5 — she can wade into a weakened or Frightened squishy and nearly one-shot them, but she is not a duelist: 71 HP and +5 to-hit means she fights behind guardians, not in front of them. If the demon summons keep failing and taking psychic backlash, hang back and heal; when the sanctum falls, escape via levitate and passageways and let Lolth's spiders cover her retreat.

name: Druid

actions.name: Quarterstaff
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit (+4 to hit with shillelagh), reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage, or 6 (1d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage with shillelagh or if wielded with two hands.

traits.name: Spellcasting
traits.description:
The druid is a 4th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks). It has the following druid spells prepared:

Cantrips (at will): druidcraft, produce flame, shillelagh
1st level (4 slots): entangle, longstrider, speak with animals, thunderwave
2nd level (3 slots): animal messenger, barkskin

description: Druids dwell in forests and other secluded wilderness locations, where they protect the natural world from monsters and the encroachment of civilization. Some are tribal shamans who heal the sick, pray to animal spirits, and provide spiritual guidance.
combat-strategy: Open with entangle on the armored, slow vanguard to strip their movement and reactions to nothing, then thunderwave to knock pursuers back, scatter archers, or dump anyone over a cliff or into water. Cast shillelagh for +4 to-hit 1d8+2 bludgeoning and swing at entangled targets (helpless in the grasp of the plants but not prone — still, they can't flee), and barkskin on whichever ally is about to take a melee beat. Stay in heavy cover at 30 ft. edge-range, letting terrain do the killing: thickets, mud, animals you've befriended, and cliffs. At 27 HP you die in two solid hits — when the fight overwhelms you, fade into the wild, speak-with-animals for word passing, and re-entangle another day.

name: Dryad

actions.name: Club
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit (+6 to hit with shillelagh), reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 2 (1 d4) bludgeoning damage, or 8 (1d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage with shillelagh.

actions.name: Fey Charm
actions.description:
The dryad targets one humanoid or beast that she can see within 30 feet of her. If the target can see the dryad, it must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or be magically charmed. The charmed creature regards the dryad as a trusted friend to be heeded and protected. Although the target isn't under the dryad's control, it takes the dryad's requests or actions in the most favorable way it can.
Each time the dryad or its allies do anything harmful to the target, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success. Otherwise, the effect lasts 24 hours or until the dryad dies, is on a different plane of existence from the target, or ends the effect as a bonus action. If a target's saving throw is successful, the target is immune to the dryad's Fey Charm for the next 24 hours.
The dryad can have no more than one humanoid and up to three beasts charmed at a time.
actions.save_effect: Failure: be magically charmed.

traits.name: Innate Spellcasting
traits.description:
The dryad's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 14). The dryad can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

At will: druidcraft
3/day each: entangle, goodberry
1/day each: barkskin, pass without trace, shillelagh

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The dryad has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Speak with Beasts and Plants
traits.description: The dryad can communicate with beasts and plants as if they shared a language.

traits.name: Tree Stride
traits.description: Once on her turn, the dryad can use 10 ft. of her movement to step magically into one living tree within her reach and emerge from a second living tree within 60 ft. of the first tree, appearing in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the second tree. Both trees must be large or bigger.

description:
Travelers entering a forest might catch a glimpse of a feminine form flitting through the trees. Warm laughter hangs on the air, drawing those who hear it deeper into the emerald shadows.

Treebound. Powerful fey will sometimes bind lesser fey spirits to trees, transforming them into dryads. This is sometimes done as a punishment when the fey spirit falls in love with a mortal and that love is forbidden.
A dryad can emerge from the tree and travel the lands around it, but the tree remains her home and roots her to the world. As long as the tree remains healthy and unharmed, the dryad stays forever youthful and alluring. If the tree is harmed, she suffers. If the tree is ever destroyed, the dryad descends into madness.

Reclusive Fey. Dryads act as guardians of their woodland demesnes. Shy and reclusive, they watch interlopers from the trees. A dryad struck by the beauty of a stranger might investigate more closely, perhaps even try to lure the individual away to be charmed.
Dryads work with other sylvan creatures to defend their forests. Unicorns, treants, and satyrs live alongside them, in addition to druids that share the dryads' devotion to the woods they call home.

Woodland Magic. Dryads can speak with plants and animals. They can teleport from one tree to another, luring interlopers away from their groves. If pressed, a dryad can beguile humanoids with her enchantments, turning enemies into friends. They also know a handful of useful spells.
combat-strategy: Talk first, fight second — but if violence comes, lead with Fey Charm on the party's leader or most persuadable face: DC 14 Wisdom or they're your 'trusted friend' for 24 hours, and every harmful act merely invites another save. In an actual grove defense, shillelagh gives the club +6 to-hit for 8 damage, entangle (3/day) roots the brutes, and barkskin or pass without trace vanish you and your allies into the woods. Tree Stride is the core survival trick — step into any large tree and pop out beside another 60 ft. away, immune to opportunity attacks, repositioning every round to stay out of reach while the forest itself fights. Charm beasts into the fight as extra bodies (up to three charmed at once), and when the party proves too strong, disappear tree-to-tree and let pursuers hack uselessly at trunks; her tree is home, so if the grove burns, she withdraws to rebuild it.

name: Duergar

actions.name: Enlarge
actions.description: For 1 minute, the duergar magically increases in size, along with anything it is wearing or carrying. While enlarged, the duergar is Large, doubles its damage dice on Strength-based weapon attacks (included in the attacks), and makes Strength checks and Strength saving throws with advantage. If the duergar lacks the room to become Large, it attains the maximum size possible in the space available.

actions.name: War Pick
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage, or 11 (2d8 + 2) piercing damage while enlarged.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage, or 9 (2d6 + 2) piercing damage while enlarged.

actions.name: Invisibility
actions.description: The duergar magically turns invisible until it attacks, casts a spell, or uses its Enlarge, or until its concentration is broken, up to 1 hour (as if concentrating on a spell). Any equipment the duergar wears or carries is invisible with it .

traits.name: Duergar Resilience
traits.description: The duergar has advantage on saving throws against poison, spells, and illusions, as well as to resist being charmed or paralyzed.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: While in sunlight, the duergar has disadvantage on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

description:
The tyrannical duergar, also known as gray dwarves, dwell in fantastic cities deep in the Underdark. Using ancient dwarven knowledge and myriad slaves, they work tirelessly to expand their subterranean kingdoms.
Most duergar (including females) are bald and have ashen gray skin. They wear drab clothing designed to blend in with stone, along with simple jewelry that reflects their severe and utilitarian demeanor.

Slaves to Slavers. The duergar were once dwarves, before their greed and endless delving beneath the earth brought them into contact with the mind flayers. Held in captivity for generations by the illithids, the dwarves eventually won their independence with the aid of the evil god Laduguer. Slavery had forever changed them, however, darkening their spirits to make the duergar as evil as the tyrants they had escaped. Despite winning their freedom, duergar are dour, pessimistic, untrusting creatures, always toiling and complaining, with no memory of what it means to be happy or proud. Their craftsmanship and accomplishments endure, yet they are bereft of warmth or artistry.
Duergar make war against their dwarven kin and all other subterranean races. They forge alliances when it is convenient, then break those alliances when they have nothing more to gain. They take and hold slaves to toil in the Underdark, regarding them as free labor and crude currency.

Tough as Stone. Like dwarves, duergar have strong constitutions. Adding to their physical stamina is an incredible mental fortitude resulting from their time as slaves of the illithids. A duergar's mind is a fortress, able to shrug off charms, illusions, and other spells.

Born of Darkness. The Underdark is saturated with strange magical power, which the duergar absorbed over generations of imprisonment. A duergar can increase its size and strength for a short time, becoming a powerful ogre-sized warrior. If it faces a foe it can't fight, or when spying on creatures approaching its territory, it can just as easily become invisible to slip away into the darkness.
Eons spent in the Underdark also sharpened their darkvision, allowing them to see twice as far as other dwarves. This keen eyesight comes at a cost, however, as a duergar's vision is compromised by sunlight.

Infernal Master. Asmodeus, Lord of the Nine Hells, has been known to impersonate duergar gods in order to cultivate the evil brimming in the hearts of the gray dwarves. He offers them divine guidance and vengeance against their enemies while urging them on toward greater acts of tyranny, all the while concealing his true identity.
combat-strategy: Fight dirty: turn Invisibility before the party enters the tunnel, hurl javelins at +4 while unseen (first strikes often land with surprise), then Enlarge to go Large — war picks now hit for 11 and javelins for 9 — and wade into the shaken survivors with advantage on every Strength check and save against being shoved or tripped. Focus fire matters: duergars coordinate ambushes, so mark one victim and bury them before reinforcements act. Duergar Resilience means don't waste charm, paralysis, or illusion effects on them; assume those bounce. When the ambush breaks or you drop below half HP, drop concentration on nothing — just vanish back into Invisibility and melt into the dark rock to reform the ambush deeper in the complex, dragging prisoners or loot as you go.

name: Duodrone

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The duodrone makes two fist attacks or two javelin attacks.

actions.name: Fist
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 2 (1d4) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage.

traits.name: Axiomatic Mind
traits.description: The duodrone can't be compelled to act in a manner contrary to its nature or its instructions.

traits.name: Disintegration
traits.description: If the duodrone dies, its body disintegrates into dust, leaving behind its weapons and anything else it was carrying.

description: The blocky duodrones supervise units of monodrones and can perform up to two tasks at a time.
combat-strategy: A grinding, fearless advance: march in lockstep formation, two javelin shots per round at anyone who shows itself, then step in and double-fist anyone who closes. Its 120-ft. truesight makes invisibility, illusions, shape-changes, and displaced positions useless in its presence — the modron is the party's stealth-killer, so advance it straight at hidden threats and light sources. It can't be charmed, frightened, or lied into standing down (Axiomatic Mind), so fear, disguise, and persuasion all fail — fight it or flee it. Fire and thunder hit like trucks, so don't group near those; 11 HP is a round of arrows. When it dies it disintegrates, leaving only its weapons — expect no loot and infinite reinforcements, and remember the squad keeps its programmed route even as drones fall around it.

name: Dust Mephit

actions.name: Claws
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) slashing damage.

actions.name: Blinding Breath (Recharge 6)
actions.description: The mephit exhales a 15-foot cone of blinding dust. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or be blinded for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
actions.save_effect: The target is blinded for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

actions.name: Variant: Summon Mephits
actions.description: The mephit has a 25 percent chance of summoning 1d4 mephits of its kind. A summoned mephit appears in an unoccupied space within 60 feet of its summoner, acts as an ally of its summoner, and can't summon other mephits. It remains for 1 minute, until it or its summoner dies, or until its summoner dismisses it as an action.

traits.name: Death Burst
traits.description: When the mephit dies, it explodes in a burst of dust. Each creature within 5 ft. of it must then succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or be blinded for 1 minute. A blinded creature can repeat the saving throw on each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

traits.name: Innate Spellcasting
traits.description: The mephit can innately cast sleep, requiring no material components. Its innate spellcasting ability is Charisma.

description: Composed of earth and air, dust mephits are drawn to catacombs and find death morbidly fascinating.
combat-strategy: Open with sleep on the biggest martial threat — one 1st-level spell can remove the party's damage dealer — then hit the waking survivors with Blinding Breath (DC 10 Dex) to strip their aim and let the swarm claw the sightless. Hover at 30 ft. out of most reach, dive, claw for 4, and rise again; when a mephit must die, die in a melee cluster so Death Burst blinds the killers for a minute of re-saves. Stay far from wizards with fire cantrips and alchemist's fire — vulnerability and 17 HP mean immolation is instant — and use the variant Summon Mephits when cornered to flood the sky with replacements. When alone or if fire dominates the field, flee into dust storms, chimney flues, or cracks too small for anyone else to follow.

name: Eagle

actions.name: Talons
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) slashing damage.

traits.name: Keen Sight
traits.description: The eagle has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

combat-strategy: No combat plan beyond harassment: ride thermals at 60-ft. fly speed high over the battlefield, using Keen Sight advantage to scout, tail, and relay positions to its master or druidic allies. If forced to strike, dive on lone stragglers, isolated archers, or exposed camp guards, rake once with talons for 4 slashing, and ascend straight back out of reach — never land within grappling distance of anything bigger than itself. 3 HP means a single bad roll ends it, so the moment anyone aims a weapon or spell at it, climb beyond range and disengage; its value is information, not damage.

name: Earth Elemental
damage_resistances: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical weapons

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The elemental makes two slam attacks.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage.

traits.name: Earth Glide
traits.description: The elemental can burrow through nonmagical, unworked earth and stone. While doing so, the elemental doesn't disturb the material it moves through.

traits.name: Siege Monster
traits.description: The elemental deals double damage to objects and structures.

description:
An earth elemental plods forward like a walking hill, club-like arms of jagged stone swinging at its sides. Its head and body consist of dirt and stone, occasionally set with chunks of metal, gems, and bright minerals.
Earth elementals glide through rock and earth as though they were liquid. Earthbound creatures have much to fear from an earth elemental, since the elemental can pinpoint the precise location of any foe that stands on solid ground in its vicinity.
combat-strategy: Ambush from below: Earth Glide through unworked stone unseen, burst up behind the party's back line, and Multiattack Slam the softest casters for 14 a blow before they regroup. Its 60-ft. tremorsense negates all their stealth — anyone walking on stone or dirt is automatically detected, so they'll think they have surprise when you do not let them. Use Siege Monster to smash doors, walls, pillars, and wagons for double damage, collapsing cover and crushing structures rather than chasing mobile foes; fight beside ruins, quarries, and caves where you belong. Slow at 30 ft., so choose the ground: funnel enemies through passages you can burrow beside and emerge ahead of them. Thunder hurts you double — if the party finds thunder hammers or thunderwave spam, collapse the tunnel and vanish into the earth to choose the next engagement point.

name: Efreeti

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The efreeti makes two scimitar attacks or uses its Hurl Flame twice.

actions.name: Scimitar
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.

actions.name: Hurl Flame
actions.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +7 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (5d6) fire damage.

traits.name: Elemental Demise
traits.description: If the efreeti dies, its body disintegrates in a flash of fire and puff of smoke, leaving behind only equipment the djinni was wearing or carrying.

traits.name: Innate Spellcasting
traits.description:
The efreeti's innate spell casting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 15, +7 to hit with spell attacks). It can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

At will: detect magic
3/day: enlarge/reduce, tongues
1/day each: conjure elemental (fire elemental only), gaseous form, invisibility, major image, plane shift, wall of fire

traits.name: Variant: Genie Powers
traits.description:
Genies have a variety of magical capabilities, including spells. A few have even greater powers that allow them to alter their appearance or the nature of reality.

Disguises.
Some genies can veil themselves in illusion to pass as other similarly shaped creatures. Such genies can innately cast the disguise self spell at will, often with a longer duration than is normal for that spell. Mightier genies can cast the true polymorph spell one to three times per day, possibly with a longer duration than normal. Such genies can change only their own shape, but a rare few can use the spell on other creatures and objects as well.
Wishes.
The genie power to grant wishes is legendary among mortals. Only the most potent genies, such as those among the nobility, can do so. A particular genie that has this power can grant one to three wishes to a creature that isn't a genie. Once a genie has granted its limit of wishes, it can't grant wishes again for some amount of time (usually 1 year). and cosmic law dictates that the same genie can expend its limit of wishes on a specific creature only once in that creature's existence.
To be granted a wish, a creature within 60 feet of the genie states a desired effect to it. The genie can then cast the wish spell on the creature's behalf to bring about the effect. Depending on the genie's nature, the genie might try to pervert the intent of the wish by exploiting the wish's poor wording. The perversion of the wording is usually crafted to be to the genie's benefit.

description:
Hulking genies o f the Elemental Plane of Fire, the efreet are masters of flame, immune to fire and able to create it on a whim. Fine silk caftans and damask robes drape their magma-red or coal-black skin, and they bedeck themselves in brass and gold torcs, chains, and rings, all glittering with jewels. When an efreeti flies, its lower body transforms into a column of smoke and embers.

Haughty and Cruel. The efreet are deceptive, cunning, and cruel to the point of ruthlessness. They despise being forced into servitude and are relentless in pursuit of vengeance against creatures that have wronged them. Efreet don't see themselves in this light, naturally, and regard their race as fair and orderly, even as they admit to an enlightened sense of self-interest.

Spiteful Slavers. Efreet view all other creatures as enemies or potential serfs. They raid the Material Plane and the elemental planes for slaves, which they capture and bring back to their homes on the Elemental Plane of Fire. The efreet rule as oppressive tyrants, promoting only the cruelest among their slaves. Those overseers are given whips to help keep the rank-and-file slaves in line.

Planar Raiders. Most efreet reside on the Elemental Plane of Fire, either in great domed fortresses of black glass and basalt surrounded by churning lakes of fire, or in the fabled City of Brass. Additionally, efreet military outposts thronging with their minions and slaves can be found scattered throughout the planes.
On the Material Plane, efreet dwell in fiery regions such as volcanoes and the burning expanses of the world's deserts. Their love of the desert brings them into conflict with the djinn that ride the desert whirlwinds, and with the earthbound dao. Efreet utterly despise marids, with whom they have maintained a passionate conflict throughout the history of both races.
combat-strategy: Open with Invisibility or Gaseous Form plus Wall of Fire to shape the battlefield, then hammer from 120 feet with Hurl Flame (two per Multiattack, 17 fire damage each) against the squad's concentrated fire sources — casters and healers first, since their damage types can't hurt an efreeti anyway. Use Enlarge on yourself for +1 damage and reach intimidation, or Enlarge an ally, and consider Conjure Elemental (fire) early to add bodies that buy you Hurl Flame volleys. Fly at 60 feet above hazardous terrain to stay out of melee reach, dropping to strike with two Scimitars (20 damage per hit) only against isolated targets who wasted their reaction. As a lawful creature bound by etiquette, parley is a legitimate tactic: it prefers to dominate slaves and can withdraw via Plane Shift if reduced below roughly a quarter of its health or if its phylactery-like token is threatened.

name: Elemental Cataclysm

traits.name: Earth Glide
traits.description: The cataclysm can burrow through nonmagical, unworked earth and stone. While doing so, the cataclysm doesn't disturb the material it moves through.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the cataclysm fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead. (4/Day)

traits.name: Siege Monster
traits.description: The cataclysm deals double damage to objects and structures.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The cataclysm makes two Elemental Burst attacks.

actions.name: Elemental Burst
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +15, reach 30 ft. or range 150 ft. Hit: 25 (5d6 + 8) damage of a type chosen by the cataclysm: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder.

actions.name: Cataclysmic Event
actions.description:
The cataclysm creates one of the following effects at random (roll 1d4):
  • Clinging Flames. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 23, each creature in a 60-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point the cataclysm can see within 150 feet. Failure: 45 (13d6) Fire damage. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: The target starts burning.
  • Freezing Waves. Strength Saving Throw: DC 23, each creature in a 90-foot Cone. Failure: 22 (5d8) Bludgeoning damage plus 22 (5d8) Cold damage, and the target has the Prone condition. Success: Half damage only. Failure or Success: The target's Speed is reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn.
  • Raging Storm. A storm cloud fills a 60-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point the cataclysm can see within 150 feet. The cloud lasts for 1 minute or until the cataclysm uses Cataclysmic Event again. Creatures entirely in the cloud have the Blinded and Deafened conditions and can't cast spells with a Verbal component. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 23, each creature that enters the cloud for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there. Failure: 18 (4d8) Lightning damage plus 18 (4d8) Thunder damage. Success: Half damage.
  • Swallowing Earth. Strength Saving Throw: DC 23, each creature in a 90-foot Cube originating from a point on the ground within 150 feet. Failure: 18 (4d8) Bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) Acid damage, and the target has the Prone condition and is buried under rubble. A buried target has the Restrained condition, has Total Cover, and is suffocating. As an action, a buried creature or another creature within 5 feet of it can make a DC 18 Strength (Athletics) check. On a successful check, the creature is no longer buried. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: Multiple effects depending on the event rolled: Clinging Flames - 45 (13d6) Fire damage, target starts burning (Dexterity save). Freezing Waves - 22 (5d8) Bludgeoning damage plus 22 (5d8) Cold damage, target has the Prone condition (Strength save). Raging Storm - 18 (4d8) Lightning damage plus 18 (4d8) Thunder damage, cloud causes Blinded and Deafened conditions (Dexterity save). Swallowing Earth - 18 (4d8) Bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) Acid damage, target has the Prone condition and is buried under rubble (Restrained, Total Cover, suffocating) (Strength save). Success on all saves: Half damage only.

rays.name: Clinging Flames
rays.shape_note: 60-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point the cataclysm can see within 150 feet
rays.duration_note: Sphere coverage is GM point-placed within 150 ft (attacker-origin range gate not enforced — advisory).
rays.advisory: Clinging Flames: the target starts burning on Failure OR Success (both outcomes). The burning te is registered; this engine has no both-outcome te grant consumer, so the ongoing burn is GM-enforced (add the Burning badge manually).

rays.name: Freezing Waves
rays.save_effect: Success: Half damage only. Failure or Success: the target's Speed is 0 until the end of its next turn.
rays.duration_note: Prone on a failed save; Speed 0 until the end of its next turn (MA-0146 speed_zero te).
rays.advisory: Freezing Waves: RAW reduces Speed to 0 on Failure OR Success. The picker grants speed_zero on failed saves only; the success-leg speed-zero grant is GM-enforced (add the Speed 0 badge manually).

rays.name: Raging Storm
rays.shape_note: 60-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point the cataclysm can see within 150 feet
rays.duration_note: Recurring storm cloud lasts 1 minute (or until Cataclysmic Event is used again) — recurring zone has no persisting-cloud consumer (advisory).
rays.advisory: Raging Storm: the cloud is a persisting recurring zone — creatures entirely inside are Blinded, Deafened, and can't cast spells with a Verbal component, and re-save each turn they enter/start there for 4d8 Lightning + 4d8 Thunder. This engine adjudicates only the one-shot save/damage/coverage; the recurring cloud conditions, no-verbal ban, and 1-minute duration are GM-enforced (§70-class residual).

rays.name: Swallowing Earth
rays.duration_note: Restrained (buried) until freed — the bury/escape pass is GM-enforced.
rays.advisory: Swallowing Earth: RAW is a 90-foot Cube originating from a point on the ground; the picker has no Cube parser so coverage is rendered as the largest supported shape (90-ft radius) — GM positions the cube. Buried targets have Total Cover and are suffocating; a DC 18 Strength (Athletics) action frees a buried creature. Total cover, suffocation, and the Athletics escape are GM-enforced (§70-class residual).

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The cataclysm casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Constitution as the spellcasting ability: At Will: Control Weather

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, the cataclysm can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The cataclysm regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Eruption
legendary_actions.description: The cataclysm makes one Elemental Burst attack.

legendary_actions.name: Rumbling Movement
legendary_actions.description: The cataclysm moves up to its Speed, Fly Speed, or Swim Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Each creature within 5 feet of the cataclysm as it moves is targeted once by the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 23. Failure: The target has the Prone condition. Failure or Success: The cataclysm can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.
legendary_actions.save_effect: Failure: The target has the Prone condition. Failure or Success: The cataclysm can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.

combat-strategy: This titan wants a wide-open battlefield or a fortress, where Siege Monster doubles its work against structures. Open with Control Weather to set the tactical tone, then let Cataclysmic Event decide the fight: Swallowing Earth's 90-foot cube buries clusters under rubble (Restrained and suffocating, forcing them to spend actions digging out), while Freezing Waves drops frontliners Prone with Speed 0 so your 30-foot-reach Elemental Bursts punish them at no risk. Multiattack two Elemental Bursts each turn, picking a damage type the target lacks resistance to, and spend legendary actions on Eruption after a caster finishes casting or Rumbling Movement to reposition without opportunity attacks while knocking pursuers Prone. Save Legendary Resistance for power-word kills, hold, and banishment-type effects; truesight renders invisibility and illusions pointless, so the party's only real lever is damage. It fights to destruction rather than retreat, but if literally reduced near zero it will burrow or dive into water to buy time.

name: Elemental Cultist

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The cultist makes three attacks, using Elemental Flail or Elemental Claw in any combination.

actions.name: Elemental Flail
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 25 (6d6 + 4) damage of a type chosen by the cultist: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder.

actions.name: Elemental Claw
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +7, range 120 ft. Hit: 22 (4d10) damage of a type chosen by the cultist: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, the cultist moves the target up to 10 feet straight toward or away from itself.
actions.save_effect: If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, the cultist moves the target up to 10 feet straight toward or away from itself.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The cultist casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15): At Will: Elementalism, Mage Hand

reactions.name: Elemental Absorption
reactions.trigger: The cultist takes Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage.
reactions.description: The cultist gives itself Resistance to that instance of damage and gains 10 Temporary Hit Points.

flavor_text:
Dread Tharizdun, power of the Elder Elemental Eye and master of all destructive forces, I am the Champion of Elemental Evil and am ready to carry out your wishes.
—Rites of the Cult of Elemental Evil
combat-strategy: Open by absorbing the party's biggest damage type with Elemental Absorption (resistance plus 10 temporary HP), then stay at mid range using Elemental Claw's 120-foot reach, pulling spellcasters 10 feet closer into reach of your flail or shoving allies off cliffs and into hazards. Multiattack three attacks mixing Claw control with Flail damage (25 average each), choosing types a target already shows weakness to. Position behind cover between attacks, since AC 16 with no magic resistance means volume fire drops you in a few rounds, and use Elementalism to reshape terrain — conjuring walls, fog, or storms to break line of sight. Target the squishiest backline first; your reaction makes you a nuisance to burst casters, so bait cantrips and small hits to trigger the absorption rather than saving it.

name: Elemental Spirit (Air)

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d10+4+spell level Lightning damage.

traits.name: Amorphous Form
traits.description: The spirit can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without it counting as Difficult Terrain.

description: An elemental spirit summoned by Summon Elemental. Air variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: As a conjured swarm-lite skirmisher, use 40-foot flight and Amorphous Form to slip through arrow slits, portcullises, and cracks the party doesn't guard, appearing behind their archers and casters. Slam for lightning damage and kite away before melee can reach you; fight near stormy or conductive terrain where the GM can justify advantage or extra lightning flavor. Fly vertically above enemies who lack reach, dropping into melee only when flanking an isolated target, and exploit your 60-foot darkvision in dim ruins to ambush. If focused, don't trade hits — spend the turn flying through walls and repositioning until the summoner's concentration or duration re-engages you.

name: Elemental Spirit (Earth)

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d10+4+spell level Bludgeoning damage.

traits.name: Amorphous Form
traits.description: The spirit can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without it counting as Difficult Terrain.

description: An elemental spirit summoned by Summon Elemental. Earth variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: Use 40-foot burrow to vanish underground and reappear beside the party's ranged casters, hitting with Slam and burrowing away before they can focus you; burrowing denies them line of sight entirely between your turns. Its piercing and slashing resistance makes it a natural blocker against fighters and rogues — park in doorways and corridors, forcing martial attackers to waste turns or switch to bludgeoning or spells. Amorphous Form lets it squeeze through inch-wide gaps, so it can emerge from cracks in dungeon floors or walls for surprise appearances. Target lone stragglers, drag fights into tight tunnels where the party can't surround it, and when badly hurt keep burrowing to reset the fight rather than trading blows.

name: Elemental Spirit (Fire)

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d10+4+spell level Fire damage.

traits.name: Amorphous Form
traits.description: The spirit can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without it counting as Difficult Terrain.

description: An elemental spirit summoned by Summon Elemental. Fire variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: Fight in darkness, smoke, and enclosed rooms where its fire Slam and glowing form terrify, and where touching it logically threatens the party's gear and combustibles. Use 40-foot flight to hop between elevated perches, swooping into melee against a target that just cast with a somatic component or is holding oil or paper, then back off. Amorphous Form through cracks makes doors and barricades meaningless — flank through walls and keyholes to strike the backline. It has no ranged attack, so commit to adjacent hit-and-run against isolated targets, and refuse to grapple-range fights against many opponents; if surrounded, fly out through any gap and return when the party splits.

name: Elemental Spirit (Water)

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d10+4+spell level Cold damage.

traits.name: Amorphous Form
traits.description: The spirit can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without it counting as Difficult Terrain.

description: An elemental spirit summoned by Summon Elemental. Water variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: Fight near water, swamps, or flooded ruins where its 40-foot swim lets it pursue into depths the party can't follow without breathing. Slam with cold damage and use Amorphous Form to slide under doors, through grates, and into flooded passages, ambushing from pools and wells. Kite on land: retreat into deep water when hurt, since most humanoids can't dive effectively in armor while you fight at home there. Target anyone carrying mundane gear or standing in water if you can team with lightning effects, and in ship or dockside scenes drag small or Medium creatures into deep water where drowning pressure replaces your missing condition tools.

name: Elephant

actions.name: Gore
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (3d8 + 6) piercing damage.

actions.name: Stomp
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one prone creature. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

traits.name: Trampling Charge
traits.description: If the elephant moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and then hits it with a gore attack on the same turn, that target must succeed on a DC 12 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. If the target is prone, the elephant can make one stomp attack against it as a bonus action.

combat-strategy: Open at a full 40-foot run straight at the tightest cluster or a frontliner standing near a cliff, stairs, or the party's formations, landing Gore for 19 damage and a DC 12 Strength save to knock them Prone, then Stomp the fallen target as a bonus action for 22 more. Trampling Charge is the entire game plan: always move 20+ feet in a straight line before Gore, so never open adjacent and never fight in a phone booth. Prefer charging past enemies into open ground, wheeling around for another 20-foot charge next round rather than standing and trading. Huge size gives you superior over the field; trample prone or Restrained targets and use your body to block corridors or pin cavalry. A wounded war-elephant may rout if mistreated and its rider loses control, so panicking elephants flee in random directions — play up the rampage when it takes heavy damage.

name: Elk

actions.name: Ram
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one prone creature. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

traits.name: Charge
traits.description: If the elk moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and then hits it with a ram attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 7 (2d6) damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

combat-strategy: A low-CR threat that lives entirely on Charge: start at least 20 feet away, thunder straight in for Ram's extra 7 damage and a DC 13 Strength save to knock the target Prone, then follow with Hooves (8 damage) against the downed prey. Attack startled travelers, foragers, or anyone single-file on a trail or bridge where the knockdown shoves them into water or off a path. After a charge, keep moving — circle 20 feet back out and charge again rather than trading hoof-for-hoof at 13 hit points. Flee when an elk drops to a few hit points or faces armed riders; herds can also stampede as a herd-mobility hazard, knocking multiple travelers down in a line.

name: Empyrean

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the empyrean fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead. (4/Day)

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The empyrean has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The empyrean makes two attacks, using Sacred Weapon or Divine Ray in any combination.

actions.name: Sacred Weapon
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +17, reach 10 ft. Hit: 31 (6d6 + 10) Force damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the start of the empyrean's next turn. The target can choose not to be Stunned, in which case it takes an extra 21 Force damage that bypasses Resistance or Immunity.

actions.name: Divine Ray
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +15, range 600 ft. Hit: 35 (6d8 + 8) Necrotic or Radiant damage (empyrean's choice).

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The empyrean casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 23): At Will: Calm Emotions, Greater Restoration, Pass Without Trace, Water Breathing 1/Day Each: Commune, Dispel Evil and Good, Plane Shift

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 1
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, the empyrean can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The empyrean regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Bolster
legendary_actions.description: The empyrean gains 10 Temporary Hit Points, and the empyrean and each ally within 30 feet of it gain Advantage on D20 Tests until the end of the empyrean's next turn. The empyrean can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.

legendary_actions.name: Shockwave of Glory
legendary_actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 23, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the empyrean. Failure: 27 (6d8) Force damage, and the target has the Prone condition. Success: Half damage only. Failure or Success: The empyrean can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.
legendary_actions.save_effect: 27 (6d8) Force damage, and the target has the Prone condition. Success: Half damage only.

legendary_actions.name: Smite
legendary_actions.description: The empyrean makes one Divine Ray attack.

description:
Empyreans are the celestial children of the gods of the Upper Planes. They are universally beautiful, statuesque, and self-assured.

Manifest Emotion. An empyrean can experience deity-like fits of serenity or rage. It can affect the environment around it by its mood. When an empyrean is unhappy, the clouds might cry tears of salt water, the wildflowers in surrounding meadows might wilt, dead fish might wash ashore in lakes or rivers, or a nearby forest might lose the leaves from its trees. When an empyrean is jubilant, sunlight follows it everywhere, small animals frolic in its footsteps, and birds fill the sky with their pleasing songs.

Evil Empyreans. A few empyreans have turned to evil after venturing to the Lower Planes and becoming corrupted, or as the result of being cursed by evil gods. An evil empyrean can't survive long on the Upper Planes and usually retreats to the Material Plane, where it can rule over a kingdom of mortals as an indomitable tyrant.

Immortal Titans. Empyreans don't age but can be slain. Because few empyreans can imagine their own demise, they fight fearlessly when drawn into battle, refusing to believe that the end is upon them even when standing at death's door. When an empyrean dies, its spirit returns to its home plane. There, one of the fallen empyrean's parents resurrects the empyrean unless he or she has a good reason not to.
combat-strategy: A 30-Strength titan that should open by hovering above the battlefield and punching someone with Sacred Weapon: 31 force damage plus Stunned (or the target eats an extra 21 unavoidable force to refuse) effectively removes one PC per swing — Stun the healer or the martial leader first. Divine Ray's 600-foot range and 35 average damage let it snipe fleeing or hidden targets anywhere, choosing radiant or necrotic per target's resistances. Spend its single legendary action after the party's biggest turn: Bolster before allies attack for group advantage, Shockwave of Glory when melee closes to 30 feet to knock the cluster Prone for free opportunity attacks from allies, or Smite to finish a wounded target mid-round. With Magic Resistance plus four Legendary Resistances, burn your saves on banishment and domination, not damage; if it must leave, it simply Plane Shifts away. Hold Dispel Evil and Good for a fiend or undead teammate being corrupted, and Greater Restoration to free itself or allies from control.

name: Empyrean Iota

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.description: The empyrean can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The empyrean has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Otherworldly Strike
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. or range 30 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Necrotic or Radiant damage (empyrean's choice).

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The empyrean casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability: 1/Day Each: Bless, Lesser Restoration (as an action)

bonus_actions.name: Healing Word
bonus_actions.description: The empyrean casts Healing Word, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

combat-strategy: A fragile 22-HP ghostly support: begin the fight already invisible via incorporeal flight hovering above cover, and let it cast Bless on the party's attackers while Healing Word (bonus action) resurrects or tops off a fallen ally at 30 feet. Otherworldly Strike's 30-foot spectral melee-or-ranged attack lets it plink at stragglers without ever entering danger, choosing necrotic or radiant by target. Incorporeal Movement lets it walk through enemies and walls as difficult terrain — never end its turn inside an object (5 force damage), and use solid cover it can phase through to negate opportunity attacks entirely. It is squishy with STR 1: if any martial reaches it or an AoE covers it, fly through a wall into adjacent chambers and kite, casting Lesser Restoration on a poisoned or blinded ally only when safe. Retreat to rejoin its greater empyrean master when it drops below 8 hit points.

name: Erinyes

traits.name: Diabolical Restoration
traits.description: If the erinyes dies outside the Nine Hells, its body disappears in sulfurous smoke, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Nine Hells.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The erinyes has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Magic Rope
traits.description: The erinyes has a magic rope. While bearing it, the erinyes can use the Entangling Rope action. The rope has AC 20, HP 90, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. The rope turns to dust if reduced to 0 Hit Points, if it is 5+ feet away from the erinyes for 1 hour or more, or if the erinyes dies. If the rope is damaged or destroyed, the erinyes can fully restore it when finishing a Short or Long Rest.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The erinyes makes three Withering Sword attacks and can use Entangling Rope.

actions.name: Withering Sword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Slashing damage plus 11 (2d10) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Entangling Rope
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 16, one creature the erinyes can see within 120 feet. Failure: 14 (4d6) Force damage, and the target has the Restrained condition until the rope is destroyed, the erinyes uses a Bonus Action to release the target, or the erinyes uses Entangling Rope again.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Restrained condition until the rope is destroyed, the erinyes uses a Bonus Action to release the target, or the erinyes uses Entangling Rope again.

reactions.name: Parry
reactions.trigger: The erinyes is hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon.
reactions.description: The erinyes adds 4 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

description:
The most beautiful and striking of all lesser and greater devils, the erinyes are fierce and disciplined warriors. Sweeping down from the skies, they bring swift death to creatures that have wronged their masters or defied the edicts of Asmodeus. The erinyes appear as male or female humanoids with statuesque builds and large feathery wings. Most wear stylized armor and horned helms, and carry exquisite swords and bows. A few also use ropes of entanglement to ensnare powerful foes.
Legends tell that the first erinyes were angels that fell from the Upper Planes because of temptation or misdeed. Erinyes are always willing to take advantage of being mistaken for celestials in their missions of conquest and corruption.
combat-strategy: A devilish duelist built around the Entangling Rope: open round one by snaring the party's most mobile threat — the rogue, monk, or flying caster — at 120 feet (DC 16 STR), then close with 60-foot flight and Multiattack three Withering Swords (24 damage each) against the Restrained target who can't move and grants advantage to melee attackers. Use your bonus action only deliberately: releasing a caught target re-targets the rope onto someone else next turn, so chain the snare onto whoever proves most dangerous. Parry (+4 AC) against the fighter's big swing, and note the rope itself has AC 20 and 90 HP but turns to dust 5+ feet from you — keep the rope taut and between you and anyone reaching for it. Magic Resistance plus truesight makes control spells and invisibility poor counters, so kite flyers above spell ranges and let necrotic damage grind fighters down. Below roughly a quarter HP, disengage upward out of reach and Plane Shift or retreat to the Nine Hells, where Diabolical Restoration makes death a temporary inconvenience.

name: Ettercap

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The ettercap can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

traits.name: Web Walker
traits.description: The ettercap ignores movement restrictions caused by webs, and the ettercap knows the location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The ettercap makes one Bite attack and one Claw attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the ettercap's next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the ettercap's next turn.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Web Strand
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, one Large or smaller creature the ettercap can see within 30 feet. Failure: The target has the Restrained condition until the web is destroyed (AC 10; HP 5; Vulnerability to Fire damage; Immunity to Bludgeoning, Poison, and Psychic damage).
actions.save_effect: The target has the Restrained condition until the web is destroyed (AC 10; HP 5; Vulnerability to Fire damage; Immunity to Bludgeoning, Poison, and Psychic damage).

bonus_actions.name: Reel
bonus_actions.description: The ettercap pulls one creature within 30 feet of itself that is Restrained by its Web Strand up to 25 feet straight toward itself.

description:
Ettercaps are humanoid spiders that tend, feed, and watch over spiders the way a shepherd oversees a flock of sheep. They lair deep in remote forests.
Fine strands of silk stream from glands in an ettercap's abdomen, letting it shoot sticky strands of webbing to bind, entrap, or strangle its victims. It can also use its webbing to fashion elaborate snares and nets, which often festoon its lair.

Quiet Killers. When travelers and explorers venture into an ettercap's territory, the ettercap stalks them. Some meet their end wandering blindly into traps or sections of forest enclosed by webs. Others, the ettercap garrotes with strands of web or envenoms with its poisonous bite.

Sylvan Despoilers. Though they dwell in the wilds, ettercaps have no desire to live in harmony with nature. A forest infested with ettercaps transforms into a gloomy place, choked with webs and infested with giant spiders, giant insects, and other sinister predators. Creatures that wander too far into such a wood are soon lost in a maze of webs that dangle with the bones and lost treasures of the ettercaps' victims.

Enemies of the Fey. Ettercaps are natural enemies of fey creatures. The foul creatures set web snares to catch sprites and pixies, which they hungrily devour, and will encase a dryad's tree in webbing in a vain attempt to trap the dryad. Otherwise timid fey will sometimes approach outsiders for help in dealing with an ettercap infestation, being ill-equipped to deal with the malevolent creatures themselves.
combat-strategy: Never let the party reach you on your web-free terms: lair in a webbed cavern ceiling, drop Web Strand (DC 12 DEX) on the point-man or a caster, then Reel them 25 feet straight up into the webbing as a bonus action where allies and rising damage finish them. A Restrained target takes advantage-attacks, so Multiattack Bite (which also applies Poisoned) and Claw against the webbed prey while the party wastes actions cutting AC 10, 5 HP webs that are vulnerable to fire — warn players the fire option exists but costs their turn. Cling to ceilings and use Web Walker's free movement to flank, attacking down through the web so ground-based melee must climb to reach you. Ambush surprised travel parties from above and prefer isolating the smallest or lone scouts to wrap in webs; when the fight turns against it, scurry up passages too narrow to follow and flee to its burrow.

name: Ettin

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The ettin makes one Battleaxe attack and one Morningstar attack.

actions.name: Battleaxe
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Slashing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Morningstar
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Piercing damage, and the target has Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target has Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.

flavor_text:
Twice the malice, aggressiveness, and appetite—the ettin demonstrates that two heads aren't necessarily better than one.
—Bertrand, Inquisitor of the Mind Fire
description:
An ettin is a foul, two-headed giant with the crude characteristics of an orc. It never bathes if it can help it, and its thick skin is usually encrusted with a thick layer of dirt and grime beneath the stinking hides it wears. Its long stringy hair hangs in an unkempt mess about its faces, and its breath reeks from mouths filled with crooked teeth and tusks.

Dual Personality. The twin heads of an ettin are two individuals trapped in the same brutish body. Each head has its own mind, personality, and name, and possesses unique preferences and quirks. Bound from birth, both minds only rarely experience privacy or solitude. This familiarity breeds contempt, and an ettin bullies and argues with itself constantly, its two heads each taking constant offense at the other's slights.
When other creatures refer to an ettin, they combine its double names to form a single compound name that applies to the creature as a whole. If an ettin has one head named Hargle and another named Vargle, other creatures call the ettin Harglevargle.

Solitary Lives. As much as an ettin argues with itself, it is even less tolerant of other ettins, since a conversation between two ettins almost always amounts to a shouting match between a crowd of four belligerent heads. Most ettins are solitary creatures as a result, tolerating one another only to reproduce.
An ettin's twin heads are always the same gender, with a body to match. Females are the dominant gender among ettins, and they initiate the ettins' mating rituals. After finding a suitable den, a female ettin hunts and conquers a male, which cares for and feeds her during her six­ month pregnancy. Once the child is born, the male ettin is released from servitude. When the child is old enough to hunt for itself, the mother sends it away and abandons the den.

Two Heads are Better than One. When focused on a mutually beneficial purpose or united by a common threat, an ettin can resolve its personality differences and dedicate itself fully to a task. An ettin fights with a weapon in each hand, making twin attacks directed by its respective heads. When an ettin sleeps, one of its heads remains ever alert, gaining its only moments of privacy and keeping two eyes open for any creature that disturbs its precious solitude.

Orcish Ties. In ancient dialects of Common, the word "ettin" translates as "ugly giant." Legends tell of orcs that once stumbled upon a temple to Demogorgon, the magic of which transformed them into giant mockeries of the twin-headed Prince of Demons. Driven to near madness, these creatures scattered into the wilderness to become the first ettins.
Whatever the truth of the ettins' origin, orcs treat them as distant cousins, and orc tribes often entice ettins to serve as guards, scouts, and marauders. An ettin isn't particularly loyal to its orc handlers, but the orcs can win it over with the promise of food and loot.
combat-strategy: Two heads means one target that punishes flanking assumptions: Multiattack Battleaxe and Morningstar every round, since the axe knocks Large-or-smaller targets Prone for free follow-up melee and the morningstar leaves its victim with Disadvantage on its next attack. Open by charging whichever martial is standing in front — two +7 attacks averaging 14 damage each is 28 damage per round — and focus prone targets, because a knocked-down PC eats the axe one round and punishment the next. Target spellcasters with the morningstar to blunt their counterattacks. Slow Perception and dumb tactics mean it should be led into corridors and doorways where its 40-foot speed matters less and its two bodies can be fought in a chokepoint, and persuasion or deception can sometimes split its bickering heads' attention. It fights until dead unless its last head is wounded and the party flees in a direction it finds distasteful.

name: Faerie Dragon

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 1 piercing damage.

actions.name: Euphoria Breath
actions.description: The dragon exhales a puff of euphoria gas at one creature within 5 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 11 Wisdom saving throw, or for 1 minute, the target can't take reactions and must roll a d6 at the start of each of its turns to determine its behavior during the turn: 1-4. The target takes no action or bonus action and uses all of its movement to move in a random direction. 5-6. The target doesn't move, and the only thing it can do on its turn is make a DC 11 Wisdom saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.
actions.save_effect: The target can't take reactions and must roll a d6 at the start of each of its turns to determine its behavior: 1-4. The target takes no action or bonus action and uses all of its movement to move in a random direction. 5-6. The target doesn't move, and the only thing it can do on its turn is make a DC 11 Wisdom saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

traits.name: Superior Invisibility
traits.description: As a bonus action, the dragon can magically turn invisible until its concentration ends (as if concentrating on a spel1). Any equipment the dragon wears or carries is invisible with it.

traits.name: Limited Telepathy
traits.description: Using telepathy, the dragon can magically communicate with any other faerie dragon within 60 feet of it.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The dragon has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Innate Spellcasting
traits.description:
The dragon's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 13). it can innately cast a number of spells, requiring no material components. As the dragon ages and changes color, it gains additional spells as shown below.

Red, 1 / day each: dancing lights, mage hand, minor illusion
Orange, 1/day: colorspray
Yellow, 1/day: mirror image
Green, 1/day: suggestion
Blue, 1/day: major image
Indigo, 1/day: hallucinatory terrain
Violet, 1/day: polymorph

description:
A faerie dragon is a cat-sized dragon with butterfly wings. It wears a sharp-toothed grin and expresses its delight by the twitching of its tail, its merriment fading only if it is attacked.

Invisible Tricksters. The only warning of a faerie dragon's presence is a stifled giggle. The dragon stays out of sight, watching invisibly as its victims contend with its pranks. When its fun is done, the dragon might reveal itself, depending on the disposition of its "prey."

Friendly and Bright. A faerie dragon has a sharp mind, a fondness for treasure and good company, and a puckish sense of humor. Travelers can play to a faerie dragon's draconic nature by offering it "treasure" in the form of sweets, baked goods, and baubles in exchange for information or safe passage through its territory.

The Colors of Age. A faerie dragon's scales change hue as it ages, moving through all the colors of the rainbow. All faerie dragons have innate spellcasting ability, gaining new spells as they mature.
Dragon ColorAge Range
Red5 years or less
Orange6-10 years
Yellow11-20 years
Green21-30 years
Blue31-40 years
Indigo41-50 years
Violet51 years or more
combat-strategy: A tiny prankster that opens by turning invisible (Superior Invisibility bonus action) and flitting to 60-foot flight height, then pops in for Euphoria Breath (DC 11 WIS) on the most disciplined member — a success costs them reactions and most of their turn stumbling randomly for a minute, which is pure chaos in the party's ranks. Color-specific spells layer the trickery: Orange blasts Color Spray at point-blank groups, Green whispers Suggestion on a goblin-warden or guard, and Violet Polymorphs a favorite wizard into a newt-territory hazard. Only bite as a last resort; its 1-damage bite is theater. It never fights to the death: once spells are spent or a friend is threatened, go invisible, fly off laughing, and harass later with illusions and hallucinatory terrain.

name: Faerie Dragon Adult
languages: Draconic, Sylvan; telepathy 60 ft. (faerie dragons only)

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The dragon has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d4 + 5) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Euphoria Breath
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: The target has the Incapacitated condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically. While Incapacitated, the target uses all its movement on each of its turns to move in a random direction.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Incapacitated condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically. While Incapacitated, the target uses all its movement on each of its turns to move in a random direction.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The dragon casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13): At Will: Dancing Lights, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion 1/Day Each: Hallucinatory Terrain, Polymorph

bonus_actions.name: Superior Invisibility
bonus_actions.description: The dragon casts Greater Invisibility on itself, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

combat-strategy: Open with Superior Invisibility as a bonus action, hover at range, and detonate Euphoria Breath's 15-foot cone on clustered humanoids — each failure is Incapacitated and wandering randomly, with repeating saves only at the end of their turns, which can neutralize an entire wedge for a minute. Follow with Polymorph to transform the party's martial leader into a crab or hippo form depending on whether you want to remove them from the fight or grant an ally a mount, and use Hallucinatory Terrain to mask escape routes or fake a dead end. Its 60-foot flight, Stealth +7, and Magic Resistance mean it dictates when it is touched: never stop flying, never hold position, and bite (7 piercing plus 3 psychic) only invisible from behind against isolated stragglers. It's a good creature, so the fight typically ends when the dragons have taught the party a lesson or its young are threatened; when truly outmatched, greater invisibility plus hallucinatory terrain makes pursuit a joke — leave and let them wander a fake forest.

name: Faerie Dragon Youth
languages: Draconic, Sylvan; telepathy 60 ft. (faerie dragons only)

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The dragon has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Euphoria Breath
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: The target has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn and uses all its movement on its turn to move in a random direction.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn and uses all its movement on its turn to move in a random direction.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The dragon casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 12): At Will: Dancing Lights, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion

bonus_actions.name: Superior Invisibility
bonus_actions.description: The dragon casts Greater Invisibility on itself, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

combat-strategy: A smaller, scrappier version: open by going invisible (bonus action) and closing to 15 feet of a clustered pair or trio for Euphoria Breath (DC 12 WIS), which Incapacitates one target through its next turn and sends it wandering randomly — enough to break a formation. Minor Illusion and Dancing Lights are your control theater: fake voices down side tunnels, light torches to lure pursuers, and cover your approach. Bite (5 plus 2 psychic) only from invisibility against stragglers, then fly out at 60 feet; its AC 13 and 21 HP cannot survive a focused round, so never be visible and stationary on the same turn. Fight as a pack using telepathy to coordinate swoop-and-vanish passes, and flee to the Feywild-tinged depths of its warren when hurt or when its spells are spent.

name: Fenrir

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If Fenrir fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Unbound
traits.description: When the bonds that bound him break, Fenrir's jaws can swallow the sun itself. He can't be magically restrained, and spellcasting DCs against him are lowered by 2.

traits.name: Iceborn Fangs
traits.description: Fenrir's Bite deals an extra 7 (2d6) Cold damage.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Fenrir makes two Bite attacks and one Claw attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +18, reach 10 ft. Hit: 32 (4d10 + 10) Piercing damage. Plus 7 (2d6) Cold damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +18, reach 10 ft. Hit: 29 (3d12 + 10) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Devour (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 26, one Huge or smaller creature Fenrir has Grappled. Failure: 43 (6d10 + 10) Piercing damage. Success: Half damage.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Bite
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Bite attack.

legendary_actions.name: Claw
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Claw attack.

legendary_actions.name: Winter's Howl (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 24, each creature within 60 ft. The target also has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn.

description: The monstrous wolf of Ragnarok, a cold famine with fur and fangs whose growl shakes the nine worlds and whose destined meal is the light of the sun.
combat-strategy: He hammers the biggest warrior first; Bite, Claw, then Devour a pinned foe before the healers can reach them.

name: Fey Spirit

actions.name: Fey Blade
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 2d6+3+spell level Force damage.

description: A fey spirit summoned by Summon Fey or Fey Spirit. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: A conjured fey skirmisher: use 30-foot flight to stay off the ground where most enemies lack reach, striking with Fey Blade's 2d6+3 force damage (scaling with spell level) against the nearest spellcaster or archer. Force damage is rarely resisted, so hit whatever the party's resistances can't excuse — then hop behind columns, trees, or allies to deny opportunity attacks. Fey spirits are mischievous and flighty: it prefers to harass, feint, and cut pursuers through the Feywild's warped geometry rather than trade blows, so kiting through difficult terrain or between bursts of magic suits its nature. When it drops to single-digit HP or its summoning spell's concentration shows cracks, flit into brush and vanish; it has no reason to die for the caller.

name: Fey Spirit (Trickster)

actions.name: Fey Blade
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 2d6+3+spell level Force damage.

description: A fey spirit summoned by Summon Fey (Trickster form). Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: The trickster variant fights dirty: fly 30 feet to stay out of reach and feint with Fey Blade, appearing to commit to one attacker before zipping behind a column or an ally for a free strike at the unguarded backline. Use the environment's illusions and Feywild tricks — misdirection, mirrored paths, stolen items — to split the party's focus, then stab the separated target with force damage its armor doesn't protect against. It thrives in feycrossing scenes where it can vanish mid-chase through hedge-gates and reappear elsewhere. If the party starts winning, it doesn't die bravely — laugh, taunt, and slip into the underbrush to fight another day.

name: Fey Spirit (Warrior)

actions.name: Fey Blade
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 2d6+3+spell level Force damage.

description: A fey spirit summoned by Summon Fey (Warrior form). Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: The warrior variant fights with discipline rather than mischief: advance in a straight line at the party's front rank, Fey Blade (2d6+3 force, scaling with spell level) aimed at whoever breaks formation, and use 30-foot flight to stay above spears and reach weapons while dropping into striking range. Prefer 5-foot steps after each strike to stay just outside counterattack range, hovering rather than landing in the middle of a melee it can't win. It holds ground in defense of a fey grove, circle, or patron's summoning site where it will fight to dissolution, using cover and height between exchanges. When three or more attackers surround it, lift off and re-engage the isolated straggler instead of trading blows.

name: Fey Spirit (Guide)

actions.name: Fey Blade
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 2d6+3+spell level Force damage.

description: A fey spirit summoned by Summon Fey (Guide form). Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: The guide variant is the tactician of the set: rather than dueling, it hovers at the edge of melee at 30-foot flight height, calling out targets and striking only the spellcaster or healer exposed at the party's rear with Fey Blade's force damage. Use height and cover to stay outside every reach weapon, and use the fey wilds' paths to redirect pursuers into circles and hazards while the rest of the encounter wears the party down. It fights to protect or shepherd — a grove, a lost traveler, or its conjurer's interests — and will break off the moment that duty is served, melting into brush or mist. When focused by ranged fire, descend through tree canopy or into burrows and hollows the party can't follow, then reappear behind them on the next turn.

name: Fiend Cultist

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The cultist makes three Pact Axe attacks.

actions.name: Pact Axe
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (1d12 + 4) Slashing damage plus 13 (3d8) Fire damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The cultist casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15, +7 to hit with spell attacks): At Will: Scorching Ray (level 5 version), Thaumaturgy 2/Day: Fireball (level 6 version)

reactions.name: Hellish Rebuke
reactions.description: The cultist casts Hellish Rebuke in response to that spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

combat-strategy: Open with Fireball (6th level, 42 average fire damage, DC 15 DEX) on the tightest cluster the party presents — nine 6d8 dice into a doorway is the whole thesis of this monster — then let 5th-level Scorching Ray (six beams, 2d6+3 each, +7 to hit) finish scattered survivors at range. Its Pact Axe Multiattack is three swings of 23 fire-slashe damage each, so once it closes on a cornered target it grinds them in three round; save the melee phase for when the party is spread or out of spell slots. Hellish Rebuke (as a reaction, using full caster power) punishes anyone who trades blows, so bait a rogue's sneak attack or a wizard's cantrip into the reaction rather than standing in melee unclaimed. Its fire focus means parties with Fire Shield, fire resistance, or water-heavy terrain hard-counter it — in those fights, kite backwards at 30 feet, ray-focused, never axe-focused. Below half health it should fallback behind the fiend it summoned, casting Scorching Ray from cover and praying for the beast to tank.

name: Garmr

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If Garmr fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Bound at the Gate
traits.description: Garmr can't be lured more than 30 ft. from a corpse or grave; he is immune to effects that force movement while near the dead.

traits.name: Grave-Tied
traits.description: If a creature dies within 60 ft. of Garmr, Garmr regains 15 Hit Points.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Garmr makes two Bite attacks and one Claw attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +17, reach 10 ft. Hit: 25 (3d10 + 9) Piercing damage. Plus 9 (2d8) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +17, reach 10 ft. Hit: 22 (3d8 + 9) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Corpse-Fire Breath (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 24, each creature in a 60-foot Cone. Failure: 66 (12d10) Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage.
