legendary_actions.name: Bite
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Bite attack.

legendary_actions.name: Knockdown Howl
legendary_actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 23, each creature within 30 ft. Failure: knocked Prone and takes 9 (2d8) Thunder damage. Success: half damage and not Prone.

legendary_actions.name: Chain Snap (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Garmr lunges, making one Claw attack against a target up to 20 ft. away without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

description: The howling hound of the death-goddess, chained at the mouth of the underworld with blood dripping from his jaws, destined to break free and run last.
combat-strategy: He anchors defensive fights around the dead, healing as his victims fall, then uses the Corpse-Fire breath to punish the clusters that dare cluster.

name: Garuda

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If Garuda fails a saving throw, they can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Solar Majesty
traits.description: Undead, Fiends, and Serpents that start their turn within 30 ft. of Garuda have Disadvantage on attack rolls.

traits.name: Sky Sovereign
traits.description: Garuda can hover and doesn't need to move to stay aloft.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Garuda makes two Talon attacks and one Beak attack. They can replace one attack with a Sunfire Ray.

actions.name: Talon
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +15, reach 10 ft. Hit: 26 (4d8 + 8) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Beak
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +15, reach 10 ft. Hit: 24 (3d10 + 8) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Sunfire Ray
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +15, range 120 ft. Hit: 27 (6d8) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Whirlwind Flight (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 23, each creature within a 60-ft. radius in the air. Failure: 55 (10d10) Bludgeoning damage. Success: Half damage.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Talon
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Talon attack.

legendary_actions.name: Detection
legendary_actions.description: Garuda makes one Perception check.

legendary_actions.name: Swoop (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Garuda flies up to double their Speed, then makes one Talon attack without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

description: A radiant half-man, half-eagle sovereign of the skies and ancient enemy of the serpents, said to be the size of a palace and swifter than any arrow.
combat-strategy: They keep the fight vertical, diving to Talon, climbing back above the party, and unleashing Whirlwind Flight to scatter climbers and flyers alike.

name: Godzilla

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (5/Day)
traits.description: If Godzilla fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.description: Godzilla regains 30 Hit Points at the start of its turn if it took any Fire, Radiant, or energy damage since its last turn.

traits.name: Siege Monster
traits.description: Godzilla deals double damage to objects and structures.

traits.name: Thermic Nucleus
traits.description: When Godzilla takes 50 or more damage of a single damage type in one turn, its Atomic Breath recharges immediately.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Godzilla makes three attacks: one with its Bite and two with its Claws. It can replace one Claw attack with a Tail attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 20 ft. Hit: 32 (4d10 + 10) Piercing damage. The target has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 15 ft. Hit: 26 (3d10 + 10) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 25 ft. Hit: 36 (5d12 + 4) Bludgeoning damage. The target has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Atomic Breath (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 27, each creature in a 120-foot-long, 10-foot-wide Line. Failure: 91 (26d6) Radiant damage. Success: Half damage.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Bite
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Bite attack.

legendary_actions.name: Tail
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Tail attack.

legendary_actions.name: Nuclear Pulse (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 25, each creature within 30 ft. Failure: 56 (16d6) Radiant damage. Success: Half damage. Failure: the target also has the Poisoned condition for 1 minute.

description: A primordial titan awakened by the world's folly, Godzilla is a walking catastrophe — a mountain of scale and fury whose footsteps flatten skylines and whose roar is a warning shot fired across all of history.
combat-strategy: It simply walks toward the largest concentration of weapons, trading blows it can absorb, and times Atomic Breath for the moment its foes bunch up or when Thermic Nucleus lets it fire early.

name: Jormungandr

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (4/Day)
traits.description: If Jormungandr fails a saving throw, they can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Encircling the World
traits.description: Attacks against Jormungandr from beyond 100 ft. have their range ignored; the serpent's body looms everywhere.

traits.name: Tidal Tail
traits.description: When Jormungandr leaves the water, they make one free Tail attack against every creature within 30 ft.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Jormungandr makes two Bite attacks and one Tail attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 25 ft. Hit: 37 (5d10 + 10) Piercing damage. Plus 27 (6d8) Poison damage.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 30 ft. Hit: 34 (4d12 + 9) Bludgeoning damage. The target has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Venomous Surge (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 27, each creature within 90 ft. of the water's surface. Failure: 91 (26d6) Poison damage. Success: Half damage.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Bite
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Bite attack.

legendary_actions.name: Venom Drip
legendary_actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +17, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 18 (4d8+1) Poison damage and the target has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn.

legendary_actions.name: Capsize (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Jormungandr thrashes the water beneath a vehicle or structure. Each creature within 30 ft. of it must succeed on a DC 25 Strength saving throw or fall Prone and take 18 (4d8) Bludgeoning damage.

description: The Midgard Serpent, so vast it encircles the earth and bites its own tail; when it releases that grip, the oceans will boil and the world will drown.
combat-strategy: It commands the water itself, flooding positions, toppling ships and towers, and saving Venomous Surge for when enemies pile onto the shallows to hunt it.

name: King Kong

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If Kong fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Reckless
traits.description: At his option, Kong gains Advantage on all attack rolls with all of his melee attacks until the start of his next turn, and attack rolls made against him have Advantage while he is Reckless.

traits.name: Thick Fur
traits.description: Cold and Wind damage against Kong is reduced by 5.

traits.name: Tree-Swimmer
traits.description: Kong's climbing speed equals his walking speed and he can move through difficult terrain of trees and rubble without penalty.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Kong makes three Slam attacks. If a Slam hits a creature, he can replace one of his remaining attacks with a Grab.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +17, reach 10 ft. Hit: 26 (3d10 + 10) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Grab
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +17, reach 10 ft. Hit: 26 (3d10 + 10) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it must succeed on a DC 25 Strength saving throw or have the Grappled condition (escape DC 25) and be Restrained until Kong's next turn.

actions.name: Thunder Roar (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 23, each creature within 60 ft. that can hear Kong. Failure: the target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. Success: no effect. No damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: the target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. Success: half damage and not Frightened.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Slam
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Slam attack.

legendary_actions.name: Rock Throw
legendary_actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +17, range 90 ft. Hit: 26 (3d10 + 10) Bludgeoning damage.

legendary_actions.name: Climbing Dash (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Kong moves up to his Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, climbing or swinging, and can make one Slam attack at any point along the path.

description: The Eighth Wonder of the World — a colossal great ape of startling gentleness and earth-shaking wrath. He guards the forgotten isle's jungle as jealously as he shields the small, curious things he befriends within it.
combat-strategy: He closes instantly, Reckless and hugging the group so ranged attackers have to trade with his hides and grabs, then Roars when foes pile in, ending fights with Rock Throw on fleeing targets.

name: Ladon

traits.name: Never Sleeps
traits.description: Ladon can't be put to sleep by magic and always sees attackers coming.

traits.name: Sworn Guardian
traits.description: Ladon gains Advantage on opportunity attacks against any creature that moves within reach of his tree.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If Ladon fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Ladon makes two Bite attacks and one Constrict attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +15, reach 10 ft. Hit: 26 (4d8 + 8) Piercing damage. Plus 14 (4d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Constrict
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +15, reach 10 ft., one Huge or smaller creature. Hit: 25 (4d8 + 8) Bludgeoning damage and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 22). Ladon has five coils; each Grappled target is held by a separate coil. While Grappled this way, a target takes 18 (4d8) Bludgeoning damage at the start of its turn.

actions.name: Sleeping Mist (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 23, each creature in a 60-foot Cone. Failure: the target has the Unconscious condition until the end of its next turn, repeating the saving throw at the end of each of its turns to end the effect early. Success: no effect. No damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: the target has the Unconscious condition until the end of its next turn, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns. Success: it isn't affected. No damage.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Bite
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Bite attack.

legendary_actions.name: Coil
legendary_actions.description: One of Ladon's coils makes a Constrict attack.

legendary_actions.name: Vigilant Watch (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Ladon fixes one target. Until the start of his next turn, his next Opportunity Attack against that target has +5 to hit.

description: The hundred-headed dragon who coiled around the tree of golden apples, vigilance incarnate and the last monster of the old world to be beaten by a trick.
combat-strategy: He fights stationary at the tree, Constrict on the biggest intruder and Sleeping Mist down the climbers.

name: Monkey Clone

traits.name: Hair Trick
traits.description: A monkey clone is a conjured duplicate of Sun Wukong spun from one of his magical hairs. It dies instantly when it takes any damage, and it vanishes when the summon ends.

traits.name: Mimic Strike
traits.description: The clone swings a hair-forked copy of the Ruyi Jingu Bang.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +14, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d8 + 2) Bludgeoning damage.

description: A monkey-shaped duplicate born from one of Sun Wukong's eight thousand four hundred hairs — fierce, fragile, and gone in a heartbeat.
combat-strategy: It exists to swing once and vanish; swarm, harass, and never tank.

name: Nidhogg

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If Nidhogg fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Rot Wing
traits.description: Creatures that start their turn within 20 ft. of Nidhogg take 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage.

traits.name: Root Gnawer
traits.description: Whenever Nidhogg deals Necrotic damage to a structure or a rooted plant creature, he regains Hit Points equal to half the damage dealt.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Nidhogg makes two Bite attacks and one Claw attack.

actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +17, reach 10 ft. Hit: 25 (3d10 + 9) Piercing damage. Plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Claw

legendary_actions.name: Bite
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Bite attack.

legendary_actions.name: Claw
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Claw attack.

legendary_actions.name: Grave Gale (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Nidhogg beats his wings, exhaling a blast of corpse-light wind: one creature within 60 ft. must succeed on a DC 24 Strength saving throw or take 18 (4d8) Necrotic damage and be pushed 30 ft.

description: The dread dragon who gnaws the roots of the world tree, feeding on the corpses of oath-breakers and carrying their stolen memories in his scales.
combat-strategy: He strafes from above with Bite and Corpse Wind, then dives to root-graze on anything that falls, healing himself with the carrion he leaves behind.

name: Orcus
armor_class_details: 17 (natural armor), 20 with the Wand of Orcus
immunities: Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing from Nonmagical Attacks
damage_immunities: Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing from Nonmagical Attacks

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If the orcus fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: Orcus has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Master of Undeath
traits.description: Orcus can cast Animate Dead (at will) and Create Undead (3/Day), choosing the level at which the spells are cast. Creatures created by them remain under his control indefinitely, and he can cast Create Undead even when it isn't night.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Orcus makes three Wand of Orcus, Tail, or Necrotic Bolt attacks.

actions.name: Wand of Orcus
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 10 ft. Hit: 24 (3d8 + 11) Bludgeoning damage. Plus 13 (2d12) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +16, reach 10 ft. Hit: 21 (3d8 + 8) Force damage. Plus 9 (2d8) Poison damage.

actions.name: Necrotic Bolt
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +15, range 120 ft. Hit: 29 (5d8 + 7) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Conjure Undead (1/Day)
actions.description: While holding the Wand of Orcus, Orcus conjures Undead creatures whose combined average Hit Points don't exceed 500. The creatures rise from the ground or form in unoccupied spaces within 300 ft. of him and obey his commands until destroyed or dismissed.

automation.advisory: Combined average Hit Points of the conjured undead never exceed 500 (§70 GM-enforced cap). They obey Orcus until destroyed or dismissed as an action.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: Orcus casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 23): At Will: Detect Magic. 3/Day: Dispel Magic. 1/Day: Time Stop.

actions.name: Wand Spellcasting
actions.description: While holding the Wand of Orcus, Orcus casts one of the following spells (spell save DC 18). The wand has 7 charges: At Will (no charge): Animate Dead, Blight, Speak with Dead. 1 Charge: Circle of Death. 2 Charges: Power Word Kill. It regains 1d4 + 3 charges daily at dawn.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Attack
legendary_actions.description: Orcus makes one Tail or Necrotic Bolt attack.

legendary_actions.name: Creeping Death (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Area Effect: a 60-foot-tall, 10-foot-radius Cylinder of swirling necrotic energy rises from a point it can see within 100 ft. and lasts until the end of Orcus's next turn. Creatures in the area have Vulnerability to Necrotic damage. No saving throw, no damage.

description: The Demon Prince of Undeath, the Blood Lord, Orcus stalks the multiverse as a towering, bull-skulled butcher wreathed in creeping death, wielding the bone-white Wand that bears his name.
combat-strategy: He unleases Conjure Undead early to flood the field, then hovers at range behind his horde, alternating Wand swings up close with Necrotic Bolts, and drops Creeping Death on clusters to make Necrotic damage a death sentence.

name: Otherworldly Steed

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d8+4 Bludgeoning damage.

traits.name: Spellcasting
traits.description: The steed can cast two cantrips of your choice from the Paladin spell list. It casts a cantrip on itself or its rider as its target. Spellcasting Ability: Charisma.

description: An otherworldly steed summoned by Find Steed. Resembles a Large, rideable animal of the caster's choice; the caster chooses its type (Celestial, Fey, or Fiend). AC and Hit Points scale with the spell's level (AC 12 + spell level; 20 HP + 10 per spell level above 2nd).
combat-strategy: A summoned mount, not a combatant: its job is 60-foot speed for its rider, so fight as a mobile platform — let the mounted paladin or knight make every attack while the steed Disengages or Dash to control spacing, staying out of reach of enemy reach weapons. Hooves (1d8+4 bludgeoning) are only for when an enemy grapples the rider or the steed is cornered: kick whatever is adjacent, then gallop clear. With only 20 HP, if anyone targets the horse instead of the rider, wheel away and use the steed's spellcasting cantrips (chosen from the paladin list, cast on itself or its rider) to buff or shield — think Protection from Evil and Good style cantrips as auras of defense. If the rider is dismounted or the steed drops below 8 HP, withdraw from the front line and keep it alive behind terrain; a dead steed costs its rider mobility for the rest of the day.

name: Fiendish Spirit (Demon)

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d12+3+spell level Necrotic damage.

traits.name: Death Throes
traits.description: When the spirit drops to 0 Hit Points or the spell ends, the spirit explodes. DEX Saving Throw: DC = your spell save DC, each creature in a 70-foot Emanation originating from the spirit. Failure: 2d10+spell level Fire damage. Success: Half damage.

description: A fiendish spirit summoned by Summon Fiend or Fiendish Spirit. Demon variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: A living bomb: its Death Throes deals 2d10+spell level fire damage in a 70-foot radius on death, so fight where the explosion does the most work. Open by charging (40-foot walk or 40-foot climb up walls) at the densest cluster of casters, bite for necrotic damage, and deliberately stand next to the party when its 50 HP are spent — let their own overkill trigger the blast into their formation. Fire resistance means the party's fire cantrips and burning ground barely slow it, so it can wade through a wall of fire to reach its detonation spot. Climb walls and ceilings to drag the fight vertical, forcing the party to choose between killing it on the ceiling (explosion overhead) or luring it down. Ideally, the conjurer keeps it alive just long enough to walk into the party — the demon wants to die next to them.

name: Fiendish Spirit (Devil)

actions.name: Fiery Strike
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. or range 150 ft. Hit: 2d6+3+spell level Fire damage.

traits.name: Devil's Sight
traits.description: Magical Darkness doesn't impede the spirit's Darkvision.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The spirit has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description: A fiendish spirit summoned by Summon Fiend or Fiendish Spirit. Devil variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: A flying artillery spirit: Fiery Strike reaches 150 feet (2d6+3+spell level fire), so open hovering high above the party's range and snipe the spellcasters out of position, descending only to bite-strike isolated targets then back up to height. Magical darkness is its home turf — with Devil's Sight, the party's Darkness spell just becomes your cover: cast or arrange magical darkness, attack out of it from 150 feet, and they can't see you to attack back. Magic Resistance blunts their counter-spells, so force them into mundane arrows and reach, then kite at 60-foot flight speed, staying above the melee entirely. Fire resistance lets it sit in burning terrain between shots. Below roughly a third HP, ascend into darkness or cloud cover, heal nothing, and reposition to a new firing angle, saving the final dive-and-detonate (when its spell duration expires) for wherever the party has clustered last.

name: Fiendish Spirit (Yugoloth)

actions.name: Claws
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d8+3+spell level Slashing damage. Immediately after the attack hits or misses, the spirit can teleport up to 30 ft. to an unoccupied space it can see.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The spirit has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description: A fiendish spirit summoned by Summon Fiend or Fiendish Spirit. Yugoloth variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: Open by summoning into a place already dangerous to the party, since this CR 0 skirmisher exists to harass and vanish. Use Claws as a spell attack against the weakest armor class in reach, then immediately teleport 30 feet away after the swing — hit-and-run is its whole game, and with 40 ft. walk plus 30 ft. teleport it can rarely be pinned. Never let it end a turn adjacent to a martial character; kite around corners and pillars where its 60 ft. darkvision still lets it re-acquire targets. Magic Resistance means spend your smites and buffs elsewhere; finish it quickly before reinforcements arrive, and don't waste save-or-suck spells on its +3 saves.

name: Fire Elemental

traits.name: Fire Aura
traits.description: At the end of each of the elemental's turns, each creature in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the elemental takes 5 (1d10) Fire damage. Creatures and flammable objects in the Emanation start burning.

traits.name: Fire Form
traits.description: The elemental can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so, and it can enter a creature's space and stop there. The first time it enters a creature's space on a turn, that creature takes 5 (1d10) Fire damage.

traits.name: Illumination
traits.description: The elemental sheds Bright Light in a 30-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet.

traits.name: Water Susceptibility
traits.description: The elemental takes 3 (1d6) Cold damage for every 5 feet the elemental moves in water or for every gallon of water splashed on it.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The elemental makes two Burn attacks.

actions.name: Burn
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Fire damage. If the target is a creature or a flammable object, it starts burning.

description: A faint humanoid shape threads through the core of this wild, moving flame. A fire elemental is a force of capricious devastation. Wherever it moves, it sets its surroundings ablaze, turning the world to ash, smoke, and cinders. Water can halt its destructive progress, causing the fire elemental to shrink back, hissing and smoking in pain and rage.
combat-strategy: Charge straight into the thickest cluster of foes — Fire Aura deals free damage at the end of every turn and sets flammable creatures alight, so proximity is the strategy despite Fire Form's touch damage. Open with a 50 ft. dash into melee and Multiattack with Burn on the two lowest-Dexterity or most-flammable-looking targets, letting burning victims spread panic and force action economy into extinguishing itself. Avoid water obsessively: route around ponds, rain, and any wizard hoarding create water or ice, and bully the party away from it since each 5 feet in water costs 1d6. Use Fire Form to slip through portcullises, cracks, and creature spaces to bypass front-line defenders and reach squishy casters, stopping inside a target's space to stack aura damage each round. It fights to the death — mindless elemental fury, no retreat — so make the party pay in fire damage for every foot it advances.

name: Fire Giant

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The giant makes two attacks, using Flame Sword or Hammer Throw in any combination.

actions.name: Flame Sword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +11, reach 10 ft. Hit: 21 (4d6 + 7) Slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) Fire damage.

actions.name: Hammer Throw
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +11, range 60/240 ft. Hit: 23 (3d10 + 7) Bludgeoning damage plus 4 (1d8) Fire damage, and the target is pushed up to 15 feet straight away from the giant and has Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target is pushed up to 15 feet straight away from the giant and has Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.

description:
Master crafters and organized warriors, fire giants dwell among volcanoes, lava floes, and rocky mountains. They are ruthless militaristic brutes whose mastery of metalwork is legendary.

Fire Forged. Fire giant fortresses are built around and inside volcanoes or near magma-filled caverns. The blistering heat of their homes fuels the fire giants' forges, and causes the iron of their fortress walls to glow a comforting orange. In lands far removed from volcanic heat, fire giants mine coal to burn. Traditional smithies occupy places of honor in their demesnes, and the giants' stony fortresses constantly belch plumes of sooty smoke. In more remote outposts, fire giants burn wood to keep their forge fires lit, deforesting leagues of land in all directions.
Fire giants shun cold as much as their cousins the frost giants hate heat. They can adapt to cold environments with effort, though, keeping their hearth fires burning bright and wearing heavy woolen clothing and furs to stay warm.

Martial Experts. From birth, a fire giant is taught to embrace a legacy of war. At the cradle, its parents chant songs of battle. As children, fire giants play at war, hurling igneous rocks at one another across the banks of magma rivers. In later years, formal martial training becomes an integral part of life in the giants' fortresses and underground realms of smoke and ash. The fire giants' songs are odes of battles lost and won, while their dances are martial formations of pounding feet that resound like smiths' hammers throughout their smoky halls.
Just as fire giants pass down their knowledge of crafting from generation to generation, their renowned fighting prowess comes not from wild fury but from endless discipline and training. Enemies make the mistake of underestimating fire giants based on their brutish manner, learning too late that these giants live for combat and can be shrewd tacticians.

Feudal Lords. Humanoids conquered in war become serfs to the fire giants. The serfs work the farms and fields on the outskirts of fire giant halls and fortresses, raising livestock and harvesting fields whose bounty is almost entirely tithed to the fire giant kings.
Fire giant crafters work through insight and experience rather than writing or arithmetic. Though most fire giants place little worth on such frivolousness' they sometimes keep slaves at court who are versed in such skills. Serfs not destined for court or the fields (especially dwarves) are taken to the fire giants' mountainous realms to mine ore and gemstones from deep within the earth.
Fire giants low in the ordning manage the mine tunnels and the slaves that toil there, few of which survive the difficult and dangerous work for long. Though fire giants are skilled in the engineering of mine tunnels and the gathering of ore, they place less importance on the safety of their slaves than on smelting and working the bounty those slaves produce.

Skilled Artisans. Fire giants have a fearsome reputation as soldiers and conquerors, and for their ability to burn, plunder, and destroy. Yet among the giants, fire giants produce the greatest crafters and artists. They excel at smelting and smith work, as they do at the engineering of metal and stone, and the quality of their artistry shows even in their implements of destruction and their weapons of war.
Fire giants strive to build the strongest fortresses and most potent siege weapons. They experiment with alloys to create the hardest armor, then forge the swords that can pierce it. Such work requires brawn and brains in equal measure, and fire giants high in the ordning tend to be the smartest and strongest of their kind.
combat-strategy: Open at range with Hammer Throw against whoever is clustered or standing near a cliff, chasms, or bonfires — the 15 ft. push plus Disadvantage on their next attack makes it a premier opener and control tool at 60/240 ft. Once foes close, switch to Multiattack with Flame Sword (10 ft. reach) and mix in Hammer Throw at melee range to knock back the healer or a charging barbarian into danger. Fight in forges, lava fords, and burning buildings where it is comfortable and the party is not; its 18 AC and 162 HP let it stand toe-to-toe with anyone, and its +11 to hit punishes low armor relentlessly. Target stragglers and push them off ledges or into magma — think knockback geometry every round. Slow (30 ft.) but no reason to retreat; if the fight turns against it, it should fall back toward deeper fire terrain while continuing to throw hammers, never turning its back.

name: Fire Snake

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The snake makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its tail.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) fire damage.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) fire damage.

traits.name: Heated Body
traits.description: A creature that touches the snake or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 3 (1d6) fire damage.

description: Salamanders hatch from eggs that are two-foot-diameter spheres of smoldering obsidian. When a salamander is ready to hatch, it melts its way through the egg's thick shell and emerges as a fire snake. A fire snake matures into a salamander adult within a year.
combat-strategy: These fragile CR 1 elementals work in packs — open by surrounding a single mid-rank target and Multiattack (Bite + Tail) to bury them in fire damage they can't easily shrug. Swarming matters: Heated Body punishes every melee attacker who swings at you, so cluster around fighters and let their own sword-swings burn their hands, making the party reluctant to melee. Prioritize unarmored casters and anyone wielding a shield they can't drop; fire immunity means friendly area fire is free cover. Hide in hearths, braziers, and furnaces, erupting when foes come near, and exploit fire-heavy lairs where the party can't use their own flames against you. They're bold but brittle — at half strength (11 HP) with cold-users still fresh, slip back into the embers they came from; cold vulnerability means a wizard casting ice is the retreat signal.

name: Flameskull

traits.name: Illumination
traits.description: The flameskull sheds Bright Light in a 15-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 15 feet.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The flameskull has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Undead Restoration
traits.description: If the flameskull is destroyed, it regains all its Hit Points in 1 hour unless Holy Water is sprinkled on its remains or the Dispel Evil and Good spell is cast on them.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The flameskull makes two Fire Ray attacks.

actions.name: Fire Ray
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) Fire damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The flameskull casts one of the following spells, requiring no Somatic or Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13): At Will: Mage Hand 2/Day: Magic Missile (level 2 version) 1/Day: Fireball

description:
Blazing green flames and mad, echoing laughter follow a disembodied skull as it patrols its demesne. When the undead flameskull discovers trespassers, it blasts the intruders with fiery rays from its eyes and dreadful spells called up from the dark recesses of its memory.
Dark spellcasters fashion flameskulls from the remains of dead wizards. When the ritual is complete, green flames erupt from the skull to complete its ghastly transformation.

Legacy of Life. A flameskull only dimly recalls its former life. Though it might speak in its old voice and recount key events from its past, it is but an echo of its former self. However, its undead transformation grants it full access to the magic it wielded in life, letting it cast spells while ignoring the material and somatic components it can no longer employ.

Eternally Bound. Intelligent and vigilant, a flameskull serves its creator by protecting a hidden treasure hoard, a secret chamber, or a specific individual. A flameskull carries out the directives given to it when it was created, and it interprets those commands to the letter. A flameskull's master must craft its instructions with care to ensure that the creature carries out its tasks properly.

Wreathed in Flame. The fire wreathing a flameskull burns continually, giving off bright light that the creature controls. It uses those flames as a weapon, focusing them to loose them as fiery rays from its eye sockets.

Eldritch Rejuvenation. A flameskull's shattered fragments reform unless they are splashed with holy water or subjected to a dispel magic or remove curse spell. If it can no longer fulfill its intended purpose, the re-formed flameskull is beholden to no one and becomes autonomous.

Undead Nature. A flameskull doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Open with Fireball the moment two or more foes cluster in a corridor or chamber — this is its single biggest damage spike and it should usually spend it early from behind full cover. Stay at range with Multiattack Fire Ray (60 ft.) against the lowest-AC target, hovering at high altitude since its flying hover and Tiny size make it nearly untouchable by melee. Magic Resistance plus 60 ft. flight means it should bait cantrips and save-or-suck spells, then punish repositioning rounds by saving Magic Missile as a no-miss finisher on wounded targets. Keep Magic Missile and Fireball separate turns; on its third big turn it will be out of big spells, so fall back on Fire Rays. Retreat by phasing through keyholes and cracks when out of spells and below roughly 15 HP — and remember the party must desecrate its remains, so fleeing to a defensible tomb chamber to regenerate later is a legitimate long-game.

name: Flaming Skeleton
languages: Understands Common plus one other language but can't speak

traits.name: Death Burst
traits.description: The skeleton explodes when it dies. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the skeleton. Failure: 14 (4d6) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.

traits.name: Illumination
traits.description: The skeleton sheds Bright Light in a 15-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 15 feet.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The skeleton makes two attacks, using Flame Scepter or Hurl Flame in any combination.

actions.name: Flame Scepter
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) Fire damage.

actions.name: Hurl Flame
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 60 ft. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) Fire damage.

combat-strategy: Open at range with Hurl Flame volleys while its glowing silhouette baits enemy attention, then let foes come to it — Death Burst makes closing the distance costly. Multiattack is flexible: two Hurl Flames on backline casters at 60 ft., or Flame Scepter plus Hurl Flame to split between a melee defender and a squishy target; hit whoever is furthest from cover first. Fight near wooden structures, tapestries, and thatched roofs where the party cannot bring its full force to bear without burning itself, and use bright illumination to pick off foes in otherwise dark ruins. At around 20 HP, stop hanging back — deliberately wade into the tightest knot of enemies so Death Burst's 4d6 fire in a 10 ft. emanation lands on three or four clustered heroes. Its fire immunity means the party's own flames are no threat to it; cold damage, however, is its cue to fall back behind allies.

name: Flesh Golem
languages: Understands Common plus one other language but can't speak

traits.name: Aversion to Fire
traits.description: If the golem takes Fire damage, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn.

traits.name: Berserk
traits.description: Whenever the golem starts its turn Bloodied, roll 1d6. On a 6, the golem goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the golem attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the golem attacks an object. Once the golem goes berserk, it remains so until it is destroyed or it is no longer Bloodied. The golem's creator, if within 60 feet of the berserk golem, can try to calm it by taking an action to make a DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check; the golem must be able to hear its creator. If this check succeeds, the golem ceases being berserk until the start of its next turn, at which point it resumes rolling for the Berserk trait again if it is still Bloodied.

traits.name: Immutable Form
traits.description: The golem can't shape-shift.

traits.name: Lightning Absorption
traits.description: Whenever the golem is subjected to Lightning damage, it regains a number of Hit Points equal to the Lightning damage dealt.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The golem has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The golem makes two Slam attacks.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 4 (1d8) Lightning damage.

description:
A flesh golem is a grisly assortment of humanoid body parts stitched and bolted together into a muscled brute imbued with formidable strength. Its brain is capable of simple reason, though its thoughts are no more sophisticated than those of a young child. The golem's muscle tissue responds to the power of lightning, invigorating the creature with vitality and strength. Powerful enchantments protect the golem's skin, deflecting spells and all but the most potent weapons.
A flesh golem lurches with a stiff-jointed gait, as if not in complete control of its body. Its dead flesh isn't an ideal container for an elemental spirit, which sometimes howls incoherently to vent its outrage. If the spirit breaks free of its creator's will, the golem goes berserk until calmed, or until its shell of flesh is destroyed or completely healed.
combat-strategy: Charge the moment combat starts — Multiattack Slam (two slams, 17 avg each) against the nearest squishy target, and never stop moving; this golem exists to bulldoze. Keep enemies between itself and any spellcaster, since Magic Resistance soaks attempts to stop it and its AC 9 invites (and tanks) melee. Steer the party's fire away from you: Aversion to Fire cripples your attacks and draws the whole table toward fire damage, so burn-proof your approach, fight in smoke and clutter, and punish anyone forced to attack you barehanded into Heated-Body-style reach. Lightning casters are your battery — never line up a wizard with a shock spell unless you want your HP back. Berserk activates when bloodied: if you drop below half HP and roll a 6, you become a chaotic whirlwind that can actually save you from a creator-commanded stalemate, so letting it rage near the party's backline while it's still healthy enough to survive is a real gamble worth taking. It never retreats; it fights until destroyed.

name: Flumph
languages: Understands Undercommon but can't speak; telepathy 60 ft.

traits.name: Advanced Telepathy
traits.description: The flumph perceives the content of any telepathic communication within 60 feet of it.

traits.name: Prone Deficiency
traits.description: If the flumph receives the Prone condition, roll a die. On an odd number, it has the Incapacitated condition. At the end of each of its turns, the flumph makes a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw, ending the Incapacitated condition on a success.

traits.name: Telepathic Shroud
traits.description: The flumph's thoughts can't be read by any means, and magic can't detect its location or observe it remotely.

actions.name: Tentacle
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 feet. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Acid damage.

actions.name: Stench Spray
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 10, one creature the flumph can see within 15 feet. Failure: The target is coated in a foul-smelling liquid, exudes a stench for 1d4 hours, and has the Poisoned condition while the stench lasts. Other creatures have the Poisoned condition while in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the coated target. The target can remove the stench on itself if it bathes during a Short or Long Rest.
actions.save_effect: The target is coated in a foul-smelling liquid, exudes a stench for 1d4 hours, and has the Poisoned condition while the stench lasts. Other creatures have the Poisoned condition while in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the coated target. The target can remove the stench on itself if it bathes during a Short or Long Rest.

description:
The mysterious flumphs drift through the Underdark, propelled through the air by the jets whose sound gives them their name. A flumph glows faintly, reflecting its moods in its color. Soft pink means it is amused, deep blue is sadness, green expresses curiosity, and crimson is anger.

Intelligent and Wise. Flumphs communicate telepathically. Though they resemble jellyfish, flumphs are sentient beings of great intelligence and wisdom, possessing advanced knowledge of religion, philosophy, mathematics, and countless other subjects.
Flumphs are sensitive to the emotional states of nearby creatures. If a creature's thoughts suggest goodness, a flumph seeks that creature out. When facing creatures that exude evil, a flumph flees.

Psionic Siphons. Flumphs feed by siphoning mental energy from psionic creatures, and they can be found lurking near communities of mind flayers, aboleths, githyanki, and githzerai. As passive parasites, they take only the mental energy they need, and most creatures feel no loss or discomfort from such feeding.
Consuming psionic energy reveals the thoughts and emotions of the creatures on which the flumphs feed. Since so many of those creatures are evil, flumphs are often subjected to thoughts, emotions, and hungers that sicken their pure nature. When flumphs encounter good­ hearted adventurers, they eagerly share the dark secrets they have learned in the hopes of casting down their evil sources of energy, even if doing so means they must seek out new sources of nourishment.

Flumph Society. Flumphs live in complex and organized groups called cloisters, within which each flumph has a place and purpose. These harmonious groupings have no need for leaders, since all flumphs contribute in their own way.
combat-strategy: This pacifist-leaning creature rarely fights: use Stench Spray first (15 ft., DC 10 Dex) on the loudest or most aggressive foe, coating them so their mere presence poisons everyone adjacent — a social-combat hybrid tool perfect for nonlethal encounters. Tentacle attacks (+4, 1d4+2 acid) are your only real offense and barely matter; the goal is harassment and escape, not victory. Protect the flumph at all costs: 7 HP and Prone Deficiency mean any knockdown could incapacitate it permanently on a bad roll, so keep it hovering at 30 ft. altitude out of opportunous reach. Advanced Telepathy and Telepathic Shroud make it an ideal spy — it hears all telepathic conspiracies and can't be scryed — so its best 'combat strategy' is being nowhere near the fight, leaking secrets instead. Flee the instant anyone draws a weapon with hostile intent; this is a messenger, not a monster.

name: Flying Snake

traits.name: Flyby
traits.description: The snake doesn't provoke an Opportunity Attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage plus 5 (2d4) Poison damage.

description: A flying snake is a brightly colored, winged serpent found in remote jungles. Tribespeople and cultists sometimes domesticate flying snakes to serve as messengers that deliver scrolls wrapped in their coils.
combat-strategy: Use Flyby hit-and-run: fly in from any direction, Bite once, and circle out at 60 ft. without ever provoking an opportunity attack — melee characters simply cannot punish you. Target the pack's lowest-HP or concentration-holding caster; the 2d4 poison can finish an already-wounded hero, and Tiny size plus 14 AC makes it hard to spare the attack to swat. Attack from above and behind, at odd angles where reach weapons can't follow, and swarm one at a time so each gets its free pass. Pack tactics multiply this: five snakes diving in sequence will whittle a mid-level party's HP through sheer unanswerable chip damage. Retreat into dense underbrush, cracks, or water (it swims 30 ft.) the moment a fireball-capable caster starts aiming — one splash weapon ends it — and disperse so a single AoE doesn't kill multiple snakes.

name: Flying Sword

actions.name: Longsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) slashing damage.

traits.name: Antimagic Susceptibility
traits.description: The sword is incapacitated while in the area of an antimagic field. If targeted by dispel magic, the sword must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against the caster's spell save DC or fall unconscious for 1 minute.

traits.name: False Appearance
traits.description: While the sword remains motionless and isn't flying, it is indistinguishable from a normal sword.

description: A flying sword dances through the air, fighting with the confidence of a warrior that can't be injured. Swords are the most common weapons animated with magic. Axes, clubs, daggers, maces, spears, and even self­ loading crossbows are also known to exist in animated object form.
combat-strategy: Ambush from stillness: wait motionless on a rack, altar, or scabbard where False Appearance hides it, then rise and strike the first creature that walks past. Fly 50 ft. hover makes it pure mobility — dive in with Longsword, hover out of reach, and re-dive, since few creatures can punish a hovering target at height. Immunities to poison, psychic, and most conditions mean charm and enervation do nothing, and its blindsight 60 ft. lets it fight in total darkness or behind smoke where the party is blind. Prioritize lone stragglers and squishies; its +3, 1d8+1 hits are modest, so numbers and ambush beats fair fights — set two or three in an ambush from different angles. If antimagic field or dispel magic hits the party's arsenal, expect suppression: fall back to hovering at maximum height and keep attacking with numbers until a caster is dealt with, otherwise fight until destroyed since it has no self-preservation.

name: Fomorian

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The fomorian makes two Stone Club attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Warping Hex if available.

actions.name: Stone Club
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 15 ft. Hit: 24 (4d8 + 6) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Warping Hex
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 16, one creature the fomorian can see within 120 feet. Failure: 21 (6d6) Psychic damage, and the target gains 1 Exhaustion level. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: The target gains 1 Exhaustion level.

flavor_text:
All-Father Annam banished his son, Karontor, for Karontor's part in the fomorian assault on the Feywild. That day, the ordning—the hierarchy of the giants and their gods—changed forever, and the fomorians were part of it no more.
—Bigby
description:
The most hideous and wicked of all giantkind are the godless fomorians, whose deformed bodies reflect their vile demeanors. Some have facial features randomly distributed around their misshapen, warty heads. Others have limbs of grossly different sizes and shapes, or emit terrible howls each time they draw breath through misshapen mouths. Their wretched appearance rarely evokes sympathy, however, for the fomorians brought their doom upon themselves with the evil that rules their hearts and minds.

Fey Curse. The elves remember when the fomorians were among the most handsome of races, possessed of brilliant minds and unrivaled magical ability. That physical perfection did not extend to their hearts, however, as a lust for magic and power consumed them.
The fomorians sought to conquer the Feywild and enslave its inhabitants, claiming those creatures' magic for themselves. When the fey united to defend their realm, the fomorians fought them and were subjected to a terrible curse.
One by one, the giants fell as their bodies were warped to reflect the evil in their hearts. Stripped of their grace and magical power, the wretched horrors fled from the light, delving deep beneath the world to nurse their hatred. Cursing their fate, they have ever after plotted vengeance against the fey that wronged them.

Giants of the Underdark. The fomorians dwell in eerily beautiful caverns in the Underdark, rarely venturing to the surface. Their lairs feature abundant access to water, fish, and mushroom forests, as well as to the creatures whose slave labor keeps the fomorians fed. When those slaves can no longer toil, they are slain and devoured. Wickedness and depravity are the cornerstones of fomorian society, in which the strongest and cruelest giants rule. Fomorians mark their territories with the corpses of their enemies, painting their cavern walls with blood or stitching together limbs and body parts to make mockeries of the creatures they have killed.

Ruined Flesh, Evil Minds. The deformities visited on the fomorians prevent them from hurling rocks like their giant kin, or wearing anything more than scraps of cloth. However, the grotesque positioning of their eyes, noses, and ears gives fomorians keen perceptive abilities, making it hard to surprise or ambush them.
The greed and evil of the fomorians lies at the heart of their degeneration and fall, and continues to plague them. Fomorians make alliances with other creatures when it suits them, but they are disloyal by nature and betray their allies on a whim.

Curse of the Evil Eye. Fomorians can pass their curse onto others using a power called the evil eye-a last vestige of the giants' once-remarkable spellcasting ability. A creature cursed by a fomorian's evil eye is magically twisted and deformed, gaining a glimpse into the pain and malice that has consumed this evil race.
combat-strategy: Open from stealth or darkness — 120 ft. darkvision, +3 Stealth on a Huge body, and Perception +18 make the fomorian a nightmare that strikes unannounced. Lead with Warping Hex on the wisdom-weak spellcaster or the party's exhaustion-sensitive frontrunner: 21 psychic plus a level of Exhaustion is a game-ending tax at DC 16. Then Multiattack with Stone Club (15 ft. reach, average 24 bludgeoning) to keep everyone outside their own reach; the extra reach is the whole melee identity, so never let foes claim it for free. Swap one club swing for Warping Hex on a fresh target each round to stack Exhaustion — a target at one level of Exhaustion who keeps failing gets dragged toward the unreachable second level. Use ruined towers, stone quarries, and night terrain: throw rubble for cover, fight in tunnels where the party can't flank. If reduced to roughly 60 HP with its hex spent, retreat into deeper darkness to return another night — fomorians remember insults.

name: Frog

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The frog can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Standing Leap
traits.description: The frog's Long Jump is up to 10 feet and its High Jump is up to 5 feet with or without a running start.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage.

description: A frog has no effective attacks. It feeds on small insects and typically dwells near water, in trees, or underground. The frog's statistics can also be used to represent a toad.
combat-strategy: A frog is scenery that occasionally bites. In the rare case it fights, Bite (+3, 1 damage) is token chip damage — hop into tall grass or water where its Stealth +3 and amphibious nature make it invisible, then lunge at an ankle. Standing Leap lets it clear 10 ft. gaps or drop onto a target from a rock or lily pad for surprise positioning. Honestly, its tactical role is misdirection: a croaking chorus of frogs masks the approach of something worse, or a familiar spy flinging itself off a cliff to escape a dungeon. It flees at the first footstep, first shadow, first anything — that is the authentic frog strategy.

name: Frost Giant

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The giant makes two attacks, using Frost Axe or Great Bow in any combination.

actions.name: Frost Axe
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 10 ft. Hit: 19 (2d12 + 6) Slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) Cold damage.

actions.name: Great Bow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +9, range 150/600 ft. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Cold damage, and the target's Speed decreases by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target's Speed decreases by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

bonus_actions.name: War Cry
bonus_actions.description: The giant or one creature of its choice that can see or hear it gains 16 (2d10 + 5) Temporary Hit Points and has Advantage on attack rolls until the start of the giant's next turn.

description:
Gigantic reavers from the freezing lands beyond civilization, frost giants are fierce, hardy warriors that survive on the spoils of their raids and pillaging. They respect only brute strength and skill in battle, demonstrating both with their scars and the grisly trophies they take from their enemies.

Hearts of Ice. Frost giants are creatures of ice and snow. Their hair and beards are pale white or light blue, matted with frost and clattering with icicles. Their flesh is as blue as glacial ice.
Frost giants dwell in high peaks and glacial rifts where the sun hides its golden head by winter. Crops don't grow in their frozen homelands, and they keep little livestock beyond what they capture in their raids against civilized lands. They hunt the wild game of the tundra and mountains but don't cook it, since meat from a fresh kill tastes sufficiently hot to their palate.

Reavers of the Storm. The war horns of the frost giants howl as they march from their ice fortresses and glacial rifts amid the howling blizzard. When that storm clears, villages and steadings lay in ruins, ravens descending to feed on the corpses of any creatures foolish or unlucky enough to stand in the giants' path.
Inns and taverns suffer the brunt of the damage, their cellars gutted and their casks of ale and mead gone. Smithies are likewise toppled, their iron and steel claimed. Curiously undisturbed are the houses of moneylenders and wealthy citizens, for the reavers have little use for coins or baubles. Frost giants prize gems and jewelry large enough to be worn and noticed. However, even those treasures are most often saved for trading opportunities with other giants more adept at crafting metal weapons and armor.

Rulers by Might. Frost giants respect brute strength above all else, and a frost giant's place in the ordning depends on evidence of physical might, such as superior musculature, scars from battles of renown, or trophies fashioned from the bodies of slain enemies. Tasks such as hunting, childrearing, and crafting are given to giants based on their physical strength and hardiness.
When frost giants of different clans meet and their status is unclear, they wrestle for dominance. Such meetings might resemble festivals where giants cheer on their champions, making bold boasts and challenges. At other times, the informal ceremony can become a chaotic free-for-all where both clans rush into a melee that fells trees, shatters the ice on frozen lakes, and causes avalanches on the snowy mountainsides.

Make War, Not Goods. Though frost giants consider the menial crafting of goods beneath them, carving and leatherwork are valued skills. They make their clothing from the skins and bones of beasts, and carve bone or ivory into jewelry and the handles of weapons and tools. They reuse the weapons and armor of their smaller foes' stringing shields into scale armor and lashing sword blades to wooden hafts to make giant-sized spears. The greatest battle trophies come from conquered dragons, and the greatest frost giant jarls wear armor of dragon scales or wield picks and mauls made of a dragon's teeth or claws.
combat-strategy: Open with a War Cry on the toughest allied giant or the champion bruiser — 16 temp HP plus Advantage on attacks turns any ally into a duelist and costs only a bonus action. Then Multiattack: Great Bow volleys (150/600 ft., plus 10 ft. slow) on the enemy backline to shred formation and freeze stragglers, or Frost Axe in melee against whoever lingers in its 10 ft. reach. The slow from Great Bow is the control lever: kiting casters cannot outrun a 40 ft. giant, so shoot the runner, then walk them down next round. Fight on snow, ice, and frozen lakes where you tower over footing that already troubles the party; shove into freezing water for double jeopardy. Hit-and-run against weaker foes — 40 ft. speed lets you disengage, volley, and re-engage — and only retreat to the longhouse when the party's damage output clearly exceeds your 149 HP pool, ideally covered by bow fire on the way back.

name: Galeb Duhr

speed.walk: 15 ft. (30 ft. when rolling, 60 ft. rolling downhill)

actions.name: Avalanche Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature and the galeb duhr moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 7 (2d6) Bludgeoning damage and has the Prone condition.

conditional_damage.condition: moved 20+ feet straight toward target immediately before the hit

actions.name: Animate Boulders
actions.description: The galeb duhr magically animates one or two boulders it can see within 60 feet of itself. Each boulder uses the Galeb Duhr stat block, except it has Intelligence and Charisma scores of 1 and lacks this action. The boulder takes its turn immediately after the galeb duhr on the same Initiative count, and it obeys the galeb duhr. A boulder remains animate for 1 minute or until it or the galeb duhr dies.

combat-strategy: Open by animating two boulders immediately — Animate Boulders turns a lone golem into a triple threat on turn one, and the animated rocks act on the same initiative right after you, so the party faces three 123-HP walls at once. Use Avalanche Slam after a 20 ft. charge for the extra 2d6 and knockdown; on open ground that means rolling downhill (60 ft.) for free distance before the slam lands. Boulder minions should flank and pin opponents, denying flanking while you concentrate fire on whoever is trapped between them. Terrain is everything: rocky hillsides, quarries, and rubble fields let you animate endless replacement boulders, while soft sand or deep snow slows your 15 ft. walk to a crawl. Keep animating as boulders fall — one per round minimum — and bully the battlefield's geography rather than chasing. As the battle goes against you, pull back toward more rock to restock minions; only the parent dying ends the threat, so keep yourself behind your stone children.

name: Galib Duhr

speed.walk: 15 ft. (30 ft. when rolling, 60 ft. rolling downhil1)

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Animate Boulders
actions.description: The galeb duhr magically animates up to two boulders it can see within 60 feet of it. A boulder has statistics like those of a galeb duhr, except it has Intelligence 1 and Charisma 1, it can't be charmed or frightened, and it lacks this action. The galeb duhr maintains concentration, up to 1 minute (as if concentrating on a spell).

traits.name: False Appearance
traits.description: While the galeb duhr remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal boulder.

traits.name: Rolling Charge
traits.description: If the galeb duhr rolls at least 20 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a slam attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 16 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

description:
The galeb duhr is a boulder-like creature with stumpy appendages that act as arms and legs. It has the ability to animate the rocks and boulders around it, and is thus usually encountered in rocky terrain.
Powerful magic allows a spellcaster to summon a galeb duhr from the Plane of Earth. Some galeb duhr also form naturally in places touched by that plane. The galeb duhr is imbued with greater intelligence than most elementals, allowing it to better assess threats and to communicate with creatures entering its guarded area.

Stone Guardian. A galeb duhr doesn't age or require sustenance, making it an excellent sentinel. A powerful druid might charge a galeb duhr with protecting a stone circle or sacred hilltop. Another galeb duhr might be created to guard an underground tomb or a wizard's tower. When it chooses to, the galeb duhr can make itself look like an ordinary boulder, remaining perfectly still for years at a time.
A galeb duhr is permanently bound to the Material Plane, so that when it dies, it doesn't return to the Plane of Earth. It has an excellent memory and is more than happy to share information regarding its environment with creatures it doesn't regard as threats.

Stone Connection. A galeb duhr can become one with the earth around it, allowing it to imbue nearby rocks and boulders with a semblance of life. The galeb duhr uses its animated boulders to frighten away interlopers and defend whatever it has been charged to protect. When it needs to move close to those intruders, it presses its limbs tight to its body and rolls forward at a furious pace.
combat-strategy: Ambush from False Appearance: sit motionless as a 'boulder' until the party passes, then explode upright with a Rolling Charge slam (+7, plus 2d6 and a DC 16 Str knockdown) on the nearest target before they can form up. Immediately Animate Boulders (concentration, 1 minute) to add up to two minion boulders — they fight like you minus the animation trick and can't be charmed or frightened, so they are pure bodies to hold corridors. Rolling Charge demands straight-line 20 ft. runs: use slopes for 60 ft. plunging charges and knock foes down toward cliffs, pits, or allied monsters. Immunities to poison and exhaustion plus resistance to mundane weapons make the party's attrition tools useless against you — win by damage and knockdowns instead. Position minions to trap knocked-prone targets while you reposition for the next charge, maintaining concentration at all costs since losing it thins your army to one. Retreat uphill toward rocky scree where you can vanish back into False Appearance and rest one round, then charge again; if boulders run out and you're bloodied, melt into the landscape.

name: Gargoyle

traits.name: Flyby
traits.description: The gargoyle doesn't provoke an Opportunity Attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The gargoyle makes two Claw attacks.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) Slashing damage.

flavor_text:
Where evil passes in the Elemental Plane of Earth, it stains the rock and spoils the soil. Malice vanishes amid other elements, but in the dismal dark, the wicked shape it into nightmares.
—Tiv, scholar of the Elemental Planes
description:
The inanimate gargoyles that perch atop great buildings are inspired by these malevolent creatures of elemental earth that resemble grotesque, fiendish statues. A gargoyle lurks among masonry and ruins, as still as any stone sculpture, and delights in the terror it creates when it breaks from its suspended pose, as well as the pain it inflicts on its victims.

Animate Stone. Gargoyles cling to rocky cliffs and mountains, or roost on ledges in underground caves. They haunt city rooftops, perching vulture-like among the high stone arches and buttresses of castles and cathedrals, and they can hold themselves so still that they appear inanimate. Able to maintain this state for years, a gargoyle makes an ideal sentry.

Deadly Reputation. Gargoyles have a reputation for cruelty. Statues carved into the likenesses of gargoyles appear in the architecture of countless cultures to frighten away trespassers. Although such sculptures are only decorative, real gargoyles can hide among them to ambush unsuspecting victims. A gargoyle might alleviate the tedium of its watch by catching and tormenting birds or rodents, but its long wait only increases its craving for harming sentient creatures.

Cruel Servants. Gargoyles are easily inspired by the cunning of an intelligent master. They enjoy simple tasks such as guarding a master's home, torturing and killing interlopers, and anything else that involves minimum effort and maximum pain and carnage.
Gargoyles sometimes serve demons for their propensity for wanton chaos and destruction. Powerful spellcasters can also easily enlist gargoyle guardians to keep watch over their gates and walls. Gargoyles have the patience and fortitude of stone, and will serve even the cruelest master for years without complaint.

Elemental Nature. A gargoyle doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Perch on rooftops, buttresses, and arches invisible in the dark — +4 Stealth and 60 ft. fly let you ambush from a height no one watches. Dive with Flyby (no opportunity attacks), Multiattack two Claws (average 14 slashing) on a straggler or caster, then loop back up to safety; the fly-claw-hover cycle is the whole playbook. Fight at night or in unlit dungeons where the party lacks light sources and you own the 60 ft. darkvision edge. Pick off the archer or wizard with repeated dive passes — two passes per round of claw damage from unreachable altitude wins attrition fights against parties without a ranged answer. 67 HP is respectable but not infinite: once below roughly 25 HP, disengage to the spire, heal the fight by refusing it, and dive again only when a hero separates from the group. If the party brings fly-speed pursuers or a mage slinger, relocate the ambush to another rooftop line.

name: Gas Spore

actions.name: Touch
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: + 0 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 1 poison damage, and the creature must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or become infected with the disease described in the Death Burst trait.
actions.save_effect: The target becomes infected with the disease described in the Death Burst trait.

traits.name: Death Burst
traits.description: The gas spore explodes when it drops to 0 hit points. Each creature within 20 feet of it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 10 (3d6) poison damage and become infected with a disease on a failed save. Creatures immune to the poisoned condition are immune to this disease. Spores invade an infected creature's system, killing the creature in a number ofhours equal to 1dl2 + the creature's Constitution score, unless the disease is removed. In half that time, the creature becomes poisoned for the rest ofthe duration. After the creature dies, it sprouts 2d4 Tiny gas spores that grow to full size in 7 days.

traits.name: Eerie Resemblance
traits.description: The gas spore resembles a beholder. A creature that can see the gas spore can discern its true nature with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Nature) check.

description:
The first gas spores are thought to have been spawned from dead beholders, whose moldering corpses fed a parasitic fungus with aberrant magic. Having long since adapted into a unique plant creature, a gas spore grows quickly and purposefully out of any corpse, creating a malevolent-looking mockery of the most feared denizen of the Underdark.

Eye Tyrant's Form. A gas spore is a spherical, balloon-like fungus that resembles a beholder from a distance, though its true nature becomes increasingly obvious as one approaches it. The monster possesses a blind central "eye" and rhizome growths sprouting from its upper surface, superficially resembling a beholder's eyestalks.

Death Burst. A gas spore is a hollow shell filled with a lighter-than-air gas that enables it to float as a beholder does. Piercing the shell with even the weakest attack causes the creature to burst apart, releasing a cloud of deadly spores. A creature that inhales the spores becomes host to them, and is often dead within a day. Its corpse then becomes the spawning ground from which new gas spores arise.

Beholder Memories. A gas spore that sprouts from a beholder's corpse sometimes carries within it memories of its deceased parent. When the gas spore explodes, its deadly spores cast those memories adrift. Any creature that inhales the spores and survives inherits one or more of the beholder's fragmented memories, and might gain useful information about the beholder's former lair and other nearby places and creatures of interest.
combat-strategy: Float toward the party disguised as a... beholder? Eerie Resemblance fools the unprepared; DC 15 Nature is the only warning before this hoverer drifts in. The entire strategy is dying on your terms: Touch (DC 10 Con or the death disease) or simply let yourself be hit — Death Burst detonates at 0 HP with a DC 15 Con or 3d6 poison plus the same killing disease. Drift into the tightest, most enclosed cluster of heroes — corridors, chambers, stairwells — and detonate there, where the 20 ft. burst cannot be dodged by foot since you hover 10 ft. into any room. The lethal disease (death in 1d12+Con hours, poisoned at half) turns a 'cleared' room into a ticking time bomb and the corpses into spore gardens. Parties immune to poison (paladins, constructs) should be ignored; focus on flesh. Nothing to retreat — you walk/fly forward at 10 ft. and death is the punchline.

name: Gas Spore Fungus

traits.name: Death Burst
traits.description: The gas spore bursts when it dies. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 10, each creature in a 20-foot Emanation originating from the gas spore. Failure: The target takes 10 (3d6) Poison damage and has the Poisoned condition for 1d12 hours. Unless the Poisoned condition is removed, the target dies at the end of that time and sprouts 2d4 Tiny Gas Spore Fungi (each with 1 Hit Point). After 2d6 days, they become Large and have 13 Hit Points.

actions.name: Tendril
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +0, reach 5 ft. Hit: 3 (1d6) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn.

combat-strategy: Hover forward at 10 ft. and Touch (Tendril) to inflict Poisoned and chip 1d6; the real payload is Death Burst — DC 10 Con or 3d6 poison plus a Poisoned condition that kills in 1d12 hours and sprouts 2d4 new fungi from the corpse. Because the burst save is only DC 10 and 20 ft. wide, suicide into a doorway or camp where the party rests or eats maximizes long-term carnage. Set the ambush where corpses can't be burned or consecrated — the 2d6-day maturation from Tiny (1 HP) to Large (13 HP) turns a buried casualty into a fresh wave. Use the 5 ft. walk and 10 ft. hover to drift out of reach between Tendril attempts; AC 8 and 13 HP guarantee a quick death, so the goal is one Touch plus detonation in the worst possible spot. Focus on the weakest Constitution members, since low-Con heroes fail DC 10 saves routinely. There is no retreat — the fungus wants to infect.

name: Gazer

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1 piercing damage.

actions.name: Eye Rays
actions.description: The gazer shoots two of the following magical eye rays at random (reroll duplicates), choosing one or two targets it can see within 60 feet of it:
actions.save_effect: Dazing Ray: charmed condition (speed is halved; disadvantage on attack rolls). Fear Ray: frightened condition. Frost Ray: 10 (3d6) Cold damage, zero on a successful save. Telekinetic Ray: Medium or smaller target moved up to 30 feet directly away.

rays.name: Dazing Ray
rays.duration_note: Charmed until the start of the gazer's next turn (rounds:2 clock); speed is halved (speed_half te); disadvantage on attack rolls while charmed is GM-enforced (no NPC attack-disadvantage consumer).
rays.save_effect: The target is charmed until the start of the gazer's next turn. While charmed, the target's speed is halved and it has disadvantage on attack rolls. Success: none — the ray deals no damage.

rays.name: Fear Ray
rays.duration_note: Frightened until the start of the gazer's next turn (rounds:2 clock).
rays.save_effect: The target is frightened until the start of the gazer's next turn. Success: none — the ray deals no damage.

rays.name: Frost Ray
rays.duration_note: 3d6 Cold damage on a failed save only — RAW carries no half-on-success clause (dc_success:"none").
rays.save_effect: The target takes 10 (3d6) Cold damage. Success: none — the ray deals no damage.

rays.name: Telekinetic Ray
rays.duration_note: Medium or smaller target moved up to 30 feet directly away from the gazer (telekinetic_movement te, rounds:2 clock); grid token placement and fine object control are GM-enforced (no grid-move consumer).
rays.save_effect: If the target is Medium or smaller, it is moved up to 30 feet directly away from the gazer. If the target is an object weighing 10 pounds or less not being worn or carried, the gazer moves it up to 30 feet in any direction. Success: none — the target is not moved.

actions.name: 1. Dazing Ray
actions.description: The target creature must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed until the start of the gazer's next turn.  While the target is charmed in this way, its speed is halved, and it has disadvantage on attack rolls.
actions.save_effect: The target is charmed until the start of the gazer's next turn. While charmed, the target's speed is halved and it has disadvantage on attack rolls.

actions.name: 2. Fear Ray
actions.description: The targeted creature must suceed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened until the start of the gazer's next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target is frightened until the start of the gazer's next turn.

actions.name: 3. Frost Ray
actions.description: The targeted creature must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or take 10 (3d6) cold damage.
actions.save_effect: The target takes 10 (3d6) Cold damage.

actions.name: 4. Telekinetic Ray
actions.description: If the target is a creature that is Medium or smaller, it must succeed on a DC 12 Strength saving throw or be moved up to 30 feet directly away from the gazer. If the target is an object weighting 10 pounds or less that isn't being worn or carried, the gazer moves it up to 30 feet in any direction. The gazer can also exert fine control on ovjects with this ray, such as manipulating a simple tool or opening a container.
actions.save_effect: If the target is Medium or smaller, it is moved up to 30 feet directly away from the gazer. If the target is an object weighing 10 pounds or less not being worn or carried, the gazer moves it up to 30 feet in any direction. The gazer can also exert fine control on objects, such as manipulating a simple tool or opening a container.

traits.name: Agressive
traits.description: As a bonus action, the gazer can move up to its speed toward a hostile creature that it can see.

traits.name: Mimicry
traits.description: The gazer can mimic simple sounds of speech it has heard, in any language. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful DC 10 Wisdom (In· sight) check.

description:
A gazer is a tiny manifestation of a beholder's dreams. It resembles the beholder who dreamed it into existence, but its body is only 8 inches wide, and it has only four eyestalks.
