It follows its creator like a devoted, aggressive puppy, and sometimes small packs of these creatures patrol their master's lair for vermin to kill and lone creatures to harass.

Nuisance Pet. A gazer can't speak any languages but can approximate mimicking words and sentences in a high-pitched, mocking manner. Beholders find gazers amusing and tolerate their presence like spoiled pets. A gazer can't be tamed by anyone but its creator, except through the use of magic or by bonding with a spell- caster (see sidebar). Some beholders with wizard min- ions insist they take a gazer as a familiar because they can see through the eyes of these creatures.

Aggressive Vermin-Eater. A wild gazer (one living separately from a beholder) is territorial, eats bugs and small animals, and is known for playing with its food. A lone gazer avoids picking fights with creatures that are Medium or larger, but a pack of them might take on larger prey. A gazer might follow humanoids in its territory, noisily mimicking their speech and generally being a nuisance, until they leave the area, but it flees if confronted by something it can't kill.
combat-strategy: Open with Eye Rays at 60 ft. — they're random, but Dazing Ray (charmed, halved speed, Disadvantage) and Fear Ray on a martial hero make the first round memorable, and Telekinetic Ray can hurl a Medium or smaller foe 30 ft. away, off a ledge, or into the jaws of an ally. Hover high (Tiny, 13 AC, Stealth +5, darkvision) where melee can't reach and cantrips must be aimed upward. Aggressive bonus action closes the gap when a target tries to retreat, or pushes you toward cover mid-fight. Fear Ray pairs brutally with allies: a frightened target fleeing is driven straight into an ambush line, and Telekinetic Ray repositions enemies into hazards you control. 13 HP means the moment a martial character takes flight or aims a ranged weapon, you should flee — use Aggressive to break to cover, Mimicry to fake a distant call and misdirect pursuit, and vanish down a crack.

name: Gelatinous Cube

traits.name: Ooze Cube
traits.description: The cube fills its entire space and is transparent. Other creatures can enter that space, but a creature that does so is subjected to the cube's Engulf and has Disadvantage on the saving throw. Creatures inside the cube have Total Cover, and the cube can hold one Large creature or up to four Medium or Small creatures inside itself at a time. As an action, a creature within 5 feet of the cube can pull a creature or an object out of the cube by succeeding on a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check, and the puller takes 10 (3d6) Acid damage.

traits.name: Transparent
traits.description: Even when the cube is in plain sight, a creature must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check to notice the cube if the creature hasn't witnessed the cube move or otherwise act.

actions.name: Pseudopod
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (3d6 + 2) Acid damage.

actions.name: Engulf
actions.description: The cube moves up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. The cube can move through the spaces of Large or smaller creatures if it has room inside itself to contain them (see the Ooze Cube trait). Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature whose space the cube enters for the first time during this move. Failure: 10 (3d6) Acid damage, and the target is engulfed. An engulfed target is suffocating, can't cast spells with a Verbal component, has the Restrained condition, and takes 10 (3d6) Acid damage at the start of each of the cube's turns. When the cube moves, the engulfed target moves with it. An engulfed target can try to escape by taking an action to make a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check. On a successful check, the target escapes and enters the nearest unoccupied space. Success: Half damage, and the target moves to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the cube. If there is no unoccupied space, the target fails the save instead.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target is engulfed. An engulfed target is suffocating, can't cast spells with a Verbal component, has the Restrained condition, and takes 10 (3d6) Acid damage at the start of each of the cube's turns. When the cube moves, the engulfed target moves with it. An engulfed target can try to escape by taking an action to make a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check. On a successful check, the target escapes and enters the nearest unoccupied space. Success: Half damage, and the target moves to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the cube. If there is no unoccupied space, the target fails the save instead.

description:
Gelatinous cubes scour dungeon passages in silent, predictable patterns, leaving perfectly clean paths in their wake. They consume living tissue while leaving bones and other materials undissolved.
A gelatinous cube is all but transparent, making it hard to spot until it attacks. A cube that is well fed can be easier to spot, since its victims' bones, coins, and other objects can be seen suspended inside the creature.
combat-strategy: Attack from transparency: DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) means most parties walk straight into you in a corridor. Move Engulf (no opportunity attacks) down the tunnel and swallow the largest possible cluster of Medium creatures — engulfed foes are Restrained, suffocating, unable to speak spells, and take 3d6 acid every turn. Fill the corridor width so the only counters are Athletics checks from allies outside you, then drag victims deeper as you move. Target the caster first: no Verbal components means your swallowed wizard is disarmed by definition. 15 ft. walk is the weakness — the party's answer is hit-and-run and pulled allies, so hunt in tight passages where kiting is impossible and corner them at junctions. As HP drops toward 30, prioritize holding your swallowed prey rather than chasing new ones; acid damage inside you finishes the fight even if you stop moving, and the party must split actions between pulling and killing.

name: Ghast

traits.name: Stench
traits.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 10, any creature that starts its turn in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the ghast. Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition until the start of its next turn. Success: The target is immune to this ghast's Stench for 24 hours.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Slashing damage. If the target is a non-Undead creature, it is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 10. Failure: The target has the Paralyzed condition until the end of its next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Paralyzed condition until the end of its next turn.

description: Orcus sometimes infuses a ghoul with a stronger dose of abyssal energy, making a ghast. Whereas ghouls are little more than savage beasts, a ghast is cunning and can inspire a pack of ghouls to follow its commands.
combat-strategy: Stench (DC 10 Con, 5 ft., re-stink every turn) is your opening move: close to melee and the front line is Poisoned every round, and that DC 10 makes rogues and wizards fail constantly. Claw (+5) is the money action — a DC 10 Con save or Paralyzed for a round lets the pack strip and kill any non-undead who fails. Bite adds 9 necrotic on top, so Multiattack Claw+Bite on a separated target, then pile on: paralyzed victims are auto-hit by everyone. Focus whoever holds concentration or the healing cantrips, since Stench is the metronome and paralysis the finisher. 36 HP means you fall fast to concentrated fire — never engage the whole party head-on: pick off the tail of the marching order in crypt darkness, then retreat into narrow passages between waves. Undead allies are immune to your paralysis, so coordinate the swarm around it.

name: Ghast Gravecaller

traits.name: Stench
traits.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, any creature that starts its turn in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the ghast. Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition until the start of its next turn. Success: The target is immune to this ghast's Stench for 24 hours.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The ghast makes two Horrific Necrosis attacks. It can replace one attack with a Claw attack.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) Slashing damage. If the target isn't an Undead, it has the Paralyzed condition until the end of its next turn.

actions.name: Horrific Necrosis
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Necrotic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The ghast casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability: At Will: Speak with Dead, Thaumaturgy

combat-strategy: Horrific Necrosis is the opener: 120 ft. range, +7 to hit, 15 necrotic plus Frightened until end of the target's next turn — snipe the party's concentrated healer or caster from safety every round. Multiattack two Necrosis rays to frighten two foes at once, then wade in only after the fear splits their formation; replace one with Claw, which paralyzes any non-undead it hits with no save, to delete a trapped target. Stench (DC 13) poisons anyone staying within 5 ft., so the creature that 'bravely' closes is debuffed for free. Use Speak with Dead as interrogation and psychological warfare between encounters — dead witnesses talk, which is its own kind of tactical control. Command the undead swarm from the back rank: Necrosis from 120 ft. frightens, paralyzed thralls advance, and gravecaller moves to the next firing lane. Retreat at roughly 40 HP into the deepest tomb, raising what dead there is, and speak to the fallen to plan the next ambush.

name: Ghost

traits.name: Ethereal Sight
traits.description: The ghost can see 60 feet into the Ethereal Plane when it is on the Material Plane.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.description: The ghost can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The ghost makes two Withering Touch attacks.

actions.name: Withering Touch
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 19 (3d10 + 3) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Ethereality
actions.description: The ghost casts the Ethereality spell, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability. The ghost is visible on the Material Plane while on the Border Ethereal and vice versa, but it can't affect or be affected by anything on the other plane.

actions.name: Horrific Visage
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 60-foot Cone that can see the ghost and isn't an Undead. Failure: 10 (2d6 + 3) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the start of the ghost's next turn. Success: The target is immune to this ghost's Horrific Visage for 24 hours.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Frightened condition until the start of the ghost's next turn.
actions.immunity: Success: The target is immune to this ghost's Horrific Visage for 24 hours.

actions.name: Possession
actions.description: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 13, one Humanoid the ghost can see within 5 feet. Failure: The target is possessed by the ghost; the ghost disappears, and the target has the Incapacitated condition and loses control of its body. The ghost now controls the body, but the target retains awareness. The ghost can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, except ones that specifically target Undead. The ghost's game statistics are the same, except it uses the possessed target's Speed, as well as the target's Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution modifiers. The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 Hit Points or the ghost leaves as a Bonus Action. When the possession ends, the ghost appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target, and the target is immune to this ghost's Possession for 24 hours. Success: The target is immune to this ghost's Possession for 24 hours.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target is possessed by the ghost; the ghost disappears, and the target has the Incapacitated condition and loses control of its body. The ghost now controls the body, but the target retains awareness. The ghost can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, except ones that specifically target Undead. The ghost's game statistics are the same, except it uses the possessed target's Speed, as well as the target's Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution modifiers. The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 Hit Points or the ghost leaves as a Bonus Action. When the possession ends, the ghost appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target, and the target is immune to this ghost's Possession for 24 hours. Success: The target is immune to this ghost's Possession for 24 hours.

description:
A ghost is the soul of a once-living creature, bound to haunt a specific location, creature, or object that held significance to it in its life.

Unfinished Business. A ghost yearns to complete some unresolved task from its life. It might seek to avenge its own death, fulfill an oath, or relay a message to a loved one. A ghost might not realize that it has died and continue the everyday routine of its life. Others are driven by wickedness or spite, as with a ghost that refuses to rest until every member of a certain family or organization is dead.
The surest way to rid an area of a ghost is to resolve its unfinished business. A ghost can be destroyed more easily by invoking a weakness tied to its former life. The ghost of a person tortured to death might be killed again by the implements of that torture. The ghost of a gardener might become more vulnerable when exposed to a potent floral fragrance.

Ghostly Manifestations. Sensations of profound sadness, loneliness, and unfulfilled yearning emanate from places where ghostly hauntings occur. Strange sounds or unnatural silences create an unsettling atmosphere. Cold spots settle in rooms that have roaring fires. A choking stench might seep into the area, inanimate objects might move of their own accord, and corpses might rise from the grave. The ghost has no control over these manifestations; they simply occur.

Undead Nature. A ghost doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Open with Horrific Visage (60 ft. cone, DC 13 Wis) on any clustered group — 2d6+3 psychic plus Frightened — then Ethereality to vanish to the Border Ethereal where nothing can touch you while you watch through walls. Return to Material for Multiattack Withering Touch (two x 19 necrotic) on a panicked or isolated hero, then blink away again; the ethereal fade is the ghost's get-out-of-jail card on every lethal round. Possession is the checkmate move: DC 13 Charisma on a Humanoid within 5 ft., then the ghost is invulnerable (except vs undead-targeting effects) while piloting a full-HP party member, forcing the heroes to attack their own friend. Use Incorporeal Movement to walk through locked doors, closed portcullises, and the party's own shield wall to reach the backline. Fight at night, in crypts, and in fog where fear stacks; never start the fight if outnumbered and can watch first. When the body is spent, drain into the Ethereal and return later — ghosts are patient; the unfinished business is the campaign, not the fight.

name: Ghoul

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The ghoul makes two Bite attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Slashing damage. If the target is a creature that isn't an Undead or elf, it is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 10. Failure: The target has the Paralyzed condition until the end of its next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Paralyzed condition until the end of its next turn.

description:
Ghouls roam the night i n packs, driven by a n insatiable hunger for humanoid flesh.

Devourers of Flesh. Like maggots or carrion beetles, ghouls thrive in places rank with decay and death. A ghoul haunts a place where it can gorge on dead flesh and decomposing organs. When it can't feed on the dead, it pursues living creatures and attempts to make corpses of them. Though they gain no nourishment from the corpses they devour, ghouls are driven by an unending hunger that compels them to consume. A ghoul's undead flesh never rots, and this monster can persist in a crypt or tomb for untold ages without feeding.

Abyssal Origins. Ghouls trace their origins to the Abyss. Doresain, the first of their kind, was an elf worshiper of Orcus. Turning against his own people, he feasted on humanoid flesh to honor the Demon Prince of Undeath. As a reward for his service, Orcus transformed Doresain into the first ghoul. Doresain served Orcus faithfully in the Abyss, creating ghouls from the demon lord's other servants until an incursion by Yeenoghu, the demonic Gnoll Lord, robbed Doresain of his abyssal domain. When Orcus would not intervene on his behalf, Doresain turned to the elf gods for salvation, and they took pity on him and helped him escape certain destruction. Since then, elves have been immune to the ghouls' paralytic touch.
combat-strategy: Swarm and claw: Claw (+4) forces a DC 10 Con save or Paralyzed for non-elves, non-undead, and DC 10 is a coin flip — paralyzed prey is an auto-hit feeding frenzy for the whole pack. Open by rushing the nearest humanoid, one ghoul Clawing to paralyze, the rest Bite (+4, avg 8 each) on the paralyzed target. Elves and elves-of-heart are immune to the paralysis: leave them for last or bring them down with bites first. 30 ft. speed and 22 HP make ghouls expendable — attack in waves, commit fully, and accept casualties; the pack wins on action economy. Pick off stragglers in dark corridors, crypts, and charnel houses where darkvision lets the pack see and torch-bearing prey stands out in the dark. Retreat only by vanishing into 5-ft. cracks and tunnels too small for armored pursuers, returning to bleed the party over repeated raids.

name: Giant Ape

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The ape makes two Fist attacks.

actions.name: Fist
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 10 ft. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Boulder Toss
actions.description: The ape hurls a boulder at a point it can see within 90 feet. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 17, each creature in a 5-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point. Failure: 24 (7d6) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

bonus_actions.name: Leap
bonus_actions.description: The ape jumps up to 30 feet by spending 10 feet of movement.

combat-strategy: Open with Boulder Toss (DC 17 Dex, avg 24 bludgeoning, prone for Large or smaller) at the clustered backline — knocking the wizard into a rock on turn one sets the fight. Leap (30 ft. for 10 movement) into the middle, then Multiattack two Fists (avg 22 each, 10 ft. reach) on anyone adjacent; prone victims get melee attacks with Advantage, so re-proning and pile-on is the combo. Use 40 ft. climb to drag the fight vertical — up cliff faces, into the canopy — then pelt climbers with boulders from above where the party's reach weapons can't follow. Grapple-adjacent tactics: prone + melee Advantage synergy after a boulder hit, then relocate to the next elevated perch. 168 HP means it wins most stand-up fights, but at roughly 50 HP against a spellcasting party it should climb or swing to the high ground and convert to boulder-hurling attrition rather than standing in Fireball range. Territorial defense, not murder — often a display of violence (shaking trees, hurling warning rocks) ends the encounter before a fatal one begins.

name: Giant Axe Beak

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The axe beak makes one Sharpened Beak attack and one Talons attack.

actions.name: Sharpened Beak
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 18 (2d12 + 5) Slashing damage, and a creature within 5 feet of the target (axe beak's choice) takes 6 (1d12) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Talons
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

combat-strategy: Charge in at 50 feet and open with Talons to knock a front-line fighter Prone, then follow with Sharpened Beak so the fallen target's neighbor also eats the splash slashing damage. Focus down whoever gets knocked prone first — a prone fighter standing costs half their movement, and the axe beak's 10-foot beak reach lets it punish enemies who stand and re-engage. Fight in open ground where its speed matters; kiting into tight corridors neutralizes its multiattack spread. It is fearless and dumb (Int 3), so it fights to the death, but a target that drops below roughly a quarter HP may turn if the party is hammering it — use its aggression to bait it into prepared ground.

name: Giant Badger

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (2d4 + 1) Piercing damage.

combat-strategy: A trivial skirmisher: burrow 10 feet to break line of sight or pop up behind the party, then Bite whoever is closest. Do not expect tactics — target isolated or small characters, and use its 17 Con to trade hits while it digs away when cornered. Best used in packs or as an ambush surprise in tunnels where its burrow speed lets it appear from unexpected directions. It flees when reduced to a handful of hit points.

name: Giant Bat

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

combat-strategy: Attack at night or in darkness where its 120-foot blindsight dominates and light-based tactics fail. Dive from altitude, Bite a straggler, and fly back out of melee reach before the party can retaliate — its 60-foot fly against 10-foot walk makes it nearly untouchable by ground foes without reach. Target spellcasters or archers positioned at the edges of the group. At 22 HP it is fragile; a couple of solid hits sends it scattering.

name: Giant Boar

traits.name: Bloodied Fury
traits.description: The boar has Advantage on melee attack rolls while it is Bloodied.

actions.name: Gore
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature and the boar moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 7 (2d6) Piercing damage and has the Prone condition.

combat-strategy: Always set up Gore charges: circle out of reach, then run 20+ feet straight at a target for the extra 2d6 damage and a Prone knockdown. Knocked-down targets are free melee for the boar and its pack mates, and the boar's Bloodied Fury gives it Advantage once it has taken damage, so early hits make it more dangerous, not less. Corner prey against walls or cliffs where there is no straight-line escape. A wounded boar fights harder — it does not retreat, so expect a fight to the death.

name: Giant Centipede

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Piercing damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the centipede's next turn.

combat-strategy: Swarm tactics: attack in numbers so Pack-style concentration and the Poisoned condition stack across the party. Every bite imposes Poisoned (disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks), so even missed-adjacent chip damage degrades the party's accuracy over several rounds. Climb walls and ceilings to attack from unexpected angles and slip through cracks to escape. Individually they die to any stray AoE; use swarms of 6+ in confined tunnels where the party cannot spread out.

name: Giant Constrictor Snake

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The snake makes one Bite attack and uses Constrict.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Constrict
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 14, one Large or smaller creature the snake can see within 10 feet. Failure: 13 (2d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14).
actions.save_effect: The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14).

flavor_text:
We skirted the coastlines of several islands, sailing south by west until we reached a small peninsula cut off from the main island by a massive stone wall. We were well received by the people of Tanaroa, the small village that guards this wall. The villagers have no name for the large island other than the Isle of Dread.
—Rory Barbarosa, log of the Gallivant
combat-strategy: Open in water or tall grass, then Bite and Constrict the same target when possible — the DC 14 Strength save grapples and sets up automatic crush damage next round. Drag grappled victims into deep water where they fight at a disadvantage and the snake's 30-foot swim dominates. Never let go of a grapple if you can help it; re-grappling escaped targets with Constrict each turn is the whole game. Target the lowest-Strength characters first. It may release and slither away into water only when near death.

name: Giant Crab

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The crab can breathe air and water.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 11) from one of two claws.

combat-strategy: Ambush from shallow water or buried in sand using its Stealth +3, then Claw to grapple (escape DC 11) and drag Medium or smaller victims into deeper water where they must swim or drown. Two claws means two grappled victims at once; split the party by hauling one pc under while the second crab takes another. Retreat between fights into the water where ground-based pursuit fails. Individually weak (13 HP), so run them in pairs or larger packs.

name: Giant Crocodile

traits.name: Hold Breath
traits.description: The crocodile can hold its breath for 1 hour.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The crocodile makes one Bite attack and one Tail attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 21 (3d10 + 5) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 15). While Grappled, the target has the Restrained condition and can't be targeted by the crocodile's Tail.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 18 (3d8 + 5) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

combat-strategy: The premier ambush predator: lie submerged with Stealth +5 until a boat or shore party passes, then burst out and Bite to grapple-then-restrain, dragging the victim underwater to drown. While the target is Restrained by the bite it cannot be targeted by Tail, so sequence Bite-grapple on one victim and Tail-prone on another with Multiattack. Pull grappled prey into deep water immediately — drowning is the kill mechanic, not the bite damage. Fights near riverbanks and reeds are ideal; on open land it is slow (30 ft.) and should retreat to water when badly hurt at roughly half HP.

name: Giant Eagle
languages: Celestial; understands Common and Primordial (Auran) but can't speak them

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The eagle makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) Radiant damage.

combat-strategy: Dive from the sky, Multiattack with two Rend attacks on an exposed target, and climb back out of reach — its 80-foot fly makes hit-and-run the default. Radiant damage bypasses common resistances, so target undead or fiends preferentially, or snatch small companions, message pouches, and low-flying familiars. Pick off isolated spellcasters on the battlefield's edge. At 26 HP it will break off and fly away after two or three solid hits.

name: Giant Elk
languages: Celestial; understands Common, Elvish, and Sylvan but can't speak them

actions.name: Ram
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 5 (2d4) Radiant damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature and the elk moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 5 (2d4) Bludgeoning damage and has the Prone condition.

conditional_damage.condition: moved 20+ feet straight toward target immediately before the hit

description: The majestic giant elk is rare to the point that its appearance is often taken as a foreshadowing of an important event, such as the birth of a king. Legends tell of gods that take the form of giant elk when visiting the Material Plane. Many cultures therefore believe that to hunt these creatures is to invite divine wrath.
combat-strategy: Use 60-foot kiting: canter away out of melee reach, then wheel around and Ram with the 20-foot straight-line charge for bonus bludgeoning and a Prone knockdown. Knocking mounted or front-line fighters prone protects the elk and disrupts the party's formation. Radiant damage makes it effective against undead. In open terrain it is very hard to catch; circle, never stand still, and flee at low HP unless it is defending its herd.

name: Giant Fire Beetle

traits.name: Illumination
traits.description: The beetle sheds Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +1, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Fire damage.

description: A giant fire beetle is a nocturnal creature that takes its name from a pair of glowing glands that give off light. Miners and adventurers prize these creatures, for a giant fire beetle's glands continue to shed light for ld6 days after the beetle dies. Giant fire beetles are most commonly found underground and in dark forests.
combat-strategy: Effectively non-combat: its 1-fire-damage Bite is irrelevant. Its tactical value is as a light source (Illumination) in dark dungeons — position it behind the party's front line in safe corners, or climb it up walls to light ceilings and ledges. If forced into a fight, hide in the rear and bite ankles for nuisance damage. Do not waste party resources killing them; the party will likely just capture them for light.

name: Giant Frog

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The frog can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Standing Leap
traits.description: The frog's Long Jump is up to 20 feet and its High Jump is up to 10 feet with or without a running start.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 11).

actions.name: Swallow
actions.description: The frog swallows a Small or smaller target it is grappling. While swallowed, the target isn't Grappled but has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, and it has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the frog. While swallowing the target, the frog can't use Bite, and if the frog dies, the swallowed target is no longer Restrained and can escape from the corpse using 5 feet of movement, exiting with the Prone condition. At the end of the frog's next turn, the swallowed target takes 5 (2d4) Acid damage. If that damage doesn't kill it, the frog disgorges it, causing it to exit Prone.
actions.save_effect:
While swallowed, the target isn't Grappled but has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, and it has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the frog. While swallowing the target, the frog can't use Bite, and if the frog dies, the swallowed target is no longer Restrained and can escape from the corpse using 5 feet of movement, exiting with the Prone condition.

At the end of the frog's next turn, the swallowed target takes 5 (2d4) Acid damage. If that damage doesn't kill it, the frog disgorges it, causing it to exit Prone.

combat-strategy: Ambush from pond edges or tall reeds using Stealth +4, then Bite to grapple a Small-or-smaller target and Swallow it whole — the victim is Blinded, Restrained, and in total cover, effectively removed from combat for a round. The frog cannot Bite while swallowing, so use the swallow turn purely for repositioning toward deeper water. Spellcasters and rogues are prime snacks. Attack at night using darkvision, then hop (20-foot standing leap) back into the pond. It disgorges automatically after a round, so re-grapple to keep pressure on. Retreat into water at half HP.

name: Giant Goat

actions.name: Ram
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature and the goat moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 5 (2d4) Bludgeoning damage and has the Prone condition.

conditional_damage.condition: moved 20+ feet straight toward target immediately before the hit

combat-strategy: Charge down slopes and narrow mountain paths: 20-foot straight-line Ram for the bonus damage and Prone knockdown, ideally sending targets tumbling off cliffs or off mountain-goat-friendly rocky inclines where the goat's 30-foot climb gives it home ground. Attack pack-style — several goats can pin a fighter prone on a ledge and gore the helpless. Target mounted companions or porters carrying gear. On flat open ground it is much weaker; lure the party onto inclines. Flees when wounded unless defending herd.

name: Giant Hyena

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Rampage
bonus_actions.description: Immediately after dealing damage to a creature that was already Bloodied, the hyena can move up to half its Speed, and it makes one Bite attack.

combat-strategy: Pack hunter: coordinate multiple hyenas to get Advantage via surrounding, Bite a Bloodied target, then Rampage for a free 25-foot move and extra Bite — chain Rampages let a hyena cross the battlefield and gang up on the weakest fallen foe. Focus whoever is already hurt; the Bloodied trigger makes focus-fire the core sequence. Harass and withdraw: bite, then use Rampage movement to slip out of reach before ripostes. Run in packs of 4+; individual hyenas scatter at low HP, and a pack whose members keep dropping will break and flee.

name: Giant Lizard

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The lizard can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Piercing damage.

description: A giant lizard can be ridden or used as a draft animal. Lizardfolk also keep them as pets, and subterranean giant lizards are used as mounts and pack animals by drow, duergar, and other Underdark dwellers.
combat-strategy: Ambush from ceilings using Spider Climb — drop onto isolated targets from above for surprise, Bite, then scurry back up walls out of melee reach. Hunt in packs at night with darkvision, surrounding for Advantage. Its 40-foot climb and walk make vertical terrain its ally; fight near ruins, cliffs, or cave walls. Individually fragile (19 HP); avoid sustained fights with heavily armed foes and scatter up walls when wounded.

name: Giant Octopus

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The octopus can breathe only underwater. It can hold its breath for 1 hour outside water.

actions.name: Tentacles
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13) from all eight tentacles. While Grappled, the target has the Restrained condition.

reactions.name: Ink Cloud
reactions.trigger: The octopus takes damage while underwater.
reactions.description: The octopus releases ink that fills a 10-foot Cube centered on itself, and the octopus moves up to its Swim Speed. The Cube is Heavily Obscured for 1 minute or until a strong current or similar effect disperses the ink.

zone.advisory: Cube NOT parsed (§62): 10-foot Cube modeled at 5-ft centered radius, heavily obscured for 1 minute or until a strong current disperses the ink; octopus moves up to its Swim Speed; underwater trigger precondition — all GM-enforced. No vision model (§70).

combat-strategy: Ambush underwater from concealment (Stealth +5) hugging the seabed, then Tentacles to grapple-then-restrain a spearfisher or swimming pc. The moment it is attacked or any ally is threatened, trigger Ink Cloud to create heavy obscurement and swim 60 feet away — attack from total concealment, grapple, vanish, repeat. Drag grappled victims into crevices or drown them away from the party. Tentacle's 10-foot reach lets it strike from the ink's edge. It flees into holes or ink at low HP, dragging prey if possible.

name: Giant Owl
languages: Celestial; understands Common, Elvish, and Sylvan but can't speak them

traits.name: Flyby
traits.description: The owl doesn't provoke an Opportunity Attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

actions.name: Talons
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The owl casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability: At Will: Detect Evil and Good, Detect Magic 1/Day: Clairvoyance

combat-strategy: Mostly a scout and messenger, not a brute: use at will Detect Magic/Detect Evil and Good and Clairvoyance to warn its allies or its druid master. In a fight, hunt at night using 120-foot darkvision and Stealth +6, dive silently, strike with Talons, and Flyby out of opportunity attacks. Snatch small items, scrolls, or Small familiars from unaware adventurers. Avoid prolonged melee at 19 HP; disengage into the sky when attacked.

name: Giant Poisonous Snake

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) piercing damage, and the target must make a DC 11 Constitution saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
actions.save_effect: On a failure, the target takes 10 (3d6) poison damage. On a success, the target takes half as much damage.

combat-strategy: Bite is the win condition: +6 to hit with the DC 11 Constitution save for 3d6 poison damage roughly triples its output. Hunt in swarms so multiple save-or-suck bites land in one round, targeting the lowest-Constitution characters first. Hide in grass, rubble, or cargo (small, quiet, 10-foot blindsight) for ambushes, then strike and slither into cracks it can flee through. Even one round of swarm bites can drop a low-level pc on the save. Scatter into hiding spots when the party brings AoE to bear.

name: Giant Rat

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The rat has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the rat's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 feet. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Piercing damage.

description:
Some giant rats carry vile diseases that they spread with their bites. A diseased giant rat has a challenge rating of l/8 (2S XP) and the following action instead of its normal bite attack.
Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach S ft., one target. Hit: 4 (l d4 + 2) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or contract a disease. Until the disease is cured, the target can't regain hit points except by magical means, and the target's hit point maximum decreases by 3 (ld6) every 24 hours. If the target's hit point maximum drops to 0 as a result of this disease, the target dies.
combat-strategy: Classic swarm nuisance: attack in packs to trigger Pack Tactics Advantage against anyone flanked, and gnaw isolated or prone targets. Dive out of drains, refuse heaps, or wall holes for hit-and-run, then scurry back into crevices between attacks. Target spellcasters holding concentration (a hit forces a con save) and anyone knocked down. Individually they die in one hit, so mass them — swarms of 8+ can overwhelm a low-level party. The pack routs when several bodies pile up.

name: Giant Scorpion

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The scorpion makes two Claw attacks and one Sting attack.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13) from one of two claws.

actions.name: Sting
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage plus 11 (2d10) Poison damage.

combat-strategy: Multiattack sequence matters: use Claws to grapple (escape DC 13), then Sting the grappled target — in many tables held prey is easy, and even flat-footed the +5 Sting with 11 poison damage is the money hit. Fight in tight corridors and burrows where its 40-foot walk and 15 AC let it anchor a choke point and enemies crowd into claw range. Use 60-foot blindsight to fight in pitch-black tunnels it knows. Grapple one target and drag it aside to split the party. Retreat into burrows when reduced to about a quarter HP.

name: Giant Sea Horse

actions.name: Ram
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) bludgeoning damage.

traits.name: Charge
traits.description: If the seahorse moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and then hits it with a ram attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 11 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The seahorse can breathe only underwater.

description: Like their smaller kin, giant seahorses are shy, colorful fish with elongated bodies and curled tails. Aquatic elves train them as mounts.
combat-strategy: Underwater only: swim 40 feet in a straight line and Ram with Charge for the extra 2d6 and a DC 11 knockdown — knocking swimmers prone underwater disrupts their aim and can push them into currents or hazards. Hit-and-run around kelp forests and rocks where the party cannot maintain formation. Target isolated swimmers and small boats, capsizing attention toward the crew. At 16 HP they break off after one good hit each; use them in pods of 3+ to stack charges.

name: Giant Seahorse

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The seahorse can breathe only underwater.

actions.name: Ram
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) Bludgeoning damage, or 11 (2d8 + 2) Bludgeoning damage if the seahorse moved 20+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit.

conditional_damage.condition: moved 20+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit

bonus_actions.name: Bubble Dash
bonus_actions.description: While underwater, the seahorse moves up to half its Swim Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

combat-strategy: Ram is the whole game: use Bubble Dash to reposition 20 feet without opportunity attacks, then accelerate 20+ feet straight in for the 2d8+2 charge damage. Kite underwater — dash in, strike, Bubble Dash back out of reach, forcing enemies to chase it through 3D aquatic terrain at their peril. Target lone swimmers near surface or near hazards like rocks and whirlpools. Fight in pairs to flank. Bubble Dash escape makes it hard to pin; disengage to open water when hurt.

name: Giant Shark

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The shark can breathe only underwater.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The shark makes two Bite attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9 (with Advantage if the target doesn't have all its Hit Points), reach 5 ft. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) Piercing damage.

description: A giant shark is 30 feet long and normally found in deep oceans. Utterly fearless, it preys on anything that crosses its path, including whales and ships.
combat-strategy: Hunt in dark or murky water where its 60-foot blindsight rules and the party cannot see it coming. Multiattack with two Bites, each at Advantage against wounded targets (Bloodied), so focus one prey to half HP and then shred it — two attacks at +9 with Advantage average roughly 29 damage per round on a wounded target. Attack from below and behind, circle away, and re-charge; in open deep water it is nearly untouchable, and it drags the fight away from boats and shore. On land it is crippled (5 ft. walk); never follow the party ashore. It is relentless and usually fights to the death.

name: Giant Spider

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The spider can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

traits.name: Web Walker
traits.description: The spider ignores movement restrictions caused by webs, and it knows the location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Web
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature the spider can see within 60 feet. Failure: The target has the Restrained condition until the web is destroyed (AC 10; HP 5; Vulnerability to Fire damage; Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage).
actions.save_effect: The target has the Restrained condition until the web is destroyed (AC 10; HP 5; Vulnerability to Fire damage; Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage).

description: To snare its prey, a giant spider spins elaborate webs or shoots sticky strands of webbing from its abdomen. Giant spiders are most commonly found underground, making their lairs on ceilings or in dark, web-filled crevices. Such lairs are often festooned with web cocoons holding past victims.
combat-strategy: Web first: cast Web (DC 13 Dex, Restrained) on the party's ranged attackers or the weakest Arcana/Agility-lacking pc, then close and Bite for poison damage on the Restrained target (melee attacks against Restrained have Advantage). Hang from ceilings using Spider Climb so foes must look up and spread out, and bait pursuit into pre-warmed web zones — Web Walker means it knows exactly who touches its webs and the webs hide it. Fire-wielding foes are the counter: keep distance from torches and burning hands. Ambush at night, wrap isolated victims and haul them up to the ceiling. Retreat up walls when at low HP.

name: Giant Squid

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The squid can breathe only underwater.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The squid makes one Bite attack and one Tentacle attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 28 (4d10 + 6) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Tentacle
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 15 ft. Hit: 19 (3d8 + 6) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 16) from one of two tentacles, and the squid can pull the target up to 10 feet straight toward itself.

reactions.name: Ink Cloud
reactions.trigger: The squid takes damage while underwater.
reactions.description: The squid releases ink that fills a 15-foot Cube centered on itself, and the squid moves up to its Swim Speed. The Cube is Heavily Obscured for 1 minute or until a strong current or similar effect disperses the ink.

zone.advisory: Cube NOT parsed (§62): 15-foot Cube modeled at 8-ft centered radius, heavily obscured for 1 minute or until a strong current disperses the ink; squid moves up to its Swim Speed; underwater trigger precondition — all GM-enforced. No vision model (§70).

combat-strategy: Tentacle first from 15-foot reach: grapple (escape DC 16) a target and pull them 10 feet closer, then Bite for 4d10+6 next turn — dragged victims into the beak is the kill combo. Two tentacles means two grappled victims at once; split the party and drown or eat them one at a time. When the party focuses fire, trigger Ink Cloud and swim 80 feet away into the murk, then resurface somewhere else to grab another pc. Attack ships and boats by grappling rowers off the rails or smashing at the waterline. Fight only in deep water; it flees into the depths, sometimes dragging prey, when brought below roughly a third HP.

name: Giant Toad

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The toad can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Standing Leap
traits.description: The toad's Long Jump is up to 20 feet and its High Jump is up to 10 feet with or without a running start.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage plus 5 (2d4) Poison damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 12).

actions.name: Swallow
actions.description: The toad swallows a Medium or smaller target it is grappling. While swallowed, the target isn't Grappled but has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, and it has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the toad. In addition, the target takes 10 (3d6) Acid damage at the end of each of the toad's turns. The toad can have only one target swallowed at a time, and it can't use Bite while it has a swallowed target. If the toad dies, a swallowed creature is no longer Restrained and can escape from the corpse using 5 feet of movement, exiting with the Prone condition.
actions.save_effect: While swallowed, the target isn't Grappled but has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, and it has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the toad. In addition, the target takes 10 (3d6) Acid damage at the end of each of the toad's turns. The toad can have only one target swallowed at a time, and it can't use Bite while it has a swallowed target. If the toad dies, a swallowed creature is no longer Restrained and can escape from the corpse using 5 feet of movement, exiting with the Prone condition.

flavor_text:
Beware the furred giant snakes of the Yatil Mountains. Their pelts might be warm, but their bites are deadly.
—Bannik Vorl, agent of the Margrave of the March of Bissel
combat-strategy: Open with a Standing Leap (20 ft.) to close on the most isolated Medium-or-smaller target, then Bite to grapple (DC 12) and Swallow next turn — a swallowed PC has Total Cover, Blinded, and takes 3d6 acid per round, which forces the party to focus fire on the toad. Fight near water or bogs where its 30 ft. swim speed lets it drag engagements and retreat; the weak DC 12 escape means keep re-grappling rather than biting for damage once a hold breaks. Position so grappled targets are away from allies who can easily help them escape. With only 39 hp and AC 11 it can't trade blows — once the swallow is lost or half its hp are gone, hop into deep water and flee, since the party needs a swim check or flying to follow.

name: Giant Venomous Snake

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) Piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) Poison damage.

combat-strategy: Use its 40 ft. speed and 10 ft. reach Bite to strike from beyond most enemies' reach, then slither away — hit-and-run is the whole game for an 11 hp, AC 14 skirmisher. Its +6 to hit makes it dangerous against low-AC casters and rogues, so prioritize those soft targets over armored front-liners. Fight in tall grass, reeds, or water where its swim speed and Stealth-friendly terrain let it Hide between strikes; 10 ft. blindsight keeps it effective in darkness or fog it hides in. Snakes scatter when wounded — at half hp or after losing a bite exchange, retreat into thick cover or water where pursuers can't easily chase.

name: Giant Vulture

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The vulture has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the vulture's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Gouge
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) Piercing damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn.

description: A giant vulture has advanced intelligence and a malevolent bent. Unlike its smaller kin, it will attack a wounded creature to hasten its end. Giant vultures have been known to haunt a thirsty, starving creature for days to enjoy its suffering.
combat-strategy: Circle in flight (60 ft.) and dive onto wounded or prone foes, using Pack Tactics with at least one other vulture adjacent to the same target for reliable advantage on Gouge's 2d6+2 piercing hits. Sequence attacks so one vulture lands to trigger Pack Tactics while another stays at range to avoid opportunity attacks from reach weapons. The Poisoned condition from Gouge imposes disadvantage on the victim's attacks — gang up on whoever it poisons to blunt their retaliation. It only walks 10 ft., so never let it get engaged on the ground away from allies; once an individual drops below about 10 hp it should take to the air and either disengage or flee, as vultures only fight when the odds are already lopsided.

name: Giant Wasp

traits.name: Flyby
traits.description: The wasp doesn't provoke an Opportunity Attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

actions.name: Sting
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage plus 5 (2d4) Poison damage.

combat-strategy: Use Flyby to dive in from above, Sting a target, and fly straight out beyond melee reach without provoking opportunity attacks — the classic wasp hit-and-run. 50 ft. fly speed against 30 ft. walkers means it controls engagement range almost completely; harass archers and casters at the back of the formation where retaliation is thinnest. As an Int 1 beast it can't be reasoned with or intimidated, so it fights until swatted; send it repeatedly at the same target to stack poison damage rather than splitting attacks. If cornered in tight quarters where reach weapons threaten it at every hover, it keeps stinging anyway, but kiting it over water or dense canopy forces ranged attacks at disadvantage.

name: Giant Weasel

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Piercing damage.

combat-strategy: Strike from Stealth (its +5) in dark or cluttered terrain, bite a lone target for 1d4+3 piercing, then use 40 ft. speed and 30 ft. climb to vanish up a wall, tree, or into underbrush before a counterattack lands. It's fragile (9 hp), so never start combat in the open — ambush or flank, and prefer targets without armor. Attack from heights: drop from a ceiling or branch to bite, then climb away, since most humanoids can't follow without spending their whole turn. Flee immediately once it takes meaningful damage; a wounded weasel that shows itself twice usually dies twice.

name: Giant Wolf Spider

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The spider can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Piercing damage plus 5 (2d4) Poison damage.

description: Smaller than a giant spider, a giant wolf spider hunts prey across open ground or hides in a burrow or crevice, or in a hidden cavity beneath debris.
combat-strategy: Ambush from Stealth +7 on walls or ceilings using Spider Climb, dropping onto trailing or isolated targets with its 40 ft. climb speed. Two bites land roughly 1d4+3+2d4 poison each — dangerous against low-HP characters — so focus a single victim rather than splitting attacks, and drag the fight into dark tunnels where its darkvision and 10 ft. blindsight dominate while torchless pursuers suffer. Kite with terrain: scramble up walls to break opportunity attacks and force the party to attack at disadvantage or waste movement. It's only 11 hp, so disengage to a ceiling or crevice after any bad round, and flee into tight cracks the party can't follow when badly hurt.

name: Gibbering Mouther

traits.name: Aberrant Ground
traits.description: The ground in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the mouther is Difficult Terrain.

traits.name: Gibbering
traits.description: The mouther babbles incoherently while it doesn't have the Incapacitated condition. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 10, any creature that starts its turn within 20 feet of the mouther while it is babbling. Failure: The target rolls 1d8 to determine what it does during the current turn: 1-4. The target does nothing. 5-6. The target takes no action or Bonus Action and uses all its movement to move in a random direction. 7-8. The target makes a melee attack against a randomly determined creature within its reach or does nothing if it can't make such an attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (2d6) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition. The target dies if it is reduced to 0 Hit Points by this attack. Its body is then absorbed into the mouther, leaving only equipment behind.
actions.save_effect: If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition. The target dies if it is reduced to 0 Hit Points by this attack. Its body is then absorbed into the mouther, leaving only equipment behind.

actions.name: Blinding Spittle
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 10, each creature in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within 30 feet. Failure: 7 (2d6) Radiant damage, and the target has the Blinded condition until the end of the mouther's next turn.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 7 (2d6) Radiant damage, and the target has the Blinded condition until the end of the mouther's next turn.

description:
Of all the terrors created b y foul sorcery, gibbering mouthers are among the most wicked and depraved. This creature is the composite eyes, mouths, and liquefied matter of its former victims. Driven to insanity by the destruction of their bodies and absorption into the mouther, those victims gibber incoherent madness, forced to consume everything in reach.

Amoeboid Form. The gibbering mouther's body is an amorphous mass of mouths and eyes that propels itself by oozing forward, fastening several mouths to the ground and pulling its bulk behind. Though it moves slowly, it swims through water, mud, and quicksand with ease.

Mouths of Madness. When a gibbering mouther senses prey, its mouths begin to murmur and chatter, each with a different voice: deep or shrill, wailing or ululating, crying out in agony or ecstasy. This cacophonous gibbering overcomes the senses of any creature that hears it, causing most to flee in terror. Others are overcome with madness or stand paralyzed, fixated on the horrific creature as it oozes forward to consume them.

All-Consuming. Driven to devour any creature it can reach, a gibbering mouther flows over victims transfixed by its mad ranting, its multitudinous voices temporarily silenced as it gnaws and swallows living flesh. The monster liquefies stone with which it comes into contact, hindering creatures that overcome its gibbering and attempt to flee.
A gibbering mouther leaves nothing of its prey behind. However, even as the last of a victim's body is consumed, its eyes and mouth boil to the surface, ready to join the chorus of tormented gibbering that welcomes the monster's next meal.
combat-strategy: Charge straight into the middle of the party — Aberrant Ground makes the 10 ft. around it difficult terrain, slowing anyone trying to leave, while Gibbering (DC 10 Wis) reliably confuses weaker-willed PCs each round, with an 1-in-8 chance they swing at each other. Use Blinding Spittle (DC 10 Dex save) into clusters of enemies, especially archers and spellcasters who need sight, then close and Bite prone victims, remembering a creature killed by its Bite is absorbed. Because its babbling makes mindless melee chaotic, wade into spellcasters first: a Blinded or confused wizard can't aim, and the mouther's 52 hp and pool of hit dice let it soak punishment while its victims flail. It never retreats (Int 3), so expect a fight to the death — run it relentlessly, groaning and churning through anything in reach.

name: Githyanki Dracomancer

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The githyanki makes three Draconic Strike attacks.

actions.name: Draconic Strike
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +10, reach 10 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Slashing damage plus 17 (5d6) Fire damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the start of the githyanki's next turn.

actions.name: Conjured Dragon's Breath
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 18, each creature in a 90-foot Cone. Failure: 27 (6d8) Fire damage plus 27 (6d8) Force damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Half damage

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The githyanki casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 18, +10 to hit with spell attacks): At Will: Mage Hand (the hand is Invisible) 2/Day Each: Nondetection (self only), Plane Shift, Tongues

bonus_actions.name: Misty Step
bonus_actions.description: The githyanki casts Misty Step, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

combat-strategy: Open at range (120 ft.) with Multiattack Draconic Strikes — each hit deals 2d6+5 slashing + 5d6 fire and leaves the target Frightened, which suppresses retaliation while its +10 attacks keep landing on the frightened. Once the party clusters or a fright save is coming up, unleash Conjured Dragon's Breath (90 ft. cone, DC 18, 54 damage half on save) against bunched foes, ideally funneling them through a corridor first. Use Misty Step and 30 ft. hover fly to stay out of melee reach, repositioning behind cover or rising vertically where ground-based martial characters can't reach, and Misty Step + 3 attacks in one turn after a teleport. Nondetection at the start defeats scrying and divination counters; hold Plane Shift as a trump card — banish a separated PC to the Astral or escape the fight when it turns against it (below ~80 hp or when the party burns its big resources). As a rare commander, never let itself become the only enemy in melee; kite, frighten the healer, and punish clumping with the cone.

name: Githyanki Knight

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The githyanki makes three Silver Sword attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting to cast Telekinesis if available.

actions.name: Silver Sword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Slashing damage plus 14 (4d6) Psychic damage. Critical Hit: If the target is in an astral body (as with the Astral Projection spell), the githyanki can cut the silvery cord that tethers the target to its material body instead of dealing damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The githyanki casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13): At Will: Mage Hand (the hand is Invisible) 2/Day Each: Nondetection (self only), Tongues 1/Day Each: Plane Shift, Telekinesis

bonus_actions.name: Misty Step
bonus_actions.description: The githyanki casts Misty Step, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

description:
The githyanki plunder countless worlds from the decks of their astral vessels and the backs of red dragons. Feathers, beads, gems, and precious metals decorate their armor and weapons-the legendary silver swords with which they cut through their foes. Since winning their freedom from the mind flayers, the githyanki have become ruthless conquerors under the rulership of their dread lich-queen, Vlaakith.

Astral Raiders. The githyanki despise all other races, undertaking devastating raids that take them from their strongholds in the Astral Plane to the farflung corners of the multiverse. War is the ultimate expression of githyanki culture, and their pitiless black eyes know no mercy. After a raid, they leave shattered survivors enough food and resources to weakly endure. Later, the githyanki return to their conquered foes, plundering them again and again.

Followers of Gith. In their own language, githyanki means "followers of Gith." Under the guidance of Gith, the githyanki stratified into a militaristic society, with a strict caste system, dedicated to the ongoing fight against the victims and sworn enemies of their race. When their leader Gith perished, she was replaced by her undead adviser, Vlaakith. The lich-queen forbade worship of all beings except herself.
Of all their enemies, the githyanki most hate their former masters, the mind flayers. Their close kin, the githzerai, are second in their enmity. All other creatures are treated with simple contempt by the githyanki, whose xenophobic pride defines their view of inferior races.

Silver Swords. In ancient times, gith knights created special weapons to combat their mind flayer masters. These silver swords channel the force of the wielder's will, dealing psychic as well as physical damage. A githyanki can't become a knight until it masters the singular discipline needed to will such a blade into existence. A silver sword is equivalent to a greatsword, and takes on the properties of a +3 greatsword in the hands of its creator.
In the eyes of the githyanki, each silver sword is a priceless relic and a work of art. Githyanki knights will hunt down and destroy any non-githyanki that dares to carry or wield a silver sword, reclaiming it for their people.

Red Dragon Riders. In the uprising against the illithids, Gith sought allies. Her adviser Vlaakith appealed to Tiamat, the goddess of evil dragonkind, and Gith ventured into the Nine Hells to meet with her. Only Tiamat now knows what passed between them, but Vlaakith returned to the Astral Plane with the Dragon Queen's red dragon consort Ephelomon, who proclaimed that his kind would forever act as allies to the githyanki. Not all red dragons honor the alliance kindled so long ago, but most at least don't consider the githyanki their enemies.

Outposts in the Mortal Realm. Since creatures that dwell on the Astral Plane don't age, the githyanki establish creches in remote areas of the Material Plane to raise their young. Doubling as military academies, these creches train young githyanki to harness their psychic and combat abilities. When a githyanki grows to adulthood and slays a mind flayer as part of a sacred rite of passage, it is permitted to rejoin its people on the Astral Plane.
combat-strategy: Fight at the front of githyanki strikes with three Silver Sword attacks (2d6+3 slashing + 4d6 psychic, +6 to hit) — target the enemy with the worst saving throw profile or lowest HP pool first to thin numbers fast. Replace one attack with Telekinesis (1/day) to hurl a caster off a ledge, disarm a martial fighter, or lift an enemy prone and helpless while its allies gang up; save Nondetection for when the party's divination or scrying would spoil an ambush. Use Misty Step to leap onto backline spellcasters or break free of encirclement, then attack and step away before being pinned. In the Astral Plane, it can sever the silvery cord of projected astral bodies on a critical hit — in that setting, hunt projected PCs deliberately. Retreat via Plane Shift once badly wounded (below ~40 hp) or if outnumbered beyond recovery; githyanki knights value their lives and their silver swords, dying only when the objective demands it.

name: Githyanki Warrior

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The githyanki makes two Psi Blade attacks.

actions.name: Psi Blade
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The githyanki casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability: At Will: Mage Hand (the hand is Invisible) 2/Day: Nondetection (self only)

bonus_actions.name: Misty Step
bonus_actions.description: The githyanki casts Misty Step, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

combat-strategy: Skirmish with two Psi Blade attacks (2d6+2 slashing + 2d6 psychic at +4) against the softest target, using Misty Step (bonus action) to blink behind cover, onto high ground, or behind the enemy line — then strike a caster and step back out before opportunity attacks land. Nondetection (2/day) on the squad before an ambush defeats the party's magic perception; coordinate timing so warriors attack from unexpected angles after githyanki raider spells fade. It's 49 hp and AC 17 — good but not unkillable — so break contact whenever it takes heavy damage: Misty Step away, re-hide, and disengage rather than trading blows with a focused martial character. As a squad fighter, split targets only to finish a wounded foe, and fall back to regroup if the pack breaks; githyanki warriors obey mission objectives over personal glory.

name: Githzerai Monk

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The githzerai makes two Psi Strike attacks.

actions.name: Psi Strike
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Bludgeoning damage plus 9 (2d8) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The githzerai casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability: At Will: Mage Hand (the hand is Invisible) 1/Day: See Invisibility

bonus_actions.name: Psi-Powered Leap
bonus_actions.description: The githzerai casts Jump, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

reactions.name: Psionic Defense
reactions.description: The githzerai casts Feather Fall or Shield in response to the spell's trigger, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

automation.description: GM adjudicates: or cast Shield per spell rules — no mechanical consumer

description:
Focused philosophers and austere ascetics, the githzerai pursue lives of rigid order. Lean and muscular, they wear unadorned clothing free of ornamentation, keeping their own counsel and trusting few creatures outside of their own kind. Having turned their backs on their warlike githyanki kin, the githzerai maintain a strict monastic lifestyle, dwelling on islands of order in the vast sea of chaos that is the plane of Limbo.

Psionic Adepts. The progenitors of the githzerai adapted to-and were transformed by-the psychic environment imposed on them by their illithid overlords. Under the teachings of Zerthimon, who called on his people to abandon the warlike ambitions of Gith, the githzerai focused their mental energy on creating physical and psychic barriers to protect them from attack, psychic or otherwise. Fighting is personal to a githzerai, which uses its mind to daze and incapacitate opponents, leaving them vulnerable to physical punishment.

Order amid Chaos. The githzerai willingly dwell in the heart of utter chaos in Limbo-a twisting, mercurial plane prone to manipulation and subjugation by githzerai minds strong enough to master it. Limbo is a maelstrom of primal matter and energy, its terrain a storm of rock and earth swept up in torrents of murky liquid, buffeted by strong winds, blasted by fire, and chilled by crushing walls of ice. The forces of Limbo react to sentience, however. Using the power of their minds, the githzerai tame the plane's chaotic elements, causing them to settle into fixed and survivable forms and creating oases and sanctuaries within the maelstrom.
Githzerai fortress-monasteries stand resolute against the chaos that surrounds them, virtually impervious to the turmoil of their surroundings, because the githzerai will it. Each monastery is overseen by monks that impose a strict schedule of chants, meals, martial arts training, and devotions according to their own philosophy. Behind their psionically fortified walls, the githzerai embrace thought, learning, psionic power, order, and discipline above all other things.
The social hierarchy of the githzerai is based on merit, and those githzerai who are the wisest teachers and the most skilled at physical and mental combat become leaders. The githzerai revere great heroes and teachers of the past, emulating those figures' virtues in their everyday lives.

Disciples of Zerthimon. Githzerai revere Zerthimon, the founder of their race. Although Gith won their people's freedom, Zerthimon saw her as unfit to lead. He believed that her warmongering would soon make her a tyrant no better than the mind flayers.
Skilled githzerai monks that best exemplify the teachings and principles of Zerthimon are called zerths. These powerful and disciplined monks can shift their bodies from one plane to another using only the power of their minds.

Beyond Limbo. Though githzerai rarely deal with the realms beyond Limbo, advanced monks of other races sometimes seek out a githzerai monastery and attempt to gain admittance as students. More rarely, a githzerai master establishes a hidden monastery on the Material Plane to train young githzerai or to spread the philosophy and teachings of Zerthimon.
As disciplined as they are, the githzerai have never forgotten their long imprisonment by the mind flayers. As a special devotion, they organize a rrakkma-an illithid hunting party-to other planes, not returning to their monasteries until they slay at least as many illithids as there are hunters in the party.
combat-strategy: Open at range if possible, then close with 40 ft. speed and Psi-Powered Leap (Jump as a bonus action) to bound onto the enemy line, landing with two Psi Strikes (1d8+2 bludgeoning + 2d8 psychic) on the weakest adjacent target. Psionic Defense matters more than offense: save the reaction's Shield for a big incoming attack or spell (it triggers once, so bait cantrips first), and Feather Fall whenever knocked off height. Fight defensively and let the enemy overextend — its +5 Acrobatics and 14 AC with the reaction Shield make it hard to pin down in one round, so hit-and-cycle: strike, move out of reach, shield the counterattack. Target spellcasters whose save profiles suit psychic punishment and who lack heavy armor. Retreat by leaping to defensible high ground or a doorway when it drops below roughly 15 hp, covering allies' withdrawal — a cornered monk still swings twice, so never assume it's finished.

name: Githzerai Psion

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The githzerai makes three Psychic Warp attacks.

actions.name: Psychic Warp
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit: 26 (4d10 + 4) Psychic damage, and the target has the githzerai's choice of (A) the Charmed condition until the start of the githzerai's next turn or (B) the Prone condition, provided the target is a Large or smaller creature.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The githzerai casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16): At Will: Mage Hand (the hand is Invisible) 1/Day Each: Plane Shift, See Invisibility

reactions.name: Psionic Defense
reactions.description: The githzerai casts Feather Fall or Shield in response to the spell's trigger, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

automation.description: GM adjudicates: or cast Shield per spell rules — no mechanical consumer

combat-strategy: Fight at range with hover-fly 40 ft., using three Psychic Warp attacks (120 ft., +8, 4d10+4 psychic) — apply Prone to targets who wield reach weapons or are standing on elevated ground (drop them), and Charmed to neutralize the party's striker or turn them against the githzerai's other foes. Hold the reaction Shield for the single biggest attack of each round or an incoming save-or-suck spell, and use Feather Fall only if enemies try knockback tricks against it. Kite constantly: 40 ft. hover fly means it can stay 30+ ft. above melee characters who can't reach, raining psychic bolts while spellcasters exhaust their range-limited counters. See Invisibility (1/day) at the start strips stealth and invisibility tactics; Plane Shift is its escape hatch and its punishment — banish a separated PC or flee when it drops below roughly 60 hp or loses concentration-worthy pressure. Never stop moving vertically; ground-level melee is a death sentence for a 169 hp, 18 Dex caster with no natural weapons.

name: Githzerai Zerth

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The githzerai makes two Psi Strike attacks.

actions.name: Psi Strike
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 13 (3d8) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The githzerai casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14): At Will: Mage Hand (the hand is Invisible) 1/Day Each: Phantasmal Killer (level 6 version), Plane Shift, See Invisibility

bonus_actions.name: Psi-Powered Leap
bonus_actions.description: The githzerai casts Jump, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

reactions.name: Psionic Defense
reactions.description: The githzerai casts Feather Fall or Shield in response to the spell's trigger, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

automation.description: GM adjudicates: or cast Shield per spell rules — no mechanical consumer

description:
Focused philosophers and austere ascetics, the githzerai pursue lives of rigid order. Lean and muscular, they wear unadorned clothing free of ornamentation, keeping their own counsel and trusting few creatures outside of their own kind. Having turned their backs on their warlike githyanki kin, the githzerai maintain a strict monastic lifestyle, dwelling on islands of order in the vast sea of chaos that is the plane of Limbo.

combat-strategy: Save Phantasmal Killer (6th-level version, DC 14 Wis) for the party's biggest threat or a PC separated from help — a fail means instant death, so bait it behind an opening Psi Strike exchange once you know each target's Wisdom defense.
