Open with two Psi Strikes (+7, 2d6+4 bludgeoning + 3d8 psychic) on the nearest soft target while Psi-Powered Leap repositions it onto rooftops, ledges, or across chasms where only ranged attackers can follow. Psionic Defense's Shield should eat the round's biggest single attack; Feather Fall protects it from being knocked off the high ground it exploits. See Invisibility (1/day) denies rogue and scout advantages — cast it the moment an engagement starts. Kite with 40 ft. speed and vertical terrain, hitting and leaping away; retreat via Plane Shift when it falls below roughly 30 hp or after Phantasmal Killer is spent and the party turns its full attention on it.

name: Glabrezu

traits.name: Demonic Restoration
traits.description: If the glabrezu dies outside the Abyss, its body dissolves into ichor, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Abyss.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The glabrezu has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The glabrezu makes two Pincer attacks and uses Pummel or Spellcasting.

actions.name: Pincer
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 10 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) Slashing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 15) from one of two pincers.

actions.name: Pummel
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 17, one creature Grappled by the glabrezu. Failure: 15 (3d6 + 5) Bludgeoning damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 15 (3d6 + 5) Bludgeoning damage. Success: Half damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The glabrezu casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16): At Will: Darkness, Detect Magic, Dispel Magic 1/Day Each: Confusion, Fly, Power Word Stun

description:
A glabrezu takes great pleasure in destroying mortals through temptation, and these creatures are among the few demons to offer their service to creatures foolish enough to summon them.
Although glabrezus are devastating in combat, they prefer to tempt victims into ruin, using power or wealth as a lure. Engaging in guile, trickery, and evil bargains, a glabrezu hoards riches that it uses to fulfill promises to shortsighted summoners and weak-willed mortals. However, if its attempts to entice or deceive fail, a glabrezu has the strength to fight and win.
combat-strategy: Open with Confusion (DC 16 Wis) to scatter the party's attacks — a confused front-line swinging at allies lets the glabrezu pick its fights — or Darkness on its own position if the party relies on spell attack rolls and sight-based saves (its 120 ft. truesight keeps it seeing perfectly). Close with two Pincer attacks (+9, 10 ft. reach) to grapple two Medium-or-smaller foes (DC 15), then Pummel one every turn for 3d6+5 bludgeoning while the other struggles to escape; control two grapplers and grind them down. Save Power Word Stun (no save, works at ≤150 hp — but devastating on a just-wounded tank or the healer) for the single most dangerous target once they're injured. Use Fly on an airborne grappled victim — fly upward and drop them, or hold them helpless while pincers and pummels finish them; Dispel Magic strips protection spells, buffs, and conjurations before they matter. It has 189 hp, AC 17, and Magic Resistance — it wins long slugfests, so hold it in reserve until melee merges, then dominate. Demonic Restoration means killing it outside the Abyss is temporary: fight to route the party, not merely to die well, and retreat through portals or summoned escorts when truly overwhelmed.

name: Gladiator

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The gladiator makes three Spear attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Shield Bash.

actions.name: Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Shield Bash
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 15, one creature within 5 feet that the gladiator can see. Failure: 9 (2d4 + 4) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.
actions.save_effect: If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

reactions.name: Parry
reactions.trigger: The gladiator is hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon.
reactions.description: The gladiator adds 3 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

flavor_text:
IN AN UNDERSEA ARENA, THE CROWD GOES WILD
AS A GLADIATOR TRIUMPHS OVER A GIANT SQUID
combat-strategy: Fight in the arena style: three Spear attacks (+7, 11 piercing each) on a single target to drop them fast, replacing one attack with Shield Bash (DC 15 Str, prone) to knock a foe down — then attack the prone target with advantage while they waste their turn standing. Use Parry (+3 AC, one reaction) against the enemy's most accurate attacker or their big attack of the round to make them miss. Spears with 20/60 ft. thrown range let it soften charging foes or keep spacing against fast skirmishers before melee merges. Target the lowest-AC or already-wounded front-liner first, pinning them with prone + multiattack combos; grapple-adjacent tactics matter — Athletics +10 supports shoving and holding position in chokepoints of a crowded arena. It fights to please a crowd and to survive the purse: it won't flee early, but at single-digit hp in a no-holds-barred pit it may appeal to the mob or surrender; outside the arena, retreat at roughly a quarter hp when there's no audience demanding a death.

name: Gnoll

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.

actions.name: Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage, or 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.

traits.name: Rampage
traits.description: When the gnoll reduces a creature to 0 hit points with a melee attack on its turn, the gnoll can take a bonus action to move up to half its speed and make a bite attack.

description:
Gnolls are feral humanoids that attack settlements along the frontiers and borderlands of civilization without warning, slaughtering their victims and devouring their flesh.

Demonic Origin. The origin of the gnolls traces back to a time when the demon lord Yeenoghu found his way to the Material Plane and ran amok. Packs of ordinary hyenas followed in his wake, scavenging the demon lord's kills. Those hyenas were transformed into the first gnolls, parading after Yeenoghu until he was banished back to the Abyss. The gnolls then scattered across the face of the world, a dire reminder of demonic power.

Nomadic Destroyers. Gnolls are dangerous because they strike at random. They emerge from the wilderness, plunder and slaughter, then move elsewhere. They attack like a plague of locusts, pillaging settlements and leaving little behind but razed buildings, gnawed corpses, and befouled land. Gnolls choose easy targets for their raids. Armored warriors holed up in a fortified castle will survive a rampaging gnoll horde unscathed, even as the towns, villages, and farms that surround the castle are ablaze, their people slaughtered and devoured.
Gnolls rarely build permanent structures or craft anything of lasting value. They don't make weapons or armor, but scavenge such items from the corpses of their fallen victims, stringing ears, teeth, scalps, and other trophies from their foes onto their patchwork armor.

Thirst for Blood. No goodness or compassion resides in the heart of a gnoll. Like a demon, it lacks anything resembling a conscience, and can't be taught or coerced to put aside its destructive tendencies. The gnolls' frenzied bloodlust makes them an enemy to all, and when they lack a common foe, they fight among themselves. Even the most savage orcs avoid allying with gnolls.
combat-strategy: Open with a Longbow volley (150 ft.) from cover or a rank behind the front line, then close with two-handed Spears (1d8+2 piercing) once the party charges in. The heart of gnoll tactics is Rampage: once any gnoll drops a creature with a melee hit, it bonus-action bites and moves — so concentrate fire on the weakest PC to trigger a chain of bonus-action bites as the pack cycles through fresh victims. Use Pack-Tactics-style numbers: surround targets in pairs so attacks land with advantage and 0.5-CR bodies trade efficiently. Corner prey against cliffs, walls, or wagons so fleeing targets must run through the gauntlet, and let the pack spread to prevent the party reforming in formation. Individual gnolls fight savagely until downed — they don't retreat unless the pack breaks or their leader falls — so expect every gnoll to fight to 0 hp in a frenzy.

name: Gnoll Demoniac

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The gnoll makes two Abyssal Strike attacks.

actions.name: Abyssal Strike
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. Hit: 20 (5d6 + 3) Poison damage.

actions.name: Hunger of Yeenoghu
actions.description: The gnoll conjures a 30-foot Cube of magical Darkness originating from a point it can see within 60 feet, which lasts for 1 minute or until the gnoll's Concentration ends on it. This area is Difficult Terrain. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 14, any creature that starts its turn in this area or enters it for the first time on a turn. Failure: 28 (8d6) Necrotic damage, and the gnoll or a creature of its choice it can see gains 10 Temporary Hit Points. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: The gnoll or a creature of its choice it can see gains 10 Temporary Hit Points.

bonus_actions.name: Rampage
bonus_actions.description: Immediately after dealing damage to a creature that is already Bloodied, the gnoll moves up to half its Speed, and it makes one Abyssal Strike attack.

combat-strategy: Open with Hunger of Yeenoghu (30 ft. cube of magical Darkness + difficult terrain, DC 14 Dex, 8d6 necrotic) centered on the densest cluster of the party — its 60 ft. darkvision lets it and its gnoll allies see inside while the party attacks at disadvantage, and every failed save feeds it 10 temporary hit points to soak retaliation. Follow with Multiattack Abyssal Strikes (reachable at 60 ft. as ranged poison bolts, 5d6+3 each) from inside or at the edge of the darkness where enemies can't see it, then use Rampage (bonus action after damaging a Bloodied target) to step in for a bonus-action Abyssal Strike — chain this to finish wounded PCs and keep temp HP stacking. Focus fire on whoever fails the save and is Bloodied, because Rampage turns every hit into two attacks per round while it kites half its speed between engagements. Hold concentration on the darkness as long as it's feeding it temp HP; if the party spreads out or silence/concentration-break threats appear, drop it and switch to two-handed ranged focus fire. It's a 135 hp fiend with +3 poison at +6 to hit — grind fights favor it, but if it loses darkness and half its hp, fall back through its own magical darkness where only it can navigate.

name: Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The gnoll makes one Bite attack and two Bone Flail attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the gnoll's next turn.

actions.name: Bone Flail
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Rampage
bonus_actions.description: Immediately after dealing damage to a creature that is already Bloodied, the gnoll moves up to half its Speed, and it makes one Bite attack.

flavor_text:
Yeenoghu claims gnolls not as his brood but as maggots purposefully released to infest a despised carcass. They are a pernicious rot the Beast of Butchery spreads across mortal worlds. Whatever they once were, they were remade and are now his.
—Iggwilv, Demonomicon of Iggwilv
description: Gnolls celebrate their victories by performing demonic rituals and making blood offerings to Yeenoghu. Sometimes the demon lord rewards his worshipers by allowing one of them to be possessed by a demonic spirit. Marked as Yeenoghu's favorite, the lucky recipient becomes a fang of Yeenoghu, the chosen of the Gnoll Lord. In much the same way Yeenoghu created the first gnolls, a hyena that feasts on a fang's slain foe undergoes a horrible transformation, becoming a full­ grown adult gnoll. Depending on the number of hyenas in a region, a fang of Yeenoghu can lead to a startling increase in the gnoll population. Finding and killing the fang is the only way to keep that population in check.
combat-strategy: Use its Bone Flail reach (10 ft.) to attack from just outside enemy counterattack range with two strikes, plus Bite to apply the Poisoned condition (disadvantage on the victim's attacks) — lock down a martial striker with poison and win the action economy battle. Once a foe is Bloodied (halved hp), Rampage gives a bonus-action Bite: sequence Bone Flail → Bloodied target → bonus Bite to move in for the kill, then shift to the next victim at flail range. Bite a spellcaster or duelist early to saddle them with disadvantage, then flail them freely; the +5 to hit punishes low-AC backline targets. Fight in packs with regular gnolls so enemies face reach from every side, and use 10 ft. reach to control the perimeter of the pack fight. At around 20 hp or after losing half its squad, fall back and let the pack screen it — fangs are predators, not martyrs, and prefer wounded prey over whole walls of shields.

name: Gnoll Pack Lord

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The gnoll makes two attacks, using Bone Whip or Bone Javelin in any combination, and it uses Incite Rampage if available.

actions.name: Bone Whip
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Bone Javelin
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +5, range 30/120 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Incite Rampage
actions.description: The gnoll targets another creature it can see within 60 feet of itself that has the Rampage Bonus Action. The target can take a Reaction to make one melee attack.

bonus_actions.name: Rampage
bonus_actions.description: Immediately after dealing damage to a creature that is already Bloodied, the gnoll moves up to half its Speed, and it makes one Bone Whip attack.

description: The alpha of a gnoll pack is the pack lord, ruling by might and cunning. A pack lord earns the best of a gnoll pack's spoils, food, valuable trinkets, and magic items. It ornaments its body with brutal piercings and grotesque trophies, dyeing its fur with demonic sigils, hoping Yeenoghu will make it invulnerable.
combat-strategy: Open with Incite Rampage on a Bloodied target — a nearby gnoll with Rampage gets a free reaction melee attack, effectively adding an extra attack to the pack's first volley — then Multiattack Bone Whip (10 ft. reach) or Bone Javelin (thrown 30 ft.) in any mix to soften from reach. Position in the second rank where the whip's 10 ft. reach lets it hit without being reached, using javelins first on closing charges, then whip once melee merges. Chain Rampage on itself after any Bone Whip hit lands on a Bloodied foe — move and whip again — and keep Incite Rampage going every round it's available to multiply its gnolls' output; protecting it is the pack's real objective. Target PCs who drop to half hp near the pack; the reaction attacks from Incite Rampage punish anyone who steps into reach to rescue them. It's only 49 hp — if the pack breaks or it drops below ~15 hp, withdraw behind loyal gnolls or flee into terrain the party must slow down to traverse; the pack fights harder while the lord lives.

name: Gnoll Warrior

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Bone Bow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +3, range 150/600 ft. Hit: 6 (1d10 + 1) Piercing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Rampage
bonus_actions.description: Immediately after dealing damage to a creature that is already Bloodied, the gnoll moves up to half its Speed, and it makes one Rend attack.

combat-strategy: Volley with the Bone Bow (150 ft., +3) from cover or behind allies first, then close with Rend when the enemy commits to melee; never open by charging into a wall of shields alone. The bonus-action Rampage is the win condition: focus attacks on an already-Bloodied PC to chain move-and-Rend for free extra damage, so spread damage across the party to create Bloodied targets rather than finishing one at a time. Fight in coordinated pairs or trios — swarm to flank, cutting off retreat so wounded prey can't back away from the Rampage chain. Use darkvision and underbrush to shadow a retreating party, firing bone arrows to bleed them before the melee finish. Individually it's fragile (27 hp); break off and re-hide once badly wounded, but gnoll discipline (none) means it more often fights savagely until downed unless the pack routs.

name: Goat

actions.name: Ram
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Bludgeoning damage, or 2 (1d4) Bludgeoning damage if the goat moved 20+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit.

conditional_damage.condition: moved 20+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit

combat-strategy: This is a nuisance, not a combatant — but a goat that runs 20+ ft. straight at a target gets double Ram damage (2 bludgeoning), so stampede-charge down a corridor or slope at an isolated, low-AC target, ideally a wizard mid-spell, where 1–2 damage plus the shock of a charging animal still matters in a farmyard brawl. Use 40 ft. speed and 30 ft. climb to bounce the fight onto stairs, wagons, or rocky terrain it can scale and pursuers can't. In a herd scenario, spook multiple goats into a charging mob so the party faces a stampede of minor ram damage and difficult movement around overturned stalls and market goods. It won't fight anything that looks dangerous — startled, it bolts; run it as panicked chaos, an obstacle and comic distraction that turns ugly only when cornered with a clear charging lane.

name: Goblin

actions.name: Scimitar
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.

actions.name: Shortbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

traits.name: Nimble Escape
traits.description: The goblin can take the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action on each of its turns.

description:
Goblins are small, black-hearted, selfish humanoids that lair in caves, abandoned mines, despoiled dungeons, and other dismal settings. Individually weak, goblins gather in large-sometimes overwhelming-numbers. They crave power and regularly abuse whatever authority they obtain.

Goblinoids. Goblins belong to a family of creatures called goblinoids. Their larger cousins, hobgoblins and bugbears, like to bully goblins into submission. Goblins are lazy and undisciplined, making them poor servants, laborers, and guards.

Malicious Glee. Motivated by greed and malice, goblins can't help but celebrate the few times they have the upper hand. They dance, caper with sheer joy when victory is theirs. Once their revels have ended, goblins delight in the torment of other creatures and embrace all manner of wickedness.

Leaders and Followers. Goblins are ruled by the strongest or smartest among them. A goblin boss might command a single lair, while a goblin king or queen (who is nothing more than a glorified goblin boss) rules hundreds of goblins, spread out among multiple lairs to ensure the tribe's survival. Goblin bosses are easily ousted, and many goblin tribes are taken over by hobgoblin warlords or bugbear chiefs.

Challenging Lairs. Goblins festoon their lairs with alarms designed to signal the arrival of intruders. Those lairs are also riddled with narrow tunnels and bolt-holes that human-sized creatures can't navigate, but which goblins can crawl through with ease, allowing them to flee or to circle around and surprise their enemies.

Rat Keepers and WolfRiders. Goblins have an affinity for rats and wolves, raising them to serve as companions and mounts, respectively. Like rats, goblins shun sunlight and sleep underground during the day. Like wolves, they are pack hunters, made bolder by their numbers. When they hunt from the backs of wolves, goblins use hit-and-run attacks.

Worshipers of Maglubiyet. Maglubiyet the Mighty One, the Lord of Depths and Darkness, is the greater god of goblinoids. Envisioned by most goblins as an eleven-foot-tall battle-scarred goblin with black skin and fire erupting from his eyes, he is worshiped not out of adoration but fear. Goblins believe that when they die in battle, their spirits join the ranks of Maglubiyet's army on the plane ofAcheron. This is a "privilege" that most goblins dread, fearing the Mighty One's eternal tyranny even more than death.
combat-strategy: Open with Shortbow (+4, 80 ft.) shots from behind cover, then use Nimble Escape (bonus action Hide or Disengage) to vanish into brush, dark corners, or behind furniture — goblins rarely fight fair and never fight face-forward. Hit-and-run in pairs: fire, hide, let the archer next to them gain hidden-attacker advantage, and melt away when the party advances. Scimitar only against a separated, wounded, or distracted PC, jabbing in with advantage from hiding then Disengaging before the counterattack lands. 7 hp means any solid hit kills — the moment it's spotted and engaged in the open it should flee, using Stealth +6 and Small size to slip through cracks, under tables, and into tunnels. Ambush the baggage bearer, the straggler, the sentry asleep; never the whole party at once.

name: Goblin Boss

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The goblin makes two attacks, using Scimitar or Shortbow in any combination.

actions.name: Scimitar
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Slashing damage, plus 2 (1d4) Slashing damage if the attack roll had Advantage.

actions.name: Shortbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 80/320 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage, plus 2 (1d4) Piercing damage if the attack roll had Advantage.

bonus_actions.name: Nimble Escape
bonus_actions.description: The goblin takes the Disengage or Hide action.

reactions.name: Redirect Attack
reactions.trigger: A creature the goblin can see makes an attack roll against it.
reactions.description: The goblin chooses a Small or Medium ally within 5 feet of itself. The goblin and that ally swap places, and the ally becomes the target of the attack instead.

description: Goblins are ruled by the strongest or smartest among them. A goblin boss might command a single lair, while a goblin king or queen (who is nothing more than a glorified goblin boss) rules hundreds of goblins, spread out among multiple lairs to ensure the tribe's survival. Goblin bosses are easily ousted, and many goblin tribes are taken over by hobgoblin warlords or bugbear chiefs.
combat-strategy: Fight from behind cover with two attacks per round (Scimitar/Shortbow mix), banking the +1d4 bonus damage by engineering Advantage — hidden openings, flanking with minions, or attacking Frightened/Prone foes. Use Redirect Attack (reaction) to swap places with a nearby goblin minion when a big attack or spell targets it, taking hits off itself and dumping punishment onto expendable underlings; keep one goblin within 5 ft. at all times as a human shield. Nimble Escape lets it fire two shots then Hide as a bonus action — the classic archer-boss loop — so kiting from rubble, rafters, or behind wagons makes it nearly untargetable. 21 hp and AC 17 make it dangerous but not durable: once minions fall and the party focuses, flee through back tunnels, climbing routes, or escape routes prepared for exactly this, stealing loot as it goes. Ambush at chokepoints: fire, swap with a minion when punished, reposition, repeat.

name: Goblin Hexer

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The goblin makes two Hex Stick attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting.

actions.name: Hex Stick
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The goblin casts one of the following spells, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13): At Will: Minor Illusion 1/Day Each: Blindness/Deafness, Faerie Fire, Grease

reactions.name: Jinx
reactions.trigger: A creature the goblin can see hits it with an attack roll.
reactions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, the triggering creature. Failure: The attack misses instead.

combat-strategy: Open by opening the fight with Hex Stick shots (+5, 60 ft., 12 psychic) from cover while opening with a debuff: Grease at the entry chokepoint (prone and drop concentration on spellcasting), Faerie Fire on hidden rogues or invisible scouts, or Blindness/Deafness on the party's best attacker or spellcaster. Its Jinx reaction (DC 13 Wis) is the star defense — a failed save makes an incoming attack miss entirely; save it for the biggest attack of each round, and never waste it on a multiattack opener whose first swing lands. Fight backline, behind cover or its own illusions (Minor Illusion, at will) with Stealth +7, using its 60 ft. ranged Hex Stick to punish clumped or trapped targets whose saves already failed. Split the party: Grease a doorway behind the tanks while Blinding their marksman, then snipe panicked targets as they bunch up. 45 hp with AC 13 is soft — once spotted and pressured it should Nimble-Escape via its own Grease and illusion cover into back passages, popping out to snipe from new positions.

name: Goblin Minion

actions.name: Dagger
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Piercing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Nimble Escape
bonus_actions.description: The goblin takes the Disengage or Hide action.

combat-strategy: Expendable numbers are the strategy: swarm in with daggers (+4, 5 piercing), six of them turning one attack per body into a tide of small cuts, and use Nimble Escape to Hide behind barrels, undergrowth, or each other between shots. Thrown daggers (20/60 ft.) let a line of minions soften a corridor before melee, then Disengage as a bonus action and drop from the firing line when the party charges. Fight only from ambush, advantage, or against wounded and isolated targets — a single area spell, trampling mount, or unlucky crit eats one whole, and the pack should shatter the moment it takes real casualties. Corner them and they'll still fight when commanded, but their instinct is hit, hide, repeat; once half the pack is down the survivors flee to the boss, spreading panic and pulling the party into deeper traps.

name: Goblin Warrior

actions.name: Scimitar
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Slashing damage, plus 2 (1d4) Slashing damage if the attack roll had Advantage.

actions.name: Shortbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 80/320 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage, plus 2 (1d4) Piercing damage if the attack roll had Advantage.

bonus_actions.name: Nimble Escape
bonus_actions.description: The goblin takes the Disengage or Hide action.

combat-strategy: Open with Shortbow shots from cover or partially obscured positions, then use Nimble Escape as a bonus action to Hide or Disengage after firing. Both Scimitar and Shortbow add +2 (1d4) damage when the attack roll had Advantage, so engineer Advantage constantly: attack prone, restrained, or flanked targets, and have other goblins help or shove. Never fight fair in open melee — a 10 HP goblin that loses Advantage and is exposed should Hide and relocate. In packs, surround a separated PC together and drop the body with concentrated scimitar hits before it finishes killing your friends.

name: Gold Dragon Wyrmling

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The dragon can breathe air and water.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dragon makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Fire Breath
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: 22 (4d10) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Half damage

actions.name: Weakening Breath
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature that isn't currently affected by this breath in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: The target has Disadvantage on Strength-based D20 Tests and subtracts 2 (1d4) from its damage rolls. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.
actions.save_effect: The target has Disadvantage on Strength-based D20 Tests and subtracts 2 (1d4) from its damage rolls. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

combat-strategy: Open from the air with Fire Breath down a 15-foot cone onto the tightest cluster of enemies — 22 fire damage at DC 13 is its alpha strike. Save Weakening Breath for the biggest Strength-dependent threat (greatsword brute, grappling barbarian, archer); the -2 damage and Strength disadvantage cripples martial damage while the target keeps re-rolling. Use flyby attacks: dive, Multiattack two Rend attacks, and ascend out of melee reach rather than standing in the scrum where 60 HP evaporates fast. Amphibious escape into deep water is a get-out-of-jail card when cornered.

name: Gorgon

actions.name: Gore
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 18 (2d12 + 5) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature and the gorgon moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Petrifying Breath
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. First Failure: The target has the Restrained condition and repeats the save at the end of its next turn if it is still Restrained, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second Failure: The target has the Petrified condition instead of the Restrained condition.
actions.save_effect: First Failure: The target has the Restrained condition and repeats the save at the end of its next turn if it is still Restrained, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second Failure: The target has the Petrified condition instead of the Restrained condition.

bonus_actions.name: Trample
bonus_actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 16, one creature within 5 feet that has the Prone condition. Failure: 16 (2d10 + 5) Bludgeoning damage. Success: Half damage.

description:
Few creatures that encounter a gorgon live to tell about it. Its body is covered in iron plates, and its nostrils fume with green vapor.

Horrific Structure. A gorgon's iron plates range from steely black to gleaming silver, but this natural armor in no way hinders its movement or mobility. The oils of its body lubricate the armor. A sick or inactive gorgon gathers rust like fungus or mange. When a rusty gorgon moves, its plates squeal as they rub together.

Monstrous Predator. When a gorgon spots potential prey, it charges with a hideous clamor of metal on metal. When the gorgon hits, it pulverizes the foe and sends its sprawling, then tramples it to death with its cruel hooves. Faced with multiple foes, the gorgon exhales its deadly vapor to overcome the creatures it touches by turning them to stone. When it grows hungry, it smashes its petrified prey to rubble and uses its strong teeth to grind the stone into a powder that provides nourishment. The crisscrossing network of trampled trails and splintered trees that surrounds a gorgon lair is strewn with the uneaten fragments of its shattered foes.
combat-strategy: Lead with Petrifying Breath into a crowd — a first failed save Restrains the target, granting Advantage on the Gore charge that follows, and a second fail petrifies them outright; prioritize low-Constitution humanoids. In melee, use its 40-foot movement to loop 20+ feet straight at a target, Gore for 18 piercing plus knockdown, then Trample the prone victim as a bonus action for another 16 bludgeoning. Chain the sequence: cone, charge-knockdown, trample, repeat on the next victim. It is an unthinking construct that fights to the death, so lean on terrain funnels and chokepoints to maximize cone coverage.

name: Goristro

traits.name: Demonic Restoration
traits.description: If the goristro dies outside the Abyss, its body dissolves into ichor, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Abyss.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The goristro has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Siege Monster
traits.description: The goristro deals double damage to objects and structures.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The goristro makes one Brutal Gore attack and two Slam attacks.

actions.name: Brutal Gore
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +13, reach 10 ft. Hit: 40 (6d10 + 7) Piercing damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it is pushed up to 20 feet straight away from the goristro and has the Prone condition.
actions.save_effect: If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it is pushed up to 20 feet straight away from the goristro and has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +13, reach 10 ft. Hit: 29 (4d10 + 7) Bludgeoning damage.

bonus_actions.name: Charge
bonus_actions.description: The goristro moves up to half its Speed straight toward an enemy it can see.

description:
The goristro resembles a fiendish minotaur towering more than twenty feet tall. When controlled by a demon lord, goristros make formidable living siege engines and prized pets. Goristros possess preternatural cunning when navigating labyrinthine passages and shifting corridors, pursuing foes in a terrifying hunt.
A hulking goristro sometimes bears a palanquin, carrying smaller demons on its broad shoulders, much like an elephant carries riders on its back.
combat-strategy: Turn its 50-foot walk into a demolition run: use Charge as a bonus action to close, then Brutal Gore for 40 piercing, hurling the target 20 feet away and knocking them Prone, followed by two Slams on anyone still in 10-foot reach. Siege Monster doubles damage to doors, walls, and towers — breach fortifications rather than dueling in the open, and let falling rubble scatter the party. Magic Resistance makes banishment, hold monster, and power word attempts unreliable, so presume control fails. It never routs outside the Abyss (Demonic Restoration), so the battle is about survival and delay: keep moving forward, trample the fallen, and focus the squishiest backline casters it can reach.

name: Graveyard Revenant

traits.name: Undead Restoration
traits.description: If the revenant dies, it revives 24 hours later unless Dispel Evil and Good is cast on its remains. If it revives, it animates another group of corpses elsewhere on the same plane of existence; it now looks different but uses the same stat block and returns with all its Hit Points.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The revenant makes two Suffocate attacks.

actions.name: Suffocate
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 10 (1d10 + 5) Bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 15). Until the grapple ends, the target is suffocating. The revenant can have up to two targets Grappled in this way at a time.

actions.name: Haunting Glare
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the revenant. Failure: The target has the Paralyzed condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Paralyzed condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

combat-strategy: Open with Haunting Glare on the clustered party — Paralysis at DC 15 (Wisdom) shuts down multiple PCs for a round — then wade in with Suffocate to grapple two victims, each taking bite-equivalent bludgeoning plus 10 necrotic and slowly suffocating in its grip. Pin the healer or archer first, since a grappled target bleeding necrotic while paralyzed allies watch is nearly unstoppable without action economy against it. Its 40-foot speed closes kiting attempts; drag grappled victims out of reach of their friends. If destroyed it returns in 24 hours, so the real counter is Dispel Evil and Good on its remains — hint this through lore before the second fight.

name: Gray Ooze

traits.name: Amorphous
traits.description: The ooze can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

traits.name: Corrosive Form
traits.description: Nonmagical ammunition is destroyed immediately after hitting the ooze and dealing any damage. Any nonmagical weapon takes a cumulative −1 penalty to attack rolls immediately after dealing damage to the ooze and coming into contact with it. The weapon is destroyed if the penalty reaches −5. The penalty can be removed by casting the Mending spell on the weapon. The ooze can eat through 2-inch-thick, nonmagical metal or wood in 1 round.

actions.name: Pseudopod
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d8 + 1) Acid damage. Nonmagical armor worn by the target takes a −1 penalty to the AC it offers. The armor is destroyed if the penalty reduces its AC to 10. The penalty can be removed by casting the Mending spell on the armor.

description: A gray ooze is stone turned to liquid by chaos. When it moves, it slithers like a liquid snake, rising to strike.
combat-strategy: Ambush from above or from a disguised patch of floor: it has Stealth +2, blindsight, and 10-foot speed, so surprise and chokepoints are the whole encounter. Let martial attackers swing — Corrosive Form makes every nonmagical hit destroy ammunition and chew -1 off their weapon until it breaks, punishing the party economically more than hit points do. Target armored PCs with Pseudopod to drag AC down toward destruction, then keep coating them in acid. It cannot chase, so pick tunnels, stairwells, and doorways where prey must come to it, and drip through 1-inch cracks to escape being sealed off.

name: Gray Slaad

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The slaad has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.description: The slaad regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns if it has at least 1 Hit Point.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The slaad makes two Chaos Claw attacks.

actions.name: Chaos Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Slashing damage plus 11 (2d10) Necrotic damage. Until the start of the slaad's next turn, the target has a condition determined by rolling 1d4: on a 1, Charmed; on a 2, Frightened; on a 3, Poisoned; or on a 4, Incapacitated.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The slaad casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16): At Will: Detect Magic, Detect Thoughts, Invisibility (self only), Mage Hand, Major Image 1/Day Each: Cloudkill, Fly, Plane Shift (self only), Tongues

bonus_actions.name: Shape-Shift
bonus_actions.description: The slaad shape-shifts into a Small or Medium Humanoid, or it returns to its true form. Other than its size, its game statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

description:
Outside of Limbo, gray slaadi act as living extensions of the will of their masters, the death slaadi. A gray slaad journeys to the Material Plane on errands of doom, often taking humanoid form. A gray slaad learns how to master the use of a greatsword and imbue it with its own innate magic.
A gray slaad that eats the entire corpse of a dead death slaad instantly transforms into a death slaad.
combat-strategy: Open combat (or an infiltration) with Invisibility, use Detect Thoughts to read the party's plan, then land two Chaos Claws from 10-foot reach — each hit slaps on a random condition (Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned, or Incapacitated) that punishes the target while the slaad's Magic Resistance blunts retaliation. Regeneration 10 per turn means Disengage-and-regroup is always viable: disengage, reposition 40 feet, and dare them to burst you down before you recover. Fly + Cloudkill turns the battlefield into a kill zone for the low-Constitution party members while you rain claws from the air. Only Plane Shift out when reduced to single-digit hit points, since 10 HP/turn regen makes it nearly immortal at range.

name: Green Dragon Wyrmling

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) poison damage.

actions.name: Poison Breath
actions.description: The dragon exhales poisonous gas in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 11 Constitution saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
actions.save_effect: The target takes 21 (6d6) Poison damage. Success: Half damage.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The dragon can breathe air and water.

combat-strategy: Open with Poison Breath (DC 11 Constitution, 21 poison damage) onto the tightest formation, then hit-and-run with its 60-foot fly — never land in a melee cluster with only 38 hit points. Its Bite adds poison damage and it is immune to poison, so cloud or grease terrain it creates costs it nothing. Green dragons are schemers: use forest or swamp canopy for cover, dive from behind foliage, and bluff with feigned retreat to split the party. Target the weakest-looking or lowest-Constitution members with the cone, and douse any mundane fires it might fear by staying over water where its Amphibious trait wins the escape.

name: Green Hag

actions.name: Claws
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage.

actions.name: Illusory Appearance
actions.description:
The hag covers herself and anything she is wearing or carrying with a magical illusion that makes her look like another creature of her general size and humanoid shape. The illusion ends if the hag takes a bonus action to end it or if she dies.
The changes wrought by this effect fail to hold up to physical inspection. For example, the hag could appear to have smooth skin, but someone touching her would feel her rough flesh. Otherwise, a creature must take an action to visually inspect the illusion and succeed on a DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check to discern that the hag is disguised.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target can't perceive the hag and is blinded until the illusion ends.

actions.name: Invisible Passage
actions.description: The hag magically turns invisible until she attacks or casts a spell, or until her concentration ends (as if concentrating on a spell). While invisible, she leaves no physical evidence of her passage, so she can be tracked only by magic. Any equipment she wears or carries is invisible with her.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The hag can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Innate Spellcasting
traits.description:
The hag's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 12). She can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

At will: dancing lights, minor illusion, vicious mockery

traits.name: Mimicry
traits.description: The hag can mimic animal sounds and humanoid voices. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) check.

description:
The wretched and hateful green hags dwell in dying forests, lonely swamps, and misty moors, making their homes in caves. Green hags love to manipulate other creatures into doing their bidding, masking their intentions behind layers of deception. They lure victims to them by mimicking voices calling out for help, or drive unwanted visitors away by imitating the cries of fierce beasts.

Obsession with Tragedy. Green hags revel in the failings and tragedies of other creatures. They derive joy from bringing people low and seeing hope turn into despair, not just for individuals but also for whole nations.

Covens. A green hag that is part of a coven (see the "Hag Covens" sidebar) has a challenge rating of 5 (1,800 XP).
combat-strategy: Lure victims off the trail with Mimicry — a child's cry or a distressed voice — then strike with Claws (13 slashing) from ambush, using Illusory Appearance to look like a harmless refugee until the killing moment. Invisible Passage lets it reposition mid-fight, steal keys, children, or gear, and vanish without a trace; attack, go invisible, relocate, repeat. Vicious Mockery at will is the answer to the party's spellcaster — advantage-free noise that taxes Wisdom saves while the hag's 17 AC soaks the rest. Fight in deep forest or murky water where its 82 HP stretch, and flee into the wilds when bloodied, dragging stolen prey with her.

name: Green Slaad

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The slaad makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws or staff. Alternatively, it uses its Hurl Flame twice.

actions.name: Bite (Slaad Form Only).
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage.

actions.name: Claw (Slaad Form Only)
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage.

actions.name: Staff
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Hurl Flame
actions.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +4 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (3d6) fire damage. The fire ignites flammable objects that aren't being worn or carried.

traits.name: Shapechanger
traits.description: The slaad can use its action to polymorph into a Small or Medium humanoid, or back into its true form. Its statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

traits.name: Innate Spellcasting
traits.description:
The slaad's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 12). The slaad can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

At will: detect magic, detect thoughts, invisibility (self only), mage hand
2/day each: fear, invisibility (self only)
1/day: fireball

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The slaad has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.description: The slaad regains 10 hit points at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 hit point.

description:
Green slaadi are surprisingly intelligent and possess innate spellcasting ability. A green slaad can change its shape to appear as a humanoid. If it was born of a humanoid host, the slaad usually adopts its host's form.
At some unpredictable point in its existence, a green slaad unlocks the means to magically, instantly, and permanently transform itself into a gray slaad. Unlocking this knowledge can take years, even decades.
combat-strategy: Open at range with Multiattack → two Hurl Flame (20 fire damage total) while its fire, acid, cold, and lightning resistances make most party damage weak. Shape-Shift into a trusted humanoid to infiltrate before combat even starts, and use Invisibility and Fear (DC 12) to scatter the party so you can isolate a straggler for bite-and-claws melee. Fireball once per day only into a genuinely clustered group — its 127 HP and Regeneration 10 favor attrition, not alpha strikes. When focused down, Disengage (or turn invisible), let regeneration tick, and re-engage elsewhere; retreat to water or a portal when the fight turns hopeless.

name: Grell

traits.name: Abduct
traits.description: The grell needn't spend extra movement to move a creature it is grappling.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The grell makes one Beak attack and one Paralyzing Tentacles attack.

actions.name: Beak
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d8 + 2) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Paralyzing Tentacles
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 10 ft. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 12) from two of ten tentacles. The target is also subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 11. Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically. While Poisoned, the target has the Paralyzed condition.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Poisoned condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically. While Poisoned, the target has the Paralyzed condition.

description:
A grell resembles a bulbous floating brain with a wide, sharp beak. Its ten long tentacles are made of hundreds of ring-shaped muscles sheathed in tough fibrous hide. Sharp barbs line the tip each tentacle and inject paralytic venom. The grell can partially retract its barbs into its tentacles to handle or manipulate objects it doesn't want to pierce or tear.
Grells have no eyes and floats by means of a sort of levitation. They have keen hearing, however, and their skin is sensitive to vibrations and electrical fields, allowing them to detect the presence of creatures and objects in their immediate vicinity. The creature's ability to manipulate electricity to sense and move also allow it to absorb lightning without harm.
Although solitary by nature, grells sometimes gather in small groups called covens.

Floating Ambushers. A grell prefers to ambush lone creatures or stragglers, hovering silently near the ceiling of a passage or cavern until a suitable target passes below, whereupon it descends quickly and wraps its tentacles around its prey. It then floats away to its lair with the paralyzed creature in its clutches.

Alien Devourers. Grell are alien predators that group other creatures into three categories: edibles, inedibles, and Great Eaters (those rare creatures that might prey on a grel1). Grells have no compunction about attacking creatures they classify as edible, including humanoids. They tend to avoid bigger creatures that they have little hope of carrying away.
A grell will sometimes allow adventurers to wage war on the other monstrous inhabitants of the dungeon complex it calls home, staying out of the adventurers' way as they dispose of larger threats while waiting for the right time to strike.
combat-strategy: Hover and grapple: Paralyzing Tentacles (reach 10) Grapples a Medium-or-smaller target and, on a failed DC 11 Constitution save, chains Poisoned → Paralyzed — a helpless victim the grell can peck with Beak for free Advantage damage each round. Use Abduct to lift the paralyzed prey straight up off the battlefield and carry it away, forcing the party into desperate climbing or ranged shots with the hostage at risk. Its 10-foot walk means it must stay airborne; fight over pits, water, or cliffs where a carried PC is doomed without quick rescue. Target isolated backline members at the edge of the formation, and flee upward into caves or canopy when the party's ranged damage starts stacking.

name: Grick

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The grick makes one Beak attack and one Tentacles attack.

actions.name: Beak
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Tentacles
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) Slashing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 12) from all four tentacles.

description:
The wormlike grick waits unseen, blending in with the rock of the caves and caverns it haunts. Only when prey comes near does it rear up, its four barbed tentacles unfurling to reveal its hungry, snapping beak.

Passive Predators. Gricks rarely hunt. Instead, they drag their rubbery bodies to places where creatures regularly pass, lurking out of sight amid rocky rubble and debris, squeezing into burrows, holes, or crevices, climbing up to ledges, or coiling around stalactites to drop on unwary prey. A grick consumes virtually anything that moves except for other gricks. It targets the nearest prey, grabbing a fallen creature with its tentacles and dragging it off to eat alone.

Roving Ambushers. Gricks remain in an area until the food supply dwindles, often because sentient creatures become aware of their presence and plot alternate routes around their lairs. When prey is scarce in the Underdark, gricks venture aboveground to hunt in the wilderness, lurking in trees or on cliff-side ledges. A grick pack is often led by a single well-fed, oversized alpha around which the others congregate.

Spoils of Slaughter. Over time, grick lairs accumulate the cast-off possessions of intelligent prey, and expert guides know to look out for these telltale signs. Underdark explorers sometimes seal off the routes leading to and from a grick lair to starve them, then claim the wealth of the foul creatures' victims.
combat-strategy: Ambush predator: hang from a cave ceiling or burrow in rubble, then drop onto the rearmost explorer with Multiattack Beak + Tentacles, Grappled (escape DC 12) by all four tentacles. Use its 30-foot climb speed to drag prey up walls or into cracks where allies can't reach, then reposition vertically between rounds — hit, climb, vanish into stone crevices. It has no special durability (54 HP, AC 14), so fights that go long in the open are losses: commit hard in the surprise round, then kite through vertical terrain. Attack alone or in pairs, never in the open daylight.

name: Grick Alpha

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The grick makes two attacks: one with its tail and one with its tentacles. If it hits with its tentacles, the grick can make one beak attack against the same target.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Tentacles
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (4d8 + 4) slashing damage.

actions.name: Beak
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage.

traits.name: Stone Camouflage
traits.description: The grick has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in rocky terrain.

description:
The wormlike grick waits unseen, blending in with the rock of the caves and caverns it haunts. Only when prey comes near does it rear up, its four barbed tentacles unfurling to reveal its hungry, snapping beak.

Passive Predators. Gricks rarely hunt. Instead, they drag their rubbery bodies to places where creatures regularly pass, lurking out of sight amid rocky rubble and debris, squeezing into burrows, holes, or crevices, climbing up to ledges, or coiling around stalactites to drop on unwary prey. A grick consumes virtually anything that moves except for other gricks. It targets the nearest prey, grabbing a fallen creature with its tentacles and dragging it off to eat alone.

Roving Ambushers. Gricks remain in an area until the food supply dwindles, often because sentient creatures become aware of their presence and plot alternate routes around their lairs. When prey is scarce in the Underdark, gricks venture aboveground to hunt in the wilderness, lurking in trees or on cliff-side ledges. A grick pack is often led by a single well-fed, oversized alpha around which the others congregate.

Spoils of Slaughter. Over time, grick lairs accumulate the cast-off possessions of intelligent prey, and expert guides know to look out for these telltale signs. Underdark explorers sometimes seal off the routes leading to and from a grick lair to starve them, then claim the wealth of the foul creatures' victims.
combat-strategy: Ambush from stone camouflage in rocky terrain, then use its 10-foot reach to control the frontline: Multiattack Tail + Tentacles, and if the Tentacles hit, chain a free Beak attack for a triple-strike round of up to 46 damage. Its 18 AC and resistance to nonmagical weapons mean low-level martial parties literally cannot hurt it — lean into the exchange and punish every missed swing. Keep the big body between the party's melee fighters and their casters, using 10-foot reach on whoever edges close. Retreat into deep crevices only when a magical weapon or heavy damage starts landing.

name: Grick Ancient

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The grick makes one Beak attack, one Slam attack, and one Tentacles attack.

actions.name: Beak
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 22 (4d8 + 4) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Tentacles
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Slashing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from all four tentacles.

combat-strategy: Open from ambush (Stealth +6) with Multiattack: Beak for 22 piercing, Slam to knock the target Prone, and Tentacles to Grapple (DC 14) them — a pinned, prone victim takes full multiattack every round while stuck under 10-foot reach tentacles. Grapple the biggest melee threat to neutralize it, then let the 135 HP body endure retaliation while tentacle slash and beak grind the victim down. Fight in tunnels, ruins, or caves where its 30-foot climb speed and huge frame dominate and the party can't surround it effectively. It has no ranged options, so force the party to come through its claimed corridor; withdraw into unmappable cracks if driven off.

name: Griffon

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The griffon makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from both of the griffon's front claws.

description:
Griffons are ferocious avian carnivores with the muscular bodies of lions and the head, forelegs, and wings of eagles. When they attack, griffons are as swift and deadly as eagles, even as they strike with a lion's savage might and grace.

Horse Eaters. Griffons hunt in small prides, flying high over plains and forests near their rocky cliff-side aeries. Herd animals and horses are the prey they crave above all others, though they also hunt and kill hippogriffs. When it spots horses, a griffon screeches to alert its pride mates, which descend quickly toward their prey.
Those riding or herding horses dread the griffon's piercing cry, preparing themselves for the bloody fight that inevitably follows. A griffon ignores a horse's rider when possible, and a rider that abandons its mount, or a herder that releases one or two horses, can escape unharmed while the griffon targets its chosen prey. Riders who attempt to protect their horses attract the full fury of an attacking griffon.

Sky Dwellers. Griffons lair in high rocky clifftop aeries, building their nests from sticks, leaves, and the bones of their prey. Once griffons establish a territory, they remain in that area until the food supply has been exhausted.
Aggressive and territorial, griffons engage in brutal aerial combat to defend their aeries, tearing and shredding the wings of flying intruders to send them spiraling to the ground. Creatures that climb to a griffon's lair are plucked from the cliffs and eaten, or are knocked from the heights to go tumbling to their deaths.

Trained Mounts. A griffon raised from an egg can be trained to serve as a mount. However, such training is time consuming, expensive (mostly for the ample food the creature requires), and dangerous. Expert trainers well versed in the griffon's legendary ferocity are typically the only ones able to raise these creatures safely.
Once trained, a griffon is a fierce and loyal steed. It bonds with one master for life, fighting to the death to protect that rider. A griffon mount retains its ravenous appetite for horseflesh, and a wise master ensures that a griffon remains satiated with other prey when passing through civilized lands.
combat-strategy: Strike from the air: dive with Multiattack Rend, each hit Grappling (DC 14) with both front claws — two hits mean the victim is pinned while the griffon tears at 8 piercing per claw. Fly upward with a grappled Medium-or-smaller prey and carry them toward cliffs or treetops, forcing the party to cut loose the victim or watch them drop. Use flyby attacks rather than landing; its 80-foot flight lets it dive, strike, and climb beyond melee reach every round. With only 59 HP and AC 12, disengage and circle once bloodied, then re-dive at a separated target; trained griffons fight alongside riders or in pairs.

name: Grimlock

actions.name: Bone Cudgel
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Bludgeoning damage plus 2 (1d4) Psychic damage.

description:
The degenerate subterranean grimlocks were once human, but their worship of the mind flayers over generations of prowling the Underdark transformed them into blind, monstrous cannibals long ago.

Debased Cultists. The empire of the mind flayers once spread across many worlds, enslaving countless races. Among those were human cultures whose high priests the mind flayers subverted using their insidious powers of thought control. Those leaders gradually turned the faiths of their followers toward the illithids, which they worshiped as blasphemous deities.
Over time, the rituals of these enslaved humans created fervent cannibal cults that regarded the brain eating of the mind flayers as a holy sacrament. The illithids commanded their worshipers to abduct other sentient creatures to be sacrificed. After the victims' brains had been consumed, the mind flayers gave the lifeless bodies to the cultists.

Blind Hunters. When the rule of the mind flayers crumbled, their cults faced constant warfare from their enemies, the same creatures that had once been their victims. The cults fled into the Underdark domains of their illithid gods. Over generations in that lightless realm, the cultists learned to rely on their other senses for survival. In time, their eyes withered away and eyelids sealed, leaving only covered eye sockets behind.
A grimlock's ears prick up at the faintest footfall or whisper echoing down stone passageways. It can speak in tones too lowfor most other humanoids to hear. The odors of sweat, flesh, and blood awaken its hunger, and it can track by such scents like a bloodhound. To enhance their senses, grimlocks leave trails of blood, piles of dung, or the viscera of slain prey in places far from their lairs. When intruders pass through those areas, they carry the foul scents with them, warning the grimlocks of their approach.
For most creatures, blindness is an enormous hindrance. For a grimlock with its other heightened senses, sightlessness is a boon. A grimlock isn't fooled byvisual illusions or misperceptions. It is fearless as it stalks prey.

Endless War. Grimlocks still venerate the mind flayers, serving them whenever possible. Grimlocks also recall the war in which they were driven underground. To them,it has never ended. They continue to return to the surface world to abduct captives for their illithid masters.
combat-strategy: Fight in pitch dark: 30-foot blindsight and 5 Stealth mean the grimlocks should snuff torches, lure the party into black tunnels, and swarm from the darkness where they effectively can't be seen. Bone Cudgel hits at +5 for bludgeoning plus psychic damage — gang up three or four on one isolated PC, beating them quietly and dragging the body back into the warrens. They are cowardly predators: flee into cracks and passages the moment an enemy lands a solid hit or bright magical light returns to the fight. Use noise — scraping, whispering, clanging bone — to terrify and misdirect before the ambush.

name: Guard

actions.name: Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) Piercing damage.

description: Guards include members of a city watch, sentries in a citadel or fortified town, and the bodyguards of merchants and nobles.
combat-strategy: Fight in formation with other guards: brace spears (reach) at chokepoints, doorways, and stairwells so attackers trigger Opportunity Attacks, and use the 20/60-foot spear range to jab at charging threats before they close. With only 11 HP, never stand alone — mutual protection, overlapping cover, and shield-wall discipline stretch their numbers. Their real weapon is the alarm: shout, ring bells, and buy seconds for reinforcements rather than trying to win the duel. Back off one step after a successful shove or block, hold the line, and let numbers do the killing.

name: Guard Captain

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The guard makes two attacks, using Javelin or Longsword in any combination.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Longsword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Slashing damage.

combat-strategy: Open at range with two Javelins (+6, 14 piercing each) at a priority target before the lines meet, then draw the Longsword and Multiattack for 30 slashing per round. Its 18 AC and 75 HP make it a frontline anchor: stand in a doorway or behind a spear wall of regular guards, protected while your javelins soften the first wave. Focus the party's healer or spellcaster once they reveal themselves — javelins at 30 feet punish casters who hold the back line. Rally retreating guards behind you; if the rank-and-file fall and you face the whole party alone at half health, fall back to a defensible position and hold for reinforcements.

name: Guardian Naga

traits.name: Celestial Restoration
traits.description: If the naga dies, it returns to life in 1d6 days and regains all its Hit Points unless Dispel Evil and Good is cast on its remains.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The naga makes two Bite attacks. It can replace any attack with a use of Poisonous Spittle.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 17 (2d12 + 4) Piercing damage plus 22 (4d10) Poison damage.

actions.name: Poisonous Spittle
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 16, one creature the naga can see within 60 feet. Failure: 31 (7d8) Poison damage, and the target has the Blinded condition until the start of the naga's next turn. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Blinded condition until the start of the naga's next turn.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The naga casts one of the following spells, requiring no Somatic or Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16):
At Will: Thaumaturgy
1/Day Each: Clairvoyance, Cure Wounds (level 6 version), Flame Strike (level 6 version), Geas, True Seeing

description:
Wise and good, the beautiful guardian nagas protect sacred places and items of magical power from falling into evil hands. In their hidden redoubts, they research spells and hatch convoluted plots to thwart the evil designs of their enemies.
A guardian naga doesn't seek out violence, warning off intruders rather than attacking. Only if its foes persist does the naga attack, accosting enemies with its spells and poisonous spittle.
combat-strategy: Open with Poisonous Spittle (DC 16, 31 poison damage plus Blinded) on the martial leader — a blinded warrior can't land the killing blows it needs. Stay at 10-foot Bite reach (17 piercing + 22 poison) or 60-foot standoff while delivering a 6th-level Flame Strike on clustered foes, and use 6th-level Cure Wounds to undo burst damage the moment it lands. Its 40-foot climb/swim speed lets it coil on columns, arches, or in temple pools — fight from vertical or submerged terrain where melee can't flank. True Seeing and Clairvoyance make stealth useless against it; use Geas on a captured trespasser for long-term leverage, and remember its Celestial Restoration means slaying it is temporary unless Dispel Evil and Good touches its remains.

name: Gulthias Blight

traits.name: Blight Seeds
traits.description: When it finishes a Long Rest, the blight expels 1d6 seeds into unoccupied spaces on the ground within 30 feet of itself. After 24 hours, the seeds become creatures under the blight's control. Roll 1d8 for each seed to determine the creature it becomes: on 1-4, Twig Blight; on 5-6, Needle Blight; on 7-8, Vine Blight.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The blight makes two attacks, using Slam or Thorn Volley in any combination. It also uses Life-Draining Root.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +12, reach 10 ft. Hit: 25 (4d8 + 7) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Thorn Volley
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +12, range 60/180 ft. Hit: 20 (3d8 + 7) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Life-Draining Root
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 20, one Huge or smaller creature the blight can see within 30 feet. Failure: 14 (2d6 + 7) Necrotic damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 17) from one of six roots. Until the grapple ends, the target has the Restrained condition and takes 14 (4d6) Necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns. The target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken, and the blight regains Hit Points equal to that amount.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 17) from one of six roots. Until the grapple ends, the target has the Restrained condition and takes 14 (4d6) Necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns. The target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken, and the blight regains Hit Points equal to that amount.

combat-strategy: It IS the battlefield: 264 HP, AC 20, 50-foot movement — march straight at the party and dare them to chew through it. Life-Draining Root (DC 20 Constitution) on the biggest threat Grapples and Restrains them, deals 4d6 necrotic each round, shrinks their hit point maximum permanently, and heals the blight — pin the healer or martial DPS first. Use Thorn Volley (60/180 ft.) to shell the back line and Slam to scatter clusters while grappled victims writhe. Its Blight Seeds turn every long rest into new blight minions, so it wants a slow war: let the party exhaust slots against it in the corrupted forest it poisons, and never retreat — retreat is for things that can be killed.

name: Gynosphinx
damage_resistances: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical weapons

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The sphinx makes two claw attacks.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage.

traits.name: Inscrutable
traits.description: The sphinx is immune to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, as well as any divination spell that it refuses. Wisdom (Insight) checks made to ascertain the sphinx's intentions or sincerity have disadvantage.

traits.name: Magic Weapons
traits.description: The sphinx's weapon attacks are magical.

traits.name: Spellcasting
traits.description:
The sphinx is a 9th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 16, +8 to hit with spell attacks). It requires no material components to cast its spells. The sphinx has the following wizard spells prepared:

Cantrips (at will): mage hand, minor illusion, prestidigitation
1st level (4 slots): detect magic, identify, shield
2nd level (3 slots): darkness, locate object, suggestion
3rd level (3 slots): dispel magic, remove curse, tongues
4th level (3 slots): banishment, greater invisibility
5th level (1 slot): legend lore

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 2
legendary_actions.description: The sphinx takes 2 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only immediately after another creature's turn. The sphinx regains expended legendary uses at the start of its turn.

legendary_actions.name: Claw Attack
legendary_actions.description: The sphinx makes one claw attack.

legendary_actions.name: Teleport (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.advisory_message: magically teleports up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space it can see — advisory record: GM moves the token, no position consumer (CLA-320). Canonical cost is 2 legendary uses — the engine spends 1 per click; the extra cost is GM-enforced.
legendary_actions.description: The sphinx magically teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.

legendary_actions.name: Cast a Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
legendary_actions.advisory_message: casts a spell from its list of prepared spells, using a spell slot as normal — advisory record: GM adjudicates spell choice and spell-slot spend; no monster spell-slot machinery app-wide and the spell list lives only in the prose Spellcasting trait. RAW costs 3 legendary uses — exceeds this card's disk-canonical 2-use pool, RAW-unusable as printed; the engine spends 1 per click; the extra cost is GM-enforced.
legendary_actions.description: The sphinx casts a spell from its list of prepared spells, using a spell slot as normal.

description:
A gynosphinx bears the head of a humanoid female. Many have the regal countenances of worldly queens, but some are marked with wild, leonine features. A gynosphinx's eyes see beyond the present time and place, and penetrate veils of invisibility and magic. Supplicants who look deep into those eyes might find themselves magically displaced, banished to some far­ flung plane where a difficult trial awaits them.
Gynosphinxes are virtual libraries of knowledge and lore. They ask riddles and present puzzles to test the wit of supplicants that come to learn their secrets. Some are willing to bargain with such supplicants for treasure or service.
combat-strategy: Start with riddles and negotiation — it is Lawful, proud, and vastly intelligent; combat is often avoidable, and a solved riddle can end the encounter before initiative. If it fights, open with Greater Invisibility (its 120-foot Truesight sees through the party's illusions while they can't see it) plus Shield against the big attack rolls, and Banishment on the chief martial threat. Fight at range with 60-foot flight and wizard spells (DC 16), descending only for Multiattack Claw strikes on a separated target. Use the two legendary actions to claw an overreaching fighter or, when focused down, Teleport (2 actions) 120 feet to a new perch and reset the fight; Darkness combined with Truesight is a free hide the party can't answer without magic.

name: Half Ogre

actions.name: Battleaxe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 14 (2d10 + 3) slashing damage if used with two hands.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage.

description:
When an ogre mates with a human, hobgoblin, bugbear, or ore, the result is always a half-ogre. (Ogres don't mate with dwarves, halflings, or elves. They eat them.) Human mothers rarely survive the birth of a half-ogre offspring.
The half-ogre offspring of an ogre and an ore is also called an ogrillon. An adult half-ogre or ogrillon stands 8 feet tall and weighs 450 pounds on average.
combat-strategy: Volley Javelins from 30–120 feet at the start of a fight or an ambush, then charge in with a two-handed Battleaxe for 17 slashing per swing. They are dim and bullying: fight where the fight is, in the open, head-on, behind or beside ogres and goblin bosses where their size deters the party's melee. Target the smallest-looking opponents first — half-ogres pick on weak prey and break shield walls with brute reach. Morale is brittle in some troops: if the warband routs, the half-ogre often breaks and flees once it's bloodied and its companions scatter.

name: Half-Dragon

traits.name: Draconic Origin
traits.description: The half-dragon is related to a type of dragon associated with one of the following damage types (DM's choice): Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison. This choice affects other aspects of the stat block.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The half-dragon makes two Claw attacks.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) damage of the type chosen for the Draconic Origin trait.

actions.name: Dragon's Breath
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 14, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. Failure: 28 (8d6) damage of the type chosen for the Draconic Origin trait. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Half damage

bonus_actions.name: Leap
bonus_actions.description: The half-dragon jumps up to 30 feet by spending 10 feet of movement.

combat-strategy: Open with Dragon's Breath (DC 14, 28 energy damage) down a 30-foot cone onto the tightest cluster, then use Leap (bonus action, 30 feet for 10 movement) to close instantly into two-reach Claw Multiattack before the party can react. Its 40-foot walk makes hit-and-run brutal: strike, disengage 40 feet, repeat — melee creatures can't pin it. Pick your Draconic Origin damage type to punish the party's weak spots and resistances before the fight starts. With 105 HP but no flight, don't stand in concentrated fire once bloodied: disengage, reposition behind terrain, and re-engage on your terms.

name: Half-Red Dragon Veteran

actions.name: Multiattack
