actions.description: The veteran makes two longsword attacks. If it has a shortsword drawn, it can also make a shortsword attack.

actions.name: Longsword
actions.description: Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) slashing damage if used with two hands.

actions.name: Shortsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.

actions.name: Heavy Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d10 + 1) piercing damage.

actions.name: Fire Breath
actions.description: The veteran exhales fire in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 24 (7d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 24 (7d6) fire damage. Success: Half damage.

description:
When a dragon in polymorphed form mates with an­ other creature, the union sometimes produces half­ dragon offspring. A creature might also transform into a half-dragon as a result of a mad wizard's spell or a ritual bath in dragon's blood. In all these cases, the result is a creature that combines the essence of a dragon with the form of its original race. Regardless of origin, all half-dragons have similar appearances and special abilities.

Draconic Nature. Half-dragons can't procre­ate. Those that wish to do so must almost always resort to magic. By way of compensation, half-dragons are blessed with long life. A typical half-dragon's life span is twice that of its nondraconic line, so that a half-dragon human might live more than a century and a half.
Half-dragons inherit personality traits common to their draconic heritage. For example, half-gold dragons are often shy and secretive, while half-copper dragons are impish and playful. Half-green dragons are deceitful, while half-white dragons are often dim-witted brutes. These traits are tempered by a half-dragon's other lin­eage, but greed, arrogance, and paranoia are qualities that even good-aligned half-dragons often possess.
combat-strategy: Open at range with Heavy Crossbow if the party charges, but prefer closing with Fire Breath (DC 15, 24 fire, 15-foot cone) the moment two or more foes cluster. Then Multiattack for up to three sword strikes (Longsword x2 + drawn Shortsword) — 20 slashing a round against isolated targets. Its fire resistance lets it wade through grease, alchemist's flasks, and burning oil without flinching; drag the fight through or into fire if the party tries to use it. Frontline discipline: hold chokepoints, protect softer allies with its body, and fall back on reinforcements once below half health rather than dying for a paycheck.

name: Harpy

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (2d4 + 1) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Luring Song
actions.description: The harpy sings a magical melody, which lasts until the harpy's Concentration ends on it. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 11, each Humanoid and Giant in a 300-foot Emanation originating from the harpy when the song starts. Failure: The target has the Charmed condition until the song ends and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. While Charmed, the target has the Incapacitated condition and ignores the Luring Song of other harpies. If the target is more than 5 feet from the harpy, the target moves on its turn toward the harpy by the most direct route, trying to get within 5 feet of the harpy. It doesn't avoid Opportunity Attacks; however, before moving into damaging terrain (such as lava or a pit) and whenever it takes damage from a source other than the harpy, the target repeats the save. Success: The target is immune to this harpy's Luring Song for 24 hours.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Charmed condition until the song ends and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. While Charmed, the target has the Incapacitated condition and ignores the Luring Song of other harpies. If the target is more than 5 feet from the harpy, the target moves on its turn toward the harpy by the most direct route, trying to get within 5 feet of the harpy. It doesn't avoid Opportunity Attacks; however, before moving into damaging terrain (such as lava or a pit) and whenever it takes damage from a source other than the harpy, the target repeats the save.

description:
Taking glee in suffering and death, the sadistic harpy is always on the hunt for prey. Its sweet song has lured countless adventurers to their deaths, drawing them in close for the harpy to kill and then consume.
A harpy combines the body, legs, and wings of a vulture with the torso, arms, and head of a human. Its wicked talons and bone club make it a formidable threat in combat, and its eyes reflect the absolute evil of its soul.

Divine Curse. Long ago, an elf wandering a forest heard birdsong so pure and wholesome that she was moved to tears. Following the music, she came upon a clearing where stood a handsome elf youth who had also paused to hear the bird's song. This was Fenmarel Mestarine, a reclusive elf god. His divine presence stole her heart as he fled, vanishing into the woods as if he was never there.
Though the elf searched the woods and called for her stranger, she found no sign of his passage. Driven to despair by her longing, she begged the gods to help her. Aerdrie Faenya, elf goddess of the sky, heard the elf's cries and was moved to her aid. She appeared as the bird whose song had entranced the outcast god, then taught that song of beauty and seduction to the elf.
When her singing failed to draw Fenmarel Mestarine to her side, the elf cursed the gods, invoking a dreadful power and transforming her into the first harpy. The curse worked its magic on the elf's spirit as well as her body, turning her desire for love into a hunger for flesh, even as her beautiful song continued to draw creatures to her deadly embrace.

Harpy Song. To hear a harpy's song is to hear music more beautiful than anything else in the world. A traveler that succumbs to the entrancing effect of that singing is compelled to blunder toward its source. A harpy sometimes charms victims before it attacks, but a more effective use of its song is to lure prey over cliffs, into bogs and quicksand, or into deadly pits. Creatures trapped or incapacitated then become easy targets for the harpy's wrath.

Sadistic Cowards. Harpies haunt bleak coastal cliffs and other places hazardous to non-flying creatures. Harpies have no interest in a fair fight, and they never attack unless they have a clear advantage. If a fight turns against a harpy, it lacks the cunning to adapt and will flee and go hungry rather than risk straight-up combat.
When they attack, harpies play with their food, delighting in the "music" their victims make as they scream. A harpy takes its time dismembering a helpless foe and can spend days torturing a victim before the merciful end.

Gruesome Collectors. Harpies take shiny baubles, valuable objects, and other trophies from their victims, sometimes fighting with each other for the right to claim the choicest prizes. When no valuable objects can be found, a harpy takes hair, bones, or body parts to line its nest. A harpy's lair is usually hidden in remote ruins, where adventurers can discover valuable treasure and magic hidden beneath foul piles of offal.
combat-strategy: Perch where the party must pass and open with Luring Song (DC 11 Wisdom, 300 feet) — charmed targets become Incapacitated and walk by the most direct route toward her, straight off cliffs, into bogs, or into the waiting claws of hidden allies. Position the song so victims cross pits, spike-covered ground, or the reach of other harpies (they ignore other harpies' songs but not their claws). Fight with hit-and-run: 40-foot fly vs. 20-foot walk means she can land, Claw, and be airborne beyond melee again every round. Damage from anything other than the harpy lets a victim re-save, so cluster attacks break the trance — if the mob starts dying, take to the air and lure again on the next travel day.

name: Haunting Revenant

traits.name: Haunted Zone
traits.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 17, any creature that casts a spell while inside the revenant's space. Failure: The spell fails and is wasted.

traits.name: Undead Restoration
traits.description: If the revenant dies, it revives 24 hours later unless Dispel Evil and Good is cast on its remains. If it revives, it animates another Gargantuan object or structure elsewhere on the same plane of existence; it now looks different but uses the same stat block and returns with all its Hit Points.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The revenant makes two Object Slam attacks and uses Invitation.

actions.name: Object Slam
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +9 (with Advantage if the target is inside the revenant's space), reach 10 ft. or range 30/90 ft. Hit: 27 (5d8 + 5) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Invitation
actions.description:
Charisma Saving Throw: DC 17, each creature in a 60-foot Cone. Failure: The target is teleported inside the revenant's space and swallowed. A swallowed creature has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the revenant.

While the revenant has Hit Points, a swallowed creature can leave the revenant's space only by using magic that enables planar travel, such as the Plane Shift spell.
actions.save_effect: The target is teleported inside the revenant's space and swallowed. A swallowed creature has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the revenant. While the revenant has Hit Points, a swallowed creature can leave the revenant's space only by using magic that enables planar travel, such as the Plane Shift spell.

combat-strategy: Open with Invitation on the casters' side of the party, teleporting a victim into its Gargantuan space where allies can't shoot it without risking the swallow, then Multiattack with Object Slam for automatic Advantage on anyone trapped inside. Haunted Zone punishes casters who attack in melee range: their spells fail on a failed DC 17 Con save, so it wants spellcasters either swallowed or standing back while it hammers the martial front line at 30-foot ranged. Focus down isolated targets with 27-damage slams, and if the party clusters, re-use Invitation to swallow another. It never routs — Undead Restoration guarantees revenge in 24 hours — so spend the first encounter draining resources and saving its swallow for the biggest healer, and let the party discover that Dispel Evil and Good on its remains is the only true kill.

name: Hawk

actions.name: Talons
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Slashing damage.

combat-strategy: A hawk is a scout, not a fighter: use its 60-foot flight and +6 Perception to spot and track the party from above, staying well out of bowshot. If combat is forced, dive in for a single Talons attack (1 damage, hit or miss) against an unarmored or distracted target, then fly straight back up out of reach. It has 1 HP, so any scratch kills it — disengage and retreat the moment anyone draws a ranged weapon or looks likely to attack, and treat it as an alarm that alerts whatever it's scouting for.

name: Hell Hound

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The hound has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the hound's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The hound makes two Bite attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Fire damage.

actions.name: Fire Breath
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: 17 (5d6) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Half damage

description:
Monstrous, fire-breathing fiends that take the form of powerful dogs, hell hounds are found on the battlefields ofAcheron and throughout the Lower Planes. On the Material Plane, hell hounds are most commonly seen in service to devils, fire giants, and other evil creatures that use them as guard animals and companions.

Burning Hunger. Hell hounds hunt in packs, feeding on any creature that appears edible. They avoid potentially dangerous foes in favor of targeting the weakest prey with their savage bite and fiery breath, demonstrating a relentless determination as they pursue that prey to the bitter end.
When hell hounds feed, the flesh they consume stokes the infernal fires that burn within them. When a hell hound dies, that fire consumes the creature's remains in a billowing eruption of smoke and blazing embers, leaving nothing behind but scorched tufts of black fur.

Evil to the Core. Hell hounds are smarter than mundane beasts, and their lawful nature makes them good at following orders. However, a hell hound's evil disposition means that the creature can't be trained to be anything other than a ruthless killer. If a hell hound isn't allowed to indulge its malevolent hunger, it quickly abandons or turns against its master.
combat-strategy: Hunt in packs: spread around the target so Pack Tactics gives every Bite attack Advantage, and coordinate arrivals so at least two hounds flank a victim before either attacks. Open with Fire Breath only when it catches two or more clustered targets, since at 17 average damage in a 15-foot cone it's better as a opener than the two Bite attacks; otherwise save it for a tightly packed grapple cluster. Its 50-foot speed makes it ideal for chasing fleeing survivors and for hit-and-run repositioning between attacks. Target the party's weakest or most isolated member first, and once down to a single hound against armed foes, use speed to kite, breath once, and break off to rejoin allies.

name: Helmed Horror
languages: Understands Common plus one other language but can't speak

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The helmed horror has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Spell Immunity
traits.description: The helmed horror is immune to three spells chosen by its creator. Typical choices include Heat Metal, Lightning Bolt, and Magic Missile.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The helmed horror makes two Arcane Sword attacks.

actions.name: Arcane Sword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Slashing damage plus 5 (1d10) Force damage.

description:
This construct possesses intelligence, the ability to reason and adjust its tactics, and an unswerving devotion to its maker that persists even after its maker's demise. Resembling an animated suit of empty plate armor, a helmed horror serves without ambition or emotion.

Magical Purpose. Though it takes more magical resources to create a helmed horror than a lesser suit of animated armor, the helmed horror requires Jess direction and maintenance as it carries out its appointed tasks. A helmed horror follows its orders with complete loyalty, and is intelligent enough to understand the difference between an order's intent and its exact wording. Unlike many constructs, it seeks to fulfill the former rather than slavishly follow the latter.

Tactical Cunning. A helmed horror fights with the cunning of a skilled warrior, taking to the air as it attacks weaker characters and spellcasters first. However, a helmed horror lacks the insight to change its environment, fortify it, or otherwise take active measures to improve its defensive position.

Constructed Nature. A helmed horror doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: An unstoppable sentinel: march straight at the nearest intruder and Multiattack with Arcane Sword, banking on its AC 20 and Magic Resistance to shrug off the party's opening volley. Confirm which three spells it's immune to early — if the caster wastes slots on Heat Metal or Magic Missile, the fight is already won. Force damage bypasses most resistances, so it never needs to switch targets for damage-type reasons; prioritize whoever is casting, since it has no fear and no self-preservation instinct. Standing its ground is the strategy: hover over doorways and chokepoints to block passage, and if the fight drags, keep closing regardless of damage — it obeys its orders until destroyed.

name: Hezrou

traits.name: Demonic Restoration
traits.description: If the hezrou dies outside the Abyss, its body dissolves into ichor, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Abyss.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The hezrou has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Stench
traits.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 16, any creature that starts its turn in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the hezrou. Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition until the start of its next turn.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The hezrou makes three Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) Slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) Poison damage.

bonus_actions.name: Leap
bonus_actions.description: The hezrou jumps up to 30 feet by spending 10 feet of movement.

description: Hezrous serve as foot soldiers in the demonic hordes of the Abyss. Although physically powerful, they are weak­ minded and hezrous can easily be duped into sacrificing themselves by more powerful demons. As they press their attacks into the heart of an enemy's forces, their foul stench can sicken even the toughest foes.
combat-strategy: A relentless brute: open with Leap (30 feet for 10 feet of movement) to close distance and land directly in melee, where its 10-foot Stench emanation forces the whole front line into DC 16 Con saves every turn they start adjacent. Its strategy is simply to stand in the thickest melee and Multiattack three Rends for ~57 average damage per round, letting Stench keep the Poisoned condition — with disadvantage on attack rolls — cycling across enemies. Magic Resistance means the party's save-or-suck will often bounce, so it can ignore controller casters and focus the biggest physical threat. It never routs (Demonic Restoration reforms it in the Abyss anyway), so fight to the death, and if backed into water or open ground where Stench loses value, wade in anyway — its hit points let it trade against almost anything.

name: Hill Giant

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The giant makes two attacks, using Tree Club or Trash Lob in any combination.

actions.name: Tree Club
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 18 (3d8 + 5) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Trash Lob
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +8, range 60/240 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn.

description:
Hill giants are selfish, dimwitted brutes that hunt forage, and raid in constant search of food. They blunder through hills and forests devouring what they can, bullying smaller creatures into feeding them. Their laziness and dullness would long ago have spelled their end if not for their formidable size and strength.

Primitive. Hill giants dwell in hills and mountain valleys across the world, congregating in steadings built of rough timber or in clusters of well-defended mud­ and-wattle huts. Their skins are tan from lives spent lumbering up and down the hilly slopes and dozing beneath the sun. Their weapons are uprooted trees and rocks pulled from the earth. The sweat of their bodies adds to the reek of the crude animal skins they wear, poorly stitched together with hair and leather thongs.

Bigger Means Better. In a hill giant's world, humanoids and animals are easy prey that can be hunted with impunity. Creatures such as dragons and other giants are tough adversaries. Hill giants equate size with power.
Hill giants don't realize they follow an ordning. They know only that other giants are larger and stronger than they are, which means they are to be obeyed. A hill giant tribe's chief is usually the tallest and fattest giant that can still move about. Only on rare occasion does a hill giant with more brains than bulk use its cunning to gain the favor of giants of higher status, cleverly subverting the social order.

Voracious Eaters. With nothing else to occupy them, hill giants eat as often as possible. A hill giant hunts and forages alone or with a dire wolf companion, so as to not have to share with other tribe members. The giant eats anything that isn't obviously deadly, such as creatures known to be poisonous. Rotten meat is fair game, though, as are decaying plants and even mud.
Farmers fear and loathe hill giants. Where a predator such as an ankheg might burrow through fields and consume a cow or two before being driven off, a hill giant will consume a whole herd of cattle before moving on to sheep, goats, and chickens, then tearing into fruits, vegetables, and grain. If a farm family is at hand, the giant might snack on them too.

Stupid and Deadly. The hill giants' ability to digest nearly anything has allowed them to survive for eons as savages, eating and breeding in the hills like animals. They have never needed to adapt and change, so their minds and emotions remain simple and undeveloped.
With no culture of their own, hill giants ape the traditions of creatures they manage to observe for a time before eating them. They don't think about their own size and strength, however. Tribes of hill giants attempting to imitate elves have been known to topple entire forests by trying to live in trees. Others attempting to take over humanoid towns or villages get only as far as the doors and windows of a building, taking out its walls and roof as they attempt to enter.
In conversation, hill giants are blunt and direct, and they have little concept of deception. A hill giant might be fooled into running from another giant if a number of villagers cover themselves in blankets and stand on one another's shoulders holding a giant-painted pumpkin head. Reasoning with a hill giant is futile, although clever creatures can sometimes encourage a giant to take actions that benefit them.

Raging Bullies. A hill giant that feels as though it has been deceived, insulted, or made into a fool vents its terrible wrath on anything it encounters. Even after smashing those who offended it into pulp, the giant rampages until its rage abates, it notices something more interesting, or it grows hungry.
If a hill giant proclaims itself king over a territory where other humanoids Jive, it rules strictly by terror and tyranny. Its decisions shift with its mood, and if it forgets the title it bestowed upon itself, it might eat its subjects on a whim.
combat-strategy: A dim, petty bully: open at range with Trash Lob to Poisonen martial attackers (disadvantage on their attacks) while closing the 60-foot gap, then switch to Tree Club up close, where a hit also knocks Large or smaller targets Prone. Its +8 to hit and 18-damage clubs mean it should gang up on fallen or isolated foes — Prone gives the party disadvantage to get up while the giant and any allies hammer them at Advantage. Its low Int means no tactical patience: it charges whoever insults or wounds it first, so decoys work. Poor Dex save and AC 13 mean it soaks damage through 105 HP rather than dodging; if reduced to a quarter health or its pack is wiped, it may tantrum and retreat, throwing Trash Lob on the way out.

name: Hippogriff

traits.name: Flyby
traits.description: The hippogriff doesn't provoke an Opportunity Attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The hippogriff makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Slashing damage.

description:
A beast whose magical origins are lost to history, a hippogriff possesses the wings and forelimbs of an eagle, the hindquarters of a horse, and a head that combines the features of both animals.
Reclusive and omnivorous, hippogriffs mate for life and seldom venture more than a few miles from their nest. When defending its mate or its young, a hippogriff fights to the death. Hippogriffs don't lay eggs but give birth to live young.
Dragons, griffons, and wyverns have a taste for hippogriff meat and frequently prey on these creatures.

Flying Mounts. A hippogriff raised in captivity can be trained to be a faithful companion and mount. Of all the creatures that can serve as flying mounts, hippogriffs are among the easiest to train and the most loyal once trained properly.
combat-strategy: Use Flyby hit-and-run: swoop in from altitude, Multiattack two Rends against an isolated target on the ground, and fly straight out of reach without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Its 60-foot fly speed and 40-foot walk let it control engagement range completely — dive on stragglers, archers, and mounts, then circle back at the edge of melee reach. At only 26 HP and AC 11 it dies fast in a sustained brawl, so never commit two rounds in a row against concentrated fire without losing it; if the first pass fails or it takes 10+ damage, climb out of bowshot and look for another lone victim or disengage entirely. As a mount, keep its rider's actions separate and use it to reposition the rider out of danger.

name: Hippopotamus

traits.name: Hold Breath
traits.description: The hippopotamus can hold its breath for 10 minutes.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The hippopotamus makes two Bite attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) Piercing damage.

combat-strategy: Ambush from the water: with Hold Breath it can lie submerged with only nostrils and eyes showing until prey comes within its 30-foot swim speed, then explode into a Bite charging attack targeting the nearest Small or Medium creature in the shallows. Two +7 Bites for 16 piercing each make it a brutal close-quarters bully, so drag fights into deep water where it swims at 30 feet while most armored PCs flounder or swim half-speed. Its 30-foot land speed is deceptively good in a straight charge — commit to closing and trampling rather than kiting, since Dex 7 and AC 14 mean it can't dodge and must trade damage through 82 HP. Once bloodied below half health in open ground, it may turn and plunge back into the river to recover; pursue into the water at your peril.

name: Hobgoblin

actions.name: Longsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) slashing damage, or 6 (1d10 + 1) slashing damage if used with two hands.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.

traits.name: Martial Advantage
traits.description: Once per turn, the hobgoblin can deal an extra 7 (2d6) damage to a creature it hits with a weapon attack if that creature is within 5 ft. of an ally of the hobgoblin that isn't incapacitated.

description:
War horns sound, stones fly from catapults, and the thunder of a thousand booted feet echoes across the land as hobgoblins march to battle. Across the borderlands of civilization, settlements and settlers must contend with these aggressive humanoids, whose thirst for conquest is never satisfied.
Hobgoblins have dark orange or red-orange skin, and hair ranging from dark red-brown to dark gray. Yellow or dark brown eyes peer out beneath their beetling brows, and their wide mouths sport sharp and yellowed teeth. A male hobgoblin might have a large blue or red nose, which symbolizes virility and power among goblinkin. Hobgoblins can live as long as humans, though their love of warfare and battle means that few do.

Goblinoids. Hobgoblins belong to a family of creatures called goblinoids. They are often found lording over their cousins, the smaller goblins and the ferocious bugbears.

Martial Might. A hobgoblin measures virtue by physical strength and martial prowess, caring about nothing except the opportunity to demonstrate skill and cunning in battle. Hobgoblins of high military rank attain their positions by force, then hold those positions by imposing their authority through draconian measures.
Hobgoblins train to fight with a variety of weapons, and have great skill at crafting arms, armor, siege engines, and other military devices. Organized and disciplined, they take exceptional care of their weapons, armor, and personal possessions. They favor the bold colors associated with their tribes, and trim their often-elaborate uniforms with blood-red piping and leather dyed black.

Military Legions. Hobgoblins organize themselves into tribal bands known as legions. In their martial society, every hobgoblin has a rank, from the powerful leaders and champions, to the rank-and-file foot soldiers, to the goblins that find themselves driven into the front lines at spear point. A legion is headed by a warlord with several captains serving under its command. A hobgoblin warlord is a ruthless tyrant more interested in strategy, victory, glory, reputation, and dominion than leading troops into battle.
As loyal and disciplined as hobgoblins are in their own legion, rival legions compete constantly for reputation and status. Meetings between legions erupt in violence if troops aren't restrained, and only exceptionally powerful leaders can force legions to cooperate on the battlefield.

Strategic Thinkers. Hobgoblins have a strong grasp of tactics and discipline, and can carry out sophisticated battle plans under the direction of a strategically minded leader. However, they hate elves and attack them first in battle over any other opponents, even if doing so would be a tactical error.
Legions often supplement their ranks with less reliable and more expendable troops, including goblins, bugbears, orcs, evil humans, ogres, and giants.

Beast Trainers. Hobgoblins have a long history of training animals to service. Like the more civilized races, they use oxen and horses to transport goods and weaponry over long distances. They communicate with each other using trained ravens, and keep vicious wolves to guard prisoners and protect hobgoblin camps. Hobgoblin cavalry use trained worgs as steeds, in the same way that goblins ride wolves. Some tribes even keep carnivorous apes as fighting beasts.

Conquer and Control. Hobgoblins claim lands with abundant resources, and they can be found in forests and mountains, near mines and humanoid settlements, and anywhere else that wood, metal, and potential slaves can be found. They build and conquer strongholds in strategically advantageous locations, which they then use as staging areas to expand their territory.
Hobgoblin warlords never tire of combat, but they don't take up arms lightly. Before they attack, hobgoblins conduct thorough reconnaissance to gauge the strengths and weaknesses of their foes. When assaulting a stronghold, they surround it first to cut off escape routes and supply lines, then slowly starve their enemies out.
Hobgoblins fortify their own holdings, bolstering existing defenses with innovations of their own. Whether they lair in cavern complexes, dungeons, ruins, or forests, they protect their strongholds with ditches, fences, gates, guard towers, pit traps, and crude catapults or ballistas.

Legion of Maglubiyet. Hobgoblins worship Maglubiyet the Mighty One, the greater god of goblinoids. As terrifying as this figure is, hobgoblins don't fear death, believing that when they die in battle, their spirits join the honored ranks of Maglubiyet's army on the plane of Acheron.
combat-strategy: Fight as disciplined squads, never alone: mass in ranks of three or more so Martial Advantage's +7 bonus damage lands on the first hit each round, and focus fire one designated target at a time on the commander's cue. Open at range with Longbow volleys from behind cover until the party closes, then step back in lockstep, keeping 5-foot spacing between goblins to deny area control while still granting adjacency for Martial Advantage. Target isolated or already-injured PCs — the flat +2d6 bonus makes finishing wounded targets cheap. AC 18 from mail is decent but only 11 HP, so break off to fallback positions (the second-rank soldiers swap front line duty) when half their number fall; a hobgoblin never routs individually, but a squad will execute an orderly withdrawal when the mission stops being winnable.

name: Hobgoblin Captain

traits.name: Aura of Authority
traits.description: While in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the hobgoblin, the hobgoblin and its allies have Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws, provided the hobgoblin doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The hobgoblin makes two attacks, using Greatsword or Longbow in any combination.

actions.name: Greatsword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) Slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 150/600 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Piercing damage plus 5 (2d4) Poison damage.

description: A legion is headed by a warlord with several captains serving under its command. A hobgoblin warlord is a ruthless tyrant more interested in strategy, victory, glory, reputation, and dominion than leading troops into battle.
combat-strategy: Command from the middle of the pack: its 10-foot Aura of Authority grants the captain and every nearby goblinoid Advantage on attacks and saves, so it must stay alive and in the thick of the fight for the squad to function. Position it one step behind the front rank, still touching an ally, so enemies must overextend through the aura's goblin shield wall to reach it. Open with Longbow shots (poison darts on the first volley) at charging PCs, then switch to Greatsword multiattacks against whoever closes, prioritizing concentrated focus fire called down on a single target each round. Because the aura also boosts allies' saves, the party's turn control lands poorly while it stands — treat the captain as the win condition: if the squad breaks, withdraw with them, since a captain without troops is just a 58-HP duelist.

name: Hobgoblin Warlord

traits.name: Aura of Authority
traits.description: While in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the hobgoblin, the hobgoblin and its allies have Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws, provided the hobgoblin doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The hobgoblin makes three attacks, using Javelin or Longsword in any combination.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage, and the target's Speed decreases by 10 feet until the start of the hobgoblin's next turn.

actions.name: Longsword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Slashing damage.

reactions.name: Parry
reactions.trigger: The hobgoblin is hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon
reactions.description: The hobgoblin adds 3 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

description: A legion is headed by a warlord with several captains serving under its command. A hobgoblin warlord is a ruthless tyrant more interested in strategy, victory, glory, reputation, and dominion than leading troops into battle.
combat-strategy: The battlefield anchor: its 30-foot Aura of Authority blankets an entire company in Advantage, so keep it centered on the massed ranks and never let it get isolated — protect it with a bodyguard detail of at least four hobgoblins. Open at range with Javelin throws to slow chargers (Speed -10 stacks round over round if they let it keep throwing), then meet the melee with three Longsword attacks while Parry (AC +3) soaks the enemy's best swing of the turn. Focus fire on the party's striker once the aura has boosted the rank-and-file's attacks. At AC 20 with 112 HP it can tank head-on, but if the aura's allies are wiped and it faces the full party alone, fall back behind fortifications — the warlord is smart enough to know a leaderless last stand is just suicide, and will attempt an orderly retreat to fight another day.

name: Hobgoblin Warrior

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The hobgoblin has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the hobgoblin's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Longsword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d10 + 1) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +3, range 150/600 ft. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) Piercing damage plus 7 (3d4) Poison damage.

combat-strategy: A disciplined rank soldier: fight in tight formation with allies so Pack Tactics grants Advantage on every Longsword swing (+3 to hit becomes overwhelmingly likely), and focus-fire the target the squad leader designates. Ranged openers come from Longbows loaded with poisoned ammunition — the 3d4 poison (not the 1d8 base) is the point, so land shots on martial attackers to grind them down with Poisoned disadvantage even when the arrow itself misses big. AC 18 armor makes individual warriors durable enough to hold a shield line, but 11 HP means each one breaks after one solid hit — swap wounded warriors to the back rank rather than letting them die in place. They obey orders to the death, so only a withdrawal command or the collapse of the entire formation will make them leave the field.

name: Homunculus
languages: Understands Common plus one other language but can't speak

traits.name: Telepathic Bond
traits.description: While the homunculus is on the same plane of existence as its master, the two of them can communicate telepathically with each other.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage, and the target is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12. Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition until the end of the homunculus's next turn. Failure by 5 or more: The target has the Poisoned condition for 1 minute. While Poisoned, the target has the Unconscious condition, which ends early if the target takes any damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition until the end of the homunculus's next turn.

description:
A homunculus is a construct that acts as an extension of its creator, with the two sharing thoughts, senses, and language through a mystical bond. A master can have only one homunculus at a time (attempts to create another one always fail), and when its master dies, the homunculus also dies.

Shared Mind. A homunculus knows everything its creator knows, including all the languages the creator can speak and read. Likewise, everything the construct senses is known to its master, even over great distances, provided both are on the same plane. Functioning as a spy, a scout, an emissary, or a messenger, a homunculus is an invaluable servant for a spellcaster engaged in secret experimentation or adventuring.
combat-strategy: Rarely a combatant — use it as the wizard's eyes, sensor, and message relay via Telepathic Bond, staying invisible-adjacent, hidden in an attic or riding a shoulder. If forced into a fight, harry from the edges: Bite for the Poisoned/sleep effect (DC 12 Con), since a failed save by 5 knocks a target Unconscious for a minute — ideal for silencing a guard or dropping a resting PC, though the sleep ends on any damage, so pair the bite with an ally's follow-up. Its 40-foot fly, Tiny size, and +4 to hit make it a nuisance skirmisher that can hover out of melee reach and pop in to bite. At 4 HP anything kills it, so it should never be in anyone's reach at the end of its turn; if the master is nearby, retreat into the master's protection and let the real caster fight.

name: Hook Horror

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The hook horror makes two Hook attacks.

actions.name: Hook
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, the hook horror moves the target 5 feet straight toward or away from itself.
actions.save_effect: If the target is a Large or smaller creature, the hook horror moves the target 5 feet straight toward or away from itself.

description:
A fierce predator of the Underdark, the hook horror aggressively defends its hunting grounds. The subterranean caverns where these creatures dwell echo with the constant clacking and scraping of their hooks as they wend their way up cliffs and along cavern walls.
The monstrous hook horror has a head resembling a vulture's and the torso of an enormous beetle, with an exoskeleton studded by sharp, bony protuberances. It gains its name from its long, powerfully built arms and legs, which end in wickedly curved hooked claws.

Echoes in the Dark. Hook horrors communicate by striking their hooks against their exoskeletons or the stone surfaces around them. What sounds to others like random clacking noise is actually a complex language that only hook horrors understand, and which carries for miles through the echoing Underdark.

Pack Predators. The omnivorous hook horrors eat lichens, fungi, plants, and any creature they can catch. A hook horror's hooked limbs give it excellent purchase on rock surfaces, and these creatures use their climbing skills to ambush prey from above. They hunt in packs, working together against the largest and most dangerous opponents. If a battle goes poorly, a hook horror quickly climbs a cavern wall to flee.

Dedicated Clans. Hook horrors live in extended family groups or clans. Each clan is ruled by the eldest female, who typically places her mate in charge of the clan's hunters. Hook horrors lay eggs, which are clustered in a central, well-defended area of a clan's home caverns.
combat-strategy: An Underground ambush predator: drop from ceilings or lurch out of side tunnels, using Blindsight 60 feet and Climb speed to attack from darkness where the party's torches matter less than they think. Its Hook's 10-foot reach plus the pull/push 5 feet effect is the weapon to master: pull a shield-bearing defender out of the phalanx into the dark, or shove a pc toward a pit, chasm, or another monster's maw. Multiattack two hooks against the same target, repositioning it brutally between hits. Fight in tunnels and caverns where the party can't surround it, using verticality to disengage upward out of melee reach, then drop back down next round. Bloodied and outmatched, it skitters into a crack too small to follow, promising a return visit.

name: Horned Devil

traits.name: Diabolical Restoration
traits.description: If the devil dies outside the Nine Hells, its body disappears in sulfurous smoke, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Nine Hells.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The devil has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The devil makes three attacks, using Searing Fork or Hurl Flame in any combination. It can replace one attack with a use of Infernal Tail.

actions.name: Searing Fork
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 10 ft. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) Piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) Fire damage.

actions.name: Hurl Flame
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +8, range 150 ft. Hit: 26 (5d8 + 4) Fire damage. If the target is a flammable object that isn't being worn or carried, it starts burning.

actions.name: Infernal Tail
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 17, one creature the devil can see within 10 feet. Failure: 10 (1d8 + 6) Necrotic damage, and the target receives an infernal wound if it doesn't have one. While wounded, the target loses 10 (3d6) Hit Points at the start of each of its turns. The wound closes after 1 minute, after a spell restores Hit Points to the target, or after the target or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to stanch the wound, doing so by succeeding on a DC 17 Wisdom (Medicine) check.
actions.save_effect: The target receives an infernal wound if it doesn't have one. While wounded, the target loses 10 (3d6) Hit Points at the start of each of its turns. The wound closes after 1 minute, after a spell restores Hit Points to the target, or after the target or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to stanch the wound, doing so by succeeding on a DC 17 Wisdom (Medicine) check.

description:
Horned devils are lazy to the point of belligerence and reluctant to put themselves in harm's way. Moreover, they hate and fear any creature stronger than themselves. When they are sufficiently provoked or antagonized, the fury of these fiends can be terrifying.
A malebranche stands as tall as an ogre and is sheathed in scales as tough as iron. The flying infantry of the hellish legions, horned devils follow orders to the letter. Their huge wings and sweeping horns create an intimidating presence as they drop from the sky and strike with deadly forks and lashing tails.
combat-strategy: A fearsome aerial artilleryman: stay at altitude or hover above melee, opening with Hurl Flame (26 fire damage at 150 feet) against any caster or archer at range, and igniting flammable gear, tents, and oil-soaked ground to control the field. In melee, Multiattack Searing Fork (+10, reach 10) for 24 average damage per swing, replacing one attack with Infernal Tail on a durable target — the infernal wound's 3d6 bleed per turn punishes tanks who think they can out-sustain it, and forces the party to spend actions and healing to stanch it. Magic Resistance blunts save-or-suck, so it advances methodically and dares the party to burn resources. Fly out of reach to reset when focused, and only withdraw to the Nine Hells through the portals it commands when the fight is truly lost — Diabolical Restoration means death is a setback, not a defeat.

name: Hunter Shark

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The shark can breathe only underwater.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6 (with Advantage if the target doesn't have all its Hit Points), reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) Piercing damage.

description: Smaller than a giant shark but larger and fiercer than a reef shark, a hunter shark haunts deep waters. It usually hunts alone, but multiple hunter sharks might feed in the same area. A fully grown hunter shark is 1 5 to 20 feet long.
combat-strategy: An underwater ambush killer: it can only breathe water and walks at 5 feet, so never let it be surprised on land and never give the party open water to swim in safely. Attack from below and behind in murky or deep water, where Blindsight 60 feet finds thrashing swimmers and Bite rolls with Advantage against anyone missing even a single hit point — which, underwater, is nearly everyone after the first bite. Drag grappled victims down and away from the group; its 40-foot swim speed outruns most armored PCs treading water. Target the smallest or already-wounded prey first, and once a target is down, circle back to the next. In shallow water where it can't dive or can be flanked by ranged attacks, disengage into deeper water — sharks are opportunists, not martyrs.

name: Hydra

traits.name: Hold Breath
traits.description: The hydra can hold its breath for 1 hour.

traits.name: Multiple Heads
traits.description: The hydra has five heads. Whenever the hydra takes 25 damage or more on a single turn, one of its heads dies. The hydra dies if all its heads are dead. At the end of each of its turns when it has at least one living head, the hydra grows two heads for each of its heads that died since its last turn, unless it has taken Fire damage since its last turn. The hydra regains 20 Hit Points when it grows new heads.

traits.name: Reactive Heads
traits.description: For each head the hydra has beyond one, it gets an extra Reaction that can be used only for Opportunity Attacks.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The hydra makes as many Bite attacks as it has heads.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 10 (1d10 + 5) Piercing damage.

description:
The hydra is a reptilian horror with a crocodilian body and multiple heads on long, serpentine necks. Although its heads can be severed, the hydra magically regrows them in short order. A typical specimen has five heads.
At the dawn of time, Tiamat, the Queen of Evil Dragons, slew a rival dragon god named Lernaea and cast her blood across the multiverse. Each drop that fell upon a world spawned a multi-headed hydra consumed by a hunger as great as the fallen god's hatred. Great champions are known to test their mettle against these fearsome creatures.

Everlasting Hunger. A rapacious and gluttonous monster, a hydra snatches and tears apart its prey in a frenzy of feeding. When a hydra has cleared a territory of food and driven off any creatures smart enough to avoid it, it moves on to seek its meals elsewhere. A hydra's hunger is so great that if it can't feed, it might turn against itself, its heads attacking each other as the creature eats itself alive.

Hardy Water Dwellers. Hydras are natural swimmers, dwelling in rivers, along lakeshores, in ocean shallows, and in wetland bogs. A hydra rarely requires shelter from the elements, so it doesn't normally have a lair. Only in colder climes are hydras drawn to the protection of sheltered caverns and ruins.
When a hydra sleeps, at least one of its heads remains awake and alert, making the creature difficult to catch by surprise.
combat-strategy: A five-headed meat grinder that rewards fire-wielding opponents and punishes blunt hacking: its core tactic is to wade into deep water or a bog where the party can't easily deliver fire damage, forcing them to chew through heads that regrow two-for-one with +20 HP each cycle. Multiattack puts out one Bite attack per living head — five attacks at +8 for 10 damage each round, rising as heads regrow — so it wants to be adjacent to as many enemies as possible, and Reactive Heads grants a stack of Opportunity Attacks against anyone attempting to withdraw from its 10-foot reach zone. Its counterintuitive weakness: deliberately targeting one cluster of PCs concentrates damage per head, letting the party kill heads cleanly, so spread bites across multiple targets instead to avoid dealing 25+ damage to any single point. Lure it onto land if the party has no fire — in fact, fight near water and submerge heads. Only when all heads stay dead does it fall, so kiting, fire, and disciplined alpha-strikes are the party's tools; the hydra's counter is to keep them separated and in the shallows, biting endlessly.

name: Hyena

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The hyena has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the hyena's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 3 (1d6) Piercing damage.

combat-strategy: A scavenger that only fights when the odds are unfair: circle in packs of five or more, using 50-foot speed to hem in a target so Pack Tactics guarantees Advantage on every Bite. Open by cutting off and harrying a lone traveler or wounded animal, snapping and retreating before reprisals land. Individual hyenas (5 HP, +2 to hit) contribute almost nothing alone, so they scatter the instant one falls or a big spell lands — the pack breaks after two or three dead. Use them to finish prey already brought down by something bigger, to drive characters toward an ambush, or as a harassing delay force that melts away into the brush the moment resistance hardens.

name: Ice Devil

traits.name: Diabolical Restoration
traits.description: If the devil dies outside the Nine Hells, its body disappears in sulfurous smoke, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Nine Hells.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The devil has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The devil makes three Ice Spear attacks. It can replace one attack with a Tail attack.

actions.name: Ice Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +10, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) Cold damage. Until the end of its next turn, the target can't take a Bonus Action or Reaction, its Speed decreases by 10 feet, and it can move or take one action on its turn, not both. Hit or Miss: The spear magically returns to the devil's hand immediately after a ranged attack.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 10 ft. Hit: 15 (3d6 + 5) Bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) Cold damage.

actions.name: Ice Wall
actions.description: The devil casts Wall of Ice (level 8 version), requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17).

description:
Found most commonly on the cold layers of Stygia and Cania, ice devils serve as commanders of the infernal armies of the Nine Hells, tormenting lesser devils as an outlet for their anger and resentment. Coveting the power of their pit fiend superiors, ice devils work ceaselessly toward promotion, slaughtering the enemies of the Nine Hells and claiming as many souls as they can for their archdevil masters.
Resembling a giant bipedal insect, an ice devil has clawed hands and feet, powerful mandibles, and a long tail covered in razor-sharp spikes. Some carry barbed spears whose icy touch can render a foe all but helpless in combat.
combat-strategy: A patient, calculating general of the cold: open with Ice Wall (DC 17, Intelligence-based) to split the party, sealing healers and archers behind ice corridors while its Ice Spears (+10 melee or 30/120 range, spear returns) pick apart the isolated half. Each spear hit is a lockdown: no bonus actions, no reactions, Speed -10, and only move or take an action — hammer a striker with two spears and it becomes a statue that can only trudge. Tail (reach 10, 33 average cold-bludgeoning) replaces a spear when a grappled or boxed-in target is within reach. Magic Resistance plus 228 HP make it a fortress; it should control space relentlessly — wall off lines of sight, freeze the ground it doesn't want crossed, and never let the party focus-fire it clustered. It routs only by choice, withdrawing behind walls of ice to fight attrition on its terms, and if genuinely defeated outside the Nine Hells, it returns there; a cunning ice devil may break off at half HP to scheme another day.

name: Ice Mephit

traits.name: Death Burst
traits.description: The mephit explodes when it dies. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 10, each creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the mephit. Failure: 5 (2d4) Cold damage. Success: Half damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) Slashing damage plus 2 (1d4) Cold damage.

actions.name: Fog Cloud
actions.description: The mephit casts Fog Cloud, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability.

actions.name: Frost Breath
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 10, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: 7 (3d4) Cold damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Half damage

description: Comprising frigid air and water, ice mephits are aloof and cold, surpassing all other mephits in pitiless cruelty.
combat-strategy: A slippery nuisance: open with Fog Cloud to blind the party, then use Frost Breath (DC 10 Con, 15-foot cone) on clustered targets — low damage but cold + concealment makes it a harass-and-vanish skirmisher. Its 30-foot fly and Stealth +3 let it pop out of fog, breathe, and vanish again where arrows can't find it. Position deaths deliberately: Death Burst (2d4 cold, 5-foot radius) means it should die adjacent to an armor-clad or fire-vulnerable pursuer rather than alone, ideally inside a fog bank where the target can't see it coming. At 21 HP it falls to any serious hit; the moment a PC closes for melee without a penalty, fly back into the cloud. Deploy in mephit packs where overlapping fog and breath cones create chaos no low-level party can coordinate through.

name: Imp

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The imp has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Sting
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Invisibility
actions.description: The imp casts Invisibility on itself, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability.

actions.name: Shape-Shift
actions.description: The imp shape-shifts to resemble a rat (Speed 20 ft.), a raven (20 ft., Fly 60 ft.), or a spider (20 ft., Climb 20 ft.), or it returns to its true form. Its game statistics are the same in each form, except for its Speed. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

description:
Imps are found throughout the Lower Planes, either running errands for their infernal masters, spying on rivals, or misleading and waylaying mortals. An imp will proudly serve an evil master of any kind, but it can't be relied on to carry out tasks with any speed or efficiency.
An imp can assume animal form at will, but in its natural state it resembles a diminutive red-skinned humanoid with a barbed tail, small horns, and leathery wings. It strikes while invisible, attacking with its poison stinger.
combat-strategy: A devilish spy and saboteur: shape-shift into a rat, raven, or spider for infiltration long before combat, then in a fight use Invisibility and 40-foot flight to sting from the dark — Sting deals 13 average damage (7 poison) at +5, and attacking invisible gives it Advantage on the hit. It wants to be the thorn in the party's side: steal keys, relay party movements telepathically to its master, and harass anyone separated from the group. Magic Resistance plus small size make it hard to pin with save-or-suck or area effects. If the fight turns against it — which it should, since 21 HP is glass — it flies off in animal form to report and return with reinforcements; imps are cowards with contracts, never fight to the death unless bound by the letter of one.

name: Incubus

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The incubus makes two Restless Touch attacks.

actions.name: Restless Touch
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 15 (3d6 + 5) Psychic damage, and the target is cursed for 24 hours or until the incubus dies. Until the curse ends, the target gains no benefit from finishing Short Rests.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The incubus casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15):
At Will: Disguise Self, Ethereality
1/Day Each: Dream, Hypnotic Pattern
actions.save_effect: The incubus casts one of the following spells using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15): At Will: Disguise Self, Ethereality; 1/Day Each: Dream, Hypnotic Pattern.

bonus_actions.name: Nightmare
bonus_actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 15, one creature the incubus can see within 60 feet. Failure: If the target has 20 Hit Points or fewer, it has the Unconscious condition for 1 hour, until it takes damage, or until a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to wake it. Otherwise, the target takes 18 (4d8) Psychic damage.

traits.name: Succubus Form
traits.description: When the incubus finishes a Long Rest, it can shape-shift into a Succubus, using that stat block instead of this one. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

combat-strategy: A seducer, not a brawler: the fight should almost never start as a fight. Open with Hypnotic Pattern on a clustered group or Dream a long-resting victim into nightmares, and use Disguise Self / Succubus Form to isolate the most emotionally vulnerable PC before steel is drawn. In combat, use fly 60 to stay out of reach, Multiattack Restless Touches (psychic damage plus the 24-hour no-short-rests curse) against whoever is most dangerous, and spend Nightmare on any PC at 20 HP or fewer to drop them Unconscious for an hour without a kill — the 4d8 psychic alternative still grinds down mid-health targets. Weak STR and 66 HP mean it cannot trade blows; it should control, charm, and vanish into the Ethereal whenever the party turns focused violence on it, retreating to the dreamscape to strike at their rest cycles instead.

name: Intellect Devourer
languages: Understands Deep Speech but can't speak; telepathy 60 ft.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The intellect devourer makes one Claw attack and uses Devour Intellect.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Devour Intellect
actions.description: Intelligence Saving Throw: DC 12, one creature the intellect devourer can see within 5 feet. Failure: 11 (2d10) Psychic damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the end of the intellect devourer's next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target takes 11 (2d10) Psychic damage, and has the Stunned condition until the end of the intellect devourer's next turn.

actions.name: Steal Body
actions.description:
Intelligence Saving Throw: DC 12, one Small or Medium creature within 5 feet that has the Incapacitated condition, is a Humanoid or Beast, and has 10 Hit Points or fewer. Failure: The intellect devourer possesses the target, consumes its brain, and teleports inside its skull. While there, the intellect devourer has Total Cover against attacks and other effects originating outside its host. The intellect devourer retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; its understanding of Deep Speech; its telepathy; and its Detect Intelligence trait. It otherwise adopts the target's game statistics. It knows everything the target knew, including spells and languages.

If the host body dies, the intellect devourer must leave it. The intellect devourer is also forced out if the target regains its devoured brain by means of a Wish spell. By spending 5 feet of its movement, the intellect devourer can voluntarily leave the body, teleporting to the nearest unoccupied space within 5 feet of it. The body then dies unless its brain is restored before the end of the intellect devourer's next turn.
actions.save_effect: The intellect devourer possesses the target, consumes its brain, and teleports inside its skull. While there, the intellect devourer has Total Cover against attacks and other effects originating outside its host. It retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, its understanding of Deep Speech, its telepathy, and its Detect Intelligence trait. It otherwise adopts the target's game statistics and knows everything the target knew. If the host body dies, the intellect devourer must leave and is forced out if the target regains its brain via Wish spell. By spending 5 feet of movement, the intellect devourer can voluntarily leave, teleporting to the nearest unoccupied space within 5 feet. The body then dies unless its brain is restored before the end of the intellect devourer's next turn.

traits.name: Detect Intelligence
traits.description: The intellect devourer magically senses the location of any creature within 300 feet of itself that has an Intelligence score of 3 or higher, regardless of interposing barriers.

description:
An intellect devourer resembles a walking brain protected by a crusty covering and set on bestial clawed legs. This foul aberration feeds on the intelligence of sentient creatures, taking over a victim's body on behalf of its mind flayer masters.

Illithid Creations. Mind flayers breed intellect devourers to serve as roaming hunters of the Underdark, creating an intellect devourer by taking the brain of a thrall and subjecting it to a horrible ritual. As it sprouts legs, the brain becomes an intelligent predator as twisted and evil as its masters.

Deadly Puppet Masters. An intellect devourer consumes a creature's mind and memories, then turns the host body into a puppet under its control. An intellect devourer typically uses its puppet host to lure others into the domain of the mind flayers to be enthralled or consumed.
combat-strategy: A horror that hunts smart prey: use Detect Intelligence (300 feet, through walls) to find the party long before they see it, then stalk and ambush the highest-Intelligence caster in darkness with Blindsight backing it up. Open with Devour Intellect (DC 12 Int or take 11 psychic and be Stunned until its next turn) — a stunned target takes automatic crits and can't act, and Multiattack pairs the stun with a Claw hit on the same round. Chain stuns: once a victim is Incapacitated with 10 HP or fewer and is a humanoid, Steal Body possesses them, granting Total Cover inside the skull and all their spells, memories, and languages — turn the party's own wizard into the monster. As a Tiny lurker with Stealth +4 and 40-foot speed, disengage into crevices and shadows between kills; the possessing host only dies if cornered, and it ejects into an unoccupied space if the host falls, then flees to find another skull.

name: Invisible Stalker

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The stalker makes three Wind Swipe attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Vortex.

actions.name: Wind Swipe
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Force damage.

actions.name: Vortex
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 14, one Large or smaller creature in the stalker's space. Failure: 7 (1d8 + 3) Thunder damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13). Until the grapple ends, the target can't cast spells with a Verbal component and takes 7 (2d6) Thunder damage at the start of each of the stalker's turns.
actions.save_effect: The target takes 7 (1d8 + 3) Thunder damage, and has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13). Until the grapple ends, the target can't cast spells with a Verbal component and takes 7 (2d6) Thunder damage at the start of each of the stalker's turns.

traits.name: Air Form
traits.description: The stalker can enter an enemy's space and stop there. It can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

traits.name: Invisibility
traits.description: The stalker has the Invisible condition.

description:
An invisible stalker is an air elemental that has been summoned from its native plane and transformed by powerful magic. Its sole purpose is to hunt down creatures and retrieve objects for its summoner. When it is defeated or the magic that binds it expires, an invisible stalker vanishes in a gust of wind.

Directed Hunter. When an invisible stalker is created, it stays at its summoner's side until it is given a task to perform. If an assignment doesn't involve hunting down and slaying a specific creature or recovering an object, the magic that created the invisible stalker ends and the elemental is released. Otherwise, it completes the task, then returns to its summoner for more commands, forced to serve until the magic that binds it expires. If its summoner dies in the interim, the invisible stalker vanishes after completing its task.
An invisible stalker is an unwilling servant at best. It resents any undertaking assigned to it. A mission that requires significant time might drive the invisible stalker to pervert the intent of a command unless it is worded carefully.

Unseen Threat. Invisible stalkers are composed of air and are naturally invisible. A creature might hear and feel an invisible stalker in passing, but the elemental remains invisible even when it attacks. A spell that allows someone to see the invisible reveals only the invisible stalker's vague outline.

Elemental Nature. An invisible stalker requires no air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: An unseen assassin that fights like weather: it is permanently Invisible with +10 Stealth and 50-foot fly, so the party can only guess where it is until it strikes. Fly into a spellcaster's space and use Vortex (DC 14 Con, grapple DC 13) — the grappled target cannot cast spells with Verbal components, shutting down casters completely while taking 2d6 thunder at the start of each of its turns. Against martial foes, Multiattack three Wind Swipes (Force damage) from an invisible position, then use Air Form to slip between bars, through keyholes, and into spaces no pursuer can follow. It never speaks or taunts; it simply arrives at its assigned target and attacks, disengaging out of reach each round. Only True Seeing or faerie fire, or area damage makes it fight fair — it will pursue its quarry to the ends of the earth and never rout, but may hold back in tight, defended spaces until the target separates from the pack.

name: Iron Golem
languages: Understands Common plus two other languages but can't speak

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The golem makes two attacks, using Bladed Arm or Fiery Bolt in any combination.

actions.name: Bladed Arm
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +12, reach 10 ft. Hit: 20 (3d8 + 7) Slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) Fire damage.

actions.name: Fiery Bolt
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +10, range 120 ft. Hit: 36 (8d8) Fire damage.

actions.name: Poison Breath
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 18, each creature in a 60-foot Cone. Failure: 55 (10d10) Poison damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 55 (10d10) Poison damage. Success: Half damage.

traits.name: Fire Absorption
traits.description: Whenever the golem is subjected to Fire damage, it regains a number of Hit Points equal to the Fire damage dealt.

traits.name: Immutable Form
traits.description: The golem can't shape-shift.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The golem has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
The mightiest of the golems, the iron golem i s a massive, towering giant wrought of heavy metal. An iron golem's shape can be worked into any form, though most are fashioned to look like giant suits of armor. Its fist can destroy creatures with a single blow, and its clanging steps shake the earth beneath its feet. Iron golems wield enormous blades to extend their reach, and all can belch clouds of deadly poison.
An iron golem's body is smelted with rare tinctures and admixtures. Though other golems bear weaknesses inherent in their materials or the power of the elemental spirit bound within them, iron golems were designed to be nearly invulnerable. Their iron bodies imprison the spirits that drive them, and are susceptible only to weapons imbued with magic or the strength of adamantine.
combat-strategy: A walking fortress: march straight at the enemy at 30 feet with AC 20, 252 HP, Magic Resistance, and Fire Absorption — never dodge, never fear, and laugh at the fireballs they throw since every flame heals it. Open by closing distance on ranged casters with Fiery Bolt (36 fire at 120 feet, which it absorbs from friendly area effects and misdirected fireballs), then transition to Bladed Arm (+12 reach 10) for 30 average damage per swing in melee. Save Poison Breath (DC 18, 60-foot cone, 55 poison average) for the moment the party clusters — a double-hit round with Multiattack plus breath can end a fight in one turn. It cannot be fooled, bribed, frightened, or reasoned with, and does not retreat: it simply walks toward its objective through every obstacle, and corners only become deadly when its 10-foot reach finally connects.

name: Jackal

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +1, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 (1d4 − 1) Piercing damage.

combat-strategy: Jackals are 3-hit scavengers that win only through numbers and speed. Open by circling at their 40 ft. speed and biting isolated or prone targets, then trot away before the party's turn — never stand in melee with a mid-level adventurer. Hit wounded or distracted prey, disengage via movement, and let a pack converge on stragglers; the pack scatters once half are dead or a fire shows.

name: Jackalwere

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The jackalwere makes two Rend or Slam attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage. (Jackal or Hybrid Form Only)

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Bludgeoning damage. (Human or Hybrid Form Only)

actions.name: Sleep Gaze
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 10, one creature the jackalwere can see within 30 feet (Constructs and Undead succeed automatically). Failure: The target has the Unconscious condition for 10 minutes or until it takes damage or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to wake it. Success: The target is immune to this jackalwere's Sleep Gaze for 24 hours.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target has the Unconscious condition for 10 minutes or until it takes damage or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to wake it. Success: The target is immune to this jackalwere's Sleep Gaze for 24 hours.

bonus_actions.name: Shape-Shift
bonus_actions.description: The jackalwere shape-shifts into a Medium human or a Medium jackal-humanoid hybrid, or it returns to its true form (that of a Small jackal). Other than its size, its game statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The jackalwere has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the jackalwere's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

description:
Ordinary jackals tainted by demonic power, jackalweres haunt roads and trails, waylaying and murdering those they meet.
A jackalwere has three physical forms that it shifts between. In its true form, it is indistinguishable from a normal jackal. It can take human form, often appearing gaunt and affecting a wretched demeanor to beg goodwill from strangers. When travelers welcome a jackalwere into their midst, the monster adopts its human-sized hybrid form, with the fur and head of a jackal but standing on two legs as it attacks.

Beguilers and Cowards. The demon lord Graz'zt created jackalweres to serve his devoted servants, the lamias. Reaching out from the Abyss, he bestowed jackals with the gift of speech and the ability to assume humanoid forms. A jackalwere is born to lie, and perceptive creatures might notice it wincing in pain when it speaks the truth.
A jackalwere prefers to fight alongside jackals and others of its kind. Under the direction of jackalweres, jackals are fierce and loyal companions.

Supernatural Servants. Jackalweres kidnap humanoids for their lamia masters, condemning victims to a lifetime of slavery or an agonizing death. A jackalwere's magical gaze renders a foe unconscious, allowing the monster to bind a creature or drag it away. A jackalwere might also use its gaze to incapacitate a deadly enemy long enough to make good its escape.
combat-strategy: Open combat with Sleep Gaze (DC 10 Wisdom) on the spellcaster or archer with the weakest Wisdom — avoid constructs and undead, who auto-succeed and gain 24-hour immunity. Once a target drops unconscious, fall back on Multiattack Rend/Slam with Pack Tactics, keeping an ally within 5 feet of the target. Use Shape-Shift as a bonus action to slip into jackal form to flee or hybrid form to pass as a cursed traveler, and kite threats with 40 ft. speed rather than trading hits at AC 12.

name: Juvenile Shadow Dragon

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dragon makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Shadow Breath
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. Failure: 17 (5d6) Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: A Humanoid reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage dies, and a Shadow rises from its corpse. The shadow is under the dragon's control and shares the dragon's Initiative count but acts immediately after the dragon.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 17 (5d6) Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: A Humanoid reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage dies, and a Shadow rises from its corpse. The shadow is under the dragon's control and shares the dragon's Initiative count but acts immediately after the dragon.

bonus_actions.name: Shadow Stealth
bonus_actions.description: While in Dim Light or Darkness, the dragon takes the Hide action.

traits.name: Living Shadow
traits.description: While in Dim Light or Darkness, the dragon has Resistance to damage that isn't Force, Psychic, or Radiant.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: While in sunlight, the dragon has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls.

combat-strategy: Fight only in dim light or darkness, opening each encounter with Shadow Stealth to Hide as a bonus action and banking Living Shadow resistance against everything except force, psychic, and radiant. On the first turn, dive through clustered humanoids with Shadow Breath (DC 13 Dex cone) — any humanoid killed becomes a Shadow minion under its initiative, snowballing action economy. Use 10-foot-reach Rend on anyone who closes, then use its 60 ft. fly speed to kite between buildings or into shadow; if forced into sunlight, disengage and flee to cover until dusk.

name: Kenku

actions.name: Shadow Blade
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Necrotic damage. Hit or Miss: The blade magically returns to the kenku's hand immediately after a ranged attack.

bonus_actions.name: Eldritch Lantern
bonus_actions.description: The kenku casts Faerie Fire, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 10).

traits.name: Mimicry
traits.description: The kenku can mimic any sounds it has heard, including voices. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) check.

description:
Kenku are feathered humanoids that wander the world as vagabonds, driven by greed. They can perfectly imitate any sound they hear.
Fallen Flocks. Kenku wear ill-fitting cloaks, robes, and rags. These garments cover the soft, sleek feathers of their bodies, shrouding their bare arms and legs. They tread lightly when they walk, on talons made for grasping the branches of trees and seizing prey from the lofty skies. Soft as the wind they move, so as not to draw attention to their shameful forms.
Once, the kenku held the wind in their wings, embracing the gusty sky and singing the sweet language of birdsong. Serving a master whose identity is now lost to their memory, the kenku coveted the glittering baubles of his household, and longed to speak so that they could cajole and swindle others out of such treasures.
