Wielding a wicked blade in each of its six hands, a marilith is a devastating foe that few can match in battle. These demons possess keen minds and a finely honed sense of tactics, and they are able to lead and unite other demons in common cause. Mariliths are often encountered as captains at the head of a demonic horde, where they embrace any opportunity to rush headlong into battle.
combat-strategy: Open by teleporting (bonus action) into the middle of the back line, then Multiattack: six Pact Blades plus Constrict to grab and Restrained a Medium caster or healer, chewing it with auto-hit-adjacent necrotic blades. Use its Reactive trait to Parry each round against the biggest incoming attack (+5 AC), and re-teleport when surrounded or after a heavy round to break reach and reset. Grapple the party's key support, drag the fight into open ground where its 40 ft. speed dominates, and let Magic Resistance shrug off control spells. Retreat only by teleport into tight quarters or off-plane when the fight is clearly lost — its Demonic Restoration makes dying in the Prime a temporary inconvenience anyway.

name: Mastiff

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

description: Keen Hearing and Smell. The mastiff has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.
combat-strategy: Bark the alarm and lunge: Bite knocks Medium or smaller targets prone, so target isolated travelers at the edge of the group and harry them while they're down. Use 40 ft. speed to circle and cut off escape routes, biting, then trotting out of reach before the target stands and retaliates. In pairs, flank the same prone victim for advantage and keep knocking it over again. It has only 5 HP — once it's bloodied or a master's whistle sounds, break off and lope back to safety rather than fighting to the death.

name: Medusa

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The medusa makes two Claw attacks and one Snake Hair attack, or it makes three Poison Ray attacks.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Snake Hair
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Poison Ray
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +5, range 150 ft. Hit: 11 (2d8 + 2) Poison damage.

bonus_actions.name: Petrifying Gaze
bonus_actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. If the medusa sees its reflection in the Cone, the medusa must make this save. First Failure: The target has the Restrained condition and repeats the save at the end of its next turn if it is still Restrained, ending the effect on itself on a success. Second Failure: The target has the Petrified condition instead of the Restrained condition.

description:
As deadly as they are ravishing, the serpent-haired medusas suffer an immortal curse brought on by their vanity. They lurk in quiet exile among the tumbled ruins of their former lives, surrounded by the petrified remains of past admirers and would-be heroes.

Immortal Splendor. Men and women who desire eternal youth, beauty, and adoration might pray to malicious gods, beg dragons for ancient magic, or seek out powerful archmages to fulfill their wishes. Others make sacrifices to demon lords or archdevils, offering all in exchange for this gift, oblivious to the curse that accompanies it. Those who strike such bargains gain physical beauty, restored youth, immortality, and the adoration of all who behold them, granting them the influence and power they so desire. However, after years of the living like a demigod among mortals, the price for their vanity and hubris is exacted, and they are forever transformed into medusas. A medusa's hair turns into a nest of venomous serpents, and all who gaze upon the medusa are petrified, becoming stone monuments to its corruption.
combat-strategy: Lair ambush: let the party come to her island or temple, using Stealth and lair statues to confuse approaches, then open combat with Petrifying Gaze (bonus action, 30-ft. cone) at a clustered group — first fail Restrains, second fail petrifies, so keep the cone focused on the same victim to finish the job. Fallback to Multiattack Poison Ray at 150 ft. against targets that avert their eyes or use mirrors, and use Claw/Snake Hair only on cornered prey. Position backward toward escape routes, never facing reflections (she must save against her own gaze if she sees her reflection in the cone), and use darkvision to fight in darkness where mirroring is awkward. Kite into side passages when bloodied; she prefers to turn victims to stone and vanish rather than die.

name: Merfolk

actions.name: Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d6) piercing damage, or 4 (1d8) piercing damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The merfolk can breathe air and water.

description:
Aquatic humanoids with the upper body of a human and the lower body of a fish, merfolk adorn their skin and scales with shell decorations.
Merfolk tribes and kingdoms span the world, and their people are as varied in color, culture, and outlook as the human races of the surface. Land folk and merfolk rarely meet except by chance, though starry­ eyed mariners tell tales of romance with these creatures along the shoals of faraway islands.
Merfolk lack the materials and practical means to forge weapons beneath the waves, to write books and keep lore, or to shape stone to raise buildings and cities. As a result, most live in small hunter-gatherer tribes, each of which holds unique values and creeds. Only occasionally do merfolk unite under the rule of a single leader. They do so to face a common threat or to complete a conquest. Such unifications can be the beginning of undersea kingdoms with dynasties lasting hundreds of years.

Merfolk Settlements. Merfolk build their settlements in vast undersea caverns, mazes of coral, the ruins of sunken cities, or structures they carve from the rocky seabed. They Jive in water shallow enough that the passage of time can be marked by the gleam and fade of sunlight through the water. In the reefs and trenches near their settlements, merfolk harvest coral and farm the seabed, shepherding schools of fish as land-based farmers tend sheep. Only rarely do merfolk venture into the darkest depths of the ocean. In such depths and in their undersea caverns, merfolk rely on the light of bioluminescent flora and fauna, such as jellyfish, whose slow pulsing movements lend merfolk settlements an otherworldly aesthetic.
Merfolk defend their communities with spears crafted from whatever materials they can salvage from shipwrecks, beaches, and dead undersea creatures.
combat-strategy: Attack from the water where their 40 ft. swim speed dominates and land-walkers crawl at 10 ft. on deck or shore. Spear-fight at range (20/60 ft.), jabbing sailors off boats and drowning pursuers who enter deep water, then dive below to break line of sight. Swarm a single isolated swimmer, dragging them under with numbers. They're cowards in fair fight: if a boat is armed or magic flashes, retreat underwater and harass later.

name: Merfolk Skirmisher

actions.name: Ocean Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 3 (1d6) Piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) Cold damage. If the target is a creature, its Speed decreases by 10 feet until the end of its next turn. Hit or Miss: The spear magically returns to the merfolk's hand immediately after a ranged attack.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The merfolk can breathe air and water.

combat-strategy: Harass from the water: throw Ocean Spears (60 ft., self-returning) at boats, docks, and shore parties, stacking the -10 speed penalty to slow pursuers while staying out of melee reach. Fight hit-and-run in the surf — close, jab, swim 40 ft. away — and use cold-tipped hits to slow heavy armor toward deeper water or onto reefs. Target the party's slowest or lowest-HP members at the water's edge and drag the fight into the waves where their swim speed rules. Disappear under the surface when a fireball, bolt of lightning, or a ship's ballista turns attention on them.

name: Merfolk Wavebender

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The merfolk makes two Aquatic Burst attacks.

actions.name: Aquatic Burst
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. Hit: 20 (3d10 + 4) Cold damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The merfolk casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15):
At Will: Elementalism, Light
1/Day Each: Control Water, Create or Destroy Water

reactions.name: Watery Rebuke
reactions.trigger: An enemy the merfolk can see enters a space within 5 feet of the merfolk
reactions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 15, the triggering enemy. Failure: 14 (4d6) Cold damage. If the target is Large or smaller, it is pushed up to 30 feet straight away from the merfolk by conjured water.
reactions.save_effect: 14 (4d6) Cold damage. If the target is Large or smaller, it is pushed up to 30 feet straight away from the merfolk by conjured water.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The merfolk can breathe air and water.

combat-strategy: Commander of the surf: position in deeper water out of ranged reach, spam Aquatic Burst (60 ft., 20 cold plus knockdown on Large-or-smaller) at anyone wading in, then use Control Water or Create or Destroy Water to bury the battlefield under waves or drain the ground their allies stand on. Save-of-the-round pick: use Control Water to raise a wave over pursuers, then Burst the prone targets it drops. Watery Rebuke (reaction) punishes any melee approach with 14 cold damage and a 30-ft. push — attackers essentially never get a free hit. Its 10 ft. land speed is the weakness: lure it ashore if possible, so stay in the water and drag enemies out to it; withdraw into deep currents when reduced to about a third of HP.

name: Merrow

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The merrow makes two attacks, using Bite, Claw, or Harpoon in any combination.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) Piercing damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the end of the merrow's next turn.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d4 + 4) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Harpoon
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, the merrow pulls the target up to 15 feet straight toward itself.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The merrow can breathe air and water.

description:
Merrow haunt coastal waters, preying on fisherfolk, merfolk, and any other edible creature that crosses their path. These savage monsters snatch and devour unwary prey, hauling drowned corpses back to their underwater grottoes to feed.

Transformed Merfolk. Long ago, a tribe of merfolk found an idol of Demogorgon at the bottom of the sea. Not knowing what it was, they brought the artifact to their king. Everyone who touched the idol became afflicted with madness, including the king, who decreed that a sacrificial ritual be performed to open a gateway to the Abyss. The ocean turned red with the blood of slaughtered merfolk, but the ritual worked, and the king led the survivors through the underwater gate to Demogorgon's layer of the Abyss. The merfolk remained there for generations, fighting for their lives as the Abyss warped them completely, transforming them into hulking, evil monstrosities. Thus, the first merrow were born.

Coastal Bullies. Whenever an opportunity presents itself, the Prince of Demons sends merrow back to the Material Plane to wreak havoc in the oceans. The merrow are bullies, attacking all creatures smaller and weaker than themselves.
Merrow dwell in undersea caves filled with treasures and trophies, taken from their victims and sunken ships. They tie the rotting corpses of dead enemies and drowned sailors to strands of kelp to mark the borders of their territory.
combat-strategy: Ambush from beneath the waves: surface behind swimmers or under a boat, Multiattack with Harpoon to spear and reel a target 15 ft. closer, then Bite (poisoned condition) and Claw the dragged victim. Harpoon fishers off the side of boats and pull them into dark water where the 40 ft. swim speed wins the fight instantly. In shallows, spear then drag prey off-balance, using the pull to break shield lines and separate the healer from the tank. Stay in water versus land threats; it retreats to its underwater cave, dragging treasure and captives with it, once bloodied or when torches and magic drive it off.

name: Mezzoloth

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The mezzoloth makes two attacks, using Claws or Mercurial Trident in any combination.

actions.name: Claws
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d4 + 4) Slashing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from two of four claws, and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.

actions.name: Mercurial Trident
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) Force damage. Hit or Miss: The trident magically returns to the mezzoloth's claw immediately after a ranged attack.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The mezzoloth casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13):
1/Day Each: Cloudkill, Darkness, Dispel Magic

bonus_actions.name: Teleport
bonus_actions.description: The mezzoloth teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. It can teleport one creature it is grappling to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of its destination space.

traits.name: Fiendish Restoration
traits.description: If the mezzoloth dies outside Gehenna, its body dissolves into ichor, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in Gehenna.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The mezzoloth has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
The bulk of the yugoloth population is made up of mezzoloths, which are human-sized insect creatures covered in dense chitinous plates. Mezzoloths serve as foot soldiers in yugoloth armies, their wide-set eyes glowing red as the mezzoloths bear down on their foes.
Violence and reward are the fundamental drives of a mezzoloth, and powerful beings that promise one or the other can easily attract them into service. Although it has lethal claws on its four arms, a mezzoloth typically wields a trident in two of them. If surrounded by enemies, a mezzoloth exhales toxic fumes that can choke and kill whole groups of creatures.
combat-strategy: Disciplined duelist: open with Claws to Grapple and Restrained a Medium-or-smaller foe (escape DC 14), then stab it repeatedly with Mercurial Trident (force damage, self-returning) for auto-advantage-free but reliable 18-damage hits. Use Teleport (bonus action) to relocate itself or, worse, drag its grappled victim 60 ft. away — snatching a party member to a cliff edge or into the middle of the yugoloth line. Cast Cloudkill downwind or in corridors to flush hidden enemies, Darkness to blind non-devil sight, and Dispel Magic defensively against the party's buffs and control (Magic Resistance already gives it advantage). Fight in the open where 40 ft. speed wins; teleport away with its captive when heavily wounded.

name: Mimic

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5 (with Advantage if the target is Grappled by the mimic), reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage—or 12 (2d8 + 3) Piercing damage if the target is Grappled by the mimic—plus 4 (1d8) Acid damage.

conditional_damage.condition: the target is Grappled by the mimic

actions.name: Pseudopod
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage plus 4 (1d8) Acid damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13). Ability checks made to escape this grapple have Disadvantage.

bonus_actions.name: Shape-Shift
bonus_actions.description: The mimic shape-shifts to resemble a Medium or Small object while retaining its game statistics, or it returns to its true blob form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

traits.name: Adhesive (Object Form Only)
traits.description: The mimic adheres to anything that touches it. A Huge or smaller creature adhered to the mimic has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13). Ability checks made to escape this grapple have Disadvantage.

description:
Mimics are shapeshifting predators able to take on the form of inanimate objects to lure creatures to their doom. In dungeons, these cunning creatures most often take the form of doors and chests, having learned that such forms attract a steady stream of prey.

Imitative Predators. Mimics can alter their outward texture to resemble wood, stone, and other basic materials, and they have evolved to assume the appearance of objects that other creatures are likely to come into contact with. A mimic in its altered form is nearly unrecognizable until potential prey blunders into its reach, whereupon the monster sprouts pseudopods and attacks.
When it changes shape, a mimic excretes an adhesive that helps it seize prey and weapons that touch it. The adhesive is absorbed when the mimic assumes its amorphous form and on parts the mimic uses to move itself.

Cunning Hunters. Mimics live and hunt alone, though they occasionally share their feeding grounds with other creatures. Although most mimics have only predatory intelligence, a rare few evolve greater cunning and the ability to carry on simple conversations in Common or Undercommon. Such mimics might allow safe passage through their domains or provide useful information in exchange for food.
combat-strategy: Ambush as furniture: stay Shape-Shifted as a chest, door, or pillar until someone touches it, then the Adhesive trait auto-Grapples (escape DC 14 with Disadvantage) the victim while it Pseudopod-grapples another and Bite-mauls with advantage and bonus damage on grappled prey. Grab one or two people, drag them against walls, and let acid damage grind the pinned. In a lair full of fake furniture, shift between object forms (bonus action) to reposition between fights and unsettle the party's trust. Retreat by going still as an object mid-fight to break targeting, then slither 20 ft. into a dark corner or up a wall; it flees to its hoard or burrows when down to its last couple of hits.

name: Mind Flayer

actions.name: Tentacles
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 22 (4d8 + 4) Psychic damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from all the mind flayer's tentacles, and the target has the Stunned condition until the grapple ends.

actions.name: Extract Brain
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 15, one creature that is Grappled by the mind flayer's Tentacles. Failure: 55 (10d10) Piercing damage. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, the mind flayer kills it and devours its brain.
actions.save_effect: 55 (10d10) Piercing damage. If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, the mind flayer kills it and devours its brain. Success: Half damage.

actions.name: Mind Blast
actions.description: Intelligence Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 60-foot Cone. Failure: 31 (6d8 + 4) Psychic damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the end of the mind flayer's next turn. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: 31 (6d8 + 4) Psychic damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the end of the mind flayer's next turn. Success: Half damage only.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The mind flayer casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15):
At Will: Detect Thoughts
1/Day Each: Dominate Monster, Plane Shift (self only)

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The mind flayer has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
Mind flayers, also called illithids, are the scourge of sentient creatures across countless worlds. Psionic tyrants, slavers, and interdimensional voyagers, they are insidious masterminds that harvest entire races for their own twisted ends. Four tentacles snake from their octopus-like heads, flexing in hungry anticipation when sentient creatures come near.
In eons past, illithids controlled empires that spanned many worlds. They subjugated and consequently warped whole races of humanoid slaves, including the githyanki and githzerai, the grimlocks, and the kuo-toa. Conjoined by a collective consciousness, the illithids hatch plots as far-reaching and evil as their fathomless minds can conceive.
Since the fall of their empires, illithid collectives on the Material Plane have resided in the Underdark.

Psionic Commanders. Mind flayers possess psionic powers that enable them to control the minds of creatures such as troglodytes, grimlocks, quaggoths, and ogres. Illithids prefer to communicate via telepathy and use their telepathy when issuing commands to their thralls.
When an illithid meets strong resistance, it avoids initial combat as it orders its thralls to attack. Like physical extensions of the illithid's thoughts, these thralls interpose themselves between the mind flayer and its foes, sacrificing their lives so that their master can escape.

Hive Mind Colonies. Solitary mind flayers are likely rogues and outcasts. Most illithids belong to a colony of sibling mind flayers devoted to an elder brain-a massive brain-like being that resides in a briny pool near the center of a mind flayer community. From its pool, an elder brain telepathically dictates its desires to each individual mind flayer within 5 miles of it, for it is able to hold multiple mental conversations at once.

Hunger of the Mind. Illithids subsist on the brains of humanoids. The brains provide enzymes, hormones, and psychic energy necessary for their survival. An illithid healthy from a brain-rich diet secretes a thin glaze of mucus that coats its mauve skin.
An illithid experiences euphoria as it devours the brain of a humanoid, along with its memories, personality, and innermost fears. Mind flayers will sometimes harvest a brain rather than devour it, using it as part of some alien experiment or transforming it into an intellect devourer.
combat-strategy: Lead with Mind Blast (60-ft. cone, Int save or 31 psychic and Stunned) at the clustered party, then fly in (hover) to Tentacle-grapple a Stunned or Medium target — a failed grapple Stuns it until the grapple ends. Next turn, Extract Brain for 55 piercing (flat half on save) to execute the pinned victim and devour its brain. Use Magic Resistance to soak control spells, and Dominate Monster to turn a fallen or isolated hero into a meat shield before it gets a legendary-risk moment. Hover above chokepoints where the cone catches everyone; flee via Plane Shift when the thralls fall and it drops below roughly 30 HP — losing an illithid and its secrets is worse than losing the fight.

name: Mind Flayer Arcanist

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The mind flayer makes three Arcane Tentacles attacks.

actions.name: Arcane Tentacles
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit: 27 (4d10 + 5) Psychic damage, and the mind flayer can teleport the target up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space the mind flayer can see on a surface or liquid large enough to support the target. If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, the mind flayer kills it and magically devours its brain.

actions.name: Mind Burst
actions.description: Intelligence Saving Throw: DC 17, each creature in a 40-foot Emanation originating from the mind flayer. Failure: 41 (8d8 + 5) Psychic damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the end of the mind flayer's next turn. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: 41 (8d8 + 5) Psychic damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the end of the mind flayer's next turn. Success: Half damage only.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The mind flayer casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17):
At Will: Detect Magic, Detect Thoughts, Disguise Self, Mage Hand (the hand is Invisible)
1/Day Each: Clairvoyance, Dimension Door, Fireball (level 5 version), Lightning Bolt (level 5 version), Plane Shift (self only), Sending

reactions.name: Shield
reactions.trigger: The mind flayer is targeted by a spell
reactions.description: The mind flayer casts Shield in response to that spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The mind flayer has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

combat-strategy: Fight from the air at range: Multiattack Arcane Tentacles (120 ft., 27 psychic each) and on hit teleport a target 30 ft. into danger — off a cliff, into lava, or into the middle of its own traps. Open with Mind Burst (40-ft. Emanation centered on itself, Stun on fail) when the party closes, then back to 120 ft. hover and snipe the Stunned casters; drop Fireball or Lightning Bolt (5th level) on clustered groups when they bunch up. Shield (reaction) eats their early wizard saves, and Magic Resistance plus Dimension Door keeps control spells and encirclement from sticking. Use Disguise Self and clairvoyance to scout before the fight on its terms; Dimension Door out when reduced to about a quarter of HP, carrying dead men's secrets rather than dying for them.

name: Minotaur

actions.name: Greataxe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d12 + 4) slashing damage.

actions.name: Gore
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage.

traits.name: Charge
traits.description: If the minotaur moves at least 10 ft. straight toward a target and then hits it with a gore attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 9 (2d8) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 14 Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 10 ft. away and knocked prone.

traits.name: Labyrinthine Recall
traits.description: The minotaur can perfectly recall any path it has traveled.

traits.name: Reckless
traits.description: At the start of its turn, the minotaur can gain advantage on all melee weapon attack rolls it makes during that turn, but attack rolls against it have advantage until the start of its next turn.

description:
A minotaur's roar is a savage battle cry that most civilized creatures fear. Born into the mortal realm by demonic rites, minotaurs are savage conquerors and carnivores that live for the hunt. Their brown or black fur is stained with the blood of fallen foes, and they carry the stench of death.

The Beast Within. Most minotaurs are solitary carnivores that roam labyrinthine dungeons, twisting caves, primeval woods, and the maze-like streets and passages of desolate ruins. A minotaur can visualize every route it might take to close the distance to its prey.
The scent of blood, the tearing of flesh, and the cracking of bones spur a minotaur's lust for carnage, overwhelming all thought and reason. In a blood rage, a minotaur charges anything it sees, butting and goring like a battering ram, then chopping the fallen in twain. Apart from ambushing creatures that wander into its labyrinth, a minotaur cares little for strategy or tactics. Minotaurs seldom organize, they don't respect authority or hierarchy, and they are notoriously difficult to enslave, let alone control.

Cults of the Horned King. Minotaurs are the dark descendants of humanoids transformed by the rituals of cults that reject the oppression of authority by returning to nature. Inductees often mistake these cults for druidic circles or totemic religions whose ceremonies involve entering a labyrinth while wearing a ceremonial animal mask.
Within these bounded environments, cultists hunt, kill, and eat wild beasts, indulging their basest primal urges. In the end, however, sacrificial animals are exchanged for humanoid sacrifice-sometimes an inductee that tried to escape the cult after learning its secrets. These labyrinths become blood-soaked halls of slaughter, echoing to the cultists' savagery.
Unknown to all but their highest-ranking leaders, these mystery cults are creations of the demon lord Baphomet, the Horned King, whose layer of the Abyss is a gigantic labyrinth. Some of his followers are fervent supplicants that plead for strength and power. Others come to the cult seeking a life free from authority's chains-and are liberated of their humanity instead as Baphomet transforms them into the minotaurs that echo his own savage form.
Although they begin as creations of the Horned King, minotaurs can breed true with one another, giving rise to an independent race of Baphomet's savage children in the world.
combat-strategy: Charge down corridors: use 40 ft. of straight-line movement then Gore or Greataxe with Charge for extra 9 piercing and a DC 14 Str save or knockdown — in a 5-ft. dungeon passage there is nowhere to dodge. Turn on Reckless each round for advantage on its attacks, accepting the enemy's return advantage since its AC and HP trade blows well. Ambush from dark tunnels it knows by heart (Labyrinthine Recall), separating stragglers and goring them against walls. Fight to the death in its maze; it never flees, but if it has guardians or an idol to protect, it breaks off to guard that instead.

name: Minotaur of Baphomet

actions.name: Abyssal Glaive
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 10 (1d12 + 4) Slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Gore
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 18 (4d6 + 4) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature and the minotaur moved 10+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 10 (3d6) Piercing damage and has the Prone condition.

conditional_damage.condition: the minotaur moved 10 or more feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit

combat-strategy: Fanatical berserker: stand in the open and swing the Abyssal Glaive (10 ft. reach, necrotic-tipped) at whoever gets closest, or Gore with a 10-ft. straight-line rush for 18+10 piercing and a knockdown on Large-or-smaller targets. Charge down halls and fight through crowds, using reach to punish fighters who step in and the gore charge to trample lines of defense. Unlike the base minotaur it has no Reckless, so lean on its tougher 85 HP and reach control instead of all-in trading. Seeks martyrdom for Baphomet rather than retreat; only divine intervention or a collapsing dungeon pulls it off the field.

name: Minotaur Skeleton

actions.name: Gore
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature and the skeleton moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 9 (2d8) Piercing damage and has the Prone condition.

conditional_damage.condition: the skeleton moved 20 or more feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

combat-strategy: Charge the corridors: run 20+ ft. straight in and Gore for 11+9 piercing plus knockdown, then Slam (15 bludgeoning) the prone or anyone adjacent on subsequent rounds. Fearless and tireless, it fights to destruction with no need for food, air, or morale, so use it as an inexorable dungeon patrol that ambushes in tight halls where its charge can't be dodged. Target isolated explorers at tunnel corners and knock them into pits or other traps with the charge knockdown. It never retreats; AC 12 and 45 HP mean blunt weapons and radiant damage end it fast, so let it grapple-free swing until it falls apart.

name: Modron Duodrone

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The modron makes two Clockwork Blade attacks.

actions.name: Clockwork Blade
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. or range 30 ft. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) Force damage. Hit or Miss: The blade magically returns to the modron's hand immediately after a ranged attack.

traits.name: Disintegration
traits.description: If the modron dies, it disintegrates into dust, leaving behind anything it was wearing or carrying.

combat-strategy: Reliable rank-and-file: Multiattack two Clockwork Blades (melee or 30-ft. returning ranged) at whatever is nearest, marching in lockstep formations that block corridors and force the party to spend actions clearing the line. Fight in tight formations with monodrones above and pentrones behind, covering both melee and the 30-ft. ranged band. Truesight 120 ft. pierces invisibility, illusions, and shapechanges — point it at the rogue or the disguised caster. It follows orders without self-preservation; when destroyed it Disintegrates into dust, leaving no body to question, so expect it to fight to the last cog.

name: Modron Monodrone

actions.name: Gear
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Force damage.

actions.name: Gear Flinger
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 120 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Force damage.

traits.name: Disintegration
traits.description: If the modron dies, it disintegrates into dust, leaving behind anything it was wearing or carrying.

combat-strategy: Overwatch scout: hover at 30 ft. altitude and spam Gear Flinger (120 ft., force) beyond melee reach while reporting the party's positions up the modron chain. Harass from angles where the party's melee can't reach, dropping to Gear melee only against an isolated or fallen target, and ascend out of range when archers focus it. Use truesight 120 ft. to spot stealth and illusion attempts and direct duodrone patrols toward the true positions. With 5 HP it dies to any solid hit — its value is surveillance and volume; when broken it disintegrates dust-clean, having completed its patrol function.

name: Modron Pentadrone

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The modron makes five Slam attacks or five Electrical Discharge attacks.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Force damage.

actions.name: Electrical Discharge
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 120 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Lightning damage.

actions.name: Paralysis Gas
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throws: DC 11, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. Failure: The target has the Paralyzed condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Paralyzed condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

traits.name: Disintegration
traits.description: If the modron dies, it disintegrates into dust, leaving behind anything it was wearing or carrying.

combat-strategy: Open at range with Multiattack of five Electrical Discharge attacks (120 ft.), using its 40 ft. walk to keep distance from melee brutes; its 120-ft. truesight makes invisibility and illusions useless against it. Switch to Slams only when cornered, since five attacks at +4 spread damage across low-HP targets. Hold Paralysis Gas (DC 11 Con) for a clustered group or to neutralize a controller/healer for a round — it ends on a save each turn, so use it when the target has already spent its mobility. As a Lawful Neutral construct it fights to its instructions without self-preservation: it never routs, so expect it to fight to the death even after allies fall.

name: Modron Quadrone

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The modron makes four Slam attacks or four Gears Launcher attacks.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Force damage.

actions.name: Gears Launcher
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 320 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Force damage.

traits.name: Disintegration
traits.description: If the modron dies, it disintegrates into dust, leaving behind anything it was wearing or carrying.

combat-strategy: Use flight (30 ft.) immediately to gain altitude and open with four Gears Launcher attacks from beyond melee reach — the 320-ft. range lets it snipe from safety while ground-bound attackers close. Ascend above 30 ft. each turn so climbers and most melee attackers can't reach it without spending extra movement. Drop to Slam range only against isolated stragglers it can out-DPS. With just 22 HP, kite persistently rather than trade; its truesight means darkness and invisibility won't help the party flank it, so use it as a overwatch unit guarding corridors or as a messenger that disengages and flies out when threatened.

name: Modron Tridrone

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The modron makes three Clockwork Spear attacks.

actions.name: Clockwork Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) Force damage. Hit or Miss: The spear magically returns to the modron's hand immediately after a ranged attack.

traits.name: Disintegration
traits.description: If the modron dies, it disintegrates into dust, leaving behind anything it was wearing or carrying.

combat-strategy: Open with three Clockwork Spear attacks at range (120 ft.), falling back as foes close since the returning spear means it never runs out of ammunition. Use its 30 ft. walk to maintain a hit-and-run distance band, and switch to melee throws only when an enemy is isolated. Individually weak (16 HP, AC 15), so deploy in squads where multiattack volume adds up, screening larger modrons or objective guards. Truesight at 120 ft. makes sneaking up on it impossible, so it can't be ambushed — instead use terrain like chokepoints where its thrown volleys concentrate on forced approach lanes. It follows orders rigidly and doesn't retreat beyond its task.

name: Monodrone

actions.name: Dagger
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d6) piercing damage.

traits.name: Axiomatic Mind
traits.description: The monodrone can't be compelled to act in a manner contrary to its nature or its instructions.

traits.name: Disintegration
traits.description: If the monodrone dies, its body disintegrates into dust, leaving behind its weapons and anything else it was carrying.

description: A monodrone can perform one simple task at a time and can relay a single message of up to forty-eight words.
combat-strategy: Mass is the tactic: monodrones are expendable (5 HP, one attack), so throw large groups at the party from multiple directions to grind down limited attacks and reactions. Open at range with javelin volleys (30 ft. normal range), then close with daggers once contact is made; the lowly +2 ranged bonus means they matter more as a swarm than as individuals. Use its 30 ft. fly speed to cross gaps, hazards, and reach elevated perches that ground-based parties must detour around. Axiomatic Mind means fear, charm, and mind-affecting tricks fail — but it also means they dutifully follow literal instructions, so a cleverly worded order or obvious bait can misdirect them. They'll fight to destruction without morale, so plan the swarm's numbers around how many party attacks you want to absorb.

name: Mud Mephit

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Mud Breath
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 11, one creature the mephit can see within 15 feet. Failure: The target has the Restrained condition until the end of the mephit's next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Restrained condition until the end of the mephit's next turn.

traits.name: Death Burst
traits.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 11, each creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the mephit. Failure: The target has the Restrained condition until the end of its next turn.

description: Mud mephits are slow, unctuous creatures of earth and water. They drone their complaints to all who will listen, and beg incessantly for attention and treasure.
combat-strategy: Open with Mud Breath (DC 11 Dex, 15 ft.) on the most mobile threat — a Restrained target can't escape the mephit's touch range and has advantage taken against it. Slam the restrained target while hovering or standing in mud or water where it feels natural, using its 20 ft. fly/swim to bob out of reach between turns. Its real weapon is Death Burst: at 13 HP it dies quickly, so deliberately sacrifice it by flying into a clustered group for the free Restrained burst, letting allies pile on the grabbed target. Pair with other mephits so the party must split reactions, and use Stealth (+3) in swampy terrain for ambush openings. It's too weak to trade blows, so hit, kiter at 20 ft., and die loudly.

name: Mule

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Bludgeoning damage.

traits.name: Beast of Burden
traits.description: The mule counts as one size larger for the purpose of determining its carrying capacity.

combat-strategy: The mule isn't a combatant — it's cargo with hooves. In an ambush, turn it loose or hide it behind cover away from the fight line; its 40 ft. speed means it can often outrun the engagement on its own if it breaks away. If cornered, use Hooves (+4, 1d4+2) against whatever adjacent creature threatens it, and remember its 11 HP won't last against anything serious. Handlers should position it in the middle of the party column, shielded from the line of fire, since the party may instinctively defend it if they recognize it as pack animal rather than monster. If the mule carries plot-critical goods, add handlers or hirelings to guard it — the mule's only tactical value is its Beast of Burden carrying capacity, not its fighting.

name: Mummy

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The mummy makes two Rotting Fist attacks and uses Dreadful Glare.

actions.name: Rotting Fist
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, it is cursed. While cursed, the target can't regain Hit Points, its Hit Point maximum doesn't return to normal when finishing a Long Rest, and its Hit Point maximum decreases by 10 (3d6) every 24 hours that elapse. A creature dies and turns to dust if reduced to 0 Hit Points by this attack.

actions.name: Dreadful Glare
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 11, one creature the mummy can see within 60 feet. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition until the end of the mummy's next turn. Success: The target is immune to this mummy's Dreadful Glare for 24 hours.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Frightened condition until the end of the mummy's next turn.

description:
Raised by dark funerary rituals, a mummy shambles from the shrouded stillness of a time-lost temple or tomb. Having been awoken from its rest, it punishes transgressors with the power of its unholy curse.

Preserved Wrath. The long burial rituals that accompany a mummy's entombment help protect its body from rot. In the embalming process, the newly dead creature's organs are removed and placed in special jars, and its corpse is treated with preserving oils, herbs, and wrappings. After the body has been prepared, the corpse is typically wrapped in linen bandages.

The Will of Dark Gods. An undead mummy is created when the priest of a death god or other dark deity ritually imbues a prepared corpse with necromantic magic. The mummy's linen wrappings are inscribed with necromantic markings before the burial ritual concludes with an invocation to darkness. As a mummy endures in undeath, it animates in response to conditions specified by the ritual. Most commonly, a transgression against its tomb, treasures, lands, or former loved ones will cause a mummy to rise.

The Punished. Once deceased, an individual has no say in whether or not its body is made into a mummy. Some mummies were powerful individuals who displeased a high priest or pharaoh, or who committed crimes of treason, adultery, or murder. As punishment, they were cursed with eternal undeath, embalmed, mummified, and sealed away. Other times, mummies acting as tomb guardians are created from slaves put to death specifically to serve a greater purpose.

Creature of Ritual. A mummy obeys the conditions and parameters laid down by the rituals that created it, driven only to punish transgressors. The overwhelming terror that foreshadows a mummy's attack can leave the intended victim paralyzed with fright. In the days following a mummy's touch, a victim's body rots from the outside in, until nothing but dust remains.

Ending a Mummy's Curse. Rare magic can undo or dispel the ritual that gave rise to a mummy, allowing it to truly die. More commonly, a mummy can be sent back to its endless rest by undoing the transgression that caused it to rise. A sacred idol might be replaced in its niche, a stolen treasure could be returned to its tomb, or a temple might be purified of despoiling bloodshed.
More ephemeral or permanent offenses, such as revealing a secret the mummy wished kept or killing an individual the mummy loved, can't be so easily remedied. In such cases, a mummy might slaughter all the creatures responsible and still not sate its wrath.

Undead Archives. Though they seldom bother to do so, mummies can speak. As a result, some serve as undead repositories of lost lore, and can be consulted by the descendants of those who created them. Powerful individuals sometimes intentionally sequester mummies away for occasional consultation.

Undead Nature. A mummy doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Open with Dreadful Glare (DC 11 Wis) on the party's melee striker to frighten them, then wade in with Multiattack: two Rotting Fists plus Glare each turn. Target the toughest front-liner first — the HP-maximum-draining curse is a slow kill that outlasts healing, and repeated Rotting Fist hits stack curses that Remove Curse must strip away individually. Its 20 ft. speed is its weakness: fight in tight tombs and corridors where the party can't kite it, and let it grapple the terrain advantage of chokepoints. Curse the character who can least afford it — the healing-dependent tank — and remember the dust-death clause at 0 HP turns a fallen foe into permanent loss unless resurrection intervenes. It doesn't retreat: it shambles relentlessly toward intruders, which is itself a terrifying, inexorable tactic in enclosed ruins.

name: Mummy Lord

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The mummy makes one Rotting Fist or Channel Negative Energy attack, and it uses Dreadful Glare.

actions.name: Rotting Fist
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, it is cursed. While cursed, the target can't regain Hit Points, it gains no benefit from finishing a Long Rest, and its Hit Point maximum decreases by 10 (3d6) every 24 hours that elapse. A creature dies and turns to dust if reduced to 0 Hit Points by this attack.

actions.name: Channel Negative Energy
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +9, range 60 ft. Hit: 25 (6d6 + 4) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Dreadful Glare
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 17, one creature the mummy can see within 60 feet. Failure: 25 (6d6 + 4) Psychic damage, and the target has the Paralyzed condition until the end of the mummy's next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target takes 25 (6d6 + 4) Psychic damage and has the Paralyzed condition until the end of the mummy's next turn.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The mummy casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17, +9 to hit with spell attacks):
At Will: Dispel Magic, Thaumaturgy
1/Day Each: Animate Dead, Harm, Insect Plague (level 7 version)
actions.save_effect: Varies by spell cast. Spell save DC 17, +9 to hit with spell attacks.

reactions.name: Whirlwind of Sand
reactions.trigger: The mummy is hit by an attack roll
reactions.description: The mummy adds 2 to its AC against the attack, possibly causing the attack to miss, and the mummy teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. Each creature of its choice that it can see within 5 feet of its destination space has the Blinded condition until the end of the mummy's next turn.

automation.description: GM-enforced advisory legs (gridless): the mummy teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see, then each creature of its choice it can see within 5 feet of its destination has the Blinded condition until the end of the mummy's next turn — no token-move or position-burst consumer; GM moves the token and grants Blinded manually. The +2 AC against the triggering attack is automated (MA-0341 parry channel).

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: The mummy lord takes 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only immediately after another creature's turn. The mummy lord regains expended legendary uses at the start of its turn.

legendary_actions.name: Dread Command
legendary_actions.description: The mummy casts Command (level 2 version), using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting. The mummy can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.
legendary_actions.save_effect: Failure: The target obeys the mummy lord's one-word command on its next turn (GM-enforced — obey-the-command is not a registered condition and no command-word-to-condition consumer exists; Death Knight Dread Authority advisory twin MA-0058). Success: The target is unaffected.

legendary_actions.name: Glare
legendary_actions.description: The mummy uses Dreadful Glare. The mummy can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.

legendary_actions.name: Necrotic Strike
legendary_actions.description: The mummy makes one Rotting Fist or Channel Negative Energy attack. Delegates to Rotting Fist (the primary damage attack it mirrors; the Channel Negative Energy alternative is GM-enforced at the delegate seam, MA-1057 twin).

lair_actions.name: Pinpoint Living Creatures
lair_actions.advisory_message: grants each undead creature in the lair the ability to pinpoint the location of each living creature within 120 feet of it until initiative count 20 on the next round — advisory record: the lair-wide senses boon and its initiative-20 expiry are GM-enforced (no lair-senses consumer, CLA-325 precedent)
lair_actions.description: Each undead creature in the lair can pinpoint the loca­tion of each living creature within 120 feet of it until initiative count 20 on the next round.

lair_actions.name: Turn Undead Warding
lair_actions.advisory_message: grants each undead in the lair advantage on saving throws against effects that turn undead until initiative count 20 on the next round — advisory record: the lair-side turn-undead save advantage and its initiative-20 expiry are GM-enforced (no lair-advantage consumer, CLA-325 precedent)
lair_actions.description: Each undead in the lair has advantage on saving throws against effects that turn undead until initiative count 20 on the next round.

lair_actions.name: Spellcasting Pain
lair_actions.description: Until initiative count 20 on the next round, any non-undead creature that tries to cast a spell of 4th level or lower in the mummy lord's lair is wracked with pain. The creature can choose another action, but if it tries to cast the spell, it must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 1d6 necrotic damage per level of the spell, and the spell has no effect and is wasted.
lair_actions.save_effect: The creature takes 1d6 necrotic damage per level of the spell, and the spell has no effect and is wasted. — advisory: the save chip rolls a flat 1d6 Necrotic (zero on a successful save, dc_success none); the 1d6-per-spell-level multiplier, the spell-wasted clause, the non-undead spell-cast trigger and the initiative-20 expiry are GM-adjudicated at the RAW moment (no spell-slot multiplier, no lair-spellcast-trigger consumer, no initiative lair seam, CLA-325 precedent)

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the mummy fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead. (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The mummy has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Undead Restoration
traits.description: If destroyed, the mummy gains a new body in 24 hours if its heart is intact, reviving with all its Hit Points. The new body appears in an unoccupied space within the mummy's lair. The heart is a Tiny object that has AC 17, HP 10, and Immunity to all damage except Fire.

description:
In the tombs of the ancients, tyrannical monarchs and the high priests of dark gods lie in dreamless rest, waiting for the time when they might reclaim their thrones and reforge their ancient empires. The regalia of their terrible rule still adorns their linen-wrapped bodies, their moldering robes stitched with evil symbols and bronze armor etched with devices of dynasties that fell a thousand years before.
Under the direction of the most powerful priests, the ritual that creates a mummy can be increased in potency. The mummy lord that rises from such a ritual retains the memories and personality of its former life, and is gifted with supernatural resilience. Dead emperors wield the same infamous rune-marked blades that they did in legend. Sorcerer lords work the forbidden magic that once controlled a terrified populace, and the dark gods reward dead priest-kings' prayers by imparting divine spells.

Heart of the Mummy Lord. As part of the ritual that creates a mummy lord, the creature's heart and viscera are removed from the corpse and placed in canopic jars. These jars are usually carved from limestone or made of pottery, etched or painted with religious hieroglyphs.
As long as its shriveled heart remains intact, a mummy lord can't be permanently destroyed. When it drops to 0 hit points, the mummy lord turns to dust and re-forms at full strength 24 hours later, rising out of dust in close proximity to the canopic jar containing its heart. A mummy lord can be destroyed or prevented from re-forming by burning its heart to ashes. For this reason, a mummy lord usually keeps its heart and viscera in a hidden tomb or vault.
The mummy lord's heart has AC 5, 25 hit points, and immunity to all damage except fire.

effects: Food instantly molders and water instantly evaporates when brought into the lair. Other nonmagical drinks are spoiled-wine turning to vinegar, for instance.

Divination spells cast within the lair by creatures other than the mummy lord have a 25 percent chance to provide misleading results, as determined by the DM. If a divination spell already has a chance to fail or become unreliable when cast multiple times, that chance increases by 25 percent.

A creature that takes treasure from the lair is cursed until the treasure is returned. The cursed target has disadvantage on all saving throws. The curse lasts until removed by a remove curse spell or other magic.
regional_effects.summary: A mummy lord's temple or tomb is warped in any of the following ways by the creature's dark presence:

combat-strategy: Open with an AoE opener or go straight to Dreadful Glare (DC 17 Wis) on a key caster — Paralysis plus 6d6+4 psychic damage removes that target for a round, and it can re-apply via a Glare legendary action. Multiattack combos: Rotting Fist on whoever stands adjacent, Channel Negative Energy (60 ft., 25 necrotic avg) against ranged clusters, always paired with Dreadful Glare. Use Whirlwind of Sand as a reaction whenever an attack would land: +2 AC and a 60-ft. teleport that Blinds pursuers at the destination, letting it reposition to safety and open the next round with Glare on the blinded foe. Deploy Animate Dead and Insect Plague early to control area and split the party's actions, and use Dread Command legendary actions to halt a caster mid-spell or force a foe to kneel next to it for a free Rotting Fist. Save its 3 Legendary Resistances for banishment, hold person, and the party's biggest save-or-die; in its lair it has 4 plus Undead Restoration makes the heart (AC 17, 10 HP, fire-only vulnerability) the real objective — never let the party near it, keeping the mummy lord positioned between them and its burial chamber.

name: Myconid Adult

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d8) Bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Pacifying Spores
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 11, one creature the myconid can see within 10 feet. Failure: The target has the Stunned condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Stunned condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

actions.name: Rapport Spores
actions.description: The myconid expels spores in a 30-foot Emanation originating from itself. Creatures in that area with an Intelligence score of 2 or higher that aren't Constructs, Elementals, or Undead gain telepathy with a range of 30 feet for 1 hour.

zone.advisory: 30-foot Emanation originating from the myconid — picker multi-selects creatures in the area (selection advisory; gridless selection is lenient, §42). Creatures with Intelligence 2 or higher that aren't Constructs, Elementals, or Undead gain telepathy with a range of 30 feet for 1 hour — the INT/type exclusion and the 1-hour expiry are GM-enforced (the MA-0043 zone picker grant carries no addExpiration clock — §165 residual).

traits.name: Sun Sickness
traits.description: While in sunlight, the myconid has Disadvantage on D20 Tests. The myconid dies if it spends more than 1 hour in sunlight.

description:
Myconids are intelligent, ambulatory fungi that live in the Underdark, seek enlightenment, and deplore violence. If approached peacefully, myconids gladly provide shelter or allow safe passage through their colonies.

Circles and Melds. The largest myconid in a colony is its sovereign, which presides over one or more social groups called circles. A circle consists of twenty or more myconids that wo k, live, and meld together.
A meld is a form of communal meditation that allows myconids to transcend their dull subterranean existence. The myconids' rapport spores bind the participants into a group consciousness. Hallucination spores then induce a shared dream that provides entertainment and social interaction. Myconids consider melding to be the purpose of their existence. They use it in the pursuit of higher consciousness, collective union, and spiritual apotheosis. Myconids also use their rapport spores to communicate telepathically with other sentient creatures.

Myconid Reproduction. Like other fungi, myconids reproduce by mundane sporing. They carefully control their spores' release to avoid overpopulation.
combat-strategy: These are support non-combatants at best: open by staying behind allies and using Pacifying Spores (DC 11 Con, 10 ft.) on whoever charges deepest, Stunning them while spore-servants or kin handle the melee. Slam only when unavoidable — +2 to hit means it rarely contributes damage. Position adults in dark tunnels where their 120 ft. darkvision matters and sunlight can't reach them; Sun Sickness means any daylight engagement is a running clock, so fight deep, fast, or not at all. Use Rapport Spores during negotiations or to lull intruders into telepathic contact before an ambush triggers. When the lair is lost, the colony's priority is protecting the sovereign and spores — adults should cover a retreat into narrow passages where the party's numbers don't matter, rather than die defending open ground.

name: Myconid Sovereign

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The myconid makes one Slam attack and uses Pacifying Spores.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (2d4 + 1) Bludgeoning damage plus 5 (2d4) Poison damage.

actions.name: Animating Spores
actions.description: The myconid releases spores at a Medium or Small corpse within 5 feet of it that wasn't a Construct or an Undead. In 24 hours, the corpse rises as a Myconid Spore Servant. The corpse stays animate for 1d4 + 1 weeks or until destroyed, and it can't be animated again in this way.

automation.advisory: Spores must target a Medium or Small corpse within 5 ft that was not a Construct or Undead; the corpse rises 24 hours after release and remains animate 1d4+1 weeks or until destroyed and cannot be re-animated — timers and corpse eligibility are GM-adjudicated; pressing this chip models the rise.

actions.name: Pacifying Spores
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12, one creature the myconid can see within 10 feet. Failure: The target has the Stunned condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Stunned condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

actions.name: Rapport Spores
actions.description: The myconid expels spores in a 30-foot Emanation originating from itself. Creatures in that area with an Intelligence score of 2 or higher that aren't Constructs, Elementals, or Undead gain telepathy with a range of 30 feet for 1 hour.

zone.advisory: 30-foot Emanation originating from the myconid — picker multi-selects creatures in the area (selection advisory; gridless selection is lenient, §42). Creatures with Intelligence 2 or higher that aren't Constructs, Elementals, or Undead gain telepathy with a range of 30 feet for 1 hour — the INT/type exclusion and the 1-hour expiry are GM-enforced (the MA-0043 zone picker grant carries no addExpiration clock — §165 residual).

traits.name: Sun Sickness
traits.description: While in sunlight, the myconid has Disadvantage on D20 Tests. The myconid dies if it spends more than 1 hour in sunlight.

combat-strategy: Open at range with Rapport Spores if parley is possible; if combat starts, use Multiattack's Pacifying Spores (DC 12 Con) on the front-rank heavy attacker, Stunning them, then let spore servants swarm the paralyzed or stunned target. Keep 10 ft. of reach buffer with the 30 ft. walk, using Slam only on isolated foes it can finish or pacify in sequence. Animate Dead's real work is pre-battle: any humanoid corpse in the lair should already be a Spore Servant guard before the party arrives, and a fresh corpse during combat can be seeded for later revenge. Fight in total darkness where 120 ft. darkvision favors it, and collapse tunnels or use vertical fungal shelves to break line of sight. As the colony's leader it retreats last but should fall back toward the deepest sanctum when reduced to half HP or when sunlight begins penetrating the fighting area — its death collapses the colony's cohesion.

name: Myconid Spore Servant

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Bludgeoning damage plus 2 (1d4) Poison damage.

combat-strategy: It has no tactics — it does exactly what the sovereign ordered, which is the whole point. Program it to guard a specific corridor, doorway, or corpse-cache and it will stand motionless until something crosses its 30 ft. blindsight radius, then charge and Slam (+5) the nearest creature relentlessly. Use packs of them as silent tripwires: they don't need to sleep, eat, or fear death, so blind corners and dark tunnels can each hold a servant that explodes into violence at point-blank without warning. In an active fight, send them into grapples and pinning chases to bleed the party's attacks, since 37 HP and STR 16 make them durable walls of fungus-infected muscle. The counter is fire and radiant damage and blinding it with loud area effects won't confuse it — warn players that only destroying it or its sovereign stops it.

name: Myconid Sprout

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +1, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 (1d4 - 1) Bludgeoning damage plus 2 (1d4) Poison damage.

actions.name: Rapport Spores
actions.description: The myconid expels spores in a 30-foot Emanation originating from itself. Creatures in that area with an Intelligence score of 2 or higher that aren't Constructs, Elementals, or Undead gain telepathy with a range of 30 feet for 1 hour.

zone.advisory: 30-foot Emanation originating from the myconid — picker multi-selects creatures in the area (selection advisory; gridless selection is lenient, §42). Creatures with Intelligence 2 or higher that aren't Constructs, Elementals, or Undead gain telepathy with a range of 30 feet for 1 hour — the INT/type exclusion and the 1-hour expiry are GM-enforced (the MA-0043 zone picker grant carries no addExpiration clock — §165 residual).

traits.name: Sun Sickness
traits.description: While in sunlight, the myconid has Disadvantage on D20 Tests. The myconid dies if it spends more than 1 hour in sunlight.

combat-strategy: Sprouts are messengers, tripwires, and bargaining chips, not fighters. In combat, their only useful action is Rapport Spores — a sprout can pacify a confrontation mid-fight by broadcasting telepathy, so have one appear, emit spores, and flee at 10 ft. per round while adults negotiate or reposition. If forced to fight, Slam (+1) is a nuisance 1d4+1 poison chip; use hit-and-run in dark, cramped tunnels where small size and 120 ft. darkvision let it slip through an inch-wide crack to safety. Deploy them as early-warning pickups at tunnel junctions: intruders who startle one know the colony will learn of them within moments, so the sprout's tactical job is to be seen briefly and disappear. Sunlight is a death sentence, so never lure the fight upward toward the surface where the sprout perishes.

name: Nalfeshnee

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The nalfeshnee makes three Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 10 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) Slashing damage plus 11 (2d10) Force damage.

actions.name: Teleport
actions.description: The nalfeshnee teleports up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.
actions.advisory_message: teleports up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space it can see — advisory record: relocation to an unoccupied visible space ≤120 ft is GM-enforced, GM moves the token; no grid-position consumer app-wide (CLA-320). No attack roll, no saving throw, no dice.

bonus_actions.name: Horror Nimbus
bonus_actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 15-foot Emanation originating from the nalfeshnee. Failure: 28 (8d6) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition for 1 minute, until it takes damage, or until it ends its turn with the nalfeshnee out of line of sight. Success: The target is immune to this nalfeshnee's Horror Nimbus for 24 hours.

reactions.name: Pursuit
reactions.trigger: Another creature the nalfeshnee can see ends its move within 120 feet of the nalfeshnee
reactions.description: The nalfeshnee uses Teleport, but its destination space must be within 10 feet of the triggering creature.
reactions.advisory_message: RAW trigger — a visible creature ending its move within 120 ft — has no move-end producer app-wide, and teleport relocation is GM-enforced gridless (CLA-320); pressing this chip records the reaction use: the GM adjudicates trigger and lands the nalfeshnee within 10 ft of the triggering creature. No attack roll, no saving throw, no dice.

traits.name: Demon Restoration
traits.description: If the nalfeshnee dies outside the Abyss, its body dissolves into ichor, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Abyss.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The nalfeshnee has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
The nalfeshnee is one of the most grotesque demons-a corpulent mockery of ape and boar standing twice the height of a human, with feathered wings that seem too small for its bloated body. These brutish features conceal a remarkable intelligence and cunning.
Nalfeshnees are devastating in combat, using their wings to soar above the front ranks and reach vulnerable adversaries that can be dispatched with little effort. From the thick of battle, they telepathically bellow commands to lesser demons, even as they inspire a sense of dread that forces their foes to scatter and run.
Nalfeshnees feed on hatred and despair, but they crave humanoid flesh above all else. They keep their larders filled with humanoids abducted from the Material Plane, then eat those creatures alive during elaborate feasts. Thinking of themselves as refined and cultured, nalfeshnees employ stained and rusted cutlery when they dine.
combat-strategy: Open with Horror Nimbus (DC 15 Wis, 15 ft. emanation) as a bonus action the moment the party closes — Frightened plus 28 psychic damage against clustered foes, and those who fail keep fearing it while it's in sight, so pair this with its 20 ft. walk-and-rend advances. Multiattack with three Rends (+10, 10 ft. reach, avg 27 each) against whoever stands in reach; its 18 AC and 184 HP mean it can trade blows with almost anything. Use Teleport (120 ft.) to break grapples, cross hazards, or pop behind the party's squishy backline, and save Pursuit reactions to teleport adjacent to a foe who disengages or flees — it can chase down kiting casters mid-retreat. Magic Resistance makes dispel and banishment attempts need to be overwhelming or wasted, and outside the Abyss it resurrects anyway, so it fights recklessly and without retreat. Watch that the Nimbus fails once per target (24-hr immunity): once the party tanks it, fall back to pure Rend brutality or teleport to reposition and threaten a different cluster.

name: Needle Blight

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (2d4 + 1) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Needles
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +3, range 30/60 ft. Hit: 6 (2d4 + 1) Piercing damage.

description:
In the shadows of a forest, needle blights might be taken at a distance for shuffling, hunched humanoids. Up close, these creatures reveal themselves as horrid plants whose conifer-like needles grow across their bodies in quivering clumps. A needle blight lashes out with these needles or launches them as an aerial assault that can punch through armor and flesh.
When needle blights detect a threat, they loose a pollen that the wind carries to other needle blights throughout the forest. Alerted to their foes' location, needle blights converge from all sides to drench their roots in blood.
combat-strategy: Open at 30 ft. with Needles volleys, then hold position: 16 HP means it can't survive a melee exchange with most martial characters, so keep the fight at ranged-needle distance (up to 60 ft. at disadvantage). Force combat through the dark or fog-free terrain it dislikes — its 60 ft. blindsight is its only sense beyond normal sight, so light and silence are its counters, but in its forest home that blindsight makes silent-stealth parties irrelevant; target whoever moves noisiest. Blights are mindless servants of a greater evil: they don't rout, fan out to cover multiple approach paths, and fight to destruction as a delay alarm for their commander. In groups, concentrate fire with needle volleys on one target to drop a scout before reinforcements hear, then close with Claws on anything already downed. If it must close, Claw first-round charges the archers who've exhausted needle-safe range, exploiting the moment they're caught between ranges.

name: Night Hag

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The hag makes two Claw attacks.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Nightmare Haunting
actions.description: While on the Ethereal Plane, the hag casts Dream, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting. Only the hag can serve as the spell's messenger, and the target must be a creature the hag can see on the Material Plane. The spell fails and is wasted if the target is under the effect of the Protection from Evil and Good spell or within a Magic Circle spell. If the target takes damage from the Dream spell, the target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to that damage. If the spell kills the target, its soul is trapped in the hag's soul bag, and the target can't be raised from the dead until its soul is released.
actions.save_effect: If the target takes damage from the Dream spell, the target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to that damage. If the spell kills the target, its soul is trapped in the hag's soul bag, and the target can't be raised from the dead until its soul is released.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The hag casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14):
At Will: Detect Magic, Etherealness, Magic Missile (level 4 version)
2/Day Each: Phantasmal Killer, Plane Shift (self only)
actions.save_effect: Varies by spell cast. Spell save DC 14.

bonus_actions.name: Shape-Shift
bonus_actions.description: The hag shape-shifts into a Small or Medium Humanoid, or it returns to its true form. Other than its size, its game statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

traits.name: Coven Magic
traits.description: While within 30 feet of at least two hag allies, the hag can cast one of the following spells, requiring no Material components, using the spell's normal casting time, and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14): Augury, Find Familiar, Identify, Locate Object, Scrying, or Unseen Servant. The hag must finish a Long Rest before using this trait to cast that spell again.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The hag has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Soul Bag
traits.description: The hag has a soul bag. While holding or carrying the bag, the hag can use its Nightmare Haunting action. The bag has AC 15, HP 20, and Resistance to all damage. The bag turns to dust if reduced to 0 Hit Points. If the bag is destroyed, any souls the bag is holding are released. The hag can create a new bag after 7 days.

description:
Sly and subversive, night hags want to see the virtuous turn to villainy: love turned into obsession, kindness turned to hate, devotion to disregard, and generosity to selfishness. Night hags take perverse joy in corrupting mortals.
Night hags were once creatures of the Feywild, but their foulness saw them exiled to Hades long ago, where they degenerated into fiends. The night hags have long since spread across the Lower Planes.

Soulmongers. While a humanoid sleeps, a night hag can straddle the person ethereally and intrude upon its dreams. Any creature with truesight can see the hag's spectral form straddling its prey. The ethereal hag fills her victim's head with doubts and fears, in the hope of tricking it into performing evil acts in the waking world. The hag continues her nightly visitations until the victim finally expires in its sleep. If the hag has driven her victim to commit evil deeds, she traps its corrupted soul in her soul bag (see the "Night Hag Items" sidebar) for transport to Hades.

Covens. A night hag that is part of a coven (see the "Hag Covens" sidebar) has a challenge rating of 7 (2,900 XP).
combat-strategy: This is a raid-then-vanish predator, not a frontline brawler. By day (or day's equivalent), shapeshift via bonus action into a benign humanoid and use Deception (+6) to scout or negotiate; in combat, open with Phantasmal Killer (DC 14 Wis) on the strongest mind, backed by Magic Missile's unerring damage while Magic Resistance soaks the party's control spells. Etherealness is the signature: step to the Ethereal Plane, then Nightmare Haunting with the soul bag to whittle sleepers' HP maximum across nights, killing quietly outside any Protection from Evil and Good or Magic Circle the party can maintain. In direct fights use Multiattack Claws (+7, ~13 each) on isolated victims, staying near two hag allies for Coven magic (Scrying, Locate Object, Unseen Servant at will-equivalent). Plane Shift (2/day, self) is the escape hatch: disengage ethereally when reduced to half HP or when the soul bag is threatened — the bag (AC 15, 20 HP, resistant) is both her treasure and her weakness, so keep it on her person and never let the party focus it without paying in Claws.

name: Nightmare
languages: Understands Abyssal, Common, and Infernal but can't speak

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) Fire damage.

actions.name: Ethereal Stride
actions.description: The nightmare and up to three willing creatures within 5 feet of it teleport to the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane or vice versa.
actions.advisory_message: shifts itself and up to three willing creatures within 5 feet to/from the Ethereal Plane — advisory record: planar travel is GM-enforced, no Ethereal-plane state consumer app-wide (§70). Up-to-three passenger selection GM-adjudicated. No attack roll, no saving throw, no dice.

traits.name: Confer Fire Resistance
traits.description: The nightmare can grant Resistance to Fire damage to a rider while it is on the nightmare.

traits.name: Illumination
traits.description: The nightmare sheds Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet.

description:
