A nightmare appears i n a cloud of roiling smoke, its mane, tail, and hooves wreathed in flame. The creature's unearthly black form moves with supernatural speed, vanishing in a cloud of brimstone as quickly as it appeared.

Dread Steed. Also called a "demon horse" or "hell horse," the nightmare serves as a steed for creatures of exceptional evil, carrying demons, devils, death knights, liches, night hags, and other vile monsters. It resembles a fiendish horse, and a nightmare's fiery red eyes betray its malevolent intelligence.
A nightmare can be summoned from the Lower Planes, but unless a worthy sacrifice is offered to it as food upon its arrival, the· nightmare displays no special loyalty to the creature it serves.

Creating a Nightmare. Nightmares don't appear naturally in the multiverse. They must be created from pegasi. The ritual that creates a nightmare requires the torturous removal of a pegasus's wings, driving that noble creature to evil as it is transformed by dark magic.
combat-strategy: The nightmare is an escape vehicle and fire-kite mount first, combatant second. In combat, Hooves (+6, bludgeoning plus 11 fire) punish adjacent melee attackers while its 90 ft. hover-fly circles overhead, and Illumination's 10/10-ft. light glow makes it a decoy target for enemy archers while riders fire from safety. Confer Fire Resistance to its rider so flame-wielding foes — or its own burning hooves — can't hurt the one doing the real damage. Ethereal Stride is the master key: on the round the fight turns bad, or to begin an abduction raid, it teleports itself plus up to three willing riders (a raider party, or a kidnapped victim's party) to the Ethereal Plane and vanishes; use it mid-combat to leap a chasm or rear-end the party's flank. It won't stand and slug with concentrated fire — 68 HP evaporates against focused volleys, so use its 60 ft. ground speed to hit-and-run charges, Hooves a lone traveler, then gallop before the formation closes.

name: Nimblewright
languages: understands one language known to its creator but can't speak

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The nimblewright makes three attacks: two with its rapie r and one with its dagger.

actions.name: Rapier
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hiti reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage.

actions.name: Dagger
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack~+6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) piercing damage.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The nimblewright has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Magic Weapons
traits.description: The nimblewright's weapon attacks are magical.

traits.name: Repairable
traits.description: As long as it has at least 1 hit point remaining, the nimblewright regains 1 hit point when a mending spell is cast on it.

traits.name: Sure-Footed
traits.description: The nimblewright has advantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws made against effects that would knock it prone.

reactions.name: Parry
reactions.description: The nimblewright adds 2 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, the nimblewright must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

description:
A nimblewright is a magical construct created to serve as a guard or assassin. Composed predominantly of lightweight wood and powered by magic, it can pass for humanoid while wearing clothing. Some nimblewrights wear plain clothing, while others are clad in flashier attire. A nimblewright is emotionless, its face frozen in whatever expression was given to it by its creator.

Duelist. A nimblewright moves like a dancer and fights like a swashbuckler, using dodges and parries to avoid damage while deftly skewering its foes.

Constructed Nature. A nimblewright doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep. Damage it takes can be re- paired with mending spells, but a nimblewright reduced to 0 hit points is permanently destroyed.
combat-strategy: Open by closing the 60 ft. ground speed in a single dash or use Acrobatics (+8) to vault through the battlefield, then Multiattack: two Rapiers (8 piercing each) and a Dagger, focusing the squishy backline caster since nothing on the battlefield moves like this. Parry is your reaction tax: save it for the fighter's big swing or a critical threat, letting it shrug the 18 AC up to 20 against the single worst incoming attack. Magic Resistance plus immunity to poisoned, frightened, and charmed makes control spells near-useless, so the party will have to damage-control it — its 45 HP is the real clock, and its Dex save (+7) means it's not weak to anything except raw accuracy and area damage. Use Sure-Footed and vertical terrain freely: dash up walls, across chandeliers, and through crowds it can't be knocked prone out of. If its master's objective can be achieved without killing, disengage at high speed (Dash then Dagger parting shots) and race back to defend the true objective — it's a courier-assassin, and losing it in a chase is often the winning play.

name: Noble

actions.name: Rapier
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) Piercing damage.

reactions.name: Parry
reactions.trigger: The noble is hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon
reactions.description: The noble adds 2 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

description:
Nobles wield great authority and influence as members of the upper class, possessing wealth and connections that can make them as powerful as monarchs and generals. A noble often travels in the company of guards, as well as servants who are commoners.
The noble's statistics can also be used to represent courtiers who aren't of noble birth.
combat-strategy: The noble is a bodyguard prop, not a threat: Rapier (+3) chips for 5 damage and Parry (+2 AC) buys one extra beat of survival per round. Position nobles behind hired guards or in the back of the room where they can issue commands while retainers fight, using Persuasion (+5) and Deception (+5) to de-escalate, bluff, or betray rather than draw steel. If the fight goes against them, the noble's real action is the Parry-reaction retreat: block one hit, then Disengage at 30 ft. toward an escape route, guards closing behind. They'll surrender when their guard is broken or a blade is at their throat — 9 HP makes combat terminal fast, so use them as leverage: hostage situations, bounty bait, or the reason the party hesitates to swing. If cornered, the noble fights with the desperate, clumsy ferocity of someone who's never bled, repositioning behind furniture and throwing insults while Parrying the inevitable.

name: Noble Prodigy

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The noble makes three Beguiling Strike attacks.

actions.name: Beguiling Strike
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. Hit: 18 (4d6 + 4) Psychic damage, and the target has the Charmed condition until the start of the noble's next turn.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The noble casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16):
At Will: Mage Armor (included in AC), Mage Hand, Minor Illusion
1/Day Each: Befuddlement, Detect Thoughts, Fly, Scrying, Shatter (level 7 version)
actions.save_effect: The target makes a Charisma saving throw against the noble's spell save DC. The save effect depends on which spell is cast: Befuddle (Intelligence DC check or save depending on version), Detect Thoughts (Wisdom save to resist), Shatter (Constitution save for half damage on success).

reactions.name: Shield
reactions.trigger: The noble is targeted by a spell
reactions.description: The noble casts Shield in response to that spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

combat-strategy: Open at range with Beguiling Strikes (+8, 60 ft. ranged, 18 psychic plus Charmed) — a Charmed target can't attack the noble and may well switch sides, so pick off the party's most charismatic defender first. Hold Mage Armor's 16 AC and Shield (reaction, +5 AC vs one attack or magic missile volley) to bait the party's big hitters into wasted bursts, then punish with three Beguiling Strikes a round from beyond their reach. Level-7 Shatter (35 thunder damage, DC 16 Con, 60-ft. radius) is the opener against clustered foes or anyone in enclosed stone; cast the moment two or more cluster at 60 ft. Use Fly (1/day) to lift the fight vertical where ground-based melee can't follow, and Befuddlement or Detect Thoughts to break the party's OOC coordination and expose secrets mid-fight. With 148 HP and no STR (8) it's a durable kite: fall back 30 ft. per turn, striking at range, and use Scrying afterward to track and haunt the party. Retreat begins when its Charms are worn thin and the party is immune — it flees with its dignity, entourage, and secrets intact, planning the social kill for later.

name: Nothic

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The nothic makes two Claw attacks.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Rotting Gaze
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature the nothic can see within 120 feet. Failure: 17 (5d6) Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target takes 17 (5d6) necrotic damage. Success: The target takes half damage.

bonus_actions.name: Weird Insight
bonus_actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 14, one creature the nothic can see within 120 feet. Failure: The nothic magically learns one fact or secret about the target.

description:
A baleful eye peers out from the darkness, its gleam hinting at a weird intelligence and unnerving malevolence. Most times, a nothic is content to watch, weighing and assessing the creatures it encounters. When driven to violence, it uses its horrific gaze to rot the flesh from its enemies' bones.

Cursed Arcanists. Rather than gaining the godlike supremacy they crave, some wizards who devote their lives to unearthing arcane secrets are reduced to creeping, tormented monsters by a dark curse left behind by Vecna, a powerful lich who, in some worlds, has transcended his undead existence to become a god of secrets. Nothics retain no awareness of their former selves, skulking amid the shadows and haunting places rich in magical knowledge, drawn by memories and impulses they can't quite understand.

Dark Oracles. Nothics possess a strange magical insight that allows them to extract knowledge from other creatures. This grants them unique understanding of secret and forbidden lore, which they share for a price. A nothic covets magic items, greedily accepting such gifts from creatures that seek out its knowledge.

Lurkers in Magical Places. Nothics are notorious for infiltrating arcane academies and other places rich in magical learning. They are driven by the vague knowledge that there exists a method to reverse their condition. This isn't a clear sense of purpose, but rather an obsessive tug at the end of the mind. Some nothics are clever enough to realize that this is merely part of the strange lesson for their folly, a false hope to drive them to seek out more arcane secrets.
combat-strategy: Open with Rotting Gaze (DC 13 Con, 120 ft., avg 17 necrotic, half on save) at maximum range — it's the nothic's opener, harassment tool, and kiting weapon rolled into one, and half damage on a save means it's always worth firing. Use Weird Insight (bonus action) on a caster to strip a fact or secret, then weaponize it socially mid-fight — knowing who dies next, where the healers hide, or which ally is possessed lets the nothic call out targeting priorities out loud to its allies. Multiattack two Claws (+5, 8 slashing) only when an enemy closes past gaze range or after Rotting Gaze has softened them. Stealth (+5) and 120 ft. truesight make it an unmatched watcher in ruined halls and cities — ambush from hidden positions, gaze-round, then melt back into the dark while truesight lets it see the party's invisible scouts and lie in wait. When reduced to a third HP or when its secrets are exposed, retreat through routes only it can see, taking its stolen knowledge to whoever pays; the party kills it only if they close the distance faster than it blinks between shadows.

name: Nycaloth

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The nycaloth makes two Mercurial Axe attacks.

actions.name: Mercurial Axe
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +9, reach 10 ft. or range 30/90 ft. Hit: 18 (2d12 + 5) Slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) Force damage. Hit or Miss: The axe magically returns to the nycaloth's hand immediately after a ranged attack.

bonus_actions.name: Shadowy Teleport
bonus_actions.description: The nycaloth has the Invisible condition for 1 minute, and it teleports up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. The condition ends early immediately after it deals damage.

traits.name: Fiendish Restoration
traits.description: If the nycaloth dies outside Gehenna, its body dissolves into ichor, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in Gehenna.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The nycaloth has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
The elite airborne shock troops of the yugoloths, nycaloths look like muscular gargoyles. Powerful bat wings bear them swiftly aloft in battle, and the razor­ sharp claws of their hands and feet cut through flesh and bone with ease. A nightmarish foe, a nycaloth strikes hard and fast without warning, then teleports away. It uses its innate magic to turn invisible or create illusory doubles of itself, further confounding its enemies.
Nycaloths are the most loyal of the yugoloths. When they find an evil master that treats them well, they are unlikely to break their agreement unless the reward for doing so is extreme.
combat-strategy: Open with Shadowy Teleport (bonus action): 1 minute of Invisibility plus a 30-ft. blink, letting it vanish before the party even acts, reposition behind their backline, and open with Mercurial Axe (+9, 2d12+3d6 avg 28 per swing) from the dark — the invisibility breaks only when it deals damage, so every attack is a surprise round's worth of value. Multiattack two axes, mixing reach (10 ft.) melee with thrown returns (up to 90 ft.) to hit two targets or kite and strike the same turn. Use 60 ft. fly and 40 ft. walk to dominate vertical space, diving on isolated casters then blinking away via another Shadowy Teleport the moment focus-fire starts. Magic Resistance makes charm and dispel attempts a wasted action, and outside Gehenna it respawns, so it fights like an immortal mercenary — but it is a hired blade: cut a deal, feign a rout, or drop its contract fee and it may simply stop fighting. Retreat on the client's terms, not pain: nycaloths don't die for pride, and a teleport into shadow the round the battle turns is a professional's exit.

name: Ochre Jelly

actions.name: Pseudopod
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (3d6 + 2) Acid damage.

reactions.name: Split
reactions.trigger: While the jelly is Large or Medium and has 10+ Hit Points, it becomes Bloodied or is subjected to Lightning or Slashing damage
reactions.description: The jelly splits into two new Ochre Jellies. Each new jelly is one size smaller than the original jelly and acts on its Initiative. The original jelly's Hit Points are divided evenly between the new jellies (round down).

traits.name: Amorphous
traits.description: The jelly can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The jelly can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

description:
Ochre jellies are yellowish blobs that can slide under doors and through narrow cracks in pursuit of creatures to devour. They have enough bestial cunning to avoid large groups of enemies.
An ochre jelly follows at a safe distance as it pursues its meal. Its digestive enzymes dissolve flesh quickly but have no effect on other substances such as bone, wood, and metal.
combat-strategy: Drop from a ceiling — Spider Climb plus Amorphous means it should start the fight overhead in a dark corridor, then fall onto the middle of the party for a free Pseudopod (+4, avg 12 acid) and to smear itself across the floor. Fight in cramped dungeons and corridors (20-ft. crawl per turn is fine when the space forces the party into it): they'll slash it, which triggers Split as a reaction, and now two jellies at half HP each surround them — a trap the party must recognize or keep cutting into. AC 8 means everything hits, so the jelly never dodges; its defense is that slashing and most control split, reform, and shrug off the wrong damage, while fire and cold (DM's call per edition conventions) end it. Let it engulf fallen weapons and gear, sliding through inch-wide cracks to pursue through sealed doors, and slide along walls and ceilings to flank without provoking opportunity attacks from a party watching the floor. It cannot be reasoned with, frightened, or out-marched once cornered, but it also won't chase past its hunting grounds: seal it in a flooded or fire-lit chamber and it dies where it stands.

name: Octopus

actions.name: Tentacles
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Bludgeoning damage.

reactions.name: Ink Cloud
reactions.trigger: A creature ends its turn within 5 feet of the octopus while underwater
reactions.description: The octopus releases ink that fills a 5-foot Cube centered on itself, and the octopus moves up to its Swim Speed. The Cube is Heavily Obscured for 1 minute or until a strong current or similar effect disperses the ink.

zone.advisory: Cube NOT parsed (§62): 5-foot Cube modeled at centered radius, heavily obscured 1 minute or until strong current disperses — GM-enforced; octopus moves up to its Swim Speed; end-turn-within-5ft + underwater trigger preconditions GM-enforced. No vision model (§70).

traits.name: Compression
traits.description: The octopus can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The octopus can breathe only underwater.

combat-strategy: An octopus isn't a threat — it's a squirming, 3-Hit-Point puzzle with one trick: Ink Cloud. When grabbed or attacked, trigger Ink Cloud (5-ft. heavily obscured cube) as a reaction and jet 30 ft. away through it, vanishing with Stealth +6 into reef, rocks, or a drain. Use Compression to escape any capture: it slips through a one-inch gap, so grappling, jars, and nets can hold it only if the closing is airtight, and the party will waste turns feeling for it in the ink. In shallow tide pools and shipwreck debris its 30 ft. swim speed versus the party's awkward surface swimming makes it a perfect harrier — steal a shiny object from a belt loop with Tentacles, then vanish into a hull crack. Deploy them as ambient nuisance encounters, messenger retrieval hazards, or the familiar of a sea witch, where the real fight is the chase: the octopus never wins combat, but it almost always gets away.

name: Ogre

actions.name: Greatclub
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage.

description:
Ogres are as lazy of mind as they are strong of body. They live by raiding, scavenging, and killing for food and pleasure. The average adult specimen stands between 9 and 10 feet tall and weighs close to a thousand pounds.

Furious Tempers. Ogres are notorious for their quick tempers, which flare at the smallest perceived offense. Insults and name-calling can rouse an ogre's wrath in an instant-as can stealing from it, bumping, jabbing, or prodding it, laughing, making faces, or simply looking at it the wrong way. When its rage is incited, an ogre lashes out in a frustrated tantrum until it runs out of objects or creatures to smash.

Gruesome Gluttons. Ogres eat almost anything, but they especially enjoy the taste of dwarves, halfiings, and elves. When they can, they combine dinner with pleasure, chasing scurrying victims around before eating them raw. If enough of its victim remains after the ogre has gorged itself, it might make a loincloth from its quarry's skin and a necklace from its leftover bones. This macabre crafting is the height of ogre culture.

Greedy Collectors. An ogre's eyes glitter with avarice when it sees the possessions of others. Ogres carry rough sacks on their raids, which they fill with fabulous "treasure" taken from their victims. This might include a collection of battered helmets, a moldy wheel of cheese, a rough patch of animal fur fastened like a cloak, or a squealing, mud-spattered pig. Ogres also delight in the gleam of gold and silver, and they will fight one another over small handfuls of coins. Smarter creatures can earn an ogre's trust by offering it gold or a weapon forged for a creature of its size.

Legendary Stupidity. Few ogres can count to ten, even with their fingers in front of them. Most speak only a rudimentary form of Giant and know a smattering of Common words. Ogres believe what they are told and are easy to fool or confuse, but they break things they don't understand. Silver-tongued tricksters who test their talents on these savages typically end up eating their eloquent words-and then being eaten in turn.

Primitive Wanderers. Ogres clothe themselves in animal pelts and uproot trees for use as crude tools and weapons. They create stone-tipped javelins for hunting. When they establish lairs, they settle near the rural edges of civilized lands, taking advantage of poorly protected livestock, undefended larders, and unwary farmers.
An ogre sleeps in cave ;, animal dens, or under trees until it finds a cabin or isolated farmhouse, whereupon it kills the inhabitants and lairs there. Whenever it is bored or hungry, an ogre ventures out from its lair, attacking anything that crosses its path. Only after an ogre has depleted an area of food does it move on.
combat-strategy: Charge: 40 ft. of closing speed plus Greatclub (+6, avg 13) or Javelin volleys (up to 120 ft.) at the party's archers. Target the smallest or most fragile foe first — ogre tactics are simple: hit the soft thing hardest, and its 19 STR says shove them into walls, bull-rush them prone (contest their Athletics), or hurl them (DM-granted for flavor) before following up at 30 ft. of movement per round. Bring multiple javelins to the opening round to soften the backline, then wade in swinging; low INT (5) means it doesn't disengage, doesn't flank, and doesn't stop when hurt — it grins and swings again. Poor 8 Dex and 11 AC mean it eats opportunity attacks and saves, so use it where the terrain bottlenecks the party into its reach, not in open fields where rogues and rangers kite it to death. It routs only when near-dead and out of options, bellowing and smashing its way out with javelins in hand — or it dies where it stands, which is most of the time.

name: Ogre Zombie
languages: Understands Common and Giant but can't speak

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

traits.name: Undead Fortitude
traits.description: If damage reduces the zombie to 0 Hit Points, it makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 5 plus the damage taken) unless the damage is Radiant or from a Critical Hit. On a successful save, the zombie drops to 1 Hit Point instead.

combat-strategy: The zombie's entire strategy is Undead Fortitude: at CON 18 and +6 to the DC 5 + damage save, it will stand up from near-fatal blows over and over, so the party will burn its best attacks for nothing — the GM's job is to make every hit feel futile until someone lands radiant damage or a critical hit. Walk straight at the nearest creature at 30 ft. per turn; there is no tactics beyond the inevitable — one Slam (+6, avg 13) per round, endlessly, through every barrier, door, and pin. Corner it in corridors where the party can't all reach at once, letting its 85 effective HP soak attacks one at a time; it doesn't feel pain, fear, or fatigue, so night marches and sealed tomb patrols are its natural hunting ground. Warn players through description — the club blow that should fell it merely staggers it — then make the kill a puzzle: fire, radiant damage, or sustained focus fire past its save threshold. If its arms are torn away or it's sunk in deep water, it still crawls; the only retreat is dust.

name: Ogrillon Ogre

actions.name: Battleaxe
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

combat-strategy: Ogrillon ogres are blunt instruments: open by hurling javelins at approaching ranged casters or archers, then close to swing the battleaxe once enemies are in reach. Target the squishiest backline first — their +5 attacks and 17 Strength punish lightly-armored wizards and clerics who get within 5 feet. Keep them in packs so the party's attention splits across multiple +5 attack rolls, and don't bother with complex maneuvers; their 7 Intelligence means simple, direct aggression works best. They fight until reduced to roughly a quarter HP, then flee if a leader or treasure is at stake, otherwise they brawl to the death.

name: Oni

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The oni makes two Claw or Nightmare Ray attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 10 (1d12 + 4) Slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Nightmare Ray
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +5, range 60 ft. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the start of the oni's next turn.

actions.name: Shape-Shift
actions.description: The oni shape-shifts into a Small or Medium Humanoid or a Large Giant, or it returns to its true form. Other than its size, its game statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The oni casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13):
1/Day Each: Charm Person (level 2 version), Darkness, Gaseous Form, Sleep
actions.save_effect: The target makes a Charisma saving throw against the oni's spell save DC. The save effect depends on which spell is cast: Charm Person (Wisdom save to be charmed), Darkness (no save), Gaseous Form (no save), Sleep (no save).

bonus_actions.name: Invisibility
bonus_actions.description: The oni casts Invisibility on itself, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.description: The oni regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns if it has at least 1 Hit Point.

description:
In nursery rhymes, oni are fearsome bogeymen that haunt the nightmares of children and adults alike, yet they are very real and always hungry. They find human babies especially delicious. Oni look like demonic ogres with blue or green skin, dark hair, and a pair of short ivory horns protruding from their foreheads. Their eyes are dark with strikingly white pupils, and their teeth and claws are jet black.

Night Haunters. By the light of day, an oni hides its true form with magic, gaining the trust of those it intends to betray when darkness descends. These creatures can change their size as well as their shape, appearing as humanoids as they pass through towns, pretending to be travelers, woodcutters, or frontier folk. In such a form, an oni takes stock of the selection of humanoids in a settlement and devises ways to abduct and devour some of them.

Magical Ogres. Oni are sometimes called ogre mages because of their innate magical ability. Though they are only distantly related to true ogres, they share the ogres' habit of joining forces with other evil creatures. An oni serves a master if doing so proves lucrative or provides it with a luxurious, well-defended home. Oni covet magic, and they work for evil wizards and hags in exchange for useful magic items.
combat-strategy: Open with Invisibility as a bonus action, then stalk invisible firing Nightmare Rays (which frighten on hit) or casting Charm Person and Sleep on the party's leader or a low-Wisdom straggler. Regeneration of 10 HP per turn means the oni trades blows happily — use Multiattack with 10-foot Claws (necrotic on top) and let it kite 30 feet of hover to stay out of melee reach while it heals. Use Darkness to blind non-magical pursuers and Gaseous Form or Shape-Change to escape or infiltrate before a fight. Focus down one isolated target with focused attacks before the party can cluster, and disengage via flight or Gaseous Form when HP drops near 30, since acid and fire are the only reliable ways to stop its regeneration.

name: Orc

actions.name: Greataxe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d12 + 3) slashing damage.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.

traits.name: Aggressive
traits.description: As a bonus action, the orc can move up to its speed toward a hostile creature that it can see.

description:
Orcs are savage raiders and pillagers with stooped postures, low foreheads, and piggish faces with prominent lower canines that resemble tusks.

Gruumsh One-Eye. Orcs worship Gruumsh, the mightiest of the orc deities and their creator. The orcs believe that in ancient days, the gods gathered to divide the world among their followers. When Gruumsh claimed the mountains, he learned they had been taken by the dwarves. He laid claim to the forests, but those had been settled by the elves. Each place that Gruumsh wanted had already been claimed. The other gods laughed at Gruumsh, but he responded with a furious bellow. Grasping his mighty spear, he laid waste to the mountains, set the forests aflame, and carved great furrows in the fields. Such was the role of the orcs, he proclaimed, to take and destroy all that the other races would deny them. To this day, the orcs wage an endless war on humans, elves, dwarves, and other folk.
Ores hold a particular hatred for elves. The elven god Corellon Larethian half-blinded Gruumsh with a well­ placed arrow to the orc god's eye. Since then, the orcs have taken particularjoy in slaughtering elves. Turning his injury into a baleful gift, Gruumsh grants divine might to any champion who willingly plucks out one of its eyes in his honor.

Tribes like Plagues. Orcs gather in tribes that exert their dominance and satisfy their bloodlust by plundering villages, devouring or driving off roaming herds, and slaying any humanoids that stand against them. After savaging a settlement, orcs pick it clean of wealth and items usable in their own lands. They set the remains of villages and camps ablaze, then retreat whence they came, their bloodlust satisfied.

Ranging Scavengers. Their lust for slaughter demands that orcs dwell always within striking distance of new targets. As such, they seldom settle permanently, instead converting ruins, cavern complexes, and defeated foes' villages into fortified camps and strongholds. Orcs build only for defense, making no innovation or improvement to their lairs beyond mounting the severed body parts of their victims on spiked stockade walls or pikes jutting up from moats and trenches.
When an existing territory is depleted of food, an orc tribe divides into roving bands that scout for choice hunting grounds. When each party returns, it brings back trophies and news of targets ripe for attack, the richest of which is chosen. The tribe then sets out en masse to carve a bloody path to its new territory.
On rare occasions, a tribe's leader chooses to hold onto a particularly defensible lair for decades. The orcs of such a tribe must range far across the countryside to sate their appetites.

Leadership and Might. Orc tribes are mostly patriarchal, flaunting such vivid or grotesque titles as Many-Arrows, Screaming Eye, and Elf Ripper. Occasionally, a powerful war chief unites scattered orc tribes into a single rampaging horde, which runs roughshod over other orc tribes and humanoid settlements from a position of overwhelming strength.
Strength and power are the greatest of orcish virtues, and orcs embrace all manner of mighty creatures in their tribes. Rejecting notions of racial purity, they proudly welcome ogres, trolls, half-orcs, and orogs into their ranks. As well, orcs respect and fear the size and power of evil giants, and often serve them as guards and soldiers.

Ore Crossbreeds. Luthic, the orc goddess of fertility and wife of Gruumsh, demands that orcs procreate often and indiscriminately so that orc hordes swell generation after generation. The orcs' drive to reproduce runs stronger than any other humanoid race, and they readily crossbreed with other races. When an orc procreates with a non-ore humanoid of similar size and stature (such as a human or a dwarf), the resulting child is either an orc or a half-orc. When an orc produces young with an ogre, the child is a half-ogre of intimidating strength and brutish features called an ogrillon.
combat-strategy: Orcs are a melee swarm: use Aggressive as a bonus action to close 30 extra feet on turn one, then attack with the greataxe for heavy 1d12+3 damage. Fire javelins only at fleeing or isolated targets, since a thrown javelins wastes the chance to swing. Coordinate in packs to surround solo party members — orcs outnumbered by armored knights should fall back toward cover or allies, and broken warbands rout when half their number fall.

name: Orc Eye of Gruumsh

actions.name: Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft.. one target. Hit: 11 (1d6 + 3 plus 1d8) piercing damage, or 12 (2d8 + 3) piercing damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack.

traits.name: Aggressive
traits.description: As a bonus action, the orc can move up to its speed toward a hostile creature that it can see.

traits.name: Gruumsh's Fury
traits.description: The orc deals an extra 4 (1d8) damage when it hits with a weapon attack (included in the attacks).

traits.name: Spellcasting
traits.description:
The orc is a 3rd-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 11 , +3 to hit with spell attacks). The orc has the following cleric spells prepared:

Cantrips (at wil1): guidance, resistance, thaumaturgy
1st level (4 slots): bless, command
2nd level (2 slots): augury, spiritual weapon (spear)

description:
When an orc slays an elf in Gruumsh's name and offers the corpse of its foe as a sacrifice to the god of slaughter, an aspect of the god might appear. This aspect demands an additional sacrifice: one of the orc's eyes, symbolizing the loss Gruumsh suffered at the hands of his greatest enemy, Corellon Larethian.
If the orc plucks out one of its eyes, Gruumsh might grant the orc spellcasting ability and special favor, along with the right to call itself an Eye of Gruumsh. When not using their auguries to advise their war chiefs, these savage devotees of the god of slaughter hurl themselves into battle, their weapons stained with blood.
combat-strategy: Open by casting bless on nearby orcs (their +1d4 attack bonus stacks fast across a warband), then hang back behind the front line and use command to make a martial attacker stop or grovel mid-charge. Two-handed spear attacks for 1d6+3+1d8 when safe, keep spiritual weapon (spear) spinning in the middle of a melee cluster to add damage without exposing the cleric, and save augury for the GM's foreshadowing, not combat. Position behind other orcs at 20–60 feet so enemies must cross the melee line to reach the healer-support; use guidance on party-facing troublemakers and retreat into the horde when focused.

name: Orc War Chief

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The orc makes two attacks with its greataxe or its spear.

actions.name: Greataxe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (1d12 + 4 plus 1d8) slashing damage.

actions.name: Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (1d6 + 4 plus 1d8) piercing damage, or 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack.

actions.name: Battle Cry
actions.description: Each creature of the war chief's choice that is within 30 feet ofit, can hear it, and not already affected by Battle Cry gain advantage on attack rolls until the start of the war chief's next turn. The war chief can then make one attack as a bonus action.
actions.advisory_message: grants advantage on ATTACK ROLLS to creatures of the war chief's choice within 30 ft that can hear it and are not already affected, until the start of the war chief's next turn, then one weapon attack as a bonus action — advisory record: ally selection, can-hear, and the bonus-action attack leg are GM-enforced (§42 choice/enforcement + §123 bonus-action zero-consumer); advantage is not auto-applied because targets are GM-chosen per RAW. 1/Day tracked by GM (cosmetic usage).

traits.name: Aggressive
traits.description: As a bonus action, the orc can move up to its speed toward a hostile creature that it can see.

traits.name: Gruumsh's Fury
traits.description: The orc deals an extra 4 (1d8) damage when it hits with a weapon attack (included in the attacks).

description:
The war chief of an orc tribe is its strongest and most cunning member. The reign of a war chief lasts only as long as it commands the fear and respect of other tribe members, whose bloodlust must be regularly satisfied lest the chief appear weak.

Scions of Slaughter. Gruumsh bestows special blessings upon war chiefs who prove themselves in battle time and again, imbuing them with slivers of his savagery. A war chief so blessed finds that his weapons cut deeper into his enemies, allowing him to inflict more carnage.
combat-strategy: Open with Battle Cry the moment melee joins — the whole warband gains advantage on attacks and the chief gets a free bonus-action greataxe swing. Multiattack with greataxe for 15+1d8 damage per swing, focusing the party's front-line fighter or whoever breaks formation, and use Aggressive as a bonus action to stay locked on a target rather than chasing. Save javelin-phase fights by staying in the back rank throwing spears until the lines meet. The chief is the buff engine: protect it by keeping orcs in a 30-foot bubble around it, and when HP falls below half, fall back fighting, relying on Gruumsh's Fury two-handed spear reach and advantage from Battle Cry to cover the retreat.

name: Orog

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The orog makes two greataxe attacks.

actions.name: Greataxe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (1d12 + 4) slashing damage.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage.

traits.name: Aggressive
traits.description: As a bonus action, the orog can move up to its speed toward a hostile creature that it can see.

description:
Orogs are orcs blessed with a surprisingly keen intellect that ordinary ores believe is a gift from the orc goddess Luthic. Like Luthic, orogs prefer to live underground, although the scarcity of food often brings them to the surface to hunt. Orcs respect an orog's strength and cunning, and a lone orog might command an orc war band.

Stronger and Smarter. An orog uses its strength to bully other orcs and its intelligence to surprise enemies on the battlefield. Many an overconfident elf, human, or dwarf commander has watched a "simple" orc warlord execute a clever maneuver to outflank and destroy an opposing force, not realizing the orc is an orog.
When encountered in great numbers, orogs form their own detachments within much larger orc hordes, and they are always at the forefront of any attack, relying on their superior strength and tactical insight to overcome anything that stands in their way.
Few orc tribes actively seek out orogs to bolster their ranks. The orogs' superiority makes them ideal leaders, and thus deadly rivals to orc war chiefs, who must be wary of orog treachery.

Detached Killers. Wanting nothing more than to hack their enemies to pieces, orogs are a terrifying presence on the battlefield. They form no attachments, even to their parents and siblings, and have no concept of love or dedication. They worship the orc pantheon of gods­ Gruumsh and Luthic foremost-because they believe that the gods have strength beyond reason, and physical might is all they respect.

Servants of Darkness. Mistrusted by orcs, some orogs form independent mercenary war bands that sell themselves to the highest bidder. As long as they are rewarded, orog mercenaries gladly serve as elite warriors and shock troops for evil wizards, depraved giants, and other villains.
combat-strategy: Orogs are elite heavy hitters: charge with Aggressive to convert bonus-action movement into two greataxe attacks (+6, 1d12+4 each) the same turn they appear. Prioritize heavily armored front-line fighters — a crit or a double hit can drop a knight in one round — and pair them in pairs so the party must split its front line. Use javelins at fleeing or ranged enemies, then close; they wear plate-like AC 18 from natural toughness and fight savagely to the death, but tactically smart orogs will disengage toward cover or a chieftain when half-dead.

name: Otyugh
languages: Otyugh; telepathy 120 ft. (doesn't allow the receiving creature to respond telepathically)

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The otyugh makes one Bite attack and two Tentacle attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Piercing damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition. Whenever the Poisoned target finishes a Long Rest, it is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 15. Failure: The target's Hit Point maximum decreases by 5 (1d10) and doesn't return to normal until the Poisoned condition ends on the target. Success: The Poisoned condition ends.

actions.name: Tentacle
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13) from one of two tentacles.

actions.name: Tentacle Slam
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 14, each creature Grappled by the otyugh. Failure: 16 (3d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the start of the otyugh's next turn. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 16 (3d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the start of the otyugh's next turn. Success: Half damage only.

description:
An otyugh is a grotesque, bulbous creature borne along on three sturdy legs, its eyes and nose set along a vine­ like stalk that snakes from the top of its bloated body. Two rubbery tentacles end in spiky, leaf-like appendages that the otyugh uses to shovel food into its gaping maw.
An otyugh buries itself under mounds of offal and carrion, leaving only its sensory stalk exposed. When an edible creature happens by, the otyugh's tentacles erupt from the filth and grab hold of it.
Otyughs make the most ofany opportunity to ambush and devour prey. They use a limited form of telepathy to urge sentient creatures toward their lairs, sometimes by pretending to be something else.

Dwellers in Darkness. Otyughs tolerate bright light only when considerable stores of carrion or garbage lie within reach. In the wilderness, they dwell in stagnant swamps, scum-filled ponds, and damp forest dells. The scent of graveyards, city sewers, village middens, and manure-filled animal pens attracts them to civilized areas.
Since otyughs lack concern for anything but food, their nests sometimes accumulate a variety of treasures shed from their victims and mixed among the junk.

Symbiotic Guardians. Sentient subterranean beings can coexist with otyughs, employing them as garbage disposals. With such plentiful sustenance, otyughs grow fat in their wallows, unmoved by any other drive or desire. This sedentary gluttony makes them reliable guardians. As long as it is fed, an otyugh refrains from attacking other creatures. However, would-be otyugh masters can easily underestimate the quantity of waste, carrion, and meat necessary to keep an otyugh from wandering off in search of food. More than one "trained" otyugh has eaten its keeper after devouring all the waste in its wallow.
combat-strategy: Ambush from filth or a pit: the otyugh wants to grapple with two Tentacles (reach 10 feet, escape DC 13), then blast both grappled victims with Tentacle Slam (DC 14 Con or stunned) while it bites another adjacent foe. Grab the squishiest or most mobile characters first — rogues and casters — since a grappled target can't escape the slam and the stuns let it freely reposition its victims toward allies for follow-up slams. It's an ambush predator that prefers terrain where prey must approach it (tunnels, garbage pits, sewer junctions), and it will drag grappled prey into the muck or away from the party. It fights to the death defending its lair but flees into deep sludge or burrowed tunnels once reduced to about a third HP, since its Bite also inflicts a lingering disease that punishes long rests.

name: Owl

actions.name: Talons
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Slashing damage.

traits.name: Flyby
traits.description: The owl doesn't provoke an Opportunity Attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

combat-strategy: A scout, not a warrior: use Flyby and 60-foot flight to dive, snatching nothing but delivering one Talon scratch, then wheel away without provoking opportunity attacks. Its real combat value is passive perception 15 and 120-foot darkvision — keep it circling above as an aerial spotter for other monsters. If forced into a fight, simply stay out of reach aloft and harass; anything that can hurt a 1-HP bird ends it instantly, so never land near enemies.

name: Owlbear

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The owlbear makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Slashing damage.

description:
An owlbear's screech echoes through dark valleys and benighted forests, piercing the quiet night to announce the death of its prey. Feathers cover the thick, shaggy coat of its bearlike body, and the limpid pupils of its great round eyes stare furiously from its owlish head.

Deadly Ferocity. The owlbear's reputation for ferocity, aggression, stubbornness, and sheer ill temper makes it one of the most feared predators of the wild. There is little, if anything, that a hungry owlbear fears. Even monsters that outmatch an owlbear in size and strength avoid tangling with it, for this creature cares nothing about a foe's superior strength as it attacks without provocation.

Consummate Predators. An owlbear emerges from its den around sunset and hunts into the darkest hours of the night, hooting or screeching to declare its territory, to search for a mate, or to flush prey into its hunting grounds. These are typically forests familiar to the owlbear, and dense enough to limit its quarry's escape routes.
An owlbear makes its den in a cave or ruin littered with the bones of its prey. It drags partially devoured kills back to its den, storing portions of the carcass among the surrounding rocks, bushes, and trees. The scent of blood and rotting flesh hangs heavy near an owlbear's lair, attracting scavengers and thus luring more prey.
Owlbears hunt alone or in mated pairs. If quarry is plentiful, a family of owlbears might remain together for longer than is required to rear offspring. Otherwise, they part ways as soon as the young are ready to hunt.

Savage Companions. Although they are more intelligent than most animals, owlbears are difficult to tame. However, with enough time, food, and luck, an intelligent creature can train an owlbear to recognize it as a master, making it an unflinching guard or a fast and hardy mount. People of remote frontier settlements have even succeeded at racing owlbears, but spectators bet as often on which owlbear will attack its handler as they do on which will reach the finish line first.
Elven communities encourage owlbears to den beneath their treetop villages, using the beasts as a natural defense during the night. Hobgoblins favor owlbears as war beasts, and hill giants and frost giants sometimes keep owlbears as pets. A starved owlbear might show up in a gladiatorial arena, ruthlessly eviscerating and devouring its foes before a bloodthirsty audience.

Owlbear Origins. Scholars have long debated the origins of the owlbear. The most common theory is that a demented wizard created the first specimen by crossing a giant owl with a bear. However, venerable elves claim to have known these creatures for thousands ofyears, and some fey insist that owlbears have always existed in the Feywild.
combat-strategy: Ambush from cover or dark woods with a 40-foot charge and two Rend attacks (+7, 2d8+5 each) on whoever is nearest and squishiest. It has no cunning — play it as pure brute aggression: always Multiattack, always attack the closest target, and never retreat or reposition intelligently. Use its 40-foot walk and 40-foot climb to burst out of unexpected angles (down trees or off rocks) onto travelers on a road, and let it fight to the death since it is mindless-temperament and too stupid to disengage.

name: Panther

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Slashing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Nimble Escape
bonus_actions.description: The panther takes the Disengage or Hide action.

combat-strategy: Classic ambush predator: use Stealth +7 and darkvision to lie in wait, then pounce from hiding with advantage on its Rend attack, using 50-foot speed to close distance before prey reacts. Use Nimble Escape as a bonus action to Hide mid-combat and break line of sight — panthers often disengage, vanish into undergrowth, and strike again from a different direction. Target isolated stragglers, pack animals, or light-armored scouts, and after one or two hits on a wounded prey, fade away rather than fight to the death; a wounded panther is exactly what Nimble Escape is for.

name: Pegasus
languages: Understands Celestial, Common, Elvish, and Sylvan but can't speak

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 5 (2d4) Radiant damage.

description:
The white winged horses known a s pegasi soar through the skies, a vision of grace and majesty. When they touch down on solid ground, they linger only for a moment, drinking from mountain springs and pristine lakes. Any sound or sign of another creature startles them, sending them off to fly once more among the clouds.

Noble Mounts. Pegasi are highly prized as swift and reliable steeds, being faster and less temperamental than griffons, hippogriffs, and wyverns. However, these wild and shy creatures are as intelligent as humanoids, and so can't be traditionally broken and tamed. A pegasus must be persuaded to serve a good-aligned creature as a mount, but when it does so, it forges a life­ long bond with its new companion.

Born of the Planes. Pegasi trace their origins to the Olympian Glades of Arborea, where they soar through the skies of that plane and serve as faithful mounts to the Seldarine, the pantheon of elven gods. These gods have been known to send pegasi to the Material Plane to aid those in need.

Pegasi Nests. Pegasi mate for life, build their nests in hard-to-reach locations, and give birth to live young.
combat-strategy: A celestial steed first, fighter second: use 90-foot flight to dive on enemies, striking with Hooves (bludgeoning plus radiant) and rising back out of reach before melee can engage. Target evil or wicked creatures it opposes, focusing on single mid-squadron passes where the target is exposed. In a defensive role it should stay airborne, keeping melee-only enemies wasting actions, and retreat by simply flying away when its rider is in danger — pegasus will not fight to the death if its rider can be spirited off.

name: Pentadrone

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The pentadrone makes five arm attacks.

actions.name: Arm
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Paralysis Gas
actions.description: The pentadrone exhales a 30 foot cone of gas. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or be paralyzed for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target is paralyzed for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

traits.name: Axiomatic Mind
traits.description: The pentadrone can't be compelled to act in a manner contrary to its nature or its instructions.

traits.name: Disintegration
traits.description: If the pentadrone dies, its body disintegrates into dust, leaving behind its weapons and anything else it was carrying.

description: Pentadrones oversee Mechanus's worker populace and can improvise in response to new situations.
combat-strategy: March straight at enemies — a modron never flanks, feints, or retreats. Open by closing the 40-foot gap and unleashing Multiattack (five +4 arm attacks) on the nearest cluster, then reserve Paralysis Gas for when two or more enemies group up or when a spellcaster steps forward: a DC 11 Con save or 1-minute paralysis (repeat save each turn) removes a key combatant. Save it for the widest cone you can get, ideally against a corridor or doorway choke point. It cannot be charmed or turned, so it fights to disintegration — its corpse literally explodes into dust — and it happily self-sacrifices to complete its orders.

name: Performer

actions.name: Shortsword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

reactions.name: Uncanny Dodge
reactions.trigger: The performer is hit by an attack roll
reactions.description: The performer halves the damage (round down) it takes from that attack.

combat-strategy: A lightly armored skirmisher: use Uncanny Dodge reaction to halve the biggest incoming hit, then fight with the shortsword against whoever closes, exploiting Acrobatics +5 to tumble through enemies' spaces and disengage. Prefer hit-and-run: strike an exposed target, Dodge or move behind cover, and avoid sustained melee against martial characters since only 27 HP cannot last a slugfest. Outside combat, its Performance +7 and Charisma make it better at defusing, distracting, or talking its way out — a cornered performer will talk, bluff, or flee rather than die.

name: Performer Legend

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The performer makes three Bejeweled Baton attacks.

actions.name: Bejeweled Baton
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d4 + 5) Bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Majestic Song
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 17, each creature in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within 120 feet. Failure: 22 (4d8 + 4) Psychic damage, and the target has the Charmed or Frightened condition (performer's choice) until the end of the performer's next turn. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 22 (4d8 + 4) Psychic damage, and the target has the Charmed or Frightened condition (performer's choice) until the end of the performer's next turn. Success: Half damage only.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The performer casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17):
At Will: Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Prestidigitation
1/Day Each: Major Image, Project Image

reactions.name: Warding Charm
reactions.trigger: A creature hits the performer with an attack roll
reactions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 17, the triggering creature. Failure: The attack roll misses the performer, and the target has the Charmed condition until the end of the performer's next turn.
reactions.save_effect: Failure: The attack roll misses the performer, and the target has the Charmed condition until the end of the performer's next turn.

combat-strategy: Open with Majestic Song (DC 17 Wis or 22 psychic damage plus Charmed or Frightened) at the densest cluster of the party, choosing Charmed on martial leaders to turn them and Frightened on anyone with fear weaknesses. Use Warding Charm reaction freely — a failed DC 17 Wis save means the attack simply misses AND the attacker is Charmed, so bait attacks from the strongest striker. Multiattack three Bejeweled Batons (+9, 20 damage each) on isolated or charmed targets, who can be freely attacked (attacking a Charmed creature doesn't break charm instantly, but keep the song re-applying it). Use Project Image or Major Image to fake a dueling double while the real performer repositions, and kite with 30-foot movement and AC 20; withdraw via illusion and Stealth +9 when the song's control lapses and HP drops below half.

name: Performer Maestro

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The performer makes three Rapier attacks.

actions.name: Rapier
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Beguiling Song
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within 120 feet. Failure: 20 (3d10 + 4) Psychic damage, and the target has the Charmed condition until the end of the performer's next turn. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 20 (3d10 + 4) Psychic damage, and the target has the Charmed condition until the end of the performer's next turn. Success: Half damage only.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The performer casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15):
At Will: Minor Illusion, Prestidigitation
1/Day: Tasha's Hideous Laughter (level 3 version)

combat-strategy: Lead with Beguiling Song (DC 15 or Charmed) on the party's clustered members, then follow with a 3rd-level Tasha's Hideous Laughter (DC 15) on a different target to drop two controllers at once. Multiattack three rapiers (+7, 15 damage) on charmed or prone victims, and use kiting footwork: Acrobatics +10, Stealth +7, and 30-foot movement let the maestro strike, tumble to cover, and Hide, staying 120 feet from casters when casting. Save the song for moments when the party bunches up, and Minor Illusion or Prestidigitation for misdirection during repositioning. When focus turns nasty, charm the martial front-runner, then escape through crowd or cover; a maestro never lets itself get surrounded.

name: Peryton
languages: Understands Common and Elvish but can't speak

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The peryton makes one Gore attack and one Talons attack.

actions.name: Gore
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage. If the peryton moved 30+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 9 (2d8) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Talons
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) Piercing damage. If the attack reduces a Humanoid target to 0 Hit Points, the peryton kills the target by removing its heart.

traits.name: Flyby
traits.description: The peryton doesn't provoke an Opportunity Attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

description:
Although this monstrous carnivore feeds on any creature, it prefers humanoids, especially elves, half-elves, and humans. When it kills a humanoid, a peryton rips out its prey's heart and takes it back to its nest to be devoured.
The peryton is a bizarre creature that blends the body and wings of a bird of prey with the head of a stag. Its strangest feature is its shadow, which appears humanoid rather than reflecting the creature's physical form. Sages postulate that the first perytons were humans transformed by a hideous curse or magical experiment, but bards tell a different tale of a man whose infidelity caused his scorned wife to cut out the heart of her younger, more beautiful rival and consume it in a ritual intended to forever win her husband's heart. The ritual succeeded until the woman's villainy was exposed. She was hanged for her crime, but the lingering magic of her foul ritual caused the carrion birds that feasted on her corpse to transform into the first perytons.

Unnatural Hunger. Aperyton's reproductive cycle depends on the heart of a freshly killed humanoid. The organ must be consumed by a female peryton before she can reproduce. When a peryton consumes a heart, its shadow changes for a brief time to reflect its true monstrous form.
When attacking a humanoid, a peryton is single­ minded and relentless, fighting until it or its prey dies. If a peryton is somehow driven away, it stalks lost prey from afar, attacking again when the opportunity arises.

Bane of the Mountains. Perytons roost atop mountain ridges and lair in high caves. They prey on creatures living or wandering in the vales below, and travelers on lonely mountain roads learn to keep a wary eye on the sky. Because normal weapons are less effective against perytons, the folk of the mountains know to avoid confrontations with these monsters at all costs.
Established settlements are attractive to perytons as a renewable food source. As such, village councils and local nobles often hire adventurers to eliminate peryton nests.
combat-strategy: Sky hunter: circle at altitude, then dive with a 30+ foot straight run for the Gore bonus damage (extra 2d8) followed by Talons on the same swoop, and Flyby back to the air. Hunt on the ground where they can't chase — target stragglers and anyone isolated from the pack, and go for the kill shot on humanoids, since Talons at 0 HP rips out the heart instantly. Fly past a target to bait opportunity attacks it never provokes, and dive from the sun side to use Stealth +3 and glare. Flocks of four or five can surround a lone traveler; individual perytons break off when bloodied or when prey proves dangerous.

name: Phase Spider

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The spider makes two Bite attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) Poison damage. If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, the target becomes Stable, and it has the Poisoned condition for 1 hour. While Poisoned, the target also has the Paralyzed condition.

bonus_actions.name: Ethereal Jaunt
bonus_actions.description: The spider teleports from the Material Plane to the Ethereal Plane or vice versa.

traits.name: Ethereal Sight
traits.description: The spider can see 60 feet into the Ethereal Plane while on the Material Plane and vice versa.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The spider can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

traits.name: Web Walker
traits.description: The spider ignores movement restrictions caused by webs, and the spider knows the location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

description: A phase spider possesses the magical ability to phase in and out of the Ethereal Plane. It seems to appear out of nowhere and quickly vanishes after attacking. Its movement on the Ethereal Plane before coming back to the Material Plane makes it seem like it can teleport.
combat-strategy: Fight between planes: start in the Ethereal Plane (invisible on the Material) using Ethereal Sight to pick a straggler, shift in as a bonus action, Multiattack two Bites (poison and paralysis), then jaunt back ethereal before the party can punish. Target the backline — archers, casters, healers — since it can phase through them unopposed, and remember its 0-HP bite trick: victims are stabilized but poisoned-paralyzed for an hour, perfect for dragging live trophies away. Use ceiling web terrain and climb speed to attack from above. Disengage ethereally whenever focus lands on it; it never stands and trades.

name: Piercer

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Drop
actions.description: The piercer falls. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 11, one creature directly underneath the piercer. Failure: 10 (3d6) Piercing damage. Failure or Success: The piercer reduces any damage it takes from the fall by 20.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 10 (3d6) Piercing damage

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The piercer can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

description:
Clinging to the ceilings of caverns and large subterranean passages, piercers blend in perfectly with natural rock, dropping in silence to impale unsuspecting foes on the ground below.
A piercer is the larval form of a roper, and the two creatures often attack in tandem. A rock-like shell encases a piercer's body, giving it the look and texture of a stalactite. That shell protects a soft, slug-like upper body that lets the piercer move across cavern walls and ceilings to position itself for prey. With its eye and mouth closed, the piercer is difficult to distinguish from ordinary rock formations.

Patient Hunters. Piercers can see, but they can also respond to noise and heat, waiting for Jiving creatures to pass beneath them, then falling to attack. A piercer that misses its chance to kill must make its slow way back to the ceiling. A fallen piercer excretes a foul-smelling slime when attacked, making most predators think twice about eating it.
Piercers gather in colonies to maximize the effectiveness of their attacks, dropping simultaneously to increase the odds of striking prey. After a piercer successfully slays a creature, the others slowly creep toward the corpse to join in the feast.
combat-strategy: A living ambush trap: attach to a ceiling (spider climb, Stealth +5, DC 11 to notice) and Drop onto anyone passing below for 10 piercing damage, taking no fall damage thanks to its 20-damage fall reduction. Pick the densest foot-traffic corridor — a bridge, tunnel entrance, or doorway above. After dropping, Bite the prone victim (+3) and use its 15-foot climb to retreat back up a wall toward a new perch if attacked. It's a 22-Hp ambusher that should strike once from above, disengage, and re-climb rather than fight on the ground; its 30-foot blindsight means hiding from it visually helps it locate prey by vibration.

name: Piranha

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5 (with Advantage if the target doesn't have all its Hit Points), reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage.

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The piranha can breathe only underwater.

combat-strategy: Attack only in swarms, and only in water: dozens biting at once (one damage each) grind down a swimming character, and the swarm auto-advantages on any target that is already wounded — so they instinctively pile onto the bloodied. Lure PCs into deep, fast water, or scatter them mid-river crossing, then descend as a cloud. A handful of piranhas is a nuisance; twenty is a drowning threat. They cannot survive out of water, so any PC who climbs onto a boat, bank, or rock is effectively safe.

name: Pirate

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The pirate makes two Dagger attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Enthralling Panache.

actions.name: Dagger
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Enthralling Panache
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 12, one creature the pirate can see within 30 feet. Failure: The target has the Charmed condition until the start of the pirate's next turn.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target has the Charmed condition until the start of the pirate's next turn.

combat-strategy: Skirmish with daggers: Multiattack two stabs on whoever closes, or pelt from 60 feet with thrown daggers, and use Enthralling Panache (DC 12 Wis, Charmed) on a martial character to make them hesitate or turn. Charm is the opener — enthrall the front-line fighter, then stab the distracted target or rob them blind. Fight on ships and docks where cover, rigging, and tight corridors favor quick daggers, and leap overboard to swim away when a fight turns against them; pirates rarely die for their captain's cargo.

name: Pirate Admiral

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The pirate makes three attacks, using Scimitar or Pistol in any combination.

actions.name: Scimitar
actions.description:
Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 5 ft. Hit: 16 (3d6 + 6) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage, and the target suffers one of the following effects of the pirate's choice:
Awestruck. The target has the Charmed condition until the start of the pirate's next turn.
Poison. The target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the pirate's next turn.

actions.name: Pistol
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +10, range 30/90 ft. Hit: 28 (4d10 + 6) Piercing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Rally
bonus_actions.description: The pirate chooses up to three other creatures it can see within 30 feet. Until the start of the pirate's next turn, the targets have Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws.

reactions.name: Defensive Stance
reactions.trigger: The pirate is hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon
reactions.description: The pirate adds 4 to its AC against melee attack rolls (including the triggering attack) until the start of its next turn, possibly causing the attacks to miss.

combat-strategy: Open combat with Rally on three lieutenants or heavy-hitting allies — advantage on attacks AND saves for the whole crew is the force multiplier — then wade in with three-attack Multiattack. Mix pistol range shots (28 piercing each) at casters across the deck with scimitar duels, choosing Poison on a target already disadvantaged or Awestruck (Charm) on the party's commander to neutralize leadership. Hold Defensive Stance reaction against the enemy's biggest melee striker (+4 AC can flip several hits to misses). Fight anchored on the quarterdeck with crew screen it, and withdraw to the ship's wheel or a escape launch when the crew falls and HP drops below half, always keeping 30 feet of Rally range between itself and surviving allies.

name: Pirate Captain

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The pirate makes three attacks, using Rapier or Pistol in any combination.

actions.name: Rapier
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Piercing damage, and the pirate has Advantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of this turn.

actions.name: Pistol
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +7, range 30/90 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Piercing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Captain's Charm
bonus_actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 14, one creature the pirate can see within 30 feet. Failure: The target has the Charmed condition until the start of the pirate's next turn.

reactions.name: Riposte
reactions.trigger: The pirate is hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon
reactions.description: The pirate adds 3 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss. On a miss, the pirate makes one Rapier attack against the triggering creature if within range.

combat-strategy: The rapier chain is the signature: each Rapier hit grants advantage on the next attack that turn, so Multiattack three rapiers in a row (potentially +7/+7+adv/+adv) on a single target, or mix in 90-foot pistol shots to open at range. Open with Captain's Charm (DC 14) on the enemy's martial leader to freeze or turn them, then riposte (Riposte gives +3 AC and a free rapier counter) any fighter who takes the bait and attacks. Fight on moving decks and narrow gangways where the party can't surround; use 30-foot movement to stay edge-to-edge, riposte the charge, then leap to rope or rail and disengage. Retreat to the helm or a ship's boat when the fight turns, charming the closest pursuer as she goes.

name: Pit Fiend

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The pit fiend makes one Bite attack, two Devilish Claw attacks, and one Fiery Mace attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +14, reach 10 ft. Hit: 18 (3d6 + 8) Piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must make the following saving throw. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 21. Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition. While Poisoned, the target can't regain Hit Points and takes 21 (6d6) Poison damage at the start of each of its turns, and it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition

actions.name: Devilish Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +14, reach 10 ft. Hit: 26 (4d8 + 8) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Fiery Mace
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +14, reach 10 ft. Hit: 22 (4d6 + 8) Force damage plus 21 (6d6) Fire damage.

actions.name: Hellfire Spellcasting
actions.description: The pit fiend casts Fireball (level 5 version) twice, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 21). It can replace one Fireball with Hold Monster (level 7 version) or Wall of Fire
actions.save_effect: Dexterity saving throw. Failure: Full damage. Success: Half damage. Wisdom saving throw. Failure: The target is paralyzed. Success: The target is not affected. Dexterity saving throw. Failure: Full damage and the target must move away. Success: Half damage.

traits.name: Diabolical Restoration
traits.description: If the pit fiend dies outside the Nine Hells, its body disappears in sulfurous smoke, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Nine Hells.

traits.name: Fear Aura
traits.description: The pit fiend emanates an aura in a 20-foot Emanation while it doesn't have the Incapacitated condition. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 21, any enemy that starts its turn in the aura. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition until the start of its next turn. Success: The target is immune to this pit fiend's aura for 24 hours.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the pit fiend fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead. (4/Day)

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The pit fiend has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
The undisputed lords of most other devils, pit fiends attend the archdukes and archduchesses of the Nine Hells and carry out their wishes. These mighty devils are the generals of the Nine Hells, leading its infernal legions into battle.
With an inflated sense of superiority and entitlement, pit fiends form a grotesque aristocracy in the infernal realm. These domineering and manipulative tyrants conspire to eliminate anything that stands between them and their desires, even as they negotiate the convoluted and dangerous politics of the Nine Hells.
A pit fiend is a hulking monster with a whip-like tail and enormous wings that it wraps around itself like a cloak. Armored scales cover its body, and its fanged maw drips a venom that can lay the mightiest mortal creatures low. Fearless in battle, a pit fiend takes on the most powerful foes in single combat, demonstrating its supremacy and an arrogance that prevents it from acknowledging any chance of defeat.
combat-strategy: Command the battlefield from the air: hover with 60-foot flight, letting Fear Aura (DC 21 Wis or Frightened) melt the courage of anyone who closes. Open at range with two level-5 Fireballs (35d6 total across two casts), swapping one for level-7 Hold Monster on the party's tank or healer, or Wall of Fire to carve the battlefield in half. Then land and Multiattack (bite, two claws, fiery mace) on separated or held targets, aiming the Bite's DC 21 Con save to inflict no-healing poison that shreds healing-dependent parties. Bite applies a no-regeneration poison that's brutal vs. a cleric — chain that on whoever soaks the most fire. Magic Resistance plus four Legendary Resistances means save-or-suck rarely sticks; spend resistances on the biggest control spells (Power Word Kill, Dominate, Banishment). Fight in the Nine Hells or a summoned infernal stronghold whenever possible since death elsewhere just regens it back in Hell; withdraw to leverage politics, hostages, or devil bargains when the fight turns genuinely lethal.

name: Pixie

actions.name: Faerie Dust
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. Hit: 1 Radiant damage, and the target has the Charmed or Poisoned condition (pixie's choice) until the start of the pixie's next turn.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The pixie casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 12):
At Will: Dancing Lights, Druidcraft, Invisibility (self only)
1/Day Each: Detect Thoughts, Fly, Sleep

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The pixie has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
Standing barely a foot tall, pixies resemble diminutive elves with gossamer wings like those of dragonflies or butterflies, bright as the clear dawn and as luminous as the full moonrise. Curious as cats and shy as deer, pixies go where they please. They like to spy on other creatures and can barely contain their excitement around them. The urge to introduce themselves and strike up a friendship is almost overwhelming; only a pixie's fear of being captured or attacked stays its hand. Those who wander through a pixie's glade might never see the creatures, yet hear the occasional giggle, gasp, or sigh.
Pixies array themselves like princes and princesses of the fey, wearing flowing gowns and doublets of silk that sparkle like moonlight on a pond. Some dress in acorns, leaves, bark, and the pelts of tiny woodland beasts. They take great pride in their regalia and beam with joy when they are complimented on their ensembles.

Magical Faerie Folk. With their innate power of invisibility, pixies rarely appear unless they wish to be seen.
