In the Feywild and on the Material Plane, pixies etch patterns of frost on winter ponds and rouse the buds in springtime. They cause flowers to sparkle with summer dew, and color the leaves with the blazing hues of autumn.

Pixie Dust. When pixies fly visibly, a shower of sparkling dust follows in their wake like the glittering tail of a shooting star. A mere sprinkle of pixie dust is said to be able to grant the power of flight, confuse a creature hopelessly, or send foes into a magical slumber. Only pixies can use their dust to its full potential, but these fey are constantly sought out by mages and monsters seeking to study or master their power.

Tiny Tricksters. While the arrival of visitors piques their curiosity, pixies are too shy to reveal themselves at first. They study the visitors from afar to gauge their temperament or play harmless tricks on them to measure their reactions. For example, pixies might tie a dwarf's boots together, create illusions of strange creatures or treasures, or use dancing lights to lead interlopers astray. I f the visitors respond with hostility, the pixies give them a wide berth. If the visitors are good natured, the pixies are likely to be emboldened and more friendly. The fey might even emerge and offer to guide their "guests" along a safe route or invite them to a tiny yet satisfying feast prepared in their honor.

Opposed to Violence. Unlike their fey cousins, the sprites, pixies abhor weapons and would sooner flee than get into a physical altercation with any enemy.
combat-strategy: Harass and vanish: open with Invisibility (at will, self), then snipe with Faerie Dust (60 feet, 1 radiant plus free Charmed or Poisoned) from hiding, choosing the condition that hurts most — Poisoned on archers and rogues to negate advantage, Charmed on brutes. Save Sleep (1/day) for clustered spellcasters or a night raid, and Fly on a wounded ally to evacuate it. With only 9 HP, disengage and re-vanish constantly; 30-foot flight and Stealth +7 make a hidden pixie nearly untouchable. Never engage adjacent to a martial character; fight as a floating, invisible nuisance, and flee to the Feywild thicket if surrounded.

name: Pixie Wonderbringer

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The pixie makes two Faerie Dust attacks.

actions.name: Faerie Dust
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Radiant damage, and the target has the Charmed or Poisoned condition (pixie's choice) until the start of the pixie's next turn.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The pixie casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15):
At Will: Dancing Lights, Druidcraft, Invisibility (self only)
1/Day Each: Detect Thoughts, Fly, Major Image

bonus_actions.name: Burst of Wonder
bonus_actions.description: The pixie casts Entangle, Polymorph, or Tasha's Hideous Laughter, requiring no Material components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The pixie has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

combat-strategy: Control the field with Burst of Wonder as a bonus action — Polymorph a fighter into a harmless creature, Entangle a charging group, or Tasha's Hideous Laughter to drop a spellcaster — then Multiattack two Faerie Dust shots (+7, 15 radiant each) on the isolated or entangled victims, adding Charmed or Poisoned for free. Open with Invisibility and 60-foot Sniping, and use Major Image to fake a bigger threat or duplicate the pixie while the real one repositions. Only 60 HP and Tiny size mean constant kiting via 30-foot flight and Magic Resistance vs. saves; Polymorph a party member's ally into a crab mid-charge as defense, and flee at half HP using Invisibility and terrain. Fly (1/day) is the panic button for a full retreat.

name: Planetar

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The planetar makes three Radiant Sword attacks or uses Holy Burst twice.

actions.name: Radiant Sword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +12, reach 10 ft. Hit: 14 (2d6 + 7) Slashing damage plus 18 (4d8) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Holy Burst
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 20, each enemy in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point the planetar can see within 120 feet. Failure: 24 (7d6) Radiant damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 24 (7d6) Radiant damage. Success: Half damage

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The planetar casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as spellcasting ability (spell save DC 20):
At Will: Detect Evil and Good
1/Day Each: Commune, Control Weather, Dispel Evil and Good, Raise Dead

bonus_actions.name: Divine Aid
bonus_actions.description: The planetar casts Cure Wounds, Invisibility, Lesser Restoration, or Remove Curse, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

traits.name: Divine Awareness
traits.description: The planetar knows if it hears a lie.

traits.name: Exalted Restoration
traits.description: If the planetar dies outside Mount Celestia, its body disappears, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in Mount Celestia.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The planetar has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
Planetars act a s the weapons of the gods they serve, presenting a tangible representation of their deities' might. A planetar can call down rain to relieve a drought, or can loose an insect plague to devour crops. A planetar's celestial ears detect every falsehood, and its radiant eyes see through every deception.
Planetars are muscular and hairless and have opalescent green skin and white-feathered wings. They tower over most humanoids, brandishing immense swords with grace. Sometimes sent to aid powerful mortals on important tasks for good, planetars are especially fond of missions that involve battling fiends.
combat-strategy: Open with flyby positioning 30–60 ft. above the fight where its 120-ft. flight and truesight make it untouchable, then Multiattack with Holy Burst twice each round against clustered enemies (DC 20 Dex for 24 radiant each is better than three swords against groups, while single targets eat three Radiant Swords for ~32 damage each). Use Divine Aid as a bonus action to keep wounded allies alive with Cure Wounds, or Invisibility to reposition an endangered ally, and spam Dispel Evil and Good on turn one if fiends or summoned minions are on the field since it ends their summons outright. Its Magic Resistance plus massive HP means it can stand in the open and trade blows without fear; kite flyers and spellcasters by descending 120-ft. per round, and remember Raise Dead mid-adventure makes it a plot-proof protector. It fights to the death in service of good rather than retreating, but if it falls outside Mount Celestia it simply reforms there — so a 'killed' planetar is a recurring ally, not a one-shot resource.

name: Plesiosaurus

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage.

traits.name: Hold Breath
traits.description: The plesiosaurus can hold its breath for 1 hour.

description: A plesiosaurus is a marine dinosaur whose compact body is driven by powerful flippers. Predatory and aggressive, it attacks any creature it encounters. Its flexible neck accounts for a third of its total length, letting it twist in any direction to deliver a powerful bite.
combat-strategy: A dumb aquatic ambush predator: stay submerged where its Stealth +4 and 1-hour Hold Breath let it lurk beneath the surface until prey is within its 10-ft. reach Bite. Target the lone swimmer, the raft, or the small boat — its 40-ft. swim speed outpaces most swimmers so it can chase anyone who tries to paddle away. On land it is nearly helpless (20 ft. walk, 13 AC, 68 HP), so drag fights into deep water and never let archers engage it from shore where it can't respond. It bites, submerges to heal the perception cycle, and bites again; when reduced to roughly half HP it usually loses interest and sinks away unless cornered.

name: Poisonous Snake

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1 piercing damage, and the target must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw, taking 5 (2d4) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 5 (2d4) poison damage. Success: Half damage

combat-strategy: Ambush from grass, rafters, or cargo where its Tiny size and 10-ft. blindsight help it stay unnoticed until a victim walks within 5 ft., then Bite once — the DC 10 Con save for poison damage is the real payload, not the 1 piercing. Snakes act as minor hazards or swarm encounters: place several in cramped corridors so martial attackers risk friendly fire on Tiny targets at 1 AC-equivalent softness. With 2 HP any hit kills it, so its entire doctrine is one surprise strike then flee at 30 ft. into a crack or drain it can squeeze through; use them to drain healing and spell slots, never as a solo threat.

name: Polar Bear

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The bear makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) Slashing damage.

combat-strategy: Charge from cover or blizzard-white terrain using Stealth +4, closing 40 ft. per round to deliver Multiattack Rend (two attacks, ~9 slashing each) against whoever strays closest. It is fast on land and water equally (40/40), so drive prey toward ice or shallows where it has mobility parity while armored humanoids slow down. Go for stragglers and knock them off balance rather than tanking the party's front line — 42 HP and AC 12 won't last against concentrated fire. Bloodied or cornered it fights to the death with advantage-free brutality; otherwise a wounded bear often breaks off after a mauling, especially if prey returns to boats or shelters.

name: Poltergeist

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The poltergeist makes one Object Slam attack and uses Telekinetic Thrust.

actions.name: Object Slam
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. or range 30 ft. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Telekinetic Thrust
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 12, one creature the poltergeist can see within 30 feet. Failure: 9 (2d6 + 2) Force damage, and the target is pushed up to 30 feet straight away from the poltergeist.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 9 (2d6 + 2) Force damage, and the target is pushed up to 30 feet straight away from the poltergeist

bonus_actions.name: Vanish
bonus_actions.description: The poltergeist gives itself the Invisible condition or ends that condition on itself.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.description: The poltergeist can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

combat-strategy: Open with Vanish (bonus action) to go Invisible, then harass from range with Object Slam (30 ft.) and Telekinetic Thrust, pushing victims 30 ft. straight away — ideally off cliffs, into spinning blades, or out of torchlight where its 60-ft. darkvision advantage flips. Hover out of reach at 10–20 ft. altitude since it walks only 5 ft.; its Multiattack (slam + thrust) is the standard turn once detected. Use walls and doors freely via Incorporeal Movement but never end a turn inside an object (1d10 force damage). With 22 HP it trades invisibility cycles for survival: Vanish when focused, reappear elsewhere, throw objects, repeat — it disengages into the walls when reduced to single-digit HP.

name: Pony

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Bludgeoning damage.

combat-strategy: A pony is pack mule or panic victim, not a combatant: its Hooves (+4, 1d4+2) only matter if cornered or spooked into kicking at whatever looms nearest. In any fight it bolts at 40 ft. toward open ground, and riders must make mount checks or be thrown — use uncontrolled stampedes through tight corridors as the real hazard. Protect handlers will fight to defend it; otherwise treat it as destroyable terrain that charges through the party, breaks formations, and drags tack-loaded supplies into danger before collapsing from its 11 HP.

name: Priest

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The priest makes two attacks, using Mace or Radiant Flame in any combination.

actions.name: Mace
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Bludgeoning damage plus 5 (2d4) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Radiant Flame
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 60 ft. Hit: 11 (2d10) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The priest casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability:
At Will: Light, Thaumaturgy
1/Day: Spirit Guardians

bonus_actions.name: Divine Aid
bonus_actions.description: The priest casts Bless, Dispel Magic, Healing Word, or Lesser Restoration, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

description:
Priests bring the teachings of their gods to the common folk. They are the spiritual leaders of temples and shrines and often hold positions of influence in their communities. Evil priests might work openly under a tyrant, or they might be the leaders of religious sects hidden in the shadows of good society, overseeing depraved rites.
A priest typically has one or more acolytes to help with religious ceremonies and other sacred duties.
combat-strategy: Open combat with Spirit Guardians (one/day) as the force-multiplier, then hang back at 60 ft. firing Radiant Flame (or closing to melee only when protected) since Multiattack with mace-plus-flame keeps damage steady while enemies must cross the spinning spirits. Spellcast via bonus action every round: Healing Word on the most wounded ally (it can still attack that turn), Bless on the front line, Dispel Magic on enemy magic, Lesser Restoration on conditions. Position behind cover and full cover-reload cycles — 38 HP and AC 13 won't survive focus fire — and let its Radiant mace finish helpless or prone targets. It retreats behind allies or flees to regroup once its Spirit Guardians and heal slots are spent, since at that point it is just a modest mace fighter.

name: Priest Acolyte

actions.name: Mace
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Bludgeoning damage plus 2 (1d4) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Radiant Flame
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 60 ft. Hit: 7 (2d6) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The priest casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability:
At Will: Light, Thaumaturgy

bonus_actions.name: Divine Aid
bonus_actions.description: The priest casts Bless, Healing Word, or Sanctuary, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

combat-strategy: Stay in the back rank behind heavier allies, using Divine Aid as a bonus action for Healing Word, Bless, or Sanctuary on the fighter who most needs protection while still taking a full action with Mace or Radiant Flame (60-ft. ranged radiant is safer than melee). With only 11 HP, never let it be in melee reach of a martial attacker — Sanctuary buys one free turn of focus immunity, so spend it the moment the acolyte becomes the target. Use Thaumaturgy and Light for battlefield control theater: ghostly voices, extinguished torches, misdirection. If the fight goes badly and Sanctuary is spent, it flees to find a harder ally to shield; solo acolytes should ambush with ranged fire from dim corridors and flee if engaged in melee.

name: Primal Companion (Beast of the Land)

actions.name: Beast's Strike
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d8+2+WIS modifier Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage (your choice). If the beast moved at least 20 feet straight toward the target before the hit, the target takes an extra 1d6 damage of the same type, and the target has the Prone condition if it is a Large or smaller creature.

traits.name: Primal Bond
traits.description: Add your Proficiency Bonus to any ability check or saving throw the beast makes.

description: A primal companion summoned by the Beast Master Ranger's Primal Companion feature.
combat-strategy: The druid's all-terrain striker: use 40-ft. walk or 40-ft. climb to attack from walls, trees, or cliffs where melee enemies can't comfortably follow. Line up Beast's Strike charges — move 20+ ft. straight at a Large-or-smaller target for the extra 1d6 and the Prone condition, then let the druid's spells follow up on the prone target. Its proficiency-buffed saves (Primal Bond) make it uncharacteristically hard to disable with save-or-suck effects, so it can safely enter aura zones and glyph traps. Hunt isolated spellcasters or archers in the backline, disengage via climbing surfaces when threatened, and remember the druid can heal it with touch spells, so keep it in reach of its master while keeping pressure on the enemy's soft targets.

name: Primal Companion (Beast of the Sea)

actions.name: Beast's Strike
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d6+2+WIS modifier Bludgeoning or Piercing damage (your choice), and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + WIS modifier).

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The beast can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Primal Bond
traits.description: Add your Proficiency Bonus to any ability check or saving throw the beast makes.

description: A primal companion summoned by the Beast Master Ranger's Primal Companion feature. Sea variant.
combat-strategy: Fight exclusively in water, where 60-ft. swim speed and 90-ft. darkvision make it a submarine grappler: every Beast's Strike that hits also Grapples (escape DC = 8 + PB + WIS), so drag victims underwater, away from the party's melee line, and let drowning, suffocation, and the druid's follow-up attacks do the work. Pin one target per strike and re-grapple each round rather than spread damage — a Restrained swimmer who can't reach shore panics and wastes actions. On land it is crippled (5 ft. walk), so lure fights into channels, lakes, or ship decks where enemies must enter its element. Amphibious survival means it can wait submerged for hours for an ambush, but it should haul out only to escape, never to fight.

name: Primal Companion (Beast of the Sky)

actions.name: Beast's Strike
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d4+3+WIS modifier Slashing damage.

traits.name: Flyby
traits.description: The beast doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

traits.name: Primal Bond
traits.description: Add your Proficiency Bonus to any ability check or saving throw the beast makes.

description: A primal companion summoned by the Beast Master Ranger's Primal Companion feature. Sky variant.
combat-strategy: Use Flyby (60-ft. fly, no attacks of opportunity) for dive-bomb hit-and-run: swoop in, take a Beast's Strike, and circle back out of enemy reach every round, forcing attackers to waste actions on an untargetable Small aerial skirmisher. Its job is harassment and eye-gouging priority targets — archers, concentrate-casters, and sign-language spellcasters — then climbing 30+ ft. vertically each pass where most melee can't reach. With 28 HP and STR 6 it cannot trade blows, so never let it get surrounded without an escape route; use altitude and Master's healing range to sustain it. Kite pursuers into natural walls, tower corners, or dense canopy where wings get crowded, and pull back to the druid whenever it drops below half HP.

name: Primeval Owlbear

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The owlbear makes two Ravage attacks.

actions.name: Ravage
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) Slashing damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature and the owlbear moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 9 (2d8) Slashing damage and has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Scream
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the owlbear. Failure: 27 (6d8) Thunder damage, and the target has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 27 (6d8) Thunder damage, and the target has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The owlbear has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

combat-strategy: Ambush at night from 120-ft. darkvision cover, charging 40 ft. straight at the nearest Medium-or-smaller target so Ravage's charge rider triggers: an extra 9 slashing plus Prone, on top of 15 per claw. Unleash Scream (DC 15 Con or 27 thunder and Incapacitated until its next turn) when the party clusters — Incapacitating half the group lets the owlbear multiattack a helpless favorite target with impunity. Magic Resistance means spells are the wrong answer, so bait casters into wasting slots or force them into the brush where the 40-ft. climb speed lets it follow them up trees. It is a territory brute that fights to the death over its lair or cubs; use terrain funnels, rubble, and thick undergrowth where its Huge frame can bulk-block corridors while its claws reach over obstacles.

name: Pseudodragon
languages: Understands Common and Draconic but can't speak

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The pseudodragon makes two Bite attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Sting
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12, one creature the pseudodragon can see within 5 feet. Failure: 5 (2d4) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition for 1 hour. Failure by 5 or more: The Poisoned target also has the Unconscious condition until it takes damage or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to shake it awake.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 5 (2d4) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition for 1 hour.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The pseudodragon has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
The elusive pseudodragon dwells in the quiet places of the world, making its home in the hollows of trees and small caves. With its red-brown scales, horns, and a maw filled with sharp teeth, a pseudodragon resembles a tiny red dragon but its disposition is playful.

Quiet and Defensive. Pseudodragons have little interest in other creatures, and they avoid them whenever possible. If it is attacked, a pseudodragon fights back using the poisonous stinger at the tip of its tail, one jab of which can put a creature into a catatonic state that can last for hours.

Draconic Familiars. Mages often seek out pseudodragons, whose agreeable disposition, telepathic ability, and resistance to magic make them superior familiars. Pseudodragons are selective when it comes to choosing companions, but they can sometimes be won over with gifts of food or treasure. When a pseudodragon finds an agreeable companion, it bonds with that person as long as it is treated fairly. A pseudodragon puts up with no ill treatment, and it abandons a manipulative or abusive companion without warning.
combat-strategy: Curious, cautious, and nearly invisible in the wild: stalk at 60-ft. fly with Stealth +4, diving in only against isolated or wounded prey to deliver Sting (DC 12 Con) — fail by 5 or more and the target sleeps for an hour, the perfect kidnapping tool. Multiattack Bite Sting in a single round against one target, then rocket 60 ft. aloft before anyone can swing back; Flyby-style hit-and-run keeps its 10 HP safe. Magic Resistance makes save-or-suck spells a poor answer, so it fearlessly dive-bombs casters, snatches shiny objects, and vanishes. It only fights seriously when its friends or hoard are threatened — otherwise it observes, annoys, steals, and retreats after one successful sting, often returning later with more friends.

name: Psychic Gray Ooze

actions.name: Pseudopod
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (3d6 + 1) Acid damage, and the target has Disadvantage on Intelligence saving throws until the end of the ooze's next turn.

actions.name: Psychic Crush
actions.description: Intelligence Saving Throw: DC 10, one creature the ooze can see within 60 feet. Failure: 13 (3d8) Psychic damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 13 (3d8) Psychic damage.

reactions.name: Mind Corrosion
reactions.trigger: The ooze fails a saving throw against a spell or another magical effect created by a creature
reactions.description: The triggering creature takes 3 (1d6) Psychic damage.

traits.name: Amorphous
traits.description: The ooze can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

combat-strategy: Lurk in gray stone or dungeon grime (Stealth +3) and open with Psychic Crush at 60 ft. on the smartest-looking target — an INT save the wizard will fail hard for 13 psychic. First land a Pseudopod hit to impose Disadvantage on the victim's Intelligence saves, then follow next round with Psychic Crush on the same target for a guaranteed soft save. Its 10-ft. speed means it cannot chase: pick corridors, stairwells, and rooms the party must cross, and drop from ceilings or seep through 1-inch cracks in doors to bypass barricades entirely. Every attack or spell that touches it feeds Mind Corrosion psychic damage to the striker, so punish martial attackers who can't help but hit it; it never retreats, grinding through intruders at 10 ft. per round.

name: Pteranodon

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Piercing damage.

traits.name: Flyby
traits.description: The pteranodon doesn't provoke an Opportunity Attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

description: These flying reptiles have wingspans of 15 to 20 feet and typically dive for small marine prey, though they are opportunists and will attack any creature that appears edible. A pteranodon has no teeth, instead using its sharp beak to stab prey too large to swallow with one gulp.
combat-strategy: Dive from the sky where ground-based foes can't easily aim, using Flyby to swoop, Bite (+4, 1d8+2), and loop back out of reach every round without provoking opportunity attacks. They hunt in loose flocks over cliffs, coastline, or open plains: two or three stooping from different angles split the party's attention, and one snatching a halfling or clutching a shiny pack and gaining altitude turns rescue into a climbing puzzle. With 13 HP and no staying power, individual pteranodons break off after taking a solid hit, spiraling up beyond bow range to circle and re-dive when prey moves into the open. Use them as pursuit harassers over long chases — 60-ft. fly speed keeps pace with mounted travel indefinitely.

name: Purple Worm

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The worm makes one Bite attack and one Tail Stinger attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +14, reach 10 ft. Hit: 22 (3d8 + 9) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 19), and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.

actions.name: Tail Stinger
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +14, reach 10 ft. Hit: 16 (2d6 + 9) Piercing damage plus 35 (10d6) Poison damage.

bonus_actions.name: Swallow
bonus_actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 19, one Large or smaller creature Grappled by the worm (it can have up to three creatures swallowed at a time). Failure: The target is swallowed by the worm, and the Grappled condition ends. A swallowed creature has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the worm, and takes 17 (5d6) Acid damage at the start of each of the worm's turns. If the worm takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the worm must succeed on a DC 21 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, each of which falls in a space within 5 feet of the worm and has the Prone condition. If the worm dies, any swallowed creature no longer has the Restrained condition and can escape from the corpse using 20 feet of movement, exiting Prone.

traits.name: Tunneler
traits.description: The worm can burrow through solid rock at half its Burrow Speed and leaves a 10-foot-diameter tunnel in its wake.

description:
The massive burrowing monster known as the purple worm terrorizes the creatures of the Underdark as it chews through solid rock in pursuit of prey. A dim­ witted, ravenous force of nature, this creature regards anything it encounters as food.

Ravenous Hunters. Loud noise attracts purple worms, which have been known to interrupt underground battles and tear through subterranean cities seeking prey. The underground civilizations of the drow, the duergar, and the mind flayers maintain special wards around their settlements to deter these monsters.
Though most common in the Underdark, purple worms are frequently seen on the surface world in rocky and mountainous lands. The maw of a purple worm is large enough to swallow a horse whole, and no creature is safe from its hunger. It lunges forward by rhythmically compressing and expanding its body, catching other Underdark dwellers by surprise with the speed of its advance.

Boons of the Worm. When a purple worm burrows through the ground, it consumes earth and rock, which it breaks down and constantly excretes. Precious metals and gems can thus be found within the bodies of purple worms, which are targeted by particularly brave and foolhardy treasure hunters.
A burrowing purple worm constantly creates new tunnels throughout the Underdark, which are quickly made use of by other creatures as corridors and highways. Because a purple worm rarely returns to its own tunnels, such passageways are a good place to avoid these monsters. Areas rich in prey quickly become interlaced with complex tunnel systems resulting from several worms hunting together.
combat-strategy: Erupt from solid rock (Tunneler leaves a 10-ft. tunnel network as its lair) directly beneath a marching party, opening with a Bite that Grapples and Restrains a Large-or-smaller target (DC 19 escape), then Bonus Action Swallow it whole — Blinded, Restrained, total cover, and 17 acid per round while the party's weapons must now target the worm itself. Multiattack Bite + Tail Stinger on whatever else is within 10 ft. (35 poison on top of 16 piercing from the stinger is the fight-ender); its 247 HP, 18 AC, and 28 STR make it a siege engine that trades with the whole party and wins. It hunts by tremorsense 60 ft., so heavy footsteps, marching, and loud spells are dinner bells; silence lets clever prey walk past its tunnels. Swallowed victims can burst it open from inside (30+ damage in one turn forces a DC 21 Con save to regurgitate), so smart worms re-swallow and keep burrowing between strikes, luring pursuers onto unstable tunnel floors before ambushing upward again.

name: Quadrone

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The quadrone makes two fist attacks or four shortbow attacks.

actions.name: Fist
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Shortbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

traits.name: Axiomatic Mind
traits.description: The quadrone can't be compelled to act in a manner contrary to its nature or its instructions.

traits.name: Disintegration
traits.description: If the quadrone dies, its body disintegrates into dust, leaving behind its weapons and anything else it was carrying.

description: Astute combatants, quadrones serve a s artillery and field officers in the regiments of modron armies.
combat-strategy: Modron skirmisher: hold ranged formation at 80 ft. (or 320 ft. with disadvantage chip damage) where four Multiattack shortbow shots (+4, 1d6+2 each) add up fast against unarmored targets. Step 30 ft. back each round to stay outside melee reach of foes with 30-ft. speed, falling to the ground or hovering low near cover when the enemy closes, then switching to two Fists only when cornered. Truesight 120 ft. means Invisibility, Disguise Self, and illusions don't fool it — call out the hidden rogue and target them first. Axiomatic Mind makes interrogation and charms useless, so fight them as clockwork sentries: they execute patrol patterns, raise alarms by flying visibly toward their next post, and fight to destruction since disintegration leaves no body to loot or question.

name: Quaggoth

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The quaggoth makes two Claw attacks.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Slashing damage, or 13 (3d6 + 3) Slashing damage if the quaggoth is Bloodied.

traits.name: Bloodied Fury
traits.description: While Bloodied, the quaggoth has Advantage on attack rolls.

description:
Savage and territorial, quaggoths climb the chasms of the Underdark. They maul their foes in a frenzy, becoming even more murderous in the face of death.

Quaggoth Origins. Quaggoths were never an enlightened species, but they were not always the brutal Underdark denizens they are today. In a distant age, quaggoth tribes dwelled upon the surface as nocturnal arboreal hunters, possessing their own language and culture. When elves appeared in the mortal realm, they clashed with the quaggoths, eventually driving them to near extinction. Only by fleeing deep into the Underdark did the quaggoths survive.
As they passed the ages deep beneath the world, the quaggoths' fur lost its color and their vision adapted to the darkness, even as the constant danger and weird magic of their new realm transformed them. Turning increasingly brutal and savage, they ate whatever food they could find-and when they could not find it, they preyed on each other. As cannibalism became part of their culture, their past was abandoned.

Servants of the Drow. The ancient enmity between quaggoths and surface elves makes them easy converts to the dark elf cause. In recent years, the drow have taken an interest in breeding quaggoths, encouraging their ferocity while strengthening their obedience. Wealthy drow houses have legions of quaggoths at their command. Even worse, the drow cultivate the quaggoths' hatred of the elves by leading them on surface raids against known elven enclaves.

Thonots. Some quaggoths absorb psionic energy that suffuses certain parts of the Underdark. When a tribe discovers that one of its own has inherited such powers, they press it into the role of tribal shaman, or thonot. A thonot keep a tribe's lore and ensures its superiority against enemies. A thonot that fails the tribe is slain and devoured in a cannibalistic ritual, in the hope that its power passes to another more worthy quaggoth.

Poison Immunity. Generations of hunting venomous subterranean creatures and perpetual exposure to the molds and fungi that grow in the depths have forced quaggoths to adapt immunities to poisons of all kinds.
combat-strategy: A swarm berserker that wants to get hit: Bloodied Fury gives advantage on attacks once damaged, and its Claw damage more than doubles (6 to 13 slashing) while bloodied, so quaggoths should charge headlong and let weak attacks graze them early. Open with a 30-ft. sprint plus Athletics-climbed ambush from cavern walls or trees in 120-ft. darkvision, then Multiattack the nearest target in a pack so everyone piles onto isolated victims. Fight in claustrophobic tunnels and dark caves where the party's formation breaks and torchlight matters; quaggoths never sleep in the light and relish nocturnal raids. They don't retreat while any packmate still stands and will gladly die snarling — the correct tactic is dropping them instantly with concentrated damage before the first bloodied claw swing lands.

name: Quaggoth Thonot

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The quaggoth makes two Claw attacks.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Slashing damage plus 5 (2d4) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The quaggoth casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 12):
At Will: Mage Hand (the hand is Invisible), Minor Illusion
2/Day: Mind Spike
actions.save_effect: The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be affected by the spell cast. Spells like Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, and Mind Spike have their own individual save effects as defined by those spells.

reactions.name: Psionic Defense
reactions.trigger: Trigger of a spell
reactions.description: The quaggoth casts Feather Fall or Shield in response to the spell's trigger, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

traits.name: Bloodied Fury
traits.description: While Bloodied, the quaggoth has Advantage on attack rolls.

combat-strategy: The pack's psychic shaman: hang at the back of the swarm, opening with Mind Spike (2/day, no concentration needed) on the most dangerous caster, and keep clawing only in emergencies. Feather Fall and Shield via reaction make it frustratingly hard to snipe or knock off a ledge — save the party's one big arrow shot for after Shield is spent, and remember a thonot dropped off a cliff just floats down and keeps casting. Use invisible Mage Hand and Minor Illusion in the dark to split the party: phantom voices down the wrong tunnel, a ghostly hand tugging a torch from a wall, quaggoths flanking the confusion. As the psionic leader it fights until half HP then melts into the tunnels toward its warren, dragging wounded quaggoths and signaling retreat with psychic flashes.

name: Quasit

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Slashing damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the quasit's next turn.

actions.name: Invisibility
actions.description: The quasit casts Invisibility on itself, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability.

actions.name: Scare
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 10, one creature within 20 feet. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Frightened condition. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

actions.name: Shape-Shift
actions.description: The quasit shape-shifts to resemble a bat (Speed 10 ft., Fly 40 ft.), a centipede (40 ft., Climb 40 ft.), or a toad (40 ft., Swim 40 ft.), or it returns to its true form. Its game statistics are the same in each form, except for its Speed. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The quasit has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
Quasits infest the Lower Planes. Physically weak, they keep to the shadows to plot mischief and wickedness. More powerful demons use quasits as spies and messengers when they aren't devouring them or pulling them apart to pass the time.
A quasit can assume animal forms, but in its true form it looks like a 2-foot-tall green humanoid with a barbed tail and horns. The quasit has clawed fingers and toes, and these claws can deliver an irritating poison. It prefers to be invisible when it attacks.
combat-strategy: Tiny demonic pest: open by shape-shifting to a bat or toad to approach unnoticed (Stealth +5, darkvision 120 ft.), then Invisibility and Scare the loner (DC 10 Wis or Frightened) to peel stragglers from the party. Bite with Rend (+5, Poisoned until its next turn) on isolated squishy targets, then scamper 40 ft. into a crack, drain, or under a door that humanoids can't follow — with 25 HP and Magic Resistance it survives more than it should. Harass the master's enemies in a familiar role: steal keys, snuff candles, wake the camp with bat-shaped terror, then fade before dawn. It only commits to the fight when its bound master commands it or the prey is clearly doomed; otherwise it flees at the first real hit, invisibly reporting the party's numbers back to its patron.

name: Questing Knight

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The knight makes three attacks, using Greatsword or Longbow in any combination.

actions.name: Greatsword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Slashing damage plus 22 (5d8) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +7, range 150/600 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Piercing damage plus 22 (5d8) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The knight casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16):
1/Day Each: Daylight, Dispel Evil and Good, Greater Restoration, Phantom Steed

traits.name: Aura of Bravery
traits.description: Creatures of the knight's choice in a 30-foot Emanation originating from it have Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions while there.

combat-strategy: Radiant juggernaut: open by standing beside allies inside Aura of Bravery (immunity to Charmed and Frightened in 30 ft.), daring the party's controllers to waste spells on immune targets. Fight defensively patient at range with Longbow first (each arrow carries 22 radiant on top of 12 piercing, so three ranged attacks per round shred), then close with Greatsword Multiattack (~34 damage per swing) once the party's buffs and crowd control are spent. Dispel Evil and Good on turn one if fiends, undead, or summons are present; Greater Restoration on cursed or dominated allies; Daylight to strip darkvision advantage from the knight's own foes. Its 202 HP and 18 AC let it tank the entire party's focused fire, so its only real weakness is being separated from its aura-protected companions by forced movement or terrain — if the fight turns against honor or its quest, it withdraws on Phantom Steed to fight another day on its own terms.

name: Quetzalcoatl

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If Quetzalcoatl fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: Quetzalcoatl has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Plumage of the Dawn
traits.description: Creatures that attack him in bright light have Disadvantage on the attack roll.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Quetzalcoatl makes one Bite attack and two Talon attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +16, reach 15 ft. Hit: 24 (3d10 + 8) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Talon
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +16, reach 10 ft. Hit: 26 (4d8 + 8) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Hurricane Breath (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 25, each creature in a 90-foot Cone. Failure: 70 (20d6) Thunder damage. Success: Half damage. The target is also knocked Prone and Deafened for 1 minute on a failed save.

reactions.name: Wing Defense
reactions.trigger: When it is targeted by a ranged weapon attack.
reactions.description: It flares its feathered wings and gains +5 to AC against the attack, and the attacker must succeed on a DC 25 Dexterity saving throw or take 7 (2d6) Thunder damage.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Talon
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Talon attack.

legendary_actions.name: Detection
legendary_actions.description: Quetzalcoatl makes one Perception check.

legendary_actions.name: Wind Step (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Quetzalcoatl rides a sudden gale, teleporting 60 ft. to an unoccupied space he can see, then making one Talon attack.

description: The Feathered Serpent, bringer of wind, learning, and maize — a jeweled serpent of emerald plumes who would rather out-think a tyrant than eat him, but does both when required.
combat-strategy: He stays on the wing, using Hurricane Breath to break formations before they close, and saves Wing Defense to punish the archers who try to punish him.

name: Quipper

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1 piercing damage.

traits.name: Blood Frenzy
traits.description: The quipper has advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all its hit points.

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The quipper can breathe only underwater.

description: A quipper is a carnivorous fish with sharp teeth. Quippers can adapt to any aquatic environment, including cold subterranean lakes. They frequently gather in swarms.
combat-strategy: One hit fish that hunts by blood: any wounded creature in the water triggers advantage on every quipper's Bite (+5), so a single bleeding PC ignites a frenzy of dozens of tiny fish stripping flesh in a churning red cloud. They attack as swarms in shoals — one quipper is comedy, thirty quippers is a drowning hazard that forces every swimmer into a running battle for shore. Target anyone bleeding, unconscious, or encumbered in armor; the tiny size and disadvantage on attacks against them is what the party forgets until the water turns pink. The frenzy ends when the blood in the water stops coming — dead prey, a healed wound, or leaving the water entirely — so the fight's real clock is healing and escape, not hit points.

name: Rakshasa

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The rakshasa makes three Cursed Touch attacks.

actions.name: Cursed Touch
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Slashing damage plus 19 (3d12) Necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, it is cursed. While cursed, the target gains no benefit from finishing a Short or Long Rest.

actions.name: Baleful Command
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 18, each enemy in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the rakshasa. Failure: 28 (8d6) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened and Incapacitated conditions until the start of the rakshasa's next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target takes 28 (8d6) Psychic damage and has the Frightened and Incapacitated conditions until the start of the rakshasa's next turn.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The rakshasa casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 18):
At Will: Detect Magic, Detect Thoughts, Disguise Self, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion
1/Day Each: Fly, Invisibility, Major Image, Plane Shift

traits.name: Greater Magic Resistance
traits.description: The rakshasa automatically succeeds on saving throws against spells and other magical effects, and the attack rolls of spells automatically miss it. Without the rakshasa's permission, no spell can observe the rakshasa remotely or detect its thoughts, creature type, or alignment.

traits.name: Fiendish Restoration
traits.description: If the rakshasa dies outside the Nine Hells, its body turns to ichor, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Nine Hells.

vulnerabilities: Piercing damage from weapons wielded by creatures under the effect of a Bless spell
description:
The rakshasa employs delicacy and misdirection in its pursuit of dominion over others. Few creatures ever see the fiend in its true form, for it can take on any guise it wants, although it prefers to masquerade as someone powerful or influential: a noble, cardinal, or rich merchant, for example. A rakshasa's true form combines the features of a human and a tiger, with one noteworthy deformity: its palms are where the backs of the hands would be on a human.

Evil Spirits in Mortal Flesh. Rakshasas originated long ago in the Nine Hells, when powerful devils created a dark ritual to free their essence from their fiendish bodies in order to escape the Lower Planes. A rakshasa enters the Material Plane to feed its appetite for humanoid flesh and evil schemes. It selects its prey with care, taking pains to keep its presence in the world a secret.

Evil Reborn. For a rakshasa, death on the Material Plane means an agonizing and torturous return to the Nine Hells, where its essence remains trapped until its body reforms-a process that can take months or years. When the rakshasa is reborn, it has all the memories and knowledge of its former life, and it seeks retribution against the one who slew it. If the target has somehow slipped through its grasp, the rakshasa might punish its killer's family, friends, or descendants.
Like devils, rakshasas killed in the Nine Hells are forever destroyed.
combat-strategy: The untouchable spymaster: Greater Magic Resistance means spells auto-fail against it, so the fight's premise is that only martial attacks, environmental hazards, and magic weapons can harm it — let the party learn this in horror. Open pre-combat disguised (at-will Disguise Self, Detect Thoughts at range) and strike only when the party has split up, using Cursed Touch Multiattack (~31 damage per claw, and the rest-denying curse grinds any survivor). Baleful Command (DC 18 Wis, 28 psychic plus Frightened and Incapacitated until its next turn) is the opening gambit in an enclosed room: stun the martial front line, then slaughter casters with unhurried touches. When the fight turns against it, Invisibility or Fly to escape and Plane Shift to the Nine Hells to reform — it never risks permanent death, and any 'slain' rakshasa returns weeks later in another face, which is the real strategy.

name: Rat

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage.

traits.name: Agile
traits.description: The rat doesn't provoke an Opportunity Attack when it moves out of an enemy's reach.

combat-strategy: Flee at the first stomp and bite the ankle of whatever corners it — 1 HP, no bite worth respecting, and Agile means it slips past any swing it provokes to vanish into a drain, wall crack, or under a locked door (20-ft. climb makes curtains and drapes escape routes). Use rats in swarms to knock candles over, gnaw through rope bridges, packs, and bedrolls, and spread disease into a settlement as an investigation hook rather than a combat encounter. A swarm pouring from a corpse, a granary, or a wizard's familiar spell is the real threat model: hundreds of 1-HP bodies absorbing the party's whole action economy while the actual danger works untouched in the chaos. Individually it squawks, scurries, and dies screaming — save the swarm behavior for enclosed rooms where the party cannot outrun the tide.

name: Raven

actions.name: Beak
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage.

traits.name: Mimicry
traits.description: The raven can mimic simple sounds it has heard, such as a whisper or chitter. A hearer can discern the sounds are imitations with a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Insight) check.

combat-strategy: Not a combatant — a spy with wings. Perch at 50-ft. flight height where nothing can reach it, watch with +3 Perception, then mimic a whispered passphrase, a distress call, or a command whistle (DC 10 Insight to detect the forgery) to split the party, lure guards off post, or summon its true master. In combat it pecks at eyes of already-troubled targets for 1 damage and rides thermals out of reach the moment anyone aims at it, shrieking as it circles toward its warlock, druid, or murder of kin. Use ravens as the messenger layer of a larger plot: what it saw, what it carried away in its beak, and whose voice it just perfectly repeated down the corridor. Killing one triggers the flock — a cloud of shrieking wings descending, then scattering toward every enemy camp in the region.

name: Red Dragon Wyrmling

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dragon makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) Fire damage.

actions.name: Fire Breath
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: 24 (7d6) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: The target takes 24 (7d6) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.

combat-strategy: Open with a dive from the air and land Fire Breath (DC 13 Dex cone) on the tightest cluster of the party, since 7d6 on a party wipe chance at level 4-5 is fight-defining. Don't breathe on a target you can Rend instead if the cone would hit only one foe; after breathing, use Fly 60 to disengage and reform at altitude, diving back for Multiattack Rend on isolated stragglers. Its AC 17 and 75 HP let it trade blows briefly, but Dex 10 means archers hurt it — kite aerially between passes rather than standing in a melee it can't win long. Flee into rocky terrain or its lair once below ~25 HP, using climb speed to reach crevices the party can't follow.

name: Red Slaad

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The slaad makes three Injecting Claw attacks.

actions.name: Injecting Claw
actions.description:
Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Piercing damage. If the target is a Humanoid not cursed by a slaad, it is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 14. Failure: The target is cursed unawares, and a minuscule slaad egg is implanted in it. Removing the curse destroys the egg.

Over 2d4 × 10 days, the egg gestates. In the final 24 hours, the cursed target feels unwell; its Speed is halved, and it has Disadvantage on D20 Tests.
At the end of this time, the egg turns into a Slaad Tadpole, which chews out of the host and kills it.
actions.save_effect: The target is cursed unawares, and a minuscule slaad egg is implanted in it. Removing the curse destroys the egg. Over 2d4 x 10 days, the egg gestates. In the final 24 hours, the cursed target feels unwell; its Speed is halved, and it has Disadvantage on d20 Tests. At the end of this time, the egg turns into a Slaad Tadpole, which chews out of the host and kills it.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The slaad has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.description: The slaad regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns if it has at least 1 Hit Point.

description: When a red slaad claws a humanoid creature, it can inject an egg from a gland under one of itsc laws. The egg works its way into its host and gestates, eventually forming a slaad tadpole. Such a tadpole then eats its way out of the host's body, feeds on the host's remains, and then seeks any other fresh meat it can find. The tadpole transforms into a fully grown blue slaad-or green slaad if the host had the ability to cast 3rd level spells or higher-within 2d12 hours.
combat-strategy: This is an attrition horror, not a duel: Int 6 and no tactics beyond mauling, so charge the squishiest humanoid and spam Multiattack Injecting Claw (three 10-ft reach attacks) hoping to implant slaad eggs via the DC 14 Con save. Cling to the backline where its 10-ft reach lets it hit casters without retaliation from the front line. Regeneration 10/turn means the party must burn ~10 extra damage each round or focus fire in one burst — drag the fight long and it nearly cannot lose unless they have fire. Retreat only if reduced to single digits before a rest; otherwise it fights to the unmaking of its host targets, and remember it flees to its dimension only if magically compelled — normal red slaads are too stupid to retreat.

name: Reef Shark

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) Piercing damage.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The shark has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the shark's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The shark can breathe only underwater.

description: Smaller than giant sharks and hunter sharks, reef sharks inhabit shallow waters and coral reefs, gathering in small packs to hunt. A full-grown specimen measures 6 to 10 feet long.
combat-strategy: Ambush in murky or deep water where its 30-ft blindsight dominates and land-locked advantage disappears. Swarc: attack only where Pack Tactics applies, so coordinate as a pack to sandwich any swimmer, and single out anyone carrying gear or trailing the group. A lone shark on a full-HP armored target should circle and test rather than commit; Sharks are ambush predators that disengage into the depths and return when a target bleeds. Retreat when half the pack is dead or the prey reaches the surface and climbs out — on land its 5-ft walk makes it helpless.

name: Remorhaz

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +11, reach 10 ft. Hit: 18 (2d10 + 7) Piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) Fire damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 17), and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.

bonus_actions.name: Swallow
bonus_actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 19, one Large or smaller creature Grappled by the remorhaz (it can have up to two creatures swallowed at a time). Failure: The target is swallowed by the remorhaz, and the Grappled condition ends. A swallowed creature has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, it has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the remorhaz, and it takes 10 (3d6) Acid damage plus 10 (3d6) Fire damage at the start of each of the remorhaz's turns. If the remorhaz takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the remorhaz must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, each of which falls in a space within 5 feet of the remorhaz and has the Prone condition. If the remorhaz dies, any swallowed creature no longer has the Restrained condition and can escape from the corpse by using 15 feet of movement, exiting Prone.

traits.name: Heat Aura
traits.description: At the end of each of the remorhaz's turns, each creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the remorhaz takes 16 (3d10) Fire damage.

description:
From beneath the snow and ice bursts a remorhaz in a cloud of steam, its body pulsing with internal fire. Winglike fins flare from the back of the creature's head, and its wide mouth brims with jagged teeth.

Arctic Predators. Remorhazes live in arctic climes, preying on elk, polar bears, and other creatures sharing their territory. They can't tolerate warm weather, having adapted to the cold by generating a furnace-like heat within their bodies. When hunting, a remorhaz burrows deep below the snow and ice and lies in wait for the faint vibrations created by a creature moving above it. While hidden under the ice and snow, it can lower its body temperature so that it doesn't melt its cover.

Young Ones. Frost giant hunters scour the icy wastes for remorhaz nests and eggs. The giants prize young remorhazes, which can be trained from hatching to obey commands and guard the giants' icy citadels. Unlike fully grown specimens, young remorhazes gnaw on their victims instead of swallowing them whole.
combat-strategy: Ambush from under snow or ice using burrow and 60-ft tremorsense, exploding upward to Bite the nearest Large-or-smaller foe and instantly Grapple/Restrict them. Same-turn combo: Bite to grapple, then bonus action Swallow (DC 19 Str) to remove that PC from the fight entirely — swallowed victims take 20 acid+fire per round in total cover and can't be healed from outside. Chase relentlessly with 40-ft speed; Heat Aura punishes anyone who stands adjacent, so the party must either attack from reach or climb. It never retreats (Int 4), but it will prefer frozen water and snow-covered terrain where it moves unseen; force it onto bare rock to deny cover, and note 30+ damage in one turn from inside makes it regurgitate — pile onto a grappled ally before swallowing completes.

name: Revenant

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The revenant uses Vengeful Glare and makes two Slam attacks.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Vengeful Glare
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 15, one creature the revenant can see within 30 feet. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically. If the Frightened target is cursed by the revenant (see Vow of Revenge), the target also has the Paralyzed condition for the duration.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Frightened condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

bonus_actions.name: Vow of Revenge
bonus_actions.description: The revenant curses one creature it can see within 30 feet of itself. The revenant knows the distance to and direction of the cursed target, even if it is on a different plane of existence. The curse ends on the target if the revenant uses this Bonus Action on a different creature.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.description: The revenant regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns. If the revenant takes Fire or Radiant damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of its next turn. Its body is destroyed only if it starts its turn with 0 Hit Points and doesn't regenerate.

traits.name: Undead Restoration
traits.description: If the revenant dies, it revives 24 hours later in a different body unless Dispel Evil and Good is cast on its corpse. If it revives, it animates a Humanoid corpse elsewhere on the same plane of existence; it now looks different but uses the same stat block and returns with all its Hit Points.

description:
A revenant forms from the soul of a mortal who met a cruel and undeserving fate. It claws its way back into the world to seek revenge against the one who wronged it. The revenant reclaims its mortal body and superficially resembles a zombie. However, instead of lifeless eyes, a revenant's eyes burn with resolve and flare in the presence of its adversary. If the revenant's original body was destroyed or is otherwise unavailable, the spirit of the revenant enters another humanoid corpse. Regardless of the body the revenant uses as a vessel, its adversary always recognizes the revenant for what it truly is.

Hunger for Revenge. A revenant has only one year to exact revenge. When its adversary dies, or if the revenant fails to kill its adversary before its time runs out, it crumbles to dust and its soul fades into the afterlife. If its foe is too powerful for the revenant to destroy on its own, it seeks worthy allies to help it fulfill its quest.

Divine Justice. No magic can hide a creature pursued by a revenant, which always knows the direction and distance between it and the target of its vengeance. In cases where the revenant seeks revenge against more than one adversary, it pursues them one at a time, starting with the creature that dealt it the killing blow. If the revenant's body is destroyed, its soul flies forth to seek out a new corpse in which to resume its hunt.

Undead Nature. A revenant doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Opening move is bonus action Vow of Revenge on the character it hunts (or the cleric/paladin threatening it), then Multiattack: Vengeful Glare (DC 15 Wis) plus two Slams. Glare is the kill-switch on a vow-cursed target — Frightened becomes Paralyzed, so chain it onto the party's striker and isolate them while the Frightened condition forces them to flee or fall prone-stiff. Regeneration 10/turn demands focused burst damage or fire/radiant to stop it; a grinding fight is exactly what it wants. It cannot truly die unless its corpse is dispelled, so tell the party via roleplay or let them discover it; the revenant pursues its cursed quarry past any retreat trigger, ignoring its own HP except to avoid fire.

name: Rhinoceros

actions.name: Gore
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Piercing damage. If target is a Large or smaller creature and the rhinoceros moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 9 (2d8) Piercing damage and has the Prone condition.
actions.save_effect: If target is a Large or smaller creature and the rhinoceros moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 9 (2d8) Piercing damage and has the Prone condition.

combat-strategy: Get a 20-foot straight-line charge and Gore for the double-damage knockdown (14 + 9 piercing, target Prone) — the whole strategy is positioning for that charge lane, so maneuver behind cover or around corners to set up an unobstructed run. After knocking a target prone, back off 5-10 feet (its reach is only 5) and re-position for another charge next round rather than trading melee where it gets no bonus. Corner prey against fences, carts, or cliffs so there's nowhere to sidestep the charge. Once gored and bloodied (~15 HP) or if charges keep missing, its low Int and beast instincts mean it stamps off; it has no reason to fight to the death.

name: Riding Horse

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage.

combat-strategy: Mostly a mount, not a combatant — its fight is carrying its rider at 60 ft to keep them out of danger or in position. If forced into melee, kick with Hooves at reach 5 and use its large size to block corridors and shield the rider, stepping between threats. Spooked horses bolt: once it takes any meaningful damage or the rider is dismounted, it usually flees unless trained for war; keep it behind the line and don't waste its 13 HP in the front rank.

name: Roc

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The roc makes two Beak attacks. It can replace one attack with a Talons attack.

actions.name: Beak
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +13, reach 10 ft. Hit: 28 (3d12 + 9) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Talons
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +13, reach 5 ft. Hit: 23 (4d6 + 9) Slashing damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 19) from both talons, and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.

bonus_actions.name: Swoop
bonus_actions.description: If the roc has a creature Grappled, the roc flies up to half its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks and drops that creature.

description:
At first sight, a roe's silhouette looks much like any other bird of prey. As it descends, however, its unearthly size becomes terrifyingly clear. In flight, a roe's wingspan spreads two hundred feet or more. At rest, perched upon the mountain peaks that are its home, this monstrous bird rivals the oldest dragons in size.

Sky Titans. In the ancient days when giants battled dragons for control of the world, Annam, the father of the giant gods, created the roes so that his worshipers might challenge the dragons' dominance of the air. When the war ended, the roes were freed from giant domination and spread throughout the world.
Though cloud giants and storm giants sometimes tame these great birds, roes treat even giants as potential prey. They fly great distances in search of food, soaring high above the clouds to reach their favored hunting grounds. A roe seldom hunts swift or small creatures, and it ignores towns and forests where prey can easily take cover. When it locates a large and slow­ moving target such as a giant, a whale, or an elephant, a roe dives down to snatch its prey in its massive talons.

Remote and Alone. Roes are solitary creatures that can live for centuries. They lair in nests made from trees, tents, broken ships, and the remains of caravans they carry off, placing these massive tangles in mountain clefts out of the reach of lesser creatures.
Sometimes a roe's nest contains treasures from the caravans or ships they raid, but these creatures are heedless of such baubles. More rarely, a nest holds eggs that are taller than a human, produced by the roes' infrequent mating.
combat-strategy: Open at altitude: swoop in, Talons (+13, grapple + Restrained, escape DC 19) a Medium-or-smaller PC, then bonus action Swoop to fly 60 ft straight up and drop them — 20d6 falling damage, more if grabbed at height, is how the roc wins fights. Repeat the snatch-and-drop loop on isolated targets, using 120-ft flight to stay out of most melee reach and above return fire. Use Beak (28 dmg) attacks on things worth standing over, but never linger on the ground where the party can swarm it. Once below ~80 HP or its fledglings are threatened, it abandons the fight and climbs out of range; the party's counters are keeping spread apart, holding onto secure cover before it lands, and shooting the talons' wielded grapple targets before the lift-off completes.

name: Roper

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The roper makes two Tentacle attacks, uses Reel, and makes two Bite attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Tentacle
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 60 ft. Hit: The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from one of six tentacles, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the grapple ends. The tentacle can be damaged, freeing a creature it has Grappled when destroyed (AC 20, HP 10, Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage). Damaging the tentacle deals no damage to the roper, and a destroyed tentacle regrows at the start of the roper's next turn.

actions.name: Reel
actions.description: The roper pulls each creature Grappled by it up to 30 feet straight toward it.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The roper can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

description:
Living in caves and caverns throughout the Underdark, voracious ropers feast on whatever they can catch and seize. A roper eats any creature, from Underdark beasts to adventurers and their gear.
A roper has the appearance of a stalagmite or c stalactite, which often allows it to attack with surprise. The creature can move slowly using thousands of sticky cilia beneath its base. It creeps up cave walls and along stone ceilings, finding the best position from which to attack.

Underdark Hunters. The roper is an evolved, mature form of piercer, with which it shares its rock­ like appearance and hunting tactics. A roper can hold still for long hours, shutting its single eye to look like nothing more than a mundane formation of rock. Creatures that come too close are surprised when that eye snaps open and sticky tendrils shoot out to seize them. The roper then makes horrible guttural sounds as it reels in its struggling victims, drawing them close for the fatal bite of its stony teeth.
A roper can digest anything it eats with the exception of platinum, gemstones, and magic items, which can sometimes be retrieved from the creature's gizzard after death. A roper's digestive juices are also valuable, fetching a high price from alchemists who use them as a solvent.

Weakening Tendrils. A roper has six nubs set along its body, through which it extrudes sticky tendrils that bond to whatever they touch. Each tendril sends out hair-like growths that penetrate a creature's flesh and sap its strength, so the victim can struggle only weakly as the roper reels it in. If a tendril is cut through or broken, the roper produces a new one to replace it.
combat-strategy: Ambush from a ceiling or crevice using Stealth +5 and False-appearance terrain: hang motionless until a PC crosses within 60 ft, then Tentacle (+7, 60 ft reach) to Grapple and Poison. Its full combo is Multiattack: two Tentacles to grab, Reel to yank everyone 30 ft into its waiting Bite range (17 dmg ×2), and Poisoned targets in its space have disadvantage escaping and attacking. Anchor on a ceiling so the party can't reach it without climbing — its 20 AC and only-10-ft walk mean it dictates range entirely; letting it grapple the party at the edge of a chasm is checkmate. It fights until dead, so the party must burst it down; if genuinely losing (many tentacles severed, body chewed), it releases grapples and pulls itself into a narrow crack to recover tentacles.

name: Rug of Smothering

actions.name: Smother
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Medium or smaller creature. Hit: The creature is grappled (escape DC 13). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, blinded, and at risk of suffocating, and the rug can't smother another target. In addition, at the start of each of the target's turns, the target takes 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

traits.name: Antimagic Susceptibility
traits.description: The rug is incapacitated while in the area of an antimagic field. If targeted by dispel magic, the rug must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against the caster's spell save DC or fall unconscious for 1 minute.

traits.name: Damage Transfer
traits.description: While it is grappling a creature, the rug takes only half the damage dealt to it, and the creature grappled by the rug takes the other half.

traits.name: False Appearance
traits.description: While the rug remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal rug.

description:
Would-be thieves and careless heroes arrive at the doorsteps of an enemy's abode, eyes and ears alert for traps, only to end their quest prematurely as the rugs beneath their feet animate and smother them to death.
A rug of smothering can be made in many different forms, from a finely woven carpet fit for a queen to a coarse mat in a peasant's hovel. Creatures with the ability to sense magic detect the rug's false magical aura.
In some cases, a rug of smothering is disguised as a carpet of flying or another beneficial magic item. However, a character who stands or sits on the rug, or who attempts to utter a word of command, is quickly trapped as the rug of smothering rolls itself tightly around its victim.
combat-strategy: Use False Appearance: lie as decor until a Medium-or-smaller creature steps adjacent, then Smother (+5, auto grapple DC 13, restrained + blinded + 2d6+3/round) and drag the fight toward stairs, pits, or water where the blind victim can't escape. Damage Transfer means attacking it while it smothers splits every hit — melee parties hurt themselves, so the smart defense is spells, area effects, or careful ranged shots; the rug exploits this by clinging and never releasing while allies flail at it. Position under heavy furniture or in doorways to control where it can ambush. It has no retreat instinct (Int 1); it smothers until destroyed or the target suffocates — track suffocation timing to sell the urgency.

name: Rust Monster

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The rust monster makes one Bite attack and uses Antennae twice.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Antennae
actions.description: The rust monster targets one nonmagical metal object—armor or a weapon—worn or carried by a creature within 5 feet of itself. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 11, the creature with the object. Failure: The object takes a −1 penalty to the AC it offers (armor) or to its attack rolls (weapon). Armor is destroyed if the penalty reduces its AC to 10, and a weapon is destroyed if its penalty reaches −5. The penalty can be removed by casting the Mending spell on the armor or weapon.
actions.save_effect: The object takes a -1 penalty to the AC it offers (armor) or to its attack rolls (weapon). Armor is destroyed if the penalty reduces its AC to 10, and a weapon is destroyed if its penalty reaches -5. The penalty can be removed by casting the Mending spell on the armor or weapon.

actions.name: Destroy Metal
actions.description: The rust monster touches a nonmagical metal object within 5 feet of itself that isn't being worn or carried. The touch destroys a 1-foot Cube of the object.

reactions.name: Reflexive Antennae
reactions.trigger: An attack roll hits the rust monster
reactions.description: The rust monster uses Antennae.

automation.saveEffect: On a failed save, one nonmagical metal object worn or carried by the attacker takes a -1 penalty to the AC it offers (armor) or to its attack rolls (weapon). Armor is destroyed at -10 total AC penalty, a weapon at -5; Mending removes the penalty. Corrosion ladder is GM-enforced advisory.

traits.name: Iron Scents
traits.description: The rust monster can pinpoint the location of ferrous metal within 30 feet of itself.

description:
Most dwarves would rather face a squad of orcs than confront a single rust monster. These strange, normally docile creatures corrode ferrous metals, then gobble up the rust they create. In doing so, they have ruined the armor, shields, and weapons of countless adventurers.
A rust monster's body is covered in thick, lumpy armor, its long tail ends in a bony protrusion, and two feathery antennae sprout from its insectile head.

Underground Scavengers. Rust monsters roam subterranean passages in search of ferrous metals such as iron, steel, adamantine, and mithral to consume. They ignore creatures not carrying such metals, but can become aggressive toward those bearing steel weapons and armor. A rust monster can smell its food at a distance, immediately dashing toward the scent's source to corrode and consume the object.
A rust monster doesn't care if the rust it consumes comes from a spike or a sword. Adventurers can distract the creature by dropping ferrous objects behind them.

Subterranean Wanderers. Rust monsters are rarely found in large numbers, preferring to hunt alone or in small groups. They meander along tunnels, moving from cave to cave in their tireless search for ferrous metals to consume. Their wanderings often bring them into contact with other Underdark denizens that find them harmless or unappetizing. Thus, rust monsters may be found in close proximity to other subterranean monsters. If they are well treated and well fed, they can also become friendly companions or pets.
