combat-strategy: Zero threat to bodies, total threat to gear: charge (40 ft) the most heavily armored or ferrous-metal-wielding PC, lured in by Iron Scents, and Multiattack with two Antennae uses to rack up −1 penalties toward weapon/armor destruction (armor dies at −4/AC 10, weapons at −5). Reflexive Antennae punishes anyone who swings at it or closes the door, so the party's own melee attackers feed its economy of metal-eating. Bite only as filler; its real game is two saves per round (DC 11 Dex) against equipment. Retreat the moment metal runs out or it takes real damage — it has no loyalty to a fight once it's fed, and clever parties throw iron pots or use non-magical misdirection to redirect it.

name: Saber-Toothed Tiger

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The tiger makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Slashing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Nimble Escape
bonus_actions.description: The tiger takes the Disengage or Hide action.

traits.name: Running Leap
traits.description: With a 10-foot running start, the tiger can Long Jump up to 25 feet.

combat-strategy: Ambush predator: Hide (Stealth +7) in grass or undergrowth, then explode out with a Running Leap (25 ft) onto the trailing or isolated victim for full Multiattack Rend (22 dmg average) and Knockback-free alpha-strike damage. Dex 17 and Nimble Escape let it Disengage or Hide as a bonus action after each pass — hit, bounce away 40 ft, vanish, repeat; it should almost never be in melee at the end of its turn. Target the squishiest backliner it can reach past the frontline, exploiting the element of fear to split the party's formation. It flees once bloodied (below ~25 HP) or if the first ambush fails and the party stands in a tight, ready phalanx — commit only to easy prey.

name: Sahuagin

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The sahuagin makes two melee attacks: one with its bite and one with its claws or spear.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.

actions.name: Claws
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) slashing damage.

actions.name: Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, or 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack.

traits.name: Blood Frenzy
traits.description: The sahuagin has advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all its hit points.

traits.name: Limited Amphibiousness
traits.description: The sahuagin can breathe air and water, but it needs to be submerged at least once every 4 hours to avoid suffocating.

traits.name: Shark Telepathy
traits.description: The sahuagin can magically command any shark within 120 feet of it, using a limited telepathy.

description:
Across fog-shrouded coasts or endless ocean swells, an ominous drone sounded on a conch shell chills the blood of all who hear it. This is the sound of the sahuagin hunting horn-a call to raid and battle. Coastal settlers refer to sahuagin as "sea devils," for sahuagin have no compassion in them, slaughtering the crews of ships and decimating coastal villages.

Devils of the Deep. Sahuagin are a predatory, piscine race that ventures from the ocean's black depths to hunt the creatures of the shallows and shore. Though they dwell in the deepest trenches of the ocean, sahuagin view the entire aquatic realm as their kingdom and the creatures in it as blood sport for their hunting parties.
The self-styled rulers of sahuagin ocean domains are massive mutant males that grow second sets of arms. They are terrible foes in battle, and all sahuagin bow down before these powerful barons.

Way of the Shark. Sahuagin worship the shark god Sekolah. Only female sahuagin are deemed worthy of channeling the god's power, and priestesses hold tremendous sway in sahuagin communities.
Sahuagin are driven into a frenzy by the smell of fresh blood. As worshipers of Sekolah, they also have a special kinship with sharks, which they train as attack animals. Even untrained sharks recognize sahuagin as allies and don't prey on them.

Elven Enmity. The sahuagin might control the oceans if not for the presence of their mortal enemies, the aquatic elves. Wars between the two races have raged for centuries across the coasts and seas of the world, disrupting maritime trade and drawing other races into the bloody conflict.
So intense is sahuagin hatred for the aquatic elves that the sea devils have adapted to combat their ancient foes. A sahuagin born near enough to an aquatic elf community can enter the world as a malenti-a sahuagin that physically resembles an aquatic elf in every way. Sahuagin are prone to mutation, but whether this rare phenomenon is a result of the wars between the sahuagin and the aquatic elves-or whether it preceded or even began the conflict-none can say.
The sahuagin put the malenti to good use as spies and assassins in aquatic elf cities and the societies of other creatures that pose a threat to sahuagin. The mere shadow of the malenti threat incites paranoia and suspicion among aquatic elves, whose resilience is weakened as the prelude to an actual sahuagin invasion.
combat-strategy: Hunt underwater in pods with commanded sharks via Shark Telepathy, using darkvision 120 and Perception +5 to ambush in dark water. Open with ranged Spears (20/60) to draw blood, then close for Multiattack bite + claw/spear where Blood Frenzy gives advantage on anyone already wounded — the pack doctrine is: chip a target at range, then all swarm the bleeding one. Surround targets so Pack-Tactics-style pressure and shark minions multiply attacks; drag prey into deep water or caves where surface access matters. Individual sahuagin break off if badly wounded (22 HP goes fast), but Blood Frenzy makes them fanatical against injured prey — they pursue the wounded even as the healthy withdraw.

name: Sahuagin Baron

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The sahuagin makes three Trident attacks.

actions.name: Trident
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Piercing damage.

reactions.name: Fiendish Blood
reactions.trigger: The sahuagin takes Piercing or Slashing damage
reactions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 14, each creature of the sahuagin's choice in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the sahuagin. Failure: 10 (3d6) Acid damage, and the target is cursed until it finishes a Short or Long Rest. While cursed, the target can't benefit from the Invisible condition, its Speed decreases by 10 feet, and all Fiends within 120 feet of the target can sense its location regardless of interposing obstacles.

traits.name: Blood Frenzy
traits.description: The sahuagin has Advantage on attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all its Hit Points.

traits.name: Limited Amphibiousness
traits.description: The sahuagin can breathe air and water, but it must be submerged at least once every 4 hours to avoid suffocating outside water.

traits.name: Shark Telepathy
traits.description: The sahuagin can magically control sharks within 120 feet of itself, using a special telepathy.

combat-strategy: Fight in water amid his shark pod: Multiattack three Trident attacks (+7, 13 dmg each, 20/60 ranged) and use Blood Frenzy advantage on anyone already hurt — focus fire the first PC wounded to make them a free-advantage magnet. Save Fiendish Blood (reaction, DC 14 Con, 3d6 acid + curse) for a big damage dealer or the healer: the curse kills invisibility, cuts Speed 10, and lets all fiends within 120 ft sense the target — broadcast it to summon reinforcements or mark the party's runner. Command sharks via telepathy to harry the backline while he duels at range with tridents, swimming 50 to reposition. He retreats to deeper caves or the surface only if his pod is destroyed and he drops below ~25 HP; otherwise he fights in water where his 50-ft swim outmaneuvers most land-bound armor, and he must return to submersion every 4 hours, so don't chase him onto land for long.

name: Sahuagin Priest

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The sahuagin makes two Spectral Jaws attacks.

actions.name: Spectral Jaws
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit: 11 (2d8 + 2) Force damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description:
The sahuagin casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 12):
At Will: Thaumaturgy
2/Day Each: Hold Person, Tongues

bonus_actions.name: Fiendish Aid
bonus_actions.description: The sahuagin casts Bless or Healing Word, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

traits.name: Blood Frenzy
traits.description: The sahuagin has Advantage on attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all its Hit Points.

traits.name: Limited Amphibiousness
traits.description: The sahuagin can breathe air and water, but it must be submerged at least once every 4 hours to avoid suffocating outside water.

traits.name: Shark Telepathy
traits.description: The sahuagin can magically control sharks within 120 feet of itself, using a special telepathy.

combat-strategy: Stay at the back of the shoal and pump out bonus-action Bless on attacking sahuagin (advantage stacks beautifully with their Blood Frenzy) or Healing Word on downed allies at 120 ft. On its action, Spectral Jaws (120 ft, force damage, +4) lets it snipe without exposure; hold Hold Person (DC 12 Wis) for the biggest melee bruiser separated from saving-throw help, then let the pod dogpile the paralyzed target. It has no escape tricks — 38 HP and AC 12 — so physically stay behind sharks or coral cover, using Tongues to negotiate or taunt before combat. If the front line collapses or it takes ~20 damage, it swims for deep water or the barrier reef; its survival is the pod's survival.

name: Sahuagin Priestess

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The sahuagin makes two attacks: one with her bite and one with her claws.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.

actions.name: Claws
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) slashing damage.

traits.name: Blood Frenzy
traits.description: The sahuagin has advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all its hit points.

traits.name: Limited Amphibiousness
traits.description: The sahuagin can breathe air and water, but it needs to be submerged at least once every 4 hours to avoid suffocating.

traits.name: Shark Telepathy
traits.description: The sahuagin can magically command any shark within 120 feet of it, using a limited telepathy.

traits.name: Spellcasting
traits.description:
The sahuagin is a 6th-level spellcaster. Her spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks). She has the following cleric spells prepared:

Cantrips (at wil1): guidance, thaumaturgy
1st level (4 slots): bless, detect magic, guiding bolt
2nd level (3 slots): hold person, spiritual weapon (trident)
3rd level (3 slots): mass healing word, tongues

combat-strategy: Open pre-combat with Bless on the war party and position behind coral, rocks, or shark cover at 60+ ft. Action economy: Spiritual Weapon (trident) as a bonus action keeps damage flowing while her action casts Hold Person (DC 12) on the party's front-line striker — freeze them and the sahuagin swarm with Blood Frenzy advantage; Mass Healing Word at 3rd level resurrects downed fiends mid-fight, so the party should save damage spikes for after it's spent. She's only AC 12/33 HP and its bite/claws are filler — never let melee reach her; kite by swimming 40 ft away each round. Retreat when she's burned key slots or drops below ~15 HP, diving for deeper trenches or summoning sharks via telepathy as she withdraws.

name: Sahuagin Warrior

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The sahuagin makes two Claw attacks.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) Slashing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Aquatic Charge
bonus_actions.description: The sahuagin swims up to its Swim Speed straight toward an enemy it can see.

traits.name: Blood Frenzy
traits.description: The sahuagin has Advantage on attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all its Hit Points.

traits.name: Limited Amphibiousness
traits.description: The sahuagin can breathe air and water, but it must be submerged at least once every 4 hours to avoid suffocating outside water.

traits.name: Shark Telepathy
traits.description: The sahuagin can magically control sharks within 120 feet of itself, using a special telepathy.

combat-strategy: Open with bonus action Aquatic Charge (40 ft swim) to slam into a target from ambush range, then Multiattack two Claws (+3) — in a pod, surround so multiple warriors pressure the same target and force ability-check spam. Blood Frenzy advantage on anyone already wounded means the pack should focus whatever is bleeding rather than spreading damage; they relish the hunt. Fight in their element — submerged, dark water where darkvision 120 levels the field; on land they lose the swim bonus and become ordinary fodder with 22 HP. Individual warriors flee at single-digit HP or when the pod breaks, diving for cover among rocks or summoned sharks.

name: Salamander

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The salamander makes two Flame Spear attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Constrict.

actions.name: Flame Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Fire damage. Hit or Miss: The spear magically returns to the salamander's hand immediately after a ranged attack.

actions.name: Constrict
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 15, one Large or smaller creature the salamander can see within 10 feet. Failure: 11 (2d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Fire damage. The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14), and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 11 (2d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Fire damage. The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) and has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.

traits.name: Fire Aura
traits.description: At the end of each of the salamander's turns, each creature of the salamander's choice in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the salamander takes 7 (2d6) Fire damage.

description:
Salamanders slither across the Sea of Ash on the Elemental Plane of Fire, their sinuous coils and jagged spines smoldering. Intense heat washes off their bodies, while their yellow eyes glow like candles in the deep-set hollows of their hawkish faces.
Salamanders adore power, and they delight in setting fire to things. Outside their home plane, they play among the burning skeletons of charred trees as forest fires rage around them, or slither down the slopes of erupting volcanoes to linger in fire pits and magma floes.

Fire Snakes. Salamanders hatch from eggs that are two-foot-diameter spheres of smoldering obsidian. When a salamander is ready to hatch, it melts its way through the egg's thick shell and emerges as a fire snake. A fire snake matures into a salamander adult within a year.

Slaves of the Efreet. Long ago, the efreet hired azers to build the fabled City of Brass, but then failed in their attempt to enslave that mystical race when the azers' work was done. Turning instead to strike against the salamanders, the efreet had better luck in establishing a slave race, which they use to unleash war and destruction across the planes.
Salamanders despise the azers, believing that if the efreet had succeeded in dominating that race of ' elemental crafters, the salamanders would still be free. The efreet use this enmity to their own advantage, stoking the salamanders' hatred and pitting them against the efreets' former servants.
The efreet suffer salamanders to serve no other master; when efreet encounter salamanders dedicated to the cults of Elemental Evil, they slay them rather than taking them as slaves.

Domineering Nobles. Although salamanders follow the destructive impulses of their fiery nature, slavery under the efreet has impacted the culture of free salamanders. They rule their own societies according to the efreet model, in which larger and stronger salamanders claim dominion over their lesser kin.
As salamanders age, they increase in size and status, rising to positions of power as cruel nobles among their kind. Nobles rule wandering bands of salamanders, which move across the Elemental Plane of Fire like desert nomads, raiding other communities for treasure.

Living Forges. Salamanders generate intense heat, and when they fight, their weapons glow red and sear the bodies of their enemies on contact. Even approaching a salamander is dangerous, since flesh blisters and burns in its proximity.
This inherent heat is an asset to salamanders' skill as smiths, allowing them to soften and shape iron and steel with their bare hands. Although not as meticulous as azers, salamanders number among the greatest metalsmiths in all the planes. Powerful creatures summon them as warriors, but others enlist the salamanders for their crafting skills, or bind them to forges and ovens to generate limitless heat.
combat-strategy: Grab and burn: Multiattack two Flame Spears (ranged 20/60, self-returning, no ammo worries) or replace one with Constrict (DC 15 Str) to Grapple + Restrict a target, then walk them across your Fire Aura. The winning combo is Constrict a Medium foe, drag them around with 30-ft speed, and let Fire Aura (2d6 end of turn) plus grapple damage grind them to ash while they can't reach help — a Restrained, burning grapnel also forces the party to split attacks between you and the grapple. Fight near flammable terrain — wood, oil, thatched docks — since you immune fire and your grapple-victims ignite the map against the party. Stand in water only to bait; it's your worst terrain (its own flavor, but RAW the aura still works). Retreat when the party focuses with cold or reach weapons and you drop below ~30 HP, climbing 30 up into a chimney or forge where the fight becomes yours.

name: Salamander Fire Snake

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Fire damage.

traits.name: Fire Aura
traits.description: At the end of each of the salamander's turns, each creature of the salamander's choice in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the salamander takes 3 (1d6) Fire damage.

combat-strategy: Pack hunter of the fire pits: swarm in groups, darting in for Bite (fire-tinged) and letting Fire Aura tick anyone adjacent at the end of your turn. Use climb 30 to drop from ceilings or braziers onto surprised PCs, then scurry back up out of melee reach — its 27 HP won't survive sustained contact, so hit-and-burn is the loop. Set fires: bite into flammable goods, oil, or thatch in torch-lit rooms and let the party split between you and the blaze. They scatter into cracks and chimneys once half the pack is dead or they're individually bloodied.

name: Salamander Inferno Master

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The salamander makes two Flame Trident attacks.

actions.name: Flame Trident
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +12, reach 5 ft. or range 30/90 ft. Hit: 16 (2d8 + 7) Piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) Fire damage. Hit or Miss: The trident magically returns to the salamander's hand immediately after a ranged attack.

actions.name: Inferno Blast
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 18, each creature in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point the salamander can see within 120 feet. Failure: 35 (10d6) Fire damage, and the target starts burning, taking 5 (1d10) Fire damage at the start of each of its turns instead of the normal burning damage. The target gains 1 Exhaustion level whenever it takes this burning damage. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 35 (10d6) Fire damage, and the target starts burning, taking 5 (1d10) Fire damage at the start of each of its turns instead of the normal burning damage. The target gains 1 Exhaustion level whenever it takes this burning damage. Success: Half damage only.

bonus_actions.name: Blazing Movement
bonus_actions.description: The salamander moves up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. During this movement, fire fills a 5-foot Emanation originating from the salamander. When the Emanation enters a creature's space, that creature takes 7 (2d6) Fire damage. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

traits.name: Fire Aura
traits.description: At the end of each of the salamander's turns, each creature of the salamander's choice in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the salamander takes 10 (3d6) Fire damage.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The salamander has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

combat-strategy: Open with Inferno Blast (DC 18 Dex, 30-ft radius, 35 dmg + exhaustion-generating burning) on the densest cluster — the escalating 1d10 burning plus 1 exhaustion level per tick snowballs and wins attrition fights if the party doesn't extinguish immediately. Use bonus action Blazing Movement every round: 40-ft free disengage plus a 2d6 fire trail means the party can never pin it, and it can charge through them, aura-pooling adjacent for its 10-ft Fire Aura on top. Flame Trident (+12, 16+14 dmg, 30/90 ranged) punishes anyone who breaks off to help burning victims or extinguish flames — snipe the healers doing bucket brigades. Magic Resistance blunts the party's control spells; bully the front line physically, set the map alight in a forge/volcanic lair, and let the terrain burn them out. Retreat into lava, magma flows, or deep fire where nothing can follow once below ~80 HP or if the party consistently beats DC 18 — it has no business standing still in a fight it can move out of.

name: Satyr

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, the satyr pushes the target up to 10 feet straight away from itself.

actions.name: Mockery
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 12, one creature the satyr can see within 90 feet. Failure: 5 (1d6 + 2) Psychic damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 5 (1d6 + 2) Psychic damage.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The satyr has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
Satyrs are raucous fey that frolic in wild forests, driven by curiosity and hedonism in equal measure.
Satyrs resemble stout male humans with the furry lower bodies and cloven hooves of goats. Horns sprout from their heads, ranging in shape from a pair of small nubs to large, curling rams' horns. They typically sport facial hair.

Hedonistic Revelers. Satyrs crave the strongest drink, the most fragrant spices, and the most dizzying dances. A satyr feels starved when it can't indulge itself, and it goes to great lengths to sate its desires. It might kidnap a fine minstrel to hear lovely songs, sneak through a well-defended garden to gaze upon a beautiful lad or lass, or infiltrate a palace to taste the finest food in the land. Satyrs allow no festivity to pass them by. They partake in any holiday they've heard of. Civilizations of the world have enough festivals and holy days among them to justify nonstop celebration.
Inebriated on drink and pleasure, satyrs give no thought to the consequences of the hedonism they incite in others. They leave such creatures mystified at their own behavior. Such revelers might have to scrounge for excuses to explain their disordered state to parents, employers, family, or friends.
combat-strategy: Skirmish prankster: 40-ft speed, Magic Resistance, and Stealth +5 mean it opens with Mockery (DC 12 Wis, psychic at 90 ft) from cover, then strafes with Hooves on anything that closes. Hooves push a Medium-or-smaller target 10 ft away after a hit — pair with terrain like cliffs, spike pits, or a thorn hedge: Mock, hoof, push, repeat, kiting melee types in circles while other revelers or bow-fire bleed them. Stay 90 ft from casters its Magic Resistance already handles, and never stand still at the end of a turn — its 31 HP evaporates in focused fire. It dances away laughing once bloodied or bored; satyrs fight for sport, not to the death, and flee at half HP or when the fun ends.

name: Satyr Revelmaster

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The satyr makes three Prance attacks.

actions.name: Prance
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Charmed condition until the start of the satyr's next turn.

actions.name: Fey Melody
actions.description:
The satyr conjures a charming or frightening song. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 14, each enemy in a 60-foot Emanation originating from the satyr. Failure: The target is subjected to the song's effect:
Charming. The target has the Charmed condition for 1 minute. While Charmed, the target has the Incapacitated condition and uses all its movement to dance in place. The effect ends on the target if it takes any damage.
Frightening. 10 (2d6 + 3) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition for 1 minute. If the target ends its turn out of line of sight from the satyr, the condition ends on it.
actions.save_effect: Failure: the target is subjected to the GM-chosen song variant picked at the variant chooser — Charming (the dance) or Frightening (the fear). Per-variant conditions and damage resolve from the variants payload.

variants.label: Charming
variants.description: The target has the Charmed condition for 1 minute. While Charmed, it has the Incapacitated condition and uses all its movement to dance in place. The effect ends on the target if it takes any damage. No damage.
variants.duration_note: until the start of the satyr's next-to-next turn (1 minute); ends early if the target takes any damage (dance-in-place and end-on-damage clauses GM-enforced)

variants.label: Frightening
variants.description: 10 (2d6 + 3) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition for 1 minute. If the target ends its turn out of line of sight from the satyr, the condition ends on it.
variants.duration_note: for 1 minute; ends if the target ends its turn out of line of sight from the satyr (line-of-sight clause GM-enforced)

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The satyr has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

combat-strategy: Open with Fey Melody (DC 14 Wis, 60-ft emanation) — the Charming mode is the fight-winner: Charmed + Incapacitated enemies dance in place for a minute, helpless, and the effect only ends on damage, which your melee must avoid dealing to them. Use Frightening mode on the party's ranged/caster line where the frightened condition drives them out of position, then kiting them from 40-ft speed. Multiattack Prance (+7, 13 dmg + auto-Charm until your next turn) lets you lock down a grappler or bruiser hand-to-hand — Charm on the biggest threat, then dance away before the effect lapses. Magic Resistance makes control spells a coin flip in your favor; stay in the middle of the revel where allies and dancing victims blur targeting. Retreat when the dancers wake up (they'll take themselves out with friendly fire if you position them well) and you drop below ~30 HP, vanishing into the revel with Stealth +5... err, Acrobatics +7 through cover.

name: Scarecrow

actions.name: Fearsome Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (2d4 + 1) Slashing damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the end of the scarecrow's next turn.

actions.name: Terrifying Glare
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 11, one creature the scarecrow can see within 30 feet. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition until the end of the scarecrow's next turn. While Frightened, the target has the Paralyzed condition.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Frightened condition until the end of the scarecrow's next turn. While Frightened, the target has the Paralyzed condition.

description:
At harvest time, when death revisits the twilit world and summer's blossoms bow their withered heads, eerie scarecrows loom in silent vigil over empty fields. With immortal patience, these stoic sentinels hold their posts through wind, storm, and flood, bound to their master's command, eager to terrify prey with its sackcloth visage and rend victims with its razor-sharp claws.

Spirit-Powered Constructs. A scarecrow is animated by the bound spirit of a slain evil creature, granting it purpose and mobility. It is this uncanny presence from beyond death that allows a scarecrow to inspire fear in those it gazes upon. Hags and witches often bind scarecrows with the spirits of demons, but any evil spirit will do. Although aspects of the spirit's personality might surface, a scarecrow's spirit doesn't recall the memories it had as a creature, and its will is focused solely on serving its creator. If its creator dies, the spirit inhabiting a scarecrow either continues to follow its last commands, seeks revenge for its creator's death, or destroys itself.

Construct Nature. A scarecrow doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Night stalker: ambush at dusk from field cover, opening with Terrifying Glare (DC 11 Wis) on the lone traveler — Frightened + Paralyzed is a free execution setup while the victim can't move or act. Follow with Fearsome Claw hits that stack more Frightened on anyone who engages, so the party fights through its own fear while the scarecrow closes on the paralyzed target. It's fragile (27 HP, AC 11) — fight in cornfields, fog, or darkness where it can break line of sight between turns and reappear somewhere else, resetting the fear. It doesn't retreat from its appointed haunt (mindless malice), but disengages into the field when hacked apart or confronted by fire, which it should be kept away from.

name: Scorpion

actions.name: Sting
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Poison damage.

combat-strategy: Tiny nuisance: sting (1 piercing + 1d6 poison) whatever bare flesh it can reach, then scuttle into cracks, rubble, or boots. Its only tricks are numbers, blindsight in total darkness, and the psychological terror of a poison sting on a sleeping or prone victim — ambush at night, in tents, in beds. Swarm downed or distracted targets, attack ankles of unarmored commoners, and vanish at the first serious swing; anything that hits it kills it instantly (1 HP), so hit-and-flee is the entire doctrine.

name: Scout

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The scout makes two attacks, using Shortsword and Longbow in any combination.

actions.name: Shortsword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 150/600 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Piercing damage.

description: Scouts are skilled hunters and trackers who offer their services for a fee. Most hunt wild game, but a few work as bounty hunters, serve as guides, or provide military reconnaissance.
combat-strategy: Skirmish from range: use Stealth +6 and passive Perception 15 to spot the party first, then Multiattack with Longbow (150 ft) from concealment, relocating 30 ft after each volley so they can't return fire accurately. Only draw the Shortsword if engaged, and only against separated, isolated prey — at 16 HP this scout trades nothing. Use terrain (ridgelines, tree lines) for cover between shots, and if the party closes to melee or charges, Disengage back toward allies or fortification. It breaks off and flees to report once spotted properly, out of arrows, or once the party reaches defensible ground — its job is information, not a kill, and a dead scout delivers none.

name: Scout Captain

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The scout makes two attacks, using Shortsword or Longbow in any combination.

actions.name: Shortsword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage, plus 10 (3d6) Piercing damage if the attack was made with Advantage.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +5, range 150/600 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage, plus 10 (3d6) Piercing damage if the attack was made with Advantage.

bonus_actions.name: Aim
bonus_actions.description: The scout has Advantage on the next attack roll it makes during the current turn.

reactions.name: Uncanny Dodge
reactions.trigger: The scout is hit by an attack roll
reactions.description: The scout halves the damage (round down) it takes from that attack.

combat-strategy: Open with a Longbow at long range, using Aim as a bonus action so the shot lands with Advantage and triggers the +10 (3d6) piercing bonus damage — the bonus damage makes Advantage the single biggest lever on this stat block. Kite constantly: 30-ft movement against most foes' 30-ft speed means shooting from maximum distance, retreating, and only closing with Multiattack (mixed shortsword/longbow) when a target is already engaged by allies or has no reaction left. Save Uncanny Dodge for the biggest hits you can see coming (crits, rogue sneak attacks, smites), and save it, don't waste it on routine swings. Retreat to cover or climb (30-ft climb speed) when reduced below roughly half HP or when both its ranged advantage opportunities dry up, since 66 HP won't survive a sustained flurry at AC 15.

name: Scylla

traits.name: Six Heads
traits.description: Scylla has Advantage on Perception checks and on saving throws against being Blinded, Deafened, or knocked Unconscious.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If Scylla fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Blood Tide
traits.description: When Scylla hits a creature with a Bite, she can immediately pull it 10 ft. toward her if it is Huge or smaller.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Scylla makes three Bite attacks, each against a different target.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +16, reach 15 ft. Hit: 30 (4d10 + 8) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Blood Tide (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 25, each creature within 30 ft. of her lair mouth. Failure: 55 (10d10) Piercing damage. Success: Half damage. A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by this tide is dragged into the depths and consumed.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Bite
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Bite attack.

legendary_actions.name: Snatch
legendary_actions.description: One head lunges at a Grappled or Restrained creature. Melee Attack Roll: +16, reach 15 ft. Hit: 30 (4d10 + 8) Piercing damage.

legendary_actions.name: Shriek (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 23, each enemy within 60 ft. Failure: 11 (2d10) Thunder damage and the target is Deafened for 1 minute. Success: half damage and not Deafened.

description: A cliff-hugging horror of six snapping heads and coiled serpentine coils, once a naiad, now the toll-taker of the narrow strait who plucks sailors from the deck.
combat-strategy: She stands her ground at the strait, six heads on six targets, pulling one aboard each round with Blood Tide and shrieking to silence crossbow fire.

name: Sea Hag

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Death Glare
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 11, one Frightened creature the hag can see within 30 feet. Failure: If the target has 20 Hit Points or fewer, it drops to 0 Hit Points. Otherwise, the target takes 13 (3d8) Psychic damage.
actions.save_effect: If the target has 20 Hit Points or fewer, it drops to 0 Hit Points. Otherwise, the target takes 13 (3d8) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Illusory Appearance
actions.description: The hag casts Disguise Self, using Constitution as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13). The spell's duration is 24 hours.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The hag can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Coven Magic
traits.description: While within 30 feet of at least two hag allies, the hag can cast one of the following spells, requiring no Material components, using the spell's normal casting time, and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 11): Augury, Find Familiar, Identify, Locate Object, Scrying, or Unseen Servant. The hag must finish a Long Rest before using this trait to cast that spell again.

traits.name: Vile Appearance
traits.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 11, any Beast or Humanoid that starts its turn within 30 feet of the hag and can see the hag's true form. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition until the start of its next turn. Success: The target is immune to this hag's Vile Appearance for 24 hours.

description:
Sea hags live in dismal and polluted underwater lairs, surrounded by merrow and other aquatic monsters. Beauty drives a sea hag to fits of anger. When confronted with something beautiful, the hag might simply attack it or deface it. If something beautiful gives hope, a sea hag wants it to cause despair. If it inspires courage, the sea hag wants it to cause fear.

Ugly Inside and Out. Sea hags are by far the ugliest of all hags, with slimy scales covering their pallid skin. A sea hag's hair resembles seaweed and covers her emaciated body, and her glassy eyes seem as lifeless as a doll's. Although a sea hag can hide her true form under a veil of illusion, the hag is cursed to forever appear ugly. Her illusory form appears haggard at best.

Covens. A sea hag that is part of a coven (see the "Hag Covens" sidebar) has a challenge rating of 4 (1,100 XP).
combat-strategy: Fight in or near water where her 40-ft swim speed lets her drag the fight into an element most humanoids handle poorly, and open by appearing as something harmless via Illusory Appearance (Disguise Self, 24 hours) before the encounter turns hostile. Her kill chain is Vile Appearance + Death Glare: position so frightened creatures start their turns within 30 ft, then focus Death Glare on any frightened target at 20 HP or fewer for an instant execution — finish wounded fighters and spellcasters this way before they can react. In a coven (two hags within 30 ft), use Coven Magic to add Augury/Scrying utility or spare casting for Locate Object. Disengage and slip underwater when her Death Glare targets all save reliably or when she drops below ~20 HP; her 13 damage Claw is a fallback, not the plan.

name: Sea Horse

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The seahorse can breathe only underwater.

combat-strategy: This 1-Hit Point creature is scenery, not a combatant — it should flee. On any threat it should be attacked by or swim 20 ft directly away, using kelp, coral, or rocks as cover, and it has no attack action worth mentioning. In an encounter it exists as flavor, a familiar-style scout, or bait: use it to mark a square the heroes notice, or as a harmless target that a careless AoE attack will splatter. If cornered, it simply drifts and hopes; the GM should treat its survival as a narrative moment, not a tactical one.

name: Seahorse

actions.name: Bubble Dash
actions.description: While underwater, the seahorse moves up to its Swim Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
actions.advisory_message: moves up to its Swim Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks while underwater — advisory record: self-movement and opportunity-attack suppression are GM-enforced, GM moves the token (no movement or opportunity-attack consumer app-wide, §70). No attack roll, no saving throw, no dice.

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The seahorse can breathe only underwater.

combat-strategy: With 1 HP and no attack, this seahorse's entire tactic is Bubble Dash: swim its full 20-ft speed away without provoking Opportunity Attacks, threading through reefs, seaweed beds, or the legs of larger creatures to break line of sight. Its Stealth +5 and Tiny size make escape realistic against unaware or distracted foes, so open the moment it's threatened and head for the nearest hiding spot rather than away in the open. Keep it in the water — its 5-ft walk speed is a death sentence on land. Use it as an alarm or messenger that must reach a destination before the party intercepts it; once surrounded, it has no fight and the encounter is over.

name: Shadow

actions.name: Draining Swipe
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Necrotic damage, and the target's Strength score decreases by 1d4. The target dies if this reduces that score to 0. If a Humanoid is slain by this attack, a Shadow rises from the corpse 1d4 hours later.

bonus_actions.name: Shadow Stealth
bonus_actions.description: While in Dim Light or Darkness, the shadow takes the Hide action.

traits.name: Amorphous
traits.description: The shadow can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

traits.name: Sunlight Weakness
traits.description: While in sunlight, the shadow has Disadvantage on D20 Tests.

description:
Shadows are undead that resemble dark exaggerations of humanoid shadows.

Dark Disposition. From the darkness, the shadow reaches out to feed on living creatures' vitality. They can consume any living creature, but they are especially drawn to creatures untainted by evil. A creature that lives a life of goodness and piety consigns its basest impulses and strongest temptations to the darkness where the shadows hunger. As a shadow drains its victim's strength and physical form, the victim's shadow darkens and begins to move of its own volition. In death, the creature's shadow breaks free, becoming a new undead shadow hungry for more life to consume.
If a creature from which a shadow has been created somehow returns to life, its undead shadow senses the return. The shadow might seek its "parent" to vex or slay. Whether the shadow pursues its living counterpart, the creature that birthed the shadow no longer casts one until the monster is destroyed.

Undead Nature. A shadow doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Ambush from darkness: shadows should attack only in dim light or darkness, opening with Shadow Stealth as a bonus action to Hide, then Draining Swipe with Advantage from unseen-attacker status. Focus the weakest or lowest-Strength targets, because Strength drain of 1d4 per hit compounds rapidly and a humanoid killed by the swipe becomes a new shadow in 1d4 hours — attrition is the win condition, and 40-ft speed lets it disengage into shadows between turns. Never stand in sunlight or bright torchlight (Disadvantage on everything), so lure foes away from light sources or fight at night and in unlit ruins. It's amorphous, so slip through bars, cracks, and portcullises to escape or split the party; retreat into deeper darkness when reduced below ~10 HP or when the party starts lighting up the area.

name: Shadow Demon

actions.name: Umbral Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 16 (3d8 + 3) Psychic damage.

bonus_actions.name: Shadow Stealth
bonus_actions.description: While in Dim Light or Darkness, the demon takes the Hide action.

traits.name: Demonistic Restoration
traits.description: If the demon dies outside the Abyss, its body dissolves into ichor, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Abyss.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.description: The demon can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

traits.name: Light Sensitivity
traits.description: While in Bright Light, the demon has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls.

description:
When a demon's body is destroyed but the fiend is prevented from reforming in the Abyss, its essence sometimes takes on a vague physical form. These shadow demons exist outside the normal abyssal hierarchy, since their creation results most often from mortal magic, not from transformation or promotion.
Shadow demons all but disappear in the darkness, and they can creep about without making a sound. A shadow demon uses its insubstantial claws to feast on its victim's fears, to taste its memories, and drink in its doubts. Bright light harries this fiend and shows its distinct shape, resolving it from a blur of darkness to a winged humanoid creature whose lower body trails off into nothing, and whose claws rend a victim's mind.

Shadowy Nature. A shadow demon doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Fight exclusively in dim light or darkness: open with Shadow Stealth to Hide, then use Incorporeal Movement to pass straight through creatures and obstacles, closing to strike with Umbral Claw (16 psychic average) from hidden with Advantage. Its Fly 30 (hover) plus incorporeal travel makes walls and locked doors meaningless — hit spellcasters in the back line, then phase through a solid object adjacent to safety (but never end the turn inside an object, taking 1d10 force). Avoid bright light at all costs (Disadvantage), so snuff torches, fight at night, or drag the fight into tunnels; a daylight fight is a fight to flee. With STR 1 it can't be shoved meaningfully and can't be contained by cages, so the party must solve it with radiant light — pressure and light is your counter to plan around, and Demonistic Restoration means killing it outside the Abyss only sends it home, so stage the fight where it matters narratively.

name: Shadow Dragon

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dragon makes three Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 10 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Shadow Breath
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 17, each creature in a 60-foot Cone. Failure: 35 (10d6) Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: A Humanoid reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage dies, and a Shadow rises from the corpse. The shadow is under the dragon's control and shares the dragon's Initiative count but acts immediately after the dragon.
actions.save_effect: 35 (10d6) Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage. A Humanoid reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage dies, and a Shadow rises from the corpse. The shadow is under the dragon's control and shares the dragon's Initiative count but acts immediately after the dragon.

bonus_actions.name: Shadow Stealth
bonus_actions.description: While in Dim Light or Darkness, the dragon takes the Hide action.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 2
legendary_actions.description: The shadow dragon takes 2 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only immediately after another creature's turn. The shadow dragon regains expended legendary uses at the start of its turn.

legendary_actions.name: Pounce
legendary_actions.description: The dragon moves up to half its Speed (movement advisory — GM moves the token; no movement-distance consumer), and it makes one Rend attack.

legendary_actions.name: Veil of Shadow
legendary_actions.description: The dragon uses Shadow Stealth (stealth advisory — GM moves the token into hiding; no stealth-consumer), and one creature of its choice that it can see within 10 feet of it takes 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage. The dragon can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.

lair_actions:
Shadow dragons lair in places of darkness and despair, such as accursed ruins, the depths of the Underdark, or the Shadowfell.

The region around a shadow dragons lair is twisted by its presence, creating the following effects:

Negative Energy Suffusion. Whenever a creature within 1 mile of the lair regains Hit Points from a spell, it subtracts 1d10 from the number of Hit Points regained.
Stifling Shadows. Within 1 mile of the lair, effects that normally create Bright Light instead create Dim Light, and creatures there have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

If the dragon dies or moves its lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead. (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)

traits.name: Living Shadow
traits.description: While in Dim Light or Darkness, the dragon has Resistance to damage that isn't Force, Psychic, or Radiant.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: While in sunlight, the dragon has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls.

combat-strategy: Fight at night or in darkness where Living Shadow grants resistance to nearly all damage, opening with Shadow Stealth to vanish, then hit-and-run with 80-ft flight: dive into range, Multiattack three Rend, and climb back out of melee reach before grounded foes close. Save Shadow Breath (60-ft cone, DC 17) for clustered groups or chokepoints, and remember any humanoid it 0s becomes a controlled shadow on its initiative — the corpse army compounds the pressure, so target the party's meat shield last and their squishies with the cone first. Use legendary actions aggressively: Pounce to close or reposition with a free Rend after a PC overextends, and Veil of Shadow to snipe someone adjacent while vanishing again. Spend Legendary Resistance on banishment, power word, and hold effects, not cantrips. Retreat into deep shadow or the air when it drops low or its LR pool empties; sunlight is its true weakness, so it should break off any fight that moves into open daylight.

name: Shambling Mound

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The shambling mound makes three Charged Tendril attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Engulf.

actions.name: Charged Tendril
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 5 (2d4) Lightning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, the shambling mound pulls the target 5 feet straight toward itself.

actions.name: Engulf
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 15, one Medium or smaller creature within 5 feet. Failure: The target is pulled into the shambling mound's space and has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14). Until the grapple ends, the target has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, and it takes 10 (3d6) Lightning damage at the start of each of its turns. When the shambling mound moves, the Grappled target moves with it, costing it no extra movement. The shambling mound can have only one creature Grappled by this action at a time.
actions.save_effect: The target is pulled into the shambling mound's space and has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14). Until the grapple ends, the target has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, and it takes 10 (3d6) Lightning damage at the start of each of its turns. When the shambling mound moves, the Grappled target moves with it, costing it no extra movement. The shambling mound can have only one creature Grappled by this action at a time.

traits.name: Lightning Absorption
traits.description: Whenever the shambling mound is subjected to Lightning damage, it regains a number of Hit Points equal to the Lightning damage dealt.

description:
A shambling mound, sometimes called a shambler, trudges ponderously through bleak swamps, dismal marshes, and rain forests, consuming any organic matter in its path. This rotting heap of animated vegetation looms up half again as tall as a human, tapering into a faceless "head" at its top.

All-Consuming Devourers. A shambling mound feeds on any organic material, tirelessly consuming plants as it moves and devouring animals that can't escape it. Only the shambling mounds' rarity and plodding speed prevent them from overwhelming entire ecosystems. Even so, their presence leeches natural environments of plant and animal life, and an unsettling quiet pervades the swamps and woods haunted by these ever-hungry horrors.

Unseen Hunters. Composed of decaying leaves, vines, roots, and other natural swamp and forest compost, shamblers can blend into their environs. Because they move slowly, they rarely attempt to pursue and catch creatures. Rather, they remain in place, sustaining themselves by absorbing nutrients from their surroundings as they wait for prey to come to them. When a creature passes near or alights upon a shambling mound, the monster comes to life, seizing and absorbing the unwary prey.

Spawned by Lightning. A shambling mound results from a phenomenon in which lightning or fey magic invigorates an otherwise ordinary swamp plant. As the plant is reborn into its second life, it chokes the life from plants and animals around it, mulching their corpses in a heap around its roots. Those roots eventually give up their reliance on the soil, directing the shambling mound to seek out new sources of food.

The Weed that Walks. The instinct that drives a shambling mound is its central root-stem, buried somewhere inside its ponderous form. The rest of a shambler consists of the rotting heap that it simultaneously accumulates and feeds on, which protects the root-stem and animates to smash and smother the life from any creature.
The dense mass of a shambling mound's body shrugs off the effects of cold and fire. Lightning reinvigorates the root-stem, strengthening the shambling mound and bolstering its consumptive drive.
Despite its monstrous form, the shambling mound is a living plant that requires air and nourishment. Although it doesn't sleep the way an animal does, it can lie dormant for days on end before rising to hunt for food.

A Resurgent Menace. If a shambling mound faces defeat before an overwhelming foe, the root-stem can feign death, collapsing the remains of its mound. If not subsequently killed, the root-stem beds down in the shambler's remains to slowly regrow its full body, then once again sets out to consume all it can. In this way, shambling mound infestations long thought destroyed can recur time and again.
combat-strategy: Ambush from thick vegetation where its Stealth and Blindsight 60 let it wait unnoticed, then Multiattack with Charged Tendrils (10-ft reach), using the pull-5 property to drag a target into Engulf range. The combo is the whole game: pull with tendrils on turn one, Engulf on turn two (or replace one tendril attack with Engulf immediately), then Grapple/Blind/Restrict the victim while it takes 10 lightning each of its own turns; drag the engulfed prey away from the party's reach, since the mound moves with its captive for free. Engulf the most dangerous martial target, ideally one who can't burst damage the mound from inside. Bully the weak: DC 15 Strength on Engulf breaks most mid-level PCs. Avoid lightning casters entirely — Lightning Absorption turns their best spell into your healing — and wade into water (20-ft swim) if the fight turns into an archery contest you're losing.

name: Shield Guardian
languages: Understands commands given in any language but can't speak

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The guardian makes two Fist attacks.

actions.name: Fist
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Force damage.

reactions.name: Protection
reactions.trigger: An attack roll hits the wearer of the guardian's amulet while the wearer is within 5 feet of the guardian
reactions.description: The wearer gains a +5 bonus to AC, including against the triggering attack and possibly causing it to miss, until the start of the guardian's next turn.

traits.name: Bound
traits.description: The guardian is magically bound to an amulet. While the guardian and its amulet are on the same plane of existence, the amulet's wearer can telepathically call the guardian to travel to it, and the guardian knows the distance and direction to the amulet. If the guardian is within 60 feet of the amulet's wearer, half of any damage the wearer takes (round up) is transferred to the guardian.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.description: The guardian regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns if it has at least 1 Hit Point.

traits.name: Spell Storing
traits.description: A spellcaster who wears the guardian's amulet can cause the guardian to store one spell of level 4 or lower. To do so, the wearer must cast the spell on the guardian while within 5 feet of it. The spell has no effect but is stored within the guardian. Any previously stored spell is lost when a new spell is stored. The guardian can cast the spell stored with any parameters set by the original caster, requiring no spell components and using the caster's spellcasting ability. The stored spell is then lost.

description:
Wizards and other spellcasters create shield guardians for protection. A shield guardian treads beside its master, absorbing damage to keep its master alive as long as possible.

Master's Amulet. Every shield guardian has an amulet magically linked to it. A shield guardian can have only one corresponding amulet, and if that amulet is destroyed, the shield guardian is incapacitated until a replacement amulet is created. A shield guardian's amulet is subject to direct attack if it isn't being worn or carried. It has AC 10, 10 hit points, and immunity to poison and psychic damage. Crafting an amulet requires 1 week and costs 1,000 gp in components.
A shield guardian's solitary focus is to protect the amulet's wearer. The amulet's wearer can command the guardian to attack its enemies or to guard the wielder against attack. If an attack threatens to injure the wearer, the construct can magically absorb the blow into its own body, even at a distance.
A spellcaster can store a single spell within a shield guardian, which can then cast the spell on command or under specific conditions. Many a wizard has been rendered helpless by enemies, only to surprise those foes when its shield guardian unleashes potent magical power.

Magnificent Treasure. Because a shield guardian's ownership can be transferred by giving its matching amulet to another creature, some wizards collect exorbitant sums from princes, nobles, and crime lords to create shield guardians for them. At the same time, a shield guardian makes a mighty prize for anyone who slays its master and claims its amulet.

Construct Nature. A shield guardian doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: This is a bodyguard, not a hunter: stay within 60 ft of the amulet wearer at all times so half their damage transfers to you, and position to keep the protected charge out of reach rather than chasing the enemy. Open by closing to 10-ft Fist reach and placing yourself between threats and the wearer; use the Protection reaction on the wearer's biggest incoming attack (+5 AC can flip a hit to a miss, including the triggering attack). Two Fists average ~36 damage per Multiattack turn — punish whoever steps into reach, but never break the 60-ft tether to pursue. Its 10/turn Regeneration means chip damage is wasted on it, so force the party to burst or focus the wearer; a smart party will ignore it, which is fine — let it ignore them. If the wearer dies or the amulet leaves the plane, it loses its purpose: fight on if commanded, but without a charge it has no reason to die in place — withdraw to its binding location.

name: Shrieker

actions.name: Shriek
actions.description: When bright light or a creature is within 30 feet of the shrieker, it emits a shriek audible within 300 feet of it. The shrieker continues to shriek until the disturbance moves out of range and for 1d4 of the shrieker's turns afterward

traits.name: False Appearance
traits.description: While the shrieker remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary fungus.

description: A shrieker i s a human-sized mushroom that emits a piercing screech to drive off creatures that disturb it. Other creatures use the fungi as an alarm to signal the approach of prey, and various intelligent races of the Underdark cultivate shriekers on the outskirts of their communities to discourage trespassers.
combat-strategy: It can't move, fight, or think — the shrieker is a living alarm. Tactically it's a terrain trap: scatter clusters of them in caverns and passages as early-warning systems, since any creature or bright light within 30 ft triggers a 300-ft shriek that summons whatever else the GM parked nearby. Place them at chokepoints, behind False Appearance camouflage near treasure, or in pairs so disturbing one brings the party into an ambush zone at full noise. There is no combat to run: if attacked, it shrieks and dies shortly after — the strategy is entirely about what the noise attracts and how long the party must survive the response it calls down.

name: Shrieker Fungus

reactions.name: Shriek
reactions.trigger: A creature or a source of Bright Light moves within 30 feet of the shrieker.
reactions.description: The shrieker emits a shriek audible within 300 feet of itself for 1 minute or until the shrieker dies.

combat-strategy: Its Shriek is a reaction, making this version a smarter tripwire: it screams for a full minute (or until killed) the instant anything disturbs it, so seed corridors, doorways, and the paths to treasure with them and time the party's arrival so the 300-ft shriek pulls guardians to a chosen kill zone. False Appearance means motionless specimens are invisible to casual inspection — cluster several around a room so one alarm guarantees the rest keep up the noise. AC 5 and 13 HP mean they die to any attack, so the counterplay you're exploiting is noise, not durability: ranged attackers or AoE can silence them, but the minute-long shriek of the survivors still carries. Pair with hungry predators or patrolling guards positioned within 300 ft for maximum effect.

name: Silver Dragon Wyrmling

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dragon makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Cold Breath
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: 18 (4d8) Cold damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: The target takes 18 (4d8) Cold damage. Success: The target takes half damage.

actions.name: Paralyzing Breath
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. First Failure: The target has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn, when it repeats the save. Second Failure: The target has the Paralyzed condition, and it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.
actions.save_effect: First Failure: The target has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn, when it repeats the save. Second Failure: The target has the Paralyzed condition, and it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

combat-strategy: A good-aligned wyrmling rarely starts a fight, but when forced, it should use flight (60 ft) to control altitude: stay just above melee reach, dive in for Multiattack Rend, and climb back out. Choose Paralyzing Breath over Cold Breath when outnumbered or facing armored fighters — DC 13 Con paralysis on a 15-ft cone neutralizes one or two martial types for a round or more, letting the young dragon fight on its terms; save Cold Breath for clustered groups where 18 avg damage lands cheaply. Its 45 HP can't trade blows, so hit-and-run over rooftops, water, or cliffs where ground-based pursuers slow down. Bully weaker foes and disengage from big ones: the Paralyzed victims repeat saves, so never waste a full melee round standing next to someone who will wake up mid-fight.

name: Simurgh
languages: All; speaks to beasts and good-aligned humanoids; telepathy 120 ft.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If the Simurgh fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Purifying Aura
traits.description: At the start of its turn, the Simurgh removes one Curse, Disease, or Poison effect from each ally within 30 ft.

traits.name: Wings of Blessing
traits.description: An ally that starts its turn within 30 ft. of the Simurgh gains 10 (3d6) Temporary Hit Points.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The Simurgh makes two Talon attacks and one Beak attack.

actions.name: Talon
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +15, reach 10 ft. Hit: 26 (4d8 + 8) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Beak
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +15, reach 10 ft. Hit: 24 (3d10 + 8) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Purifying Blaze (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 24, each creature in a 60-foot Cone the Simurgh chooses to burn. Failure: 66 (12d10) Radiant damage. Success: Half damage.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Talon
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Talon attack.

legendary_actions.name: Healing Breath (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: The Simurgh exhales warm wind over one creature within 30 ft. The target regains 22 (4d10) Hit Points and the Simurgh regains 5 Hit Points.

legendary_actions.name: Soothing Cry (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Each ally within 60 ft. is calmed, ending one effect causing them to be Charmed, Frightened, or Confused.

description: The benevolent great bird of the high peaks, a healer and a counselor, who has nested in the mountain's heart since before the age of humankind and asks only courtesy in return for her aid.
combat-strategy: She fights defensively around her wounded, weaving purifying auras; when the fiends crowd, Purifying Blaze scatters them while she lifts the wounded to safety.

name: Skeleton
languages: Understands Common plus one other language but can't speak

actions.name: Shortsword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Shortbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +5, range 80/320 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

description:
Skeletons arise when animated by dark magic. They heed the summons of spellcasters who call them from their stony tombs and ancient battlefields, or rise of their own accord in places saturated with death and loss, awakened by stirrings of necromantic energy or the presence of corrupting evil.

Animated Dead. Whatever sinister force awakens a skeleton infuses its bones with a dark vitality, adhering joint to joint and reassembling dismantled limbs. This energy motivates a skeleton to move and think in a rudimentary fashion, though only as a pale imitation of the way it behaved in life. An animated skeleton retains no connection to its past, although resurrecting a skeleton restores it body and soul, banishing the hateful undead spirit that empowers it.
While most skeletons are the animated remains of dead humans and other humanoids, skeletal undead can be created from the bones of other creatures besides humanoids, giving rise to a host of terrifying and unique forms.

Obedient Servants. Skeletons raised by spell are bound to the will of their creator. They follow orders to the letter, never questioning the tasks their masters give them, regardless of the consequences. Because of their literal interpretation of commands and unwavering obedience, skeletons adapt poorly to changing circumstances. They can't read, speak, emote, or communicate in any way except to nod, shake their heads, or point. Still, skeletons are able to accomplish a variety of relatively complex tasks.
A skeleton can fight with weapons and wear armor, can load and fire a catapult or trebuchet, scale a siege ladder, form a shield wall, or dump boiling oil. However, it must receive careful instructions explaining how such tasks are accomplished.
Although they lack the intellect they possessed in life, skeletons aren't mindless. Rather than break its limbs attempting to batter its way through an iron door, a skeleton tries the handle first. If that doesn't work, it searches for another way through or around the obstacle.

Habitual Behaviors. Independent skeletons temporarily or permanently free of a master's control sometimes pantomime actions from their past lives, their bones echoing the rote behaviors of their former living selves. The skeleton of a miner might lift a pick and start chipping away at stone walls. The skeleton of a guard might strike up a post at a random doorway. The skeleton of a dragon might lie down on a pile of treasure, while the skeleton of a horse crops grass it can't eat. Left alone in a ballroom, the skeletons of nobles might continue an eternally unfinished dance.
When skeletons encounter living creatures, the necromantic energy that drives them compels them to kill unless they are commanded by their masters to refrain from doing so. They attack without mercy and fight until destroyed, for skeletons possess little sense of self and even less sense of self-preservation.

Undead Nature. A skeleton doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Mass is the tactic: skeletons fight in squads, opening with Shortbows at range (80 ft) since AC 14 and 13 HP make a shield-wall volley more valuable than closing early. Volley for two rounds, then charge as a pack so multiple +5 attacks land per round and opportunity-action coverage traps PCs who back away. Mix archers and swordsmen by situation: archers kite 30 ft backward while sword skeletons engage the first PC into reach, creating a rotate-forward wall the party must break. Focus the weakest isolated target — several skeletons hitting one fighter at AC 15 can drop them in a round. They're mindless under a controller's command and won't retreat, so the GM should spend them freely to bleed resources; on their own, a skeleton reduced to its last few HP still fights to destruction.

name: Slaad Tadpole

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The slaad has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

combat-strategy: These are vermin, not warriors: 7 HP and a +4 bite mean a slaad tadpole should never win a fair fight. Open by burrowing 10 ft into earth or under debris to Hide (Stealth +4, Tiny size), then swarm from concealment at the weakest straggler — target the lone scout, the bound captive, or a sleeping camp — bite once, and burrow away before the target turns. Fight in packs of six or more so that even missing half the attacks drains reactions and chip damage adds up, and use Magic Resistance to shrug off the cantrips and command spells that would otherwise control or kill them instantly. Never let a single tadpole get cornered: its entire survival model is hit, vanish underground, and repeat until the prey is bleeding or the swarm moves on. If exposed more than one round, burrow and flee.

name: Smaug the Golden

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If Smaug fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: Smaug has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Hoard Guardian
traits.description: While on or within 30 ft. of his hoard, Smaug gains +2 to Armor Class and Advantage on saving throws.

traits.name: Impenetrable Scales (Vulnerability)
traits.description: A shot from a Black Arrow, or any attack where the attacker knows the bare patch on his left breast and calls it out, ignores his natural armor bonus.

traits.name: Ageless Malice
traits.description: Smaug can't be surprised while he is on his hoard.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Smaug uses his Frightful Presence. He then makes three attacks: one with his Bite, two with his Claws or Tail.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +17, reach 15 ft. Hit: 27 (4d8 + 9) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +17, reach 10 ft. Hit: 22 (3d8 + 9) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +17, reach 20 ft. Hit: 25 (3d10 + 9) Bludgeoning damage. The target has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Fire Breath (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 24, each creature in a 90-foot Cone. Failure: 77 (22d6) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.

actions.name: Frightful Presence
actions.description: Each creature of Smaug's choice within 120 ft. of him and aware of him must succeed on a DC 22 Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a success or when the effect ends, the creature is immune to his Frightful Presence for 24 hours. No damage.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Claw
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Claw attack.

legendary_actions.name: Tail
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Tail attack.

legendary_actions.name: Flame Lash (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +15, range 90 ft. Hit: 33 (6d10) Fire damage.

legendary_actions.name: Detection
legendary_actions.description: Smaug makes one Perception check.

description: The last great wyrm of the mountain, a golden-scaled tyrant who laid waste to an ancient city and slept upon its gold for a century. vain, eloquent, and utterly without mercy, he considers himself more wise than any elf or man.
combat-strategy: His favorite trick is talking — learning his enemy's fears and plans while circling overhead — then dropping Fire Breath onto the cluster he has just learned is important, and diving to Bite the single survivors.

name: Smoke Mephit

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Cinder Breath
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 11, one creature the mephit can see within 15 feet. Failure: The target has the Blinded condition until the end of the mephit's next turn.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Blinded condition until the end of the mephit's next turn.

traits.name: Death Burst
traits.description: The mephit explodes when it dies. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 11, each creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the mephit. Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn.

description: Smoke mephits are crude, lazy creatures of air and fire that billow smoke constantly. They rarely speak the truth and love to mock and mislead other creatures.
combat-strategy: Open at range with Cinder Breath, Blinding a single target (DC 11 Dex is low) — ideally the party's martial leader or archer — then flutter up 30 ft where blinded foes can't easily reach it. Flyby-style hit-and-run: dive, Claw a squishy, and circle back over obstacles; its 13 HP means one solid hit ends it, so it should never end its turn within melee reach of an unblinded enemy. Blinded targets can't make opportunity attacks against things they can't see, so pair the blind with repositioning: blind the chaser, then kite at 30-ft hover. Fly into a clustered group and let itself be killed on your terms when its HP is nearly gone — Death Burst Poisons whoever finishes it, taxing their next attack rolls. Mephits fight best in packs of four or five, layering blinding breaths and poisoned corpses across the battlefield.

name: Solar

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The solar makes two Flying Sword attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Slaying Bow.

actions.name: Flying Sword
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +15, reach 10 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit: 22 (4d6 + 8) Slashing damage plus 36 (8d8) Radiant damage. Hit or Miss: The sword magically returns to the solar's hand or hovers within 5 feet of the solar immediately after a ranged attack.

actions.name: Slaying Bow
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 21, one creature the solar can see within 600 feet. Failure: If the creature has 100 Hit Points or fewer, it dies. It otherwise takes 24 (4d8 + 6) Piercing damage plus 36 (8d8) Radiant damage.

Failure or Success: The solar can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.
