traits.name: Divine Awareness
traits.description: The solar knows if it hears a lie.

traits.name: Exalted Restoration
traits.description: If the solar dies outside Mount Celestia, its body disappears, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in Mount Celestia.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the solar fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The solar has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
A solar is godlike in its glory and power. On the battlefield, the solar's sword flies into the fray on its own, and a single arrow from a solar's bow can strike a target dead on contact. So great is a solar's celestial might that even demon princes shrink at its resonant commands.
It is said that only twenty-four solars exist. The few solars that are known are stewards of specific deities. The others rest in a state of contemplation, waiting for the time when their services are needed to stave off some cosmic threat to the cause of good.
combat-strategy: Open with action economy dominance: Multiattack two Flying Swords (120-ft range, ~58 damage per hit) while hovering at 50+ ft altitude where nothing reaches it, and replace one attack with Slaying Bow on any hero at 100 HP or fewer — DC 21 Dex or instant death, so save it for the wounded healer or the tank who just got low. Cast Dispel Evil and Good first against fiend-summoning parties, and use Divine Aid as a bonus action to heal or Lesser Restoration an ally each round, making the solar an unkillable anchor for good-aligned forces. Legendary actions every round: Blinking Gaze to permanently blind the party's biggest threat (DC 25) and Radiant Teleport to blink 60 ft away from anyone who finally closes, leaving a 2d10 radiant burst in the arrival space. Truesight 120 nullifies invisibility and disguise, so don't bother sneaking. Save Legendary Resistance for power word kill, imprisonment, and gate effects. A solar rarely routs — it fights to the death or until its mission ends; Exalted Restoration means killing it outside Mount Celestia buys only a reprieve, so make the victory narrative, not numerical.

reactions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, one creature the spectator can see within 120 feet. Failure: 10 (3d6) Force damage.

description:
A spectator is a lesser beholder that is summoned from another plane of existence by a magical ritual, the components of which include four beholder eyestalks that are consumed by the ritual's magic. Appropriately, a spectator has four eyestalks, two on each side of the wide eye at the center of its four-foot diameter body.

Magical Guardians. A summoned spectator guards a location or a treasure of its summoner's choice for 101 years, allowing no creature but its summoner to enter the area or access the item, unless the summoner instructed otherwise. If the item is stolen or destroyed before the years have all passed, a summoned spectator vanishes.
It otherwise never abandons its post.

Glimmers of Madness. Though it can speak, a spectator communicates primarily by way of telepathy. It is civil while on guard, openly discussing its orders and its summoner. However, even a brief conversation with a spectator is enough to reveal quirks in its personality brought on by its years of isolation. It might invent imaginary enemies, refer to itself in the third person, or try to adopt the voice of its summoner.
Like any beholder, a spectator views itself as the epitome of its kind, and it has an intense hatred of other spectators. If two spectators encounter one another, they almost always fight to the death.

Freed from Service. When a spectator has fulfilled its service, it is free to do as it pleases. Many take up residence in the places they previously guarded, especially if their summoners have died. With the spectator's loss of purpose, the flickers of madness it displayed during its servitude flourish.
combat-strategy: Hover in the middle of the room at 20-30 ft altitude, out of easy melee reach, and fire two random Eye Rays per turn — the randomness is the flavor, so lean into it: aim Paralyzing Ray at whoever is mid-climb or mid-cast, Confusion Ray at the martial bruiser (no reactions, no movement, attacking allies is a gift), Fear Ray to peel defenders off the group, and Wounding Ray (16 necrotic) at the tank. Keep 90-ft range and use Spell Reflection as a reaction on the party's heaviest spell, turning their fireball back on themselves for 3d6 force or redirecting it. It's Lawful Neutral, so roleplay it as a curious guardian that escalates slowly — warnings, then rays — and can be talked past. Its spell reflection makes enemies waste spells on it, so bait big magic early, then kite upward through a shaft if cornered; at low HP it flees to its keeper.

name: Specter
languages: Understands Common plus one other language but can't speak

actions.name: Life Drain
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, its Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the damage taken.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.description: The specter can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: While in sunlight, the specter has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls.

description:
A specter is the angry, unfettered spirit of a humanoid that has been prevented from passing to the afterlife. Specters no longer possess connections to who or what they were, yet are condemned to walk the world forever. Some are spawned when dark magic or the touch of a wraith rips a soul from a living body.

Beyond Redemption. When a ghost's unfinished business is completed, it can rest at last. No such rest or redemption awaits a specter. It is doomed to the Material Plane, its only end the oblivion that comes with the destruction of its soul. Until then, it bears out its lonely life in forlorn places, carrying on forgotten through the ages of the world.

Undying Hatred. Living creatures remind the specter that life is beyond its grasp. The mere sight of the living overwhelms a specter with sorrow and wrath, which can be abated only by destroying said life. A specter kills quickly and mercilessly, for only by depriving others of life can it gain the slightest satisfaction. However, no matter how many lives it extinguishes, a specter always succumbs to its hatred and sorrow.

Dwellers in Darkness. Sunlight represents a source of life that no specter can ever hope to douse, and it pains them. When night falls, they leave their final resting places in search of living creatures to slay, knowing that few weapons can harm them in return. At the first light of dawn, they retreat back into the darkness, where they remain until night falls again.

Undead Nature. A specter doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Fight at night or underground (sunlight Disadvantage ruins it), phasing through walls, doors, and creatures with Incorporeal Movement to reach the back line, then Life Drain repeatedly on one target — the HP maximum drain is the kill mechanic, so focus a single PC round after round rather than spreading damage, since a specter's 22 damage of drain can erase a fighter's pool in three hits. It passes through shields and armor of bodies, so position by passing through a frontline fighter to reach the healer behind them (accepting 5 force for ending inside an object only if lethal). Hover 50-ft fly lets it disengage upward through a ceiling when hurt. Avoid radiant-damage clerics and holy ground; if a PC starts swinging radiant, shift to harassing other targets or phase into a sealed crypt where the party can't follow. A specter reduced below ~8 HP should sink into a wall and flee to haunt another day.

name: Sphinx of Lore

lair_actions:
Sphinxes typically dwell in places that hold great knowledge or prophetic magic.

The region containing a sphinx of lore's or sphinx of valor's lair is altered by its presence, creating the following effects:

Distant Sight. While in its lair, the sphinx can cast Clairvoyance, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as its Spellcasting action. When cast this way, the spell's range is 1 mile.
Infusion of Knowledge. Whenever the sphinx or one of its allies takes a Study action while within 1 mile of the lair, it adds 1d6 to any ability check it makes for that action.

If the sphinx dies or moves its lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately.

traits.name: Inscrutable
traits.description: No magic can observe the sphinx remotely or detect its thoughts without its permission. Wisdom (Insight) checks made to ascertain its intentions or sincerity are made with Disadvantage.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the sphinx fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

combat-strategy: This guardian wants to be asked nicely: begin with negotiation, riddles, and tests of worth, and fight only those who draw steel or steal its books. When combat starts, open with Mind-Rending Roar (300 ft, DC 16) the moment enemies cluster — 35 psychic plus Incapacitated for a round is the entire fight's tempo shift, then Multiattack three Claws on the Incapacitated targets with automatic critical potential against helpless foes if your table applies it. Use legendary actions to delete the caster's night: Weight of Years one round for permanent Exhaustion stacking (no save repeat, 120-ft range), Arcane Prowl to teleport behind whoever breaks formation and Claw them. Truesight 120 sees through every illusion and shapechange, so it never wastes actions misidentifying foes. Hold Legendary Resistance for banishment, domination, and feeblemind. It doesn't retreat from intruders it deems worthy of punishment, but if a Plane Shift becomes necessary to end a threat, use it; below ~40 HP it teleports deeper into its library to defend the inner vault.

name: Sphinx of Secrets

actions.name: Multiattack

actions.name: Claw

The cursed target has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls. In addition, if it takes the Action, it must succeed on a DC 15 Intelligence saving throw or that action is wasted. The cursed target can take a Study action to make a DC 15 Intelligence check, solving the riddle and ending the curse on a success. The curse ends early if the sphinx curses another target.
actions.save_effect: The target takes 21 (6d6) Psychic damage and is cursed with a riddle. The cursed target has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls. If it takes the Action, it must succeed on a DC 15 Intelligence saving throw or that action is wasted. The cursed target can take a Study action to make a DC 15 Intelligence check, solving the riddle and ending the curse on a success. The curse ends early if the sphinx curses another target.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The sphinx casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15): At Will: Detect Magic, Identify, Prestidigitation; 1/Day Each: Locate Object, Remove Curse

combat-strategy: Open with Curse of the Riddle on the party's most reliable attacker or caster — Disadvantage on all checks and attacks plus wasted actions on failed saves cripples one hero completely, and only a Study action or a new curse lifts it. Rotate the curse: if a second hero proves dangerous, curse them to shed it from the first, so the sphinx is always neutering the biggest current threat while Multiattack (two Claws plus the curse, or three Claws) punishes the rest. It has no Legendary Resistance, so Magic Resistance is its only defense against save-or-suck — spread the party's control spells thin by staying mobile with 60-ft flight, hovering above staircases and balconies. Fight at range near riddle-gates and locked doors, using the terrain as a negotiation prop. It fights defensively to protect its secrets, withdrawing through a Plane Shift-style escape route it alone knows (or into a hidden vault) when reduced below ~50 HP or when the intruders prove too strong to simply wear down.

Sphinxes typically dwell in places that hold great knowledge or prophetic magic.

The region containing a sphinx of lore's or sphinx of valor's lair is altered by its presence, creating the following effects:

Distant Sight. While in its lair, the sphinx can cast Clairvoyance, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as its Spellcasting action. When cast this way, the spell's range is 1 mile.

combat-strategy: Sequence the Roars deliberately: Multiattack includes Roar every turn, so the first Roar Frightens the entire party (DC 20, 500 ft) to scatter them, the second Paralyzes those who fail, and the third hits with 44 thunder plus Prone — plan the fight so the party has crossed open ground by round three when the save-or-die hammer drops. Multiattack's two Claws (+12, 20 damage) should finish paralyzed or prone targets, and legendary Claw attacks from Arcane Prowl teleports punish anyone who breaks cover. Weight of Years stacks Exhaustion on the tank or the martial who refuses to run, degrading them permanently over the fight. Keep flying at altitude between attacks — 60-ft flight over cliffs, spires, or battlements means fleeing is optional and charging is telegraphed. Save Legendary Resistance for banishment, power word kill, and hold effects. It tests rather than slaughters: it may halt a fight to spare heroes who show courage, but below ~40 HP against a party failing its saves repeatedly, it presses the advantage relentlessly rather than retreating.

name: Sphinx of Wonder

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Radiant damage.

reactions.name: Burst of Ingenuity
reactions.trigger: The sphinx or another creature within 30 feet makes an ability check or a saving throw.
reactions.description: The sphinx adds 2 to the roll.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The sphinx has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

combat-strategy: A Tiny, 24-HP companion is not a front-line fighter: stay behind allies or aloft with 40-ft fly, using Rend (+5, radiant) only against weak or already-engaged foes, and pop in and out of melee since its STR 6 trades nothing. The Burst of Ingenuity reaction (+2 to a roll) is its real combat contribution — spend it to save a falling ally, boost a partner's crucial attack or save, or nudge its own Stealth +5 check to break line of sight when threatened. Magic Resistance lets it shrug off the charm and control spells that would normally retire a Tiny celestial, so it can hover within caster range with some confidence. Its tactic is support and survival: hide behind armor, boost the hero, fly to cover when spells fly, and never let itself become the target — if the fight turns lethal (below ~8 HP), hide (Tiny size + Stealth +5) and wait it out.

name: Spider

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) Poison damage.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The spider can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

traits.name: Web Walker
traits.description: The spider ignores movement restrictions caused by webs, and the spider knows the location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

combat-strategy: Ambush predator: web up corridors and doorways (Web Walker means it ignores its own webs and knows the position of anything touching them), then wait on ceilings with Spider Climb and Stealth +4 for prey to blunder into the silk. Drop onto an entangled target and Bite — the damage is trivial (1 + poison), so the spider's fight is about the web alarm and attrition, not hit points: 1 HP means any attention kills it. Use it as the tripwire in a giant-spider or drider lair: any disturbance alerts the ones that matter. In swarms, drop from above onto isolated PCs, bite, and retreat up the wall before the target swings — 20-ft climb on walls and ceilings makes a grounded fighter miss every counter. It flees instantly from fire, area damage, or anyone who cuts the web.

name: Spined Devil

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The devil makes two attacks, using Infernal Fork and Tail Spine in any combination.

actions.name: Infernal Fork
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Fire damage.

actions.name: Tail Spine
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 20/80 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Fire damage.

traits.name: Flyby
traits.description: The devil doesn't provoke an Opportunity Attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The devil has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
Smaller than most other devils, spinagons act as messengers and spies for greater devils and archdevils. They are the eyes and ears of the Nine Hells, and even fiends that despise a spined devil's weakness treat it with a modicum of respect.
A spined devil's body and tail bristle with spines, and it can fling its tail spines as ranged weapons. The spines burst into flame on impact. When not delivering messages or gathering intelligence, spined devils serve in the infernal legions as flying artillery, making up for their relative weakness by mobbing together to overwhelm their foes. Though they crave promotion and power, spined devils are craven by nature, and they will quickly scatter if a fight goes against them.
combat-strategy: Exploit Flyby: hover just inside 20-ft Tail Spine range, Multiattack fork-plus-spine, then fly straight out of every enemy's reach without provoking — the fight should be a yo-yo the party can never pin. Tail Spine for the ranged poke (fire damage stacks with the fork's fire if both hit the same target), Infernal Fork when a foe steps adjacent on their turn as it backs off. Magic Resistance means save-or-suck spells bounce off, so it can hover over hazardous terrain (lava trenches, chasms) confident that banishment and burns are unlikely to stick. Bully low-AC targets and devils obey hierarchy: follow a bearded or barbed devil's orders and cover allies. Retreat upward behind smoke, flame curtains, or the protection of bigger devils when below ~15 HP, or dive into lava where non-flyers can't follow (devils have fire resistance in most lairs).

name: Spirit Naga

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The naga makes three attacks, using Bite or Necrotic Ray in any combination.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Necrotic Ray
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +6, range 60 ft. Hit: 21 (6d6) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The naga casts one of the following spells, requiring no Somatic or Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14): At Will: Detect Magic, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Water Breathing; 2/Day Each: Detect Thoughts, Dimension Door, Hold Person (level 3 version), Lightning Bolt (level 4 version)

traits.name: Fiendish Restoration
traits.description: If it dies, the naga returns to life in 1d6 days and regains all its Hit Points. Only a Wish spell can prevent this trait from functioning.

description: Spirit nagas live in gloom and spitefulness, constantly plotting vengeance against creatures that have wronged them-or that they believe have wronged them. Lairing in dismal caverns and ruins, they devote their time to developing new spells and enslaving the mortals with which they surround themselves. A spirit naga likes to charm its foes, drawing them close so that it can sink its poisonous fangs into their flesh.
combat-strategy: Open with the save-or-suck you actually have: Cast Lightning Bolt (level 4, 2/Day) into the tightest formation first, then Hold Person (level 3, DC 14) on the biggest martial threat — a held target means auto-criticals for the naga's three-attack Multiattack next turn. Bite (14 poison each) finishes held or prone foes at 10-ft reach while Necrotic Ray (60 ft, no save) pokes the back line from beyond melee. Hover at range and use Dimension Door to blink behind walls or onto high perches when the party charges, reappearing to bite the isolated caster, then dimension door out again — 40-ft walk plus two daily teleports makes it nearly uncatchable. Detect Thoughts (2/Day) reads the party's intentions before negotiations or ambushes. It never fights to the death: Fiendish Restoration means it returns in 1d6 days anyway, so disengage via Dimension Door at low HP or when outmatched, vanishing with its secrets to plague the party again later.

name: Sprite

actions.name: Needle Sword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Enchanting Bow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +6, range 40/160 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage, and the target has the Charmed condition until the start of the sprite's next turn.

actions.name: Heart Sight
actions.description: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 10, one creature within 5 feet the sprite can see (Celestials, Fiends, and Undead automatically fail the save). Failure: The sprite knows the target's emotions and alignment.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The sprite knows the target's emotions and alignment.

actions.name: Invisibility
actions.description: The sprite casts Invisibility on itself, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability.

description:
In secret groves and shaded glens, tiny sprites with dragonfly wings flutter. For all their fey splendor, however, sprites lack warmth and compassion. They are aggressive and hardy warriors, taking severe measures to ward strangers away from their homes. Interlopers that come too close have their moral character judged, then are put to sleep or frightened off.

Forest Protectors. Sprites build little villages in the boughs of trees and willing treants, in verdant glades brightened by moss, wild flowers, and toadstools. Wild nature thrives, and the sprites allow no trespassers. When intruders are spotted, the sprites lead them astray with ominous rustling from the bushes and distant snapping twigs. Creatures foolish enough to persist in intruding on a sprite's territory are stung with poisoned arrows and lulled into a senseless sleep. While they slumber, the sprites make good their escape, retreating to an even more secluded area of the forest.

Heart Seers. Sprites can sense whether a creature is good or evil by the sound and feeling of its beating heart. Weighing the balance of a creature's past actions, a sprite can tell whether its heart beats rapidly in love or flags in sorrow, or whether it is darkened by hate or greed. The sprite's power to perceive the heart always shows the truth, because the heart can't lie.

Poison Brewers. In their forest domains, sprites brew toxins, unguents, antidotes, and poisons, including the sleep poison with which they coat their arrows. They venture far into the woods to harvest rare flowers, mosses, and fungi, sometimes crossing dangerous territory to do so. If desperate, sprites even steal their ingredients from the gardens of hags.

Good-Hearted. Because they are judges of the heart and favor good creatures, sprites oppose the will of evil fey and pledge to thwart evil archfey at every turn. If they encounter adventurers on a quest to rid their forest of an evil fey creature or goblinoid menace, they will pledge their support and even come to their aid when the adventurers least expect it.
Unlike pixies, sprites rarely indulge in frivolous merriment and fun. They are firm warriors, protectors, and judges, and their stern bent causes other fey to consider them overly dour and serious. However, fey that respect the sprites' territory find them staunch allies in times of trouble.
combat-strategy: Sprites open with Invisibility, then snipe with Enchanting Bow from behind cover or above, since its 40-ft. fly and +8 Stealth make it nearly impossible to pin down. Prioritize lone or front-line humanoids: one Charmed target at a time turns the party's own weapons against them while the sprite stays out of reach. Sequence a bow shot to Charm, then either withdraw or let the charmed ally create space; re-cast Invisibility before attacking again since the spell doesn't require components. Use Heart Sight on captured or suspicious NPCs (celestials, fiends, and undead fail automatically) outside combat rather than in a fight. At 10 hp it must flee the moment an area effect or an invisible-detection trick lands—Dash upward with fly speed and vanish again.

name: Spy

actions.name: Shortsword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Hand Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 30/120 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage.

bonus_actions.name: Cunning Action
bonus_actions.description: The spy takes the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.

description: Rulers, nobles, merchants, guild masters ,and other wealthy individuals use spies to gain the upper hand in a world of cutthroat politics. A spy is trained to secretly gather information. Loyal spies would rather die than divulge information that could compromise them or their employers
combat-strategy: A Spy never picks fair fights: it fights only when ambush, poison, and escape routes are pre-planned. Open from hiding with the Hand Crossbow's poison bolts (+4, 30 ft.), then use Cunning Action to Hide or Disengage every turn, kiting through crowds, rooftops, or climbable walls it knows better than the party. Target isolated stragglers or spellcasters whose concentration breaks easily, and stack the 2d6 poison on anyone already wounded. If outnumbered, cornered, or revealed by true sight or good Perception (its Stealth +6 loses to passive checks above ~16), flee immediately—its job is intelligence, and a live spy escaping is worth more than a dead one.

name: Spy Master

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The spy makes three attacks, using Rapier or Hand Crossbow in any combination.

actions.name: Rapier
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Hand Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +9, range 30/120 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) Poison damage.

actions.name: Smoke Bomb
actions.description: The spy throws a bomb to a point it can see within 30 feet of itself. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 16, each creature in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point. Failure: 28 (8d6) Poison damage, and the target has the Blinded condition until the end of the spy's next turn. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: 28 (8d6) Poison damage, and the target has the Blinded condition until the end of the spy's next turn. Success: Half damage only

bonus_actions.name: Cunning Action
bonus_actions.description: The spy takes the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.

combat-strategy: The Spy Master wants open ground and range: open at 60-120 ft. with poisoned Hand Crossbows (12+9 damage per bolt), using Cunning Action to stay behind cover or elevated perches where its +13 Stealth and 21 passive Perception control engagement. Save Smoke Bomb for the moment melee closes or the party bunches up: DC 16 Con for 28 poison damage and Blinded until its next turn lets it Multiattack blinded targets at full accuracy, then Disengage away. Prioritize squishy back-line casters and anyone who has already failed the smoke save; 137 hp and AC 19 let it survive a round of punishment but its 12 Con means focus fire hurts. If disarmed of cover, out-flown, or Smoke Bomb is spent and brutes close in, use Cunning Action Dash to escape through pre-scouted climbable routes.

name: Steam Mephit

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 2 (1d4) Slashing damage plus 2 (1d4) Fire damage.

actions.name: Steam Breath
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 10, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: 5 (2d4) Fire damage, and the target's Speed decreases by 10 feet until the end of the mephit's next turn. Success: Half damage only. Failure or Success: Being underwater doesn't grant Resistance to this Fire damage.
actions.save_effect: 5 (2d4) Fire damage, and the target's Speed decreases by 10 feet until the end of the mephit's next turn. Success: Half damage only. Failure or Success: Being underwater doesn't grant Resistance to this Fire damage

traits.name: Blurred Form
traits.description: Attack rolls against the mephit are made with Disadvantage unless the mephit has the Incapacitated condition.

traits.name: Death Burst
traits.description: The mephit explodes when it dies. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 10, each creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the mephit. Failure: 5 (2d4) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.

description: Composed of fire and water, steam mephits leave trails of hot water wherever they go, and they hiss with tendrils of steam. Bossy and hypersensitive, they are the self­ appointed overlords of all mephits.
combat-strategy: Steam Mephits are kamikaze artillery: fly in, breathe Steam Breath (15-ft. cone, DC 10 Con) down corridors or over clustered foes to burn and slow them, then let enemies close and die explosively—Death Burst punishes anyone who finishes it in melee. Blurred Form's inherent attack disadvantage makes it tankier than 17 hp suggests, so fight in the open where allies can't pin it. Group them in clouds and have them dive through enemy ranks, cone-breathing as they pass; slowed targets can't chase the 30-ft. flyers away. Use claws only opportunistically, and deliberately let them detonate on top of the party's front line once their cones have landed.

name: Stirge

actions.name: Proboscis
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage, and the stirge attaches to the target. While attached, the stirge can't make Proboscis attacks, and the target takes 5 (2d4) Necrotic damage at the start of each of the stirge's turns. The stirge can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement. The target or a creature within 5 feet of it can detach the stirge as an action.

description:
This horrid flying creature looks like a cross between a large bat and an oversized mosquito. Its legs end in sharp pincers, and its long, needle-like proboscis slashes the air as it seeks its next meal.
Stirges feed on the blood of living creatures, attaching and draining them slowly. Although they pose little danger in small numbers, packs of stirges can be a formidable threat, reattaching as quickly as their weakening prey can pluck them off.

Blood Drain. A stirge attacks by landing on a victim, finding a vulnerable spot, and plunging its proboscis into the flesh while using its pincer legs to latch on to the victim. Once the stirge has sated itself, it detaches and flies off to digest its meal.
combat-strategy: Stirges swarm from darkness: they have 60-ft. darkvision, 40-ft. flight, and only 5 hp, so attack at night or in caves in packs of six or more, dive-biting to attach (+5, 6 piercing). An attached stirge deals 5 necrotic automatic damage each of its turns, and halving the party's actions to peel them off is the real trap—let attached stirges ride and feed while unattached ones pick new victims. Target lone porters, sentries, and spellcasters whose concentration breaks when they waste actions on removal. Flying at 40 ft. makes them hard to reach; circle-back dive attacks from above work best. When the pack is down to a couple of survivors and the party has cleared attachments, flee into tight cracks no humanoid can follow.

name: Stone Giant

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The giant makes two attacks, using Stone Club or Boulder in any combination.

actions.name: Stone Club
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 15 ft. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Boulder
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +9, range 60/240 ft. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

reactions.name: Deflect Missile
reactions.trigger: The giant is hit by a ranged attack roll and takes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage from it.
reactions.description: The giant reduces the damage it takes from the attack by 11 (1d10 + 6), and if that damage is reduced to 0, the giant can redirect some of the attack's force. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 17, one creature the giant can see within 60 feet. Failure: 11 (1d10 + 6) Force damage.

description:
Stone giants are reclusive, quiet, and peaceful as long as they are left alone. Their granite-gray skin, gaunt features, and black, sunken eyes endow stone giants with a stern countenance. They are private creatures, hiding their lives and art away from the world.

Inhabitants of a Stone World. Secluded caves are the homes of the stone giants. Cavern networks are their towns, rocky tunnels their roads, and underground streams their waterways. Isolated mountain ranges are their continents, with the vast spans of land between seen as oceans that the stone giants only rarely cross.
In their dark, quiet caves, stone giants wordlessly chip away at elaborate carvings, measuring time in the echoing drip of water into cavern pools. In the deepest chambers of a stone giant settlement, far from the chittering of bats or the patrols paced out by the giants' cave bear companions, are holy places where silence and darkness are complete. Stone takes on its most sacred quality in these cavern cathedrals, their buttresses and columns carved with a beauty that shames the legendary stonecraft of the dwarves.

Carvers and Seers. Among stone giants, artistry ranks as the greatest virtue. They create intricate murals, paint sprawling murals across cavern walls, and indulge in a wide variety of other artistic disciplines. They esteem stone carving as the greatest of skills.
Stone giants strive to draw shapes out of raw stone, which they believe reveal meaning inspired by their god, Skoraeus Stonebones. The giants appoint the tribe's best carvers as their leaders, shamans, and prophets. The holy hands of such giants become the hands of the god as they work.

Graceful Athletes. Despite their great size and musculature, stone giants are lithe and graceful. Skilled rock throwers are granted positions of high rank in the giants' ordning, testing and demonstrating their ability to hurl and catch enormous boulders. Such giants take the front ranks when a tribe has cause to defend its home or attack its enemies. However, even in combat, artistry is key. A stone giant hurling a rock performs not just a feat of brute strength but also one of stunning athleticism and poise.

Dreamers under Sky. Stone giants view the world outside their underground homes as a realm of dreams where nothing is entirely true or real. They behave in the surface world the way humanoids might behave in their own dreams, making little account for their actions and never fully trusting what they see or hear. A promise made above ground need not be kept. Insults can be made without apology. Killing prey or sentient beings is no cause for guilt in the dreaming world beneath the sky.
Stone giants lacking in athletic grace or artistic skill dwell at the fringes of their society, serving as the tribe's outlying guardians and far-wandering hunters. When trespassers stray too far into the mountain territory of a stone giant clan, those guardians greet them with hurled rocks and showers of splintered stone. Survivors of such encounters spread tales of stone giant violence, never realizing how little those brutes dwelling in the unreal dreaming world resemble their quiet and artistic kin.
combat-strategy: Stone Giants dominate vertical terrain: hurl Boulders (+9, 60/240 ft., knocks Large or smaller Prone) from hilltops or cliff edges where the party must climb to reach it. Multiattack is two Stone Club swings (22 bludgeoning each, 15-ft. reach) once foes close—keep knocked-down targets prone by attacking them first since melee attacks against prone are advantaged for its allies too. Use Deflect Missile reactively on archers and casters, and when the redirect triggers, fling the redirected force back at the same ranged attacker to punish volleys. Grapple and hurl is a classic: Athletics +12 lets it grab a foe and toss them off a ledge. If forced onto flat ground against a full party, back away throwing boulders, then retreat to higher rock where its 40-ft. speed and throwing range keep it untouchable.

name: Stone Golem
languages: Understands Common plus two other languages but can't speak

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The golem makes two attacks, using Slam or Force Bolt in any combination.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 5 ft. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) Bludgeoning damage plus 9 (2d8) Force damage.

actions.name: Force Bolt
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +9, range 120 ft. Hit: 22 (4d10) Force damage.

bonus_actions.name: Slow
bonus_actions.description: The golem casts the Slow spell, requiring no spell components and using Constitution as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17).

traits.name: Immutable Form
traits.description: The golem can't shape-shift.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The golem has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
Stone golems display great variety i n shape and form, cut and chiseled from stone to appear as tall, impressive statues. Though most bear humanoid features, stone golems can be carved in any form the sculptor can imagine. Ancient stone golems found in sealed tombs or flanking the gates of lost cities sometimes take the forms of giant beasts.
Like other golems, stone golems are nearly impervious to spells and ordinary weapons. Creatures that fight a stone golem can feel the ebb and flow of time slow down around them, almost as though they were made of stone themselves.
combat-strategy: Stone Golems are relentless objective-tanks that never maneuver: walk straight at the highest-priority target, Multiattacking Slam (force damage ignores most resistances) or Force Bolt (120 ft., 22 force) at casters hiding behind cover. Open with Slow (bonus action, DC 17 Con) on the martial brutes to halve their speed and strip their reactions, then wade in on half-speed foes who can't kite its 30-ft. walk. Magic Resistance advantage on spell saves makes banishment and hold spells poor bets—bait them out; only nonmagical attacks and its 9 Dex are exploitable, so it can safely charge through spellfire. Target the party's healer and conjurer first with Force Bolts, then grind whoever stands in front. It never retreats unless its creator commands; its 220 hp and AC 18 are the plan.

name: Storm Giant

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The giant makes two attacks, using Storm Sword or Thunderbolt in any combination.

actions.name: Storm Sword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +14, reach 10 ft. Hit: 23 (4d6 + 9) Slashing damage plus 13 (3d8) Lightning damage.

actions.name: Thunderbolt
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +14, range 500 ft. Hit: 22 (2d12 + 9) Lightning damage, and the target has the Blinded and Deafened conditions until the start of the giant's next turn.

actions.name: Lightning Storm
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 18, each creature in a 10-foot-radius, 40-foot-high Cylinder originating from a point the giant can see within 500 feet. Failure: 55 (10d10) Lightning damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: 55 (10d10) Lightning damage. Success: Half damage

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The giant casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 18): At Will: Detect Magic, Light 1/Day: Control Weather

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: The giant can breathe air and water.

description:
Storm giants are contemplative seers that live in places far removed from mortal civilization. Most have pale purple-gray skin and hair, and glittering emerald eyes. Some rare storm giants are violet-skinned, with deep violet or blue-black hair and silvery gray or purple eyes. They are benevolent and wise unless angered, in response to which the fury of a storm giant can affect the fate of thousands.

Distant Prophet-Kings. Storm giants live in isolated refuges so far above the surface of the world or below the sea that they are beyond the reach of most other creatures. Some make their abodes in cloud-top castles so high that flying dragons appear as specks below. Others live atop mountain peaks that pierce the clouds. Some occupy palaces covered with algae and coral at the bottom of the ocean, or grim fortresses in undersea rifts.

Detached Oracles. Storm giants recall the glory of ancient giant empires forged by the god Annam. They seek to restore what was lost when those empires fell. They don't compete for status in the ordning but live out the centuries of their existence in contemplative seclusion, watching the starry heavens and the ocean's depths for signs, symbols, and omens of Annam's favor.
Storm giants see the events of the world in a wide perspective. They can foretell the rise and fall of kings and empires, see the beginnings and ends of fortune and disaster, and find the patterns within seemingly unrelated events. By reading omens and prophesying, storm giants learn of vast secrets previously unknown and troves of lore utterly forgotten.
Kings will rise and fall, wars will be won and lost, and good and evil will wrestle in conflict. Storm giants have watched these events in the manner of mortal gods over many lifetimes, and they know it is pointless to intervene. Even so, a storm giant might willingly disclose certain secrets to benevolent beings that visit its remote domain with specific purpose. Such creatures must speak and act respectfully, however, for a storm giant roused to anger is a force of utter destruction.

Solitary Lives. Storm giants communicate infrequently with others of their kind. They do so usually to compare signs and omens or engage in a rare courtship. Storm giant parents stay together to raise a child to maturity, then return to the solitary isolation they cherish.
Some humanoid cultures worship storm giants as they would worship lesser gods, creating myths and stories around the giants' exploits and vast knowledge. A storm giant is governed by the dictates of its conscience, however, and not by any culture's laws or codes of honor. As such, a storm giant that bends its mind toward greed or gains a taste for petty power can easily become a terrible threat.
combat-strategy: Storm Giants open with Control Weather to summon a hurricane, then Lightning Storm (DC 18, 55 lightning in a 10-ft. cylinder, 500 ft. away) on the densest cluster of foes. Thunderbolt (+14, 500 ft.) single-targets casters and blinds plus deafens them, shutting down verbal components and spell targeting—chain these on anyone who flies or hovers near. Its 50-ft. swim and fly-hover let it fight from the sea or sky where melee can't reach, so drag naval battles onto open water where its swimming pace outclasses most boats. Melee Storm Sword (36 average damage, 10-ft. reach) is for brutes who close in; its grapples and trampling bulk punish anyone who stays adjacent. Its 30-ft. truesight negates invisibility, so rogues can't flank it. Retreat only when its hit points dip below ~60 and the party shows dispel or banishment capacity—dive underwater and vanish into the depths.

name: Succubus

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The succubus makes one Fiendish Touch attack and uses Charm or Draining Kiss.

actions.name: Fiendish Touch
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Charm
actions.description: The succubus casts Dominate Person (level 8 version), requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15).
actions.save_effect: The target is charmed until the spell ends. The charmed target regards the succubus as a trusted ally; domination and command-control are GM-enforced (charmed is the mechanical marker; no automatic-control subsystem).

actions.name: Draining Kiss
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 15, one creature Charmed by the succubus within 5 feet. Failure: 13 (3d8) Psychic damage. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: The target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the damage taken.
actions.save_effect: 13 (3d8) Psychic damage. Success: Half damage. Failure or Success: The target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the damage taken

bonus_actions.name: Shape-Shift
bonus_actions.description: The succubus shape-shifts into a Medium or Small Humanoid, or it returns to its true form. Its game statistics are the same in each form, except its Fly Speed is available only in its true form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

traits.name: Incubus Form
traits.description: When the succubus finishes a Long Rest, it can shape-shift into an Incubus, using that stat block instead of this one.

combat-strategy: Succubi never start a fair fight: infiltrate in humanoid form via Shape-Shift, separate a lonely target socially, then Charm (Dominate Person, DC 15) to turn a party member into a meat shield. In combat, Multiattack Fiendish Touch plus Draining Kiss on the Charmed victim (13 psychic + permanent max-HP reduction) grinds down its thrall while flying 60 ft. keeps it out of melee reach. Use the charmed ally's body to block opportunity attacks and spell lines, commanding it to attack its friends—harm lets them reroll the save, so keep domination comfortable until the fight is won. Fiendish Touch's 16 psychic damages psychic-weak casters; hit and fly away each turn. If outnumbered, out-buffed, or her save is failing, flee the Material Plane entirely—she'll return with a better plan and a new victim.

name: Succubus/Incubus
damage_resistances: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical weapons

actions.name: Claw (Fiend Form Only)
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.

actions.name: Charm
actions.description:
One humanoid the fiend can see within 30 feet of it must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be magically charmed for 1 day. The charmed target obeys the fiend's verbal or telepathic commands. If the target suffers any harm or receives a suicidal command, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on a success. If the target successfully saves against the effect, or if the effect on it ends, the target is immune to this fiend's Charm for the next 24 hours.
The fiend can have only one target charmed at a time. If it charms another, the effect on the previous target ends.
actions.save_effect: The target is magically charmed for 1 day. Success: The target is immune to this effect for the next 24 hours.

actions.name: Draining Kiss
actions.description: The fiend kisses a creature charmed by it or a willing creature. The target must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw against this magic, taking 32 (5d10 + 5) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The target's hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0.
actions.save_effect: 32 (5d10 + 5) psychic damage. Success: Half damage.

actions.name: Etherealness
actions.description: The fiend magically enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa.

traits.name: Telepathic Bond
traits.description: The fiend ignores the range restriction on its telepathy when communicating with a creature it has charmed. The two don't even need to be on the same plane of existence.

traits.name: Shapechanger
traits.description: The fiend can use its action to polymorph into a Small or Medium humanoid, or back into its true form. Without wings, the fiend loses its flying speed. Other than its size and speed, its statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

description:
Succubi and incubi inhabit all of the Lower Planes, and the lascivious dark-winged fiends can be found in service to devils, demons, night hags, rakshasas, and yugoloths. Asmodeus, ruler of the Nine Hells, uses these fiends to tempt mortals to perform evil acts. The demon lord Graz'zt keeps succubi and incubi as advisers and consorts.
Though legend speaks of them separately, any succubus can become an incubus, and vice versa. Most of these fiends do have a preference for one form or the other. Mortals only rarely see a succubus or incubus in its true form, however, for the fiend typically begins its corruption in veiled, insidious ways.

Beautiful Corrupters. A succubus or incubus first appears in ethereal form, passing through walls like a ghost to lurk next to a mortal's bedside and whisper forbidden pleasures. Sleeping victims are tempted to give in to their darkest desires, indulge in taboos, and feed forbidden appetites. As the fiend fills the victim's dreams with debauched images, the victim becomes more susceptible to temptation in everyday life.
Inevitably, the fiend enters the mortal realm in tempting form to directly influence a creature's actions. Appearing in the guise of a humanoid who has previously appeared only in the victim's dreams, the succubus or incubus seduces or befriends its victim, indulging all its desires so that it performs evil acts of its own free will.
A mortal bequeaths its soul to the fiend not by formal pledge or contract. Instead, when a succubus or incubus has corrupted a creature completely-some say by causing the victim to commit the three betrayals of thought, word, and deed-the victim's soul belongs to the fiend. The more virtuous the fiend's prey, the longer the corruption takes, but the more rewarding the downfall. After successfully corrupting a victim, the succubus or incubus kills it, and the tainted soul descends into the Lower Planes.
The succubus or incubus resorts to charming a victim magically only when necessary, usually as a form of self-defense. A charmed creature isn't responsible for its actions, so forcing it to behave against its will won't bring the fiend closer to the ultimate prize: the victim's soul.

Deadly Kiss. The kiss of a succubus or incubus is an echo of the emptiness that is the fiend's longing for a corrupted soul. Likewise, the recipient of the fiend's kiss gains no satisfaction from it, experiencing only pain and the profound emptiness that the fiend imparts. The kiss is nothing short of an attack, usually delivered as a final farewell before the fiend escapes.

Fiendish Offspring. Succubi and incubi can reproduce with one another to spawn more of their kind. Less commonly, a succubus or incubus reproduces with a humanoid. From this unholy union, a cambion child is conceived. Invariably, the fiendish offspring is as wicked as its fiendish parent.
combat-strategy: This classic fiend is an infiltrator who win combat before it starts: shapechange into a trusted humanoid, Charm a lonely or lonely-hearted target (DC 15 Wis, 1 day, telepathically commanded across planes), and use them as an agent or shield before ever rolling initiative. In a fight, Charm first, then Draining Kiss the charmed target for 32 psychic plus max-HP drain each round—harm lets them reroll, so command the thrall to interpose itself and take attacks instead. Etherealness is the escape hatch and the sneak-in tool: slip through walls to strike, then fade out when the party focuses fire. Claw only as a last resort (6 damage is trivial). When the charmed thrall falls, its save immunity timer, or dispel magic appears, retreat to the Ethereal Plane and resurface elsewhere—dead drops and hostages are worth more than a fight.

name: Sun Wukong
languages: All; speaks to animals and spirits; telepathy 60 ft.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If Sun Wukong fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: Sun Wukong has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: 72 Transformations
traits.description: Sun Wukong can cast Shapechange at will, limited to beasts, humanoids, and monstrosities of his size or smaller; he can also turn invisible as a Bonus Action.

traits.name: Fiery Golden Eyes
traits.description: Sun Wukong sees through Illusions and shapeshifts, and he has Advantage on saving throws against being Blinded.

traits.name: Immortal Body
traits.description: Sun Wukong doesn't age and cannot die of disease; a wish or divine decree is required to unmake him permanently.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Sun Wukong makes three attacks with the Ruyi Jingu Bang (the golden-club) or one attack with the club and two hair-clone strikes.

actions.name: Ruyi Jingu Bang
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 10 ft. Hit: 25 (3d10 + 9) Bludgeoning damage. The target has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Hair Clone Strike
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 5 ft. Hit: 20 (2d10 + 9) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Pluck a Hair (1/Day)
actions.description: Sun Wukong plucks a handful of hairs and breathes on them. Four monkey clones spring forth in unoccupied spaces within 60 ft. Each clone is a monkey-clone token: AC 18, 30 Hit Points, +14 to hit for 11 (2d8 + 2) Bludgeoning damage, acting on Wukong's initiative. A clone dies when it takes damage and a wish can't duplicate this trick.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Club
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Ruyi Jingu Bang attack.

legendary_actions.name: Somersault Leap
legendary_actions.description: Sun Wukong flies up to his full fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

legendary_actions.name: Locking Word (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 24, one creature within 60 ft. Failure: the target is unable to move, take Reactions, or speak until the start of Wukong's next turn. Success: no effect. No damage.

description: The Great Sage Equaling Heaven, a stone-born monkey trickster and immortal warrior, who waged war on heaven itself, and learned only to laugh while doing it.
combat-strategy: He fights airborne and invisible, splitting into hair-clones to multiply his golden club, and uses Locking Word on the biggest caster at the worst possible moment.

name: Swarm of Bats

actions.name: Bites
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (2d4) Piercing damage, or 2 (1d4) Piercing damage if the swarm is Bloodied.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny bat. The swarm can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

combat-strategy: Bats swarm from darkness: they roost in caves and ruins with 60-ft. blindsight, then descend on intruders in a Mass of Bites (+4, 5 piercing). Fly through occupied spaces rather than around them, moving 30 ft. each turn to bite and reposition so melee attackers can't cleanly target without risking the shoving match of a swarm in their faces. They die fast (11 hp, half damage when bloodied), so hit-and-fade is the tactic: dive through a cluster, wheel up out of reach, and drop back from the ceiling. Target anyone carrying light sources or making noise, and let thunderous or radiant spells—against which swarms are vulnerable—be the gamble you win by staying dispersed above. When half the colony dies, scatter into cracks too small to follow.

name: Swarm of Beetles

actions.name: Bites
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm's space. Hit: 10 (4d4) piercing damage, or 5 (2d4) piercing damage if the swarm has half of its hit points or fewer.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny insect. The swarm can't regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.

description: A swarm of beetles gains a burrowing speed of 5 feet.
combat-strategy: Beetle swarms overwhelm in confined tunnels: they climb walls, burrow 5 ft. through earth, and shrug off slashing, piercing, and bludgeoning plus every condition worth inflicting, so the only answers are fire and lightning. Pour down from ceilings and through narrow corridor mouths where the party can't spread out, Biting (+3, 10 piercing) those in their space and crawling over armor to stay in contact. Target spellcasters and porters who break formation first, then grind whoever stands still; a swarm occupying your space blocks line of sight for ranged allies behind it. Their 20-ft. speed means they never win chases—ambush from burrows and ceilings rather than pursuing. When reduced to 11 hp, dissolve back into the floor and walls it burrowed from.

name: Swarm of Centipedes

actions.name: Bites
actions.description:
Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm's space. Hit: 10 (4d4) piercing damage, or 5 (2d4) piercing damage if the swarm has half of its hit points or fewer.
A creature reduced to 0 hit points by a swarm of centipedes is stable but poisoned for 1 hour, even after regaining hit points, and paralyzed while poisoned in this way.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny insect. The swarm can't regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.

description: A creature reduced to 0 hit points by a swarm of centipedes is stable but poisoned for 1 hour, even after regaining hit points, and paralyzed while poisoned in this way.
combat-strategy: Centipede swarms hunt like beetles but carry a kill-hook: any creature reduced to 0 hp by their Bites is poisoned and paralyzed for an hour even after healing, so finish wounded victims inside the swarm's space deliberately. Ambush from cracks, climb walls and ceilings to drop onto trailing party members, and swarm in tight quarters where their damage-resistances and full condition immunity make them immune to swordplay and fear. Focus the lowest-HP member first, then leap that downed body to the next—each kill becomes a paralyzed snack the party must rescue. Fire and lightning are the party's only real weapons, so keep them from concentrating those spells by occupying the caster too. At half health they scatter into wall cracks and stay gone.

name: Swarm of Crawling Claws

actions.name: Swarm of Grasping Hands
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 20 (4d8 + 2) Necrotic damage, or 11 (2d8 + 2) Necrotic damage if the swarm is Bloodied. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny creature. The swarm can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

combat-strategy: Crawling Claw swarms are undead grab-and-topple specialists: climb 30-ft. walls and ceilings, drop onto the party, and Swarm of Grasping Hands (+4, 20 necrotic, knocks Medium or smaller Prone). Knocking a foe prone inside the swarm's space sets up devastating follow-ups—prone targets are hit with advantage by every claw that reaches them, and the necrotic grind continues each round. Target the party's walker-lights and climbers first, take them down, then let the horde crawl over the fallen. They can't regain hit points, so attrition works against them; conversely they ignore fear and charm, and only radiant, fire, or heavy bludgeoning area spells end them quickly. When the swarm thins to a handful of hands, scuttle up walls into crevices and vanish.

name: Swarm of Dretches
languages: Abyssal; telepathy 60 ft. (works only with creatures that understand Abyssal)

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The swarm makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (3d6 + 2) Slashing damage, or 9 (3d4 + 2) Slashing damage if the swarm is Bloodied.

traits.name: Fetid Aura
traits.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12, any creature that starts its turn in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the swarm. Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition until the start of its next turn. While Poisoned, the target can take either an action or a Bonus Action on its turn, not both, and it can't take Reactions.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Small creature. The swarm can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

combat-strategy: Dretch swarms are chaos bruisers: their Fetid Aura (DC 12 Con) strips a Poisoned target's bonus actions, reactions, and choice—neutering the party's action economy before a single Rend lands. Open by charging (40 ft.) straight into the spellcaster or archer cluster so the aura lands at the start of their turns, then Multiattack Rend (2x12 slashing) whoever fails. Fight in corridors, slums, and filth-choked ruins where fleeing is hard and the aura's area control compounds. Target whoever still has a reaction—readied actions and opportunity attacks are the aura's real prey; park the swarm on top of them and the target flails half-crippled. They never retreat willingly; they fight to the last squirming dretch unless commanded by a stronger demon.

name: Swarm of Insects

actions.name: Bites
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (2d4 + 1) Poison damage, or 3 (1d4 + 1) Poison damage if the swarm is Bloodied.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: If the swarm has a Climb Speed, the swarm can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny insect. The swarm can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

combat-strategy: Insect swarms are terrain ambushers: they climb ceilings, fly 20 ft., and pour through cracks, descending onto anyone who crosses their domain to Bite (+3, 6 poison) from within the occupied space. Drop from above onto clustered marchers in tunnels and overgrown ruins, then let the swarm crawl across walls where melee can't easily reach. Their resistances to mundane weapons and near-total condition immunity make them unwinnable by the sword—only fire, lightning, or smoke drives them off, so the real battle is area-of-effect economics. Target the rear guard and pack animals first, then spread poison across whoever stands in the cloud. When burned or shocked below half strength, the survivors scatter into crevices and walls.

name: Swarm of Larvae

actions.name: Bites
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) Necrotic damage, or 7 (2d4 + 2) Necrotic damage if the swarm is Bloodied.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through an opening large enough for a Medium creature. The swarm can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

combat-strategy: Larva swarms are the crawling shame of the Lower Planes: 30-ft. ground speed, Medium bodies, and Bites that deal necrotic (+4, 9) while occupying your space. They attack in a mass surge across open cave floors, engulfing stragglers and the fallen alike—feeding on the dead is lore-canonical, so leave corpses unattended and they'll swarm them, blocking movement and reviving into future horrors. Target anyone standing in filth or near carrion, engulf them, and grind with repeated necrotic bites while the swarm's 22 hp soaks ordinary steel. They lack flying, climbing, and any ranged answer, so elevated ground, boats, or a wall is safe. When burned, frozen, or beaten below half strength, they flee back into the muck to gestate.

name: Swarm of Lemures

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The swarm makes two Vile Slime attacks.

actions.name: Vile Slime
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d8 + 2) Poison damage, or 9 (2d6 + 2) Poison damage if the swarm is Bloodied.

traits.name: Hellish Restoration
traits.description: If the swarm dies in the Nine Hells, it revives with all its Hit Points in 1d10 days unless it is killed by a creature under the effects of a Bless spell or its remains are sprinkled with Holy Water.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through an opening large enough for a Medium creature. The swarm can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

combat-strategy: Lemure swarms are Hell's cannon fodder with stamina: 45 hp, 40-ft. speed, and Multiattack Vile Slime (2x11 poison) that they will hurl and smear across anyone in reach. Drive them straight at the front line as a slowing, stinking wall—poison damage wears down tough fighters and their sheer mass bodies-block corridors and doorways for devils behind them. In the Nine Hells they resurrect in 1d10 days unless Bless or holy water finishes them, so in their home plane they fight with total impunity and should be spent freely as delays. Outside Hell, they break apart at low hit points; keep them off balance with radiant and fire. Command them to form living bridges over pits and barricades—lemures obey without question.

name: Swarm of Piranhas

actions.name: Bites
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5 (with Advantage if the target doesn't have all its Hit Points), reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) Piercing damage, or 5 (1d4 + 3) Piercing damage if the swarm is Bloodied.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny piranha. The swarm can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The swarm can breathe only underwater.

combat-strategy: Piranha swarms strike in murky water: 40-ft. swim speed, darkvision, and Bites (+5, advantage if the target is wounded) make them relentless in river and swamp ambushes. Drag fights underwater or into flooded ruins where the party can't see, then circle-bite the first creature to take damage—the pack instinctively focuses wounded prey with advantage, so one stray wound snowballs into a feeding frenzy. Target swimmers, boat crews, and anyone carrying loot who slows them down; harried swimmers on ships can't flee at 40-ft. sprint pace. Out of water they're nearly useless (5-ft. walk), so never let them be lured ashore—stay submerged. When bloodied below half strength, the frenzy dies with the swarm; slip into the silt and vanish.

name: Swarm of Poisonous Snakes

actions.name: Bites
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 0 ft., one creature in the swarm's space. Hit: 7 (2d6) piercing damage, or 3 (1d6) piercing damage if the swarm has half of its hit points or fewer. The target must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw, taking 14 (4d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
actions.save_effect: 14 (4d6) Poison damage. Success: Half damage.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny snake. The swarm can't regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.

combat-strategy: Snake swarms are venom grinders: they slither 30 ft., swim, and swarm into a target's space for Bites (+6, 7 piercing) plus a DC 10 Con save for 14 poison damage—soak the party's weakest Con saves (paladins and rangers are fine, but wizards and warlocks crumble). They're immune to nearly every control condition and resistant to ordinary weapons, so the party's only outs are fire, area damage, and retreat. Coil in tall grass, underbrush, and ship holds, then strike from concealment; their 10-ft. blindsight makes concealment-based ambush their opening move. Target anyone who's already hurt or slowed, and stack bitten-and-poisoned victims so failed saves compound. At low numbers they burrow under rocks and go still.

name: Swarm of Quippers

actions.name: Bites
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 0 ft., one creature in the swarm's space. Hit: 14 (4d6) piercing damage, or 7 (2d6) piercing damage if the swarm has half of its hit points or fewer.

traits.name: Blood Frenzy
traits.description: The swarm has advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all its hit points.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny quipper. The swarm can't regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: The swarm can breathe only underwater.

combat-strategy: Quipper swarms own underwater encounters: 40-ft. swim, full condition immunity, mundane-weapon resistance, and Blood Frenzy advantage against wounded prey. Attack in the dark or murky depths (darkvision 60) and hammer anyone already damaged—+5 at advantage plus 14 piercing rips a wounded character apart in two rounds. Target the weakest swimmer first, draw blood with one swarm, then let the second swarm dive on the frenzy-marked victim. Their 0-ft. walk makes land a death sentence, so lure them into shallow pools or onto boats if fleeing; conversely, drag the party's fight underwater where flying and land speeds are worthless. When bloodied they scatter through openings a Tiny fish fits through, reforming later downstream.

name: Swarm of Rats

actions.name: Bites
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (2d4) Piercing damage, or 2 (1d4) Piercing damage if the swarm is Bloodied.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny rat. The swarm can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

description: Swarm. The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny rat. The swarm can't regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.
combat-strategy: Rat swarms are plague-wave ambushers: they burst from sewers, granaries, and collapsed floors (+2, 5 piercing) in tight tunnels with 30-ft. climb speed. Flood narrow corridors from drain grates and holes in walls, occupy the space of trailing party members, then melt back into the cracks—hit-and-fade attrition, not a stand-up fight. Their terrible 10 AC and 14 hp mean any serious attacker shreds them, so the tactic is mass: commit dozens at once, spread across multiple spaces so area spells waste on empty floor. Target the pack mule, the torch-bearer, anyone carrying food or disease-susceptible loot. When half the swarm dies, they rout back into the walls—and if the GM has plague or filth volleys, this is the trigger to bring the roof down.

name: Swarm of Ravens

actions.name: Beaks
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage, or 2 (1d4) Piercing damage if the swarm is Bloodied.

actions.name: Cacophony
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 10, one creature in the swarm's space. Failure: The target has the Deafened condition until the start of the swarm's next turn. While Deafened, the target also has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Deafened condition until the start of the swarm's next turn

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny raven. The swarm can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

combat-strategy: Raven swarms are omen-birds and messengers first, fighters last: they strike from the air (50-ft. fly) with Beaks (+4, 5 piercing), but their real weapon is Cacophony—a DC 10 Wis save that Deafens and burdens a target in their space with disadvantage on all attacks and checks. Open by diving onto the party's archer, duelist, or spellcaster-in-waiting and Cacophony them into a fumble machine, then harass, climb away, and dive again. Use them as spotters and harriers over battlefields, denying focus to anyone important. They die fast (11 hp), so never land in melee—stay airborne. When beaten down, burst upward and scatter into the sky to report what they saw to whatever master sent them.

name: Swarm of Spiders

actions.name: Bites
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm's space. Hit: 10 (4d4) piercing damage, or 5 (2d4) piercing damage if the swarm has half of its hit points or fewer.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny insect. The swarm can't regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The swarm can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

traits.name: Web Sense
traits.description: While in contact with a web, the swarm knows the exact location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

traits.name: Web Walker
traits.description: The swarm ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.

description:
A swarm of spiders has the following additional traits.
  • Spider Climb. The swarm can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.
  • Web Sense. While in contact with a web, the swarm knows the exact location of any other creature in contact with the same web.
  • Web Walker. The swarm ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.
combat-strategy: Spider swarms hunt by web-craft in dark, enclosed spaces: they climb walls and ceilings, ignore all webbing, and feel every vibration their webs carry. Ambush in web-choked caverns where Web Sense tells them exactly where every intruder stands, then pour down from above to Bite (+3, 10 piercing) from within the occupied space. They have almost no ranged answer and blind beyond 10 ft., so their domain is the dark web-labyrinth—lure the party deep, cut the light, and swarm the stragglers touching the silk. Target anyone tangled in webs first (they know exactly where they are), then grind the isolated. Fire and lightning clear them; when burned or broken below half strength, they skitter up walls into crevices.

name: Swarm of Stirges

actions.name: Swarm of Proboscises
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (2d10 + 3) Piercing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) Piercing damage if the swarm is Bloodied. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature in the swarm's space, the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13). Until the grapple ends, the target takes 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage at the end of each of its turns.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny creature. The swarm can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

combat-strategy: Stirge swarms are aerial leeches: 40-ft. fly, +5 Swarm of Proboscises (14 piercing) that Grapples (DC 13) Medium or smaller creatures in their space and drains 7 necrotic at the end of each grappled turn. Dive from dark tunnels onto lone explorers and rear guard, latching on and bleeding them automatically while the rest of the swarm circles above. The grapple is the trap: halving the party's actions to break free (or watching allies spend actions helping) lets the swarm dictate tempo, and hovering 15-30 ft. up forces ranged attacks against tiny evasive targets. Kill or bloodied triggers drop them to 8 average damage, so commit the whole swarm at once and never piecemeal. When the pack thins, they scatter into narrow cracks, returning later to bleed the camp at night.

name: Swarm of Venomous Snakes

actions.name: Bites
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Piercing damage—or 6 (1d4 + 4) Piercing damage if the swarm is Bloodied—plus 10 (3d6) Poison damage.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny snake. The swarm can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

combat-strategy: Open by slithering directly through the party's space—Bites hits anything it shares a square with and delivers 8 piercing plus 10 poison with a +6 to hit off its 18 Dexterity. Prioritize clustered melee characters and anyone in narrow corridors, since the swarm passes through Tiny-beast-sized openings and cannot be blocked by normal means. It has no tricks and low HP, so keep it moving: spend its full 30 ft. (or swimming speed) to flow through the fight, never ending its turn where a readied attack or area effect can catch it. It can't gain temp HP or healing, so any real damage is permanent—if reduced to half hit points, keep biting (6 piercing + 10 poison still hurts) but look to slip away through cracks or water where pursuers can't follow.

name: Swarm of Wasps

actions.name: Bites
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm's space. Hit: 10 (4d4) piercing damage, or 5 (2d4) piercing damage if the swarm has half of its hit points or fewer.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny insect. The swarm can't regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.

description: A swarm of wasps has a walking speed of 5 feet, a flying speed of 30 feet, and no climbing speed.
combat-strategy: Fly in immediately—30 ft. of flight compensates for its useless 5 ft. walk—and settle into a flyer's space to use Bites (reach 0 ft. means it must share the target's space).
