Swarm melee fighters or spellcasters holding concentration, since nothing forces it to break formation: it's immune to being grappled, restrained, prone, stunned, and frightened, and resistant to all mundane weapons. Its 22 HP is the whole clock: every point of damage is permanent (no temp HP or healing) and attacks halve its damage at half HP, so hit hard early and often. Kite between engagements using flight and its 10 ft. blindsight, diving through openings too small to pursue; flee when the swarm drops low enough that Bites no longer threatens a kill.

name: Tarrasque

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The tarrasque can use its Frightful Presence. It then makes five attacks: one with its bite, two with its claws, one with its horns, and one with its tail. It can use its Swallow instead of its bite.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +19 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 36 (4d12 + 10) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it is grappled (escape DC 20). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the tarrasque can't bite another target.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +19 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 28 (4d8 + 10) slashing damage.

actions.name: Horns
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +19 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 32 (4d10 + 10) piercing damage.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +19 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit: 24 (4d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 20 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.
actions.save_effect: Failure: knocked prone

actions.name: Frightful Presence
actions.description: Each creature of the tarrasque's choice within 120 feet of it and aware of it must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, with disadvantage if the tarrasque is within line of sight, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the tarrasque's Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours.
actions.save_effect: Failure: become frightened for 1 minute A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns with disadvantage, ending the effect on itself on a success. The creature is immune to this effect for the next 24 hours.

actions.name: Swallow
actions.description: The tarrasque makes one bite attack against a Large or smaller creature it is grappling. If the attack hits, the target takes the bite's damage, the target is swallowed, and the grapple ends. While swallowed, the creature is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the tarrasque, and it takes 56 (16d6) acid damage at the start of each of the tarrasque's turns. If the tarrasque takes 60 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the tarrasque must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which fall prone in a space within 10 feet ofthe tarrasque. If the tarrasque dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse by using 30 feet of movement, exiting prone.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 28 (8d6 + 6) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it is swallowed — Blinded, Prone, and Restrained until it is regurgitated.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the tarrasque fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The tarrasque has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Reflective Carapace
traits.description: Any time the tarrasque is targeted by a magic missile spell, a line spell, or a spell that requires a ranged attack roll, roll a d6. On a 1 to 5, the tarrasque is unaffected. On a 6, the tarrasque is unaffected, and the effect is reflected back at the caster as though it originated from the tarrasque, turning the caster into the target.

traits.name: Siege Monster
traits.description: The tarrasque deals double damage to objects and structures.

legendary_actions.name: General
legendary_actions.description: The tarrasque can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The tarrasque regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

legendary_actions.name: Attack
legendary_actions.description: The tarrasque makes one claw attack or tail attack.

legendary_actions.name: Move
legendary_actions.advisory_message: moves up to half its speed (40 ft.) — advisory record: GM moves the token; no movement-distance consumer (MA-1581). Movement-distance is GM-enforced and the spend is already adjudicated by the legendary gate.
legendary_actions.description: The tarrasque moves up to half its speed.

legendary_actions.name: Chomp (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: The tarrasque makes one bite attack or uses its Swallow.

description:
The legendary tarrasque is possibly the most dreaded monster of the Material Plane. It is widely believed that only one of these creatures exists, though no one can predict where and when it will strike.
A scaly biped, the tarrasque is fifty feet tall and seventy feet long, weighing hundreds of tons. It carries itself like a bird of prey, leaning forward and using its powerful lashing tail for balance. Its cavernous maw yawns wide enough to swallow all but the largest creatures, and so great is its hunger that it can devour the populations of whole towns.

Legendary Destruction. The destructive potential of the tarrasque is so vast that some cultures incorporate the monster into religious doctrine, weaving its sporadic appearance into stories of divine judgment and wrath. Legends tell how the tarrasque slumbers in its secret lair beneath the earth, remaining in a dormant state for decades or centuries. When it awakens in answer to some inscrutable cosmic call, it rises from the depths to obliterate everything in its path.
combat-strategy: Open with Frightful Presence at max range to scatter the party with DC 17 Wisdom fear, then charge the largest threats with Multiattack—five attacks for roughly 140 damage averaging hits on +19. Bite to grapple and restrain a priority target, then on a later turn spend 2 legendary actions on Chomp to Swallow them: 56 acid per round with total cover effectively removes that character from the fight, but remember 60+ damage in one turn from inside forces a DC 20 Con save to regurgitate. Position relentlessly between threats using legendary Move plus its 40 ft. speed, keeping the Reflective Carapace facing the back line so ranged spell attackers punish themselves (line spells, magic missile, and attack-roll spells mostly fizzle, sometimes reflect onto the caster). Bully the battlefield itself—Siege Monster lets it level walls and towers to crush cover and force the party into the open. Nothing routs it; its only 'retreat' is walking off to eat the next town when the meal stops being interesting.

name: Thri-Kreen

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The thri-kreen makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its claws.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the target is also paralyzed while poisoned in this way. The poisoned target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
actions.save_effect: Failure: poisoned for 1 minute.

actions.name: Claws
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (2d4 + 1) slashing damage.

traits.name: Chameleon Carapace
traits.description: The thri-kreen can change the color of its carapace to match the color and texture of its surroundings. As a result, it has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide.

traits.name: Standing Leap
traits.description: The thri-kreen's long jump is up to 30 feet and its high jump is up to 15 feet, with or without a running start.

description:
Thri-kreen wander the deserts and savannas o f the world, avoiding all other races.

Thri-Kreen Communication. Thri-kreen employ a language without words. To show emotion and reaction, a thri-kreen clacks its mandibles and waves its antennae, giving other thri-kreen a sense of what it is thinking and feeling. Other creatures find this manner of communication difficult to interpret and impossible to duplicate.
When forced to interact with creatures of other intelligent species, thri-kreen employ alternative methods of communication, such as drawing pictures in sand or making pictures out of twigs or blades of grass.

Limited Emotions. Thri-kreen experience the full range of emotions but aren't as prone to emotional outbursts as humans. Thri-kreen with psionic ability often demonstrate a wider range of emotions, particularly if they live near or interact with humans or other highly emotional creatures.

Isolationists and Wanderers. Thri-kreen consider all other living creatures as potential nourishment, and they love the taste of elf flesh in particular. If a creature might be useful for something other than food, the thri­ kreen aren't likely to attack it on sight. Thri-kreen kill to survive, never for sport.

Sleepless. Thri-kreen don't require sleep and can rest while remaining alert and performing light tasks. Their inability to sleep is thought to be the reason why thri­ kreen have such short lifespans, the average thri-kreen life expectancy being only thirty years.
combat-strategy: Use Chameleon Carapace and Stealth to ambush from cover, then burst out with its 40 ft. speed for a full-speed charge into a lone or soft target—Multiattack's Bite first, since the DC 11 Constitution save can poison and (failed by 5+) paralyze for a minute of repeat saves. Ambush isolated stragglers at the edge of the pack, never tankers in heavy armor; the +3 attacks are weak, so the paralysis from Bite is the win condition. Kite constantly: 40 ft. walk plus 30 ft. standing leaps let it strike, leap away over obstacles or gaps, and re-hide in the same round. Fight in packs for mutual support and disengage (or leap) out of melee when cornered—33 HP won't survive a sustained exchange, so it breaks off when an ambush fails or a foe shows heavy damage output.

name: Thri-kreen Marauder

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The thri-kreen makes two attacks, using Gythka or Chatkcha in any combination.

actions.name: Gythka
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) Slashing damage plus 2 (1d4) Poison damage.

actions.name: Chatkcha
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 30/120 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Slashing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Leap
bonus_actions.description: The thri-kreen jumps up to 15 feet by spending 5 feet of movement.

combat-strategy: Skirmish at range: open with Chatkcha (30/120 ft.) volleys from hiding spots, using its Stealth bonus and chameleon carapace to stay unseen between shots. When a target closes or charges, bonus-action Leap (15 ft. for 5 ft. of movement) to bound over obstacles or onto high ground, then Multiattack with two Gythka strikes—each adding poison—before leaping clear again. Focus fire on unarmored or isolated targets where the +4 ranged and +3 melee rolls land most often, and never stand still in melee against multiple enemies. With only 33 HP and no pack tactics listed, it should disengage or leap away whenever two or more foes can reach it, retreating into terrain only it can traverse—its leaps and 40 ft. speed outrun most humanoids chasing on foot.

name: Thri-kreen Psion

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The thri-kreen makes three Psionic Lance attacks.

actions.name: Psionic Lance
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit: 18 (4d6 + 4) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The thri-kreen casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15): At Will: Mage Hand (the hand is Invisible) 1/Day Each: Detect Thoughts, Sending, Synaptic Static

combat-strategy: Open at long range with Multiattack's three Psionic Lances (120 ft., +7, 18 psychic each) while hovering 20 ft. up—psychic damage is rarely resisted and rarely blocked by cover at altitude. Drop Synaptic Static (DC 15) on a clustered group when they bunch up to attack it, and use Detect Thoughts to locate hidden or invisible foes while its 60 ft. darkvision covers the dark. Target the party's controller or healer first: 120 ft. lance range plus hover means it dictates distance, backpedaling 40 ft. per round while still full-attacking since the lance works melee or ranged. Its AC 16 and 149 HP are decent but its saving throws are mediocre, so keep altitude and the +8 Stealth carapace in play; when half health or out of spells, Dimension Door isn't available—send a Sending for reinforcements and fly to cover where ground-bound foes can't follow.

name: Thug

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The thug makes two melee attacks.

actions.name: Mace
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Heavy Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d10) piercing damage.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The thug has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the thug's allies is within 5 ft. of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

description: Thugs are ruthless enforcers skilled at intimidation and violence. They work for money and have few scruples.
combat-strategy: Open by charging with Pack Tactics—swarm so at least two thugs flank each target and swing with advantage on the +4 mace Multiattack (10 damage per target when both hit). Focus the softest visible target the pack can surround, since advantage evaporates the moment their buddy falls; keep allies within 5 ft. of every engaged foe to keep the advantage flowing. Thugs with crossbows stand off at 100 ft. to avoid triggering opportunity attacks, firing into melees their friends are already in. With AC 11 and 32 HP they lose extended duels: once half the pack is down or a foe is clearly one-shotted-able output, break off through the nearest exit and scatter—loyalty ends where a good sword swing begins.

name: Thunderbird

traits.name: Wings of Thunder
traits.description: When the Thunderbird flies at least 30 ft. in a straight line, the air around it crackles; each creature within 5 ft. of its path must succeed on a DC 23 Dexterity saving throw or take 7 (2d6) Lightning damage.

traits.name: Sky Caller
traits.description: Once per day, the Thunderbird can summon a rainstorm covering 1 square mile, lasting up to 1 hour.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The Thunderbird makes one Beak attack and two Wing attacks.

actions.name: Beak
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +15, reach 15 ft. Hit: 24 (3d10 + 8) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Wing
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +15, reach 15 ft. Hit: 26 (4d8 + 8) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Thunderstrike (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 24, each creature within 60 ft. Failure: 66 (12d10) Lightning damage. Success: Half damage.

reactions.name: Updraft
reactions.trigger: When the Thunderbird is forced to stop flying.
reactions.description: The Thunderbird immediately rises 60 ft. vertically without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Wing
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Wing attack.

legendary_actions.name: Wing Clap
legendary_actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 23, each creature within 30 ft. Failure: pushed 20 ft. and knocked Prone; takes 7 (2d6) Thunder damage.

legendary_actions.name: Storm Call (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: The Thunderbird calls down a single bolt of lightning on one creature within 120 ft. The target must succeed on a DC 24 Dexterity saving throw or take 27 (6d8) Lightning damage.

description: The great storm-bird whose wingbeats are thunder, whose eyes flash lightning, and whose shadow over the plains is the beginning of a tempest.
combat-strategy: It stays high, calling Thunderstrike into the thick of the fight and diving through the enemy to scatter them with its wings before any reach it.

name: Tiamat
immunities: Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing from Nonmagical Attacks
damage_immunities: Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing from Nonmagical Attacks

traits.name: Discorporation
traits.description: When Tiamat drops to 0 Hit Points or dies, her body is destroyed but her essence travels back to her domain in the Nine Hells, and she is unable to take physical form for a time.

traits.name: Innate Spellcasting (3/Day)
traits.description: Tiamat can innately cast Divine Word (spell save DC 26). Her spellcasting ability is Charisma.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (5/Day)
traits.description: If Tiamat fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Limited Magic Immunity
traits.description: Unless she wishes to be affected, Tiamat is immune to spells of 6th level or lower. She has Advantage on saving throws against all other spells and magical effects.

traits.name: Magic Weapons
traits.description: Tiamat's weapon attacks are magical.

traits.name: Multiple Heads
traits.description: Tiamat can take one Reaction per turn, rather than only one per round. She has Advantage on saving throws against being knocked Unconscious. If she fails a saving throw against an effect that would stun her, one of her unspent Legendary Actions is spent instead.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.description: Tiamat regains 30 Hit Points at the start of her turn.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Tiamat can use her Frightful Presence. She then makes two Claw attacks and one Tail attack.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 15 ft. Hit: 24 (4d6 + 10) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 25 ft. Hit: 28 (4d8 + 10) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Frightful Presence
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 26, each creature of her choice within 240 ft. of her and aware of her. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to Tiamat's Frightful Presence for 24 hours. No damage. The target has the Frightened condition on a failed save. No damage.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 5
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, Tiamat can expend a use to take one of the following actions. Her options are tied to her five heads; once she picks an option for one head, she can't choose another option for that head until the start of her next turn. She regains all expended uses at the start of each of her turns.

legendary_actions.name: Black Dragon Head Bite
legendary_actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 20 ft. Hit: 32 (4d10 + 10) Slashing damage. Plus 14 (4d6) Acid damage.

legendary_actions.name: Blue Dragon Head Bite
legendary_actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 20 ft. Hit: 32 (4d10 + 10) Slashing damage. Plus 14 (4d6) Lightning damage.

legendary_actions.name: Green Dragon Head Bite
legendary_actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 20 ft. Hit: 32 (4d10 + 10) Slashing damage. Plus 14 (4d6) Poison damage.

legendary_actions.name: Red Dragon Head Bite
legendary_actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 20 ft. Hit: 32 (4d10 + 10) Slashing damage. Plus 14 (4d6) Fire damage.

legendary_actions.name: White Dragon Head Bite
legendary_actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 20 ft. Hit: 32 (4d10 + 10) Slashing damage. Plus 14 (4d6) Cold damage.

legendary_actions.name: Black Dragon Head Acid Breath (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 27, each creature in a 120-foot-long, 10-foot-wide Line. Failure: 67 (15d8) Acid damage. Success: Half damage.

legendary_actions.name: Blue Dragon Head Lightning Breath (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 27, each creature in a 120-foot-long, 10-foot-wide Line. Failure: 88 (16d10) Lightning damage. Success: Half damage.

legendary_actions.name: Green Dragon Head Poison Breath (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 27, each creature in a 90-foot Cone. Failure: 77 (22d6) Poison damage. Success: Half damage.

legendary_actions.name: Red Dragon Head Fire Breath (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 27, each creature in a 90-foot Cone. Failure: 91 (26d6) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.

legendary_actions.name: White Dragon Head Cold Breath (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 27, each creature in a 90-foot Cone. Failure: 72 (16d8) Cold damage. Success: Half damage.

description: The five-headed dragon goddess of evil, progenitor of chromatic dragons, Tiamat hoards gods' weapons and the spite of every scale she has ever shed. Each of her heads speaks, schemes, and breathes destruction in a different element.
combat-strategy: She opens with Frightful Presence, then chains one Claw, one Bite, and her Tail each turn while spending Legendary Actions to rotate her five heads' Breath Weapons down the densest ranks, never wasting two options on the same head in one round.

name: Tiger

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Slashing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

bonus_actions.name: Nimble Escape
bonus_actions.description: The tiger takes the Disengage or Hide action.

combat-strategy: Ambush—+7 Stealth and 60 ft. darkvision mean it should start hidden at night or in tall grass, then sprint 40 ft. out of hiding to Rend a lone or light target, knocking it prone automatically (Large or smaller) for +2 hit bonus on follow-up attacks. Prefers isolated prey straggling at the rear of the party; prone plus 10 slashing per round bleeds a target before help arrives. Attack from the flank or rear so the prone target can't retaliate easily, then bonus-action Disengage to leap clear, or Hide again to re-ambush from a new direction. At 30 HP it's fragile: if the prey fights back and drops it below half health, or the whole party turns on it, disengage and melt into cover—it hunts to eat, not to die.

name: Tough

actions.name: Mace
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Heavy Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +3, range 100/400 ft. Hit: 6 (1d10 + 1) Piercing damage.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The tough has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the tough's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

combat-strategy: Fight in a pack and lean entirely on Pack Tactics: surround targets so the +4 mace swings come with advantage, and let crossbowmen fire from range at anyone not engaged in melee (avoiding cover penalties by picking clean lanes). AC 12 is nothing, but 32 HP with the banded bonus makes it durable enough to hold a line or a door—stand shoulder-to-shoulder in a corridor so the party must chew through each one. Focus whoever is in reach, prefer prone-or-pin opportunities only if an ally sets them up, and don't chase: these are hirelings who hold ground they're paid to hold. They retreat only when the fight is clearly lost—typically half the group down or their employer has fled—because they take their beating where they stand.

name: Tough Boss

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The tough makes two attacks, using Warhammer or Heavy Crossbow in any combination.

actions.name: Warhammer
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, the tough pushes the target up to 10 feet straight away from itself.

actions.name: Heavy Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 100/400 ft. Hit: 13 (2d10 + 2) Piercing damage.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The tough has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the tough's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

combat-strategy: Open by engaging the party's front-liner in a chokepoint, using Multiattack warhammers to knock targets back 10 ft. straight away—repeatedly shoving a defender out of a doorway or off a ledge to control spacing. Use the heavy crossbow (13 damage, +4) at range on the second attack when a foe tries to disengage past the pack or when it wants to hit someone behind the line without closing. Pack Tactics is the engine: never swing at a target its tough minions aren't touching, keeping advantage on every attack at AC 16. Hold the line as long as allies surround it; once half health (around 40) or the pack is broken, shove free and withdraw toward defensible ground or its employer, using pushes to keep pursuers off its back.

name: Treant

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The treant makes two Slam attacks.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 5 ft. Hit: 16 (3d6 + 6) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Hail of Bark
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +10, range 180 ft. Hit: 28 (4d10 + 6) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Animate Trees
actions.description: The treant magically animates up to two trees it can see within 60 feet of itself. Each tree uses the Treant stat block, except it has Intelligence and Charisma scores of 1, it can't speak, and it lacks this action. The tree takes its turn immediately after the treant on the same Initiative count, and it obeys the treant. A tree remains animate for 1 day or until it dies, the treant dies, or it is more than 120 feet from the treant. The tree then takes root if possible.

traits.name: Siege Monster
traits.description: The treant deals double damage to objects and structures.

description:
Treants are awakened trees that dwell in ancient forests. Although treants prefer to while away the days, months, and years in quiet contemplation, they fiercely protect their woodland demesnes from outside threats.

The Sleeping Tree Awakens. A tree destined to become a treant meditates through a long cycle of seasons, living normally for decades or centuries before realizing its potential. Trees that awaken do so only under special circumstances and in places steeped with nature's magic. Treants and powerful druids can sense when a tree has the spark of potential, and they protect such trees in secret groves as they draw near the moment of their awakening. During the long process of awakening, a tree acquires face-like features in its bark, a division of the lower trunk into legs, and long branches bending downward to serve as its arms. When it is ready, the tree pulls its legs free from the clutching earth and joins its fellows in protecting its woodland home.

Legendary Guardians. After a treant awakens, it continues to grow exactly as it did when it was a tree. Treants created from the mightiest trees can reach great sizes while developing an innate magical power over plants and animals. Such treants can animate plants, using them to ensnare and trap intruders. They can call wild creatures to aid them or carry messages across great distances.

Protectors of the Wild. Even after awakening, a treant spends much of its time living as a tree. While rooted in place, a treant remains aware of its surroundings, and can perceive the effects of events taking place miles away based on subtle changes nearby.
Woodcutters who avoid culling healthy living trees and hunters who take only what they need of the forest's bounty are unlikely to arouse a treant's ire. Creatures careless with fire, those who poison the forest, and those who destroy great trees, especially a tree close to awakening, face the treant's wrath.
combat-strategy: Start disguised—it looks like an ordinary tree until it moves, so let the party walk into the grove before rising and Multiattacking whoever is closest (two Slams, 32 damage). Open with Animate Trees on two adjacent trees to create a 3-on-anyone grove fight where animated treants act on its initiative and obey it, swamping the party with bodies. Kite ranged attackers with Hail of Bark—180 ft. range, +10, 28 piercing per bolt—targeting spellcasters and anyone in the open, while its 30 ft. speed is enough to punish anyone trying to close. AC 16 and 138 HP favor a grinding defensive fight: use Huge size to block corridors and doorways, and its double damage to structures means it can smash walls, doors, and roofs to open flanks or collapse cover. It retreats only to re-root and heal; if burning is the answer (plants and their vulnerability to fire), use bark-spray range and cover to keep distance from torches and fire spells.

name: Tree Blight
languages: Understands Common and Druidic but can't speak

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The blight makes two Branch attacks and uses Grasping Root.

actions.name: Branch
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 15 ft. Hit: 16 (3d6 + 6) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Grasping Root
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 17, one Large or smaller creature the blight can see within 15 feet. Failure: The target is pulled up to 10 feet straight toward the blight and has the Grappled condition (escape DC 16) from one of six roots. Until the grapple ends, the target takes 13 (2d6 + 6) Bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns.
actions.save_effect: The target is pulled up to 10 feet straight toward the blight and has the Grappled condition (escape DC 16) from one of six roots. Until the grapple ends, the target takes 13 (2d6 + 6) Bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns.

bonus_actions.name: Gnash
bonus_actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 17, one creature Grappled by the blight. Failure: 19 (3d8 + 6) Piercing damage. Success: Half damage.

combat-strategy: Anchor in place or advance slowly—its 15 ft. reach on Branch attacks plus Grasping Root makes closing the party's problem, not its own. Open combat by snaring the closest Large-or-smaller foe with Grasping Root (DC 17 Str, grapple DC 16, 13 auto-damage per round), then follow with Multiattack's two Branch attacks on the same victim or other closers. Bonus-action Gnash a grappled target every turn it's available—19 piercing (half on save) stacks with the root's start-of-turn damage, so a snared target takes heavy unavoidable punishment while it struggles to escape. Its 60 ft. blindsight negates invisibility, darkness, and fog, so fight in the dark or smoke it creates without penalty. It can't run and doesn't need to: 115 HP and reach control win attrition fights, but grappled prey is best dragged to the edge of its roots and eaten in place rather than pursued.

name: Tribal Warrior

actions.name: Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, or 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The warrior has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the warrior's allies is within 5 ft. of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

description: Tribal warriors live beyond civilization, most often subsisting on fishing and hunting. Each tribe acts in accordance with the wishes of its chief, who is the greatest or oldest warrior of the tribe or a tribe member blessed by the gods.
combat-strategy: Fight in a warband and trigger Pack Tactics constantly—surround targets so +3 spear attacks roll with advantage, and set spears two-handed (d8, 5 damage) when holding a line against a charge. Fight in the open on their home terrain where numbers and pack coordination matter: line up in a shield-wall or skirmish chain so every warrior keeps an ally within 5 ft. of each engaged foe. Throw spears (20/60 ft.) at closing enemies before contact, then plant the line and go two-handed once they arrive in reach. At 11 HP each, one solid hit nearly kills: when the warband takes disproportionate casualties or the enemy breaks through, the warriors fall back through pre-scouted terrain—streams, dense brush, or a palisade gap—regrouping to re-form Pack Tactics rather than fighting to the last.

name: Triceratops

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The triceratops makes two Gore attacks.

actions.name: Gore
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 19 (2d12 + 6) Piercing damage. If the target is Huge or smaller and the triceratops moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 9 (2d8) Piercing damage and has the Prone condition.

conditional_damage.condition: moved 20+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit

description: One of the most aggressive of the herbivorous dinosaurs, a triceratops has a skull that flares out to form a protective plate of bone. With its great horns and formidable speed, a triceratops gores and tramples would-be predators to death.
combat-strategy: Charge: 50 ft. of speed means it can open at range and still satisfy Gore's trampling rule—move 20+ ft. straight at a target for an extra 9 piercing and auto-prone (Huge or smaller) on hit. Multiattack's two gores (19 each) crush anything Huge or smaller, so pick a target, pin it prone with a trample, and gore it again next turn while prone attacks come with advantage. Target isolated small-and-Medium foes on open ground where it can get a straight 20 ft. run; in tight corridors use its bulk to shove through shields and doorways, and its 22 Strength brute-force keeps it dominant in shoving contests. Turn radius is its weakness—fast foes circling behind it force awkward repositioning, so back into walls or turn wide early to keep the horns facing threats. It fights until dead or until its prey stops moving; a badly wounded triceratops (below half HP) may bellow and wheel away after one last trample rather than finish the job.

name: Tridrone

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The tridrone makes three fist attacks or three javelin attacks.

actions.name: Fist
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage.

traits.name: Axiomatic Mind
traits.description: The tridrone can't be compelled to act in a manner contrary to its nature or its instructions.

traits.name: Disintegration
traits.description: If the tridrone dies, its body disintegrates into dust, leaving behind its weapons and anything else it was carrying.

description: Tridrones are shaped like inverted pyramids. They lead lesser modrons in battle.
combat-strategy: Advance in perfect formation with its modron pack, filling gaps exactly as ordered—Multiattack with three javelins at approaching foes (30/120 ft. range), then switch to three fists the instant anything closes to 5 ft. Its 120 ft. truesight sees through illusions, invisibility, shapechangers, and magical darkness, so position it to face whatever the party is trying to hide. It never breaks formation, never routs, and can't be intimidated or charmed (Axiomatic Mind)—send it into kill zones and it will march in on schedule. At 16 HP it's disposable cannon fodder: its strategic value is volume and lawfulness, so commit it exactly as far as its orders say and no further; when destroyed it disintegrates, leaving nothing for the party to loot or reanimate.

name: Troglodyte

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Slashing damage.

traits.name: Stench
traits.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12, any creature (other than a troglodyte) that starts its turn in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the troglodyte. Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition until the start of its next turn. Success: The target is immune to the Stench of all troglodytes for 1 hour.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: While in sunlight, the troglodyte has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls.

description:
The savage, degenerate troglodytes squat in the shallow depths of the Underdark in a constant state of war against their neighbors and one another. They mark the borders of their territories with cracked bones and skulls, or with pictographs painted in blood or dung.
Perhaps the most loathsome of all humanoids, troglodytes eat anything they can stomach. They dwell in filth. The walls of their cavern homes are smeared with grime, oily secretions, and the debris of their foul feasting.

Simpleminded Brutes. Troglodytes have a simple, communal culture devoted almost entirely to procuring food. Too simple to plan more than a few days into the future, troglodytes rely on constant raids and hunting to survive. They take sadistic pleasure in hunting intelligent creatures weaker than themselves and show no mercy toward those they capture and drag back to their lairs to be devoured. The largest and toughest troglodytes lead the hunt and become the leaders of their tribes. However, if a leader shows any weakness or hesitation, other troglodytes attack and eat it in a frenzy.
Troglodytes make little and build less, scavenging their possessions from their prey. They understand the value of metal weapons and armor, and fight among one another for the right to have such items. A troglodyte tribe might be torn apart by battles over a single longsword.

Devotees of Laogzed. Some troglodytes venerate Laogzed, a demonic, monstrously fat toad-lizard that slumbers in the Abyss. Laogzed offers the troglodytes nothing in return except aspiration, for it is the dream of his troglodyte worshipers to become as fat, well-fed, and wearily content as he seems to be.
combat-strategy: Ambush from dark tunnels—+4 Stealth, 60 ft. darkvision, and 30 ft. climb let troglodytes drop from ceilings and side-tunnels onto passing parties, Rend (+4) in the first surprised round. Get in melee immediately and stay in melee: opponents ending their turn adjacent suffer the Stench (DC 12 Con or poisoned), and poisoned attackers' disadvantage stacks with the pack's numbers advantage in the dark. Attack in packs in darkness, never in daylight (Sunlight Sensitivity gives disadvantage on everything), so drag fights into caves or ambush at night/twilight. At 13 HP they die fast against organized parties: when the ambush fails or the prey shows heavy firepower, they flee into crevices and tunnels too small or too foul for pursuers, using their climb speed to escape up walls where ground-based foes can't follow.

name: Troll

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The troll makes three Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Slashing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Charge
bonus_actions.description: The troll moves up to half its Speed straight toward an enemy it can see.

traits.name: Loathsome Limbs
traits.description: If the troll ends any turn Bloodied and took 15+ Slashing damage during that turn, one of the troll's limbs is severed, falls into the troll's space, and becomes a Troll Limb. The limb acts immediately after the troll's turn. The troll has 1 Exhaustion level for each missing limb, and it grows replacement limbs the next time it regains Hit Points.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.description: The troll regains 15 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns. If the troll takes Acid or Fire damage, this trait doesn't function on the troll's next turn. The troll dies only if it starts its turn with 0 Hit Points and doesn't regenerate.

description:
Born with horrific appetites, trolls eat anything they can catch and devour. They have no society to speak of, but they do serve as mercenaries to orcs, ogres, ettins, hags, and giants. As payment, trolls demand food and treasure. Trolls are difficult to control, however, doing as they please even when working with more powerful creatures.

Regeneration. Smashing a troll's bones and slashing through its rubbery hide only makes it angry. A troll's wounds close quickly. If the monster loses an arm, a leg, or even its head, those dismembered parts can sometimes act with a life of their own. A troll can even reattach severed body parts, untroubled by its momentary disability. Only acid and fire can arrest the regenerative properties of a troll's flesh. The trolls, enraged, will attack individuals making acid and fire attacks against them above all other prey.

Troll Freaks. Their regenerative capabilities make trolls especially susceptible to mutation. Although uncommon, such transformations can result from what the troll has done or what has been done to it. A decapitated troll might grow two heads from the stump of its neck, while a troll that eats a fey creature might gain one or more of that creature's traits.
combat-strategy: Open with a bonus-action Charge straight at the front line, then Multiattack three Rends (11 each, 10 ft. reach) to open everyone up—slashing damage on a Bloodied troll can sever limbs into Troll Limb spawns, turning one fight into three. Regeneration (15 HP per turn) makes it nearly immortal until someone applies acid or fire, so bait out those responses early by fighting in plain sight near torches and oil, then punish the party's wasted resources—remember: if it takes acid/fire, no regeneration next turn, so protect itself from those damage types with positioning behind allies or grappled prey when the wizard reloads. Focus the squishiest target in reach, mauling downed foes with successive Rends, and use Reach 10 ft. to step out of opportunity-attack range after a full attack. If the party keeps up fire/acid and it can't reach a kill, it flees—trolls remember grudges and return at night healed, and severing exhaustion from limb loss (1 level each) is the signal to disengage before the fight turns terminal.

name: Troll Limb

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d4 + 4) Slashing damage.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.description: The limb regains 5 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns. If the limb takes Acid or Fire damage, this trait doesn't function on the limb's next turn. The limb dies only if it starts its turn with 0 Hit Points and doesn't regenerate.

traits.name: Troll Spawn
traits.description: The limb uncannily has the same senses as a whole troll. If the limb isn't destroyed within 24 hours, roll 1d12. On a 12, the limb turns into a Troll. Otherwise, the limb withers away.

combat-strategy: Attack immediately and mindlessly—it has Int 1 and the same senses as a troll, so it hunts whatever is nearest with Rend (+6, 9 slashing), a nasty surprise for a party that assumed the severed limb was harmless debris. Target the nearest foe, often the one who cut it free, at 20 ft. speed—slow enough that anyone can outrun it, so it latches onto distracted or prone victims and grapples them in the mud while the main troll fights. Its 5 HP/turn regeneration means casual damage never sticks: only acid or fire kills it permanently, and the party will instinctively reach for exactly that, so use the 14 HP cushion to force the spell slot or torch burn. With no self-preservation it never retreats—its real value is stall time, and if any limb survives the fight, it should be left somewhere it can sprout into a full troll within 24 hours.

name: Twig Blight

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Slashing damage.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The blight has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the blight's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

description:
Twig blights can root in soil, which they do when living prey are scarce. While rooted, they resemble woody shrubs. When it pulls its roots free of the ground to move, a twig blight's branches twist together to form a humanoid-looking body with a head and limbs.
Twig blights seek out campsites and watering holes, rooting there to set up ambushes for potential victims coming to drink or rest. Huddled together in groups, twig blights blend in with an area's natural vegetation or with piles of debris or firewood.
Given how dry they are, twig blights are particularly susceptible to fire.
combat-strategy: Ambush in a swarm-sizable pack from within its own woods—+4 Stealth and 60 ft. blindsight mean the party walks past dozens of 'twigs' before they move. Trigger Pack Tactics en masse surrounding the same target, so a dozen +4 claw attacks (usually +6 with advantage) hit in one wave at 4 damage per claw—attrition death by paper cuts on AC 14 armor. Focus the closest single target rather than splitting attacks, dropping a victim in three rounds of concentrated swarm attacks. At 7 HP one area spell wipes the pack, so spread out when spellcasters are visible and swarm physical fighters, using thick brush and trees as hard cover against ranged shots. The swarm doesn't rout—it is a disposable trap; its only 'retreat' is the pack failing to make contact before the party retreats out of range.

name: Typhon
languages: Speaks to gods in their own tongues.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (5/Day)
traits.description: If Typhon fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Hundred Serpent Heads
traits.description: Typhon has Advantage on saving throws against being knocked Unconscious and can't be surprised.

traits.name: Earthshaker
traits.description: When Typhon hits an object, structure, or unsecured ground target, it deals an extra 10 (3d6) Thunder damage.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Typhon makes four attacks: two with his serpent heads and two with his claws.

actions.name: Serpent Head
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 15 ft. Hit: 26 (3d10 + 10) Piercing damage. Plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +19, reach 20 ft. Hit: 28 (4d8 + 10) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Storm Breach (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 27, each creature within 120 ft. Failure: 91 (26d6) Bludgeoning damage. Success: Half damage. The area becomes difficult terrain as boulders and debris fly.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, it can expend a use to take one of the following actions. It regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Serpent Head
legendary_actions.description: It makes one Serpent Head attack.

legendary_actions.name: Firebolt Volley
legendary_actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +17, range 90 ft., two targets. Hit: 18 (4d8+1) Fire damage each.

legendary_actions.name: Earthquake (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary_actions.description: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 25, each creature within 60 ft. Failure: 27 (6d8) Bludgeoning damage and the target is knocked Prone. Success: half damage and not Prone.

description: The father of monsters, a mountain-striding serpent giant whose hundred heads each speak a different doom and whose rage once unmade the gods.
combat-strategy: He advances relentlessly; a Storm Breach every two rounds breaks any army, while his heads and claws mop up those still standing.

name: Tyrannosaurus Rex

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The tyrannosaurus makes one Bite attack and one Tail attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 10 ft. Hit: 33 (4d12 + 7) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 17). While Grappled, the target has the Restrained condition and can't be targeted by the tyrannosaurus's Tail.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 15 ft. Hit: 25 (4d8 + 7) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

description: This enormous predator terrorizes all other creatures in its territory. Despite its size and weight, a tyrannosaurus is a swift runner. It chases anything it thinks it can eat, and there are few creatures it won't try to devour whole. While prowling for substantial prey, a tyrannosaurus subsists on carrion, and on any smaller creatures that try to dart in to steal its meal
combat-strategy: Explode out of the treeline at 50 ft. speed and Bite (+10, 33 piercing) the biggest threat it can reach, automatically grappling and restraining Large-or-smaller prey (escape DC 17). Once a target is grappled, it can't be targeted by the Tail—so use Multiattack's second Bite attack on the pinned victim repeatedly, since it's helpless in the jaws, while the Tail (+10, 25 bludgeoning, auto-prone on Huge or smaller) controls everyone else trying to intervene. Pick off isolated medium and Large targets on open ground; the 15 ft. Tail reach and 10 ft. Bite reach make its reach zone lethal, so back away slightly from clustered foes and let them walk into the Tail for free prone, then lunge the 50 ft. back in next round. It has no cunning retreat—fight until dead or until the prey is dead or scattered beyond pursuit—use this to bait pursuers into bad terrain where its 50 ft. charge is a death sentence.

name: Ultroloth

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The ultroloth uses Hypnotic Gaze and makes two Mercurial Whip attacks.

actions.name: Mercurial Whip
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 15 ft. Hit: 25 (6d6 + 4) Force damage, and the ultroloth can teleport the target up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space the ultroloth can see that isn't in the air.

actions.name: Hypnotic Gaze
actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 17, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. Failure: 10 (3d6) Psychic damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the start of the ultroloth's next turn. Success: The target is immune to this ultroloth's Hypnotic Gaze for 24 hours.
actions.save_effect: The target takes 10 (3d6) Psychic damage and has the Stunned condition until the start of the ultroloth's next turn. Success: The target is immune to this ultroloth's Hypnotic Gaze for 24 hours.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The ultroloth casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17): At Will: Alter Self, Clairvoyance, Detect Magic; 1/Day Each: Dimension Door, Fireball (level 5 version), Wall of Fire
actions.save_effect: Targets of the spell's saving throw use the spell save DC 17. Various effects depending on the spell cast: Alter Self (self only), Clairvoyance, Detect Magic, Dimension Door, Fireball (DC 17 Intelligence save for half Fire damage), Wall of Fire (DC 17 Dexterity save for half Fire damage).

bonus_actions.name: Fiendish Guile
bonus_actions.description: The ultroloth casts Dispel Magic, Invisibility (self only), Misty Step, or Suggestion, requiring no Material components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

traits.name: Fiendish Restoration
traits.description: If the ultroloth dies outside Gehenna, its body dissolves into ichor, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in Gehenna.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The ultroloth has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
Ultroloths command the yugoloth armies of the Blood War. An ultroloth looks like a slender gray-skinned humanoid with an elongated head. Its face bears no features except for two ovoid eyes. These eyes can become sparkling pools of light that can transfix other creatures and leave them reeling and helpless.
Frequently at one another's throats, ultroloths continually scheme to enhance their own power. When not employed to fight in the Blood War, ultroloths lead yugoloth forces throughout the planes, acting as crime bosses or commanders of evil mercenary companies.
With a reputation for cruelty, ultroloths command their minions to fight while the ultroloths stay removed from combat themselves. Lesser yugoloths know their place when facing an ultroloth and respond to its summons without demand for payment.
combat-strategy: Open with Hypnotic Gaze (DC 17 Wis cone, 30 ft.) on the clustered party—stunned targets until its next turn are free kills for Multiattack's two Mercurial Whips (25 force each, plus teleport the victim 10 ft. into worse positions). Use Fiendish Guile generously: Misty Step to reposition behind cover, Invisibility to vanish and pick fresh angles, Suggestion to turn a party member against their friends, Dispel Magic to strip the caster's buffs. Hover at 60 ft. altitude using hover flight and truesight, raining 5th-level Fireball and Wall of Fire (once per day each) on groups that bunch up, and Dimension Door to escape when the party closes—the 15 ft. whip reach plus teleport lets it punish anyone who thinks they've cornered it. Position its whip range against the back line, pulling squishies off cliffs, into Wall of Fire, or beside gnolls if the pack is nearby. Magic Resistance plus AC 19 make it a patient duelist: fight defensively at range, never let a melee bruiser pin it, and Fiendish Guile away the moment three or more foes can reach it—outside Gehenna it respawns anyway, so it can trade its life for the mission and laugh on the way home.

name: Umber Hulk

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The umber hulk makes three Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Slashing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Confusing Gaze
bonus_actions.description: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 14, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. Failure: The target can't take Reactions until the start of the umber hulk's next turn, and the target rolls 1d8 to determine what it does on its next turn: 1-4. The target does nothing. 5-6. The target takes no action or Bonus Action and uses all its movement to move in a random direction. 7-8. The target makes a melee attack against a random creature within its reach or does nothing if it can't make such an attack.

traits.name: Tunneler
traits.description: The umber hulk can burrow through solid rock at half its Burrow Speed and leaves a 10-foot-diameter tunnel in its wake.

description:
An abominable horror from deep beneath the earth, an umber hulk burrows into cave complexes, dungeons, or Underdark settlements in search of food. Those lucky enough to survive an umber hulk attack often remember precious little of the incident, thanks to the umber hulk's mind-scrambling gaze.

Devious Delvers. Umber hulks can burrow through solid rock, forming new tunnels in their wake. The steel-hard chitin of its body can withstand the cave-ins, tunnel collapses, and rock falls that commonly follow it.
Burrowing into the wall of a cavern or passageway, an umber hulk lies in wait for creatures to pass by on the other side, its hair-like feelers sensing any movement around it. When it explodes out in a shower of earth and rock, its unsuspecting quarry turns to face the oncoming threat-and is entranced by the umber hulk's bewildering eyes, forced to stand helpless as its mandibles snap shut.

Mind Scrambler. Many survivors of an umber hulk encounter recollect little about the attack, because the monster's confusing gaze scrambles their memory of the event. Those who have fought and killed umber hulks recognize the signs. For other denizens of the Underdark, grisly tales of vanished explorers and wanton destruction speak of an unknown foe. Umber hulks take on supernatural status in these harrowing stories, many of which convey the same warning: once an umber hulk has been spotted, it is already too late to escape it.
combat-strategy: Burrow out of the floor beneath the party—Tunneler at 20 ft. burrow speed plus 60 ft. tremorsense means it picks the moment and the spot to erupt, surfacing for a full Multiattack (three Rends, 12 each) the round it appears. Use Confusing Gaze as a bonus action every round on the biggest cluster or the party's leader—DC 14 Wis chaos that strips reactions and turns warriors into random-direction wanderers or friendly-fire swing-machines, and note it costs only a bonus action so the full three-attack turn still happens. Target the front line while gaze chaos isolates the back line; its 10 ft. reach and AC 18 let it stand in melee and trade blows while confused victims stumble into each other. Underground it is apex: fight in tunnels and caverns it has tunneled in advance, and retreat into a 5 ft. crack it has already dug when the fight goes badly—most parties can't follow a burrower through rock. Aboveground in the open, still open with gaze-then-rend, but prefer to drag confused prey toward cover and dig back in when fire magic starts landing.

name: Undead Spirit (Ghostly)

actions.name: Deathly Touch
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d8+3+spell level Necrotic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition until the end of the spirit's next turn.

traits.name: Incorporeal Passage
traits.description: The spirit can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. If it ends its turn inside an object, it is shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and takes 1d10 Force damage for every 5 ft. traveled.

description: An undead spirit summoned by Summon Undead. Ghostly variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: Float through walls—the party's closed doors, locked chests, and shield wall mean nothing to Incorporeal Passage—and open by phasing through solid objects or creatures to reach the rearmost, softest target for Deathly Touch, which also frightens them until its next turn. Attack spellcasters and archers first: flying 40 ft. with no land speed, it dictates engagement range and can dive through the middle of the party to touch a wizard, then drift back through a wall where melee characters can't follow without taking force damage. Its Frightened victims attack at disadvantage, so chain the fear onto whoever is still fighting, touching the same target twice in two rounds if they fail to shake it. End every turn outside a solid object (1d10 force per 5 ft. if shunted out) and hover in corners of rooms or above doorways for hard cover—AC 11 and 30 HP mean it must stay untouchable, not tank: at half HP or against radiant-damage users, phase through the nearest wall and vanish into the structure to return later.

name: Undead Spirit (Putrid)

actions.name: Rotting Claw
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d6+3+spell level Slashing damage. If the target has the Poisoned condition, it has the Paralyzed condition until the end of the spirit's next turn.

traits.name: Festering Aura
traits.description: CON Saving Throw: DC = your spell save DC, any creature (other than the caster) that starts its turn within a 5-foot Emanation originating from the spirit. Failure: The creature has the Poisoned condition until the start of its next turn.

description: An undead spirit summoned by Summon Undead. Putrid variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: Fight at the front of a melee cluster and let Festering Aura do half the work—anyone starting their turn within 5 ft. makes a DC (spell save) Con save or is poisoned, giving attackers disadvantage and setting up the combo. That combo is Rotting Claw on a poisoned target: a hit paralyzes until the end of its next turn, so aura-fail on their turn means a paralysis save-and-suck the moment the spirit's claw lands—stack the aura on the party's martial leader and maul them. Target anyone adjacent already poisoned, prioritizing healing-capable clerics once paralyzed, since a helpless healer is worth more than any damage dealer. Its 5 ft. aura means it's always in the thick of melee: use its 30 HP and Con bonuses to soak, moving so the aura covers healers and archers who hang back at the edge, and if the party's cleric starts blessing away the poison, shift focus to the target who just failed a save rather than the one who's clean. At low HP it keeps swinging—undead don't rout—so retreat doesn't exist; instead it should have died in the worst place, poisoning whoever finished it.

name: Undead Spirit (Skeletal)

actions.name: Crave Bolt
actions.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +spell attack modifier, range 150 ft. Hit: 2d4+3+spell level Necrotic damage.

description: An undead spirit summoned by Summon Undead. Skeletal variant. Uses spell attack modifier and caster's Proficiency Bonus.
combat-strategy: Hang back at max Crave Bolt range—150 ft. outclasses most bows and lets it snipe from courtyards, rooftops, and across chasms the party must cross. Focus whichever party member is most exposed in the open at the moment, since 2d4+3+necrotic per round from untouchable range bleeds a target between every other monster's attacks in an ambush mix. Use cover religiously: its +3 Dex save and 16 Dexterity mean half-cover and full-cover shots are the fight plan, popping out to fire then dropping back behind columns, walls, and railings. With only 20 HP and AC 11, it cannot survive contact—position it on high ground or beyond the party's 30-ft. dash zone so closing costs them a whole turn of free shots, and when the party commits to the chase, retreat along pre-planned routes over roofs or through windows where its low hit points never get tested in melee.

name: Unicorn

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The unicorn makes one Hooves attack and one Radiant Horn attack.

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Radiant Horn
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: The unicorn casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14): At Will: Detect Evil and Good, Druidcraft; 1/Day Each: Calm Emotions, Dispel Evil and Good, Entangle, Pass Without Trace, Word of Recall
actions.save_effect: Targets of the spell's saving throw use the spell save DC 14. Various effects depending on the spell cast: Detect Evil and Good, Druidcraft, Calm Emotions (DC 14 Wisdom save), Dispel Evil and Good, Entangle (DC 14 Dexterity save for half Bludgeoning damage), Pass without Trace (self only), Word of Recall.

bonus_actions.name: Unicorn's Blessing
bonus_actions.description: The unicorn touches another creature with its horn and casts Cure Wounds or Lesser Restoration on that creature, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 2
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, the unicorn can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The unicorn regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Charging Horn
legendary_actions.description: The unicorn moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, and it makes one Radiant Horn attack.

legendary_actions.name: Shimmering Shield
legendary_actions.description: The unicorn targets itself or one creature it can see within 60 feet of itself. The target gains 10 (3d6) Temporary Hit Points, and its AC increases by 2 until the end of the unicorn's next turn. The unicorn can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.
legendary_actions.advisory_message: 10 (3d6) THP + AC+2 until end of unicorn's next turn, self or creature within 60 ft — GM-enforced: no THP/AC-bonus consumer, self-vs-ally chooser, gridless range; rolls ride GM adjudication

lair_actions:
Unicorns dwell in unspoiled forests, particularly where benevolent Fey creatures live.

The region containing a unicorn's lair is changed by its presence, creating the following effects:

Obscuring Foliage. The unicorn and its allies have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks while within 1 mile of the lair.
Positive Energy. Whenever a creature within 1 mile of the lair regains Hit Points from a spell, it regains the maximum number of Hit Points possible. Additionally, the effects of curses are suppressed within 1 mile of the lair.

If the unicorn dies or moves its lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the unicorn fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The unicorn has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
Unicorns dwell i n enchanted forests. Unrelated to the horses it resembles, a unicorn is a celestial creature that wanders sylvan realms, its white form glimmering like starlight.
A unicorn's brow sports a single spiraling horn of ivory whose magical touch can heal the sick and the injured. Its ears catch the words and whispers of the creatures that share its domain, and it knows the tongues of elves and sylvan folk. Unicorns allow good-hearted creatures to enter their woods to hunt or gather food, but they hold evil ever at bay. Foul-hearted creatures seldom leave a unicorn's domain alive.

Divine Guardians. Good deities placed unicorns on the Material Plane to ward away evil and preserve and protect sacred places. Most unicorns protect a bounded realm such as an enchanted forest. However, the gods sometimes send a unicorn to guard sacred artifacts or protect specific creatures. When the forces of darkness strike against an individual the gods wish to protect, they might send that individual to a unicorn's forest, where evil creatures pursue at their peril.
Unicorns most often serve deities of the forest and woodlands, including the gods of benevolent fey. Although all unicorns have natural healing power, some serve the gods in greater capacities, performing miracles normally reserved for high priests.

Forest Lords. A unicorn's forest is a celestial realm where nothing that occurs beneath the sun-dappled leaves escapes the creature's notice. A unicorn hears each breathy tune sung by the elves that reside amid the treetops. It senses where every caterpillar spins its cocoon, each leaf and branch upon which a bright butterfly rests its tired wings.
In a unicorn's forest, a sense of calm pervades. From wolves and foxes to birds, squirrels, and tiny insects, the creatures of a unicorn's domain seem quite tame. Pixies, sprites, satyrs, dryads, and other normally mercurial fey loyally serve a unicorn when they dwell within its woods. Under a unicorn's protection, creatures feel safe from the threat of encroaching civilization and the insidious spread of evil.
A unicorn roams its domain constantly, moving ever so carefully so as not to disturb other denizens. A creature might catch a passing glimpse of the unicorn then suddenly see nothing but the wild woods.

Sacred Horns. A unicorn's horn is the focus of its power, a shard of divine magic wrought in spiraling ivory. Wands of unicorn horn channel powerful magic, while unicorn horn weapons strike with divine force. Wizards can work powdered unicorn horn into potent potions and scroll ink, or use it as a component in eldritch rituals. However, any creature that takes a role, no matter how small, in slaying a unicorn is likely to become the target of divine retribution.

Blessed Mounts. When darkness and evil threaten to overwhelm the mortal world, the gods sometimes see fit to pair a unicorn mount with a champion. A paladin astride a unicorn is a sign of the gods' direct intervention in the affairs of the mortal realm. It is a holy alliance made to cleave the heads from demons and banish devils back to the Nine Hells.
As long as the troubled times of darkness persist, the unicorn stays by the champion, its horn shining brightly to drive back the night. However, if the gods' champion falls from grace or turns from the cause of righteousness and good, the unicorn departs, never to return.
combat-strategy: Unicorns are gentle defenders, not hunters: open with Pass Without Trace or Calm Emotions to shield allies, and let Magic Resistance plus three Legendary Resistances make them nearly immune to control magic. In a fight, use Multiattack (Hooves + Radiant Horn) against the nearest threat while spending bonus actions on Unicorn's Blessing to heal or cure the most wounded ally. Deploy Shimmering Shield each turn on whoever is taking the beating for temp HP and +2 AC, and use Charging Horn as a free movement attack to reposition or close gaps without provoking opportunity attacks. Entangle flying or charging enemies in soft terrain, and if the battle turns hopeless, cast Word of Recall to teleport to safety — a cornered unicorn's real value is its survivability and support, so disengage early via its 50-ft. Speed when allies are safe or it is gravely wounded.

name: Vampire

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The vampire makes two Grave Strike attacks and uses Bite.

actions.name: Grave Strike
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from one of two hands.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 17, one creature within 5 feet that is willing or that has the Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained condition. Failure: 6 (1d4 + 4) Piercing damage plus 13 (3d8) Necrotic damage. The target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken, and the vampire regains Hit Points equal to that amount. A Humanoid reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage and then buried rises the following sunset as a Vampire Spawn under the vampire's control.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 6 (1d4 + 4) Piercing, the target has the Grappled And Incapacitated And Restrained condition.

bonus_actions.name: Charm
bonus_actions.description: The vampire casts Charm Person, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17), and the duration is 24 hours. The Charmed target is a willing recipient of the vampire's Bite, the damage of which doesn't end the spell. When the spell ends, the target is unaware it was Charmed by the vampire.

bonus_actions.name: Shape-Shift
bonus_actions.description: If the vampire isn't in sunlight or running water, it shape-shifts into a Tiny bat (Speed 5 ft., Fly Speed 30 ft.) or a Medium cloud of mist (Speed 5 ft., Fly Speed 20 ft. [hover]), or it returns to its vampire form. Anything it is wearing transforms with it. While in bat form, the vampire can't speak. Its game statistics, other than its size and Speed, are unchanged. While in mist form, the vampire can't take any actions, speak, or manipulate objects. It is weightless and can enter an enemy's space and stop there. If air can pass through a space, the mist can do so, but it can't pass through liquid. It has Resistance to all damage, except the damage it takes from sunlight.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 2
legendary_actions.description: Immediately after another creature's turn, the vampire can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The vampire regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

legendary_actions.name: Beguile
legendary_actions.description: The vampire casts Command, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17). The vampire can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.
legendary_actions.save_effect: Failure: The target obeys the vampire's one-word command on its next turn (GM-enforced — obey-the-command is not a registered condition and no command-word-to-condition consumer exists; Death Knight Dread Authority advisory twin MA-0058). Success: The target is unaffected.

legendary_actions.name: Deathless Strike
legendary_actions.description: The vampire moves up to half its Speed, and it makes one Grave Strike attack.

lair_actions:
Vampires and vampire umbral lords create sanctuaries apart from the living, whether hidden in cosmopolitan cities or sequestered in ruins where they dwelled in life.

The region containing a vampire's lair is warped by its presence, creating the following effects:

Children of the Night. The vampire exerts influence over the animals in its domain. From dusk until dawn, Medium or smaller Beasts have the Charmed condition while within 1 mile of the lair.
Looming Shadows. Shadows within 1 mile of the lair seem to move as if alive. Any creature (excluding the vampire and its allies) that finishes a Short Rest while within 1 mile of the lair must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or gain no benefit from that rest.
Mists. The area within 1 mile of the lair is Lightly Obscured by a persistent, creeping fog. The vampire and any creatures of its choice are unaffected by the fog.

If the vampire dies or moves its lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the vampire fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Misty Escape
traits.description: If the vampire drops to 0 Hit Points outside its resting place, the vampire uses Shape-Shift to become mist (no action required). If it can't use Shape-Shift, it is destroyed. While it has 0 Hit Points in mist form, it can't return to its vampire form, and it must reach its resting place within 2 hours or be destroyed. Once in its resting place, it returns to its vampire form and has the Paralyzed condition until it regains any Hit Points, and it regains 1 Hit Point after spending 1 hour there.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: The vampire can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

traits.name: Vampire Weakness
traits.description: The vampire has these weaknesses: Forbiddance. The vampire can't enter a residence without an invitation from an occupant. Running Water. The vampire takes 20 Acid damage if it ends its turn in running water. Stake to the Heart. If a weapon that deals Piercing damage is driven into the vampire's heart while the vampire has the Incapacitated condition in its resting place, the vampire has the Paralyzed condition until the weapon is removed. Sunlight. The vampire takes 20 Radiant damage if it starts its turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

description:
Awakened to an endless night, vampires hunger for the life they have lost and sate that hunger by drinking the blood of the living. Vampires abhor sunlight, for its touch burns them. They never cast shadows or reflections, and any vampire wishing to move unnoticed among the living keeps to the darkness and far from reflective surfaces.

Dark Desires. Whether or not a vampire retains any memories from its former life, its emotional attachments wither as once-pure feelings become twisted by undeath. Love turns into hungry obsession, while friendship becomes bitter jealousy. In place of emotion, vampires pursue physical symbols of what they crave, so that a vampire seeking love might fixate on a young beauty. A child might become an object of fascination for a vampire obsessed with youth and potential. Others surround themselves with art, books, or sinister items such as torture devices or trophies from creatures they have killed.

Born from Death. Most of a vampire's victims become vampire spawn-ravenous creatures with a vampire's hunger for blood, but under the control of the vampire that created them. If a true vampire allows a spawn to draw blood from its own body, the spawn transforms into a true vampire no longer under its master's control. Few vampires are willing to relinquish their control in this manner. Vampire spawn become free-willed when their creator dies.

Chained to the Grave. Every vampire remains bound to its coffin, crypt, or grave site, where it must rest by day. If a vampire didn't receive a formal burial, it must lie beneath a foot of earth at the place of its transition to undeath. A vampire can move its place of burial by transporting its coffin or a significant amount of grave dirt to another location. Some vampires set up multiple resting places this way.

Undead Nature. Neither a vampire nor a vampire spawn requires air.
combat-strategy: Fight dirty and from the shadows: open with Charm on the most charismatic or isolated PC (the charmed target becomes a willing Bite recipient), or ambush from ceiling perches using Spider Climb and Stealth. The core combo is Multiattack — two Grave Strikes to Grapple (escape DC 14) with both hands, then a guaranteed Bite that drains HP and shrinks HP maximum; use Beguile legendary actions to cast Command on anyone who breaks grappled or dares to interfere ("Kneel," "Halt," "Grovel"). Kite with Deathless Strike hit-and-fade, stay out of sunlight and running water, and use Shape-Shift into mist to cross gaps, evade, or slip into defended rooms when forced. Never fight to the death away from the coffin: Misty Escape at 0 HP only works if the coffin is reachable, so retreat toward it well before damage threatens, hold healers at bay with Command, and if the party invades the resting place, buy time for spawn or minions over sunlight, holy water, and wooden stakes.

name: Vampire Familiar

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The familiar makes two Umbral Dagger attacks.

actions.name: Umbral Dagger
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Piercing damage plus 7 (3d4) Necrotic damage. If the target is reduced to 0 Hit Points by this attack, the target becomes Stable but has the Poisoned condition for 1 hour. While it has the Poisoned condition, the target has the Paralyzed condition.

bonus_actions.name: Deathless Agility
bonus_actions.description: The familiar takes the Dash or Disengage action.

traits.name: Vampiric Connection
