Vampires and vampire umbral lords create sanctuaries apart from the living, whether hidden in cosmopolitan cities or sequestered in ruins where they dwelled in life.

The region containing a vampire's lair is warped by its presence, creating the following effects:

Children of the Night. The vampire exerts influence over the animals in its domain. From dusk until dawn, Medium or smaller Beasts have the Charmed condition while within 1 mile of the lair.
Looming Shadows. Shadows within 1 mile of the lair seem to move as if alive. Any creature (excluding the vampire and its allies) that finishes a Short Rest while within 1 mile of the lair must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or gain no benefit from that rest.
Mists. The area within 1 mile of the lair is Lightly Obscured by a persistent, creeping fog. The vampire and any creatures of its choice are unaffected by the fog.

If the vampire dies or moves its lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance
traits.description: If the vampire fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Shadow Escape
traits.description: If the vampire drops to 0 Hit Points outside its resting place, it teleports into its resting place unless it is in running water or sunlight. If it can't teleport, it is destroyed. Once inside its resting place, it has the Paralyzed condition for 1 hour, after which it regains 1 Hit Point.

traits.name: Vampire Weakness
traits.description: The vampire has these weaknesses: Forbiddance. The vampire can't enter a residence without an invitation from an occupant. Running Water. The vampire takes 20 Acid damage if it ends its turn in running water. Stake to the Heart. If a weapon that deals Piercing damage is driven into the vampire's heart while the vampire has the Incapacitated condition in its resting place, the vampire has the Paralyzed condition until the weapon is removed. Sunlight. The vampire takes 20 Radiant damage if it starts its turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

combat-strategy: A tactical undead artillery duel: open by casting Hunger of Hadar (DC 18) on clustered attackers or a chokepoint, splitting the party and blinding those caught inside while hovering out of reach with 40-ft. fly/hover. Multiattack mixes Sickening Ray (Poisoned condition, which gives you advantage on your own attacks — then punish with Grave Strike melee) and keep casting Hunger of Hadar whenever targets clump; Sanguine Drain every bonus action for free self-healing and HP-max erosion at range. Use Beguile legendary actions to Command healers away or order targets to step into your hazards or melee reach, and Umbral Strike to reposition-and-shoot between turns. With blindsight 120 ft., magical darkness doesn't blind you — turn off the lights; three Legendary Resistances protect against power Word saves, but the umbral lord should still kite, heal through drain, and Shadow Escape to its resting place before damage piles up, emerging later to resume the siege.

name: Venomous Snake

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Poison damage.

combat-strategy: Ambush and single bite: venomous snakes strike once at AC 12 from hiding in grass, rubble, or a bedroll, relying on surprise rounds where a +4 attack is often automatic. Target exposed hands, feet, or lone scouts at the edge of a camp; with only 5 HP, they should bite and burrow/retreat into tight spaces where melee attackers can't reach them. Use them in groups for swarm harassment, or as a plot device: hide one where a PC rests so a single +4 bite deals 4 piercing + 3 poison. They fight without fear or tactics beyond striking and fleeing into crevices (blindsight 10 ft. helps in complete darkness), and they never pursue.

name: Veteran

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The veteran makes two longsword attacks. If it has a shortsword drawn, it can also make a shortsword attack.

actions.name: Longsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) slashing damage if used with two hands.

actions.name: Shortsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.

actions.name: Heavy Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d10 + 1) piercing damage.

description: Veterans are professional fighters that take up arms for pay or to protect something they believe in or value. Their ranks include soldiers retired from long service and warriors who never served anyone but themselves.
combat-strategy: Veterans are disciplined melee anchors: form a shield line in a corridor or doorway and Multiattack (two longswords, plus a shortsword third attack if off-hand drawn) against whatever presses in. Use Heavy Crossbow volleys first at approaching foes (+3 to hit, 100 ft.), then draw swords as the enemy closes; fight shoulder-to-shoulder to cover each other's flanks and focus down isolated characters rather than dividing damage. Hold chokepoints, let the heavily armored bodies buy time for spellcasters or archers behind them, and use Athletics +5 to shove attackers off cliffs or through lines when terrain allows. Retreat only in a organized manner — fall back one rank at a time toward reinforcements; broken morale should look like disciplined withdrawal, not panic.

name: Vine Blight

actions.name: Constricting Vine
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 10 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 12). Until the grapple ends, the target takes 4 (1d8) Bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns, and the blight can't make Constricting Vine attacks.

actions.name: Entangling Plants
actions.description: The blight casts the Entangle spell, using Constitution as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 12).
actions.save_effect: Target has the Restrained condition until the spell ends. Escape: Strength (Athletics) action vs spell save DC 12. Difficult terrain and concentration clauses are GM-enforced.

description:
Appearing a s masses o f slithering creepers, vine blights hide in undergrowth and wait for prey to draw near. By animating the plants around them, vine blights entangle and hinder their foes before attacking. Vine blights are the only blights capable of speech.
Through its connection to the evil spirit of the Gulthias tree it serves, a vine blight speaks in a fractured version of its dead master's voice, taunting victims or bargaining with powerful foes.
combat-strategy: Ambush predators on the forest floor: vine blights lie camouflaged among real vegetation and strike first with Constricting Vine from 10 ft., then rely on the auto-grapple (escape DC 12) to pin prey while constriction bleeds 1d8 damage every round. Cast Entangling Plants (DC 12) when targets bunch or flee, trapping the whole party so blights can grapple the biggest cluster without chasing — they're slow at 20 ft./turn. Grapple priority is casters and archers, then healers; a grappled victim stops the blight's own vine attacks but keeps the damage ticking, so let allies do the killing while it holds. They're fragile (19 HP) and blind to stealth within 60 ft. (blindsight), so use darkness and terrain rather than speed; if a blight is reduced near death it fights on mindlessly — the encounter ends when they're chopped down or fire is used against them.

name: Violet Fungus

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The fungus makes two Rotting Touch attacks.

actions.name: Rotting Touch
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 10 ft. Hit: 4 (1d8) Necrotic damage.

description: This purplish mushroom uses root-like feelers growing from its base to creep across cavern floors. The four stalks protruding from a violet fungi's central mass are used to lash out at prey, rotting flesh with the slightest touch. Any creature killed by a violet fungus decomposes rapidly. A new violet fungus sprouts from the moldering corpse, growing to full size in 2d6 days
combat-strategy: Violet fungi don't hunt — they're living landmines: station clusters in dark, damp cavern passages where 30-ft. blindsight triggers on approaching vibration, then swing two Rotting Touch attacks (10-ft. reach) at anything that steps close. AC 5 means every hit lands, so a patch of 4–6 fungi in a 20-ft. corridor can chew through unarmored PCs fast before being cut down. Use reach 10 ft. to keep attackers entering a zone of necrotic slams while the fungus itself barely moves at 5 ft./turn. They never retreat and don't pursue — treat them as an environmental hazard the party must notice, burn, or sprint past, and let the first surprised round deliver the real damage.

name: Violet Fungus Necrohulk

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The necrohulk makes two Rotting Slam attacks.

actions.name: Rotting Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Spore Bomb
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point the necrohulk can see within 60 feet. Failure: 28 (8d6) Necrotic damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the necrohulk's next turn. While Poisoned, the target can't regain Hit Points. Success: Half damage only.
actions.save_effect: 28 (8d6) Necrotic damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the necrohulk's next turn. While Poisoned, the target can't regain Hit Points. Success: Half damage only

bonus_actions.name: Absorb Body
bonus_actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 15, one Medium or Small creature the necrohulk can see within 5 feet. Failure: The target is pulled into the necrohulk's space and becomes grafted to its body. The necrohulk can have only one target grafted at a time. While grafted, the target has the Restrained condition and Disadvantage on Constitution saving throws. When the necrohulk moves, the grafted target moves with it. If the target dies while grafted, its body is destroyed, and the necrohulk regains 10 Hit Points. The grafted target or a creature within 5 feet of the necrohulk can take an action to make a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check. On a successful check, the target is no longer grafted and moves to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the necrohulk.

combat-strategy: Open with Spore Bomb (DC 15) on the tightest party cluster — 8d6 necrotic and no-HP-regeneration while poisoned is fight-defining, so throw it early and again whenever targets regroup into the 20-ft. sphere. Close at 40 ft. speed and Multiattack Rotting Slams (10-ft. reach), then Bonus Action Absorb Body to graft the nearest Medium/Small straggler: Restrained, disadvantage on Con saves (set up future Spore Bombs), dragged along and destroyed if they die mid-grapple. The grafted body is both a hostage and a meat-shield — opponents must spend actions on DC 15 Athletics checks to free it while you keep swinging. Kite between bursts, keep the grafted target between you and heavy hitters, and when down to about 40 HP, back toward deeper fungal growth or darkness to heal by absorption rather than stand and trade blows in open ground.

name: Vrock

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The vrock makes two Shred attacks.

actions.name: Shred
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Spores
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 20-foot Emanation originating from the vrock. Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. While Poisoned, the target takes 5 (1d10) Poison damage at the start of each of its turns. Emptying a flask of Holy Water on the target ends the effect early.
actions.save_effect: The target has the Poisoned condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. While Poisoned, the target takes 5 (1d10) Poison damage at the start of each of its turns. Emptying a flask of Holy Water on the target ends the effect early

actions.name: Stunning Scream
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 20-foot Emanation originating from the vrock (demons succeed automatically). Failure: 10 (3d6) Thunder damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the end of the vrock's next turn.
actions.save_effect: 10 (3d6) Thunder damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the end of the vrock's next turn

traits.name: Demonistic Restoration
traits.description: If the vrock dies outside the Abyss, its body dissolves into ichor, and it gains a new body instantly, reviving with all its Hit Points somewhere in the Abyss.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: The vrock has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

description:
Vrocks are dull-witted, capricious fiends that live only to create pain and carnage. A vrock resembles a giant hybrid of humanoid and vulture, its gnarled, bestial body and broad wings stinking of offal.
Vrocks gobble humanoid flesh whenever they can, stunning potential prey with an ear-splitting shriek, then swooping down to attack with beak and claw. Vrocks can shake their wings, releasing clouds of toxic spores.
Coveting pretty things, vrocks turn against each other for the chance to lay claim to cheap jewelry or ornamental stones. Despite their love of treasure, vrocks are difficult to bribe, seeing no reason to bargain when they can simply take what they want from a would-be bargainer's corpse.
combat-strategy: A demon bruiser that wants to be in the middle of the scrum: dive in with 60-ft. flight, land on top of the party, and pop Stunning Scream (DC 15) on the biggest cluster to stun key casters until the end of your next turn while demons nearby stay immune. Follow with Multiattack Shred (piercing + poison) on stunned or isolated targets, and breathe Spores (DC 15 emanation) on anyone who clusters to focus you — ongoing 1d10 poison per turn and repeat saves keep pressure even after they escape. Magic Resistance gives advantage on spell saves, so walk through fireballs; the fear is banishment or holy water, so keep the fight fast and brutal. With 152 HP and pack support, hold the center, grab healers with movement + Shred, and if banished or overwhelmed, break contact and re-enter the fray — true death only if killed on the Material Plane by good-aligned force, so provoke desperate melee far from temples.

name: Vulture

actions.name: Beak
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 2 (1d4) Piercing damage.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The vulture has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the vulture's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

combat-strategy: Vultures barely fight — they scavenge. In combat they opportunistically swoop at wounded or prone creatures (50-ft. fly lets them dive in, Peck once, and lift back out of reach), using Pack Tactics to gain advantage whenever another vulture or a fallen ally is beside the target. Treat them as atmosphere and warning: their circling telegraphs a dead or dying creature nearby, so a GM can use them as a stalking sign for something nastier. Use small flocks (4–8) to harass retreating, bloodied parties over open ground, keeping just out of melee reach since 5 HP means a single attack usually kills one. They flee after one or two casualties, using Fly speed to disengage.

name: Warhorse

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d4 + 4) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature and the horse moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 5 (2d4) Bludgeoning damage and has the Prone condition.

conditional_damage.condition: moved 20+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit

combat-strategy: Warhorses are mounts and charges: if unmounted, back them against walls or between allies to avoid trampling confusion, and use the signature 20+ ft. straight-line charge into Hooves for extra 2d4 damage and knocking the target Prone. As a mount, pair with a veteran or knight for hit-and-run: charge, strike, wheel away with 60-ft. speed while the rider attacks. Target isolated infantry, archers, or spellcasters in open terrain where a run-up is possible; use the trample-Prone combo to drop armored foes so riders or allies can finish them prone. They're only 19 HP and won't fight to the death — a wounded warhorse bolts toward its rider or cover unless trained and handled well.

name: Warhorse Skeleton

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature and the skeleton moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target has the Prone condition.

combat-strategy: Fearless undead cavalry: ride hard at enemies it can't be scared away from, repeating the 20-ft. charge + Hooves knockdown cycle — Prone targets get attacked by riders or skeleton warriors with advantage while the mount tramples again next round. No morale means it can charge into melee, wheel, and charge again even while being battered; use it to break shield lines in open corridors or courtyards where a straight run exists. Only 22 HP and AC 13, so don't let it stand in a sustained brawl — trample, reposition with 60-ft. speed, trample again. Against ranged parties, loop behind ruins or other undead for cover between charges, and if it drops, its rider dismounts and fights on — the skeleton is a delivery system, not a destination.

name: Warrior Commander

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The warrior makes three attacks, using Greatsword or Longbow in any combination.

actions.name: Greatsword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 19 (4d6 + 5) Slashing damage. The warrior also creates one of the following effects: Sap. The target has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of the warrior's next turn. Maneuver. One ally who can see or hear the warrior can take a Reaction to move up to half the ally's Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +9, range 150/600 ft. Hit: 18 (3d8 + 5) Piercing damage, and the target's Speed decreases by 10 feet until the end of the target's next turn.

bonus_actions.name: Tactical Charge
bonus_actions.description: The warrior moves up to half its Speed straight toward an enemy it can see without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

reactions.name: Counterattack
reactions.trigger: The warrior is hit by an attack roll.
reactions.description: The warrior adds 4 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss. On a miss, the warrior can make one Greatsword or Longbow attack against the attacker.

automation.description: RAW: +4 AC against the triggering attack roll (parry channel, pending-Done window). On a miss, one Greatsword or Longbow attack against the attacker is GM-adjudicated — no counterattack subsystem in-app (MA-0891-class advisory residual). Ranged triggers refuse honestly (parry gate melee-only, MA-1203). Chip label 'Parry' on a Counterattack-named row is channel-generic (MA-1203 precedent).

combat-strategy: A battlefield quarterback with devastating output: open with Longbow volleys (three +9 attacks, each slowing target speed 10 ft.) while enemies approach, then Tactical Charge (free movement, no opportunity attacks) to slam into the priority target with Greatsword Multiattack. Every greatsword hit picks between Sap (advantage denial on the strongest attacker) and Maneuver (an ally's free repositioning reaction) — Sap the boss-damage dealer, Maneuver allies into position for flanks or out of danger. Counterattack reaction turns the commander into a punisher: +4 AC to make foes miss, then a free Greatsword or Longbow swing back, so bait attacks into it. Hold the line where allies can see and hear it to trigger Maneuver, focus isolated casters, and only withdraw while counterattacking backward — it's durable enough (161 HP, AC 18) to finish any duel it starts.

name: Warrior Infantry

actions.name: Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) Piercing damage.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The warrior has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the warrior's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

combat-strategy: Cannon fodder with a point: mass them in formation and throw Spears at 20–60 ft. before the enemy closes, then level the line and rely on Pack Tactics — surround targets in pairs or threes so multiple infantry attack with advantage. Never let one stand alone: isolated spearmen get cut down one by one (9 HP each), so keep tight ranks that mutually flank and cover gaps. Archers and spellcasters behind them should shoot over the spear wall while infantry hold contact. As casualties hit roughly half the unit, command presence or an officer should trigger a disciplined fallback to the next defensive line; otherwise they rout, and routing infantry drop their formation and become easy prey.

name: Warrior Veteran

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The warrior makes two Greatsword or Heavy Crossbow attacks.

actions.name: Greatsword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Heavy Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +3, range 100/400 ft. Hit: 12 (2d10 + 1) Piercing damage.

reactions.name: Parry
reactions.trigger: The warrior is hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon.
reactions.description: The warrior adds 2 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

combat-strategy: An armored wall with Parry: advance behind shielded allies or into a chokepoint, opening with Heavy Crossbow shots (+3, 12 damage) before switching to Greatsword Multiattack (two +5 swings) in melee. Use Parry sparingly and reactively — save it for the round's biggest attack (a rogue's sneak or a paladin's smite swing) since +2 AC can flip the blow, then punish with both greatsword attacks next turn. Fight defensively, let enemy offense break on its AC 17/Parry, then take over the fight in sustained exchanges where superior HP (65) wins attrition. Target enemy front-liners who can't kite it; if outflanked by fliers or spellcasters, fall back one step toward cover or the commander rather than being isolated, keeping allies adjacent to deny flanking advantage.

name: Water Elemental

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The elemental makes two Slam attacks.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Whelm
actions.description: Strength Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in the elemental's space. Failure: 22 (4d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14). Until the grapple ends, the target has the Restrained condition, is suffocating unless it can breathe water, and takes 9 (2d8) Bludgeoning damage at the start of each of the elemental's turns. The elemental can grapple one Large creature or up to two Medium or smaller creatures at a time with Whelm. As an action, a creature within 5 feet of the elemental can pull a creature out of it by succeeding on a DC 14 Strength (Athletics) check.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 22 (4d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14). Until the grapple ends, the target has the Restrained condition, is suffocating unless it can breathe water, and takes 9 (2d8) Bludgeoning damage at the start of each of the elemental's turns.

traits.name: Freeze
traits.description: If the elemental takes Cold damage, its Speed decreases by 20 feet until the end of its next turn.

traits.name: Water Form
traits.description: The elemental can enter an enemy's space and stop there. It can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so.

description: A water elemental i s a cresting wave that rolls across the ground, becoming nearly invisible at it courses through a larger body of water. It engulfs creatures that stand against it, filling their mouths and lungs as easily as it smothers flame.
combat-strategy: Fight where water flows: open by surging out of a river, pool, or flooded chamber at 90-ft. swim speed and Whelm the biggest cluster — up to two Medium creatures restrained, suffocating, and auto-hitting for 2d8 each turn while your Slam knocks others Prone. Use Water Form to move through grates, pipes, and 1-inch cracks to flank or reach unexpected spaces, entering enemy spaces and stopping there to force Whelm saves. Drag grappled victims toward deep water or under the surface to suffocate non-water-breathers while allies finish prone targets on shore. Its critical weakness is Freeze (cold damage cuts speed 20 ft.) and arid terrain — avoid cone of cold and boiled-dry zones, retreat into deeper water to heal and vanish when hurt, and only fight inland if a water source offers an escape route.

name: Water Weird

actions.name: Surge
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) Cold damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13), and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.

traits.name: Invisible in Water
traits.description: The water weird has the Invisible condition while fully immersed in water.

traits.name: Water Bound
traits.description: The water weird dies if it leaves the water to which it is bound or if that water is destroyed.

description:
A water weird is an elemental guardian bound to a specific water-filled location, such as a pool or fountain. Invisible while immersed in water, its serpentine shape becomes clear only when it emerges to attack, using its coils to crush any creature other than its summoner and those its summoner declares as off limits. When slain, a water weird becomes an inanimate pool of water.

Good and Evil Weirds. Like most elementals, a water weird has no concept of good or evil. However, a water weird bound to a sacred or befouled source of water begins to take on the nature of that site, becoming neutral good or neutral evil.
A neutral good water weird tries to frighten away interlopers rather than kill them, while a neutral evil water weird kills its victims for pleasure and might turn against its summoner. A water weird loses its evil alignment if its waters are cleansed with a purify food and drink spell.

Elemental Nature. A water weird doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: An ambush grappler bound to one pool: stay fully immersed where Invisible in Water makes attacks against it impossible, waiting for anyone to wade, swim, or draw water within reach. Strike with Surge (10-ft. reach) from concealment — a hit grapples and Restrains (escape DC 13), then drag the victim underwater to drown while other victims panic. Target the lone or trailing party members entering the water, hauling them under; grappled prey can't reach the surface, and the weird's 60-ft. swim speed lets it haul bodies away from rescuers. It dies if it leaves its bound water, so fight at the pool's edge only, keep the target between you and the deep, and drown victims in the deepest water before the party can pull them free or burn the pool away.

name: Weasel

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage.

combat-strategy: A weasel is not a combatant — it's a distraction, a spy, or a snack. If cornered it bites (+5, 1 damage) and dives into burrows, drains, or clutter where 30-ft. climb and speed make it untouchable; use it to steal a shiny item, knock a vial over, or slip through a barred grate and report by coming and going. In play, its real value is noncombat: Perception +3 and Stealth +5 make it a plausible scout for a druid, fey, or spymaster, and its Tiny size lets it hide in plain sight on a person. It flees instantly at any real threat, since 1 HP means any missed attack or careless step kills it.

name: Werebear

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The werebear makes two attacks, using Handaxe or Rend in any combination. It can replace one attack with a Bite attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 17 (2d12 + 4) Piercing damage. If the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 14. Failure: The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes a Werebear under the DM's control and has 10 Hit Points. Success: The target is immune to this werebear's curse for 24 hours.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes a Werebear under the DM's control and has 10 Hit Points. Success: The target is immune to this werebear's curse for 24 hours.

actions.name: Handaxe
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Slashing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Shape-Shift
bonus_actions.description: The werebear shape-shifts into a Large bear-humanoid hybrid form or a Large bear, or it returns to its true humanoid form. Its game statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

description:
Werebears are powerful lycanthropes with the ability to temper their monstrous natures and reject their violent impulses. In humanoid form, they are large, muscular, and covered in hair matching the color of their ursine form's fur. A werebear is a loner by nature, fearing what might happen to innocent creatures around it when its bestial nature takes over.
When a werebear transforms, it grows to enormous size, lashing out with weapons or claws. It fights with the ferocity of a bear, though even in its bestial forms, it avoids biting so as to not pass on its curse. Typically, a werebear passes on its lycanthropy only to chosen companions or apprentices, spending the time that follows helping the new lycanthrope accept the curse in order to control it.
Solitary creatures, werebears act as wardens over their territory, protecting flora and fauna alike from humanoid or monstrous intrusion. Though most werebears are of good alignment, some are every bit as evil as other lycanthropes.
combat-strategy: An unstoppable front-line tank: open by Shape-Shifting (bonus action) into hybrid or bear form and charging into the thickest melee, Multiattacking Handaxe/Rend for brutal 14–13-swing damage. Bite humanoids to curse them (DC 14) — the curse turns a future death into an ally under your control, so mark key humanoids early and let the fight grind toward it. Throw Handaxes at charging range closers before they arrive, then Rend the biggest threats. 135 HP and 19 Str mean it wins head-on fights; use Athletics (implicit in the bulk) to bull-rush or drag opponents prone when a Strength contest is allowed, and simply stand between enemies and the weaker pack members. It rarely retreats unless reduced below ~30 HP or silvered — silver weapons should make it break off toward cover or cover a retreat.

name: Wereboar

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The wereboar makes two attacks, using Javelin or Tusk in any combination. It can replace one attack with a Gore attack.

actions.name: Gore
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Piercing damage. If the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12. Failure: The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes a Wereboar under the DM's control and has 10 Hit Points. Success: The target is immune to this wereboar's curse for 24 hours.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes a Wereboar under the DM's control and has 10 Hit Points. Success: The target is immune to this wereboar's curse for 24 hours.

actions.name: Javelin
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Tusk
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature and the wereboar moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 7 (2d6) Piercing damage and has the Prone condition.

conditional_damage.condition: moved 20+ feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit

bonus_actions.name: Shape-Shift
bonus_actions.description: The wereboar shape-shifts into a Medium boar-humanoid hybrid or a Small boar, or it returns to its true humanoid form. Its game statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

description:
Wereboars are ill-tempered and vulgar brutes. As humanoids, they are stocky and muscular, with short, stiff hair. In their humanoid and hybrid forms, they use heavy weapons, while in hybrid or animal form, they gain a devastating goring attack through which their curse is spread. A wereboar infects other creatures indiscriminately, relishing the fact that the more its victims resist the curse, the more savage and bestial they become.
Wereboars live in small family groups in remote forest areas, building ramshackle huts or dwelling in caves. They are suspicious of strangers but sometimes ally themselves with ogres.
combat-strategy: A charging nightmare: open with Javelin volleys (30/120 ft.) at ranged targets, then close and repeat Tusk charges — move 20+ ft. straight at a target for the +2d6 bonus damage and knock them Prone, where the wereboar's Multiattack continues to punish. Gore humanoids to infect the curse (DC 12), prioritizing stubborn human fighters or villagers it wants raised as allies later. Its 30-ft. speed makes the charge setup real: wheel out of reach, circle, and re-charge repeatedly in open terrain, never standing still to trade blows in corridors where momentum dies. It fights with reckless aggression and won't quit until killed, but a wise GM has it flee toward thickets or its lair when down ~30 HP, dragging cursed victims with it if possible.

name: Wererat

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The wererat makes two attacks, using Scratch or Hand Crossbow in any combination. It can replace one attack with a Bite attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) Piercing damage. If the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 11. Failure: The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes a Wererat under the DM's control and has 10 Hit Points. Success: The target is immune to this wererat's curse for 24 hours.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes a Wererat under the DM's control and has 10 Hit Points. Success: The target is immune to this wererat's curse for 24 hours.

actions.name: Scratch
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Hand Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +5, range 30/120 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Shape-Shift
bonus_actions.description: The wererat shape-shifts into a Medium rat-humanoid hybrid or a Small rat, or it returns to its true humanoid form. Its game statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

description:
Wererats are cunning lycanthropes with sly, avaricious personalities. They are wiry and twitchy in humanoid form, with thin hair and darting eyes. In their humanoid and hybrid forms, wererats prefer light weapons and use ambush tactics rather than fighting as a pack. Although a wererat can deliver a nasty bite in its rat form, it favors that form for stealthy infiltration and escape rather than combat.
A wererat clan operates much like a thieves' guild, with wererats transmitting their curse only to creatures they want to induct into the clan. Wererats that are accidentally cursed or break loose from the clan's control are quickly hunted down and killed.
Wererat clans are found throughout urban civilization, often dwelling in cellars and catacombs. These creatures are common in the sewers beneath major cities, viewing those subterranean areas as their hunting grounds. Rats and giant rats are commonly found living among wererats.
combat-strategy: A sneaky ambusher: open in humanoid form disguised among refugees, servants, or prisoners, then reveal with a multiattack of Scratch + Bite once the party is split or the target turns away. Hand Crossbow shots from 30 ft. before closing allow hit-and-run through sewers, drains, and Tiny crawlspaces (climb 30 ft.) where armored PCs can't follow. Bite humanoids (DC 11 curse) on isolated victims — wererats are cowards who ambush weak targets, never dueling the martial front line. Use Shape-Shift into rat form to slip through cracks, escape, or infiltrate between encounters; it breaks off and flees into the walls at the first sign of real resistance or once below ~20 HP, returning with a gang of rat swarms later.

name: Weretiger

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The weretiger makes two attacks, using Scratch or Longbow in any combination. It can replace one attack with a Bite attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Piercing damage. If the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13. Failure: The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes a Weretiger under the DM's control and has 10 Hit Points. Success: The target is immune to this weretiger's curse for 24 hours.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes a Weretiger under the DM's control and has 10 Hit Points. Success: The target is immune to this weretiger's curse for 24 hours.

actions.name: Scratch
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 150/600 ft. Hit: 11 (2d8 + 2) Piercing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Prowl
bonus_actions.description: The weretiger moves up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. At the end of this movement, the weretiger can take the Hide action.

bonus_actions.name: Shape-Shift
bonus_actions.description: The weretiger shape-shifts into a Large tiger-humanoid hybrid or a Large tiger, or it returns to its true humanoid form. Its game statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

description:
Weretigers are ferocious hunters and warriors with a haughty and fastidious nature. Lithe and sleekly muscular in humanoid form, they are taller than average and meticulously groomed. Weretigers grow to enormous size in animal and hybrid form, but they fight in their more refined humanoid form when they can. They don't like to pass on their curse, because every new weretiger means competition for territory and prey.
Weretigers live in jungles on the fringes of humanoid civilization, traveling to isolated settlements to trade or revel. They live and hunt alone or in small family groups.
combat-strategy: A stealth assassin that opens with Prowl (full-speed movement without opportunity attacks, ending in Hide) through tall grass or jungle, striking from concealment with Scratch or Longbow shots. Multiattack from hiding, replacing one attack with Bite to curse humanoids (DC 13) — the curse makes killing it the party's problem, since cursed humanoids who later fall join it as a 10 HP thrall under your control. Fight hit-and-hide: strike, Prowl away with a fresh Hide each turn, forcing PCs to win Perception checks to even see it; its AC 12 demands it never stand in the open. Snipe spellcasters at range, isolate stragglers, and vanish between kills; at low HP or against concentrated fire, shift to tiger form and melt into the undergrowth to recover and hunt again at night.

name: Werewolf

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The werewolf makes two attacks, using Scratch or Longbow in any combination. It can replace one attack with a Bite attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Piercing damage. If the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12. Failure: The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes a Werewolf under the DM's control and has 10 Hit Points. Success: The target is immune to this werewolf's curse for 24 hours.
actions.save_effect: Failure: The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes a Werewolf under the DM's control and has 10 Hit Points. Success: The target is immune to this werewolf's curse for 24 hours.

actions.name: Scratch
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 150/600 ft. Hit: 11 (2d8 + 2) Piercing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Shape-Shift
bonus_actions.description: The werewolf shape-shifts into a Large wolf-humanoid hybrid or a Medium wolf, or it returns to its true humanoid form. Its game statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The werewolf has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the werewolf's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

description:
A werewolf is a savage predator. In its humanoid form, a werewolf has heightened senses, a fiery temper, and a tendency to eat rare meat. Its wolf form is a fearsome predator, but its hybrid form is more terrifying by far-a furred and well-muscled humanoid body topped by a ravening wolf's head. A werewolf can wield weapons in hybrid form, though it prefers to tear foes apart with its powerful claws and bite.
Most werewolves flee civilized lands not long after becoming afflicted. Those that reject the curse fear what will happen if they remain among their friends and family. Those that embrace the curse fear discovery and the consequences of their murderous acts. In the wild, werewolves form packs that also include wolves and dire wolves.
combat-strategy: Open in wolf or hybrid form and charge the weakest-looking party member, using Pack Tactics by coordinating with other werewolves or allies so attacks land with Advantage. Prioritize Humanoids with Bite to spread the lycanthropy curse — a cursed PC who later drops to 0 HP becomes a thrall, so keep the pressure on cursed targets rather than finishing them outright. Sequencing: use Shape-Shift as a bonus action to shed suspicious gear or grab reach advantages, then Multiattack with two Scratches plus a Bite on a Humanoid. Fight in packs near cover or at night where Stealth matters, circling to keep an ally adjacent to the target every round. Retreat into the dark or assume humanoid form to melt into a settlement when reduced to roughly a quarter HP, healing before returning.

name: White Dragon Wyrmling

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dragon makes two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Slashing damage plus 2 (1d4) Cold damage.

actions.name: Cold Breath
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: 22 (5d8) Cold damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 22 (5d8) Cold damage. Success: Half damage.

traits.name: Ice Walk
traits.description: The dragon can move across and climb icy surfaces without needing to make an ability check. Additionally, Difficult Terrain composed of ice or snow doesn't cost it extra movement.

combat-strategy: Young and feral, it opens with Cold Breath on the tightest cluster of enemies, then closes with its 60-ft. fly speed to Multiattack with two Rend attacks. Target stragglers and smaller creatures, using its flight to stay out of reach of martial types and dive in only when it can strike and pull away. Fight over ice or snow where Ice Walk lets it treat difficult terrain as open ground — lure foes onto slick surfaces it can cross freely while they slow. Avoid melee against big damage dealers; its 32 HP evaporates fast, so hit-and-run, repositioning above the party between attacks. Flee into water or a burrow when reduced to about a quarter HP.

name: Wight

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The wight makes two attacks, using Necrotic Sword or Necrotic Bow in any combination. It can replace one attack with a use of Life Drain.

actions.name: Necrotic Sword
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Necrotic Bow
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 150/600 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Life Drain
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature within 5 feet. Failure: 6 (1d8 + 2) Necrotic damage, and the target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the damage taken. A Humanoid slain by this attack rises 24 hours later as a Zombie under the wight's control, unless the Humanoid is restored to life or its body is destroyed. The wight can have no more than twelve zombies under its control at a time.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 6 (1d8 + 2) Necrotic damage, and the target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the damage taken. A Humanoid slain by this attack rises 24 hours later as a Zombie under the wight's control, unless the Humanoid is restored to life or its body is destroyed. The wight can have no more than twelve zombies under its control at a time.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: While in sunlight, the wight has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls.

description:
The word "wight" meant "person" in days ofyore, but the name now refers to evil undead who were once mortals driven by dark desire and great vanity. When death stills such a creature's heart and snuffs its living breath, its spirit cries out to the demon lord Orcus or some vile god of the underworld for a reprieve: undeath in return for eternal war on the living. If a dark power answers the call, the spirit is granted undeath so that it can pursue its own malevolent agenda.
Wights possess the memories and drives of their formerly living selves. They will heed the call of whatever dark entity transformed them into undead, swearing oaths to appease their new lord while retaining their autonomy. Never tiring, a wight can pursue its goals relentlessly and without distraction.

Life Eaters. Neither dead nor alive, a wight exists in a transitional state between one world and the next. The bright spark it possessed in life is gone, and in its place is a yearning to consume that spark in all living things. When a wight attacks, this life essence glows like white­ hot embers to its dark eyes, and the wight's cold touch can drain the spark through flesh, clothing, and armor.

Shadow of the Grave. Wights flee from the world by day, away from the light of the sun, which they hate. They retreat to barrow mounds, crypts, and tombs where they dwell. Their lairs are silent, desolate places, surrounded by dead plants, noticeably blackened, and avoided by bird and beast.
Humanoids slain by a wight can rise as zombies under its control. Motivated by hunger for living souls and driven by the same desire for power that awakened them in undeath, some wights serve as shock troops for evil leaders, including wraiths. As soldiers, they are able to plan but seldom do so, relying on their hunger for destruction to overwhelm any creature that stands before them.

Undead Nature. A wight doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Ambush from darkness or underground — Sunlight Sensitivity cripples it in daylight, so pick night, dusk, or dungeon fights. Open with Life Drain on a wounded or low-Con target to permanently shave HP maximums, then Multiattack with Necrotic Sword/Bow mixes. Prioritize humanoids it can convert: use Life Drain on someone already near death to build its zombie army (max twelve), and let zombies body-block while it attacks from range with Necrotic Bow. Keep enemies killing zombies with their action economy while it drains the healers and spellcasters. Retreat to deeper darkness when the party's radiant or fire output starts tearing into it, dragging corpses along to raise later.

name: Will-o'-Wisp
damage_resistances: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical weapons
languages: the languages it knew in life

actions.name: Shock
actions.description: Melee Spell Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 9 (2d8) lightning damage.

actions.name: Invisibility
actions.description: The will-o'-wisp and its light magically become invisible until it attacks or uses its Consume Life, or until its concentration ends (as if concentrating on a spell).

traits.name: Consume Life
traits.description: As a bonus action, the will-o'-wisp can target one creature it can see within 5 ft. of it that has 0 hit points and is still alive. The target must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw against this magic or die. If the target dies, the will-o'-wisp regains 10 (3d6) hit points.

traits.name: Ephemeral
traits.description: The will-o'-wisp can't wear or carry anything.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.description: The will-o'-wisp can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

traits.name: Variable Illumination
traits.description: The will-o'-wisp sheds bright light in a 5- to 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional number of ft. equal to the chosen radius. The will-o'-wisp can alter the radius as a bonus action.

description:
Will-o'-wisps are malevolent, wispy balls of light that haunt lonely places and battlefields, bound by dark fate or dark magic to feed on fear and despair.

Hope and Doom. Will-o'-wisps look like bobbing lantern lights in the distance, although they can choose to alter their colors, or wink out completely. When they activate their lights, will-o'-wisps offer hope, hinting of safety to creatures that follow them.
Will-o'-wisps lure unwary creatures into quicksand pits, monster lairs, and other dangerous places so that they can feed on the suffering of their prey and revel in their death screams. An evil being that falls prey to a will-o'-wisp might become a wisp itself, its woeful spirit coalescing above its lifeless corpse like a flickering flame.

Consumed by Despair. Will-o'-wisps are the souls of evil beings that perished in anguish or misery as they wandered forsaken lands permeated with powerful magic. They thrive in swampy bogs and bone-strewn battlefields where the oppressive weight of sorrow stoops even heavier than the low-hanging mist and fog. Trapped in these desolate places of lost hope and memory, will-o'-wisps lure other creatures toward dismal fates and feed on their misery.

Agents of Evil. Will-o'-wisps rarely speak, but when they do, their voices sound like faint or distant whispers. In the miserable domains they haunt, will-o'-wisps sometimes form symbiotic relationships with their wicked neighbors. Hags, oni, black dragons, and evil cultists work with will-o'-wisps to draw creatures into ambush. As their evil allies surround and slaughter creatures, the wisps hover above them, drinking the agony of a last breath and savoring the sensation as the light of life goes out in a creature's eyes.

Undead Nature. A will-o'-wisp doesn't require air, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Hunt at night in fog, marsh, or deep dark where its invisibility and Variable Illumination lure travellers off the path. Open with Invisibility, drift close using Incorpororeal Movement through obstacles, then drop Consume Life on any downed PC each round — the DC 10 Con save means fallen allies often die outright and it heals 10 HP, so the party must spend actions picking it up or killing it fast. Pick fights where low-damage or nonmagical weapons are in play: AC 19, resistance to most damage, and immunity to lightning, poison, grapples, and weapons-heavy tactics make it nearly untouchable. Kite by flying 50 ft. out of melee, staying invisible except for the strike round, and Shock the lone straggler. Vanish and sink into water or undergrowth if it faces concentrated magical fire.

name: Winged Kobold

actions.name: Dragon-Tooth Blade
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Chromatic Spitfire
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +5, range 30 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) damage of a type chosen by the kobold: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The kobold has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the kobold's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: While in sunlight, the kobold has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls.

description: A few kobolds are born with leathery wings and can fly. Known as urds, they like to lurk on high ledges and drop rocks on passerby.  Although the urds' wings are seen as gifts from Tiamat, the Dragon Queen, wingless kobolds are envious of those gifts and don't get along with the urds.
combat-strategy: Never fight alone: swarm in groups of six or more so Pack Tactics gives every Dragon-Tooth Blade and Chromatic Spitfire Advantage. Open with a dive-bomb from the air using Chromatic Spitfire — pick the damage type that exploits the target (acid on metal armor, lightning in wet caves) — then stay airborne or dart back where the swarm's numbers give cover. Target isolated or low-AC party members, surrounding so at least one ally is adjacent each round. Sunlight hurts, so favor caves, night, or overcast skies; hang near the ceiling where climbers and non-flyers waste movement. Scatter and flee into tight crevices when casualties hit half the flock or a fireball-class spell lands.

name: Winter Wolf

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Cold Breath
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: 18 (4d8) Cold damage. Success: Half damage.
actions.save_effect: Failure: 18 (4d8) Cold damage. Success: Half damage.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The wolf has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the wolf's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

description: The arctic-dwelling winter wolf is as large as a dire wolf but has snow-white fur and pale blue eyes. Frost giants use these evil creatures as guards and hunting companions, putting the wolves' deadly breath weapon to use against their foes. Winter wolves communicate with one another using growls and barks, but they speak Common and Giant well enough to follow simple conversations.
combat-strategy: Run it down: 50 ft. speed lets it choose when the fight starts, so ambush from stealth in snow where its Stealth +5 and white coat hide it. Open with Cold Breath across the clustered party, then Bite the same targets — knocking Large-or-smaller creatures Prone means the wolf pack attacks prone targets with Advantage via Pack Tactics all round. Focus the squishiest rear-rank member, flanking with other wolves so someone is always adjacent. Prefer open frozen ground where its speed dominates and enemies can't reach behind it. Prefer open frozen ground where its speed dominates and enemies can't reach behind it. Retreat once half the pack falls or it takes heavy damage, leading pursuers into drifts and blizzards where Stealth resets the ambush.

name: Wisp

traits.name: Ephemeral
traits.description: The wisp can't wear or carry anything.

traits.name: Illumination
traits.description: The wisp sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.description: The wisp can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

actions.name: Shock
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d8 + 2) Lightning damage.

bonus_actions.name: Consume Life
bonus_actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 10, one living creature the wisp can see within 5 feet that has 0 Hit Points. Failure: The target dies, and the wisp regains 10 (3d6) Hit Points.

bonus_actions.name: Vanish
bonus_actions.description: The wisp and its light have the Invisible condition until the wisp's Concentration ends on this effect, which ends early immediately after the wisp makes an attack roll or uses Consume Life.

combat-strategy: Fight in dark, enclosed places where its 20-ft. bright light is itself the bait. Open with Vanish to go invisible (its light vanishing too), fly 50 ft. hover-movement to a downed or isolated PC, and pop out with Shock; as a bonus action Consume Life any fallen ally — DC 10 Con or they die and it heals, forcing the party to spend actions on revival. With AC 19, hovering flight, Incorporeal Movement through walls, and immunity to grapples and nonmagical weapons, it trades nothing: strike, vanish, relocate through solid rock. Concentrate fire is the only counter, so never let it be cornered; melt away through stone into deep dark when it takes meaningful damage or all targets stay standing and healthy.

name: Wolf

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.description: The wolf has Advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the wolf's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

combat-strategy: Hunt in a pack — alone it's a nuisance, in a pack of four or more Pack Tactics turns Bite into a consistent threat with Advantage. Open by encircling: spread out at 40 ft. speed, close on all sides simultaneously so at least one wolf is adjacent to every target. Focus the weakest or isolated member — wizard, rogue, or a wounded fighter — and Bite to knock them Prone, after which every wolf in the pack gets Advantage on the grounded prey. Bite, don't wrestle: knock prone, disengage, and re-bite from another side. Scatter into thick cover when half the pack is dead or the prey keeps standing, breaking contact and re-circling.

name: Worg

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage, and the next attack roll made against the target before the start of the worg's next turn has Advantage.

description: A worg is an evil predator that delights in hunting and devouring creatures weaker than itself. Cunning and malevolent, worgs roam across the remote wilderness or are raised by goblins and hobgoblins. Those creatures use worgs as mounts, but a worg will turn on its rider if it feels mistreated or malnourished. Worgs speak in their own language and Goblin, and a few learn to speak Common as well.
combat-strategy: Fast (50 ft.) and mean for its tier, it opens with a rush Bite on the most exposed party member, using the trait that the next attack against a bitten target has Advantage — so coordinate with gnolls, hobgoblins, or other allies to stack attacks on the fresh wound in the same round. Prioritize backline casters and anyone separated from the pack's protection, and bite a different target each round to seed Advantage for the whole allied team. Use its speed to flank and reposition rather than stand trading hits; it's only AC 13 and 26 HP. Fight in forests and open plains where the pack can circle, favoring ambush near trails.

name: Wraith

actions.name: Life Drain
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 21 (4d8 + 3) Necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, its Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the damage taken.

actions.name: Create Specter
actions.description: The wraith targets a Humanoid corpse within 10 feet of itself that has been dead for no longer than 1 minute. The target's spirit rises as a Specter in the space of its corpse or in the nearest unoccupied space. The specter is under the wraith's control. The wraith can have no more than seven specters under its control at a time.

automation.advisory: Must target a Humanoid corpse within 10 ft of the wraith that has been dead no longer than 1 minute; the spirit rises as a Specter under the wraith's control and the wraith can have no more than seven specters under its control at a time — corpse eligibility, the 1-minute corpse-age clock, and the seven-specter control cap are GM-adjudicated (§70); pressing this chip models the rise.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.description: The wraith can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: While in sunlight, the wraith has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls.

description:
A wraith is malice incarnate, concentrated into an incorporeal form that seeks to quench all life. The creature is suffused with negative energy, and its mere passage through the world leaves nearby plants blackened and withered. Animals flee from its presence. Even small fires can be extinguished by the sucking oblivion of the wraith's horrifying existence.

Vile Oblivion. When a mortal humanoid lives a debased life or enters into a fiendish pact, it consigns its soul to eternal damnation in the Lower Planes. However sometimes the soul becomes so suffused with negative energy that it collapses in on itself and ceases to exist the instant before it can shuffle off to some horrible afterlife. When this occurs, the spirit becomes a soulless wraith-a malevolent void trapped on the plane where it died. Almost nothing of the wraith's former existence is preserved; in this new form, it exists only to annihilate other life.

Bereft of Body. A wraith can move through solid creatures and objects as easily as a mortal creature moves through fog.
A wraith might retain a few memories of its mortal life as shadowy echoes. However, even the strongest events and emotions become little more than faint impressions, fleeting as half-remembered dreams. A wraith might pause to stare at something that fascinated it in life, or it might curb its wrath in acknowledgment of a past friendship. Such moments come rarely, however, because most wraiths despise what they were as a reminder of what they have become.

Undead Commanders. A wraith can make an undead servant from the spirit of a humanoid creature that has recently suffered a violent death. Such a fragment of woe becomes a specter, spiteful of all that lives.
Wraiths sometimes rule the legions of the dead, plotting the doom of living creatures. When they emerge from their tombs to do battle, life and hope shrivel before them. Even if a wraith's armies are forced to retreat, the lands its forces occupied are so blasted and withered that those who live there often starve and die.

Undead Nature. A wraith doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
combat-strategy: Attack from darkness and solid rock: Incorporeal Movement lets it phase through walls, doors, and allies to appear anywhere, so stage ambushes behind sealed doors and collapsed tunnels. Open with Life Drain on the highest-HP frontline — 21 necrotic plus a permanent HP maximum reduction grinds tanks down toward a fate worse than death. Favour night fights (Sunlight Sensitivity otherwise gives it Disadvantage), and in any fight where humanoids die nearby, use Create Specter on fresh corpses mid-battle to spawn an undead army (up to seven) that swarms the party while it stays at range. Hit-and-run through obstacles it can't be blocked by. Retreat into the Deep Shadow and darkness below a quarter HP or when radiant damage starts landing, returning with its specter roster grown.

name: Wyvern

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The wyvern makes one Bite attack and one Sting attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Sting
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage plus 24 (7d6) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the start of the wyvern's next turn.

description:
Travelers in the wild sometimes look to the skies to see the dark-winged shape of a wyvern carrying its prey. These cousins to the great dragons hunt the same tangled forests and caverns as their kin. Their appearance sends ripples of alarm through the borderlands of civilization.
A wyvern has two scaly legs, leathery wings, and a sinewy tail topped with its most potent weapon: a poison stinger. The poison in a wyvern's stinger can kill a creature in seconds. Extremely potent, wyvern poison burns through its victim's bloodstream, disintegrating veins and arteries on its way to the heart. As deadly as wyverns can be, however, hunters and adventurers often track them to claim the venom, which is used in alchemical compounds and to coat weapons.

Aerial Hunters. A wyvern doesn't fight on the ground unless it can't reach its prey by any other means, or if it has been fooled into a position from which aerial combat isn't an option. If forced into a confrontation on the ground, a wyvern crouches low, keeping its stinger poised above its head as it hisses and growls.

Aggressive and Reckless. A wyvern intent on its prey backs down only if it sustains serious injury, or if its prey eludes it long enough for another easier potential meal to wander along. If it corners a fleeing creature in an enclosure too small to enter, a wyvern guards where the quarry hides, lashing with its stinger whenever opportunity allows.
Although they possess more cunning than ordinary beasts, wyverns lack the intelligence of their draconic cousins. As such, creatures that maintain their composure as a wyvern hunts them from the air can often elude or trick it. Wyverns follow a direct path to their prey, with no thought given to possible ambushes.

Tamed Wyverns. A wyvern can be tamed for use as a mount, but doing so presents a difficult and deadly challenge. Raising one as a hatchling offers the best results. However, a wyvern's violent temperament has cost the life of many a would-be master.
combat-strategy: Solitary and brutal but simple: dive from its 80-ft. flight to land the Multiattack — Bite plus the 10-ft.-reach Sting for 35+ average damage and the Poisoned condition — then take to the air again before the party can retaliate. Prioritize the most isolated target for the Sting; Poisoned victims have Disadvantage on attacks and ability checks, so poison the champion duelist or the concentrating caster to neutralize them. Kite vertically: hover just out of reach of non-reachable melee types, stooping only when it can strike and ascend in the same turn, since 127 HP with AC 14 doesn't invite slugfests against big parties. Watch for concentrated ranged fire and disengage aloft. It fights to the death when defending a nest or territory, otherwise quits once Sting saves keep landing and it drops below half HP.

name: Xorn

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The xorn makes one Bite attack and three Claw attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 17 (4d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Slashing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Charge
bonus_actions.description: The xorn moves up to its Speed or Burrow Speed straight toward an enemy it can sense.

traits.name: Earth Glide
traits.description: The xorn can burrow through nonmagical, unworked earth and stone. While doing so, the xorn doesn't disturb the material it moves through.

traits.name: Treasure Sense
traits.description: The xorn can pinpoint the location of precious metals and stones within 60 feet of itself.

description:
Bizarre creatures native to the Elemental Plane of Earth, xorn sniff out gemstones and precious metals, then tunnel through earth and rock to consume those treasures. On the Material Plane, xorn must range far and wide through the Underdark to sustain themselves, becoming aggressive toward miners and treasure hunters when the valuable minerals of their diet are scarce.
A xorn's unnatural origins are suggested by its unusually heavy body and the large, powerful mouth sitting atop its head. Its three long arms are each tipped with sharp talons, and its three large, stone-lidded eyes see in all directions.

Elemental Travelers. Possessed of the power of elemental earth, a xorn glides through stone and dirt as • easily as a fish swims through water. It doesn't displace earth or stone when it moves, but merges with and flows through it, leaving no tunnel, hole, or hint of its passage.
Xorn prefer not to leave their home plane, where they easily eat their fill of gemstones and precious metals. When a xorn winds up on the Material Plane, whether by accident or from curiosity, it seeks sustenance and a way home.

Beggars and Thieves. Xorn scour the depths of the earth for precious metal and stones. Because they are unable to consume organic material, they ignore most other creatures. However, a xorn's ability to sniff out metals and stones often draws its attention to adventurers carrying coins and gems. Because a xorn isn't evil, it pleads or bargains in the hope of convincing owners to give up their treasure, offering up information it has learned from its travels in exchange. A xorn whose requests are ignored might resort to threats and bullying. If starving or angered, it resorts to force.
combat-strategy: Ambush from stone: it burrows silently via Earth Glide (leaving no trace) and uses tremorsense plus Treasure Sense to home in on whoever is shiny, so let the party walk over it before erupting beneath the wealthiest-looking member. Open with Charge as a bonus action straight up through the floor into melee, then Multiattack — one Bite and three Claws, roughly 41 average damage — on a target caught adjacent. AC 19 and 84 HP make it a brawler that gladly trades blows in tight tunnels where the party can't flank and its 20-ft. burrow beats their movement on rough ground. Target spellcasters and anyone carrying magical items, since it's covetous by nature. Retreat into unworked stone when reduced by half — it can't be chased underground, and it lingers just beneath the surface waiting to burst out again.

name: Yamata no Orochi

traits.name: Regenerative Heads
traits.description: When a head is severed, two more take its place at the start of its next turn unless the wound is burned with Fire or frozen with Cold.

traits.name: Eight Heads
traits.description: Orochi has Advantage on Perception checks and can't be flanked.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If Orochi fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +18, reach 15 ft. Hit: 25 (3d10 + 9) Piercing damage. Plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage.

actions.name: Venom Mist (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 26, each creature within 90 ft. Failure: 77 (22d6) Poison damage. Success: Half damage.

legendary_actions.name: Legendary Action Uses: 3

legendary_actions.name: Bite

description: The eight-forked serpent of the old river-tale, whose bodies braid like eight rivers, whose belly glows like eight lanterns, and who is fed an annual maiden.
combat-strategy: He floods the field with venom mist, biting at four targets at once, and regenerating severed heads unless his necks are burned.

name: Yeti

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The yeti can use its Chilling Gaze and makes two attacks, using Claw or Ice Throw in any combination.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) Cold damage.

actions.name: Ice Throw
actions.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +6, range 30/120 ft. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 2 (1d4) Cold damage.

actions.name: Chilling Gaze
actions.description: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature the yeti can see within 30 feet. Failure: 5 (2d4) Cold damage, and the target has the Paralyzed condition until the start of the yeti's next turn unless the target has Immunity to Cold damage. Success: The target is immune to the Chilling Gaze of all yetis (but not abominable yetis) for 1 hour.
actions.save_effect: 5 (2d4) Cold damage, and the target has the Paralyzed condition until the start of the yeti's next turn unless the target has Immunity to Cold damage. Success: The target is immune to the Chilling Gaze of all yetis (but not abominable yetis) for 1 hour.

traits.name: Fear of Fire
traits.description: If the yeti takes Fire damage, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn.

description:
A yeti's windborne howl sounds out across remote mountains, striking fear into the hearts of the scattered miners and herders that dwell there. These hulking creatures stalk alpine peaks in a ceaseless hunt for food. Their snow-white fur lets them move like ghosts against the frozen landscape. A yeti's icy simian eyes can freeze its prey in place.

Keen Hunters. Folk of the high peaks travel in groups and go armed, knowing that yetis can smell living flesh from miles away. When it finds prey, a yeti moves quickly over ice and stone to claim its meal, howling to the thrill of the hunt. Even in a blizzard, the scent of its quarry draws the yeti through the cold and snow.
Yetis hunt in solitude or in small family groups. When creatures flee from a yeti or engage it in battle, other yetis might catch the scent of blood and close in. The territorial yetis fight one another for the spoils of such battles, and yetis slain in the fight are also eaten, amid euphoric howls.

Terrifying Howlers. Before an avalanche, a blizzard, or a deadly frost, the yetis' howls sweep down the mountain slopes on the icy wind. Some people of the alpine peaks believe that the voices of loved ones killed in avalanches and blizzards sound out in the wails of the yetis, crying warnings of ill omen. More pragmatic folk attest that the yeti's howl is a reminder that, despite the great accomplishments of civilization, the civilized become the hunted in nature's untamed domain.

Brutal Rampagers. When mountain herds are abundant, yetis stay clear of humanoid realms. Driven by hunger, they attack humanoid settlements in waves, breaking down gates and stockade walls that once might have daunted them, then devouring the creatures within.
Devious mountain folk sometimes use the yetis as unwitting weapons. A warlord might lay down slaughtered sheep or goats to draw yetis into an enemy's camp, sowing chaos and thinning the ranks before battle. Mountain clan chiefs, wanting to expand their territory, overhunt local game to diminish the yetis' food supplies, inspiring attacks on humanoid settlements that are swiftly annexed in the aftermath.
combat-strategy: Fight on cliffs and icy slopes where its 40-ft. climb and Stealth +5 set up an ambush from above. Open with Chilling Gaze on a mid-rank hero — DC 13 Con or they're Paralyzed and an easy kill — then Multiattack with Claw and Ice Throw, mixing ranges so melee types waste turns closing while it throws ice. Target the weakest-looking Constitution saves first with the Gaze; paralyzed victims auto-fail Strength saves, so set up prone-and-rend combos on the cliff edge where falling is the real kill. Stay high: enemies must climb while it throws, and it can drop icestones down slopes. Fire gives it Disadvantage, so retreat into snow and blizzards when a mage starts burning, using the storm's concealment to re-hide and re-ambush.

name: Ymir
languages: Speaks to giants in their own tongues.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)

traits.name: Primordial Flesh
traits.description: Ymir can't be affected by Cold, and every weapon that hits him is numbed (Disadvantage on the attacker's next attack with that weapon).

traits.name: World-Flesh
traits.description: When Ymir takes Radiant damage, his body doesn't melt but bleeds into glaciers; he regains 15 Hit Points.

actions.name: Multiattack

actions.name: Stomp
